title: Global Regularization of the Spatial Elliptic Restricted Three-body Problem: Quaternionic, Hamiltonian Formulation
abstract: Any objects in space may encounter singularity due to the inverse-square law of the gravitational force, hindering the analysis and propagation of particle motion in space. Regularization in celestial mechanics removes such gravitational singularities in equations of motion by transforming the time and coordinates. This paper addresses a class of regularization methods known as global regularization for restricted three-body problems (R3BPs), which simultaneously removes the two singularities (e.g., Earth and Moon in cislunar space). It enables analysis, propagation, and prediction of particle motion throughout the domain of R3BPs, which is in stark contrast to regularizing each singularity individually. In particular, this paper develops a formulation for global regularization of the spatial elliptic R3BP (ER3BP) under external perturbations. The presented formulation leverages mathematical tools from quaternionic (hyper-complex) algebra and Hamiltonian mechanics. This approach enables us to (i) elegantly handle the four-dimensional coordinates arising from the dimension-lifting operation for spatial regularization, (ii) systematically derive the coordinate-momentum transformation while preserving the canonical structure and incorporating perturbing forces, and (iii) provide geometric insights for analyzing the regularity of the transformation, resulting Hamiltonian, and dynamical flow. Numerical examples demonstrate the validity of the mathematical results as well as significant numerical benefits of the regularization formulation in perturbed Earth-Moon ER3BP.

title: Tensor Degenerations for Matrix Multiplication
abstract: Let ${\mathbb K}$ be an arbitrary field. We study tensor degenerations for square matrix multiplication over the field ${\mathbb K}$, and mainly prove for any integer $n\ge5$ the uniform dyadic estimate \[ \underline{\mathrm R}_{\mathbb K}({\mathsf M}_{2^n}) \le 2^{2n+1}\] which implies that $\omega(\mathbb K)\le 2+1/n$, where the border rank $\underline{\mathrm R}_{\mathbb K}(T)$ is the least $r$ for which the scalar extension of $T$ to an algebraic closure of $\mathbb K$ lies in the Zariski closure of the tensors of rank at most $r$, and $\omega(\mathbb K)$ is the matrix multiplication exponent over the field ${\mathbb K}$. This improves the current best record $\omega(\mathbb K)<2.371177$ greatly, and answers affirmatively the long-standing open question whether the value $\omega({\mathbb K})$ is exactly $2$. The implementation disclosure and appendices in this paper give fixed source maps, interpolation data, terminal incidence ledgers, and deterministic check counts for independent reconstruction.

title: Insertion and expansion of cylinders around the unit ball
abstract: A unit ball is surrounded with a ring of $n$ equal infinite circular cylinders. Each cylinder touches the ball and its two neighbors. Can one more cylinder of the same radius be added if the configuration may be rearranged? Can the $n$ cylinders instead be enlarged, and by how much? We prove that insertion is impossible for $3\le n\le7$ and possible for $n\ge9$. The case $n=8$ remains open. The case $n=6$ is Kuperberg's problem from 1990, which was resolved recently. We prove that the ring of four cylinders cannot be expanded. This settles a conjecture of Ogievetsky and Shlosman from 2018. For $n\ge5$ the largest possible expansion radius remains unknown.

title: Bijective Non-Contractive Maps of Hereditarily Precompact Quasi-Metric Spaces Need Not Be Isometries
abstract: Zavarzina asked whether every bijective non-contractive self-map of a precompact quasi-metric space is an isometry. We answer the question in the negative, in a stronger form: on a hereditarily precompact quasi-metric space (a tolled extension of the irrational rotation over Z), the shift is a bijective non-contractive map that is not an isometry. The construction generalizes: for every metric space Y, every bijective isometry $\sigma$ of Y, and every point whose $\sigma$-orbit is aperiodic and totally bounded, the tolled Z-extension is such a counterexample; instances include the irrational rotation and the p-adic odometer. The conjugate space is not precompact, so the two-sided hypothesis of Zavarzina's positive result is sharp, and the space is not expand-contract plastic. The core results, including the general scheme and the circle instance, are machine-checked in Lean 4 over mathlib, sorry-free (no unproved steps), under a pinned toolchain. A structural section proves a monochromy theorem: for every strict pair on a hereditarily precompact space, one endpoint's backward self-returns have self-defect at least a quarter of the pair's defect, uniformly on a chain-closed displacement set. Boundary results delimit what remains open: one-sided compactness together with separation.
comments: 18 pages. The Lean 4 verification artifact (TollSpiral.lean, toolchain pins, SHA-256 manifest) is included as ancillary files and archived with the paper at Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.22801324

title: The rhombic dodecahedral conjecture
abstract: We prove that every three-dimensional parallelohedron $P$ satisfies \[ \mathcal H^2(\partial P)\ge 12\sqrt2\,r(P)^2, \] where $r(P)$ is the inradius of $P$, with equality if and only if $P$ is similar to the regular rhombic dodecahedron.

title: Local Fan-type obstructions and Ore-type conditions for rainbow Hamiltonicity in graph systems
abstract: Let $G=(G_1,...,G_n)$ be a graph system on a common $n$-vertex set $V$. For $v\in V$, set \[ \delta(v)=\min_{i\in[n]}d_{G_i}(v), \qquad E_{\cap}=\bigcap_{i=1}^n E(G_i), \] and let $d^c(u,v)$ denote the length of a shortest rainbow $u$--$v$ path. We study Hamiltonicity conditions imposed only on pairs at small rainbow distance. Suppose that every $G_i$ is $2$-connected and that \[ \delta(u),\delta(v)<\frac n2, \qquad d^c(u,v)\le2 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad uv\in E_{\cap}. \] Our main result shows that any system satisfying this local Fan-type condition but containing no rainbow Hamilton cycle must satisfy \[ E_{\cap}=\varnothing, \qquad \sum_{v\in V}\delta(v)\le\frac{n^2-1}{2}. \] Consequently, either $E_{\cap}\ne\varnothing$ or $\sum_{v\in V}\delta(v)\ge\lceil n^2/2\rceil$ guarantees a rainbow Hamilton cycle. We further prove that the local Ore-type condition \[ \delta(u)+\delta(v)<n, \qquad d^c(u,v)\le2 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad uv\in E_{\cap} \] already forces a rainbow Hamilton cycle. Along the way, the Fan-type hypothesis yields a rainbow Hamilton path and a rainbow $(n-1)$-cycle. For diagonal systems, our conditions reduce to the classical Fan and local Ore conditions. The proofs combine rainbow rotation--extension with a double-counting argument in an auxiliary digraph. Keywords: graph system; rainbow Hamilton cycle; rainbow distance; Fan-type condition; Ore-type condition; rotation--extension.

title: An Improved Lower Bound for Packing 203 Equal Spheres in a Unit Cube
abstract: This paper reports an improved numerical lower bound for packing 203 equal spheres in a unit cube. Let r denote the maximum common radius of equal non-overlapping spheres that can be packed in a unit cube. For N = 203, the configuration currently listed in Packomania has a feasible radius of approximately r = 0.088145402159. Starting from this public configuration, we perform further numerical optimization and obtain a new feasible configuration with r > 0.088145634693. The final configuration is checked by an independent verification program using 100-digit arithmetic. All 20503 sphere-pair constrains and all 1218 sphere-wall constraints are satisfied. The coordinates of the new configuration and the related programs are provided as supplementary material.

title: A Counterexample to Three Conjectures of Luo
abstract: We give a single counterexample to Conjectures 1--3 as stated in Luo's paper: a minimal two-tetrahedron triangulation of the lens space L(3,1) with a null-homotopic loop edge. The proof uses quadrilateral matching equations, an explicit calculation of shape parameters, and known results on volume maximization.

title: The strong nonfinite basis property of $S_7$
abstract: We prove that the three-element additively idempotent semiring $S_7$ is strongly nonfinitely based: every finite additively idempotent semiring whose generated variety contains $S_7$ has no finite equational basis. This answers Problem~1.2 in Yue, Ren and Gao's paper Explicit equational bases for the power semirings of $S_7$ affirmatively. The proof combines a rigidity property of set systems with private points and a probabilistic construction derived from semilinear sets of letter counts in finite semigroups. The argument allows arbitrary polynomial substitutions and does not assume commutative multiplication. As consequences, both power semirings of the multiplicative reduct of $S_7$, and both power semirings of every finite group of order at least three, are strongly nonfinitely based. All algebras are considered in the signature $(+,\cdot)$ without nullary operations.

title: A separating identity for matrix semirings over $S_7$
abstract: Jiao and Ren proved that the varieties generated by the matrix semirings $\M_n(S_7)$ form an ascending chain of nonfinitely based varieties, and asked whether consecutive members are equal for all $n\geq2$. We give a negative answer by exhibiting an identity in five variables that holds in $\M_2(S_7)$ and fails in $\M_3(S_7)$. Consequently, $\V(\M_2(S_7))$ is a proper subvariety of $\V(\M_n(S_7))$ for every $n\geq3$. The proof uses the cubic-power property established by Jiao and Ren and a description of products equal to the constant matrix $[a]_n$. The identity forces two distinct indices to exhaust the index set in dimension two; an additional index yields an explicit counterexample in dimension three.

title: Equilateral sets in $\ell_p^n$ beyond $n+1$: Linear excess and dimension cost
abstract: How many equilateral points can $\ell_p^n$ contain beyond $n+1$? For every fixed real $p>4$, we construct equilateral sets for which the number of points beyond $n+1$ grows at least linearly with $n$. For every fixed dimension, we prove that the maximum is $n+1$ at all sufficiently large finite $p$, with an explicit threshold. The least dimension admitting any fixed number of extra points is $p^{1+o(1)}$ as $p\to\infty$. The constructions and finite bounds are formalised in Lean. Thus $p=4$ marks the boundary: $n+1$ is exact in every dimension for $2\leq p\leq4$, while at every fixed finite $p>4$ the excess grows at least linearly with dimension.

title: Splitting of projective modules over some affine algebras
abstract: This article focuses on defining the Euler class group of stably free module and analyzes the condition for existence of unimodular element in corresponding projective module.This is an improvisation of work by Banerjee and Das, On a question of Nori:Obstructions,improvements and appliaction. If A is a smooth affine algebra over certain affaine algebras.

title: Energy, Passivity, and Diffusive Representations in Anisotropic Fractional Maxwell--Cole--Cole Media
abstract: This study develops an energy formulation for linear anisotropic Maxwell--Cole--Cole media with multiple fractional polarization channels, passive conductivity, prescribed currents, and finite-terminal Caputo memory with zero prehistory. A weighted solution class captures the integrable fractional initial layer generated by quiescent polarization. Fractional polarization power then separates into a nonnegative history storage and a nonnegative constitutive dissipation rate. Although the instantaneous rate may diverge at initialization, it remains integrable, while stored history energy and accumulated loss vanish initially. Combined with the Poynting theorem, this decomposition yields a global field-plus-memory identity that establishes electromagnetic passivity, closed-system energy decay, and conditional uniqueness under zero-supply boundary conditions. The framework also recovers the Debye, instantaneous-dielectric, vanishing-susceptibility, and vacuum limits under convergence assumptions. A positive diffusive representation provides a second decomposition whose storage never exceeds the history storage. Their difference is an exact nonnegative weighted variance that vanishes only for a zero polarization history. In agreement with these time-domain results, the finite-time harmonic response approaches the anisotropic multichannel Cole--Cole permittivity, whose Hermitian imaginary part ensures nonnegative cycle-averaged absorption. A reproducible single-channel study shows that fractional order broadens the dielectric-loss band, redistributes wave attenuation, strengthens the integrable initial power layer, and prolongs the step-response tail. An exact electric-step response verifies both energy representations. The formulation connects fractional initial layers, hereditary storage, passivity, diffusive relaxation, dispersion, absorption, and attenuation in a local constitutive model.

title: Triangles and quadrilaterals suffice
abstract: We prove a conjecture proposed by Robert J. Lang over 20 years ago, stating that in a circle-packed origami design, any axial polygon with 5 or more sides can be reduced by properly adding a new circle. The proof is based on the structure of the medial axis of the region enclosed by the circles, and yields a concrete algorithm for finding the added circle. The result extends to configurations involving rivers.

title: Forbidding $r$-extension of $C_4$ -- a counterexample of the Anstee-Sali conjecture
abstract: In this note we prove $\mathrm{forb}(n,\mathbf{1}_{r-2}\times C_4)=\Theta(n^{r-1/2})$, thus providing a series of counterexamples of a 2005 conjecture of the first two authors. Here $\mathbf{1}_{r-2}\times C_4$ is the $r$-extension of the 4-cycle, that is the $r$-uniform hypergraph of four edges obtained by joining a set of $r-2$ vertices to each edge of $C_4$. $\mathrm{forb}(n,F)$ is the largest number of edges of a simple hypergraph $G$ on $n$ vertices without \emph{trace} (induced subhypergraph) $F$.

title: Upper Bounds on the Comon Rank Gap of Real Symmetric Third-Order Tensors
abstract: Let $T$ be a nonzero real symmetric third-order tensor. Denote by $r(T)$ its CP rank, by $s(T)$ its symmetric rank, by $d(T)$ its essential dimension, and put $e(T)=r(T)-d(T)$. We establish two complementary upper bounds for the Comon rank gap $$\Delta(T):= s(T)-r(T)\leq\min\{C_{ec}(e(T)),\ C_{dc}(d(T))\}.$$ The excess-controlled function $C_{ec}(e)$ is zero for $0\leq e\leq3$ and equals $9e-3$ for $e\geq4$. In particular, the equality $C_{ec}(e(T))=0$ for $0\leq e\leq3$ extends Friedland's flattening-rank criterion for real symmetric third-order tensors by two additional rank layers. The dimension-controlled function $C_{dc}(d)$ is zero for $d=0$, equals $(d^2-4d+10)/3$ for $1\leq d\leq18$, and equals $d^2/4+d/4+3/2$ for $d\geq19$. The excess estimate follows from the alternating equations and decomposable-bivector support geometry; a low-wedge descent gives the vanishing range $e\leq3$. The dimension estimate combines a transverse polar-completion bound with a shifted estimate for the maximum real Waring rank. Thus the two bounds measure different features of the same tensor and remain effective in complementary regimes.

title: Multiplicity-One Structure in Graded Zero-Divisor Graphs
abstract: Let \(H\) be a multiplicative group, \(R\) a commutative \(H\)-graded ring, and \(M\) a nonzero finitely generated gr-semisimple \(H\)-graded \(R\)-module. We assume that \(M\) admits a fixed decomposition into powers of gr-simple modules with pairwise distinct annihilators, each repeated block carrying the componentwise grading. For a nonzero homogeneous element \(x\), we compute the colon ideal \((Rx:M)\) and show that it is determined by the multiplicity-one blocks on which \(x\) has a nonzero component. This leads to the criterion \( x\leftrightarrow y \text{ if and only if } \sigma(x)\cap\sigma(y)=\varnothing, \) where \(x\leftrightarrow y\) means that \(x\) and \(y\) are adjacent in \(\Gamma_H(M)\). Thus adjacency is governed by disjointness of multiplicity-one obstruction supports. The corresponding obstruction classes form a weighted disjointness structure: higher multiplicities affect the sizes of the classes, but not the adjacency relation between their supports. We use this description to study graph invariants, reconstruction, and Kneser-type layers, and, in the finite case, to obtain formulas for the obstruction-class sizes and a reduction of the adjacency spectrum.

title: What Can Language Models Inherit from Solomonoff Induction? Limits, Attainable Properties, and What Served Conditionals Reveal
abstract: A familiar line of reasoning runs as follows: language models are flexible approximators trained under a strictly proper loss, so scale brings them closer to Solomonoff induction, and their predictive success is evidence of that approach. We apply known results from algorithmic information theory, universal prediction and Bayesian consistency. In its uniform form the conclusion holds for no computable model: each has cheap environments it never learns, and every uniformly computable family of total predictors shares one on which each member fails beyond a horizon growing with its index, so ``closer'' can hold only pointwise, one environment at a time. Nor could the offered routes certify even that: finite evaluation cannot certify agreement on rarely reached contexts, perfect corpus fit selects the corpus law as prior, and asymptotic criteria cannot see the constants that carry Solomonoff's guarantee. Our lens is the Kraft inequality read for predictors. Every model has at most the same budget of predictive success, so Solomonoff's predictor, which leaves part of it unspent, differs from a language model not in having more of it but in where it spends it; on mutually singular families this is exact, and only full-mass Bayes mixtures reach the frontier. We then discuss what is inheritable, including in-context learning as amortised Bayesian inference; what survives within a context window; which Solomonoff-like properties a deployed system should have or avoid; and what served conditionals determine. A closing table states what common practices certify and what to report. Tests are developed in a companion paper.

title: Generalized PINN-Based Inverse Estimation of Spatially Varying Heat Transfer Coefficients with Transfer Learning
abstract: This study investigates generalized boundary representations and transfer learning for physics-informed neural-network (PINN) estimation of spatially varying convective heat transfer coefficients (HTCs) in jet impingement cooling. Piecewise-linear (PWL) and neural-network boundary estimators are inferred from transient interior-temperature measurements and evaluated against CFD-CHT reference HTC profiles at Reynolds numbers of 5000, 10000 and 15000. A discrete Adjoint-FEM formulation with gradient regularization based on the $H^1$-seminorm provides an independent inverse-method comparison. Transfer learning is investigated under two source-target conditions: transfer between noise levels at the same Reynolds number, and transfer from a controlled Gaussian-profile problem to CFD-CHT-derived target problems at different Reynolds numbers. For the representative Re = 5000 target with 5% measurement noise, quadratic, PWL, and neural-network PINNs achieve relative HTC-profile errors of 5.08, 5.31 and 5.19%, respectively, while generalized representations reduce the error for the Re = 15000 target from 16.76% for the quadratic PINN to 14.41% and 14.46%. Transfer learning reduces target-training time by 57.86-81.71% for fixed-Reynolds-number transfer and by 50.59-84.94% for Gaussian-to-CHT transfer. Its effect on reconstruction accuracy is target dependent: fixed-profile PWL transfer remains within 0.30 percentage points of scratch training, whereas Gaussian-to-CHT transfer produces differences of 0.10-1.52 percentage points across targets and representations. These results demonstrate that generalized PINN representations can accommodate spatially varying HTC profiles without a prescribed quadratic form, while transfer learning can substantially reduce target-training cost for repeated inverse estimation, with the resulting reconstruction accuracy depending on source-target compatibility.

title: The geometric classification of Novikov-Poisson and Gelfand-Dorfman algebras
abstract: We give the geometric classification of complex 3-dimensional Novikov-Poisson and Gelfand-Dorfman algebras. In particular, we prove that the variety of complex 3-dimensional Novikov-Poisson algebras is 12-dimensional; it has 4 irreducible components and has no rigid algebras; the variety of complex 3-dimensional Gelfand-Dorfman algebras is 11-dimensional; it has 10 irreducible components and has 3 rigid algebras. As an additional result, we have the geometric classification of complex 3-dimensional Novikov algebras: it is 9-dimensional, and it has $4$ irreducible components with one rigid algebra.

title: Perfect Reconstruction Cannot Show Whether Two Codebooks on a VAE's Latent Space Agree
abstract: Many systems read the latent space of a variational autoencoder (VAE) as discrete codes, and rely on each latent being read back as the code it was written as. Shannon (1948) took such a shared codebook as given; inside a VAE nothing enforces it. We prove that no item of a standard training report can reveal whether the written and read codes agree on encoded data. We construct two VAEs that reconstruct every input perfectly, infer exactly, and match on every per-example ELBO and every code histogram, yet agreement is one in the first and zero in the second. We then show that the ELBO's own terms bound how far a measured agreement can move: the variational gap bounds the shift to exact inference, and the rate bounds the shift to generation from the prior. For Gaussian posteriors, a mean-field encoder pays an exact price in the gap that depends on its choice of axes. On probabilistic PCA the gap certifies a trained encoder in all 75 settings we test, at agreement between 0.76 and 0.97. On 240 trained VAEs, a floor set by the rate and the dataset size rules out rate-side certification in advance for 66 models, and none of them certifies. The results yield a simple protocol, Certify-or-Measure, for any pipeline that reads a VAE as codes.
comments: 28 pages, 4 figures, 4 tables. Supplementary material (per-run results, precommit documents and verification scripts) is provided as ancillary files

title: SIREN: A nonlinear Rankine-source boundary element solver for the stationary motion of a marine vehicle in calm water
abstract: SIREN (Ship Inviscid Resistance and Elevation eNgine) is a Rankine-source panel solver for the steady wave resistance of a ship, in the tradition of Dawson's method. The free-surface condition is linearised about a base flow, and the linearisation is iterated. In the present formulation the base flow is the solution of a Neumann problem on the actual boundary: sources on the entire hull, wet and dry, and on the free surface panels, with impermeability imposed on both, so that the free surface acts as a rigid lid at the position it currently occupies. This replaces the classical double-body flow, whose image about z=0 is meaningful only for a flat surface and a hull cut at z=0, and it removes the need for desingularised free-surface panels. In the non-linear iteration the free-surface panels are moved rigidly in the vertical to the relaxed wave elevation at their centroid, the hull panels are marked wet or dry against the moved surface, and the base flow is recomputed on the moved geometry; impermeability applies to the whole hull regardless of this marking, which is used only to select which panels enter the force integral, and under-relaxation is confined to the passes where the non-linear correction accumulates without being reset. The radiation condition is imposed by a one-row upstream shift of the collocation points, and the wave resistance is obtained by pressure integration and, independently, by transverse wave-cut analysis.

title: Polygons and coplanar points on submanifolds of codimension 2
abstract: Problem 73 on Green's list of open problems asks whether a smooth submanifold of codimension two in $\mathbb{R}^n$ must meet some affine two-plane in five points when $n$ is large. In this paper, we answer this question for every $n \geq 6$. Every nonempty relatively open subset of such a submanifold contains the vertices of an affinely regular pentagon, and the bound $n \geq 6$ is sharp for affinely regular pentagons. More generally, for every prime $p \geq 5$, the graph of a continuous map from a ball in $\mathbb{R}^{p-1}$ to $\mathbb{R}^2$ contains an affinely regular $p$-gon. A second argument gives six coplanar points when $n \geq 7$. Both proofs find the points by making the low Fourier modes of the graph map vanish along a circle.

title: Sharp Antipode-Neighbor Bounds in Every Dimension
abstract: Let $P\subset\mathbb R^d$ be finite with $\operatorname{diam}(P)\le1$. For $0<\varepsilon<1$, let $\mathcal N_\varepsilon(P)$ denote the number of ordered pairs at distance at most $\varepsilon$, including the diagonal, and let $\mathcal A_\varepsilon(P)$ denote the number of ordered pairs at distance at least $1-\varepsilon$. We prove the sharp bound \[ \mathcal N_\varepsilon(P)\gtrsim_d \varepsilon^{(d-1)/2}\mathcal A_\varepsilon(P) \] conjectured by Steinerberger (2025). More generally, the same inequality holds for finite positive Borel measures. The main input is a uniform $L^2$ estimate, at cap thickness comparable to lattice spacing, for a supporting-direction incidence operator. In gnomonic coordinates, this operator is controlled by an incidence estimate for small Fenchel--Young gaps.

title: Symmetric Cryptography via Dirichlet Convolution
abstract: We discuss a new symmetric-key cipher for digital data encryption. Its implementation is fast, memory efficient, and resilient against classical, AI-assisted, and quantum attacks. Let $x$, $k$, and $c$ be elements of a finite abelian group $G$ with operation $+$ and neutral element $0$. Suppose one is given ciphertext $c=x+k$. Retrieving the plaintext $x=c-k$ from the ciphertext is trivial when the key $k$ is known. Without the key, however, recovering $x$ amounts to a blind search. Even if an efficient criterion were available for identifying the plaintext among all group elements, the average number of trials would remain prohibitively large when the group is sufficiently large. The challenge in constructing a practical cryptosystem is therefore to identify a sufficiently rich group $G$, together with efficient algorithms that enable an immersion of \emph{real digital data} into $G$ and efficient evaluation of the group operations. The proposed cipher is based on generalized Dirichlet convolution over finite fields. We investigate its security against plaintext attacks from an information-theoretic perspective. The nonlocal structure of Dirichlet convolution naturally permits plaintext salting, providing protection against plaintext attacks while allowing controlled key reuse. We establish perfect masking properties over finite fields and prove that the resulting cipher achieves information-theoretic security under key reuse when the underlying arithmetic is carried out in $\mathbb{F}_p$ with $p>2$. For arithmetic over $\mathbb{F}_2$, some information leakage remains, leading to a finite key-reuse budget.

title: $n$-Valued Analogue of Abel's Theorem
abstract: Abel's classical theorem shows that a continuously differentiable one-dimensional associative law with a two-sided unit is locally equivalent to addition under a change of coordinate. We prove an $n$-valued analogue in the algebraic and formal settings. Over a field of characteristic zero, every associative algebraic $n$-valued monoid on $\mathbb P^1$ with a strong two-sided unit is commutative. Over a reduced commutative $\mathbb Q$-algebra, any one-dimensional formal $n$-valued group is commutative. We then classify $n$-valued formal groups over arbitrary $\mathbb Q$-algebras that are integral domains: for any $n$-valued formal group there is a unique divisor $m$ of $n$ such that the law is strongly isomorphic to the $n/m$-fold diagonal of the cyclic elementary $m$-valued law $\mathbb G_m$. This proves Kholodov's classification conjecture over integral domain $\mathbb Q$-algebras.

title: Equivariant Seiberg-Witten equations on Hermitian symmetric spaces
abstract: We formulate and solve a $G$-equivariant analogue of the Seiberg-Witten equations on any irreducible Hermitian symmetric space $G/K$. We use a canonical $K$-invariant form to define a twisted Hodge operator generalising self-duality to higher dimensions. The resulting equivariant Seiberg-Witten equations arise, for a compact $G/K$, as conditions for the absolute minima of an energy functional. Their linear part has a representation theoretic interpretation: the same Weyl group data control the highest-weight realisation of the positive Dirac kernel in the compact case and its discrete-series realisation on the non-compact dual. This space of harmonic spinors collapses almost entirely by the quadratic conditions of the monopole equation. In the compact case, the equivariant moduli set, when non-empty, is a single gauge class, identifying with the $G$-invariant part of Bradlow's trichotomy for vortices, while in the non-compact case, every irreducible solution sits outside the discrete series.

title: Maximal volumes of pyramids in the unit cube
abstract: Let $Q_n=[0,1]^n$, $n\ge2$. Denote by $M_n$ be the maximal volume of a pyramid in $Q_n$ whose base is a hyperplane section of $Q_n$, and by $M_n^0$ the corresponding maximum when the section contains the center of $Q_n$. We prove that $nM_n<(n+1)M_{n+1}^0$.

title: An upper bound for the three-dimensional moving sofa problem in a snaky corridor
abstract: Let $K_M \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be the "snaky" corridor with unit-square cross-section: an infinite entry arm parallel to the $x$-axis, a middle arm parallel to the $y$-axis whose clear straight section has length $M$, and an infinite exit arm parallel to the $z$-axis, with the two turns lying in the $x$-$y$ and $y$-$z$ planes. Let $V^*(K_M)$ be the supremum of the volumes of connected bodies that can be moved continuously (by rigid motions) from the entry arm to the exit arm while remaining inside $K_M$. We prove $V^*(K_M) \le 7.8691$ for every $M \ge 3.53$ (Theorem A); by a sharper analysis of the same mechanism, $V^*(K_M) \le 4.2862$ for every $M \ge 2.61$ (Theorem B); and, by replacing the final analytic caps with a certified branch-and-bound computation over the compact family of entry tubes compatible with the forced events, $V^*(K_M) \le 3.4083$ for every $M > 2.2$ (Theorem C; computer-assisted, in double precision with conservative slack). In particular all three bounds apply to the corridor with $M = 4$ used in Problem 6.64 of Georgiev, G\'omez-Serrano, Tao and Wagner (arXiv:2511.02864), and uniformly to every "turns far apart" reading of that problem. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first upper bound for the snaky-corridor 3D moving sofa problem; previously not even finiteness of $V^*$ had been recorded. This note proves upper bounds only; combined with the certified lower bound 1.8558404 from the author's separate certification work via the problem's own evaluation pipeline, the state of the problem becomes $1.8558404 \le V^*(K_4) \le 3.4083$. Theorems A and B are elementary and self-contained: a first-crossing (elbow) event forces a definite tilt of the body's own entry tube, and Fubini-type chord estimates for tilted tubes cap the volume. Theorem C certifies, by the same forced-event skeleton, the largest corridor volume that any admissible entry tube can carry.
comments: 18 pages. Code, machine-verification scripts and resumable certificates at https://github.com/Lomnus-ai/sofa3d-upper-bound

title: New certified lower bounds for the moving sofa problem in a three-dimensional snaky corridor
abstract: Consider the "snaky" corridor $K_4 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ from Problem 6.64 of arXiv:2511.02864: a tube of unit-square cross-section whose two right-angle turns lie in perpendicular planes, with a straight middle section of clear length $4$. We exhibit explicit rigid motions of connected bodies through $K_4$ and certify their volumes with the problem's own evaluation pipeline, unmodified, at the tight motion tolerances of its final scoring stage (translation $0.005$, rotation $0.05$ degrees). The certificates give $V^*(K_4) \ge 1.8355162$ at grid fineness $0.002$ and $V^*(K_4) \ge 1.8558404$ at grid fineness $0.001$, against the previously reported $1.81$; rerunning the pipeline's published best path under the identical configuration yields $1.8179428$, so every comparison is path against path under one fixed certifier. Three stages produce the record motion: a simple "staggered twist" backbone in which the whole 90-degree twist about the tube axis happens inside the second turn; evolutionary (CMA-ES) refinement, including a mixed-fidelity scheme that re-scores each generation's leading candidates on a grid twice as fine and lets those ranks steer recombination; and a gradient polish carried out directly at the finer carve resolution, guarded by periodic rebuilding of the frozen interpolation structure and by a penalty on control-pose spacing. These guards close three documented failure modes in which an optimizer inflates its own objective: frozen-structure inflation, spacing stretch, and exploitation of a coarse grid by optimizing and selecting on it. A staircase-based predictor with two grid bases, anchored by matching grid sensitivity, forecast the certificates to about $0.001$ before the runs. With the companion note's upper bound $V^*(K_4) \le 3.4083$, the problem now sits in the bracket $1.8558404 \le V^*(K_4) \le 3.4083$. All paths, notebooks and certified results are public.

title: Hereditary NC Polynomials & Positivity Domains
abstract: Noncommutative polynomials, elements of the free algebra generated by several noncommuting variables $x_1,...,x_g,x_1^*,...,x_g^*$, are of importance in noncommutative algebra, free analysis and real algebraic geometry. We allow matrix coefficients and view these noncommutative polynomials as functions in several size-free matrix variables. The free locus of a noncommutative polynomial $f$ is the sequence of hypersurfaces $\mathscr{Z}_n(f)=\{X\in M_n(\mathbb{C})^g:\det f(X) = 0\}$. When $f$ is Hermitian, the positivity domain of $f$ is the sequence of semialgebraic sets $\mathcal{D}_n(f)=\{X\in M_n(\mathbb{C})^g:f(X)\text{ is positive semidefinite}\}$. We show for well-behaved cases that the Euclidean boundary of the positivity domain is Zariski dense in the free locus. This leads to a certificate for equality of positivity domains of coefficient-irreducible unsignatured atomic quadratics. Finally, we describe the geometric structure of positivity domains of hereditary quadratic polynomials through $\Gamma$-convexity.

title: Upper bounds for Jung constants of $\ell_1^d$
abstract: For every integer $k\ge1$, we prove that each nonempty bounded set in real $\ell_1^{4k+1}$ has an ambient enclosing ball of radius at most $(4k-1)/(4k)$ times its diameter. The bound is sharp in dimension five: $J(\ell_1^5)=3/4$. If a Hadamard matrix of order $4k$ exists, then $J(\ell_1^{4k-1})=J(\ell_1^{4k})=J(\ell_1^{4k+1})=(4k-1)/(4k)$. The upper bound for every $k\ge1$ has been formalized in Lean.

title: Linear maps preserving the matrix discriminant. An enhanced approach
abstract: The discriminant of a square matrix is defined as a discriminant of its characteristic polynomial. In this paper we provide a description of linear maps preserving the matrix discriminant assuming that the ground field is large enough. Our description generalizes the known results to the case where the field may have a finite cardinality and its characteristic may divide the size of considered matrices. To obtain this description, we extend the approach used in our previous work on the subject and, in addition to that, introduce new invariants for the action of all bijective linear maps preserving a given polynomial, which are on independent interest and could be applied to other problems in the theory of linear preservers.

title: A Proof of the Analytic Entropy Conjecture
abstract: We prove that the geodesic flow of a closed real-analytic Riemannian manifold has zero topological entropy if it admits globally defined, real-analytic Liouville integrals. This proves a longstanding conjecture proposed by Bolsinov and Taimanov.

title: Strong nonfinite basability of the three-element flat semiring $S_7$
abstract: We prove that the three-element flat semiring $S_7$ is strongly nonfinitely based within the class of additively idempotent semirings. More generally, let $\mathcal N$ be the subvariety of $\Var(S_7)$ defined by $x^2y\approx x^2$. For every finite ai-semiring $A$, each variety $\mathcal W$ satisfying $\mathcal N\subseteq\mathcal W\subseteq\Var(A)$ has infinite axiomatic rank.

title: An Explicit Bound for the First Dirichlet Eigenvalue via Two Moments
abstract: Let $(M^n,g)$, $n\ge2$, be a compact connected Riemannian manifold with smooth nonempty boundary, $\operatorname{Ric}_M\ge(n-1)Kg$ for $K>0$, and nonnegative outward boundary mean curvature. We derive an explicit algebraic lower bound $B_\eta$ for the first Dirichlet eigenvalue from Kasue's mixed inradius model. With $R$ the inradius and $s=4KR^2/\pi^2$, the bound involves one square root and approximates the model eigenvalue with relative error $O_n(s^4)$ as $s\downarrow0$ for fixed $n$. The construction uses the first two moments of a positive representation of the averaged model potential and a sharp pointwise corrector estimate. For the chosen spectral transfer, the first two moments determine an optimal bound. We also show that the model eigenvalue is the geometric infimum at fixed $(n,K,R)$. For $0<s<1$, it is approached by smooth collapsing balls with sectional curvature at least $K$ and totally geodesic boundary. At the maximal inradius, the model value is attained by the round hemisphere. The bound strictly improves the variance refinement throughout $0<s\le1$. We also give a direct algebraic comparison with an optimized power-test benchmark.

title: Associativity of discretized triangular norms
abstract: In this article, we mainly investigate when the binary operation $T^{[n]}:[0, 1]^2\rightarrow [0, 1]$ satisfies the associative law and thus becomes a triangular norm where \begin{equation*} T^{[n]}(x,y)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll} f_{n}(T(f_{n}(x),f_{n}(y))), &\text{if}\,\, (x,y)\in{[0,1)^{2}}, \\ \min\{x,y\}, &\text{otherwise,} \end{array}\right. \end{equation*} $f_{n}:[0,1]\rightarrow\left\{0, \frac{1}{n}, \frac{2}{n}, \dots, \frac{n-1}{n}, 1\right\}$ given by $f_{n}(x)=\frac{1}{n}{\lfloor nx \rfloor}$ with $n$ a positive integer and $T:[0, 1]^2\rightarrow [0, 1]$ is a triangular norm. We present some sufficient conditions for $T^{[n]}$ to be triangular norms, and for $T^{[n]}$ to be never associative when $T$ is strictly monotonic.

title: How long is a game of Uno? A counting law for large hands and the Wild Draw Four hoard
abstract: We study the length of one round of Uno under the official rules, for N players who each start with M cards. The fastest possible round takes at least M turns with two players and at least 2M-1 turns with three or more, and both bounds are attained for small M. An exact search over random deals shows that real deals rarely allow them. Under the official rules a round has no maximum length. Under forced play the probability that a round lasts more than t turns decays exponentially in t at a rate that does not depend on M. Our main result concerns very large hands. If every card a player ever holds is eventually played, a round lasts (27/19)NM turns to first order, and the constant depends only on the composition of the deck. The official rule that a Wild Draw Four may only be played by a player who holds no card of the current colour breaks this law. Every large hand hoards Wild Draw Fours, M/23 of them per player, and the round ends with a dumping endgame. For an even number of players this gives (53/46)NM turns. For an odd number of players the dumping cannot alternate round the table, and the endgame settles into a seating pattern whose turn rate we compute numerically. Simulations with up to 32,000 cards per hand support these limits. Finally we solve a small strategy game: with two players the Nash equilibrium over a family of 48 strategies is a single pure strategy that wins 62.8% of rounds against uniformly random play.
comments: 8 pages, 3 figures, 4 tables. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23232696

title: Distinguished bases and the braid group action for solutions of the tt*-Toda equations
abstract: We implement (in a concrete example) a procedure of Dubrovin which gives a braid group action on spaces of solutions of ordinary differential equations such as the quantum differential equation of complex projective space. Such actions originated in physics for the tt* (topological-antitopological fusion) equations. We make the procedure systematic by utilizing an algebraic description of braid group actions on distinguished bases. We also generalize to the case of (arbitrary) solutions of the tt*-Toda equations, one of which corresponds to the quantum cohomology of complex projective space.

title: WZIP and WLZ4: LZ77 Codecs with Match-Length-Dependent Sliding Windows
abstract: An LZ77 codec bounds every match by one sliding window, trading cheap offsets for short matches against reach for long ones. Match-length-dependent windows refine this trade-off: each match length has its own window, and the decoder infers the offset range from the decoded length. We present two such codecs: WLZ4, a byte-aligned LZ4-class format with one-byte and flagged offsets, and WZIP, an entropy-coded Zstandard-class format. Each block begins with its decoded length, from which WZIP derives its widest window and a decoder sizes its output. LZ4 blocks may expand incompressible input by 0.4%; WLZ4 adds at most 15 bytes, WZIP 2. We describe the formats, threaded match finders, decoders and parser. On Silesia, WLZ4 reaches a ratio up to 16% above LZ4HC's, decoding more slowly, and WZIP exceeds Zstandard 22's ratio while its trusted decoder runs at 91% of Zstandard's speed (87% checked; on enwik9, about as fast).
comments: 10 pages, 5 tables, 2 figures. Submitted to the 2027 Data Compression Conference (DCC). Source code: https://github.com/icodywu/WZIP (release v1.0.0). Distinct from arXiv:2610.06530, which analyzes length-dependent window schedules in theory; this paper presents two complete codecs, their formats, parser and decoders, and measurements against LZ4, Zstandard, Brotli and xz

title: Zeros and Their Distribution for Leonardo Polynomials
abstract: We investigate the zeros of Leonardo polynomials and their distribution in the complex plane. We show that the structure of the zeros differs between even and odd degrees. For even degrees, all zeros are simple and purely imaginary, with imaginary parts lying in \((-2,2)\). For odd degrees, there is exactly one positive real zero, whereas no negative real or purely imaginary zeros occur. We obtain two-sided bounds for the unique positive real zero, prove that it decreases strictly to zero as the degree increases through odd values, and determine its asymptotic behavior. Using the relation between Leonardo and Fibonacci polynomials together with a complex trigonometric parametrization, we transform the zero equation into a family of fixed-point problems. Suitable invariant disks are constructed, and the corresponding mappings are shown to be contractions. This yields a constructive description of the complete zero set, proves the simplicity of all zeros, and provides geometrically convergent iterations for their numerical approximation. The method also provides explicit control over the approximation error. Finally, we establish a degree-dependent vertical strip containing all zeros and show that its width tends to zero as the degree increases. Consequently, the zeros become uniformly concentrated near the imaginary axis. Numerical examples illustrate the convergence of the proposed method, the associated error estimates, and the resulting zero distributions.

title: Prelocality No-Go Theorems and Exactly Solvable Relational History Hamiltonians
abstract: Exact permutation covariance does not itself supply a sparse metric geometry. For permutation-covariant, full-support $k$-body interaction orbits, the incident interaction norm scales as $\binom{N-1}{k-1}|J_N|\|h\|$; such orbits cannot have uniformly finite range in metrics of diverging diameter. A permutation-invariant Hamiltonian diagonal in the graph basis has ground-state multiplicity at least $N!/|\mathrm{Aut}(G)|$ whenever $G$ is a ground graph. We give a quantitative version for approximately symmetric energies, together with fixed-radius connectivity and unitary-isometry obstructions. The trace-distance asymmetry of an arbitrary state also bounds its probability of selecting one labeled graph. We then construct two exactly solvable finite relational history Hamiltonians. A cyclic clock with a reversible incidence update has a unique ground state; gauge reduction yields a cycle Laplacian with a rank-one pin and the exact gap $\Delta_{N,L}=E_* (1-\cos\theta_L)$, where $\tan(L\theta_L/2)=1/\sin\theta_L$ and $0<\theta_L<\pi/L$. In particular, $\Delta_{N,L}/E_*=\pi^2/(2L^2)-2\pi^2/L^3+O(L^{-4})$, independently of the number of vertices. In an alternative order-free architecture, one clock qubit per unordered pair gives commuting four-local terms, $2^N$ ground states and a size-independent gap $E_*(1-1/\sqrt2)$. A fixed-weight control penalty selects $\binom Nq$ ground states without reducing the gap. These exact finite results expose clock and locality resource tradeoffs; they do not establish an emergent geometric phase.
comments: 10 pages, 1 figure. Ancillary finite-matrix verification scripts included

title: Analytic Criteria for Detecting Bernstein-Sato Roots
abstract: We study roots of Bernstein-Sato polynomials of ideals. Our first main result gives a general partial differential equation criterion for detecting roots of the Bernstein-Sato polynomial of an ideal. For homogeneous case, we recast this criterion as an analytic condition, connecting the algebraic problem of locating roots with analytic properties of the defining data. As an application, we give a series of roots for the general determinantal ideal prove the strong monodromy conjecture for them. Keywords. Bernstein-Sato polynomial, determinantal variety, monodromy conjecture.

title: A proof of the Auluck-Chowla-Gupta Conjecture
abstract: Let p(n,k) denote the number of partitions of n into exactly k parts. In 1942 Auluck, Chowla and Gupta conjectured that for every n the sequence p(n,1), p(n,2), ..., p(n,n) is unimodal. Szekeres proved this for all sufficiently large n, but with a threshold that was never made explicit. We prove the conjecture for every n >= 1. For n >= 10^5 we give an analytic argument with fully explicit constants: an exact probabilistic representation of the ratio p(n,k+1)/p(n,k), a second-order saddle-point main term with a rigorous uniform error bound in the transition window, and separate elementary or saddle-point estimates in the two tails. Every numerical constant in this argument is certified in ball arithmetic. For n <= 2*10^5 the conjecture is verified exhaustively by two independent programs, one of them using exact integer arithmetic only. Since log-concavity of k -> p(n,k) fails for every n >= 4, the argument works with first differences and never uses log-concavity.

title: Satisfiability and freezing in random integer programs
abstract: We study a model of a random centrally symmetric polytope and ask about the existence of points in the polytope with non-zero, integer coordinates. Our main results are the location of a sharp threshold for the existence of these integer points, a characterization of the typical empirical distribution of their coordinates, and showing that near the feasibility threshold these integer points are almost always totally isolated --- at linear Hamming distance to the nearest other integer point in the polytope. The behavior of these random integer programs is related to that of the symmetric binary perceptron (the case when coordinates of points are $\pm 1$-valued). The lack of symmetry in the set of potential solutions leads to new questions and phenomena, such as the distribution of the coordinate sizes in typical solutions, and requires the development of new information-theoretic techniques to deal with higher-dimensional optimization problems arising in the method of moments.
comments: Minimal AI usage. Comments welcome. 49 pages

title: Linear stability and divisibility gaps for Gaussian maxima
abstract: We study Gaussian maxima arising from isotropic families of unit vectors and show that their excess expected maximum is controlled by the distance from an orthonormal basis. We apply this stability result to correlation matrices with equal nonzero eigenvalues, obtaining an exact minimum when the matrix size is divisible by the rank and a quantitative gap otherwise. In dimension two, we determine the leading asymptotic term and describe the structure of near-optimal configurations. We also obtain covariance-block recovery results and a finite-dimensional lower bound for the higher-rank limiting problem.

title: Philip L. Roe, the British Scientist. The Cranfield Years and Beyond
abstract: Philip L. Roe, the renowned British scientist, passed away on April 26, 2026, at the age of 87, while Professor Emeritus at the University of Michigan. My association with Phil Roe began in 1984, when he joined the Cranfield Institute of Technology, UK, as Professor of Computational Fluid Dynamics, while I was a postdoctoral research fellow at the same institution. For more than four decades, his incisive ideas, physical principles and distinctive approach to research on numerical methods for solving hyperbolic partial differential equations have had a lasting influence on my own approach to research in the field. Here I recount some personal memories and anecdotes emerging from the rewarding experience of interacting with Phil during the Cranfield years and beyond. I also review, quite succinctly in places, some of the main research topics that he pursued throughout much of his academic career. These notes are intended as a modest homage to Roe's impact on the subject, as well as to his influence on the careers of generations of scientists in both academia and industry.

title: Symmetric, rational and infinitely many $(23_4)$ configurations, and the end of the existence problem for geometric $(n_4)$ configurations
abstract: A geometric $(n_4)$ configuration is a set of $n$ points and $n$ lines in the real projective plane such that every point lies on exactly four of the lines and every line contains exactly four of the points. The question of which $n$ admit such a configuration was posed by Gr\"unbaum in 2000, and successive work of Bokowski, Gr\"unbaum, Schewe, Pilaud and Cuntz settled every case but $n=23$. We settle this last case by bounding the symmetry of such configurations and classifying the most symmetric ones exactly. We prove that for every prime $n\equiv3\pmod4$ the group of projective symmetries of a geometric $(n_4)$ configuration has order at most four, explaining why symmetric constructions failed at $n=23$, and the same argument bounds the symmetry of $(n_5)$ configurations for primes $n\not\equiv1\pmod5$. Reducing the Klein four-group case to 4021 bilinear polynomial systems and solving all of them exactly with Gr\"obner bases, we show that exactly two $(23_4)$ configurations reach this bound up to projective equivalence and that there are no others even over $\mathbb{C}$. Both are self-polar; the first has integer coordinates and the second is defined over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{17})$ but not over $\mathbb{Q}$. Consequently geometric $(n_4)$ configurations exist if and only if $n\ge18$ and $n\ne19$. The same classification recovers Cuntz's $(22_4)$ and $(26_4)$ configurations and finds three new combinatorial types at $n=22$ and $94$ at $n=26$. Among self-polar $(23_4)$ configurations with a single involution we find $50$ more, defined over number fields of degree at most $7$. Four of them deform in one-parameter families, and computing three of these exactly, one birational to the modular curve $X_1(11)$, we prove that there are infinitely many geometric $(23_4)$ configurations, among them infinitely many with rational coordinates that are self-polar and have no projective symmetry.

title: Digraph Laplacian spectra: Counterexamples to the 2005 polygon conjecture
abstract: Let $\Lambda_n$ be the set of all eigenvalues of standardized Laplacian matrices of order $n$. In 2005, a polygon $S_n\subseteq\Lambda_n$ was constructed, and it was conjectured that $\Lambda_n=S_n$. We observe that $S_n$ is a zonotope, which gives a short proof of $S_n\subseteq\Lambda_n$, and we describe $\Lambda_n$ as a union, over all vectors $v$, of intersections of zonotopes $Z_i(v)$ built from the ratios $v_j/v_i$. For a vector whose components are the $n$ distinct $n$th roots of unity, every $Z_i(v)$ equals $S_n$. We then show that the conjecture is false for $n=7$: the directed $6$-cycle with one vertex duplicated has an eigenvalue lying $2.1\cdot10^{-4}$ beyond one edge of $S_7$. For the analogous digraph of order $n$, the corresponding eigenvalue lies at signed distance $\delta_n\sim\frac{\pi^2}{2n^4}$ beyond the supporting line of the analogous edge of $S_n$, so the construction yields counterexamples for all sufficiently large $n$; numerically, it does so for every $7\le n\le300$. We also prove that $S_m\subseteq S_n$ whenever $m\mid n$, with $S_m\setminus\{0,1\}$ lying in the interior of $S_n$ for $n\ge3m$.

title: The weight enumerators of irreducible cyclic codes of length $2^\ell$
abstract: Using the spectral relation between irreducible cyclic codes (ICC) and generalized Paley (GP) graphs recently found by the authors, we study the weight distribution of irreducible cyclic codes of length $2^\ell$, $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$. These codes were previously studied by Sharma, Bakshi and Raka, who divided them into two families (each having two cases). First we characterize the GP-graphs spectrally related to these families of ICCs: they are complete, semiprimitive, Hamming, or Cartesian products of semiprimitive GP-graphs. We then compute the spectrum of these graphs and hence, by the mentioned spectral relation we finally obtain neat explicit expressions for the weight enumerators of all the irreducible cyclic codes of length $2^\ell$ with $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$.

title: Comment on "Landau Levels and Riemann Zeros"
abstract: Sierra and Townsend (ST) [1] showed that the ``absorption spectrum'' model of Connes [2] arises as the lowest-Landau-level (LLL) limit of a charged particle in crossed electric and magnetic fields, and suggested that the higher Landau levels supply the fluctuation part of the Riemann-zero counting function $N(E)$. Within the approximation used by ST we construct the eigenfunctions of an arbitrary Landau level $n$ and derive their asymptotics at the two box boundaries that ST identify. The boundary condition is the same as for $n=0$ up to an $E$-independent phase $(-\ii)^n$, so no $\ln E$ term arises for any fixed $n$. We also note that the $\ln E$ term in the semiclassical Eq.~(29) of ST is the first-order shift of the smooth LLL counting function, $E\to E+\gamma z^2$.
comments: 3 pages, no figure, Comment on arXiv:0805.4079 (math-ph)

title: New mixed cages, bounds and computational results
abstract: An $(r,z,g)$-mixed cage is a mixed graph that is $r$-regular in edges, $z$-regular in arcs, of girth $g$ and of minimum order $n=n(r,z,g)$. We give a general lower bound for $n(r,z,g)$. In the case $g=3$, we determine the exact value $n(r,z,3)=r+2z+1$. For $g=4$ we give two improved lower bounds and we determine the exact value $n(r,z,4)=2r+4z$ for $r\geq 2z-2$. We also present computational results, obtaining mixed cages and computational lower bounds by means of exhaustive backtracking searches with symmetry reductions. Moreover, we give an upper bound for $n(1,z,g)$ that matches all our computed values.

title: Free products, principal sums, bipartition complete matroids and the linking operation $(\mathcal{M}_{SP} \vee \mathcal{M}_{PQ}) \times (S \uplus Q)$
abstract: In this paper we examine the special class of bipartition complete matroids, which includes free products and principal sums of matroids (Crapo and Schmitt, 2005; Bonin and Kung, 2015). A matroid $\mathcal{M}_{SQ}$ on $S \uplus Q$ is said to be $\{S,Q\}$--complete iff whenever $b^1_S \uplus b^1_Q, \, b^1_S \uplus b^2_Q,$ and $b^2_S \uplus b^1_Q$ are bases of $\mathcal{M}_{SQ},$ we also have $b^2_S \uplus b^2_Q$ as a base of $\mathcal{M}_{SQ}.$ We use the linking operation $\mathcal{M}_{SP} \leftrightarrow_{\mathcal{M}} \mathcal{M}_{PQ} :\equiv (\mathcal{M}_{SP} \vee \mathcal{M}_{PQ}) \times (S \uplus Q)$ (Theja and Narayanan, 2014) for this study. We construct the $\{S, Q\}$--augmentation of an arbitrary matroid and show that this augmentation is again a matroid, that the dual of the augmentation is the augmentation of the dual matroid and that the $\{S, Q\}$--augmentation of an $\{S, Q\}$--complete matroid leaves it unchanged. We also show that bipartition completeness is stable under minors in the appropriate bipartitioned sense. Finally, we show that free products and principal sums of matroids $\mathcal{M}_{S},\mathcal{M}_{Q}$ are $\{S, Q\}$--complete and give explicit minimal decompositions for them.

title: Not too many miles from $\ell_\infty$ to $L_\infty$
abstract: For either real or complex scalars, we improve the known upper bound for the Banach--Mazur distance between $L_\infty[0,1]$ and $\ell_\infty$, proving $d_{\operatorname{BM}}(L_\infty[0,1],\ell_\infty)\leqslant (2+\sqrt5)^2=9+4\sqrt5=17.944\ldots$. The additional input is a stabilised kernel estimate: the copy of $\ell_\infty$ in $L_\infty$ is chosen so that its kernel is an $\ell_\infty$-sum of singular two-point hyperplanes, and Cohen's bound-two construction is then applied coordinatewise. The quantitative part of the proof is an asymmetric Pe\l czy\'nski-type factorisation, with the elementary optimisation included below.
comments: 6 pp, accepted for publication in Journal of Mathematical Sciences (Japan)

title: Quantum Annealing for Resource Allocation in Next-Generation Wireless Communication Networks: A QUBO Modeling Guide
abstract: Quantum annealing (QA) offers a physics-inspired approach for such subproblems by mapping them onto an Ising Hamiltonian, which is algebraically equivalent to a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) model executable on quantum annealers or hybrid solvers. However, their practical employment in wireless systems critically depends on the specific problem formulation, on the particular variable encoding, constraint handling, solver selection, hardware embedding, and fair benchmarking. This paper develops wireless-oriented QUBO modeling guidelines for QA-assisted resource allocation. We first present a beginner-friendly toy example in which a terrestrial-aerial resource-allocation problem with a fractional signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) maximization objective is reformulated into a two-bit QUBO via Boolean interpolation, converted into an Ising representation, and decoded back into a wireless scheduling decision. The same scheduling is applicable to UAV, aircraft, satellite, and terrestrial links in SAGIN systems. We then review the QA foundations and solver ecosystems, including binary quadratic, discrete quadratic, constrained quadratic, and hybrid models from the perspective of NG wireless optimization. Furthermore, we discuss both binary and discrete encoding, penalty-based constraint conversion, embedding overhead, solution decoding, and feasibility verification. A QUBO Compatibility Index is introduced as a lightweight diagnostic metric for assessing the associated QUBO formulation readiness, rather than a predictor of runtime or solution quality. Finally, a case study on max-min uplink power control in cell-free massive MIMO illustrates how a fairness-oriented wireless problem can be discretized, constrained, converted into the concept of a QUBO, and evaluated against classical baselines. A host of key challenges and future directions are also discussed.
comments: 16 pages, 5 figures, and 7 tables. Accepted by OJ-COMS

title: A lower bound for additive complements to the primes
abstract: We study the size of sets $\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ for which $\mathbb{P}+\mathcal{B}$ contains every sufficiently large integer. We obtain $B(X)\gg\log X\log\log X$, where $B(X)=\#(\mathcal{B}\cap[0,X])$ and the implied constant is absolute. This gives a quantitative form of Conjecture 2 of Ruzsa and excludes additive complements of size $O(\log X)$, as asked in one part of Erd\H{o}s Problem 32. More generally, we construct a block of $\lfloor c\log X\log\log X/(B(X)+1)\rfloor$ consecutive integers outside $\mathbb{P}+\mathcal{B}$ in $[X/2,X]$, whenever this number is positive.

title: A Stochastic Analysis Perspective on Diffusion Models
abstract: Generative modelling involves two complementary tasks: learning a probabilistic approximation of an unknown data distribution from observations, and designing a tractable mechanism for sampling from this approximation. We present a stochastic-analysis perspective on score-based generative models, connecting ideas from classical sampling theory, score estimation, and diffusion time reversal. We first explain how score functions link Langevin sampling with score matching, and how Gaussian smoothing leads to denoising score matching and multiscale sampling methods. We then emphasize the distinction between dynamics preserving a fixed distribution and dynamics transporting a prescribed family of marginals. This motivates a path-space treatment of diffusion time reversal. Finally, we connect the ideal reverse diffusion with practical generative algorithms.

title: Null-controllable data for cascade heat equations: almost sharp spectral spaces and modal critical times
abstract: We study one-dimensional cascades of heat equations controlled through their last component. For a fixed time $T>0$, we consider the Hilbert space $\mathcal{C}_T$ of all initial data that can be steered exactly to zero at time $T$, endowed with the norm of the minimal $L^2$ control. This space can be strongly anisotropic: in explicit examples, it is incomparable with every isotropic spectral Sobolev or sub-Gaussian Gevrey scale associated with an adapted basis. For two equations, under the block Fattorini--Hautus condition, we give an almost sharp spectral description of $\mathcal{C}_T$. More precisely, in an adapted Riesz basis of generalized eigenvectors we define an explicit increasing scale $(\mathcal{V}_\tau)_{\tau\in\R}$ of Hilbert spaces such that $\mathcal{V}_{T-\varepsilon}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{C}_T\hookrightarrow\mathcal{V}_T$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. The weights of $\mathcal{V}_T$ combine heat dissipation with the loss of observation inside each double generalized eigenspace. When the coupling and control regions are disjoint, this recovers the known minimal null-control time $T^\star$ and identifies it as a transition time for controllable data: for $TT^\star$, the natural state space is properly contained in $\mathcal{C}_T$. We extend the analysis to arbitrary finite upper triangular heat cascades. The observation losses of the different directions in each spectral block may have distinct exponential orders, leading to a hierarchy of critical times rather than a single threshold. This hierarchy describes successive gains of null controllability on adapted modal subspaces and accounts for the interactions and cancellations between different coupling paths.

title: Reconstruction and Symmetry of Two-Token Graphs
abstract: We present a proof of the two-token graph reconstruction conjecture. Every finite simple graph $G,H$ of order at least three, $F_2(G) \cong F_2(H)$ if and only if $G \cong H$. We also classify the automorphism groups of two-token graphs whose connected roots have order at least five. Combining these results, we show that, for connected graphs $G,H$ of order at least five, every isomorphism $\phi:F_2(G)\to F_2(H)$ admits a factorization $\phi=\eta\circ\sigma^{(2)}$, where $\sigma^{(2)}$ is induced by a graph isomorphism $\sigma:G\to H$, and $\eta\in \operatorname{Aut}(F_2(H))$ is a product of twin-cut switches or Cartesian exchanges.

title: Geometry of semi-infinite geodesics in the Airy line ensemble
abstract: We study the geometry of semi-infinite geodesics in the Airy line ensemble. We establish sharp estimates for disjointness probabilities involving geodesics with nearby directions and endpoints in the top line of the Airy line ensemble. Moreover, we obtain a power law upper bound on the coalescence depth of two semi-infinite geodesics with same asymptotic direction and establish exponential concentration estimates for geodesic jump times more generally. We also establish pathwise H\"{o}lder $1/2^-$-continuity of Busemann profiles associated to semi-infinite geodesics with common asymptotic directions (in terms of the asymptotic direction). We characterize exceptional behaviour of semi-infinite geodesics through their Busemann profiles and establish geometric properties of the associated sets of non-coalescence and non-uniqueness. Finally, we determine the Hausdorff dimensions of collections of semi-infinite geodesics: collections with a fixed top-line endpoint and arbitrary positive asymptotic direction almost surely have Hausdorff dimension $1$, while collections with a fixed positive direction and arbitrary endpoint almost surely have Hausdorff dimension $3/2$.

title: Uniformly Bounded Orthonormal Bases of Homogeneous Polynomials on the Complex Sphere
abstract: We resolve the long-standing problem of Rudin concerning uniformly bounded orthonormal bases of homogeneous polynomials on complex unit spheres. Specifically, we show that for every $K \geq 2$ and $N \geq 0$ there exists a basis of degree $N$ homogeneous polynomials in $\mathbb{C}^K$ that is orthonormal with respect to the surface measure of the unit sphere of $\mathbb{C}^K$ and uniformly bounded by a constant depending only on $K$ on the unit ball of $\mathbb{C}^K$. Bourgain resolved the case $K = 2$ in 1985 and the case $K = 3$ in 2016. No cases $K \geq 4$ were previously known.

title: Intrinsic Contraction Theory and Stabilization of Probability Measures on the Wasserstein Space
abstract: Deterministic flows can contract Wasserstein distances between probability laws without being contractive in point-state space. We develop a differential contraction theory for pushforward flows on forward-invariant subsets of the 2-Wasserstein space that quotients out the gauge freedom of the continuity equation. Weighted Helmholtz-Hodge decomposition and the Wasserstein contingent cone define the weighted horizontal tangent cone (whtc). Requiring the contraction quadratic form to be nonpositive only on the whtc yields the Intrinsic Wasserstein Contraction Condition (IWCC), which generalizes the classical contraction LMI and recovers it on Dirac measures. An almost-everywhere Euler approximation based on the superposition principle and Banach-valued Lebesgue differentiation theorem proves that IWCC is sufficient for intrinsic Wasserstein contraction. Law contraction without point-state contraction is illustrated by a rotationally symmetric shear example. Finally, a new comparison lemma yields an incremental Wasserstein ISS theorem; for Brockett's integrator, we prove exponential stabilization of a class of axisymmetric laws to the uniform law on a circle via a smooth feedback.
comments: 17 pages. Submitted to the IEEE in August 2026 for possible publication

title: Categorifying Quantum Spin Systems
abstract: We develop a homotopical framework for understanding the space of quantum spin systems based on topological $n$-nets, which assign associative unital algebras to local regions in an $n$-dimensional space in a manner that captures the locality structure of the underlying lattice theories. The net-theoretic perspective admits a natural categorification, in which the category of topological $n$-nets carries the structure of a higher Morita category. Moreover, the nets of greatest physical interest form a Karoubi-complete subcategory that shares many of the characteristic structural features of the category of finite TQFTs. Our main result identifies the group of locality-preserving symmetries of (3+1)-dimensional quantum spin systems (i.e. quantum cellular automata modulo stabilization, finite-depth quantum circuits, and translations) with the full Witt group of nondegenerate braided fusion categories, thereby answering a question posed by Haah.

title: Exact SU($N$) symmetry resolution of bosonic Hubbard models: general boson-fermion mappings and flat-band singlet-cluster states
abstract: We show how to perform exact diagonalization of SU($N$)-symmetric Bose-Hubbard models separately in each irreducible representation of SU($N$), by exploiting the Howe duality between U($L$) and U($N$). Three structural consequences follow for any lattice and any Hamiltonian built from the U($L$) generators: (i) the spectrum in a given orbital sector is independent of $N$ and of the particle statistics, (ii) the canonical partition functions for bosons and fermions obey the exact identity $Z_{\mathrm{b}}(-N)=(-1)^{N_\mathrm{b}}Z_{\mathrm{f}}(N)$, (iii) with unfrustrated hopping the groundstate is always a color ferromagnet, so that the color-resolved method we introduce is useful to study excited sectors, frustrated lattices and finite temperatures. As applications, we first derive the finite-temperature phase diagram of attractive SU($N$) bosons on few-site rings at large $N$ for arbitrary filling. We then show the emergence of singlet-cluster states from frustrated hopping, the counterpart of fermionic ferromagnetism, with the example of the sawtooth and kagome lattice.

title: Gauss-Manin Connection in Disguise: Holomorphic Anomaly Equations and Higher Genus Real Gromov-Witten Invariants
abstract: We construct an algebraic framework for the extended holomorphic anomaly equations following ideas of Alim, Movasati, Scheidegger and Yau. We choose the quintic threefold as our main model and use this framework to solve the equations and fix the ambiguity up to genus 5. We obtain predictions for real Gromov-Witten invariants, or, equivalently, real Gopakumar-Vafa invariants that are integers and agree with their complex counterparts modulo 2. In the end, we discuss how the framework could be extended and compute the same predictions for the bicubic up to genus 9.

title: Lifting an $[n,k,d]$ Binary Linear Code to an $[[n,k,d]]$ Quantum Stabilizer Code
abstract: The codeword stabilized (CWS) framework provides a systematic method for constructing quantum error correcting codes from a simple undirected graph and a classical code. When the underlying classical code is linear, the resulting quantum code is a stabilizer code. In this work, we investigate the conditions under which an arbitrary $[n,k,d]$ classical binary linear code can be lifted to an $[[n,k,d]]$ quantum stabilizer code using the CWS framework. We analyze the random CWS code constructed from a given $[n,k,d]$ binary linear code $\mathcal{C}$ and an Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi random graph $\mathrm{G}(n, \frac12)$. We establish a lower bound on the probability that the resulting quantum code preserves the minimum distance $d$ of the classical code. This probabilistic analysis yields a Gilbert-Varshamov-type condition on the $n,k,d$ parameters of the classical code that guarantees the existence of a graph resulting in a quantum code with the same $n,k,d$ parameters.

title: Global Convergence and Reliable Stopping in a Safeguarded Modified Anderson--Bj\"orck Method
abstract: The modified Anderson-Bjorck (modAB) method was first proposed in 2023 by Ganchovski and Traykov for solving nonlinear equations in structural mechanics. It was improved further in 2026 by introducing better switching criteria with account to function symmetry, and bisection fallback based on measuring the bracket reduction rate. Although the algorithm demonstrated superior performance across a great variety of functions, it lacked formal mathematical analysis and proof of convergence. In addition, some discrepancies were noted by L. Tomov in the latest version that need to be addressed: premature application of the Anderson-Bjorck (AB) correction on the first AB step, caused by retaining the endpoint-update record from the preceding bisection step, and using the corrected endpoint ordinates in symmetry factor calculation instead of the true residuals. The purpose of the present paper is to provide rigorous mathematical proof of global convergence in exact arithmetic, remove the above discrepancies, and provide floating-point safeguards for interpolation, switching and stopping, with explicit treatment of infinite and NaN values, underflow, overflow and round-off errors. These safeguards do not certify the accuracy of the supplied function values. Additional performance improvement was introduced by allowing for early bisection fallback when AB fails to make progress on reducing either the bracket width or the residual, while retaining a finite bound on consecutive exceptions to the prescribed width condition.

title: A Functorial Classification of Toric Stacks
abstract: Toric stacks enrich the study of toric varieties by accounting for quotients of actions of diagonalizable groups. In practice, toric stacks are constructed and understood via "stacky fans" generalizing the fans appearing in toric geometry. Previous attempts to make this construction into an equivalence of categories have either run into crucial errors or have been restricted to special cases (e.g. only considering separated Deligne-Mumford stacks). In this paper, we solve this problem by introducing a new 2-category $\mathsf{StkFan}$ of stacky fans and constructing an equivalence of 2-categories between $\mathsf{StkFan}$ and a 2-category $\mathsf{TStk}$ of toric stacks. Along the way, we develop a theory of "toric categories" which categorifies the classical theory of toric monoids. We also explain how working with toric categories provides a simple axiomatic framework for Gale duality.

title: Strong-type endpoint obstructions for bilinear spherical maximal operators
abstract: For the bilinear spherical averages in dimension $d\geq2$, we show that the lacunary maximal operator is not bounded from $L^1(\mathbb R^d)\times L^q(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^r(\mathbb R^d)$ whenever $1\leq q\leq\infty$ and $1/r=1+1/q$. The obstruction is realized by fixed nonnegative inputs; a second construction proves quantitative failure on smooth compactly supported functions and finitely many dyadic scales. The same conclusions hold for the full maximal operator. We give a sharp Lorentz-index criterion in the range $q>d/(d-1)$ and extend the negative result to all multilinear spherical maximal operators with an $L^1$ input. We indicate the precise strong-type boundary statements to which these conclusions apply, without drawing conclusions about separate weak-type or interior estimates.

title: The $R_\infty$-nilpotency degree of some lollipop GBS groups
abstract: We say that a group $G$ has the $R_{\infty}$ property if the number $R(\varphi)$ of twisted conjugacy classes is infinite for any automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$. The $R_{\infty}$-nilpotency degree is the least integer $c$ such that $G/\gamma_{c+1}(G)$ has property $R_{\infty}$; in case this integer does not exist, we say that $G$ has infinite $R_\infty$-nilpotency degree. In this paper, we determine the $R_{\infty}$-nilpotency degree of some lollipop GBS groups by using different approaches, such as Sylow subgroups, normal forms and presentation of nilpotent quotients, and diagrams of exact sequences. We also compute the $R_\infty$-nilpotency degree of all 2-generated lollipop GBS groups and of all GBS groups whose associated graph is a tree.

title: Sequential Change Point Detection for PSK Modulation Switching
abstract: Transmitters in adaptive communication systems may switch their modulation scheme at an unknown time, and a receiver must detect this switch quickly without raising frequent false alarms. Existing modulation classification methods label a finite block of received data and do not provide stopping rules with controlled false-alarm and delay performance. We study the sequential detection of a switch from one phase shift keying (PSK) scheme to another over an additive white Gaussian noise channel. We build cumulative-sum (CUSUM) and moving-sum (MOSUM) detectors from the log-likelihood ratio and its low-SNR approximation. For a switch from quadrature PSK to binary PSK, we derive the moment-generating function and probability density function of the approximate statistic. We use them to relate the CUSUM threshold to the average run length to false alarm and the worst-case detection delay. For a switch between any two PSK orders, we approximate the vector of overlapping MOSUM statistics as multivariate Gaussian and obtain bounds on both measures. Monte Carlo simulations show that our derived expressions for ARL2FA and WADD closely match the empirical results across thresholds, validating the accuracy of the proposed analytical approximations and theoretical bounds.
comments: 12 Pages, 5 Figures, Online change-point detection for modulation transitions using CUSUM and MOSUM detectors

title: The Path Partition Conjecture and 3-(quasi-)Transitive Digraphs
abstract: A digraph $D = (V,E)$ is 3-transitive (respectively, 3-quasi-transitive) if whenever $(u,v,w,z)$ is a directed path of length 3, $(u,z) \in E$ (respectively, $(u,z) \in E$ or $(z,u) \in E$). These digraphs extend the concepts of transitive and quasi-transitive digraphs, respectively. For 3-transitive and 3-quasi-transitive digraphs, only the strong case has been characterized. In this paper, we introduce the notion of semi-acyclic digraphs and use it to describe completely the structure of 3-transitive and 3-quasi-transitive digraphs. As an application of this type of structure description, we prove that the path partition conjecture holds for the class of extended semi-acyclic digraphs, which generalizes two previously known results on the conjecture.

title: Tight surgeries on torus knots
abstract: We give a complete classification of tight contact structures on manifolds obtained from any surgery along any torus knot, which provides the first such classification on an infinite family of knots. The main tools are the classification of non-loose torus knots, bordered contact invariants via their immersed curve interpretations, and non-thickenable tori in knot complements.
