abstract: Let $F$ be a $p$-adic field, let $k,c\ge1$, and let $\rho$ be a $(k,c)$ representation of $\mathrm{GL}_{kc}(F)$: a complex representation of finite length whose wave front set has $(k^c)$ as its unique maximal orbit, and which admits a $(k,c)$ functional that is unique up to scaling. We prove that the functions in the $(k,c)$ model of $\rho$ are of moderate growth, by relating this model to the Zelevinsky model of $\rho$, and obtain as a consequence a bound for the restriction of these functions to the standard Levi subgroup associated with the composition $(c^k)$ of $kc$. As applications, we study convergence problems of several integrals involving $(k,c)$ models: integrals from the generalized doubling method, and a new family of integrals which extends the Rankin--Selberg integrals for Speh representations of Lapid and Mao.

title: Generic nondegeneracy of constant mean curvature radial graphs
abstract: Given a smooth domain $D\subset\mathbb S^{N-1}$, $N\geq 3$, and a positive constant $H$, we study radial graphs over $D$ with constant mean curvature $H$ which meet orthogonally the boundary of the cone spanned by $D$. The corresponding problem is given by a quasilinear elliptic equation on $D$ with homogeneous Neumann boundary condition. We investigate the structure of the solution set under smooth perturbations of the domain which are parametrized by an open set of $C^{3,\alpha}$-diffeomorphisms of the sphere. After pulling the equation back to a fixed reference domain, we apply a classical transversality theorem and prove that, in the class of domains for which $N-1$ does not belong to the Neumann spectrum of the Laplace-Beltrami operator, there is a residual set for which every solution is nondegenerate. A consequence of our result is that, for every such domain and every $R>0$, the set of solutions whose $C^{2,\alpha}$-norm is bounded by $R$ is finite.

title: Clifford Invariants and Three-Copy Quantum Tests
abstract: We give an explicit treatment of the third tensor power of the Clifford representation on $n$ qutrits, for $n\geq2$. This representation has five pairwise inequivalent irreducible constituents, with multiplicities $1,1,1,1,2$. The decomposition reduces the Clifford twirl of a tensor cube to four real parameters. Two of them are spectral moments of the input. The other two are cubic invariants expressed as sums of cubes of the Weyl characteristic function and the discrete Wigner function. On trace-one Hermitian matrices, the invariant polynomials of degree at most three are spanned by the constant function and four algebraically independent functions. These functions do not separate Clifford orbits. For pure inputs a single parameter suffices. We recover its range and the characterization of its maximum by stabilizer states. We bound the stabilizer fidelity, determine full separability across the three copies in the symmetric family, and recover the criterion for a complex projective $3$-design. We classify the jointly invariant quantum Boolean functions. For stabilizer testing and for testing unknown observables we give explicit bounds on copies and queries. We also give character formulas for the finite projective Clifford groups and record the complete character table for two qutrits.
comments: GAP code is available in the GitHub repository: https://github.com/luanyongzhi/qutrit-character-table

title: A note on Guo's perturbation result for symmetric nonnegative matrices
abstract: In 1997 Guo Wuwen proved that if $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_n)$ is the spectrum of a nonnegative matrix with Perron eigenvalue $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$ real, then $(\lambda_1+t,\lambda_2\pm t,\lambda_3,\dots,\lambda_n)$ is the spectrum of a nonnegative matrix for every $t\ge 0$. Whether the same holds for symmetric nonnegative matrices has remained an open question. We give an affirmative answer, in a slightly stronger form: if $A$ is a symmetric nonnegative matrix with eigenvalues $\lambda_1\ge\dots\ge\lambda_n$ and $d_1\ge|d_2|+\dots+|d_n|$, then there is a symmetric matrix $B\ge A$ with eigenvalues $\lambda_1+d_1,\dots,\lambda_n+d_n$, and $B$ has the same diagonal as $A$ when $d_1+\dots+d_n=0$. This leads us to call a symmetrically realizable list Guo-extreme if none of Guo's moves can be reversed within the set of symmetrically realizable lists. Every symmetrically realizable list is a Guo-extreme list plus a vector from the cone of Guo's moves. Our second main result is a certificate, modelled on a theorem of Laffey on extreme symmetric matrices: if $A$ is irreducible and every nonnegative symmetric matrix that commutes with $A$ and vanishes wherever $A$ is positive is a multiple of the identity, then the spectrum of $A$ can be moved by a small amount in every trace-preserving direction (in every direction, if $A$ has a positive diagonal entry) and remain symmetrically realizable; in particular it is not Guo-extreme.

title: A Unified Framework for Randomized Row-Action Methods for Structured Data Fitting and Constraint Geometry
abstract: We study randomized row-action methods for problems with linear observations, convex constraints, and non-Euclidean geometry. Our starting point is a unified formulation in which the data-fitting term acts in observation space, while the feasible set and the regularizer encode structure in variable space. It covers constrained least squares, nonnegative and simplex-constrained models, regularized data fitting, and equality-constrained Bregman selection problems. The structure of these problems leads naturally to two algorithmic branches. The first uses primal Bregman-proximal row steps for soft data-fitting problems. The second uses dual Bregman--Kaczmarz steps for problems with hard equality constraints. We first derive a common one-step inequality. We then give deterministic and stochastic convergence results for the soft branch under relative smoothness. For constrained least squares, the normalized row oracle has exact first- and second-moment identities. They yield an expected ergodic bound in the inconsistent case, an $O(1/K)$ bound in the interpolating case, and linear convergence of the actual iterates under a residual error bound. For equality-constrained selectors, we prove linear convergence in expected Bregman distance under a residual-to-Bregman error bound. We recall global sufficient conditions for this bound and derive local constants for the nonnegative quadratic geometry and the entropy geometry on the simplex. Numerical experiments illustrate the noisy stepsize trade-off and the local entropy selector theory, and show that entropic row-action updates can recover interpretable factors in a simplex-structured nonnegative matrix factorization problem.

title: Sum Rate Maximization for Practical RIS-Enhanced Rate-Splitting Multiple Access Systems
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) combined with rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) provide a promising solution for improving the spectral efficiency (SE) of sixth-generation (6G) communication systems. However, most existing studies neglect the practical coupling between the RIS phase shift and amplitude, which may cause phase-shift mismatch and significant performance loss. In this paper, we investigate the multiuser sum-rate maximization problem for practical RIS-enhanced RSMA systems considering amplitude-phase coupling. To address the resulting non-convex problem, an effective variable separation algorithm is proposed. The proposed algorithm is compatible with RIS reflecting optimization under the continuous phase shift or any amplitude-phase coupling relationship and can also be directly extended to practical RIS-enhanced NOMA and OMA systems. Simulation results demonstrate performance gain of over 190\% compared with the ideal-RIS-based benchmark, while the proposed RSMA scheme significantly outperforms the corresponding NOMA and OMA schemes.

title: Decomposition of functions of bounded variation in Ahlfors-regular PI spaces
abstract: We prove that, on a non-compact Ahlfors-regular PI space, every function of bounded variation $f$ can be decomposed as a countable sum $\sum_{n=1}^\infty f_n$ of monotone functions of bounded variation $f_n$, in such a way that the total variation of $f$ is the sum of the total variations of the functions $f_n$. Our result extends a Euclidean result of Bianchini and Tonon to the metric setting.

title: Graphs on Topological Spaces
abstract: Graphs defined on groups, such as power graphs, enhanced power graphs and commuting graphs, form a hierarchy under inclusion of edge sets. We develop an analogous theory for topological spaces. To a space X we attach five graphs on the vertex set X, all invariant under homeomorphisms: the specialization, inseparability, closure-meeting, Urysohn and functional graphs. They form a diamond-shaped hierarchy whose members are null exactly when X is T_1, Hausdorff, Urysohn or functionally Hausdorff. The Urysohn graph always contains the square of the inseparability graph, with equality for Alexandrov spaces, and the hierarchy is compatible with products via the strong product of graphs. Every countable graph, together with isolated vertices, is the inseparability graph of a second countable T_1 space. For finite spaces we characterize the graphs that occur as inseparability graphs (every edge lies in the closed neighbourhood of a simplicial vertex), determine all coincidences between members of the hierarchy, and show that the specialization graph determines the weak homotopy type but not the space itself. Using Dowker duality we prove that the complexes of inseparable and of closure-meeting families are always homotopy equivalent and, under an acyclicity hypothesis, recover the weak homotopy type. We show that if the closure-meeting graph is a cograph then it is chordal, an analogue of a recent result for enhanced power graphs; the same holds for the inseparability graph of an Alexandrov space but not in general. Finally, following Cameron's work on topologies preserved by permutation groups, we show that for a topology invariant under a primitive group each graph is null or connected, and that the neighbourhood filters of the five graphs reverse the hierarchy, giving spaces whose specialization graph contains the Rado graph as a spanning subgraph.

title: Classical Communication Helps Single-Shot Quantum Compression
abstract: Free classical communication can yield an unbounded single-shot saving in quantum compression, even though it leaves the asymptotic rate of an i.i.d. source unchanged. At every fixed error in $(0,1)$, we exhibit sources whose unassisted compression cost is arbitrarily large, yet a single qubit suffices with classical communication and no preshared entanglement. We establish this separation by determining the exact optimal source fidelity for compression through an $m$-dimensional noiseless quantum channel, with and without free classical communication, while preserving correlations with an inaccessible reference. Without classical assistance, the optimal fidelity is exactly the Ky Fan norm $\|\rho\|_{(m)}$, the sum of the $m$ largest eigenvalues of the source state. With classical assistance, we obtain an explicit spectral threshold formula and a protocol attaining it. Classical communication strictly improves fidelity whenever $m$ is smaller than the source rank. The corresponding compression costs are two smoothed versions of the log-rank entropy, also called max-entropy: trace-distance smoothing under local operations and quadratic smoothing under LOCC. For i.i.d. copies of a fixed source with positive entropy variance, however, the two costs have identical first-, second-, and third-order asymptotic terms. For nonlattice spectra, we determine the constant-order advantage: classical communication saves $\log_2(e)-1$ bits per block asymptotically, and the ratio of assisted to unassisted minimum communication dimensions converges to $2/e$.
comments: 23 pages, no figures, comments are welcome

title: Global Well-Posedness and Uniform Long-Time Control for a Class of Periodic NLS-Dysthe Equations
abstract:
We study a class of periodic NLS-Dysthe (NLS-Dy) equations, also referred to as higher-order nonlinear Schr"odinger equations (HNLS), of the form $i\partial_t u+a\partial_x^2u+b|u|^2u+i\varepsilon(c\partial_x^3u+d|u|^2\partial_xu+eu^2\partial_x\overline{u})=0$ with $ x\in\mathbb T$, $a,b,c,d,e\in\mathbb R$, $abc
eq0$, and $\varepsilon>0$. For $0<\varepsilon\ll1$, equations of this type arise as higher-order modulation models for some nonlinear dispersive PDEs, including the Klein-Gordon equation and the Serre-Green-Naghdi equation modeling the evolution of nonlinear shallow water waves. We prove local well-posedness in $H^s(\mathbb T)$ for $s>3/2$ for arbitrary admissible coefficients, and establish an $H^1$ continuation criterion for $s\ge2$. In the parameter regime $e
eq0$, a lower-order conservation law provides uniform $H^1$ control and, together with the continuation criterion, yields global well-posedness for $s\ge2$. This result does not require the non-resonance condition appearing in Takaoka's periodic theory, while the condition $e
eq0$ naturally arises in the modulation setting considered here. Finally, motivated by the long-time regime relevant for modulation, we establish uniform long-time control without imposing a smallness assumption on the initial datum. Using the conservation laws of cubic NLS and their invariance under the commuting complex mKdV flow, we obtain uniform $H^s$ bounds on time intervals of order $\varepsilon^{-1}$ for integer $s\ge2$. For non-integer real $s\ge2$, the maximal $H^s$ solution exists on the same time scale, while uniform control is obtained at a lower regularity, with a loss of less than one derivative.

title: On the Julia sets of the non-autonomous iteration of exponential maps
abstract: This paper studies non-autonomous iterations of $\lambda e^z$, where at each step the parameter $\lambda$ is chosen from a bounded interval. Urba\'nski and Zdunik introduced and developed a thermodynamic formalism for random dynamics of exponential maps, extending the autonomous result established independently by Rees and Lyubich to typical parameter sequences in $[A, B]^{\mathbb{N}}$ with $1/e<A<B<\infty$. In this paper, we show that the same conclusion indeed holds for all parameters in $[A, B]^{\mathbb{N}}$, Our proof is based on carefully crafted uniform versions of pullback arguments, inspired by the original methods of Rees and Lyubich. In a related direction, Urba\'nski and Zdunik established a non-autonomous analogue of Misiurewicz's theorem for the exponential map, later refined by Lech. We further extend their work by providing a refined condition for the Julia set to be the entire complex plane.

title: The CR Nirenberg Problem, Part I: Blow-up Analysis and Compactness
abstract: We establish a priori estimates and compactness results for positive solutions of the CR Nirenberg problem under natural weighted flatness conditions. The proofs combine refined blow-up analysis, Pohozaev identities, and the complete classification of positive entire solutions to the critical CR Yamabe equation recently obtained by Li--Liu--Ma \cite{LLM2026} and Li \cite{L2026}. Existence and degree results are established in our subsequent paper \cite{QTWPartII}.

title: Combinatorics of degeneracy in vertical systems
abstract: We characterize the generic consistency of vertical systems in terms of the iterated circuits of the column matroid of the coefficient matrix. More precisely, we prove that such a system is generically consistent if and only if there exists an iterated circuit such that the dimension of the Minkowski sum of the associated Newton polytopes is equal to the rank of the coefficient matrix. We also give an equivalent characterization in terms of $G$-spanning flags of the dual matroid. With this, we derive a combinatorial formula for the codimension of the locus of parameter values for which the system has a solution, extending known results on dual defects of toric varieties. When this locus has codimension one, its defining equation yields a generalization of the sparse resultant to vertical systems, which applies also to $\mathcal{A}$-discriminants. Finally, we characterize when the solution set is contained, for generic parameter values, in a finite union of hyperplanes parallel to a coordinate hyperplane.

title: On best approximation and estimates of Bohr--Favard type on the sphere for functions with bounded Laplacian
abstract: We determine the best constants in estimates of the $L^\infty$ norm of functions on the sphere with bounded Laplacian whose first spherical harmonic components vanish. In every dimension $d\geq2$, these constants are expressed through weighted $L^1$ extremal polynomials. On $S^2$ the constant is an explicit positive series, and the best coefficient of $n^{-2}$ is $7\zeta(3)/4$. On $S^3$ the best coefficient of $n^{-2}$ is a positive integral involving the H\"ormander--Bernhardsson extremal function. In higher dimensions the rescaled extremal polynomials converge to weighted entire extremals, which give asymptotic formulas for the Bohr constants on $S^4$ and $S^6$. The most unexpected and, in our view, interesting observation is that, for every fixed $n\geq2$ on $S^2$ and $S^3$, the constants in best approximation estimates are \emph{strictly smaller} than the corresponding Bohr--Favard constants.

title: A Counterexample To The TF-cone Conjecture
abstract: The TF-cone conjecture of Asai and Iyama predicts that the TF equivalence class of an integral $g$-vector is the open cone generated by the canonical summands of all its positive multiples. We give a counterexample to this conjecture. For the tensor product of the three-arrow Kronecker algebra with the path algebra of $s\to t$, a vector $w$ has a two-dimensional TF equivalence class, whereas every positive integral multiple $mw$ is generically indecomposable. The cone generated by these canonical summands is therefore a single ray. The same example disproves the relative-interior version proposed by Haerizadeh and Yassemi.

title: $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$-cohomology on multidifferential operators space
abstract: We compute cohomology spaces of the ortosymplectic Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ on the (1,1)-dimensional real superspace with coefficients in the superspace $\frak{D}_{{\lambda},\mu}$ of $n$-ary differential operators acting on weighted densities (${\lambda}\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and $\mu\in\mathbb{R}$).

title: Ex Ante and Scenario-Conditional Value of Information in Dynamic Portfolio Choice
abstract: Portfolio decisions are often made under uncertainty about expected returns, and investors revise their beliefs as new information arrives. Although richer information generally cannot reduce optimized value ex ante, the trading strategy it induces need not improve on the strategy induced by a less informative information structure in every fixed-drift scenario. We introduce scenario-conditional expected utility and value of information to evaluate strategies selected under the investor's current belief. In a finite-horizon Gaussian portfolio choice model, we compare a fixed-belief investor, a price observer, and an attentive investor who also processes an auxiliary signal under an attention capacity constraint. Ex ante, price learning and auxiliary attention are valuable, and the total value of attention increases with capacity. Scenario-conditionally, learning creates a correction benefit by reducing the initial trading-position gap relative to the full-information strategy, but also a fluctuation cost through belief revisions, so the ex ante ranking can reverse. We derive the current-belief distribution of scenario-conditional value and the associated underperformance probability, defined as the probability of negative scenario-conditional value relative to fixed-belief choice. Over sufficiently short horizons, the scenario-conditional value of learning is negative when belief error is small relative to posterior uncertainty. For a given horizon, sufficiently high attention capacity yields a higher scenario-conditional value than any fixed finite-capacity benchmark across all drift scenarios. We also derive sharp convergence rates to full-information performance under Shannon and Tsallis technologies.

title: New bounds for off-diagonal hypergraph Ramsey numbers
abstract: We study a conjecture of Conlon, Fox, Gunby, He, Mubayi, Suk, Verstra\"ete, and Yu, which characterizes the $3$-graphs $H$ for which the off-diagonal Ramsey number $r(H,n)$ is polynomial. We prove the conjecture for $3$-graphs with at most five tight components. Additionally, we show that the full conjecture is equivalent to its specialization to linear $3$-graphs. We prove quasipolynomial upper bounds for a class of `forward-doubleable' $3$-graphs, which includes the Fano plane. Finally, we give an exponential lower bound for `non-forward-laminar' $3$-graphs and use this to completely classify the Ramsey growth of a natural family of 3-graphs called chains.

title: Multi-type $\Lambda$-Wright--Fisher processes with polynomial drift: Bernstein duality, long-term behaviour, and simulation of moments
abstract: The $(d+1)$-type $\Lambda$-Wright--Fisher process with polynomial drift is a L\'evy-type process on the $d$-dimensional unit simplex whose generator entails a particular jump and diffusive component, as well as a polynomial drift component. In this work, the process is connected to a (Bernstein) dual process, which admits an interpretation as an urn model with coloured balls. Exploiting this duality, we identify various parameter regimes: one in which the $\Lambda$-Wright--Fisher process is absorbed almost surely at a vertex of the simplex, and others in which it admits a unique nontrivial ergodic probability measure. The results include verifiable criteria for absorption versus persistence, as well as representations of absorption and stationary measures. Moreover, the duality relation is exploited to devise and implement a simulation-based approach for estimating moments of the $\Lambda$-Wright--Fisher process.

title: Averaged derivatives and reverse inequalities in quasiregular Bergman spaces
abstract: We study weighted Bergman spaces of quasiregular mappings on the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$, with weight $(1-|x|)^\alpha$, $\alpha>-1$. For every fixed distortion bound $K\ge1$ and every $p>0$, we characterize Bergman integrability by averaged derivatives. We also give geometric conditions under which integration over a subset, or against another measure, controls the full Bergman integral. When $K$ is sufficiently large, the dominating sets are precisely the relatively dense sets. For comparison, we determine the dominating sets for the M\"obius class $K=1$ in dimensions $n\ge3$. At the critical exponent $p=n+\alpha$, its domination criterion differs from that for every fixed $K>1$. Our results extend aspects of the Bergman theory developed by Nolder~\cite{Nolder90} and by Oleinik and Vuorinen~\cite{OV}, and complement the recent work of Adamowicz and Gonz\'alez~\cite{AG21,AG25} and Adamowicz and Caama\~no~\cite{AC} on quasiregular Hardy spaces.
comments: 30 pages; submitted to a journal on September 21

title: Rota-Baxter operators and factorization of Lie affgebras
abstract: We introduce Rota-Baxter operators on Lie affgebras by an identity independent of the choice of origin and prove that they induce descendant Lie affgebra structures. We establish a bijection between ordered affine Lie factorizations and idempotent operators split at a chosen idempotent fixed point. A cokernel obstruction determines the existence of this point, while invariance under the structural endomorphisms characterizes splitting. We also determine when weighted descendants satisfy the affine Jacobi identity and when operators of nonzero weight give affine doubles. For canonical Lie affgebras, we describe all affine Rota-Baxter operators by Lie subalgebra decompositions and translation vectors, and classify them up to automorphism in dimensions at most two.

title: Parameter-Free Adaptive Extragradient Methods for Generalized-Smooth Variational Inequalities
abstract: Variational inequalities (VIs) provide a unified framework for optimization, saddle-point, equilibrium, and learning problems, where operators need not be globally Lipschitz. The $\alpha$-symmetric generalized-smoothness condition allows local operator variation to grow with the operator norm, but existing extragradient methods often require unknown problem-specific constants. To address this issue, we propose PF-AEG, an explicit, line-search-free extragradient method whose stepsizes use quantities generated during the iterations, without prior knowledge of these constants. Under $p$-quasi-sharpness, we prove full-sequence convergence and last-iterate squared-distance rates: linear convergence for $0<p\le2$ and $\mathcal{O}(k^{-2/(p-2)})$ for $p>2$. The latter matches existing parameter-dependent rates under comparable assumptions, while the linear guarantee extends the previous $p=2$ result to $0<p\le2$. Building on the idea of PF-AEG, we develop AEG-VR, a variance-reduced adaptive extragradient method for finite-sum VIs. We prove almost-sure convergence and, under mild conditions, obtain analogous expected last-iterate rates, while retaining independence from the unknown problem-specific constants in stepsize selection. Experiments on synthetic generalized-smooth VIs and several learning problems show that the proposed methods are competitive with, and in several tested regimes outperform, existing baselines.

title: Oscillatory Integral Operators Along the Paraboloid and Applications
abstract: We prove decay estimates for oscillatory integral operators along $(y_1, y_2, y_1^2+y_2^2)$ in the finite field and the continuous settings. In the continuous setting, our result allows a bi-parameter maximal modulation, which extends the one-parameter version previously established by Pierce and Yung. Our approach is different from theirs. Then we discuss three applications of our estimates: a power saving bound for certain pattern finding problem in finite fields, a short approach to $L^p$ boundedness of an one-parameter Pierce--Yung operator, and $L^p$ boundedness of a bi-parameter Pierce--Yung operator.

title: There are no unconditional Schauder frames of exponentials in $L^p$ spaces, $p \ne 2$
abstract: We proved recently that there are no unconditional Schauder frames of exponentials in the space $L^p(\Omega)$, $1 \le p < 2$, for any set $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ of finite measure. For $p > 2$, we proved that the same holds provided that $\Omega$ has nonempty interior, but the general case remained open. In this note we close this gap, i.e., we establish that exponentials cannot form an unconditional Schauder frame in $L^p(\Omega)$, $p \ne 2$, without any additional assumptions on the set $\Omega$ of finite measure other than measurability.

title: Lifts of symmetries to minimal nondegenerate extensions are unique up to fermion attachment
abstract: Gauging fermion parity in a $(2+1)$-dimensional fermionic topological order requires lifting its symmetries to the resulting bosonic theory. We give a direct tensor-categorical proof that, for a slightly degenerate braided fusion category $\mathcal{C}$ and a fixed minimal nondegenerate extension ${\cal E}$, the restriction homomorphism $r\colon\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{LR}}(\mathcal{E})\to \operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{LR}}(\mathcal{C})$ on classes of complex-linear locality-respecting (LR) braided autoequivalences is surjective with central kernel $\mathbb{Z}/2$, generated by fermion attachment. Thus each symmetry class has exactly two LR lift classes, related by attaching the fermion to every vortex. We apply graded Morita theory to reduce the kernel to two module types on the vortex sector, corresponding to tensoring with the vacuum or the fermion. We then prove relative rigidity to show that each type determines a unique LR class, which are distinguished by fermionic self-braiding even when their actions on simple-object labels coincide. We prove surjectivity by extending graph algebras in $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{rev}}\boxtimes\mathcal{C}$ to Lagrangian algebras in $\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{rev}}\boxtimes\mathcal{E}$. Our results require neither unitarity nor a ribbon structure. We illustrate the lifting ambiguity in the Laughlin state, the $SO(3)_3$ theory and the Ising topological order.

title: A Countable Three-Generated Orthomodular Lattice with No $\sigma$-Complete Embedding
abstract: We give an explicit countably infinite orthomodular lattice generated by three specified elements and a direct argument that it admits no injective homomorphism into any $\sigma$-complete orthomodular lattice. In particular, it does not embed into any set-sized complete orthomodular lattice. The source is a generated subalgebra of a cofinite reduced product of finite-dimensional real subspace lattices. A nonzero finite term $a$ is orthogonal to the orbit of a terminal line under every finite word in three Sasaki projections, while another finite term $X$ satisfies $\pi_a\pi_X(t)=a$. If the image of this countable orbit has a supremum in a target orthomodular lattice, Sasaki adjunction forces that supremum to commute with the generator images. This forces the image of $a$ to vanish. The proof imposes no atomicity, modularity, Hilbert representation, cardinality bound on the target, or preservation of source infinitary operations. All target lemmas are derived from the orthomodular axioms.
comments: 8 pages, no figures; AI-use disclosure updated, verification scope retained; mathematical statements and proofs unchanged

title: Stability and Error Estimates with Optimal $\varepsilon$-Dependence for Strang Splitting of the Allen--Cahn Equation
abstract: In this work, long-time Sobolev stability and error estimates with optimal $\varepsilon$-dependence are established for the Strang splitting method applied to the Allen--Cahn equation with periodic boundary conditions. By combining the modified energy dissipation law, and H\"older-Gagliardo-Nirenberg product estimates, the numerical solution is proven to admit uniform-in-time $H^r$-seminorm bounds $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-r}+1)$, consistent with the corresponding Sobolev bounds of the exact solution. A second-order error estimate $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^2\tau^2)$ is further established on any prescribed finite time interval, exhibiting quadratic dependence on $\varepsilon$. Numerical experiments are presented to verify the optimal $\varepsilon$-dependence of both the stability and error estimates.

title: An unbounded convex set with the fixed point property for nonexpansive mappings
abstract: We construct an equivalent norm on $\mathbb{R}\oplus\ell_2$ and a nonempty closed convex unbounded subset having the fixed point property for nonexpansive self-mappings. The ambient renormed space has the fixed point property on bounded closed convex subsets. The main point is a geometric localization estimate at a distinguished point of the unbounded set; the fixed point conclusion then follows from the Kirk--Ray localization theorem.

title: Global $C^{2,\alpha}$ estimate for complex Monge--Amp\`ere equations on compact K\"ahler manifolds
abstract: In this paper, we prove a global $C^{2,\alpha}$ estimate for the complex Monge--Amp\`ere equation with a positive $C^\alpha$ right-hand side on a compact K\"ahler manifold.

title: Differential operator approach to the $\imath$Howe duality
abstract: The iHowe duality for iquantum groups of type AIII/IV was established in \cite{LX22} via two approaches, based on partial flag varieties and quantum coordinate coalgebras respectively. In this paper, we provide a new construction of this iHowe duality via quantum differential operators. Moreover, by deriving explicit action formulas, we prove that our construction coincides with the two constructions given in \cite{LX22}.

title: A smooth non-compactly generated category
abstract: Let $A=\mathbb{Q}[t^{\frac{1}{2^n}}:n\geq 0]$ and consider $A[u,u^{-1};\sigma]$, a skew Laurent polynomial ring, where $\sigma(t^q)=t^{2q}$. We study the kernel of derived extension of scalars along $ A[u,u^{-1};\sigma]\longrightarrow\mathbb{Q}[u,u^{-1}], $ the quotient by $\mathfrak{m}A[u,u^{-1};\sigma]$, with $\mathfrak{m}=(t^{\frac{1}{2^n}}:n\geq 0)$. A finite free resolution of $\mathfrak{m}A[u,u^{-1};\sigma]$ over $ A[u,u^{-1};\sigma]\otimes_{\mathbb{Q}} \bigl(A[u,u^{-1};\sigma]\bigr)^{\mathrm{op}} $ proves smoothness. A specialization inequality for matrix ranks supplies a nonzero exact colimit-preserving functor that vanishes on every compact object, proving failure of compact generation.

title: Conley Index of Limit Cycles in Filippov Vector Fields
abstract: Within the framework of multivalued dynamical systems, we compute the Conley index for a class of limit cycles in planar Filippov systems. We classify these cycles according to their interaction with the switching manifold, including crossing, sliding, and mixed regimes. Using the Conley index for multivalued admissible maps developed by Mrozek, we construct the appropriate index pairs and determine the corresponding indices for each class. These computations enlarge the class of Filippov invariant sets for which the Conley index is known and extend previous results on low-codimension singularities to periodic dynamics.

title: From Cauchy to Gaussian: Sharp Lower Deviations and Ehrhard-Type Inequality
abstract: We establish dimension-free, pointwise optimal lower-deviation bounds for convex functions under spherically symmetric Cauchy-type measures. These bounds use either mean-variance normalization or moments about the median, the latter covering the Cauchy case where the mean and variance are unavailable. By approximation with a parametrized family the Cauchy-type measures, our results recover the Gaussian setting of Paouris and Valettas \cite{PaourisValettas18} and strengthen their variance-sensitive estimate to a sharp bound, with a complete equality characterization. This goes beyond the partial improvements obtained in subsequent work. We also prove an Ehrhard-type inequality for arbitrary convex sets under these Cauchy-type measures in every dimension and characterize all equality cases. This resolves a conjecture posed by Byczkowski, Ma\l ecki and \.{Z}ak \cite{ByczkowskiMaleckiZak22}. The proof follows from a variational argument combined with the joint concavity of fiber rearrangement. The geometric inequality reduces distributions of convex observables to one-dimensional convex transforms, yielding the sharp lower-deviation bounds.

title: MSE Minimization for Movable Antenna Enhanced Wireless Sensing via Array Geometry Optimization
abstract: This paper develops adaptive movable-antenna (MA) array structures to enhance wireless sensing performance under arbitrary SNR conditions, using the AoA estimation MSE as the sensing metric. Due to the presence of strong sidelobes in the ambiguity function of sparse MA arrays, the classical CRB of AoA estimation MSE fails to characterize the true MSE in the low and medium SNR regimes, rendering CRB-optimized antenna position vector designs suboptimal for MA-enabled sensing. We derive a deterministic MSE approximation that captures the local estimation error within the mainlobe of the ambiguity function and the outlier error induced by sidelobes, providing a tractable and accurate optimization objective. We then propose three adaptive MA structures that are tailored to different hardware and computational requirements. For systems with fully independent motors, a movable free array is optimized by a two-stage greedy algorithm, which approaches the performance of the globally optimal exhaustive search but with lower computational complexity. Halving the required motors, a movable nested array fixes the dense inner subarray and adjusts only the outer-subarray spacing, reducing the optimization to a one-dimensional search. As the most hardware-efficient design, a movable twin array is proposed to adjust the inter-subarray spacing only with a single motor, while still achieving significant MSE reduction over fixed array geometries. Numerical results show that the derived approximation closely matches the true MSE compared with existing performance bounds, and that the proposed structures outperform the CRB-optimized designs by orders of magnitude in MSE across the tested low-to-medium SNR range. Moreover, it reveals that in the low-SNR regime, APV reconfiguration is more effective for improving estimation accuracy than simply increasing the number of fixed antennas.

title: Are implicit schemes needed in adaptive time stepping for PDEs?
abstract: Implicit time integration is the standard way to overcome the tight CFL time step restriction when solving nonstationary PDEs numerically. However, within an adaptive time accurate integration, the time step size selection is governed not only by stability but also by accuracy requirements. Therefore, an eligible question to ask is: is (unconditionally) stable implicit time stepping really needed if the time step is restricted by accuracy considerations anyway? And how much do we then lose (in terms of the time step size) when switching from the expensive implicit time stepping to stabilized explicit schemes? An answer to this question is also important because such a switch is often done when solving large scale nonstationary PDEs on massively parallel computers. This paper attempts to answer these questions by numerical tests for two particular adaptive time accurate settings: (i)~nonstationary convection-diffusion equations and (ii)~nonlinear heat equations.

title: A Domain-specific adaptation network for elliptic interface problems
abstract: Deep learning provides a flexible mesh-free framework for solving elliptic interface problems. However, domain-specific neural approaches often rely on separate networks for individual subdomains, causing the model complexity to grow rapidly as the number of subdomains increases. To address this limitation, we propose a Domain-Specific Adaptation Network (DSAN), which combines a shared backbone with lightweight subdomain-specific adapters to provide local represen- representation flexibility without replicating a complete network for each subdomain. We further establish a stability and error analysis showing that the continuous physics-informed residual controls the solution error, and decompose the resulting error into approximation, optimization, and sampling components. Numerical experiments on two- and three-dimensional problems with multiple regular and irregular interfaces demonstrate that DSAN achieves accuracy comparable to or better than fully decomposed multi-network methods while requiring substantially fewer trainable parameters. More- over, the parameter savings become increasingly pronounced as the number of subdomains grows, demonstrating the scalability of the proposed domain-specific adaptation framework.

title: Shape Holomorphy of the Helmholtz Calder\'on Projector and the Maxwell EFIE on $C^{1,1}$ Surfaces and Screens
abstract: We establish the holomorphic dependence of the Helmholtz Calder\'on projector on closed $C^{1,1}$ surfaces and of the operator associated with the Maxwell electric field integral equation (EFIE) on closed and open surfaces of the same regularity. More precisely, after transporting the boundary integral operators (BIOs) to fixed reference spaces, we prove that the resulting maps admit bounded holomorphic extensions to complex neighborhoods of compact sets of admissible boundary transformations, a property referred to as shape holomorphy. A key step in our proof consists in extending the results in [Lanza de Cristoforis and Rossi, Analytic Methods of Analysis and Differential Equations: AMADE 2006 (2008), pp. 193--220] and [Dalla Riva, Luzzini, and Musolino, Inverse Problems 38 (2022), 055004] from Schauder to fractional Sobolev spaces. For the EFIE, the single layer representation and the surface Piola transformation give the result in Maxwell trace spaces, whereas the result for open surfaces or screens is obtained by introducing suitable restriction and extension by zero operators. As opposed to existing results, we do not rely on an affine-parametric representation of the boundary deformations, thus allowing for more general parametric shape variations. Finally, we establish shape holomorphy of the shape-to-solution map for the EFIE, subject to interior electric Maxwell nonresonance on closed surfaces but with no such condition on screens. Under suitable summability and stability assumptions, these shape holomorphy results provide an analytic basis for the dimension-robust convergence of interpolation and quadrature methods used in computational uncertainty quantification (UQ) of scattering problems with high-dimensional, shape-parametric uncertain geometry.

title: Directional and Quasi-Omnidirectional Indoor Channel Measurements at Upper 6 GHz
abstract: This paper presents wideband indoor channel measurements and measurement-based statistical modeling of channel parameters in the upper 6 GHz (U6G) band using directional and quasi-omnidirectional antenna pairs. Measurements span 6.425-7.125 GHz at 32 matched positions per configuration in an open hall and an L-shaped corridor. System calibration and frequency-dependent peak-gain normalization retain antenna radiation-pattern weighting. Close-in and floating-intercept models are fitted to line-of-sight (LOS) and non-LOS (NLOS) path loss, respectively. Shadow-fading residuals, RMS delay spread (DS), and equivalent K factors derived from power delay profiles are characterized. LOS exponents range from 1.98 to 2.14. Despite similar attenuation slopes, directional links exhibit smaller LOS residuals and DS and higher equivalent K factors. Hall DS medians are 1.78 and 36.52 ns for directional and quasi-omnidirectional links. Corridor NLOS slopes are -1.12 and 2.54, respectively, while DS ordering varies by position. These results characterize antenna-dependent parameters for U6G indoor channels.

title: Coefficientwise Extremality and Rigidity for Independent Sets in Bipartite Graph Covers
abstract: Let $G$ be a finite bipartite graph and let $\widetilde G$ be an $M$-fold cover. We compare independent sets of $\widetilde G$ with those of the trivial cover, consisting of $M$ disjoint copies of $G$, after prescribing how many vertices are selected above each vertex of $G$. A conjecture from 2011, motivated by the Bethe approximation, asserts that the trivial cover maximizes every such count. We prove this for every feasible occupation profile whose active graph has treewidth at most two or is chordal bipartite. Equality holds exactly when the restricted cover is flat, meaning that fibre relabelings make it trivial. For $M\ge2$ and positive feasible occupations, a nonflat cover of a connected bipartite graph of treewidth at most two has a deficit of at least twice the coefficient of $p_G^{M-2}$ with every occupation reduced by one. A holonomy-dependent bound improves the factor to three for odd-order holonomy; both uniform constants are sharp. Comparison and rigidity survive finite compositions along an edge or a vertex, and quantitative bounds from one piece propagate to the whole graph, giving results beyond the two original classes. On any bipartite base, the first nonzero homogeneous defect is determined by the shortest cycles with nontrivial holonomy. At singleton occupations, our counts are numbers of DP-colorings of full covers. The dual DP color function on these classes and their finite seam compositions equals the chromatic polynomial, with equality attained precisely by canonical labelings. Dong's chromatic-polynomial inequality then yields the Dual-DP Shameful inequality on the same graph class. The main theorems have been formalized in Lean 4.
comments: 39 pages. Main Theorems A-C formalized in Lean 4; code: https://github.com/ywatanabex/coefficientwise-rigidity-lean

title: Description Complexity Bounds for Analytic Approximations of Lipschitz Functions
abstract: We study how many bits are needed to write down an elementary analytic expression that uniformly approximates a Lipschitz function. Expressions are finite trees over the basis $\{+,-,\times,\div,\exp\}$ with the variables and rational constants, and their size is $\dc(f)$, the length of the shortest description of $f$ in a fixed binary description language. For functions of one variable we prove that every $L$-Lipschitz $F:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ has an everywhere-defined approximant of accuracy $\Delta$ with $\dc(f)\le C\,(L/\Delta+\lg(1/\Delta+2))$ for all $L,\Delta>0$, by a linear spline smoothed with logistic ramps in a description language with one repetition construct. We prove a matching lower bound valid for \emph{every} description language: for $\Delta\le 1/36$ and every $L>0$ some $L$-Lipschitz function needs at least $\tfrac1{16}(L/\Delta+\lg(1/\Delta+2))$ bits. Hence the worst-case description complexity is $\Theta(L/\Delta+\lg(1/\Delta+2))$. For functions on $[0,1]^d$ the same method gives $\Theta_d\bigl((L/\Delta)^d+\lg(1/\Delta+2)\bigr)$, using a tensor-product spline whose coefficients are mixed second differences and cost $O(d)$ bits each. Without the repetition construct the upper bounds carry an additional logarithmic factor, whose necessity for plain expression trees is left open. A reference encoder, decoder and evaluator confirm the constructions numerically, and figures and tables report the checks.

title: Boundary of Anosov coaffine representations
abstract: Let $\Gamma \le \mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb R)$ be a torsion-free hyperbolic group dividing a properly and strictly convex domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb R\mathrm P^d$, and let $\rho: \Gamma \to \mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb R)$ be the inclusion. We study representations of $\Gamma$ into the coaffine group that are deformations of $\rho\oplus 1 \in \mathrm{Hom}(\Gamma, \mathrm{GL}(d+2,\mathbb R))$ and that lie on the boundary of the locus of projective Anosov representations. In this setting, we identify a canonical limit set $\Lambda$ for the action and study its fine geometric features which are, in a suitable sense, stable. We prove the existence of an ending lamination that encodes the failure of the Anosov condition and the non-existence of a Cannon--Thurston map. Under certain conditions, we compute the Hausdorff dimension and show that the corresponding measure is positive.

title: Overlap distributions under the Gibbs measure of a Haar model of $\log|\zeta|$ on and near the critical line
abstract: We study the Gibbs measure of $H(h) = \Re\sum_{p^{j} \leq X}U_{p}^{j}/(j p^{j(\sigma + i h)})$, a random field modeling large values of the log-modulus of the Riemann zeta function on and near the critical line, where the $U_{p}$ are independent and uniformly distributed on the complex unit circle. Writing $t = \log \log T$, the cutoff $X$ and real part $\sigma$ may vary with $T$ subject to $T^{1/t^{\Phi}} \leq X \leq T^{1/t^{\phi}}$ and $0 \leq \sigma - 1/2 \leq C_{\sigma}t^{\Phi}/\log T$, for fixed $\Phi \geq \phi > 1/2$ and $C_{\sigma} > 0$. On $I_{\theta} = [ - (\log T)^{\theta},(\log T)^{\theta}]$, define the Gibbs measure $G_{\beta,\sigma,T}^{\mathrm{H}}(\mathrm{d}h) := e^{\beta H(h)}\mathrm{d}h/\int_{I_{\theta}}e^{\beta H(h')}\mathrm{d}h'$. For every fixed $\theta > - 1$ and inverse temperature $\beta > 0$, the limiting joint distributions of correlations (overlaps) among points sampled from this measure are determined after averaging over the Haar phases. At and below $\beta_{c}(\theta) = 2\sqrt{1 + (\theta \vee 0)}$, the limiting two-overlap distribution is concentrated at $q_{0} = |\theta \wedge 0|$. Above this threshold, it assigns masses $\beta_{c}(\theta)/\beta$ and $1 - \beta_{c}(\theta)/\beta$ to $q_{0}$ and $1$, respectively, and the limiting joint overlap distribution is described by a Poisson-Dirichlet process of parameter $\beta_{c}(\theta)/\beta$. Approximate Ghirlanda-Guerra identities are shown to hold uniformly for bounded deterministic functions of the sampled positions. This paper is the first in a series devoted to extending these results to $\log|\zeta|$ near the critical line.

title: A single LU~factorization approach to model reduction for linear system families with a quadratic matrix pencil
abstract: To solve a family of large linear systems where the system matrix depends on the family parameter quadratically, we propose a new solution approach. Our method employs the derivatives of solutions with respect to the parameter. It turns out that the accumulated solution derivatives of increasing order, evaluated at a single specially chosen parameter value, provide successively better approximations to solution subspaces for the whole linear system family. We show that the derivatives can be computed by a recurrence, involving, at each step, solving a linear system with the same matrix. Constructing an orthonormal basis for the subspace spanned by the derivatives then leads to an efficient solver where just a single (sparse) LU factorization (or a single preconditioner setup in an iterative scheme) suffices to solve the whole linear system family. We call the new method ODB (orthonormal derivative basis method). As shown in numerical tests, compared to conventional solution methods, the ODB method allows to drastically reduce computational costs.

title: Splines and Operators: Part I - Admissibility and Native Spaces
abstract: The variational theory of splines requires a native space: a Hilbert space over which the regularization energy $\|\mathrm{L} f\|_{L_2}^2$ is well defined and the minimum-energy interpolation problem admits a spline solution. In this paper, we characterize the operators $\mathrm{L}$ that enable the construction of such spaces. Our framework is based on the completion of a space $\mathcal{S}$ of test functions in a controlled Gelfand-triple configuration $\mathcal{S}\subset\mathcal{H}\subset\mathcal{S}'$, which we call a Hilbert-Gelfand space. This departs from the classical reproducing-kernel techniques. Our construction is substantially more general, as it supports arbitrary linear operators and singular behaviors, and it recovers the reproducing-kernel setting as a particular case. It is also complete and canonical: the admissibility conditions on $\mathrm{L}$ are necessary and sufficient, and $\mathrm{L}$ determines its native space as the unique Hilbert-Gelfand space on which it extends to a bounded surjection onto $L_2$. We first show that Hilbert-Gelfand spaces are in one-to-one correspondence with compatible Riesz pairs $(\mathrm{A},\mathrm{A}^{-1})$ of positive-definite operators $\mathcal{S}\to\mathcal{S}'$. We then extend this correspondence to conditional Riesz pairs, where $\mathrm{A}$ is only conditionally positive-definite, which is the scenario that is relevant to splines. The theory identifies the \emph{attainable null space} of the energy as the unique admissible conditioning, realizes the abstract completions as concrete spaces of distributions, and provides a verifiable admissibility condition in terms of a dual energy functional. The framework is illustrated with the fractional Laplacian, which covers polyharmonic and thin-plate splines, and with ordinary differential operators, which cover exponential splines.

title: Multiple non-collision periodic solutions for second order singular differential systems with parameters
abstract: In this paper, new existence and multiplicity results for positive periodic solutions of singular second-order problems under sublinear and superlinear growth assumptions at infinity are established. Two aspects of our results should be highlighted in comparison with the existing literature. On the one hand, they allow for the consideration of systems exhibiting mixed behavior: sublinear in one component and superlinear in another. On the other hand, in the superlinear case, the existence of up to four positive solutions is established, whereas only two were obtained in previous works. Our approach is based on a recently established vectorial version of the Krasnoselskii-Guo fixed point theorem in product spaces.

title: Ideal filtrations and stabilization in alternating HRS tilting
abstract: We prove that the realization functors obtained by alternating forward and backward HRS tilts of any torsion pair over a finite-dimensional algebra are equivalences from some step onward. The number of steps is bounded by the lengths of the indecomposable projective modules. The even hearts define an increasing filtration of ideals contained in a square-zero ideal. For a torsion pair induced by a two-term silting complex, we identify the successive layers with Buan-Zhou kernel ideals and compute them by reduction modulo the successive ideals. We also describe the largest quotient over which the complex becomes tilting and determine the exact stabilization index from the two parity heights. We construct algebras for which the HRS height is arbitrarily large, and compute their ideal filtrations.

title: Splines and Operators: Part II - Resolution of Inverse Problems
abstract: We present a unified treatment of the data-fitting problems with quadratic (Hilbertian) regularization that arise in approximation theory, machine learning, engineering, and statistics. The generic problem is an optimization in the continuum: given $M$ linear measurements of an unknown function, one minimizes a convex data-fidelity term that is penalized by $\|\mathrm{L} f\|^2_{L_2}$, where $\mathrm{L} $ is a differential-like (spline-admissible) operator. The natural domain of the minimization is the native space $\mathcal{H}_\mathrm{L}$ of $\mathrm{L} $ - the largest Hilbert space over which the regularizer remains meaningful - for which we provide a concise and directly usable characterization. Central to our formulation is a measurement-adapted (conditioned) basis that decouples the null-space and spline components of the solution. This basis serves in three places. First, it tightens the formulation of our representer theorem, which confines the unique solution to an $M$-dimensional space without any orthogonality constraint on the coefficients. Second, it streamlines the implementation, as the exact discretization of the problem becomes an unconstrained convex program with closed-form solutions in the least-squares case, which covers ridge regression, Tikhonov regularization, and smoothing splines. Third, it makes the bridge with the minimum-mean-square-error estimation of generalized Gaussian processes, which is the topic of a companion paper.

title: Local coherence and recollement of abelian categories
abstract: We study how local coherenAAce of abelian categories behaves under gluing. For AB5 locally finitely presentable abelian categories, we give conditions on the gluing functors under which local coherence is transferred along a gluing $(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B}, \mathcal{C})$: from $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{C}$ to $\mathcal{B}$, and conversely from $\mathcal{B}$ to $\mathcal{A}$ or $\mathcal{C}$. The coherence theorem for augmented homotopes of Bondal and Zhdanovskiy is recovered as a special case, the coherence theorem for trivial extensions of Fossum, Griffith, and Reiten is a companion result in the same direction. We also introduce quasiprojective pairs of adjoint functors and prove a coherence criterion that generalises the criterion of Gomez Pardo and Martinez Hernandez to arbitrary Grothendieck categories. Finally, we extend Stenstr{\"o}m's characterisation of coherence via FP-injective modules to compactly assembled Grothendieck categories: such a category is coherently assembled if and only if the class of CM-injective objects, defined through compact morphisms, is closed under filtered colimits. Along the way we revisit the various equivalent conditions for the coherence of a ring, collecting them in a single place. The proofs make use of the compactly assembled categories of Efimov.

title: A quantum algorithm for meshless lattice Boltzmann method with unitary interpolation
abstract: We present a mass-weighted meshless formulation for the shifted incompressible lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) whose streaming step is exactly unitary, combining with the Carleman embedding. In traditional meshless LBM, on a scattered node set the semi-Lagrangian streaming step is an interpolation, which is not unitary; a generic block encoding of this matrix therefore requires a normalization proportional to its sparsity and logarithmically many ancillas. To overcome the non-unitarity, we instead express the interpolation as the exponential exp(a Dx + b Dy) of mimetic derivative operators. Endowing each node with its Voronoi mass and applying a mass-weighted similarity transform renders these derivative operators skew-Hermitian by enforcing moment constraints together with low-wave number trigonometric differentiation conditions, so that the interpolation becomes exactly unitary. Such unitarization of interpolation leave the local collision step unchanged up to a rescaling of its quadratic term, where the same weights define the amplitude encoding of the distribution functions. For quasi-uniform node sets, the mass-weighting diagonal remains within a unit-order normalization that degrades only mildly as the Carleman truncation order grows, thereby mitigating the cost of block encoding. Numerical experiments on the Taylor Green vortex confirm that the method reproduces the full meshless LBM, with the velocity error decreasing as the Carleman order increases.

title: Continuous meets discrete: geometry dependence of the performance of iterative solutions for nonsymmetric PDEs in terms of Laplace eigenvalues
abstract: It is a classical fact in spectral geometry that the eigenvalues of the Dirichlet Laplacian depend continuously on the geometry of the underlying domain, under suitable geometric restrictions. We show that this theoretical property is reflected in a concrete numerical situation: the convergence rate of iterative solvers for convection-diffusion problems remains stable under deformations of the domain. The connection is a superlinear estimate for preconditioned GMRES/GCR in which the relative residual errors are bounded by an explicit expression of the eigenvalues of the Laplacian, or of a symmetric positive elliptic operator in divergence form. We prove that this bound depends continuously on the domain, uniformly in the iteration index, under either regularity hypotheses on the boundary or a topological constraint in dimension two. We also establish corresponding statements on the discrete level. Two examples delimit the theory: domains bounded by a fractal curve, where continuity still holds, and perforated domains, where it fails. The theoretical results, including both examples with rough domains, are confirmed by numerical experiments.

title: Dimensional transition and spectral instability in lattice Hardy inequalities
abstract: Discretization can change a sharp stability threshold even when the continuum threshold is recovered at infinity. We study this phenomenon for the Hardy inequality on the integer lattice in dimensions at least three: its best coefficient agrees with the continuum value through dimension eight and is smaller from dimension nine onwards. We characterize this transition by the total critical defect, the summable error obtained by testing the lattice operator against the critical continuum power. A theta-function representation proves that the defect is negative and strictly decreasing from dimension nine; explicit positive Hardy remainders establish its positivity in dimensions three through eight. An exact energy identity relates this defect to the energy saved by optimizing the profile outside the neighbours of the origin. This exterior remains stable in dimensions eight and nine, locating the first loss of positivity in its coupling to those neighbours. We give self-contained proofs of both dimensional ranges. We then describe how local attraction creates a negative eigenvalue in a general class of lattice operators with critical inverse-square tails. Its magnitude is exponentially small near the threshold, with both the rate and the multiplicative prefactor determined by zero-energy solutions. The result allows connected finite modifications of the lattice and nonradial corrections to the tail. The same analysis controls the spread of the emerging state and gives a two-dimensional return scale for the associated Markov chain in every ambient dimension.

title: Non-convex integer programming: a deterministic solution method of the large block sale problem
abstract: We study a non-convex, nonlinear integer mathematical program with a linear constraint. This problem originates in finance and consists of selling a large predetermined quantity of a financial asset over a fixed time horizon, while maximizing the total proceeds. The selling price is modeled using a deterministic penalty function capturing the market's adverse reaction to the selling flow. From a complexity perspective, the problem is in NP. We first solve the problem exactly using dynamic programming and propose several heuristics that yield tight numerical lower bounds. We then reformulate the problem into an equivalent factorable form and derive a tight convex relaxation using McCormick inequalities. This relaxation is embedded within an adapted Branch & Bound algorithm to find the global optimum in finite time. Numerical experiments show that our methods outperform several widely used generic solvers (LocalSolver, Scip, Baron, Couenne, and Bonmin) for selected instances, but do not yield tight upper bounds, beyond small instances.

title: Risk-Constrained MPPI Tuning with Update-Aware MA-ES Racing
abstract: We formulate offline tuning of Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) controllers as a chance-constrained black-box optimization problem and develop an update-aware framework based on Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy (MA-ES). We use statistical information from noisy controller evaluations to determine when the evolutionary update is sufficiently reliable. When the recombination direction is certified, a derivative-free nonmonotone line search (NMLS) is used to refine the candidate solution, and a separate validation stage assesses the final frozen controller. We establish a worst-case arithmetic-complexity bound for both online MPPI control and offline tuning. Numerical experiments on TurtleBot 4, Jackal-like, and Ackermann models show that the proposed NMLS refinement is competitive with standard MA-ES, transfers across the three vehicle models without model-specific retuning, and improves several cost and validation measures. Both MA-ES variants also compare favorably with the tested randomized derivative-free line search (VRBBO) configuration. The results support the practical applicability and transferability of the proposed framework, while not claiming universal superiority or hardware-level safety.

title: Stable Manifolds and Uniqueness of Parabolic Rays in the Newtonian $N$-Body Problem
abstract: We study uniqueness for parabolic motions in the Newtonian $N$-body problem with a prescribed minimal normalized central configuration at infinity. A McGehee compactification identifies their tails with the strong stable manifold of the corresponding outgoing zero-energy equilibrium. The configuration projection of this manifold is locally a smooth graph, yielding a smooth initial-velocity field and uniqueness among all parabolic motions confined to a sufficiently narrow truncated cone, without any minimizing assumption. For parabolic geodesic rays, a renormalized action excess and a quantitative no-exit argument remove the confinement hypothesis when the initial configuration lies sufficiently far inside a smaller cone. We then prove that the set of collision-free initial configurations admitting more than one such ray has Lebesgue measure zero. The global argument propagates the local stable manifold backward, discards critical values of the configuration projections by Sard's theorem, and separates distinct regular branches through an explicit differential formula for their renormalized excess. No nondegeneracy assumption on the prescribed minimal central configuration is required. The proofs combine invariant-manifold theory with direct action comparisons and do not use weak KAM theory, Busemann functions, or the differentiability theory of Hamilton--Jacobi solutions.

title: A lower bound on $\text{depth} \ \mathbf{A/I^n}$
abstract: Let $(A,\mathfrak{m})$ be a Noetherian local ring and let $I\subseteq \mathfrak{m}$ be an ideal in $A$. Let $\ell(I)$ be the analytic spread of $I$. Let $G_I(A) = \bigoplus_{n \geq 0}I^n/I^{n+1}$ be the associated graded ring of $I$ and let its depth be $t$. We prove $\text{depth} \ A/I^n \geq t - \ell(I)$ for all $n\geq 1$.

title: A Unified Kalman-Type Classification of Controllability for Linear Stochastic Systems
abstract: We provide a unified algebraic classification of approximate controllability, approximate null controllability, exact null controllability, and exact controllability for finite-dimensional linear stochastic control systems with constant coefficients and multidimensional Brownian noise. The controls may enter both the drift and the diffusion terms, and the joint diffusion-control matrix may have arbitrary rank. A finite decreasing sequence of subspaces defines a common geometric obstruction. Its vanishing characterizes the two approximate properties and exact null controllability. Exact controllability to arbitrary random targets additionally requires the joint diffusion-control matrix to be surjective. The codimension of the obstruction is given by a rank difference of explicit polynomial block matrices, yielding finite tests in the original coefficients. When the joint diffusion-control matrix is surjective, we obtain a finite Kalman-type full-rank condition for exact controllability. If the obstruction vanishes, a linear state feedback with a deterministic time-dependent gain drives every initial state to zero at any prescribed positive time with finite energy and polynomial small-time cost. An equivalent orthogonal elimination algorithm computes the rank differences with polynomial storage and cost, avoiding exponentially large block matrices. A two-noise example relates the input classification to terminal errors and control energy in penalized stochastic linear-quadratic control problems.

title: Uniqueness and stability for inverse potential scattering with multiple wavenumbers
abstract: This paper is concerned with the inverse scattering problem of determining a real-valued potential for the three-dimensional Schr\"odinger equation from multi-wavenumber data. Under suitable a priori bounds, we establish local increasing stability from near-field Dirichlet data on a fixed sphere for polynomially decaying potentials, and global increasing stability from full far-field amplitudes for exponentially decaying potentials. The stability estimates consist of a noise term and a remainder term, with the latter decreasing as the upper measured wavenumber increases. We also obtain global uniqueness from exact near-field data under weaker regularity assumptions. The analysis combines analytic continuation, weighted resolvent estimates, and half-ray identities whose differences at chord endpoints cancel the unknown exterior contribution.

title: Sharp bounds and extremal structure of minimally strongly $k$-connected digraphs
abstract: Let $D$ be a finite simple minimally strongly $k$-connected digraph, where $k\ge 2$, and let $n=|V(D)|$. Mader proved in 1985 that $|A(D)|\le 2k(n-k)$ for all sufficiently large $n$, with equality if and only if $D\cong \overleftrightarrow{K}_{k,n-k}$ (JCTB 1985). We prove that this bound holds whenever $n\ge 3k-1$ and that the order threshold $3k-1$ is best possible. Moreover, if $n\ge 3k$, then equality holds if and only if $D\cong \overleftrightarrow{K}_{k,n-k}$. The threshold $3k$ is also best possible. These results resolve the conjecture of Mader in (JCTB 1985).

title: A proof of Kahane's conjecture in the Wiener algebra
abstract: We prove Kahane's conjecture: if a continuous unimodular function $F$ on the circle satisfies $\|F^n\|_{A(\mathbb{T})}=o(\log|n|)$ as $|n|\to\infty$, $n\in\mathbb{Z}$, then $F(x)=e^{i(mx+b)}$ for some $m\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $b\in\mathbb{R}$. The main step is a logarithmic lower bound for averages: for every nonconstant real-valued $\varphi\in A(\mathbb{T})$, $\frac{1}{T}\int_a^{a+T}\|e^{it\varphi}\|_{A(\mathbb{T})}dt \ge c_\varphi\log T \quad(a\in\mathbb{R},\ T\ge T_\varphi)$, where $c_\varphi>0$ and $T_\varphi>1$ are independent of $a$. The proof uses exact sampling on finite subgroups of the circle, uniformly bounded localized modulations, and the weighted non-harmonic Littlewood inequality of Jaming--Kellay--Saba. A suitable cutoff and a small linear perturbation of the phase ensure that a fixed positive proportion of the coefficients at the beginning of the frequency ordering have modulus one. Passing to integer powers and removing the degree of the circle map yield Kahane's conjecture without any additional smoothness assumptions. We also give equivalent phase, convolution, and operator formulations, and derive consequences for homomorphisms of weighted Wiener algebras and for higher-dimensional tori.

title: Hilbert functions over the exterior algebra and f-vectors in higher rank II: Generalizing Linusson's count to sumsets of f-vectors
abstract: Let $E$ be the exterior algebra of an $n$-dimensional vector space over a field, let $F$ be a graded free $E$-module with $r$ generators of degrees $d_1 \le \dots \le d_r$, and let $M$ range over the monomial submodules of Amata and Crupi. The Hilbert function of $F/M$ is a shifted sum of $f$-vectors of simplicial complexes; the companion paper determines the convex hull of such sums, and here we count them. For $r = 1$ the count is Linusson's (1999); we show that no new recursion is needed for general $r$. Using two statistics of an $f$-vector -- its top nonvanishing degree and the initial degree of the corresponding ideal -- we prove that the number of achievable Hilbert functions is a product of $r-1$ transfer matrices, one per generator-degree gap, with entries differences of Linusson's refined counts $E^p(n,k)$. The rank enters only as the length of a matrix product. The same holds for the proper variant. Consequences: a linear recurrence in $r$ for constant gaps, with exact exponential asymptotics $K \lambda^r$ when the gap is positive; polynomiality in $r$ when all gaps vanish; a threshold beyond which the count is a plain power; and polynomiality in the number of vertices.
comments: 56 pages. Part I is arXiv:2609.23605, report LiTH-MAT-R-2026/04, DOI 10.3384/LiTH-MAT-R-2026-04. Most of the combinatorial content is formalised in Lean 4 + Mathlib (no sorry, no extra axioms; the paper says which parts are not). Formalisation, code and tables in the anc directory and at https://gitlab.liu.se/jansn19/exterior-convex

title: Mixing Regularization for Average-Reward $Q$-Learning and $Q$-Planning
abstract: The average-reward setting for reinforcement learning is challenging because its Bellman operator is known to contract in span only when the underlying Markov chain is mixing. Whereas existing work typically assumes a contraction property, e.g., through environment mixing, we consider the setting where we are given a reward-agnostic $m$-step mixing policy, and we control the contraction and exploration properties of the learned policy by regularizing toward the mixing policy. We provide finite-time analysis of $Q$-learning algorithms that can be instantiated with multiple choices of regularization, with guarantees measured with respect to the regularized fixed point. Our framework exposes novel regularizer-dependent objects that control contraction, exploration, and operator bias. In the one-step setting, our rates match the best known rates for $Q$-iteration and synchronous $Q$-learning, and for $m$-step mixing we derive new rates. We also study $Q$-planning variants, and show that planning acts as time-localized learning, where the planning horizon $H$ trades off the bias from the boundary value against the sample complexity. Finally, we present numerical studies validating the analysis: (i) knowledge of a strong mixing policy improves convergence and exploration, and its advantage increases with bottleneck severity and, (ii) our theory predicts the convergence and bias rankings of regularizers from the $\alpha$-divergence family.
comments: 10 pages main body, 56 pages references and appendix, 8 figures. Under review

title: Uniform Green packing on compact Riemann surfaces
abstract: We extend the packing results of Etayo, Hedenmalm, and Ortega-Cerda for complex tori to arbitrary compact Riemann surfaces. The construction uses two different approaches, one based on complex geometry of line bundles, and the other on Laplace designs. Both approaches give the same basic existence of close-to-optimal point configurations on the given surface. This version was written with the help of ChatGPT.

title: Affine realization of tilted Richardson varieties
abstract: Richardson varieties provide geometric representatives for products of Schubert classes, with stratifications indexed by the subintervals of Bruhat intervals. We construct analogous geometric models for tilted Bruhat intervals for all split connected reductive groups. Our construction uses Richardson varieties in affine flag varieties and yields abstract tilted Richardson varieties whose isomorphism classes, together with their labeled stratifications, are independent of the choices involved. We obtain an explicit formula for the point-counting polynomials of their open parts in terms of increasing minimal weight paths, extending Dyer's formula for Kazhdan--Lusztig $R$-polynomials. Over the real numbers, their totally nonnegative parts are regular CW complexes homeomorphic to closed balls, which gives a natural geometric realization of the posets of tilted Bruhat subintervals in all Lie types. Over the complex numbers, we prove that their fundamental classes push forward under a continuous loop evaluation map to the Poincar\'e duals of the minimal-degree coefficients of quantum Schubert products.

title: Compactness and essential norms for two-weight fractional Riesz transforms on curves
abstract: We prove a compact two-weight $T1$ theorem for the $\alpha$-fractional Riesz vector, $0\leq\alpha<n$, when one measure is supported on a compact regular $C^{1,\mathrm{Dini}}$ curve $\Gamma$. The measures may have common point masses. Under the global boundedness assumptions, we give a two-sided estimate for the essential norm in terms of Muckenhoupt and testing constants computed after restricting both measures to small cubes. Compactness is equivalent to the uniform vanishing of these local bounds as the cube side length tends to zero. The smooth truncations have a unique weak operator limit and converge in operator norm in the compact case. For arclength measure and distance power weights, we determine the compactness ranges for Green gradients on bounded tubes and for Newtonian gradients and Biot--Savart fields on the whole space. The whole-space operators in these ranges are compact but are not Hilbert--Schmidt. When $\alpha=n-1$ and both measures have positive continuous arclength densities $a,b$ on the same closed curve, we obtain the exact essential norm $\pi c_{n-1,n}\max_\Gamma\sqrt{ab}$.

title: Exponential Green energies, quantization, and minimizers on compact Riemann surfaces
abstract: We study the exponential Green energies associated with a finite point configuration on a Riemann surface. We focus on studying optimal or close-to-optimal configurations, and show that they must be well-spread out on the surface. We study in particular the round sphere and obtain values for the minimal Green energy of a configuration. The first version of this paper was written with the help of ChatGPT.

title: DisCo Algebra: Why Disintegration and Combination Are Not Inverses
abstract: We present DisCo algebra---a compositional framework for joint probability built from a symmetric cooperad (disintegration) and a symmetric operad (combination) on the bare family $\mathcal{P}_n=\mathrm{Prob}([0,1]^n)$. No probability integral transform, no external summary functions, no enrichment of objects with conditional kernels. The disintegration side uses block-wise joint CDFs as intrinsic, measure-determined 1D summaries, yielding a lossy compression. The combination side reads the same summaries and reconstructs via regular conditional measures, yielding a lossless embedding. We prove that combination followed by disintegration is the identity on admissible inputs, but disintegration followed by combination is not---the information loss is exactly the conditional KL divergence between the true conditional distribution and the conditionally independent product. This asymmetry reveals a hard limit on how much cross-block dependence can be captured by scalar block summaries.

title: Anomaly Flow II: Estimates and Long-time Existence for the Coupled Flow
abstract: In this follow-up to \cite{Sua25}, we extend the results to the coupled anomaly flow which incorporates the evolution of a Hermitian metric on a holomorphic vector bundle over a compact complex $3$-fold with general slope parameter $\alpha'$. This yields a similar sufficient smallness condition on the slope parameter $\alpha'$ in order to extend the flow on $[0, \tau)$ to $[0, \tau + \epsilon)$. We also augment the argument of \cite{Sua25} slightly to fix the peculiarity of the units in the condition for $\alpha'$ for the $k = 1$ case.

title: Stability in the determination of the coefficients for coupled relativistic Schr\"odinger system
abstract: In this article, we prove a stability result for the identification of the coefficients appearing in a coupled relativistic Schr\"odinger system posed on a bounded domain of $\mathbb{R}^{1+n}$, where $n \geq 3$. More precisely, by utilizing input-output operator, where Neumann boundary data are available only on a subset of the boundary, and constructing an appropriate geometric optics solution, we derive a stability estimate of $\log$-$\log$ type for the matrix-valued first-order coefficients. This result is subsequently used to obtain a $\log$-$\log$-$\log$ type stability estimate for the zeroth-order matrix-valued potential.

title: A Half-Space Theorem for the Allen--Cahn Equation in All Dimensions
abstract: We prove that, in every dimension, a bounded, non-constant entire solution of the Allen--Cahn equation whose zero set is contained in a half-space is a one-dimensional heteroclinic solution.

title: An Exact Branch-Price-and-Cut Algorithm for a Truck-as-Hub Vehicle Routing Problem with Drones
abstract: Rural last-mile logistics remains challenging because of sparse demand, limited road infrastructure, and long travel distances. We study a Truck-as-Hub Vehicle Routing Problem with Drones in Rural Areas, in which multiple trucks each carry a dedicated fleet of drones. Drone launch and retrieval are restricted to predesignated passive synchronization pads, where a visiting truck temporarily acts as a mobile hub, may dispatch multiple drones simultaneously, and must wait until all launched drones return before continuing its route.
