abstract: We study closed-set stabilizers in topological full groups of minimal effective ample groupoids with Cantor unit space. For almost finite or purely infinite groupoids, we extend the maximal stabilizer theorem of Grigorchuk and Vorobets to every subgroup containing the commutator subgroup. For a nonempty closed nowhere dense set, maximality of its stabilizer is equivalent to minimality of its stabilizer action, minimality of the regular reduction, and primeness of a canonical wide open subgroupoid. Without assuming almost finiteness or pure infiniteness, we prove spatial rigidity for stabilizers acting minimally on infinite closed nowhere dense sets. Their isomorphism types determine the ambient Kakutani equivalence class and, when Hausdorff, the effective reduction. We also realize every AF groupoid with compact unit space as the full restriction, with its relative topology, of any minimal effective ample groupoid with Cantor unit space to a closed nowhere dense subset. Combining rigidity and realization yields continuum many pairwise nonisomorphic stabilizers in every subgroup containing the commutator subgroup; these stabilizers are maximal when the ambient groupoid is almost finite or purely infinite. The realization also gives explicit AF subquotients of the ambient reduced groupoid $C^*$-algebra, including the CAR algebra, with compatibility on the canonical diagonal subalgebras.

title: Post-critically finite polynomials over cyclotomic closures of number fields
abstract: We prove that, for any number field K and and d at least 2, there are at most finitely many monic, centred, post-critically finite polynomials of degree d with coefficients in the extension of K by all roots of unity.

title: Weighted norm inequalities for operators with new Muckenhoupt type weights in the Bessel setting and applications
abstract: Let $\lambda>-1/2,\neq0$. Consider the Bessel operators \begin{align*} \Delta_\lambda:=-\frac{d^2}{dx^2}-\frac{2\lambda}{x}\frac{d}{dx} \end{align*} on $\mathbb{R}_+$. In this paper, we first establish several characterizations for $\widetilde{A}_{\infty,\lambda}$ weights introduced by Li et al. (Math. Z. 309(1) (2025), Paper No. 13, 29pp), which are different from the previous $A_p$ class with respect to the measure $x^{2\lambda}dx$. Among these characterizations, we obtain the sharp reverse H\"{o}lder inequality (RHI) for $\widetilde{A}_{\infty,\lambda}$ weights. As applications of RHI, we derive a precise open property of $\widetilde{A}_{p,\lambda}$ weights, and obtain a sharp weighted bounds for the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator $\mathcal{M}_\lambda$ associated to $\Delta_\lambda$, which was missing in the previous papers. Next, we also establish several extrapolation theorems related to $\widetilde{A}_{p,\lambda}$ weights. Furthermore, we characterize the restricted weighted weak type estimates for $\mathcal{M}_\lambda$ via a new class of weights $\widetilde{A}_{p,\lambda}^{\mathcal{R}}$, which is strictly larger than $\widetilde{A}_{p,\lambda}$. Meanwhile, we obtain quantitative restricted weighted weak type $(p,p)$ bounds for sparse operators. As applications, we derive various kinds of weighted inequalities for Riesz transforms, maximal operators, square functions, variation operators and their commutators associated to $\Delta_\lambda$.

title: Some Remarks on Regular Sequences and Complete Intersections
abstract: We give an ideal in a polynomial ring in three variables, generated by three elements and having height equal to three, but for which no permutation of its generators is a regular sequence. We prove that in a polynomial ring over an infinite field, an ideal of height n generated by n polynomials, always admits a set of n generators, for which any permutation is a regular sequence.

title: Bernoulli numbers and the integer group determinants of $C_p \times C_p$
abstract: For a prime $p\ge7$, let $S(C_p\times C_p)$ be the set of integer group determinants and $e(p)$ the least exponent for which $p^{e(p)}\mathbf Z\subseteq S(C_p\times C_p)$. Let $r_p$ be the least integer $r\ge1$ satisfying $(2r+1)i>r(p-1)$ for every irregular pair $(p,2i)$ with $r\mid i$. We prove the unconditional inclusion $p^{p+3+2r_p}\mathbf Z\subseteq S(C_p\times C_p)$. Equality $e(p)=p+3+2r_p$ holds when Vandiver's conjecture holds for $p$ and $r_p\le(p-5)/2$, hence for every prime $7\le p<2^{31}$. The first exception to $e(p)=p+5$ is $p=103$, where $e(103)=116$. A polynomial obstruction from Bernoulli numbers supplies the lower bound, and circular units give the construction. For regular primes, we characterize the entire determinant set through explicit affine systems over $\mathbf F_p$ and principality conditions in $\mathbf Z[\zeta_p]$. For regular $p\ge11$, prime cofactors cannot occur at valuation $p+3$; at valuation $p+4$ they have natural density $(p+1)/(hp^{(p-3)/2})$, where $h$ is the class number of $\mathbf Q(\zeta_p)$. We also show that $p^{p+5}$ is the least absolute value of a nonzero $p$-divisible determinant for these regular primes.
comments: 27 pages; supplementary Python and Magma programs and recorded outputs included as ancillary files

title: Asymptotics of Random-Lattice Enumeration: Beyond HKZ via Dense Sublattices
abstract: To bridge the gap between worst-case and heuristic analyses of lattice enumeration, we study the sizes of (unpruned) enumeration trees on $n$-dimensional Haar-random lattices. Writing $n^{cn+o(n)}$ for the tree size at the shortest vector radius, we investigate the asymptotic scaling of $c$, and which bases minimize it. For quasi-HKZ bases, we rigorously analyze the random-lattice HKZ geometry and establish $c=1/(2e)\approx 0.1839$. This matches the worst-case enumeration exponent of Hanrot-Stehl\'{e} and confirms earlier predictions for the geometry of HKZ bases on random lattices. Searching beyond quasi-HKZ bases, we prove that with high probability, the minimum achievable tree size exponent $c$ over all bases of a random lattice satisfies: \begin{align} 0.1464 \approx \frac{2-\sqrt{2}}{4}\leq c<0.1474. \end{align} For the lower bound, we use Kim's mean-value formula for nested chains of primitive sublattices to rule out bases with small prefix determinants. This strengthens the earlier Rankin-based heuristic lower bound exponent $c \geq 1/8$, discussed by Nguyen and Hanrot-Stehl\'{e}, and rules out the existence of random-lattice bases with trees as small as predicted by the geometric series assumption. For the upper bound, we show that with high probability a dense primitive half-rank sublattice exists with determinant at most $n^{n/8 + o(n)}$. Combining dual HKZ on this sublattice with HKZ on its quotient gives a basis with $c \leq 1/(4\sqrt{e}) \approx 0.1516$. Recursively splitting each half lowers the upper bound below $0.1474$, and under a natural heuristic assumption we prove that the lower bound is tight. Combined with the collision search of Feng-Gao-Liu, our two-block construction gives a polynomial-space algorithm solving the closest vector problem with preprocessing (CVPP) on random lattices in query time $n^{0.0892 n + o(n)}$ for arbitrary targets.

title: The a-number of the Serre-type maximal curves of Abd\'on-Bezerra-Quoos
abstract: For every prime power $q$, we determine the $a$-number of the Serre-type maximal curves $X(q,n)$: $y^{q^2}-y=x^{(q^n+1)/(q+1)}$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q^{2n}}$, $n\ge 3$ odd, introduced by Abd\'on, Bezerra and Quoos as a generalization of Serre's curve $y^4+y=x^3$ over $\mathbb{F}_{64}$. The Weierstrass semigroup at the unique point at infinity gives an explicit basis of holomorphic differentials, on which the Cartier operator acts by monomials; this reduces the $a$-number to a lattice-point count, which we evaluate in closed form.

title: Moment-Calibrated Conformal Prediction with Side Information
abstract: For a fixed conformal score function, standard split conformal prediction calibrates a prediction set using the empirical distribution of the conformal scores, without using available side information about the data. We propose a moment-calibrated approach that uses such information to reduce variability across calibration data sets. Side information involving the covariates, the response, or both is expressed as moment restrictions, which are enforced through empirical likelihood weights on the calibration data points. The resulting weighted empirical distribution of the scores determines the weighted empirical quantile without changing the score function. We establish finite-sample bounds on training-conditional and marginal coverage of the moment-calibrated prediction set. We derive asymptotic distributions for training-conditional coverage and average prediction-set size, show that their asymptotic variances are no larger than the corresponding variances under standard split conformal prediction, and characterize when the reductions are strict. In the semi-supervised setting, we identify an optimal moment function of a given covariate representation, develop implementations using prespecified moment functions or a function learned by cross-fitting, and quantify the effect of the unlabeled sample size. We also extend the method to coverage conditions indexed by a class of functions of the covariates through weighted quantile regression. Numerical studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

title: Tuza's Conjecture for Graphs of Maximum Degree at Most 10
abstract: For a finite simple graph $G$, let $\nu(G)$ be the maximum number of pairwise edge disjoint triangles and $\tau(G)$ the minimum number of edges meeting every triangle. Tuza conjectured in 1981 that every such $G$ satisfies $\tau(G) \le 2 \nu(G).$ We prove the conjecture for the class of graphs with $\Delta\le10.$

title: Holomorphic Bisectional Curvature on Total Spaces of Holomorphic Vector Bundles
abstract: We study complete K$\"a$hler metrics with prescribed signs of holomorphic bisectional curvature on total spaces of holomorphic vector bundles over compact complex manifolds. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions in the nonnegative and strictly negative cases, characterized respectively by unitary flatness and Griffiths negativity of the bundle, together with the corresponding curvature conditions on the base. We also obtain a global metric splitting in the nonnegative case, rule out strictly positive curvature over positive-dimensional bases, and construct counterexamples to the converse in the nonpositive case.

title: Optimal detection of geometry in random graphs and kernel matrices at critical thresholds
abstract: Detection of geometry in random graphs and matrices has been extensively studied in recent years. For testing a dense random geometric graph on $n$ vertices with latent points in dimension $d$ against an Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi graph, the detection threshold $d\asymp n^3$ is well known since Bubeck, Ding, Eldan, and R\'acz (2016). We sharpen this result by establishing the optimal asymptotic testing error in the critical regime $d/n^3\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)$. The log-likelihood ratio is shown to be asymptotically normal and dominated by the signed triangle count. Moreover, we consider testing the rank statistics of inner products between latent points against uniformly random ranks. We show that ranks preserve all asymptotic testing information available in the full matrix models, and a cubic statistic based on rank statistics attains the optimal asymptotic error. This then yields an asymptotically optimal test for random kernel matrices with a possibly unknown, strictly monotone kernel. The proofs combine the classical framework of Davies (1985) and Le Cam and Yang (1988) for asymptotic normality under information loss with conditional limit theorems for the models in consideration.

title: Weighted moments and sharp convergence rates for supercritical multitype branching processes
abstract: Let $Z_n^i=(Z_n^i(1),\cdots,Z_n^i(d)), n\geqslant0$, be a supercritical $d$-type branching process starting from a single particle of type $i\in\{1,\cdots,d\}$, where $d$ is a positive integer. The Kesten-Stigum theorem states that if the mean matrix $M$ of the offspring distribution has spectral radius $\rho>1$ with the associated positive left and right eigenvectors $u$ and $v$, then for all $1\leqslant i \leqslant d$, the sequence $W_n^i=\langle Z_n^i,u\rangle/\rho^n u(i)$ forms a non-negative martingale, and hence converges almost surely to a random variable $W^i$ as $n\rightarrow\infty$. In this paper, we investigate the asymptotic properties of the martingale $\{W_n^i\}$, focusing on weighted moments and sharp rates of convergence. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the finiteness of $\phi$-moments of $W^i$, where $\phi(x)=x^{\alpha}\ell(x)$ with $\alpha\geqslant1$ and $\ell$ is a positive function slowly varying at infinity. We also determine the sharp exponential rate of convergence of $W_n^i$ to $W^i$ in the $\phi$-moment sense, identify a phase transition at the critical rate $\rho^{1/2},$ and characterize the behavior at the critical value. Our proofs rely on the double martingale structure of the fundamental martingale and on convex inequalities for martingales.

title: Nonexistence of Stable Solutions to Lane--Emden Equations on Graphs with Polynomial Volume Growth
abstract: We study stable solutions of the Lane--Emden equation $$-\Delta u=|u|^{p-1}u$$ on graphs with polynomial volume growth. Due to the lack of a chain rule in the discrete setting, we establish suitable algebraic inequalities which serve as substitutes for the usual differential identities. Combining these inequalities with the stability condition and cutoff arguments, we obtain nonexistence results for stable solutions in a range of exponents analogous to the Joseph--Lundgren range. As an application, we derive a lower bound for the Sobolev best constant in the discrete setting.

title: A note on stability conditions on product-quotient surfaces
abstract: Let $X$ be a product-quotient surface, which is by definition a minimal resolution of $(C_1\times C_2)/G$, where $C_i$ are smooth curves of genus $\geq 2$ and $G$ is a finite group. When $G$ acts freely, we show that every product Bridgeland stability condition on $C_1\times C_2$ induces a tilt stability condition on $X$, and that, if $p_g(X)=q(X)=0$, every tilt stability condition on $X$ arises this way. When $(C_1\times C_2)/G$ has only $A_1$-singularities, we use induction \cite{MMS} and derived McKay correspondence \cite{BKR} to produce non-geometric stability conditions $\sigma_X$ on $X$, which satisfy the full support property and lie in the closure of the geometric chamber. Whether $\sigma_X$ also lies in the closure of the $\widetilde{\mathrm{GL}}^+(2,\mathbb{R})$-orbit of the tilt stability conditions depends on a single inequality, $\omega_X^2 \ge n/8$, where $n$ is the number of $A_1$-singularities. When it fails, the geometric chamber is strictly larger than this orbit.

title: Unipotent quotients in compactified Coxeter varieties
abstract: In this paper, we extend Lusztig's description of quotients of Coxeter varieties by unipotent radicals of parabolic subgroups, to quotients of certain open neighbourhoods in the smooth compactification of Coxeter varieties. These quotients are products of an affine space with a Coxeter variety for an associated Levi quotient, and this result holds uniformly for any connected reductive group over a finite field. As an application, we prove a conjecture of Wang computing the invariants, under the action of unipotent subgroups, of the cohomology of the Deligne-Lusztig coverings of Coxeter varieties. We also prove that derived Alvis-Curtis duality sends the compactly supported cohomology of these coverings to their ordinary cohomology.

title: On the Structure of the Cut Locus in Certain Classes of Warped Product Manifolds
abstract: In this paper, we determine the structure of the cut locus for a class of complete warped product manifolds $M=(R^1\times S^1,dt^2+m(t)^2d\theta^2)$, where the warping function $m(t)$ is positive and even, under the assumption that there exists a positive number $t_1$ such that the Gaussian curvature is nonpositive on the domain $t^{-1}\left((t_1,\infty) \right)$ and is decreasing along the subarc $t^{-1}([0,t_1])\cap\theta^{-1}(0)$ of the upper half meridian.

title: The Norm Spectrum of Barnes-Wall Lattices Below Twice the Minimum
abstract: Let $\Lambda_m$ be the Barnes-Wall lattice of dimension $2^m$, normalized to have minimum squared norm $d_m:=2^{m-1}$. We determine its complete norm spectrum strictly between $d_m$ and $2d_m$, proving that, for every integer $m\ge1$, $\{\|x\|^2:x\in\Lambda_m,\ d_m<\|x\|^2<2d_m\}=\{2d_m-2^j:j\in\mathbb Z,\ \lceil m/2\rceil\le j\le m-2\}$. In particular, the norm spectrum in this interval is nonempty for $m\ge4$. The proof uses a Gaussian-integer model in which lattice automorphisms arising from Clifford unitaries transform a vector into a pair of coordinate subvectors in a lower-dimensional lattice. Divisibility of the differences of their squared norms and a matrix Parseval identity provide the arithmetic and averaging constraints needed for induction on $m$. Every listed norm is realized explicitly by a sum of two minimal vectors of the lattice.

title: Amplified moments and a refinement of the quasi-Riemann hypothesis
abstract: Recently, OpenAI announced a uniform $7/8$ zero-free half-plane for finite-order Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3})$, together with its transfer to Dirichlet $L$-functions. Assuming the analytic inputs of that work, we improve the boundary from $7/8=0.875$ to $8748867/10000000=0.8748867$ for the same families. The improvement combines a relaxed direct estimate with an amplified first moment of the reflected numerator, obtained from the existing fourth-moment estimate. A two-stage parameter argument yields the stated boundary without strengthening the inverse-moment estimate.

title: A note on the logarithmic exponent of Ramsey number $r(4,t)$
abstract: In this short note, we point out that the recent lower bounds for off-diagonal Ramsey numbers $r(s,t)$ with fixed $s\ge 5$, together with the recent proof of the Ajtai--Erd\H{o}s--Koml\'os--Szemer\'edi independence conjecture, imply \[ r(4,t)=\frac{t^3}{(\log t)^{2+o(1)}}. \] This note is solely for informal circulation and will not be submitted for publication.

title: Quaternionic Elasticity Theory with Local Fractional Derivatives
abstract: We develop a quaternionic formulation of linear elasticity in which the classical derivative is replaced by Yang's local fractional derivative and the classical Cauchy--Riemann operator by a fractal Cauchy--Riemann operator. We formulate fractal kinematics, a constitutive law with a material length scale and the equilibrium equation, and show that, for displacement fields with polynomial components, the resulting homogeneous fractal Lam\'e system is equivalent to the monogenicity of an explicit quaternionic field. On the polynomial sector, that is, for finite combinations of normalized fractal monomials, we prove a fractal Kolosov--Muskhelishvili representation of the displacement field in terms of two monogenic quaternionic potentials, together with its completeness, by a direct construction that uses neither the Galerkin nor the Papkovich--Neuber potentials. The position term of the classical formula has to be replaced by a corrected position operator, which satisfies the exact Weyl relation with the partial local fractional derivatives. Finally a fractal Papkovich-Neuber representation is derived.

title: Rydberg Atomic Quantum Receivers for OFDM Systems: An Atomic-Comb Design
abstract: Rydberg atomic quantum receivers (RAQR) exhibit exceptional sensitivity to radio-frequency (RF) signals, positioning them as promising candidates for next-generation wireless systems. Extending their capabilities to orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM), however, requires atomic responses that go beyond broadband reception and are tailored to the structured interference of multicarrier signals. To bridge this gap, we develop an atomic-comb Rydberg receiver based on six-wave mixing (SWM) transduction. In particular, injecting a multi-tone local oscillator (LO) into the RAQR generates frequency-shifted replicas of the intrinsic SWM response. By subtly tuning the amplitude and phase of each LO tone, constructive and destructive interference can be selectively induced to preserve desired response components while attenuating harmful frequency offsets. Furthermore, we harness the response-reshaping capability of the proposed atomic comb to proactively mitigate OFDM interference. More explicitly, by exploiting the discrete difference-frequency structure of both carrier-frequency-offset (CFO)-induced and phase-noise (PN)-induced inter-carrier interference (ICI), we optimize the atomic-comb response to suppress dominant ICI components directly. We further reveal an intrinsic coupling between spectral shaping and the time-domain effective channel memory, motivating a joint optimization of both ICI and inter-symbol interference (ISI), which simultaneously suppresses inter-carrier leakage and post-cyclic-prefix (CP) tail energy. Extensive simulation results validate our atomic-comb design, unveiling that the proposed atomic comb can effectively reshape the receiver response over the OFDM, while mitigating ICI, shortening the effective channel memory, and substantially lowering CP overhead.
comments: This manuscript has been submitted to IEEE journal

title: Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for closed axisymmetric hypersurfaces
abstract: We establish sharp Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for closed, embedded, axisymmetric hypersurfaces Sigma in n+1 dimensional Euclidean space R^{n+1}, the dimension n > or = 2, with admissible C^{1,1} profiles. Let H_j be the j-th normalized mean curvature. If Sigma is axiconvex, i.e., every hyperplane orthogonal to the symmetry axis meets the enclosed domain in an n-dimensional ball or empty, then \[\left(\frac{\int_\Sigma H_\ell\,dA}{|\mathbb S^n|}\right)^{1/(n-\ell)} \le \left(\frac{\int_\Sigma H_k\,dA}{|\mathbb S^n|}\right)^{1/(n-k)}, \qquad 0\le\ell<k\le n-1. \] Without axiconvexity, the inequalities hold for sign-corrected integrals \[\int_\Sigma\varepsilon_\theta^{\,j}H_j\,dA,\] where varepsilon_{theta}= {sgn}(sin {theta}) denotes the sign of the azimuthal principal curvatures. As applications, the Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities remain valid whenever both l and k are even. Equality in each of the above inequalities holds if and only if Sigma is a round sphere. The proof adapts the rearrangement and tangent angle folding approach of Dalphin-Henrot-Masnou-Takahashi from surfaces of revolution in R^3 to n-dimensional axisymmetric hypersurfaces in R^{n+1}. The higher-dimensional construction uses weighted monotone rearrangement to produce convex comparison bodies with C^{1,1} boundaries.

title: Global solutions to the fully nonlinear obstacle problem
abstract: In this paper, we investigate global solutions to the fully nonlinear obstacle problem. We prove that, after factoring out invariant directions, the coincidence set of any global solution belongs to one of the following four types: a single point, a compact convex set with nonempty interior, a ray for $n=1$, or a slender body for $n\geq 2$, where $n$ denotes the spatial dimension. Furthermore, we establish a bijection between the collection of all global solutions with compact coincidence sets and a family of functions describing the asymptotic behavior of such solutions at infinity.

title: Counting Rational Points on a Certain Bihomogeneous Threefold
abstract: Let $V\subset\mathbb P^2\times\mathbb P^2$ be the threefold $x_0y_0^2+x_1y_1^2+x_2y_2^2=0$, and let $U$ be the complement of its coordinate hyperplane sections. For the anticanonical height $H([\mathbf x],[\mathbf y])=|\mathbf x|^2|\mathbf y|$, evaluated on primitive integral representatives, we prove \[ N_U(B)=\frac{12\pi-14}{\zeta(2)\zeta(3)}B\log B+o(B\log B). \] The two projections combine lattice counting with uniform conic estimates. The main arithmetic step is an average of the fiber singular series, whose two main terms are related by Hilbert reciprocity. A moment estimate controls the full bad-prime part, and shape estimates permit the errors to be summed over the height region. We also check the leading constant with Peyre's constant.
comments: We have added an effective-cone interpretation of the unequal contributions in Theorem 1.2

title: Non-vanishing of primitive cubic, quartic and sextic L-functions
abstract: We establish lower bounds for the non-vanishing proportions of primitive cubic, quartic and sextic Dirichlet $L$-functions over $\F_q[T]$ in the non-Kummer setting. Adapting the truncated-exponential method of Gao and Zhao, we improve the cubic lower bound of David, Florea and Lal\'in and obtain positive lower bounds for quartic and sextic families in which every ramified local character has full order. For each family, the lower limit of the non-vanishing proportion exceeds $e^{-e^{66}}$ as the conductor degree tends to infinity with $q$ fixed. We also establish uniform twisted first moments in the quartic and sextic cases, yielding an asymptotic formula for the sextic first moment. All results are unconditional.

title: Quadratic polynomials preserving free infinite divisibility
abstract: We characterize non-commutative polynomials of degree 2 which preserve free infinite divisibility as self-adjoint Lie polynomials of degree 2. This extends previous results which characterized homogeneous quadratic forms only. The proof is based on an involution of colored noncrossing partitions cancelling many terms; positive definiteness of the remaining terms is established by an explicit operator model on Fock space. Examples show that higher order Lie polynomials do not preserve free infinite divisibility.

title: A note on the Chern-Yamabe flow on compact Hermitian manifolds with negative Gauduchon degree
abstract: In this note, we prove that on a compact Hermitian manifold with negative Gauduchon degree, the Chern-Yamabe flow introduced in our recent work [13] converges to the solution of prescribed Chern scalar curvature problem, provided that the candidate curvature function is nonpositive and not identically zero.

title: New Minimum Storage Regenerating Codes With Small Sub-packetization Levels for All Admissible Repair Degrees
abstract: In this paper, {we propose a new family of $(n, k)$ Minimum Storage Regenerating (MSR) codes} for distributed storage systems. By structuring the parity-check matrix as a block Vandermonde matrix composed of diagonal matrices and generalized permutation matrices, the proposed code achieves a sub-packetization level of $N = (d-k+1)^{\lceil\frac{n}{2}\rceil}$ and supports any repair degree $k+1\le d<n$. A key innovation of the new construction lies in relaxing the strict commutativity condition previously required for the building blocks in the parity-check matrices of Ye-Barg codes. We introduce a novel proof technique to establish the MDS property without relying on full commutativity, thereby generalizing the applicability of block Vandermonde matrices and enriching the family of Ye-Barg codes. Additionally, the sparsity of the parity-check matrix enhances encoding and decoding efficiency by reducing computational complexity. This work provides new insights into the construction of MSR codes.

title: Cyclic steepest descent is $R$-superlinearly convergent for almost every initialization on two-spectrum quadratics
abstract: We completely classify cyclic steepest descent (CSD) on strictly convex quadratics whose Hessian has exactly two distinct eigenvalues. At the beginning of each cycle CSD recomputes an exact steepest-descent stepsize and reuses it for $m$ updates. For every $m\ge2$, write $A=aP+bQ$ with $0<a<b$ and spectral projectors $P,Q$. For nonzero spectral blocks, let $r=\|Pg\|_2/\|Qg\|_2$ at a cycle boundary. The exact projective dynamics is $r^+=r^{1-2m}$. Hence the nonzero equal-norm cone $\|Pg_0\|_2=\|Qg_0\|_2>0$ is precisely the nonterminating exceptional set: there the convergence is $R$-linear with factor $(b-a)/(b+a)$, whereas every other nonterminating initialization is $R$-superlinear and one-eigenspace initializations terminate in one step. The exceptional cone has Lebesgue measure zero, so $R$-superlinear convergence holds almost everywhere in this two-spectrum class. The main results of this paper were obtained through a generative-AI workflow using OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol, Anthropic Claude Fable 5, and OpenAI GPT-6 Astra. Further details appear in the disclosure at the end of the paper.
comments: 4 pages. Version 1 was published on Zenodo on 1 September 2026: https://zenodo.org/records/22211249 . This version updates the references and AI disclosure and revises the exposition; the main results are unchanged

title: Three-point orbits of 2-transitive groups and their combinatorial applications
abstract: Let $G$ be a finite $2$-transitive permutation group. We determine the orbits of $G$ on the unordered triples of its point set, together with the three-point stabilizer and its image inside $S_3$, for every affine and almost simple family in the finite $2$-transitive classification. These data classify the $G$-invariant triple systems and the simple $2$-\mbox{$(v,3,\lambda)$} designs admitting $G$, and yield in a uniform way the standard objects attached to them: the incidence and block graphs (with arc-transitivity and strong regularity in the Steiner case), the constant-weight and design codes, and the Schurian coherent configurations on triples.

title: Type $B$- and $C$- trigonometric weight functions
abstract: We introduce and study trigonometric weight functions of type $B$ and type $C$ arising from integrable lattice models. These functions give $q$-deformations of the factorial $K$-theoretic Schur $P$- and $Q$-functions of Ikeda and Naruse, with the $P$-functions specialized to the type $B$ case. We realize them as specializations of partition functions of a six-vertex model with triangular boundary conditions and derive their algebraic properties using the Yang-Baxter equation and properties of the $R$- and $K$-matrices. We introduce normalized weight functions and establish diagonal evaluation formulas, divisibility properties, and bounds on Newton polytopes analogous to those in type $A$, together with recursive relations and stability. We further derive branching formulas relating these functions to type $A$ weight functions, and prove equal-cardinality orthogonality and all-cardinality biorthogonality relations.

title: A categorical approach to the set-theoretic Yang-Baxter equation
abstract: We investigate set-theoretic solutions of the Yang--Baxter equation from a categorical perspective. The paper has two main objectives. On the one hand, several existing constructions and classification results in the literature are recast in categorical terms, thereby showing that certain hypotheses previously imposed on such solutions are in fact superfluous. On the other hand, the categorical approach leads naturally to new classes of Yang-Baxter solutions. Our approach consists in identifying suitable subcategories of the category $\mathcal{YB}$ of Yang-Baxter solutions and providing categorical characterisations of the solutions they encode. As an application, we prove that the category of P{\l}onka bi-magmas is isomorphic to the subcategory of $\mathcal{YB}$ consisting of solutions of the Baaj-Long-Skandalis equation. Along the way, we introduce and study a new class of Lyubashenko type solutions and examine the extent to which non-degenerate bijective solutions of the braid equation arise from skew left braces.
comments: Some of the results in this paper were included in the preprint arXiv:2305.14138v1, which is not intended for publication and will remain available only on arXiv; 22 pages

title: Supersaturation thresholds for expanded color-critical graphs
abstract: For a $k$-uniform hypergraph $L$, let $h_L(n,q)$ be the minimum number of copies of $L$ in an $n$-vertex $k$-graph with $\mathrm{ex}(n,L)+q$ edges. Let $t_L(n,q)$ be the minimum number of copies obtained by adding $q$ edges to an extremal $L$-free $k$-graph. A graph is color-critical if deleting a suitable edge decreases its chromatic number. Let $\mathcal K_k(F)$ be the expanded graph obtained by adding $k-2$ new vertices to each edge of $F$, with disjoint sets of new vertices for distinct edges. Mubayi proved that, for every clique $K_r$ with $r\ge4$ and fixed $ q>0$, $ h_{\mathcal K_3(K_r)}(n,q)\ge qt_{\mathcal K_3(K_r)}(n,1)$ for every sufficiently large $n$. Pikhurko and Yilma later proved that, for every color-critical graph $F$, there is a constant $\epsilon_F>0$ such that $h_{F}(n,q)=t_{F}(n,q)$ for every sufficiently large $n$ and $1\le q\le\epsilon_F n$. We extend this equality to expanded color-critical graphs. Let $d>k\ge3$. For every color-critical graph $F$ with $\chi(F)=d+1$, there is a constant $\epsilon>0$ such that $ h_{\mathcal K_k(F)}(n,q)=t_{\mathcal K_k(F)}(n,q)$ for every sufficiently large $n$ and $1\le q\le\epsilon n^{k-1}$. Let $q_L(n)$ be the largest integer $q$ such that $h_L(n,s)=t_L(n,s)$ for every integer $1\le s\le q$. We give a sufficient condition for $q_L(n)=\Theta_L(n^{k-1})$ and an explicit family satisfying it. We also give a different sufficient condition under which $q_L(n)=\Omega_L(n^{k-1/2})$. \noindent \emph{Keywords.} Supersaturation; extremal graph; color-critical graph; chromatic number; expanded graph; hypergraph.

title: Invariant Measures for Interacting Continuous-State Population Models
abstract: We study invariant probabilities for nonlinear two-population branching systems with competition, cooperation, or predator--prey interaction, driven by Brownian noise and spectrally positive stable jumps. Without immigration, every invariant probability of a conservative competitive or predator--prey system is concentrated on the boundary under either boundary convention. With nontrivial axis dynamics, coordinatewise continuation admits only the point mass at the origin. For cooperative systems, we give criteria for boundary concentration and interior stationarity, including a sharp criterion for bilinear cooperation with a common relative noise exponent. With immigration, explicit parameter conditions yield existence and stationary moment bounds. For square-root diffusions with positive immigration, these conditions ensure interior concentration and full support on the closed quadrant. Further lower bounds on immigration rates give uniqueness and convergence of time-averaged transition laws.

title: Regular automorphisms of periodic $p'$-groups need not be splitting
abstract: For a fixed prime $p$, a group is called a $p'$-group if the orders of all its elements are coprime to $p$. It is well known that in a finite $p'$-group an automorphism of order $p$ is regular if and only if it is a splitting automorphism of period $p$. In the Kourovka Notebook, V.\,D.~Mazurov asked whether these two notions coincide for periodic $p'$-groups. We answer this question in the negative by constructing a periodic group of prime period $q$ that admits a regular automorphism of order $p \neq q$ which is not splitting.

title: Polynomial Bohnenblust--Hille Bounds and Hardy--Littlewood Inequalities for Finite Local Systems
abstract: The complex polynomial Bohnenblust--Hille inequality states that, for a $d$-homogeneous polynomial $P:\mathbb C^N\to\mathbb C$, $P(z)=\sum_{|\alpha|=d}c_\alpha z^\alpha$, the coefficient norm $(\sum_{|\alpha|=d}|c_\alpha|^{p_d})^{1/p_d}$ is bounded by $B_d^{\mathrm{pol}}\|P\|_\infty$, where $p_d=2d/(d+1)$ and $B_d^{\mathrm{pol}}$ is independent of $N$. Here $\|P\|_\infty$ is the supremum norm on the unit polydisc. This inequality has a Boolean analogue for the Fourier--Walsh coefficients of functions of degree at most $d$, with the supremum taken over $\{-1,1\}^N$. In this setting, Defant, Masty{\l}o and P\'erez obtained subexponential bounds, and Ivanisvili established polynomial growth. Further polynomial estimates were obtained by Slote, Tseng and Volberg in the Boolean setting and by Slote and Volberg for cyclic groups. We study these coefficient inequalities in a broader framework of finite systems of functions that encompasses and extends the Boolean and cyclic settings. This framework also admits a natural $\ell_p$ formulation, leading to Hardy--Littlewood-type inequalities. For orthonormal systems, we obtain polynomial bounds for the Bohnenblust--Hille constants and, for sufficiently large $p$, for the constants in these Hardy--Littlewood-type inequalities. In the Boolean case, the polynomial power is $5/2$, with a cubic logarithmic factor.

title: pper and Lower Bounds for Blow-up Times in Coupled Reaction--Diffusion Systems with Nonlocal Sources
abstract: In this paper, we consider the following reaction-diffusion system \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} u_t=\Delta u+F\bigl(x,t,u,v,V(t)\bigr), & (x,t)\in\Om\times(0,T), v_t=\Delta v+G\bigl(x,t,u,v,U(t)\bigr), & (x,t)\in\Om\times(0,T), \mathcal B u=\mathcal B v=0, & (x,t)\in\partial\Om\times(0,T), u(x,0)=u_0(x),\quad v(x,0)=v_0(x), & x\in\Om, \end{cases} \end{equation*} where \begin{equation*} U(t)=\int_{\Om}u(x,t)\dd x,\qquad V(t)=\int_{\Om}v(x,t)\dd x, \end{equation*} and the boundary operator $\mathcal B$ is either \[ \mathcal B_D w=w \qquad\text{or}\qquad \mathcal B_N w=\partial_\nu w, \] $\Om\subset\R^N$ be a bounded domain with sufficiently smooth boundary, $N\ge 1$, and $\nu$ is the outward unit normal on $\partial\Om$. Under certain conditions, we obtain the upper and lower bounds for the blowup time of the solution to the system.

title: Three Homoscedastic Gaussian Components Have at Most Four Modes
abstract: Gaussian mixtures can have more modes than components. For three Gaussian components with a common covariance, four modes are attainable, whereas the best general upper bound was eight. We prove that four is the exact maximum in every dimension $d \ge 2$, for arbitrary means and positive weights. We further show that the sharp bound drops to three when the whitened means are collinear or form a right or obtuse triangle. The result covers degenerate modes without genericity or separate finiteness assumptions. Our proof maps modes to local minima of a separable free-energy functional on the probability simplex, reduces the problem to counting scalar inverse-function branches, and controls competing branches through curvature and stationary-height comparisons.

title: A Four-by-Four Obstruction to Polynomial Removal for Ordered Binary Matrices
abstract: We exhibit a fixed $4\times 4$ binary matrix with no polynomial induced ordered removal bound. At depth $h\geq 1$, let $m=2^h$. Our explicit host has order $(14h+2)m$, exactly $2m^6+\frac{1}{2}(m-2)m^5$ induced copies, and exact editing distance $m^2$ cells. Its normalized editing distance is $\Theta(h^{-2})$, while its induced-copy density is $\Theta(4^{-h}h^{-8})$. The lower bound holds against arbitrary cell edits through an injective family of $m^2$ protected selections. An exhaustive arithmetic classification identifies every induced copy and proves that a matching canonical repair creates none. The original-copy transversal number is exactly $m$, yielding an unbounded gap between hitting existing copies and eliminating all copies. The identities and the obstruction at every depth are formalized in Lean, with verification sources included as ancillary files.
comments: Lean formalization and verification sources included as ancillary files

title: Monotonicity of Coefficients of Interpolated Multiple Zeta Values
abstract: Let $\zeta^t(\boldsymbol{k})=\sum_{d=1}^{r}S_d(\boldsymbol{k})t^{r-d}$ be the interpolated multiple zeta value of an admissible index $\boldsymbol{k}$ of depth $r$. We show the monotonicity property of coefficients $S_1(\boldsymbol{k})\ge\cdots\ge S_r(\boldsymbol{k})>0$. In the proof, we represent the coefficients as integrals over a common measure space and compares the integrands pointwise. As consequences, we determine the sign and vanishing of $\zeta^{-1}(\boldsymbol{k})$ and locate the zeros of $\zeta^t(\boldsymbol{k})$ in the closed unit disk.

title: Constant-Loss Round-Preserving Direct Sums for Information Complexity
abstract: Strong direct-sum theorems relate the information needed to solve many independent instances of a communication problem to the information needed for one instance. For Gap-Majority composition, an optimal information bound was previously known, but preserving the number of communication rounds incurred an additional logarithmic loss. We prove a round-preserving Gap-Majority lemma with constant additive information loss, independent of both the number of instances and the number of rounds. More generally, we establish a variance direct-sum theorem for additive square-integrable observables over product distributions. For protocols with a bounded number of terminal answer values, the extracted single-coordinate protocols preserve the round budget, and their average information cost is at most the original information cost divided by the number of coordinates, plus a term depending only on the answer alphabet and the allowed variance loss. The proof uses centered counterfactual conditional means and a global variance amortization argument. Rather than encoding absolute conditional means for every possible terminal answer, we encode the information not already determined by the common view. The total squared innovation is controlled by a telescoping variance potential, yielding an information loss independent of the number of coordinates. We also derive same-round mean-square estimation bounds for arbitrary terminal outputs.

title: The sharp constant in the Chang--Marshall inequality
abstract: We prove that the optimal constant in the Chang--Marshall inequality is $e$, as conjectured by Andreev and Matheson. More precisely, if $f$ is analytic in the unit disk, vanishes to order $m\geq1$ at the origin, and has normalized Dirichlet integral $d\leq1$, then the boundary mean of $e^{|f|^2}$ is at most $e^{d/m}$. Equality holds precisely for monomials. The proof uses an auxiliary closed planar curve and the isoperimetric inequality to establish monotonicity of the exponential functional along normalized radial dilations.

title: Numerical Modeling of a Metallic Alloy Droplet Impact, Solidification, and Macrosegregation
abstract: For the first time, we study the effects of mass transfer on alloy droplet impact, solidification, and solute non-homogeneity or MacroSegregation (MS). For this purpose, a multi-physics model, including fully-coupled hydrodynamics of multiphase flow, wetting, conjugate heat transfer, phase change, and mass transfer, is established and validated carefully across several benchmarks. In addition, a concentration-flux-correction algorithm is proposed to conserve the solute mass within the droplet at the numerical discretization level. The validated model is subsequently used to explore the impact and solidification of an alloy droplet. The results show that accounting for mass transfer and solute transport improves the prediction of the dynamics of a solidifying splat, in a consistent manner with experimental observations, while this effect has been neglected in all previous studies. The analysis demonstrates that this improvement results from the flow sensitivity to the mushy region thickness, which is regulated by local solute concentration through the solidus and liquidus temperatures. Furthermore, analyses of the MS map identify several critical segregation regions most susceptible to defect initiation, such as cracking, including a long negatively segregated vein within the lamella, formed by the severe advective flow through the mush in the middle stages of the impact, a positively segregated region near the rim of the splat, appearing as a result of hook formation, and a major positively segregated zone at the top of the rim, which develops following the accumulation of the solute-rich melt sustained by washout from the lamella.

title: Maximum index of unbalanced signed graphs without a positive odd cycle
abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}_{r}^+$ be the set of all balanced signed graphs with underlying graphs $C_r$. A signed graph is called $\mathcal{C}_{r}^+$-free if it contains no subgraph isomorphic to any member of $\mathcal{C}_{r}^+$. In this paper, we characterize the extremal graphs that achieve the maximum index among all $\mathcal{C}_{2k+1}^+$-free unbalanced signed graphs of order $n$ when $k\ge 2$ and $n\ge 187k$.

title: Answer some Tkachenko's questions in factorizable semitopological groups
abstract: We construct a Hausdorff quasitopological abelian group that is second-countable and semiregular, with a bounded continuous function that does not factor through any regular first-countable semitopological group. Its regular and Tychonoff reflections coincide, have a countable network, and fail even factorizability through arbitrary first-countable semitopological groups. This gives negative answers to \cite[Problems~6.1, 6.2, 6.4, and~6.5]{Tk2026} of Tkachenko. The construction starts with a countable cone group whose common separation reflection is not Fr\'echet--Urysohn, answering \cite[Problems~6.8 and~6.9]{Tk2026} negatively. In contrast, symmetrization gives affirmative answers to \cite[Problems~6.6 and~6.7]{Tk2026} without separation assumptions. We also show that every countable semitopological group admits simultaneous factorizations of countable families through second-countable Tychonoff semitopological groups.

title: Cohen-Macaulay truncated path and Nakayama algebras
abstract: This paper characterizes Cohen-Macaulay algebras in the sense of Auslander and Reiten [Progr. Math. 95(1991)] within the following two classes of finite dimensional algebras: (i) truncated path algebras and (ii) Nakayama algebras. For the former, our characterization in terms of ordinary quivers shows that if a Cohen-Macaulay truncated path algebra $\Lambda$ is connected, then $\Lambda$ or $D(\Lambda)$ gives a dualizing module, where $D$ denotes the standard duality. For the latter, we show that every Cohen-Macaulay Nakayama algebra $\Lambda$ is Iwanaga-Gorenstein. In particular, $\Lambda$ always gives a dualizing module. Consequently, there is no non-trivial Cohen-Macaulay algebra among truncated path and Nakayama algebras.

title: Impact of matrix topological properties on the convergence of the conjugate gradient method
abstract: It is well known that the matrix structure affects the convergence of iterative methods, particularly those utilizing Krylov subspaces. The matrix structure, determined by its graph, dictates the propagation order of updates to the vector components that are recursively computed during the conjugate gradient method iterations. Along with the propagation of these component updates, round-off errors also propagate. We present a model for the propagation and accumulation of round-off errors and demonstrate that the larger the values of topological characteristics of the matrix graph, such as its diameter, effective diameter, and pseudodiameter, the slower the round-off error accumulates during the method's iterations, and the longer the propagation of round-off errors remains local when computing the components of the search direction, residual, and approximate solution vectors. Round-off errors arising during the computation of these components affect only those components whose corresponding vertices in the matrix graph are at a distance not exceeding the current iteration number. As the iteration number increases, the propagation of round-off errors between the vertices of the matrix graph becomes global, leading to the loss of orthogonality of residuals and conjugacy of search directions. In the context of mixed-precision computations, this implies that for a matrix with a larger graph diameter (or, more practically, effective diameter), a greater number of method iterations can be performed in a lower-precision mode before the onset of convergence stagnation.

title: Spectral geometry of saturated Fell bundles
abstract: Let $\mathcal B=(B_g)_{g\in G}$ be a saturated Fell bundle over a countable discrete group, equipped with a spectral triple. We give explicit sufficient conditions for lifting this triple to the reduced cross-sectional C\Star-algebra $C_r^*(\mathcal B)$. Using finite projective realizations of the homogeneous Morita equivalence $B_e$-bimodules, we transport the base Dirac operator to the individual fibres and assemble the resulting operators into a fibrewise Dirac operator. We introduce a spectral-regularity condition ensuring bounded commutators and give a sufficient criterion in terms of uniform derivative bounds on smooth factor-system data. Combining the fibrewise operator with a length operator associated with a proper translation-bounded matrix-valued length function yields the lifted spectral triple. When $B_e$ is separable, the lifted triple, with a suitable grading, represents the Kasparov product of the vertical class with the class of the unit-fibre triple. We also establish a summability criterion and sufficient conditions for stability under central cocycle twisting. A range of examples illustrates the scope of the construction, including twisted crossed products, free compact Abelian actions, and Fell bundles with nonfree homogeneous fibres.

title: Construction and analysis of an explicit fourth-order symmetric low-regularity integrator for the semilinear Klein-Gordon equation
abstract: In this paper, we propose and analyse a novel explicit fourth-order symmetric low-regularity trigonometric integrator for the semilinear Klein-Gordon equation with non-smooth solution in the $d$-dimensional space, where $d=1,2,3$. The integrator is constructed based on the full use of Duhamel's formula, the employment of a twisted function tailored for trigonometric integrals and the symmetrization procedure of trigonometric integrators. Robust error analysis is conducted, demonstrating that the proposed scheme achieves fourth-order accuracy in the energy space under a weak regularity requirement in $H^{2+\max(\mu,1)}(\mathbb{T}^d)\times H^{1+\max(\mu,1)}(\mathbb{T}^d)$ with $\mu> \frac{d}{2}$. A numerical experiment shows that the proposed low-regularity integrator is much more accurate than some well-known exponential integrators for approximating the Klein-Gordon equation with non-smooth solutions.

title: On the convergence of doubly stochastic block gradient descent method for linear inverse problems
abstract: Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) and randomized block coordinate descent (RBCD) belong to two fundamentally different classes of stochastic iterative regularization methods, and are promising and popular for solving large-scale inverse problems, due to their excellent scalability with respect to data size and signal size, respectively. In this work, we propose a doubly stochastic block gradient descent (DSBGD) method with early stopping, by integrating the updating strategies of both SGD and RBCD, for solving linear inverse problems in infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. At each iteration, the method randomly selects one data pair to obtain a stochastic gradient estimate, and then uses it to update one randomly selected block coordinate. We prove the regularizing property of DSBGD under a priori stopping rules and then derive its convergence rates with the additional source condition and a condition on the forward operator. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first convergence rate results of randomized coordinate descent-type iterative methods for inverse problems from the perspective of regularization theory. We also prove that the DSBGD iteration can be stopped by the classical discrepancy principle in finitely many steps with high probability, and that the mean squared error decreases monotonically before stopping. Several numerical experiments are provided to complement the theoretical analysis.

title: Wyner's Common Information and the Common Entropy are NP-Hard to Compute
abstract: Wyner's common information $J(p)$ and the common entropy $G(p)$ of a pair of random variables $(X,Y)$ with finite ranges and joint distribution $p$ are both defined by an optimization over the auxiliary random variables $W$ that make $X$ and $Y$ conditionally independent: $J(p)$ is the infimum of the mutual information $I(X,Y;W)$, and $G(p)$ is the infimum of the entropy $H(W)$. We prove that both quantities are NP-hard to compute. For Wyner's common information, deciding whether $J(p)$ is strictly smaller than a given integer $r$ is NP-hard, and the problem is NP-complete on tables that are uniform on their support and have the same number of positive entries in every row. The reduction is from Maximum Edge Biclique and rests on an exact criterion, in terms of rectangles in the support of $p$, for improving on the auxiliary $W=X$; every yes-instance satisfies $J(p)<r-1/(4N^2)$ and every no-instance satisfies $J(p)=r$, where $N$ is the number of positive entries of $p$. For the common entropy, deciding whether $G(p)\le r$ for a rational number $r$ is NP-hard, even for tables with at most four nonzero entries in each row, all taking one of two values. The reduction is from exact cover by $3$-sets and rests on a majorization property of the masses of the nonnegative rank-one decompositions of $p$, combined with a quantitative form of the Schur concavity of entropy. In both cases the separation between yes- and no-instances is inverse-polynomial in the size of $p$, so that approximating $J(p)$ or $G(p)$ within a suitable inverse-polynomial additive error is also NP-hard. The two mechanisms are genuinely different: we exhibit a table on which a large rectangle in the support lowers $J$ below the threshold of our first reduction while leaving $G$ on it.
comments: A preliminary version of the manuscript

title: Uniqueness of prescribed-node radial bound states for a zero-mass double-power equation
abstract: We study radial bound states of \[ \Delta u-\abs{u}^{q-1}u+\abs{u}^{p-1}u=0 \quad\text{in }\R^n, \qquad n\ge3,\qquad 1<q<p<\frac{n+2}{n-2}. \] For every integer $k\ge1$, we prove that there is exactly one radial bound state with $k$ simple zeros and $u(0)>0$. Its absolute maximum is attained at the origin. This confirms the zero-mass, Sobolev-subcritical case of Tang's double-power uniqueness conjecture. The proof adapts Tang's phase-transition analysis and combines it with a finite-level separation argument inspired by Cort\'azar--Garc\'ia-Huidobro--Yarur. Three main difficulties arise in the zero-mass double-power setting: the sign changes of key comparison quantities in the low-amplitude region, the possible failure of pointwise positivity of an auxiliary quantity when $n=3$ and $p+q<3$, and the absence of exponential decay at infinity. We overcome these difficulties by introducing bridge functionals to propagate the required sign information through low amplitudes, establishing a weighted integral positivity estimate in the exceptional three-dimensional range, and combining a radial-flux tail estimate with finite-level inverse-branch comparison. We also establish the strict ordering of the bound-state shooting heights and show that the shooting variation along the \(k\)-node state has exactly \(k+1\) simple zeros.

title: One boundary, infinitely geometries
abstract: Let $N$ be a 3-dimensional integral homology sphere. We prove the existence of a sequence of 4-dimensional topologically negatively curved manifolds $M_k$, $k=1,2,\dots$, satisfying the following: (1) all aspherical manifolds $M_k$ have the same universal cover $U_N$ depending only on $N$; (2) all fundamental groups $\pi_1(M_k)$ are hyperbolic and share the same Gromov boundary $X_N$ depending only on $N$; (3) the groups $\pi_1(M_k)$ represent infinitely many distinct quasi-isometry classes. The last conclusion, which represents the new feature, shows that negatively curved geometries in dimension 4 exhibit substantially richer structure than those in dimension 3.

title: Discrete intermediate dimensions: endpoints, spectra and quasi-isometric invariance
abstract: We introduce upper and lower discrete intermediate dimensions for unbounded subsets of Euclidean space and extend them to metric spaces. The definitions restrict the covering radii within a scale-dependent range of dyadic shells and take a supremum over an auxiliary parameter. The resulting dimensions are monotone in the parameter and recover the Barlow--Taylor discrete Hausdorff dimension at zero. We prove continuity at every positive parameter, with a sharp quantitative bound, and give an example with a jump at zero. At the upper endpoint, the upper dimension equals upper mass dimension for uniformly discrete Euclidean sets; the analogous lower mass identity fails. We establish a mass distribution principle and prove quasi-isometric invariance under a uniform coarse packing condition. For spaces with uniform polynomial volume growth, we construct clustered subsets attaining the continuity bound. Independent thinning truncates these spectra at the resulting mass dimension, almost surely for all parameters simultaneously. Applications include the discrete Heisenberg group with its word metric and the ranges of simple symmetric random walks.

title: Insdel Reed-Solomon Decoding Algorithms up to the Half-Singleton Bound
abstract: In this paper, we focus on decoding optimal Reed-Solomon codes of dimension two for insdel errors up to the half-Singleton bound. We present a decoding algorithm for the general insertion-and-deletion scenario with a time complexity smaller than brute-force decoding. Our algorithm corrects insdel errors up to the half-Singleton bound, which exceeds the scope of existing methods. Additionally, for the special cases of insertion-only and deletion-only insdel error patterns, we present two different algorithms with a time complexity smaller than our general algorithm.

title: On strongly minimal asymptotic bases of order $h$ generated by powers of $2$
abstract: Let $h\geq2$ be an integer and let $\mathbb{N}_0=W_1\cup\cdots\cup W_h$ be a partition into infinite sets. For $W\subseteq\mathbb{N}_0$, let $A(W)$ denote the set of all finite nonempty sums of distinct powers $2^w$ with $w\in W$. We give a necessary and sufficient condition for $A=A(W_1)\cup\cdots\cup A(W_h)$ to be a strongly minimal asymptotic basis of order $h$. This provides a complete answer to a problem posed by Nathanson in 1988.

title: A Berry--Esseen Bound of Order $(1+\log n)/\sqrt n$ for Peng's Central Limit Theorem
abstract: We derive a quantitative central limit theorem under sublinear expectations from a spatial endpoint regularity estimate for the one-dimensional \(G\)-heat equation. For bounded Lipschitz initial data, the second spatial derivative and the time derivative of its solution are Lipschitz in space and \(1/2\)-H\"older in time away from the initial time. In particular, \([u_{xx}(t,\cdot)]_{\mathrm{Lip}}\le C_G\Lip(\phi)/t\). Combining this estimate with the nonlinear Stein identity introduced in Song \cite{Song2020} and a replacement argument yields a bound of order \((1+\log n)/\sqrt n\) for bounded Lipschitz tests when the third absolute moment is finite and the lower variance is positive. The final replacement step is estimated directly, avoiding the nonintegrable singularity at time zero.

title: An Upper Bound to the Undetected Error Exponent with Erasure Decoding at Positive Rates
abstract: We study the undetected-error exponent of discrete memoryless channels with erasure decoding. Assuming that the undetected-error and erasure probabilities vanish, we derive an upper bound on the undetected-error exponent at positive rates. The bound uses Somekh-Baruch's genie-aided argument where an auxiliary output provides the decoder with a list of codewords. It recovers Telatar's tight rate-zero converse and is at least as tight as the straight-line bound. A numerical example shows that the improvement over the straight-line bound can be strict.

title: General Constructions of Permutation-Fair Dice
abstract: Suppose that each of $n$ players rolls a different die and the players are ordered by their rolls. Can the dice use disjoint labels such that ties are impossible, while all $n!$ orders remain equally likely? We give two general constructions of such dice and solve some related problems.

title: Universal Decoding for Unequal Error Protection
abstract: We study universal unequal error protection of a single special message over discrete memoryless channels. We construct a sequence of codes with a decoding rule that does not depend on the channel transition law. We derive an achievable error exponent for the special message while ensuring reliable decoding of the ordinary messages. The resulting exponent strictly improves on the natural equal-error-protection random-coding baseline and remains positive as the rate approaches capacity. For symmetric channels, it converges to the optimal red-alert exponent at capacity.

title: Every n points in the plane contain (m1 + o(1)) n points with no unit distance
abstract: Let $f(n)$ be the largest integer such that every set of $n$ points in the plane contains $f(n)$ points no two at distance $1$, and let $m_1$ be the supremum of the upper densities of Lebesgue measurable planar sets with no two points at distance $1$. Larman and Rogers observed that $f(n) \ge m_1 n$. We prove that $f(n)/n \to m_1$; that is, $f(n) = (m_1 + o(1))n$. This is the first half of a conjecture of D\'ucz and Varga, and with the bound $m_1 \le 0.247$ of Ambrus, Csisz\'arik, Matolcsi, Varga and Zs\'amboki it gives $f(n) \le (0.247 + o(1))n$. The proof builds a random independent subset of the algebraic plane, invariant under algebraic translations and rotations, whose probability of containing the origin is at least the worst finite independence ratio, and turns it into a measurable planar set of at least that upper density. Its only non-classical input is the Haar rigidity theorem for wild character laws from the OpenAI preprint The Euclidean plane is not five-colorable, which has a machine-checked Lean proof. The whole argument has been formalized in Lean 4 on top of it.

title: A trace Paley-Wiener theorem for $\mathrm{GL}_{n}(F)\backslash \mathrm{GL}_{n}(E)$, with $E/F$ a quadratic extension of non-Archimedean local fields
abstract: We extend the classical trace Paley-Wiener theorem for $p$-adic reductive groups, given by Bernstein, Deligne and Kazhdan in 1986, to a relative case. That is when $E/F$ is a quadratic extension of $p$-adic fields, the main result is a scalar Paley-Wiener theorem for relative Bessel distributions on $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)\backslash \mathrm{GL}_n(E)$. These distributions are relative character of the form $$\pi\mapsto I_\pi (f), \ f\in C_c^\infty(\mathrm{GL}_n(E)),$$ as $\pi$ ranges over $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$-distinguished irreducible tempered representations, and are constructed from a $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$-invariant functional and a Whittaker functional. Using the local Langlands correspondence, and the base-change from a unitary group, we show that the relative characters can be described as elements of the "generic" Bernstein center of the unitary group $U(n)$.

title: Oka complements in algebraic tori and their logarithmic covers
abstract: Suppose $n\ge2$ and $K\subset\C^n$ is compact and polynomially convex. Write $q(z)=(e^{-iz_1},\ldots,e^{-iz_n})$, $X_K=(\C^*)^n\setminus(K\cap(\C^*)^n)$, and $Y_K=\C^n\setminus q^{-1}(K)$. We prove that $X_K$ and its logarithmic covering $Y_K$ are Oka. More strongly, $Y_K$ admits normalized holomorphic families of entire embeddings through prescribed holomorphic sections. The proof combines polynomial pair Hamiltonian transport in multiplicative coordinates, compatible with the coordinate hyperplanes, with a fixed Fatou--Bieberbach model. Applications include Oka slab crosses over arbitrary nonempty connected planar domains, complements of periodic equal-radius Euclidean balls centered at products of planar lattices, and complements of sufficiently small closed metric balls in products of elliptic curves.

title: Spectral G\aa rding Elliptic Equations
abstract: We study spectral G\aa rding elliptic equations on compact K\"ahler manifolds. Smooth solvability is equivalent to the existence of a smooth representative in the admissible domain. The concavity theorem for ideal G\aa rding polynomials gives a fixed concave formulation to which Sz\'ekelyhidi's second-order argument applies in every degree $2\le d\le n$, extending Lin's top-degree solvability theorem. Combined with the numerical criteria of Fu--Li--Zhang--Zhang and Chen--Nie--Xu, this yields a Nakai--Moishezon type criterion for solvability on compact K\"ahler manifolds. A solution converts the local ideal G\aa rding structure into a global Lorentzian structure. Its mixed derivatives give a strict nonlinear Hodge--Riemann hierarchy from the degree of the equation down to degree two, and the homogenization of the intersection polynomial is Lorentzian in nef class directions. Numerical criteria then produce explicit Hodge--Riemann classes, Lefschetz isomorphisms in bidegree $(1,1)$, and weighted Hodge-index inequalities.

title: On modular vector invariant fields
abstract: Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field of any characteristic and $\rm GL(n,\mathbb{F}_q)$ the general linear group over $\mathbb{F}_q$. Suppose $W$ denotes the standard representation of $\rm GL(n,\mathbb{F}_q)$ and $\rm GL(n,\mathbb{F}_q)$ acts diagonally on the direct sum of $W$ and its dual space $W^*$. Let $G$ be any subgroup of $\rm GL(n,\mathbb{F}_q)$. Suppose the invariant field $\mathbb{F}_q(W)^G=\mathbb{F}_q(f_1,f_2,\dots,f_k)$, where $f_1,f_2,\dots,f_k\in\mathbb{F}_q[W]^G$ are homogeneous invariant polynomials. We prove that there exist homogeneous polynomials $\ell_1,\ell_2,\dots,\ell_{n}$ in the invariant ring $\mathbb{F}_q[W\oplus W^*]^{G}$ such that the invariant field $\mathbb{F}_q(W\oplus W^*)^{G}$ is generated by $\{f_1,f_2,\dots,f_k,\ell_1,\ell_2,\dots,\ell_{n}\}$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$.

title: Gorenstein Pr\"ufer domains with non-Pr\"ufer integral closure
abstract: There exists a one-dimensional local Gorenstein Pr\"ufer domain whose integral closure is not Pr\"ufer. We prove that the recently constructed coherent counterexample to the normalization problem has this stronger Gorenstein property. The argument establishes permanence of divisoriality of finitely generated ideals under ultraproducts and quotients by divided primes. It also supplies uniform matrix factorizations: in an ultraproduct of plane-curve domains, every nonzero ideal generated by $r$ elements is a cycle of a two-periodic totally acyclic complex with free terms of rank $r$. The divided prime defining the one-dimensional example is flat, so these complexes descend through the quotient and localization. A specified two-generated ideal remains noninvertible in every integral overring. Over the normalization, its associated Laurent overring has nonzero first Tor with every injective cogenerator, although both rings are Gorenstein flat over the original domain. Examples distinguish this failure from a nonnormal Gorenstein curve with Pr\"ufer normalization and show that the periodicity conclusion is stronger than the Gorenstein Pr\"ufer property alone.

title: Tur\'an Numbers of Linear Stars and Expanded Trees
abstract: For an $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal H$, let $\ex_r(n,\mathcal H)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $r$-uniform hypergraph containing no copy of $\mathcal H$. The $r$-uniform expansion $T^{(r)}$ of a tree $T$ is obtained by adding $r-2$ new vertices to each edge, with the added sets pairwise disjoint and disjoint from $V(T)$. In particular, the expansion of $K_{1,k}$ is the linear star $\mathcal L_k^r$, whose $k$ edges intersect pairwise in a single common vertex. Chung and Frankl (1987) determined $\ex_3(n,\mathcal L_k^3)$ and all extremal hypergraphs for every $k\ge3$ and sufficiently large $n$. We extend the odd-$k$ part of their result to every $r\ge5$, determining the exact Tur\'an number and the unique extremal hypergraph up to isomorphism for sufficiently large $n$. More generally, we extend this result to expansions of trees for which the minimum degree among the vertices in the smaller color class is odd and at least three. For every $r\ge5$ and sufficiently large $n$, we establish lower and upper bounds on their Tur\'an numbers. When no two vertices attaining this minimum degree in that color class have a common neighbor, we determine the exact Tur\'an number and the unique extremal hypergraph up to isomorphism. The proofs combine the delta-system method with stability arguments and a detailed analysis of extremal constructions.

title: The First Modular Zhu Algebra of $L(\frac12,0)_F$ in Characteristic Seven
abstract: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $7$, and let $V=L(\frac12,0)_F$. For the degree-four singular vector $q=(L(-2)^2-2L(-4))\mathbf1$ in the universal vacuum vertex operator algebra $\bar V$, set $V_q=\bar V/I(q)$. We prove that the natural quotient map induces an isomorphism $A_1(V_q)\cong A_1(V)\cong F[T]/(T(T-4)(T-5))\cong F^3$. Explicit $O_1(V_q)$-relations and four families of triangular PBW straightening relations give the upper bound, while three one-dimensional homogeneous subspaces give the matching lower bound.

title: An overring characterization of Gorenstein Pr\"ufer domains
abstract: We prove that a commutative integral domain is Gorenstein Pr\"ufer if and only if every overring is Gorenstein flat over the original domain. It is enough to test overrings that are finitely generated as algebras. The proof combines finite duality with a conductor-quotient argument. Under the overring hypothesis, the conductor quotient of a proper overring generated by two elements as a module is an IF-ring, and degree-one duality lifts first syzygies of finitely presented quotient modules to totally reflexive modules. This gives a bound of one for the Gorenstein flat dimension of every module annihilated elementwise by conductor powers. Quadratic integral elements provide such conductors at nonnormal localizations, while normal localizations give principal-ideal neighborhoods. Constructible compactness yields a finite cover, and a bounded complex of localizations combines these bounds over the original domain. Consequently every finitely generated ideal is Gorenstein flat and the domain is coherent. Examples distinguish finite-type from module-finite tests and Gorenstein flatness from ordinary flatness.

title: A new approach to interior estimates for fully nonlinear elliptic equations
abstract: We give new, elementary proofs of interior second derivative estimates for the Monge-Amp\`ere equation and the constant quadratic Hessian equation, based on the two-point maximum principle. The arguments require only one differentiation of the equation. For the Monge-Amp\`ere equation, the inhomogeneous term is assumed to be positive and continuously differentiable. For the quadratic Hessian equation, the estimate holds in every dimension $n\ge2$.

title: Classification of minimal-mass blowup solutions to the mass-critical Hartree equation at the $L^2$-critical level
abstract: In this paper, we study the focusing mass-critical Hartree equation \[ iu_t+\Delta u=-\bigl(|x|^{-2}*|u|^2\bigr)u \] at the ground-state mass $M(Q)$. We prove that, up to the symmetries of the equation, every global minimal-mass non-scattering solution is a solitary wave, while every finite-time minimal-mass blowup solution is a pseudo-conformal image of a solitary wave. This extends the results of \cite{LZ28,Miao-Xu-Zhao3,Wang-Gao} to the scaling-critical space $L^2$ and removes the radial assumption in the global case.

title: Boundary Vanishing Orders and Asymptotic Expansions for Planar Harmonic Functions with a Sublinear Robin Condition
abstract: We study boundary vanishing orders and asymptotic expansions of planar harmonic functions satisfying the sublinear Robin condition $\partial_\nu u=\lambda u-|u|^{p-1}u,$ with $\lambda\geq0$ and $0<p<1$. For nontrivial global solutions on bounded connected Lipschitz domains, we bound the number of nodal domains by the number of Steklov eigenvalues strictly below $\lambda$ and establish finite vanishing order at every boundary point. The boundary scaling gives the critical exponent $\frac{1}{1-p}$. On $C^1$ boundaries, every positive subcritical vanishing order is an integer, and the leading term is a unique homogeneous Neumann profile in conformal coordinates. At a noninteger critical order, the rescaled solution converges in normalized graph coordinates to an explicit homogeneous profile determined by $p$ up to sign. Every supercritical bulk vanishing order $m$ is an integer, with a unique homogeneous Dirichlet profile in conformal coordinates. The boundary trace has vanishing order $\frac{m-1}{p}>m$. Integer critical vanishing orders are excluded if the boundary is $C^1$ with Dini mean oscillation.

title: Temporal invariance of evolutionary entropy and comparative demographic analysis
abstract: Does evolutionary entropy depend on the width of the age classes used to describe a population? We show that the apparent dependence on temporal resolution is a consequence of the loss of information about reproductive timing within discrete classes. When this information is retained, corresponding continuous and discrete representations yield the same cycle entropy, generation time, evolutionary entropy, and reproductive potential in a common unit of time. When within-class timing is unknown, a uniform local reconstruction yields a logarithmic correction. For constant post-maturity hazard and fertility, continuous exponential and discrete geometric descriptions correspond exactly at every time scale. Thus, for a fixed reference duration, evolutionary entropy is a property of the reproductive process, not of its temporal partition. These results provide a mathematical basis for comparing demographic models across different temporal scales by identifying the information required to separate differences in reproductive organisation from effects of the chosen age-class representation.

title: FirstFit coloring process of random bipartite graphs and an online coloring lower bound in the random order model
abstract: FirstFit colors each arriving vertex with the smallest positive integer absent from its previously colored neighborhood. We prove that this rule can require $n^{\Omega(1)}$ many colors on certain bipartite graph of $n$ vertices even when the vertices arrive in a uniformly random order. This refutes the conjecture of Bosek, Gutowski, Laso\'{n}, and Przyby\l{}o [BGLP24] that FirstFit uses a polylogarithmic expected number of colors on every bipartite graph in the random order model. We obtain the lower bound by analyzing the FirstFit coloring process on random bipartite graphs, where vertices arrive to either side with equal probability, and with an independent edge density $n^{-x}$ for some $0 < x < 1$. Our result can also be viewed as a qualitative strengthening of Ku\v{c}era [Ku\v{c}91], who showed that, for every $\epsilon > 0$, there are graphs with chromatic number at most $n^{\epsilon}$ on which FirstFit uses $\Omega(n/\log n)$ colors in expectation under a uniformly random order. Our result shows that such poor behavior of FirstFit already occurs for $\chi(G) = 2$.

title: Bimodule duality and Artin's problem for skew field extensions
abstract: Emil Artin asked whether the left and right dimensions of an extension of skew fields must agree. Cohn and Schofield gave counterexamples through elaborate constructions. It has been a long-standing open question whether there is any division ring, infinite-dimensional over its center, for which the left and right indices agree whenever at least one is finite. We give the first such examples. Call a division ring index-symmetric if every division subring with at least one finite index has equal finite indices. Using a duality formula for bimodules over division algebras, we prove that every twisted Calabi--Yau division algebra is index-symmetric. The examples include the Weyl skew fields and, more generally, the quotient division rings of rings of differential operators on smooth affine varieties in characteristic zero. Further examples are the quotient division rings of enveloping algebras of finite-dimensional Lie algebras, Ore extensions of twisted Calabi--Yau noetherian domains, quantum affine spaces, and group algebras of torsion-free polycyclic-by-finite groups.

title: Schatten class membership of products of composition operators and their adjoints
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the Schatten class membership of the product of a composition operator and the adjoint of another composition operator on the Hardy and Bergman spaces. We provide several sufficient conditions and necessary conditions for these operators to belong to the Schatten classes. Moreover, for some specific symbols including linear fractional maps, finite Blaschke products, and inner functions, we obtain necessary and sufficient conditions.

title: A noetherian Hopf algebra has bijective antipode
abstract: We prove that a Hopf algebra over an arbitrary field has a bijective antipode if either its left or right regular module has finite uniform dimension. In particular, this solves Skryabin's conjecture, posed in 2006, that every noetherian Hopf algebra has a bijective antipode. Starting from Skryabin's injectivity theorem for weakly finite Hopf algebras, we associate to each finite-dimensional subcoalgebra an essential left ideal of common denominators that is also a right coideal in the antipode image. An annihilator identity makes this image essential in the original algebra as a left module over the image, yielding finite left uniform dimension from finite right uniform dimension. A second denominator construction inside the antipode image, together with a restricted inverse-antipode identity, proves surjectivity.

title: Whitney--Lagrange Decomposition for the First Family of Finite Element Differential Forms
abstract: We derive polynomial bubble duality in barycentric coordinates and construct explicit nodal bases for the first family of finite element differential forms. Logarithmic coordinates give an elementary proof of the Whitney--bubble decomposition. The Hessian of negative entropy defines a metric whose normalized Hodge star maps bubble generators to complementary-degree polynomial forms. This gives a direct geometric description of the known dualities and proves nondegeneracy of their integral pairings. Combining Whitney forms with shifted Lagrange polynomials then gives bases dual to tangential point evaluations in every dimension and order. The construction extends to scalar nodes that are unisolvent on every face. The interpolant is independent of the roots and commutes with face restriction.

title: On the OpenAI proof that Landau-Siegel zeros do not exist
abstract: A recent manuscript of OpenAI asserts that Landau-Siegel zeros do not exist. Here, we give a detailed account of its argument, arranged as a direct proof with explicit constants.
