There are absolute constants $q_0$ and $\delta_0>0$ such that, for every primitive real Dirichlet character $\chi$ of conductor $q\ge q_0$, every real zero $\beta\in(0,1)$ of $L(s,\chi)$ satisfies $(1-\beta)\log q\ge\delta_0$, and one can take $q_0=10^{10}$ and $\delta_0=3.0\times 10^{-3}$. Combined with a recent computation of Lu, Zaman, and Zhao, this result yields the bound $(1-\beta)\log q\ge 3.0\times 10^{-3}$ for every conductor $q\ge 3$. The proof is an interpolation determinant argument in the biquadratic field generated by $\sqrt{2}$ over the quadratic field attached to $\chi$. A real zero close to one forces $\chi(p)=-1$ for most primes $p$, and the Frobenius congruence at these primes makes a certain nonzero determinant divisible by higher powers of these primes than its Archimedean size allows. The underlying ideas are those of the OpenAI manuscript. The explicit constants, and the presentation, are new.

title: Dimension of affine iterated function systems on $\mathbb{R}^d$
abstract: Let $\{f_i(x)=M_ix+a_i\}_{i\in I}$ be an affine iterated function system on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with attractor $\Lambda$, and let $\mu$ be an associated self-affine measure. Assume that the $M_i$ generate a Zariski dense subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb{R})$. Under the strong open set condition, we show that $\dim_{\mathrm{H}}\Lambda$ equals the affinity dimension and that $\dim_{\mathrm{H}}\mu$ equals the Lyapunov dimension. The above results are consequences of the following projection theorem, which requires no separation condition. For every $1\leq n\leq d$ and for Furstenberg measure a.e. $(d-n)$-dimensional subspace $V$, \[ \dim_{\mathrm{H}} (P^V)_*\mu=\min\{n,\,\dim_{\mathrm{H}}\mu\}. \] This projection theorem in fact holds under hypotheses weaker than Zariski density: simplicity of the Lyapunov spectrum and a mild transversality condition (the Oseledets non-concentration property). The source of dimension increment in our proof is the positive dimension of the fiberwise conditional measures, exploited through Wu's one-dimensional entropy increase theorem. A key ingredient in reducing the higher-dimensional problem to this setting is a new structural result: a slab-filling property of the measure.

title: Rationality of Kontsevich moduli of stable maps, and their Galois descents
abstract: Let k be a field and X be a geometrically rational variety over k. We investigate the Kontsevich moduli spaces of genus zero, stable maps with curve classes of low degree on X over k, and define their twisted Galois descents. We study the k-rationality of these spaces in detail when X is a projective space/Severi Brauer variety and when X is moduli of genus zero n-marked points. When X is a homogeneous variety over the field of complex numbers, this is a well-known theorem of Kim-Pandharipande.

title: Hypersurfaces with constant sectional curvature of a product of two space forms
abstract: We complete the classification of hypersurfaces with constant sectional curvature of dimension greater than or equal to three in the product of two space forms.

title: SiteEvo: An LLM Agent for Autonomous Discovery of Site-Adaptive Massive MIMO Detectors
abstract: Designing a massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) detector that is tailored to each specific deployment site can improve detection performance, yet most existing detectors, including deep-unfolding methods, adapt mainly within human-prescribed algorithmic structures. This letter proposes SiteEvo, a site-adaptive agentic discovery framework that extends adaptation from parameter tuning to detector-algorithm discovery. Rather than selecting or recombining predefined architectures, the large language model (LLM) agent synthesizes complete executable detector programs under a common design contract by combining its pretrained communication knowledge, site-specific wireless evidence, and experience accumulated during the search. Each proposal defines its own processing structure and trainable parameterization, and the parameters are optimized by a communication-system backend. The resulting high-performance detector is further structurally refined to reduce block-level computational cost under a bit error rate (BER)-preservation constraint and is finally frozen for deployment without online LLM inference. Simulations across three sites demonstrate BER reductions by factors of 2.6 to 6.0 over the best-performing competing detector at each site at 6 dB, while structural refinement reduces block-level computational cost by 16.7-34.1% under a validation-BER constraint.
comments: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible

title: Toeplitz determinants for starlike mappings of order {\alpha} in several complex variables
abstract: Let $F(z)=zf(z)$, where $f$ is a normalized scalar holomorphic function on the unit ball $\mathbb B$ of a complex Banach space $X$ or on the unit polydisk $\mathbb U^n$ of $\mathbb{C}^n$. We establish sharp bounds for two Toeplitz determinants involving the second, third and fourth Fr\'echet derivatives of $F$ when $F$ is starlike of order $\alpha$, $0\leq\alpha<1$. The first bound is sharp for the full range $0\leq\alpha<1$, while the second is sharp for $0\leq\alpha\leq 2/3$. The extremal mappings are explicitly identified, confirming the sharpness of the estimates.

title: Symmetric Bases and $\ell^p$ Embeddings in Musielak--Orlicz Sequence Spaces under $\delta_2$
abstract: We study isomorphic embeddings into Musielak-Orlicz sequence spaces \(\ell_\Phi\), where the normalized generating sequence \(\Phi=\{\phi_n\}\) satisfies the \(\delta_2\) condition. Using admissible normalized blocks, we construct an associated limiting family \(\mathcal C_{\Phi,\tau}\) of Orlicz functions. If a Banach space \(X\) with a symmetric basis embeds into \(\ell_\Phi\), then there is a function \(\psi\in\mathcal C_{\Phi,\tau}\) such that the basis of \(X\) is equivalent to the canonical basis of \(\ell_\psi\). An Orlicz sequence space \(\ell_\psi\) embeds if and only if \(\psi\) is equivalent near zero to a member of \(\mathcal C_{\Phi,\tau}\); in particular, \(\ell^p\) embeds exactly when such a member is equivalent to \(t^p\). Assuming differentiability of the generators on a common interval near zero, we also derive the necessary bound \(p\leq b_{\Phi,(c_n),\delta}\), where the upper growth index incorporates the summable errors in the \(\delta_2\) condition. The same index yields cotype \(q\) for every \(q\geq2\) with \(q>b_{\Phi,(c_n),\delta}\). Examples with nonuniform growth and lacunary weights illustrate this bound. For alternating Nakano exponents, the explicit limiting family gives a sharper restriction than the index alone. For general Nakano exponents, we recover the known exact cotype criterion, including attainment of the optimal exponent. For weighted Orlicz spaces, we express the cotype criterion through summable scalar errors and recover the formula using the global upper growth index when \(w\in\mathcal A\).

title: Orbital stability of solitary wave solutions of the derivative nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation in the endpoint case
abstract: In this paper, we consider the orbital stability of solitary waves for the derivative nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation $$iq_t+q_{xx}+i\partial_x\bigl(|q|^2q\bigr)=0, \quad (t,x)\in\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}.$$ For the endpoint solitary waves satisfying $c>0$ and $c^2=4\omega$, we prove the orbital stability in $H^1(\mathbb{R})$ without any additional assumptions. The proof uses conservation of mass and the second Hamiltonian $\mathcal{H}_2$ to keep the B\"acklund-transformed solution small in $H^1(\mathbb{R})$ uniformly in time. We establish an inverse B\"acklund compactness result to reconstruct the algebraic solitary wave as the spectral zero approaches the negative real axis.

title: From Product Evidence to Access Rights: Auditing and Routing Non-Firm Grid Connections
abstract: Non-firm connection products can accelerate grid access while reinforcements are delayed, but their planning value depends on evidence supporting the contractual promise. We develop a one-way evidence-to-access framework for calendarized products. Stage A constructs and fixes directional restriction calendars from public residual-load and day-ahead price-timing signals. Stage B audits the submitted calendar and one bounded common repair, tests joint threshold attainability under the shared annual budget, and applies an aggregation-aware Power Transfer Distribution Factor (PTDF) certificate. Stage C treats the resulting ledger as fixed in queue-aware allocation and intervention planning. In the primary policy-package evaluation, the evidence-supported menu returns the same $2.119$~GW allocation as firm-only access, whereas authorizing the uniformly derated fallback raises awards to $6.442$~GW and reduces backlog from $136.076$ to $113.601$~GW-years; all $4.489$~GW of non-firm awards use the fallback. In a target-free matched control, evidence-routed and state-blind fallback menus attain primary objectives equivalent within EUR~1 and return the same accepted applicants, award years, routes, and intervention portfolio. Thus, in the reported testbed, fallback authorization rather than calendar-specific evidence support drives the access-volume effect.

title: The Brakke-BV structure of flat flows
abstract: We show that, in ambient dimension at most seven, varifold limits of the minimizing movements scheme introduced by Almgren--Taylor--Wang and Luckhaus--Sturzenhecker are integral Brakke flows. As a consequence, we show that $L^1$-limit points of the scheme, usually known as flat flows, are generalized BV flows. The result is unconditional and, in particular, remains valid even in the absence of energy convergence and in the presence of fattening.

title: On a derived equivalence classification of weakly symmetric algebras of Euclidean type
abstract: We consider a family $(\Lambda_\lambda)_{\lambda \in \Bbbk^\times}$ of weakly symmetric algebras of Euclidean type over an algebraically closed field $\Bbbk$, where $\Bbbk^\times:= \Bbbk\setminus \{0\}$, and for each $\lambda \in \Bbbk^\times$, $\Lambda_\lambda$ is socle equivalent to $\Lambda_1$, which is the trivial extension of a hereditary algebra of type $\tilde{A}$. We compute their Hochschild cohomologies, which shows that $\Lambda_\lambda$ is not derived equivalent to $\Lambda_1$ if $\lambda \neq 1$. This means that a derived equivalence classification of weakly symmetric algebras of Euclidean type given by Bocian--Holm--Skowro{\' n}ski is not complete.

title: Crystals and the parabolicity conjecture
abstract: These notes introduce crystals and crystalline Dieudonn\'e theory through the example of abelian varieties. After discussing $p$-divisible groups, $F$-isocrystals, slope filtrations, and overconvergence, we explain the parabolicity theorem for $F$-isocrystals and some of its applications to monodromy and Hecke orbits. Two appendices formulate research projects on isocrystals over formal schemes and on monodromy beyond the constant-slope setting. The exposition is intended for readers familiar with basic algebraic geometry and the \'etale and fppf topologies; prior knowledge of Witt vectors is helpful but not required.
comments: 25 pages. Course notes for the workshop 'A Sprint on Local Systems', Wuppertal, 2026. To appear in the workshop proceedings

title: A linear independence criterion for $p$-adic Hurwitz zeta values at odd integers
abstract: In this article, a new criterion is established to obtain the linear independence of some values of the $p$-adic Hurwitz zeta function at odd integers $s\geq 3$. We generalize a theorem of F.~Beukers, who gave, among others, an alternative proof---using Pad\'{e} approximation theory---of a result originally due to F.~Calegari on the irrationality of the $p$-adic Riemann zeta value $\zeta_p(3)$ for $p = 2, 3$. To prove our main theorem, we work in a general setting, where we construct and study new Pad\'e approximants of Laurent series satisfying the functional equation $f(z) = f(1-z)$. This complements our previous work on the linear independence of $p$-adic polygamma values.

title: A Viscoelastic Wave Equation with Nonlinear Damping and Supercritical Variable-Exponent Logarithmic Sources
abstract: We investigate a viscoelastic wave equation with nonlinear variable-exponent damping and a variable-exponent logarithmic source, allowing supercritical growth. The main difficulties arise from the failure of the source to map the energy space into $L^2(\Omega)$, the sign-changing logarithmic potential, and the lack of Sobolev control of the displacement for supercritical damping. Under an exponent condition linking the source and damping exponents, we prove local existence, an energy identity, and a continuation criterion. We prove finite-time blow-up for nontrivial solutions with nonpositive shifted initial energy. We also establish a blow-up criterion based on a sufficiently large initial displacement--velocity pairing, with a threshold depending on the positive part of the shifted initial energy, and derive an explicit upper bound for the lifespan. This criterion allows us to construct blow-up data at every prescribed level of the original energy. For initial data in a suitable stable region, solutions exist globally. For damping within the Sobolev range, a general relaxation condition yields energy decay estimates that include exponential and polynomial rates. Beyond this range, a time-weighted displacement estimate and a splitting of the memory integral give logarithmic decay.

title: A chain theorem for planar PM-compact bricks
abstract: A connected graph $G$ is matching covered if it contains at least one edge and every edge belongs to some perfect matching of $G$. A matching covered graph is a brick if it is 3-connected and after removing any two vertices, the resulting graph has a perfect matching. Bricks are the building blocks of matching covered graphs. A brick $G$ is extremal if the incidence vectors of all perfect matchings are linearly independent over $\mathbb{R}$. Zhou et al. [On planar extremal nonsolid bricks, J. Graph Theory, 2026] proved that for every planar extremal brick $G$, there exists a sequence of planar extremal bricks $G_0,G_1,\dots,G_n$ such that the underlying graph of $G_n$ is an odd wheel, $G_0=G$, and each $G_i$ $(0\leq i < n)$ has a triangle $T_i$ such that $G_i/T_i = G_{i+1}$, where $G_i/T_i$ means contracting the triangle $T_i$ into a single vertex. In this paper, the result of Zhou et al. is generalized to planar PM-compact bricks, a larger class of bricks including extremal bricks. We present a chain theorem for planar PM-compact bricks: for every planar PM-compact brick $G$, there exists a sequence of planar PM-compact bricks $G_0,G_1,\dots,G_n$ such that the underlying graph of $G_n$ is an odd wheel, $G_0=G$, and each $G_i$ $(0\leq i < n)$ contains a triangle $T_i$ such that $G_i/T_i = G_{i+1}$.

title: Hull Variation in Symplectic Linear Codes
abstract: We study the variation of hull dimensions of symplectic linear codes under equivalence transformations preserving the symplectic distance. For a symplectic linear code $C$, we introduce an even-valued invariant $\Delta(C)$, which depends only on the equivalence class of $C$. This invariant can be expressed as the generic rank of an associated space of alternating matrices and, equivalently, as twice a corresponding matroid matching number. If $C$ has dimension $k$, we prove that the minimum symplectic hull dimension among all codes equivalent to $C$ is $k-\Delta(C)$. Consequently, $C$ is equivalent to a symplectic LCD code if and only if $\Delta(C)=k$. We further show that every symplectic MDS code of even dimension is monomially equivalent to a symplectic LCD code. For a symplectic self-orthogonal code $C$, we determine all attainable hull dimensions: for every integer $r$ with $0\le r\le \Delta(C)/2$, there exists a monomially equivalent code whose symplectic hull has dimension $k-2r$. We also refine a standard form for the generator matrix of a symplectic self-orthogonal code and derive the corresponding parity-check matrix and the Gram matrix of the dual code. In the self-dual case, we characterize $\Delta(C)$ through minors of an associated symmetric matrix. Furthermore, we relate hull variation to graph matchings, establish a bound for $\Delta(C)$, and give graph constructions producing symplectic self-dual MDS, optimal, and best-known codes.

title: Tuza's Conjecture under an Edge-Count Condition
abstract:
For a graph $G$, let $
u(G)$ denote the maximum number of pairwise edge-disjoint triangles and let $	au(G)$ denote the minimum number of edges meeting every triangle. Tuza's conjecture asserts that $	au(G)\le 2
u(G)$ for every graph $G$. We first note that Tuza's conjecture is equivalent to the following statement: for every fixed $c\ge 0$, if $G$ is a sufficiently large $n$-vertex graph with $e(G)\ge n^2/4-cn$, then $	au(G)\le 2
u(G)$. In this paper, we prove this statement for every $c<2$.

title: Beyond Aggregate Drift: Optimal Client-Specific Windows in Federated Learning
abstract: We study federated learning from continuously arriving data: each client samples from its own distribution, these distributions drift over time, and the server must track the minimizer of the clients' weighted average loss. Clients are not alike as they collect data at different rates, with different noise, and change at different speeds. The main question is how much history should each one keep? A single shared window must serve every client at once, and so makes a fast-changing client carry the sampling noise of a slow, nearly stationary one. We give each client a memory of its own, sized to that client's noise, arrival rate, and drift, and refresh it by restarted accelerated method that starts from a common point. The tracking error is then bounded by \[ R\left(\sum_m w_m^{3/2}\,\sigma_m\sqrt{\gamma_m/\lambda_m}\right)^{2/3}, \] for clients with weight $w_m$, noise $\sigma_m$, arrival rate $\lambda_m$, and drift rate $\gamma_m$ on a domain of diameter $R$. This is never worse than what any common window can achieve, and strictly better whenever noise and drift are spread unevenly across clients. A lower bound that puts different groups of clients on different drift clocks shows this quantity is the right one. The two bounds agree up to a constant whenever the clients occupy boundedly many refresh scales, and in general differ only by the sixth root of the number of scales. Experiments show the gain comes from the memory rather than from the solver: it persists across accelerated, stochastic-gradient, and one-step methods, and against a separately tuned common-memory baseline.

title: KKT Residual Sliding Manifolds: A Projection-Free Structured Finite-Time Solver for Nonlinear Constrained Optimisation
abstract: Nonlinear Constrained Optimisation (NCO) requires simultaneous satisfaction of the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions. Existing methods enforce these conditions through projections, penalties, barriers, or sequential approximations, potentially introducing computational complexity and convergence difficulties. For nonconvex problems, a KKT point need not be a local optimum. This paper reformulates NCO as stabilisation of a unified KKT sliding residual manifold and develops SM-KKT, a projection-free solver. Stationarity, equality feasibility, and regularised Fischer-Burmeister complementarity are integrated into a unified residual system, with complementarity encoding inequality feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementary slackness. The manifold's zero set is shown to be equivalent to the KKT conditions. The required Jacobian saddle-point inertia is characterised and shown, under stated assumptions, to be equivalent to the simultaneous satisfaction of the Linear Independence Constraint Qualification (LICQ) and Second-Order Sufficient Condition (SOSC). This characterisation establishes local stability of the structured correction algorithm under these conditions and distinguishes nondegenerate locally optimal KKT solutions from points failing second-order optimality. SM-KKT computes structured primal--dual corrections and applies a discrete sliding reaching law to drive the KKT residual into a prescribed boundary layer in finite time. Four nonlinear benchmarks show recovery of reference constrained optima with KKT residuals below $10^{-6}$, earlier boundary-layer reaching, and favourable KKT accuracy compared with projected primal-dual, augmented-Lagrangian, quadratic-penalty, and log-barrier baselines.

title: Rate-Distortion Theory of Gaussian Mixtures via Posterior Label Sampling
abstract: We study the mean-squared error (MSE) rate-distortion function (RDF) of finite Gaussian mixture models (GMMs) in $\mathbb{R}^d$, for which neither the RDF nor an optimal test channel is known in closed form. It can be sandwiched between the genie-aided conditional RDF $R_{\mathbf{X} | T}(D)$, which can be characterized in closed-form for a GMM, and $R_{\mathbf{X} | T}(D)+I(\mathbf{X};T)$, where $T$ denotes the latent component label. We show that the upper bound can be achieved operationally by the proposed Gibbs-relabelling method (GRM), which conveys a label from the posterior $P_{T|\mathbf{X}}$ through \textit{channel simulation} at rate $I(\mathbf{X};T)$, followed by vector quantization of the resulting exactly Gaussian conditional sources by reverse water-filling. Using the Shannon lower bound (SLB), we prove that GRM attains the SLB, and hence the RDF, of a general finite mixture if and only if every component attains its own SLB. For a GMM this holds throughout the fully active interval $D/d<\min_{k,m}\lambda_{k,m}$, where $\lambda_{k,m}$ are the eigenvalues of the component covariances, and for scalar GMMs the condition is also necessary. Since GRM cannot operate below the label cost $I(\mathbf{X};T)$, we propose a complementary stochastic scalar quantization (SSQ) scheme for low rates, which simulates an $M$-ary reconstruction index. We show that at low rates SSQ with $M\geq 2$ matches the Shannon RDF to first order: $R(D_{\max}-\delta)=\delta/(2\tau^2)+o(\delta)$, where $\tau^2$ is a directional sub-Gaussian proxy of the mixture, and quantify the price of a finite codebook through a strict rate gap at high rates and a distortion floor whose joint scaling in $M$ and number of mixture components is characterized. Numerical results illustrate both regimes and the finite-blocklength cost of channel simulation.

title: Topological Classification of Univariate Sparse Polynomials via Tropical Geometry
abstract: We give the topological classification of some simplest univariate complex fewnomials, and find tropical fans of the fewnomial strata with each topological type. Specifically, for the support $ A=\{d,d+1,d+2,d+3,d+4\},\quad d\geq3, $ we classify the topological equivalence classes of polynomials having two critical values of ramification type $(2,2)$. There is one class for odd $d$ and two classes for even $d$. We describe the branches at infinity of the corresponding one-dimensional stratum using Newton polytopes of certain complete intersection representations of the sought strata, and determine their tropicalizations. The combinatorial types of the obtained tropical polynomials distinguishes all three kinds of topological equivalence classes. These computations suggest a correspondence between topological equivalence classes of polynomials and combinatorial types of tropicalizations of their branches at infinity, as well as a possible periodicity phenomenon under translations of the support.

title: K_1 of matroids
abstract: Using the geometric realization spectral sequence and the Serre spectral sequence, we compute $K_1(\operatorname{Mat}_*)$, the first K-theory group of the proto-exact category of pointed matroids, answering a question of Jun, Sistko and Wright.

title: Rank-based Model Average Estimator for Average Treatment Effects
abstract: Model averaging emerges as an attractive ensemble technique that strategically synthesizes all available information from potential candidate models to enhance estimation accuracy. Despite of having been widely practiced in various areas in biostatistics and economics, its application to causal inference is rather limited. We propose to estimate the average treatment effect (ATE) by forming the weighted combination of the robust rank-based estimators obtained from a series of candidate models, where the model weights, selected via the growing window cross-validation, dynamically adjust the importance of candidate models. The proposed robust rank-based model averaging ({\sf RRMA}) is not only robust to handle potential outliers and heavy-tailed error distributions but also capable to reduce the risk of model mis-specification and enhance the flexibility and the accuracy of estimation. Theoretically, we establish the desirable asymptotic properties of {\sf RRMA}, including the asymptotic optimality, consistency and asymptotic distribution. Moreover, motivated by the asymptotic distribution of {\sf RRMA}, an easy-to-implement confidence interval is also developed for the ATE. Simulation experiments and an empirical application demonstrate the superiority of {\sf RRMA} over existing competitors in estimation accuracy, coverage probabilities and widths of confidence intervals.

title: The Goldbach exceptional set: an exponent 7/12 and conditional refinement
abstract: Let \(E(X)\) count the even integers between \(4\) and \(X\) that are not sums of two primes. We combine Pintz's explicit formula for the major arcs with the exponential-sum estimate of Maynard, Pandey, and Radziwi{\l}{\l} to prove \(E(X)\ll_\varepsilon X^{7/12+\varepsilon}\) whenever all Dirichlet \(L\)-functions have a common fixed zero-free half-plane \(\Rea s>\theta_0\), with \(\theta_0<1\). The uniform \(7/8\) theorem reported in the OpenAI mathematics release supplies this input. Under the stronger hypothesis that every nontrivial Dirichlet zero has real part at most \(\theta\), where \(1/2\leq\theta\leq2/3\), we prove \[ E(X)\ll_{\theta,\varepsilon}X^{g(\theta)+\varepsilon}, \qquad g(\theta)=\frac{\theta(5-4\theta)}{2(2-\theta)}. \] Thus every fixed \(\theta<2/3\) gives an exponent strictly below \(7/12\). The latter argument uses a classical fixed-modulus zero-density estimate and is independent of the new exponential-sum theorem.

title: Walk-on-Ambient-Patch: Solver-Adapted Isometric Embeddings for Projected Walk on Spheres
abstract: Projected Walk on Spheres (PWoS) solves surface PDEs through ambient sampling and closest-point projection, but tightly folded embeddings can force short steps or ambiguous projections despite simple intrinsic geometry. We introduce Walk-on-Ambient-Patch (WoAP), which treats the embedding as a solver variable. Edge-isometry constraints and tangent-point repulsion separate intrinsically distant regions, optionally in higher codimension; patch states track residual projection branches without introducing PDE boundaries. We analyze the resulting geometry--sampling tradeoff: additional dimensions provide separation freedom but reduce uniform tangent progress, while strong tangent-biased proposals incur large importance-weight moments. Folded-surface experiments demonstrate reduced projection conflicts, a separate hard-constraint pilot verifies metric preservation, and an internal fixed-RMSE comparison favors higher dimensions at stricter accuracy targets. Together, these results motivate choosing the embedding and projection state jointly with the stochastic solver.

title: Synergistic Learning in Domain Adaptation with a Known Link: A Minimax Understanding
abstract: When can combining source and target data yield much better performance than using either alone? From a minimax viewpoint, writing $R(n,n_T)$ for the minimax risk from $n$ source and $n_T$ target observations, we ask when $R(n,n_T)$ decays strictly faster than both $R(n,0)$ and $R(0,n_T)$. We call this the Synergistic Learning Phenomenon (SLP) and quantify it by the Synergistic Advantage Ratio $\mathrm{SAR}=\min(R(n,0),R(0,n_T))/R(n,n_T)$. We study domain adaptation with a known link: source regression $f$, target regression $g=\mathcal{A}f$ for a known operator $\mathcal{A}$, and possibly different designs. Three links---identity, integration, and differentiation---and the density ratio $\rho=h_T/h_S$ determine whether synergy is possible, at what rate, and in which sample-size window. For the identity link (covariate shift) with a Beta$(a,1)$ source and uniform target, a known necessary condition for SLP is $a\geq2+1/(2\beta)$, where $\beta$ is the smoothness of $f$ (Result I). An integral link $g(x)=\int_0^xf(t)\,dt$ can yield the joint rate $(nn_T)^{-1/2}$ even for a bounded ratio (Result II), and under a Beta$(a,1)$ source has a phase diagram with cuts at $a=2$ and $a=3$: integral SLP for $1<a<2$, an extra level-split rate $n_T^{-1}$ for $2<a<3$, and covariate-shift-type spatial SLP for $a>3$ (Result III). A derivative link $g=\dot f$ synergizes only under a stronger singularity (Result IV), giving a sharp integration--differentiation asymmetry under a bounded ratio. Across all three links, synergy arises from role separation: each dataset resolves a distinct bottleneck associated with the link and designs. We characterize the sample-size windows for synergy and how SAR varies with $n$ and $n_T$. Simulations support the predicted phase structure, and a mirrored integration--differentiation analysis of real vehicle and smartphone signals illustrates the asymmetry.

title: Explicit Bounds for Restricted Invertibility with Prescribed Group Cardinalities
abstract: We prove an explicit lower spectral bound for independent random vectors with prescribed group multiplicities. Let $v_{ij}\in\mathbb C^d$, $1\le i\le l$, $1\le j\le k_i$, be independent random vectors with finite support and $\mathbb E v_{ij}v_{ij}^*=A_i$, where $\sum_{i=1}^l A_i=I_d$ and $\operatorname{Tr}(A_i)\ge\epsilon$. Set $k=\max_i k_i$, $n=\max_i\operatorname{rank}(A_i)$, and $K=\sum_{i=1}^l k_i$. If $n>(6+4\sqrt2)k$ and $2\sqrt{nk}-k<\epsilon\le n/2$, then, with positive probability, \[ \lambda_K\left(\sum_{i=1}^l\sum_{j=1}^{k_i}v_{ij}v_{ij}^*\right) \ge n-(\sqrt{k}+\sqrt{n-\epsilon})^2. \] As a consequence, we obtain a restricted invertibility result selecting exactly $k_i$ vectors from the $i$th group of a Parseval frame. The proof combines interlacing families, a reciprocal transformation of mixed characteristic polynomials, and a multivariate barrier estimate that accommodates repeated differentiation in the same variable.

title: Homogenization of an optimal control problem for a Navier-Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard system in a 3D perforated domain
abstract: We study the homogenization of an optimal control problem governed by a Navier-Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard system in a periodically perforated three-dimensional domain. The obstacles are Lipschitz sets of size $\varepsilon^\alpha$, $\alpha>3$, where $\varepsilon$ is the period. The fluid satisfies the no-slip condition on the outer boundary and the free-slip condition on the obstacles, the phase-field equation contains a source term, and the convective term carries a pore-scale Reynolds number that tends to zero as $\varepsilon\to0$. The control is a distributed body force, and the cost functional tracks the velocity in $L^2$ and the order parameter in $H^1$. Since uniqueness of weak solutions of the state system is not known for fixed $\varepsilon$, the control-to-state relation is multivalued, and we pose the microscopic problems over control-state pairs. We prove the existence of microscopic optimal pairs and the sequential $\Gamma$-convergence of the cost functionals to the cost functional of a control problem governed by the unsteady Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard system on the full domain. As a consequence, the optimal values converge, every cluster point of microscopic optimal pairs is optimal for the homogenized problem, and the optimal controls converge strongly along the corresponding subsequences. The $\liminf$ inequality follows from the homogenization of the state system, including the strong convergence of the gradients of the order parameter. Only the recovery sequence requires uniqueness of weak solutions of the homogenized system, which we prove when the outer boundary is of class $C^{2,1}$.
comments: 33 pages, 1 figure. We welcome comments and suggestions

title: Bloch torsion and modular combinations of Nahm sums
abstract: We construct a positive-definite symmetric integral $12\times12$ matrix $A$ such that, for every solution $Q$ of Nahm's equations $1-Q=Q^A$ with $Q_i\ne0,1$ for all $i$, the associated element $\sum_i[Q_i]$ is torsion in the Bloch group of $\mathbb{Q}(Q_1,\ldots,Q_{12})$. However, the Nahm sum $F_{A,B,C}(\tau)$ is nonmodular for every $B\in\mathbb{Q}^{12}$ and $C\in\mathbb{Q}$. Thus the torsion condition for all solutions in Nahm's conjecture is not sufficient for the existence of a modular Nahm sum.

title: Global solutions to the compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations in the half-space
abstract: We study the initial boundary value problem for the compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations without damping in the three-dimensional half-space. The velocity satisfies the no-slip boundary condition, and the electric potential satisfies the homogeneous Neumann boundary condition. For small perturbations of a constant state in $H^3$, with a small initial electric field in $L^2$, we establish global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions. The uniform estimates combine density dissipation, tangential and normal derivative estimates, and a modified energy that accounts for the electric boundary contribution through the Helmholtz projection. We also prove algebraic decay under an additional low-frequency assumption on the initial data. If the density perturbation, velocity and electric field have finite tangential negative Sobolev norms of order $-s$, where $1/2\leq s<1$, then the solution decays at the rate $(1+t)^{-s/2}$ in the full energy norm. The decay estimate follows from the formulation in terms of the momentum $\rho u$, uniform negative-order estimates and interpolation with the dissipation.

title: The Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture after OpenAI
abstract: We provide a simplified and more human-friendly version of the proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture recently given by OpenAI. No originality is claimed.

title: Topological extensions of elementary measurable spaces
abstract: An elementary space is a pair $(X, \mathcal A)$, where $\mathcal A$ is an algebra of subsets of $X$. Every elementary space $(X, \mathcal A)$ is naturally a topological space when equipped with the topology $\tau_{\mathcal A}$ generated by $\mathcal A$. Elementary mappings on elementary spaces are defined in a manner analogous to measurable mappings on measurable spaces. In addition, the notion of an {\it extension} of an elementary space is introduced. Let $M(X, \mathcal A)$, denote the ring of all real-valued elementary functions on $(X, \mathcal A)$. In this article, we study the ring $M(X, \mathcal A)$ and extensions of an elementary space. We show that, for any elementary space $(X, \mathcal A)$, there exists a unique compact elementary extension $(\beta_{\mathcal A}X, \bar{\mathcal A})$ of $X$, analogous to the Stone-$\check C$ech compactification, which contains every other extension of $X$. This extension has the property that every elementary map from $X$ into any compact topological space extends continuously to $\beta_{\mathcal A}X$. Next, we show that $\beta_{\mathcal A}X$ contains a realcompact extension $(\upsilon_{\mathcal A}X, \bar{\mathcal A}_R)$ of $X$, such that every elementary map from $X$ into any realcompact topological space extends continuously to $\upsilon_{\mathcal A}X$. Moreover, $\upsilon_{\mathcal A}X$ is the smallest realcompact extension of $X$ and $(X, \mathcal A)$ is realcompact if and only if $X=\upsilon_{\mathcal A}X$. Also, we see that, every metric space equipped with the $\sigma$-algebra of all Borel sets is realcompact. Finally, we observe that the maximal ring of quotients of $M(X, \mathcal A)$ is the direct limit of locally constant (continuous) functions on dense open subsets of $(X, \tau_{\mathcal A})$. Some questions raised in the literature are also answered.

title: Negative Sobolev regularity and optimal decay for the fractional Navier--Stokes--Poisson system
abstract: We study the Cauchy problem in $\R^{3}$ for the repulsive compressible Navier-Stokes-Riesz system with Riesz exponent $0<s<1$ and viscosity $0<\varepsilon\leq1$, where the Riesz interaction $\nabla(-\Delta)^{-s}(\rho-\bar{\rho})$ is a generalization of the Coulomb interaction for electrons. For small perturbations of a constant equilibrium, with the solenoidal component of the initial velocity of order $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon)$, we prove the global existence and uniqueness of smooth solutions. We derive time-decay estimates in $L^{2}$ norms and $L^{\infty}$ norms that capture both uniform-in-$\varepsilon$ dispersive behavior and viscosity-dependent dissipation. We further establish a global-in-time inviscid limit to the irrotational global solution of the compressible Euler-Riesz system whose initial data consist of the same density and the curl-free component of the velocity, with an explicit convergence rate in $W^{k,p}$ norms. The proof combines viscosity-adapted dispersive estimates, normal-form analysis and nonlinear energy estimates with control of both negative and positive Sobolev norms.

title: The CR Nirenberg Problem, Part II: Existence and Topological Degree
abstract: This paper is a continuation of Part~I \cite{QTWPartI}, where blow-up analysis and compactness results for the CR Nirenberg problem were established. We prove some existence and degree results for the CR Nirenberg problem on the standard sphere. More precisely, we first prove existence results under antipodal and, more generally, finite-group symmetries. Without symmetry, we derive a Leray--Schauder degree formula under natural flatness conditions, yielding existence results for positive prescribed curvatures with certain homogeneous expansions at critical points. We also obtain Aubin-type inequalities under a vanishing first-moment condition, uniformly near the critical exponent.

title: Beyond Amoeba Boundaries
abstract: We construct smooth plane curves whose logarithmic contours are smooth and embedded but strictly larger than their amoeba boundaries. The examples include connected irreducible curves, disconnected unions of nonlinear components with two-dimensional amoebas, nested families with arbitrarily many components, and a uniform construction realizing every positive genus. Exact critical-locus calculations distinguish the boundary-producing folds from compact or noncompact contour branches lying in the amoeba interior. These constructions show that smoothness of the complete contour does not force contour--boundary equality and that internal critical-value branches persist under monomial transformations, controlled perturbations, and finite monomial coverings.21 pages, 14 figures
comments: 21 pages, 14 figures, all comments are welcome

title: Beyond Harnack Amoeba Boundaries
abstract: We construct smooth irreducible plane curves whose complete amoeba contour is a smooth embedded curve equal to the amoeba boundary, although the curves are not torically equivalent to simple Harnack curves. Finite monomial coverings yield explicit infinite families with higher logarithmic multiplicity and nonmaximal normalized amoeba area. We classify the Newton polygons admitting such covering constructions through their exponent lattices, give an exact connectedness criterion in terms of monodromy, and treat primitive polygons by a separate phase-sensitive construction. Exact triangular and trapezoidal families are complemented by positive-genus investigations exhibiting bounded amoeba-complement components. These results show that a perfectly exposed amoeba contour does not determine the real structure, logarithmic sheet number, or Harnack type of the underlying curve.
comments: 22 pages, 10 figures, all comments are welcome

title: Diagonal recovery from noisy Fourier--Hermite coefficients: exact orders of the error
abstract: We consider the recovery of functions of the weighted Wiener classes $W_s^\mu$ from perturbed Fourier--Hermite coefficients in the metric of $L_\infty(\mathbb R)$. For the summation methods of the class $\mathcal S^\theta$ we find error estimates on $W_s^\mu$. The estimates take into account the behaviour of the Hermite functions both in the oscillatory region and near the turning point: the maxima of functions with different indices are attained at different points, and the supremum of a sum over a block of indices is substantially smaller than the sum of the suprema. Owing to this, in particular, we establish a common lower bound for all finite diagonal methods; for $s\ne4/3$ and $p\ne4/3$ it matches the upper bound and gives the exact order of the error in this class, while at the critical points the gap between the bounds does not exceed $(\log(e/\delta))^{1/4}$ up to a constant. If, in addition, $s>4/3$ or $p<4/3$, then this order is also optimal among all recovery operators that use the whole sequence of data.

title: Maximum degree for random geometric graphs in the connectivity regime and beyond
abstract: A random geometric graph is a random graph model whose vertex set is a binomial point process, where two vertices are connected by an edge if each lies within the ball of radius $r$ centered at the other. In this paper, we investigate the asymptotic fluctuations of the threshold radius required for the maximum degree of the graph to reach a target value. Assuming this target value grows with the number of vertices $n$ at an order of at least $\log n$ but strictly less than $(\log n)^d$, we show that these fluctuations follow a Gumbel distribution. We also investigate the spatial configurations of vertices with extremely large degrees, and show that the point process marked by their degrees converges in distribution to a Poisson point process.

title: Binary Codes Correcting Multiple Edits via Polynomial Hashing and Entropy Recycling
abstract: Codes in the Levenshtein metric that can correct multiple edits (including deletions, insertions, and substitutions) have attracted a lot of attention recently owing to their application in DNA-based storage and racetrack memories. In this work, we present new techniques for designing explicit binary codes of length $n$ that correct $t$ edits with at most $(2t+1)\log n+O_t(\log\log n)$ bits of redundancy. We first propose to use a polynomial hash to construct a systematic code that corrects $t$ edits with $(4t+2)\log n+O_t(\log\log n)$ bits of redundancy. Then we observe that there are many polynomial hashes like this, some are good, some are bad. So, we propose the second technique, called entropy recycling, to use the indices of good hashes to carry information. As a consequence, we obtain a partial-systematic code of length $n$ that corrects $t$ edits with at most $(2t+1)\log n+O_t(\log\log n)$ bits of redundancy. Finally, we provide deterministic polynomial-time encoding and decoding algorithms for our code.

title: Weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for noncommutative rough homogeneous singular integrals
abstract: We establish the weak type \((1,1)\) endpoint estimate for operator-valued rough homogeneous singular integrals with kernels satisfying the classical \(L\log L\) integrability and cancellation conditions. This extends Seeger's endpoint theorem [{J. Amer. Math. Soc.} \textbf{9} (1996)] to the noncommutative setting. A key ingredient is an off-diagonal analysis that controls interactions between different kernel scales and avoids an additional logarithmic loss.

title: Covering powers of cycles with equivalence subgraphs
abstract: Let $C_n^k$ denote the $k$th power of the cycle $C_n$. The equivalence covering number $\operatorname{eq}(G)$, studied by Alon, is the minimum number of equivalence subgraphs needed to cover all edges of $G$. King conjectured that $\operatorname{eq}(C_n^k)=\Omega(k)$ for sufficiently large $n$ relative to $k$. We study $\operatorname{eq}(C_n^k)$ and prove that, for every $n \geq 2k + 2$, we have $1 + \lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil \leq \operatorname{eq}(C_n^k) \leq 1 + 2\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil$. We further show that, whenever $n\ge(k+1)\max\{41,5\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil\}$, \begin{equation*} \operatorname{eq}(C_n^k)\in\left\{1+\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil,\,2+\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil\right\}. \end{equation*} Moreover, for every integer $n\ge \max\{2k+2,k^2(k+2)\}$, the following exact values hold in the indicated cases: \begin{equation*} \operatorname{eq}(C_n^k)=\begin{cases} 1+\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil, & k+1\neq2^{\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil} \text{ or }(k+1)\mid n,\\[3pt] 2+\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil, & k+1=2^{\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil} \text{ and }2\nmid n. \end{cases} \end{equation*}

title: On Mok's uniqueness problem of holomorphic isometries from complex unit balls of maximal dimension into classical domains
abstract: We prove that every holomorphic isometric embedding, with respect to the Bergman metrics, from a complex unit ball of maximal dimension into irreducible classical bounded symmetric domain of rank at least two that is not biholomorphic to a Type IV domain is equivalent to Mok's embedding. This completely resolves a problem of Mok.

title: Bistatic Delay-Doppler Sensing for 3D Target Localization in Distributed Wi-Fi Systems
abstract: This paper investigates how bistatic delay information improves the observability and localization performance of 3D moving targets in distributed Wi-Fi sensing. Motivated by emerging IEEE 802.11bf WLAN sensing, we consider one transmitter, multiple distributed receivers, and a single target with unknown position and velocity. We compare Doppler-only sensing with delay-Doppler sensing, in which delay-capable receivers provide additional bistatic path-length information for target localization. We derive the Fisher information matrix (FIM) and the position equivalent FIM (EFIM) for both sensing formulations. The resulting observability analysis shows that Doppler-only localization generically requires six receivers, whereas delay-Doppler localization can become locally identifiable with three receivers under non-degenerate geometry. We further study mixed receiver architectures in which only a subset of receivers provides delay estimates. Simulations with Wi-Fi-like bandwidths confirm the transition and quantify the roles of bandwidth, Doppler noise, receiver geometry, and delay-capable receiver availability.
comments: 6 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables. Accepted for presentation at the 1st IEEE Conference on Integrated Sensing and Communications (ISAC), Lisbon, Portugal, November 2026

title: A trace lower bound for totally positive units in $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)^+$ and its application to fusion category
abstract: Let $p = 4q + 1$ be a prime integer, where $q$ is an odd prime. Let $L = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)^+$ denote the maximal totally real subfield of the $p$-th cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)$. In this paper, we prove that if $U_L^+=U_L^2$ (i.e., every totally positive unit is a square in $L$), then for any non-trivial subfield $K \subseteq L$ and any non-trivial totally positive unit $\varepsilon \in U_K^+$, the absolute trace satisfies the sharp lower bound $\Tr_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(\varepsilon) \ge p - 4$. As an application, we show that a spherical fusion category $\C$ with global dimension $\dim(\mathcal{C})=p=4q+1$ is pointed, where $2$ is a primitive root modulo $q$, or $p=4q+1<2^{22}$ and $p\neq 29$.

title: New topological phase transitions in $\kappa$-deformed $\phi^4$ lattice models
abstract: This paper explores topological phase transitions in the momentum space of the $\kappa$-deformed $\phi^4$ lattice model within the mean-field approximation. We show that the double-well structure of the momentum space gives rise to degenerate momentum states at high energies and that this change is marked by a phase transition. We investigate this transition using both numerical and analytical methods, with the analytical approach based primarily on singularity theory. Our numerical analysis shows that the energy at which the topological phase transition occurs is related to the noncommutative parameter by the simple power law $E \sim 1/\alpha^{4}$. By mapping the constant-energy-level surface to the $A_{3}$ singularity, we obtain the same result analytically. We also present results unique to noncommutative systems, showing that the fraction of particles in degenerate momentum states has a nonzero commutative limit. As a nonperturbative effect, this result provides a testable prediction for the existence of noncommutative spacetime.

title: Weighted Frames and the Douglas-Foias problem
abstract: Let $\mathbf{T}=(T_1,\ldots,T_n)$ be a commuting tuple of bounded linear operators on a separable Hilbert space $\mathcal{K}$, and let $\{a_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\mathbb{Z}_+^n}$ be strictly positive weights. Under mild assumptions on the weights, we characterize the weighted frame vectors and weighted Parseval frame vectors, that is, those vectors $\xi$ for which $\{a_\alpha \mathbf{T}^\alpha\xi\}_{\alpha\in\mathbb{Z}_+^n}$ is a frame or a Parseval frame. We reduce the problem to characterizing surjective module maps from the reproducing analytic Hilbert module associated with the weights onto the module $\mathcal{K}$, equipped with the module structure defined by $\mathbf{T}$. It is shown that weighted Parseval frame vectors differ by a unimodular scalar whenever they exist. If the kernel defined by the weights has the complete Nevanlinna--Pick property, then any two associated weighted frame vectors are similar whenever they exist. We also focus on the case of the Hardy kernel on the polydisc, that is, the case $a_\alpha=1$ for all $\alpha\in\mathbb{Z}^n_+$. This is related to the famous Douglas--Foias problem: whether two similar quotient modules of the Hardy spaces $H^2(\mathbb{D}^n)~(n>1)$ are equal. Our result shows that the answer is negative. This leads to the conclusion that frame vectors for representations of $\mathbb{Z}_+^n$ $(n>1)$ may fail to be similar. It means that, for the case $a_\alpha=1$, there exists a tuple $\mathbf{T}=(T_1,\dots,T_n)$ with $n>1$ on $\mathcal{K}$ and two distinct frame vectors for $\mathbf{T}$ which are not similar.

title: Post-critically finite polynomials in characteristic $p$
abstract: It follows from the compactness of the connectedness locus that the locus of PCF polynomials in the moduli space of polynomials of degree d (at least 2) over the complex number is a countable union of zero-dimensional subvarieties. Over fields of characteristic p the analogous claim is certainly false, so it is natural to ask how large the components of the PCF locus can be. We show that the components of the PCF locus in the moduli space of polynomials of degree d over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0 have dimension at most d/p and that this bound is sharp, in the strong sense that for every p and d there are infinitely many distinct PCF components whose dimension is the greatest integer no greater than this bound (except in the case $p=d=2$).

title: Transport Polynomial Exactness for Direct ALE-DG Methods with Nonsmooth mesh motion: A Conservative Coefficient-Evolution Framework
abstract: High-order direct arbitrary Lagrangian--Eulerian discontinuous Galerkin (ALE-DG) methods can suffer severe order reduction under nonsmooth mesh motion despite satisfying the geometric conservation law (GCL). To address this limitation, we propose a new ALE-DG framework applicable to moving triangular and quadrilateral meshes. This framework successfully overcomes the uniform Lipschitz constraint inherent in existing direct ALE-DG methods, retaining high-order accuracy even when the mesh-velocity gradients are unbounded. This capability is driven by transport polynomial exactness (TPE($k$)), which is a structural property stronger than the GCL. TPE($k$) ensures the exact transport of polynomials of degree at most $k$ under arbitrary mesh motion. To incorporate TPE($k$) into a direct ALE-DG method, we introduce a coefficient-evolution (CE) formulation. Reconciling strict local conservation, an indispensable requirement for accurate shock capturing, with the preservation of the TPE(\(k\)) property constitutes the principal technical challenge. We resolve this by evolving the coefficients using the third-order strong-stability-preserving Runge--Kutta method, paired with a conservative correction executed via Simpson's rule integration. Crucially, this correction strictly vanishes for exactly transported quadratic polynomials, thereby ensuring that our third-order scheme rigorously satisfies the TPE($2$) property. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed scheme retains third-order accuracy when the discrete mesh-velocity Lipschitz estimate grows as $\mathcal O(h^{-1})$, whereas a representative existing direct ALE-DG scheme exhibits order reduction under the same mesh motion. Tests with discontinuous solutions further demonstrate robust and high-resolution performance under random and Lagrangian mesh motions.

title: Continuum-many discontinuous actions of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{Q})$ on manifolds
abstract: For any $n\geq 1$, we construct a continuum of non-conjugate actions by homeomorphisms of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{Q})$ on the $n$-sphere $S^{n}$ that do not extend to a continuous action of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{R})$. We do this by adapting a blow-up construction of Bowden and Mann. We motivate studying these actions and note down some related observations.

title: Non-Stationary Quantum Systems Associated with Stationary Scattering in One Dimension
abstract: Stationary scattering admits a dynamical formulation in which the scattering data are extracted from the evolution operator for an effective non-stationary and non-unitary quantum system. This provides a mathematical method of solving scattering problems. We consider the possibility of realizing such a quantum system and relating the scattering information to outcomes of quantum measurements performed on it. To this end, we examine stationary scattering problems in one dimension where the scattering data consist of reflection and transmission amplitudes and the corresponding effective quantum system is a non-unitary two-level system. The states of this system identify points in a Bloch sphere $S^2$ and their evolution yields trajectories in $S^2$. Quantum measurements turn out to be capable of providing information about the reflection amplitudes. We identify configurations displaying reflectionlessness with situations where one or both of the poles of $S^2$ undergo cyclic evolutions. Spectral singularities and coherent perfect absorption correspond to dynamical spin flips which map one of the poles of $S^2$ to the other.

title: Exact Sampling Under Campbell Cost via R\'enyi Channel Simulation Divergence
abstract: We study the communication cost of exact sampling under Campbell's exponential coding criterion. Given a target distribution $P$ and a proposal distribution $Q$, the sender and receiver share i.i.d. $Q$-distributed samples, and the sender communicates an index so that the selected sample has distribution exactly $P$. We introduce a new information measure R\'enyi channel simulation divergence $R_\alpha(P\Vert Q)$, a R\'enyi generalization of the channel simulation divergence. We then show that it lower bounds the Campbell cost of every exact sampler and is achievable, via a new layered sampling scheme, within an additive constant depending only on the Campbell parameter. This yields a tighter one-shot characterization than previous bounds based on R\'enyi divergences of different orders. For i.i.d. product distributions, under suitable non-degeneracy and moment conditions, we further show that the gap beyond the leading R\'enyi-divergence term is $\frac{1}{2}\log n+O(1)$.

title: Geodesic Models for Loop Spaces on Riemannian Manifolds
abstract: A topological group, defined in terms of ``composable minimal geodesics'' is constructed and shown to be homotopy equivalent to the pointed loop space of a path-connected, simply connected Riemannian manifold $M$ of positive convexity radius. This construction is analogous to John Milnor's free group model for the pointed loop space of a connected simplicial complex. Related models built from composable minimal geodesics are also obtained for the free loop space of $M$ and for the space of maps from any finite two-dimensional CW-complex into $M$.
comments: 27 pages, to appear in Fields Institute Communications

title: The entry-exit function and nilpotent corrections in multidimensional slow-fast systems
abstract: We study multidimensional entry-exit phenomena in slow-fast systems whose fast linearization contains a nilpotent component. We show that the classical spectral balance still determines the exit point as $\varepsilon \to 0$, however the nilpotent component induces an algebraic amplification invisible to the spectrum, producing a $\varepsilon|\log\varepsilon|$-shift of the exit point for $0 <\varepsilon \ll 1$. We further extend the analysis to systems with several spectral branches and show that mode dominance follows a hierarchical, lexicographic selection principle: accumulated spectral growth determines the leading order, while the nilpotent component resolves degeneracies between spectrally equivalent modes.

title: Blow-down and immediate onset of positivity in the Neumann problem for (super-)fast diffusion equations
abstract: For the degenerate parabolic equation $u_t=\nabla\cdot (u^{m-1}\nabla u)$, the homogeneous Neumann problem in smoothly bounded domains $\Omega\subset {\mathbb{R}}^n$ is considered in the (super-fast) diffusion range when $m\in (-\infty,1)$. Upper and lower estimates for solutions are inferred by means of two Moser-type iterations, and optimality properties of these bounds are derived using comparison arguments. On the basis of the accordingly obtained information on regularization into spaces of bounded and uniformly positive functions, a result on global solvability in an associated initial-boundary value problem is achieved for all nonnegative and nontrivial initial data belonging to $L^1(\Omega) \cap \bigcup_{s>n(1-m)/2} L^s(\Omega)$.

title: Coprime pairs with equal sum of divisors, assuming smooth shifted primes
abstract: Let $h(x)$ be the number of pairs $1\le a<b<x$ with $\gcd(a,b)=1$ and $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)$. Erd\H{o}s Problem #824 asks whether $h(x)>x^{2-o(1)}$. By an argument of Pollack and Pomerance, this follows if for every fixed $\delta>0$ there are $y^{1-o(1)}$ primes $p\le5y$ with $p+1$ free of prime factors exceeding $y^\delta$. We write this implication out with explicit parameters and formalize it in Lean 4. We then check that the argument of the recent OpenAI preprint "Weighted dilation graphs, smooth shifted primes and totient fibers", which claims the corresponding statement for $p-1$, applies to $p+1$ after a change of sign in two of its sections. Consequently $h(x)=x^{2-o(1)}$, conditionally on the correctness of that preprint, which has not been refereed and whose main new estimates we have not independently verified.
comments: 4 pages. Lean 4 formalization of the conditional lower bound available at https://github.com/daizisheng/erdos-824

title: A greedy double-block nonlinear Bregman-Kaczmarz method for nonlinear equations
abstract: In this paper, we develop a greedy double-block nonlinear Bregman-Kaczmarz method to efficiently find sparse solutions of nonlinear equations. The theoretical convergence rate of the proposed method is established under certain assumptions. Numerical experiments illustrate the competitive performance and superiority of the proposed method.

title: Bipartite edge frustration of nut graphs: proofs and constructions
abstract: The bipartite edge frustration of a graph $G$, $\varphi(G)$, is the minimum number of edges that must be removed from $G$ to obtain a graph that is bipartite. Core graphs are singular graphs on $2$ or more vertices, for which the kernel of the adjacency matrix contains a full eigenvector. A nut graph is a core graph of nullity one. Nut graphs $G$ are non-bipartite. It is proved here that $\varphi(G) \geq 2$ if $G$ is a nut graph, i.e. every nut graph requires deletion of at least two edges to produce a bipartite graph. In addition, we give a constructive proof that for every integer $k \geq 2$ there exist infinitely many chemical nut graphs $G$ with $\varphi(G) = k$. Furthermore, for $3 \leq d \leq 8$, the values $k$, for which a $d$-regular nut graph $G$ with $\varphi(G) = k$ exists, are characterised. It is shown here that for every integer $k \geq 2$ there exist infinitely many cubic polyhedral nut graphs $G$ with $\varphi(G) = k$. Two ways of producing larger nut graphs from smaller are described: the cut and frustration constructions. One straightforward consequence is that total double subdivision of a nut graph (i.e. simultaneous insertion of two degree-$2$ vertices into every edge) yields a nut graph.

title: Teams, Truthmakers, Translations
abstract: We present a faithful translation from Aloni's logic BSL into a classical modal logic over semilattices combining ideas from earlier modal translations of truthmaker semantics with algebraic representation theory. We show how our method can also be made to work for other current hyperintensional logics. Finally, we place our results in a broader setting of translating hyperintensional logics into classical modal ones, and discuss applications and new challenges that arise for both areas of philosophical logic connected in this way.

title: **Winding number forces universal synchronisation**
abstract: We prove that two completely different oscillators synchronise through arbitrarily weak reciprocal impulses. Any two planar oscillators with hyperbolic attracting limit cycles and equal natural periods lock stably one-to-one under translation impulses with generic directions and a suitable range of positive strength ratios, whatever their vector fields, limit cycles and transverse contraction rates. The mechanism is topological: the winding of the asymptotic phase gradient forces phase advances and delays, and the relative winding number of an effective impulse field gives lower bounds on attracting and unstable locked states. Equal periods are not essential: locking persists under small nonzero mismatches, with persistence and loss governed by a shifted phase balance. The analysis covers the full state-dependent impulsive dynamics, including transverse stability. Nearly simultaneous emissions may make the return discontinuous; under an explicit regularity condition the global return has a normally attracting Lipschitz invariant circle with topologically Morse--Smale dynamics.

title: Total Cohomology of Hilbert schemes of Orbisurfaces I: Reduction to Stacky Loci
abstract: We generalize Nakajima's theory of Hilbert schemes of points on surfaces to Hilbert schemes of points on \textit{orbisurfaces}, and obtain initial factorization based on stratification by stabilizers. While the usual formula is retained for the trivial stabilizer stratum and for those strata of codimension $1$, genuine difficulties arise with stacky points strata. In the local picture of an isolated stacky point, the theory reduce to the study of $\Quot^\bfv[\CC^2/G]$ for a \textit{small} finite subgroup of $GL_2(\CC)$. The generating series for their total cohomology is a geometric correction of the generating series for total cohomology of ordinary smooth surface schemes. In addition, we obtain an action of the Borel-Moore homology of the punctual fibre stacks on the total Hilbert cohomology by virtual correspondences, in analogy with the Fock space description in Nakajima's theory. The punctual fibre stacks are genuinely different from the symmetric stack, and has natural realizations via motivic integration.
comments: 42 pages, comments are welcomed. Will soon be separated into part I and II

title: When do explicit penalties improve flow matching?
abstract: Flow matching can learn structure directly from data, raising the question of when additional constraints improve generation. We study penalties that encode such constraints, with physics-informed flow matching as a motivating example. Satisfying a constraint more closely need not make the generated distribution more accurate. We therefore compare penalised and unpenalised generative modelling through their expected squared $2$-Wasserstein error. Our analysis covers both vector-valued and functional data in a Hilbert-space setting. We first derive geometric criteria that account for constraint violations and the distribution of samples after projection onto the constraint set. We then solve the statistical comparison explicitly for specific velocity-field classes and constraints via flow matching. In this model, penalisation improves accuracy exactly when the reduction in estimation variance outweighs the increase in squared bias. The resulting formula shows how this trade-off depends on sample size, the model class, the noise schedule, and the penalty weight.

title: Notes on Uniform Policy Score Bounds and Lipschitz Continuity for Truncated Gaussian, Product Cauchy, Boltzmann, and Softmax Policies
abstract: We establish uniform score bounds and Lipschitz continuity for truncated Gaussian, Cauchy, Boltzmann, and softmax policies under explicitly stated parameterizations.

title: Sharp conditions for fully nonlinear equations with $(n-1)$-Hessian matrix: Part I. Monge--Amp\`ere case
abstract: We study positive $(n-1)$-convex entire subsolutions of the normalized real $(n-1)$ Monge--Amp\`ere equation $\operatorname{det}^{\frac1n}\bigl(\Delta uI-D^2u\bigr)=f(u)+g(u)|Du|^q$ in $\mathbb R^n$. Under two sets of structural assumptions on the continuous, non-decreasing coefficients $f$ and $g$, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of entire subsolutions when $q<2-\frac1n$. Our results cover the pure-gradient degenerate case $f\equiv0$ with $0<q<1$, the gradient-singular case $q<0$, and the case where $g$ changes sign. For $q=2-\frac1n$, we recover the Keller--Osserman condition for the gradient-independent equation, prove nonexistence when $g$ is eventually positive, and obtain an exponentially weighted condition when $g$ has a nonpositive limit at infinity. This is the first of two companion papers and treats the determinant case.
comments: 44 pages, 0 figures; companion paper to Part II

title: Counting subspaces with prescribed Welch sums
abstract: Let $q=2^n$ with $n=2m+1$ for an integer $m\ge1$, and let ${\mathbb F}_q$ be the finite field with $q$ elements. Let $W_n(x)=x^{2^m+3}$ be the Welch function on ${\mathbb F}_q$. For $1\le k\le n$ and $b\in{\mathbb F}_q$, denote by $N_{n,k}(b)$ the number of $k$-dimensional ${\mathbb F}_2$-subspaces $E$ of $\mathbb F}_q$ such that \[ \sum_{x\in E}W_n(x)=b. \] In this paper, we determine $N_{n,k}(b)$ for all $k$. The only nontrivial case is $k=3$, for which the answer is given in terms of a binary Kloosterman sum. As a consequence, we prove a recent conjecture of Hou and Zhao on the third-order sum-freedom of the Welch function.

title: Sharp conditions for fully nonlinear equations with $(n-1)$-Hessian matrix: Part II. $k$-Hessian case
abstract: We study admissible entire subsolutions and radial boundary blow-up solutions of $S_k^{\frac1k}[\Delta uI-D^2u]=f(u)+g(u)|Du|^q$ for $1\leq k<n$, continuing our study of the determinant case $k=n$ in Part I. Under structural assumptions on the continuous, non-decreasing coefficients $f$ and $g$, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of entire subsolutions when $q<2$. Our results cover the non-Lipschitz case $0<q<1$ with a possibly vanishing zero-order term, the gradient-singular case $q<0$, and sign-changing gradient coefficients. We also characterize finite-radius blow-up of radial solutions and derive two-sided estimates for the blow-up radius, as well as pointwise upper bounds for their profiles in terms of inverse Keller--Osserman functions.
comments: 48 pages, 0 figures; companion paper to Part I

title: Symplectic four-manifolds and hyperbolic $\pi$-orbifolds
abstract: We construct closed symplectic 4-manifolds admitting the structure of hyperbolic $\pi$-orbifold, addressing LeBrun's conjecture. Our simplest example has Euler characteristic $304$, is tessellated by $64$ copies of the right-angled hyperbolic $120$-cell and admits a four-fold branched covering over a product of two surfaces of genus $4$.

title: Poissonian Pair Correlation for Bernoulli Orbits
abstract: Let \(\alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}\), and let \((\xi_n)_{n \ge 1}\) be independent random variables taking the values \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) with equal probability. We study the random walk \[X_n = \xi_1 + \cdots + \xi_n \pmod 1\] and present a deterministic Diophantine condition on \((\alpha, \beta)\) that implies almost sure Poisson pair correlation. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first result providing explicit examples in this framework where the increment measure is purely discrete. The classical Fourier contraction method fails in this setting; a different approach is required. Our proof uses the parabolic geometry of returns to \(1\) and an exact covariance formula for overlapping blocks.

title: Correcting Burst Errors with Applications to DNA-Based Data Storage
abstract: We introduce the problem of permutation burst error-correction, motivated by applications in molecular data storage with nanopore sequencing read platforms. A permutation burst of length $k$ is an error that affects a substring of length $k$ of a string of length $n$ by permuting its entries. Permutation burst errors can be corrected using classical burst error-correcting codes, such as Fire and Reed-Solomon codes. Here, we study how to reduce the redundancy of these classical codes by taking into account that the burst error preserves the weight of the substring. In addition, we further restrict our model to handle cyclic permutation bursts only, which are of independent practical and mathematical interest. Our main results include proving/establishing the following: a) for $k=o(\sqrt{n}),$ the redundancy of any permutation burst error correcting code is at least $\log n-k+\log \binom{2k-2}{k-2}+o(1).$ This result follows from McDiarmid's concentration bound; b) for $k \geq 9$ and $k=o\left(\sqrt{\frac{n}{\log n}}\right)$, the redundancy of any cyclic permutation burst error correcting code is at least $\log n +\log (k(k-1)-56)-\log\,80+o(1).$ c) the asymptotic redundancy upper bounds for the two types of substring errors that are twice the lower bound; d) constructions for both permutation burst and cyclic permutation burst errors that involve Varshamov-Tenegoltz type constraints or represent generalizations and extensions of Fire and other codes. In particular, we exhibit polynomially encodable and decodable codes that can correct cyclic bursts of length $\leq k$ using $\log n + k + 49\log k + O(\log \log k)$ redundant bits.

title: Solutions of $x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=D$ with small $x_3$: a spectral approach
abstract: We count the integral solutions of x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=D weighted by Phi(x_3/M), for M smaller than sqrt(D). Such solutions correspond to binary quadratic forms of discriminant D, and the count becomes a sum, over the geodesics of discriminant D, of a function of their distance to the point i, which we evaluate by the spectral theory of automorphic forms. For square D=n^2 the geodesics run from cusp to cusp, and Hecke theory reduces them to a single geodesic. For every n and both parities of x_3 we obtain an asymptotic formula with error O(n^{1+theta+eps} M^{-1/2}), theta=7/64, using the Kim-Sarnak bound and the large sieve of Deshouillers and Iwaniec; it is non-trivial for M >= n^{71/96+eps}. This improves the range n^{5/6+eps} of the elementary method and confirms the corrected main term of the author's earlier work. For non-square D=f^2 D_0 the geodesics are closed, and a Hecke relation for their traces reduces everything to the fundamental discriminant D_0. For odd D_0 we obtain an error O(D^eps f^{1+theta} D_0^{2/3} M^{-1/2}), using the formulas of Duke-Imamoglu-Toth and Baruch-Mao together with Young's cubic moment. For D = 5 mod 8 this counts all solutions, and the range M >= D^{1/2-1/1332} of Friedlander and Iwaniec improves to M >= D^{4/9+eps}. This paper was written in collaboration with Claude (Opus 5.5, High), an AI model developed by Anthropic.
comments: 27 pages, 2 tables. Written in collaboration with Claude (Opus 5.5, High), an AI model developed by Anthropic; the respective contributions are described in Subsection 1.6. Scripts for the numerical checks of Section 7 are included as ancillary files

title: Sharp Rogers--Shephard Inequalities for R\'enyi Entropy
abstract: We establish sharp weighted Rogers--Shephard inequalities for R\'enyi differential entropy. For independent copies $X,X'$ of a log-concave random vector in $\R^n$, we prove $h_p(aX-bX')\le h_p(X)+n\log(a+b)$ for all $a,b>0$ and $1\le p\le\infty$, where orders $1$ and $\infty$ correspond to Shannon entropy and min-entropy, respectively. The Shannon case settles the entropic Rogers--Shephard conjecture of Madiman and Kontoyiannis and its higher-dimensional formulation. For $1\le p<\infty$, equality holds precisely for invertible affine images of random vectors with independent exponential coordinates. At $p=\infty$, the larger equality class is characterized by possibly extended-valued convex potentials that are positively homogeneous of degree one. For every $0<p<1$, uniform laws on sufficiently high-dimensional simplices violate the unweighted bound. Thus $p=1$ is the critical order for this bound to hold in every dimension. The proof combines weighted convex intersections with an exponential lift to a log-affine probability density. At the Shannon endpoint, this lift yields an exact deficit decomposition with a conditional mutual information term for an additive channel with asymmetric Laplace noise.

title: A Smooth Autonomous Flow with Exponential Mixing on the Three-Torus
abstract: We construct a smooth autonomous divergence-free vector field on $\mathbb{T}^3$ whose flow is exponentially mixing with respect to Lebesgue measure. This answers an open question about smooth autonomous exponential mixing in three dimensions. Starting from an exponentially mixing Anosov suspension flow, we perform surgery near four periodic orbits and show that the resulting manifold is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{T}^3$. The resulting vector field has exactly sixteen hyperbolic equilibria. We also prove a general transfer theorem that preserves exponential mixing under certain singular changes of coordinates.

title: Multivariate stable mixing local limit theorem for intermittent diffeomorphisms and flows
abstract: We prove mixing local limit theorems for dynamical systems in the superdiffusive regime where there is convergence to a multivariate stable law (including the nonstandard domain of the central limit theorem). We apply our results to d-dimensional observables for intermittent maps and solenoids, as well as intermittent semiflows and flows.

title: Adaptive Robust Confidence Sets in High Dimensions
abstract: We study adaptive confidence sets for mean vectors of multivariate Gaussians with identity covariance under Huber contamination when the contamination proportion is unknown. We show that an information-theoretically optimal adaptive confidence set can be constructed by simultaneously quantifying uncertainty across all one-dimensional projections. The resulting confidence set achieves the optimal diameter and reveals a substantial adaptation cost compared with the minimax estimation error. Although statistically optimal, this construction is computationally infeasible. We establish a Statistical Query (SQ) lower bound showing that achieving diameter $O(m^{-1/2})$ requires either exponentially many queries or query tolerance $d^{-\Omega(m)}$. Thus, in contrast to robust mean estimation, adaptation to the unknown contamination proportion incurs both a statistical cost and a computational barrier within the SQ framework. Finally, we give a low-degree moment-matching algorithm that constructs an adaptive confidence set using $d^{O(m)}$ samples and time. Its diameter bound contains an additional $O(m^{-1/2})$ term beyond the information-theoretic rate, matching the dependence on $m$ in the SQ lower bound. Together, these results characterize the statistical limits of adaptive robust confidence sets under Huber contamination and quantify a computational barrier within the SQ framework.

title: Lie Algebras of Locally Finite Derivations over Fields of Positive Characteristic
abstract: Let $F$ be a field of positive characteristic, and let $A$ be a finitely generated commutative associative $F$-algebra. We study Lie subalgebras of $Der \, A$ generated by locally finite derivations. We prove that if all commutators of the generators satisfy a natural local finiteness condition, then the associative subalgebra of $End_{F}\, A$ generated by these derivations is finite-dimensional.

title: Remarks on the disjoint minimal graphs conjecture
abstract: It is known that there can be at most 3 disjoint nontrivial minimal graphs in R^3 with 0 boundary values, and conjectured that there can be at most 2. We explore properties that the graphs would have if there were 3.

title: Fractional symplectic Fourier transforms and their actions on function and distribution spaces
abstract: We consider symplectic analogues of the fractional Fourier transforms and obtain convenient representations in terms of Bargmann transforms and Wigner distributions. We show that they act as homeomorphisms on Schwartz spaces, the space of square integrable functions, the space of tempered distributions, and on Fourier-invariant Gelfand-Shilov spaces and their corresponding distribution spaces. More generally, we establish their homeomorphism properties on a broad class of spaces defined through (Wigner-)Hermite expansions. In addition, we prove that these transforms preserve norms on Schatten-von Neumann symbol classes associated with the Weyl calculus.
comments: 43 pages. This is the first version. A thorough update is expected for the second one

title: Small-speed solitary-wave stability and global well-posedness for a Bessel-regularized Airy equation
abstract: We prove orbital stability of minimizing solitary waves at sufficiently small positive speeds for an Airy equation with a quadratic interaction filtered by a Bessel potential of order one. The stability hypotheses are verified: constrained minimization gives one negative direction, the small-speed KdV limit and operator-norm perturbation of the profile resolvent give a one-dimensional translation kernel, and a differentiable rescaled branch with uniformly bounded derivative gives a positive slope of the quadratic invariant. A conserved Lyapunov functional then proves orbital stability in the three-halves-derivative energy space and the perturbation also gives uniqueness of centered minimizers at small speed.
