The dynamical framework is supplied by a direct Bourgain-space bilinear estimate, local well-posedness in the square-integrable class, unconditional uniqueness from one-quarter derivative onward, and global well-posedness in the half-derivative energy space. For every prescribed positive speed, constrained minimization constructs smooth positive profiles that are symmetric, strictly monotone away from their center, and exponentially localized. At general positive speeds the stability criterion remains conditional on nondegeneracy and the slope condition.

title: On the inverse Goldbach problem
abstract: We establish two quantitative results concerning additive decompositions of the set $\mathbb{P}$ of primes. First, we prove that, if $A,B\subseteq\mathbb N$ have at least two elements and $A+B$ differs from the primes by only finitely many elements, then $$ \frac{\sqrt{x}}{\log x}\ll A(x),B(x) \ll \sqrt{x}. $$ Second, we show that, if $A,B,C\subseteq\mathbb N$ have at least two elements each, then $$ ((A+B+C)\mathbin{\bigtriangleup}\mathbb P)(x) \gg \frac{\sqrt{x}}{(\log x)^2}. $$ An analogous estimate is obtained for sumsets of $k\ge 3$ sets. The proofs use Montgomery's large sieve, Gallagher's larger sieve, a mean-value argument for a certain multiplicative function, and a submultiplicative sumset inequality.

title: Failure of dimension drop for harmonic measure on Ahlfors regular boundaries of dimension close to $1$
abstract: For every $0<s<1$ we construct a compact $s$-Ahlfors regular set $K\subset\mathbb C$ for which harmonic measure of $\mathbb C\setminus K$ with pole at infinity is comparable to $\mathcal H^s|_K$. In particular, there is no dimension drop for any dimension $s<1$. The construction is $N$-adic and based on configurations close to the $N$-th roots of unity. We adjust the positions of the children by small polynomial deformations so that the logarithmic potential of the natural Bernoulli measure becomes constant in the limit. A first-mode correction gives the range $s<2/3$, while corrections of arbitrary finite order yield the full range $0<s<1$.

title: Parabolically induced representations of $GL_n(O_l)$
abstract: Let $\mathcal O$ be the ring of integers of a non-Archimedean local field with uniformizer $\varpi$, and let $\mathcal O_\ell=\mathcal O/\varpi^\ell\mathcal O$ for $\ell\geq1$. In this article, we study representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_\ell)$ parabolically induced from characters of the Borel subgroup $\mathrm{B}_n(\mathcal O_\ell)$. For $n=3$, we establish a criterion for the irreducibility of these induced representations in terms of the relative conductors of the inducing characters. Motivated by this result, we formulate a conjecture characterizing the irreducibility of such representations for arbitrary $n$. We further show that when all inducing characters are equal, the resulting induced representation is not multiplicity-free, implying that the corresponding triple $(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_\ell),\mathrm{B}_n(\mathcal O_\ell),\chi)$ is not a Gelfand pair. Finally, we study the irreducible decomposition of these representations for $\mathrm{GL}_3(\mathcal O_\ell)$ when two relative conductors attain their maximal values. Using the decomposition theory for $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathcal O_\ell)$, we describe the irreducible constituents and determine their dimensions.

title: On the Average List Size of VT Codes under Two Insertions or Two Deletions
abstract: Levenshtein's classical theorem shows that any code that can uniquely decode from \(t\) deletions can also uniquely decode from \(t\) insertions. This symmetry, however, does not generally hold in the list-decoding regime. Several prior results on the capacity and radii of list-decoding from insertions and deletions suggest that insertions are easier to handle than deletions. In an effort to better understand this asymmetry between insertions and deletions under list-decoding, we study an analogous version of McEliece's \emph{average list size problem}. More precisely, given a binary code \(\mathcal{C}\) of length \(n\) that uniquely corrects \(t'\) insertions (or deletions), we are interested in the average number of codewords returned by a \(t\)-insertion (or deletion) list decoder, where \(t' < t\). Focusing on the case of \(t'=1\) and \(t=2\), we find that under two insertions, this quantity is at most \((n+12)/4\) for any VT code of length \(n\), whereas under two deletions it is at least \(n/2 - 10\) when averaged over all length-\(n\) VT codes. The nearly factor-of-two gap between these upper and lower bounds serves to confirm the relative ease of list-decoding of insertions compared to deletions from an average-case perspective.

title: Tribonacci numbers that are palindromic concatenations of two distinct repdigits
abstract: Let $(T_n)_{n\ge1}$ be the Tribonacci sequence, defined by $T_1=T_2=1$, $T_3=2$, and $T_n=T_{n-1}+T_{n-2}+T_{n-3}$ for $n\ge4$. In this paper, we study the Tribonacci numbers whose decimal representation is a palindromic concatenation of two distinct repdigits, that is, numbers of the shape $\overline{d_1\cdots d_1\,d_2\cdots d_2\,d_1\cdots d_1}$ with $1\le d_1\le9$, $0\le d_2\le9$, $d_1\ne d_2$. We prove that no Tribonacci number is a palindromic concatenation of two distinct repdigits. The proof combines lower bounds for linear forms in logarithms, the Baker-Davenport reduction method, and a finite computational verification.

title: An optimization problem for $\delta'$ leaky stars
abstract: We consider singular Schr\"odinger operators with an attractive $\delta'$ interaction of strength $\beta$ supported by a star graph and prove that the ground-state eigenvalue is uniquely maximized by stars of the maximum symmetry. Two different proofs are presented, one for an even number of edges using a comparison to the $\delta$ interaction star, the other general based on Birman-Schwinger technique.

title: GPU-Accelerated Nested Schur-Complement Solvers for Atmospheric Flow Simulations Using Horizontally-Explicit, Vertically-Implicit Schemes and Discontinuous Galerkin Methods
abstract: Horizontally explicit, vertically implicit (HEVI) time integration removes the acoustic time-step restriction imposed by fine vertical grids in nonhydrostatic atmospheric models, but requires fast solvers for the resulting vertical linear systems, especially on GPUs. We present GPU-accelerated nested Schur-complement solvers for these systems for a split-form discontinuous Galerkin spectral element method on Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto (LGL) nodes applied to the compressible Euler equations with gravity. In time, we use a Rosenbrock-W method, a linearly implicit Runge-Kutta scheme that retains its order and stability with approximate Jacobians. This allows a sparse vertical Jacobian that captures vertical acoustic waves and gravity on curvilinear meshes with orography and decouples into independent column systems. The solvers are nested: a global Schur complement (static condensation) exploits the LGL sparsity to condense each column onto a few element-edge unknowns, and a local Schur complement eliminates all variables but the vertical momentum within each element, exploiting that the pressure depends only on the potential-temperature density. We propose and analyze two condensation strategies, which lead to banded and block-tridiagonal reduced systems. The resulting HEVI schemes conserve total mass and potential-temperature density to round-off. The solvers are implemented for CPUs and GPUs in TrixiAtmo.jl, the atmospheric extension of Trixi.jl. We verify high-order convergence with linear inertia-gravity waves in a 2D channel and demonstrate robustness on the sphere with the baroclinic instability, a mountain-induced baroclinic instability, and the DCMIP-2025 gap-flow and vortex-shedding cases. For the baroclinic instability without orography, the scheme achieves 18.8 and 2.9 simulated years per day at 100 and 50 km resolution on one NVIDIA GH200 GPU in double precision.

title: Minimal Product Sets in Finite Metacyclic Groups
abstract: Minimum product-set problems ask how small a product of two subsets of prescribed cardinalities can be in a finite group. Although the problem is completely understood for finite abelian groups, exact results in the nonabelian setting are available only for particular classes. We determine the minimum product-set function $\mu_G$ for every finite metacyclic group, without assuming that the relevant cyclic extension splits. Our proof converts the extremal problem into a finite recursive arithmetic description of the feasible cardinality vectors of subset trios. The recursion combines the subgroup structure of finite metacyclic groups with the structural classification of maximal critical subset trios. The resulting characterization recovers the previously known formulas for abelian and nilpotent groups, dihedral groups, and nonabelian groups of order $pq$. It also yields metacyclic examples in which the minimum product-set size lies strictly between the classical lower and upper arithmetic bounds for finite solvable groups. For faithful split metacyclic groups, we further show that requiring one factor to be symmetric, contain the identity, and generate the whole group can force a strictly larger product set than the unrestricted minimum. The latter constraint admits a vertex-isoperimetric interpretation on connected Cayley graphs.

title: $6$ powers of $2$ in the Linnik--Goldbach problem
abstract: Linnik's approximation to Goldbach's conjecture concerns the representation of sufficiently large even integers as the sum of two primes and a bounded number of powers of two. We prove that $6$ powers of $2$ suffice unconditionally and that $5$ suffice under the GRH, improving previous works.

title: Translational tilings by axis-parallel polygonal sets
abstract: The periodic tiling conjecture asserts that if a bounded set $\Omega\subset \mathbb R^d$ of finite measure tiles $\mathbb R^d$ by translations, then it admits at least one fully periodic tiling. This conjecture was proved to hold in $\mathbb R$ by Lagarias and Wang, and was recently disproved by Greenfeld and Tao in sufficiently high dimensions. Its discrete analogue in $\mathbb Z^2$ was proved by Bhattacharya, whereas the conjecture in $\mathbb R^2$ remains open. In this paper, we analyze the structure of tilings by axis-parallel polygonal sets: bounded open sets in $\mathbb R^2$ whose boundary is a finite union of line segments parallel to the axes. We prove that every such tiling that is topologically minimal is weakly periodic. Moreover, we show that if an axis-parallel polygonal set $\Omega$ tiles $\mathbb{R}^2$ then it admits a quasi-periodic tiling (i.e., a finite union of translated lattices). The proofs combine geometric decompositions of tilings with rational approximation and discrete tiling theory. As a consequence, we obtain that the translational tiling problem for axis-parallel polygonal sets with real algebraic vertex coordinates is decidable.

title: Explicit counterexamples to Frank-Loss optimizer conjectures for critical Dirac and vector Sobolev inequalities
abstract: Frank and Loss proposed critical Sobolev inequalities for the Dirac operator and for vector fields. They conjectured optimality of their spinorial family and wrote that it is conceivable that the higher-dimensional Loss-Yau potential is an optimizer. Wang and Zhang recently disproved both optimizer claims using direct comparison and instability arguments. We compute closed-form quotients for two elementary families of explicit competitors with strictly smaller quotients. For every $d\geq2$, the spinorial competitor is a constant spinor multiplied by a scalar Aubin-Talenti optimizer. For every $d\geq3$, the vector competitor is the planar azimuthal field \[ A_d(x)=\frac{d}{(1+\lvert x\rvert^2)^2} (-x_2,x_1,0,\ldots,0). \] It lies in the nonlinear gauge and its quotient is computed in closed form. For every odd $d\geq3$, it gives an explicit proof of nonoptimality of the higher-dimensional Loss-Yau-Dunne-Min potential. In dimension three, this field is a specific member of the competitor family of Wang and Zhang: it is a linear combination of the Loss-Yau potential and its reflected twin. Its axisymmetry gives a negative answer to their question about minimization within the $\mathrm{SO}(2)\times 1$-invariant class.

title: Inference on the Value of Policy Improvement in Adaptive Experiments
abstract: In this paper, we develop an asymptotically normal estimator for the value of policy improvement (VPI) under adaptively collected data. This value, which is defined as the gap between the value of the best treatment policy in a class and that of a baseline policy, gauges whether or not it is worth deploying a personalized treatment policy. Building an estimator for the VPI is naturally more difficult than estimating the value of a fixed policy. This is because, in addition to contending with the correlated data and decaying propensities associated with adaptive experiments, any estimator must also handle the non-regularity, or lack of pathwise differentiability, of the underlying estimand when the optimal policy is non-unique. Our proposed estimator works by sequentially fitting a weighted empirical welfare maximizing policy on historical data and then evaluating it using inverse propensity weighting on future samples. We neither assume that the optimal policy is unique nor make a margin assumption on the underlying heterogeneous treatment effects. A key difficulty in analyzing our estimator is showing that the regret incurred through policy learning is asymptotically smaller than the standard error of the estimator. We accomplish this by showing faster regret rates for policy learning under decaying propensities, which may be of independent interest. We not only evaluate the coverage of our estimator on a mix of synthetic and semi-synthetic data, but also employ it to estimate the VPI in an adaptive experiment evaluating the efficacy of job assistance programs in Jordan due to Caria et al. Although our estimates are generally more conservative than their hierarchical Bayesian analysis, which assumes that the optimal policy is unique, we still corroborate the benefits of personalization amongst Syrian refugees.

title: Quantum ordinal optimization under a fixed comparison budget
abstract: Ordinal optimization selects designs that are good enough rather than optimal when evaluation is expensive and the budget is small. The alignment probability measures the chance that the selected set contains at least a prescribed number of truly good designs. We formulate quantum ordinal optimization as a class of problems that maximize this probability under a fixed oracle budget. We study exact, coherent pairwise comparisons with one selected design as a first instance, with the budget counted in comparison queries. For every classical comparison budget smaller than the number of designs, we prove that a knockout among uniformly sampled designs attains the optimum. The sample is drawn without replacement and contains one more design than the number of comparisons. For a uniformly random order, the selected design's rank has a polynomial probability law. At the same comparison budget, the maximum quantum degree is at most twice the classical maximum, a factor attained whenever there are more than twice as many designs as comparisons, so a quantum algorithm can realize rank laws that no classical algorithm with the same budget can. We determine the exact quantum optimum with one comparison for every number of designs and every good-enough set. For selecting the best of n designs, the optimal success probability with one quantum comparison is approximately 3.30/n for large n, compared with 2/n for one classical comparison. When the best design is sought, one quantum comparison gives a higher alignment probability than two classical comparisons whenever there are more than nine designs.

title: A Multiplicative Horn Obstruction to the Unitary Categorification of a Rank-Twelve Modular Datum
abstract: We study the rank-twelve potential modular datum denoted $12^{39,406}_{4,1276.}$ in the low-rank classification tables. Its global dimension is $(1287+351\sqrt{13})/2$, and its fusion ring agrees with that of the known rank-twelve Haagerup modular category. The datum satisfies the modular relations, has nonnegative integral Verlinde coefficients, and passes several familiar genus-one necessary tests. We prove, nevertheless, that it cannot be realized by a unitary modular tensor category. The obstruction already occurs in the representation of the three-strand braid group on $\operatorname{Hom}(C_{[10]},B^{\otimes3})$. Generalized Frobenius--Schur indicators determine the eigenvalues of the two-strand generator on this twelve-dimensional space. The central relation in $B_3$ then reduces the problem to a product of three prescribed unitary conjugacy classes. A sixfold symmetry reduces the $1302$ determinant-compatible cases to $217$ representatives. Rank-one inequalities leave only $17$ of these, and ten explicitly displayed degree-zero rank-two Schubert inequalities exclude the remaining cases. A violated inequality with gap $2/117$ is worked out explicitly. All calculations used in the obstruction are exact. The argument uses unitarity essentially and leaves non-unitary categorification open.

title: Sub-Gaussian Confidence Intervals for Heavy-Tailed Data: Characterizing the Limits of Inference
abstract: We investigate the problem of uncertainty quantification in the mean estimation framework. Given an i.i.d. sample from a distribution with unknown mean $\mu$ and variance $\sigma^2$, we want to construct an estimator $\wh\mu_n$ and provide a computable and size-optimal upper bound for the error $|\wh \mu_n - \mu|$. While estimators possessing strong deviation guarantees are well known, no data-dependent non-asymptotic upper bounds for their performance exist in general. We show that this gap can be bridged by introducing a parameter that characterizes the ``effective sample size'' available for uncertainty quantification. This parameter captures the difficulty of the problem, interpolating between ``easy'' cases where sub-Gaussian confidence intervals exist and ``hard" cases where their construction is impossible. Using this characterization, we design confidence intervals of optimal length that are fully adaptive to the unknown variance. Numerical experiments confirm that our approach maintains nominal coverage even in asymmetric and heavy-tailed regimes where other existing methods fail.

title: A Sharp Bound for the Second Betti Number of Hyperk\"ahler Sixfolds
abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth compact irreducible hyperk\"ahler manifold of dimension six. We prove that the second Betti number satisfies $b_2(X) \le 23$. Furthermore, we show that the third cohomology vanishes whenever $b_2(X) \ge 19$, and that all odd cohomology vanishes when $b_2(X) = 23$. If the second Chern class lies in the subalgebra generated by $H^2(X,\mathbb{Q})$, then $b_2(X) \in \{5,8,23\}$. The proof uses the Looijenga--Lunts--Verbitsky decomposition, curvature inequalities for Segre classes, and the Hodge--Riemann bilinear relations on the projective cotangent bundle.

title: Failure of dimension drop for harmonic measure on Ahlfors regular flat boundaries
abstract: We develop an $N$-adic modification of the construction of David-Jeznach-Julia for compact subsets of the real line $\mathbb{R}\subset\mathbb{C}$ for which harmonic measure for the complementary domains has no dimension drop. In particular, we show that for every $s\in(0,1/2)$, there exists an $s$-Ahlfors regular compact set $K\subset\mathbb{R}\subset\mathbb{C}$ such that $\mathrm{dim}\omega^\infty=s$, where $\omega^\infty$ denotes harmonic measure for $\mathbb{C}\setminus K$ with pole at infinity. Combined with a result of the third author, this shows that the threshold $1/2$ is sharp.

title: A note on the $p$-adic inhomogeneous Littlewood conjecture
abstract: Bugeaud, Haynes and Velani (2011) resolved a metric version of the $p$-adic Littlewood conjecture. We establish a fully inhomogeneous generalisation of their result, as well as a partially inhomogeneous generalisation of a result of Harrap and Haynes (2013) in the more general mixed setting.

title: Superpolynomial Lists for Reed-Solomon Codes over Binary Extension Fields
abstract: Recent work shows that ordinary Reed--Solomon codes over prime fields admit polynomial-size lists up to list-decoding capacity on every evaluation set. We show a contrasting phenomenon over binary extension fields. For every fixed rate $0<R<1$, there exists $\varepsilon_R>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $h$, the full-field Reed--Solomon code over $\mathbb{F}_{2^h}$ has a received word with $n^{\Omega_R(\log n)}$ codewords within relative distance $1-R-\varepsilon_R$. To our knowledge, these are the first superpolynomial ordinary Reed--Solomon list-size lower bounds at fixed positive rate and a fixed positive agreement gap above the rate. Thus capacity-approaching polynomial list size for Reed--Solomon codes is not uniform over the underlying field, and the obstruction occurs at every fixed rate. As a puncturing consequence, the same holds for primitive Reed--Solomon codes; the obstruction is also robust under controlled dense puncturing. The proof begins with an exact correspondence that turns certain binary Bose--Chaudhuri--Hocquenghem weight-enumerator coefficients into sizes of single Reed--Solomon lists. A classical binary weight family gives the initial quarter-rate construction, while a quadratic-form enumeration supplies its superpolynomial multiplicity. A common-kernel quotient/descent argument and common-root padding then extend the construction to all rates. We also determine the optimized agreement envelope achieved by the construction.

title: Koszul Duality in an Equivariant Context
abstract: This article takes steps to show that an equivariant version of the well known phenomena of Koszul Duality can be formulated in a manner not considered prior: via dg (co)algebra valued functors on the orbit category. As such techniques used in this article mix traditional and modern categorical methods in homotopy theory.

title: Weak type (1,1) bound criterion for maximal truncated singular integral operators with rough kernels
abstract: This paper proves the weak type (1,1) boundedness for maximal truncated singular integral operators with rough non-convolution kernels of the form $\Omega(x-y) K(x,y)$, where $\Omega$ is homogeneous of degree zero with $\Omega \in L\log L(\sS^{d-1})$ and $K$ is a standard Calder\'on-Zygmund kernel. This extends the recent resolution of the classical convolution case by Lai \cite{Lai2025weak} to a wider class of operators.

title: Equivariant formality for rational $\C_{p^k}$-spaces
abstract: In this paper, we discuss equivariant formality for spaces equipped with a primary cyclic group action. We study the behavior of equivariant formality with some topological constructions. The algebraic complexity needs to deal with injectivity. In the end, we discuss equivariant intrinsic formality.

title: Separating Statistical Inference from Experimental Runtime: An Architecture for Sequential Scientific Analysis
abstract: Sequential statistical procedures are increasingly embedded in scientific systems in which observations arrive incrementally from heterogeneous sources. In such systems the statistical update is only one part of the computation: observations must also be acquired, aligned across inputs, ordered, delivered, persisted, and replayed, and results must be passed to systems that display them or act on them. Sequential methods are nevertheless missing from the general software toolkit. They run inside proprietary experimentation platforms and commercial statistical packages, or exist as offline functions over complete data, and the batch fit interface that dominates machine-learning libraries has no place for a procedure that listens, keeps state, and decides when to stop. We propose an architecture that separates statistical inference from data topology, execution runtime, run lifecycle, persistence, and external action. Its central abstraction is the Sequential Procedure: a state-transition function that maps an inferential state, a valid statistical input, and a statistical random state to a new state and a scientific output. The procedure does not define how observations are acquired, paired, scheduled, stored, or acted upon. We specify the architecture semantically rather than through an object model, derive seven conformance invariants that any implementation can be tested against (among them synchronous/asynchronous, checkpoint, replay, and batch equivalence), and describe a dependency-free reference implementation in which all seven hold bitwise. Lorden's 2-SPRT for the Kiefer-Weiss problem serves as the reference procedure; the same contract accommodates sequential estimators, Bayesian filters, change-point detectors, and stateful predictive models.

title: The theory of $(\lambda,\mu)$-fold factorizations of groups
abstract: Motivated by recent work on $\lambda$-fold near-factorizations by Kreher, Li, and Stinson (Designs, Codes and Cryptography, 2026), we introduce and systematically investigate $(\lambda,\mu)$-fold factorizations as combinatorial structures with prescribed representation multiplicities. Such a factorization consists of two subsets of a finite group whose products represent each nonidentity element exactly $\lambda$ times and the identity exactly $\mu$ times. These structures generalize $\lambda$-fold near-factorizations and provide a common framework for several families arising in combinatorial design theory, including strong external difference families with two equal-sized subsets, as well as binary sequence pairs with two-level correlation. Their associated $\{0,1\}$-matrices satisfy the Bridges-Ryser equation $XY=\lambda(J-I)+\mu I$, linking the factorization problem to a classical matrix framework for combinatorial designs. We establish the foundational theory of $(\lambda,\mu)$-fold factorizations, provide two general constructions, and prove several nonexistence results for finite abelian groups.
comments: Updated abstract, minor revisions, and several additional references

title: Open substacks preserving moduli spaces: classification and bounds
abstract: For a smooth locally reductive stack admitting an adequate moduli space, we show that there are finitely many open substacks preserving the adequate moduli space, and give a complete classification of such opens. For $\mathbb{G}_m$-actions, this becomes an explicit description in terms of the codimension-one Bialynicki-Birula strata. Moreover, for a stable adequate moduli space, we show that the number of preserving opens are bounded by 3 raised to the relative Picard rank. As an application, the number of fixed components for $\mathbb{G}_m$-actions is at least the relative Picard rank.

title: Finite Length of Locally Analytic Vectors for $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ and $D_F^\times$
abstract: Let $F/\mathbf Q_p$ and $E/\mathbf Q_p$ be finite extensions, and let $G=\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ or $D_F^\times$, where $D_F$ is the quaternion division algebra over $F$. Let $\Pi$ be an admissible Banach $E$-representation of $G$ whose locally $\mathbf Q_p$-analytic vectors $\Pi^{\mathrm{an}}$ have an infinitesimal character. If $p>2$ or $F=\mathbf Q_p$, we prove that $\Pi^{\mathrm{an}}$ and $\Pi$ have finite length in their respective admissible categories.

title: Regularity for Minimizers of Mixed-Smoothness Variational Integrals
abstract: We establish the first partial regularity results for minimizers of a class of suitably quasiconvex variational integrals defined on anisotropic Sobolev spaces. These variational integrals are related to higher gradient continuum models for pantographic metamaterials.
comments: 22 pages. Accepted for publication in Nonlinear Analysis

title: Iwasawa cohomology of pseudorigid families of $(\varphi,\Gamma)$-modules
abstract: We study the Iwasawa cohomology complex attached to a pseudorigid family of $(\varphi, \Gamma)$-modules and prove coadmissibility of its cohomology groups, perfectness and compatibility with base change. We apply this result to give another proof of perfectness of the Herr complex in pseudorigid family. We also use it to prove perfectness of Selmer complexes and obtain a result on variation of ranks of Selmer groups in analytic family.

title: Residual-Information Generalization Bounds Under Selective Privacy: Extended Version
abstract: Information-theoretic generalization bounds usually control dependence on the task sample, whereas selective privacy may constrain only a different, private coordinate. We study i.i.d. pairs $(X,Y)$, where a learner observes $(X^n,Y^n)$, leaks at most $\epsilon_n$ nats about $X^n$, and incurs loss on $Y$. A chain-rule transfer converts this mismatched constraint into the closed-form universal certificate $I(W;Y^n)\leq\min\{nH(Y),nH(Y\mid X)+\epsilon_n\}$. Combining the certificate with mutual-information generalization yields a bound governed by residual task uncertainty and normalized privacy leakage. We derive complementary task-compression and individual-sample refinements, identify a sharp obstruction showing why selective privacy alone need not give a vanishing certificate, and invert the bound to obtain the exact leakage allowance for a prescribed generalization tolerance. We prove exact information-level achievability for deterministic-task and independent-residual source families and show that the resulting $\sqrt{\epsilon_n/n}$ generalization rate is tight up to a universal constant. We also give a fixed-horizon adaptive application in which conditional leakage costs add.

title: Universal Shift Congruences for Weighted Permutation Sequences
abstract: The involution numbers $1,1,2,4,10,26,\ldots$ repeat modulo $3$, $5$ and $7$. We explain this, and many similar patterns, by one rule. Many sequences count permutations in which every cycle of length $m$ carries a weight $w_m$ (involutions, derangements, "sets of lists", and many others in the OEIS). Writing $A(n)$ for such a count, the rule is $A(n+k)\equiv A(n)A(k)$ modulo $\mathrm{lcm}(n,k)$. It generalizes our earlier proof of the case modulo $k$ for one such sequence, but now it holds for all weights at once, as a coefficientwise congruence between universal polynomials, and we find the largest modulus that works for the universal polynomials, $nk/\mathrm{rad}(\gcd(n,k))$, and show that nothing larger does. We then show that passing from $k$ to $pk$ behaves like raising to the $p$-th power modulo a high power of $p$, with a sharp exponent for the polynomials, which gives $A(p^r)\equiv(w_1+(p-1)w_p)^{p^{r-1}}$ modulo $p^r$ for odd $p$, and explains why the prime $2$ is special. A family of sequences defined by Lagrange inversion fits the same framework, which proves Bala's conjecture for the whole family (the single sequence A278070 had been proved earlier by an automated system) and the divisibility observed in the entries A251568 and A251569. As further applications we prove OEIS conjectures of Richman, Hanna, van Hoeij and Bala (A227937), and the theorems apply to 101 OEIS sequences, whose congruences are recorded in a supplementary catalogue. Higher-order versions of the content formula are treated in a separate paper.
comments: 30 pages. Supplementary catalogue of 101 OEIS sequences and check programs in ancillary files. Lean 4 formalization at https://github.com/ahaankallat/congruence-phenomena-lean and https://github.com/ahaankallat/congruence-phenomena-higher-order-lean

title: Unrectifiable surfaces with intrinsic regularity in Carnot groups
abstract: In any noncommutative Carnot group, for every $0\le \alpha<1$, we show the existence of a $C^{1,\alpha}_\mathrm H$ surface that is unrectifiable with respect to the Euclidean distance. Precisely, the surface has Euclidean Hausdorff dimension higher than its topological dimension. We show that in step-2 Carnot groups the construction gives hypersurfaces of maximal Euclidean Hausdorff dimension, equal to $q-\frac{1+\alpha}{2}$, where $q$ is the topological dimension of the group. Here the range of unrectifiability is sharp, since for $\alpha=1$ the surface is rectifiable in the classical sense. In step-2 Carnot groups, it is also possible to prove that the $(q-\frac12)$-dimensional Euclidean Hausdorff measure of every $C^1_\mathrm H$ hypersurface is zero. These results extend the seminal work by Kirchheim and Serra Cassano in the first Heisenberg group.

title: Uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for singular $L^k$ interaction kernels with rates
abstract: Based on a semigroup approach, we prove quantitative uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for two systems of interacting particles with singular interaction kernels $K$ of type $L^k$, $k>d$, and a contractive Lipschitz confinement force field. First, we consider a system with moderate interaction, which means that the particles interact through the mollified kernel $K\ast V^N$, for some approximation of identity $V^N = N^{d\alpha} V(N^\alpha \cdot),\, \alpha>0$. Assuming that $\|K\|_{L^k}$ is sufficiently small, we obtain that for any $\varepsilon>0$ the uniform-in-time rate is of order $N^{-\min\left(\alpha,\frac12-\frac{d\alpha}{2}-\varepsilon\right)}$, plus an exponentially small in time contribution of the initial condition. Second, for the classical, non-mollified particle system we establish uniform-in-time propagation of chaos with rate $N^{-\min\left(\alpha,\frac12-\frac{d\alpha}{2}-\varepsilon\right)} + \|K-K\ast V^N\|_{L^{k}}$, plus an exponentially small in time contribution of the initial condition. The method relies on the regularity properties of the solution of the associated nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation combined with estimates of the Duhamel formulation of the mollified empirical measure, together with partial Girsanov transforms for the non-mollified system of particles.

title: Low-Latency Belief-Propagation Decoding of Quantum LDPC Codes with Reinforcement-Learned Scheduling
abstract: Belief propagation (BP) is attractive for quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) decoding because of its low complexity and low latency, but short cycles and degeneracy can limit its error-correction performance. Reinforcement-learned sequential scheduling (RL-S) substantially improves this performance by adapting the variable node (VN) update order, although Q-table storage and heap-based selection introduce additional overhead. We propose bucket RL-S (B-RL-S), which quantizes learned Q-values into integer priorities and schedules VN updates using dynamically maintained first-in, first-out buckets. Without retraining or changing the BP message updates, B-RL-S reduces policy storage and refreshes only priorities affected by local residual syndrome changes. A fixed number of priority levels enables constant-time VN selection and queue relocation. For the $[[288,12,18]]$ bivariate bicycle code over the depolarizing channel at $p=0.05$, B-RL-S with eight priority levels achieves approximately one fifth the block error rate (BLER) of flooding BP followed by order-10 ordered-statistics decoding. The respective caps are $1000$ sequential iterations for B-RL-S and $1000$ flooding iterations for the BP stage of the reference decoder. These results highlight strong error correction with inexpensive scheduling and no additional post-processing stage.

title: The operad of anti-pre-Lie algebras and its Lie elements
abstract: We initiate a systematic operadic approach to anti-pre-Lie algebras. We study the operad controlling anti-pre-Lie algebras, its relationship to the operad of Novikov algebras and its cyclic structure. We establish that the Lie bracket of an anti-pre-Lie algebra satisfies the standard identity of degree five. We also establish a quadratic maximality property of the anti-pre-Lie operad with respect to this identity. We then show that the anti-pre-Lie operad and its Koszul dual are not Koszul and give a full description of the latter. Finally, we identify the Lie elements in the Koszul dual operad with the operad of metabelian Lie algebras.

title: A note on the Slater$\unicode{x2013}$V\'elez permutation
abstract: We study the greedy sequence of positive integers introduced by Slater and V\'elez. They proved that it is a permutation of the positive integers but left open whether its sequence of consecutive absolute differences is also a permutation. We prove that it is.

title: Auxiliary Hessian Equations
abstract: We propose k-Hessian equations as auxiliary equations for degenera- tions of K\"ahler classes to nef classes of numerical dimension k. As proof-of-concept results, we provide a uniform mean-value inequality and uniform \`a priori estimates for Hessian equa- tions.

title: Higher-order nonhomomorphicity under affine restrictions
abstract: We study the behavior of the $k$-th-order nonhomomorphicity of Boolean functions under restriction to affine subspaces. For odd $k\ge3$ and $0\le t<n$, we introduce the $t$-restriction $k$-th-order nonhomomorphicity $P_{k,t}(f)$, defined as the minimum of $P_k(f_{\mid A})$ over affine spaces of codimension at most $t$. For a direct sum of $m$ monomials of degrees at least two, we determine $P_{k,t}$ exactly. When $t<m$, a minimum is obtained by setting one variable equal to zero in each of the $t$ monomials of lowest degree. When $m\le t<n$, the minimum is zero. The proof combines multiplicativity of even Walsh moments with a contraction argument for affine restrictions. We establish a general formula for the Walsh transform of a Boolean function restricted to an affine subspace of arbitrary codimension, yielding an exact spectral characterization of the $t$-restriction normalized nonlinearity $\rnnl_t(f)$. As odd $k$ tends to infinity, $(1-2P_{k,t}(f))^{1/(k+1)}$ converges to $1-2\rnnl_t(f)$. We further prove that every non-affine function has a hyperplane restriction with strictly smaller odd-order nonhomomorphicity. Finally, we determine $\rnnl_1(T_{d,n})$ exactly for all threshold functions with $n\ge3$. This proves the two threshold-function conjectures left open in~\cite{SergeAnaPante2025}, including the previously unresolved odd-majority case, where a minimizing hyperplane is $x_1+x_2=0$.

title: Semiprime and real submodules of arbitrary modules are intersections of prime and real prime submodules
abstract: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. A submodule $N$ of an $R$-module $M$ is semiprime if $m\in(N:m)M$ implies $m\in N$. It is known that every semiprime submodule of $R^n$ is an intersection of prime submodules, and Aryapoor extended this to finitely generated modules. We show that no finiteness assumption is needed: every semiprime submodule of an \emph{arbitrary} $R$-module is the intersection of the prime submodules containing it. The proof is short and uses neither coordinates nor presentations; its key step is that a nonzero element $q$ of a semiprime module $Q$ satisfies $sq\notin\p Q$ for all $s\notin\p$, where $\p$ is any minimal prime over the annihilator of $q$. We define an $R$-module $M$ to be real if $\sum_i m_i\otimes m_i=0$ in $M\otimes_RM$ implies $m_i=0$ for all $i$, and a submodule $N\subseteq M$ real if the module $M/N$ is real. We prove the corresponding result for real submodules: every real submodule of an arbitrary module is the intersection of the real prime submodules containing it. On $R^n$ our notion of realness coincides with the coordinate definition used in earlier work on real Nullstellens\"atze for free modules.

title: Entropy-Regularized Mean-Field Games with Average-Reward Criterion: Span-Seminorm Contractions and Model-Free Learning
abstract: We study stationary discrete-time mean-field games with finite state and action spaces under the average-reward criterion, with an entropy-regularized objective and population-dependent dynamics and rewards. Under a minorization condition, the soft Q-operator is a span-seminorm contraction for the full transition kernel, so relative value iteration does not require the minorizing measure. When the Lipschitz constant of the kernel is below the minorization mass and the temperature exceeds an explicit threshold, the equilibrium fixed-point operator is a contraction: an equilibrium exists, its population distribution is unique, and a fixed-point iteration converges to it geometrically. We then learn the equilibrium model-free from a simulator, combining soft Q-learning at a fixed population distribution with an empirical transition kernel. We prove a finite-sample bound for soft Q-learning in the span seminorm, with temperature-independent constants, and derive convergence rates for the learned population distribution and policy. A congestion-aware routing game illustrates the results.

title: Fine asymptotics for approximate simulation of symmetric channels
abstract: We study the approximate channel simulation problem in the normal approximation regime. Our starting point is the fact established by Cao et al.~\cite{Cao_channel_simulation}, that the minimal codebook size $M_\epsilon^*(W)$ for a fixed error tolerance $\epsilon>0$ is closely related to the $\epsilon$-smooth channel max-information, $I_{\max}^\epsilon(W)$. Using this, we refine earlier large-blocklength approximations to $M_\epsilon^*(W^{\otimes n})$ for discrete memoryless channels. Specifically, we provide tight third-order expansions for Gallager-symmetric channels and demonstrate that the third-order term is channel-dependent. As in corresponding channel coding expansions, we identify a substantial rate gap between singular and nonsingular channels. Notably, the direction of this gap is reversed relative to channel coding: The third-order term is $-\frac{1}{2}\log n$ for singular channels but $O(\log\log n)$ for nonsingular channels.

title: Radial Schur multipliers on trees and the failure of Fourier-Schur transference
abstract: Given $1 < p < \infty$ and a function $m \colon \mathbf{N}_0 \to \mathbf{C}$, we provide a characterization of radial Schur multipliers $M(x,y) = m(d(x,y))$ on the Schatten $p$-class of a tree $(X,d)$ equipped with its graph metric. That is, the operator norm of the radial Schur multiplier $S_M$ is controlled by the norm of the Fourier multiplier $T_m$ on the torus: \[ \big\| S_M \colon S_p(X) \to S_p(X) \big\|_{\mathrm{cb}} \lesssim \frac{p^4}{(p-1)^2} \, \big\| T_m \colon L_p(\mathbf{T}) \to L_p(\mathbf{T}) \big\|_{\mathrm{cb}}, \] with both quantities being comparable when the tree $X$ has infinite diameter. This is a rather unexpected inequality, which necessarily fails at the endpoints $p=1,\infty$ due to the work of Haagerup, Steenstrup and Szwarc. As an application, we construct the first examples of completely $S_p$-bounded Herz-Schur multipliers in the free group that are unbounded as Fourier multipliers. This result disproves Fourier-Schur transference---a longstanding open problem since the work of Neuwirth and Ricard in 2011. In line with this, our main result also implies the surprising fact that free balls Schur multipliers are uniformly $S_p$-bounded, in sharp contrast to their Fourier behavior. In addition, we disprove Fourier-Schur transference over the algebraic groups $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbf{Q}_q)$ and $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbf{R})$ with $\mathrm{K}$-biinvariant counterexamples, the latter involving additional geometric and probabilistic techniques.

title: Hilbert's Nullstellensatz and the real Nullstellensatz for modules and sheaves
abstract: We prove the geometric halves of Hilbert's Nullstellensatz and of the real Nullstellensatz for submodules of finitely generated modules and for coherent sheaves, complementing our earlier result that semiprime (resp. real) submodules are intersections of prime (resp. real prime) submodules. First, we pass from prime to maximal submodules: over a Jacobson ring, a prime submodule $P$ of $M$ is an intersection of maximal submodules whenever $M/P$ is a torsionless $R/(P:M)$-module, in particular whenever $M/P$ is finitely generated (the latter case is due to Maani Shirazi and Sharif). Consequently, if $R$ is a finitely generated algebra over an algebraically closed field and $M$ is finitely generated, the smallest semiprime submodule containing a submodule $N$ of $M$ consists of all $f\in M$ such that, for every point $a$, the value $f(a)$ (i.e. the image of $f$ in the fibre $M/\mathfrak{m}_aM$) lies in $N(a)$ (i.e. the image of $N$ in $M/\mathfrak{m}_aM$). We prove the real analogues over real Jacobson rings; for finitely generated algebras over a real closed field they are determined by the real points. The module classifications and directional vanishing formulas yield both Nullstellens\"atze for coherent sheaves on schemes of finite type over a field. We also prove compatibility of semiprimeness, reality and both radicals with arbitrary localization, and the resulting stalk criteria.

title: The $p$-Bures-Wasserstein distance via $3\times3$ block matrices (with application to $p$-Bures-Wasserstein barycenters)
abstract: We study the $p$-Bures-Wasserstein distance $D_p(A,B)=(\mathrm{tr}\,A^p+\mathrm{tr}\,B^p-2\|A^{1/2}B^{1/2}\|_p^p)^{1/2}$ on positive semidefinite matrices; it equals the Bures-Wasserstein distance for $p=1$, and the Hilbert-Schmidt distance for $p=2$. We prove that $D_p$ is a metric for every $1\le p\le2$, by proving a stronger 2014 conjecture of Lin and van den Driessche on $3\times3$ block matrices. Our main tool is a partition inequality for Schatten norms, proved by complex interpolation. We also characterize Fr\'echet means for $D_p$ by a fixed-point equation and prove geometric convergence of the associated iteration.
comments: 20 pages; 4 appendices; one synthetic experiment included

title: Lack of exponential stability for thermoelastic Timoshenko and Bresse systems with full homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions
abstract: In this paper we prove that the classical thermoelastic Timoshenko and Bresse systems with thermal coupling acting only on the bending moment are not exponentially stable under full homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions if the equal wave speed condition is not satisfied. Combined with their well-known converses, our results provide complete characterizations of exponential stability in terms of the coefficients of each system. To the best of our knowledge, these characterizations were previously known only under mixed boundary conditions. The proof is based on the introduction of a boundary correction term in the standard trigonometric ansatz so that the full homogeneous Dirichlet conditions are satisfied.

title: Two Linear Programs are Better than One
abstract: The extension complexity $\operatorname{xc}(P)$ of a polytope $P$ is the minimum number of facets of a polytope that projects onto it. Motivated by the complexity of neural networks, Hertrich and Loho introduced the virtual extension complexity $\operatorname{vxc}(P)$ of a polytope $P$, which is the minimum of $\operatorname{xc}(Q) + \operatorname{xc}(R)$ among all polytopes $Q$ and $R$ such that $P+Q=R$. We show the following results pertaining to virtual extension complexity. First, we resolve the core open problem on the topic by showing the virtual extension complexity can be exponentially smaller than extension complexity. Second, we show there are matroid base polytopes with exponential virtual extension complexity by adapting a semi-algebraic counting argument by Hrube\v{s} that extends the counting arguments of Rothvoss. Finally, we show that the maximum virtual extension complexity of a polygon with $n$ vertices is $\Theta(\sqrt{n})$. This resolves an analogue of a question on extension complexity of Fiorini, Rothvoss, and Tiwary in 2011 in the case of virtual extension complexity.

title: An Efficient, Lean 4 Verified Necessary and Sufficient Condition for Membership in Pedigree Polytopes
abstract: The set \(P_{n}\) consists of the characteristic vectors of pedigrees, which are combinatorial encodings in one-to-one correspondence with Hamiltonian cycles. For \(n \geq 4\) and \(\tau_{n} = \binom{n}{3}-1\), the Membership Problem for the Pedigree Polytope (M3P) asks whether a given vector \(X \in \mathbb{Q}^{\tau_{n}}\) belongs to \(\mathrm{conv}(P_n)\). This paper gives a complete account, with the full proof statements and machine-verified Lean~4 certificates, of the necessary and sufficient (\NS) condition established in Chapter~5 of \emph{Pedigree Polytopes: New Insights on Computational Complexity of Combinatorial Optimisation Problems} (Arthanari, 2023): membership of $X$ in $\mathrm{conv}(P_n)$ is characterised by the feasibility, at every stage $k=4,\dots,n-1$, of a recursively constructed layered network, together with, when needed, a multicommodity flow problem $\mathrm{MCF}(k-1)$ achieving its maximum possible flow $z_{\max}$. We present the construction, the \NS{} condition itself, and the proofs of this characterisation, together with the resulting polynomial-time algorithm for M3P. Both directions of the \NS{} condition --- sufficiency and necessity (the multicommodity-flow feasibility argument of the book's Chapter~5) --- are machine-verified in Lean~4/Mathlib4 with zero unresolved \texttt{sorry}s in either dependency chain. The \NS{} characterisation therefore follows directly from the two machine-checked implications. The complete Lean~4 project is publicly available. A companion introductory article (arXiv:2507.09069) presents the same material for a broader readership, without the Lean~4 verification; the present paper adds full statements, proof sketches, and the complete machine-checked certificates.
comments: 23 pages, 1 Table giving Lean~4 files and their corresponding results in $\emph{Pedigree Polytopes} \cite{arthanari2023book}$

title: Sharp stability for mixed bubbles on hyperbolic space
abstract: We prove sharp residual stability estimates for the critical Poincar\'e-Sobolev equation near sums of one positive hyperbolic solution and one projected Euclidean bubble in dimensions at least four. The estimates are uniform in the relative positions of the centers. The sharp rate is linear except in dimension six, where it contains a square root of a logarithm. For nonnegative functions, the same estimates hold under an energy constraint near the sum of the two profile energies for \(\lambda\) outside a finite set, and an additional mass constraint removes this restriction. For arbitrary finite numbers of profiles, we identify and realize all nonnegative Palais-Smale levels. We characterize the parameters at which different pairs of profile numbers have the same energy and show that the limiting energy and mass determine both profile numbers.

title: Finite Root Sums in Symmetrizable Kac-Moody Algebras
abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebra with root system $\Phi$. A subset $S\subseteq\Phi$ is \emph{closed} if $\alpha,\beta\in S$ and $\alpha+\beta\in\Phi$ imply $\alpha+\beta\in S$. For finite and affine Kac-Moody algebras, this closure property is known to extend from pairs to arbitrary finite sums that are roots. We prove that every closed subset of the root system of any symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebra is closed under arbitrary finite sums that are roots. The proof uses real-root strings and simultaneous separation of positive imaginary roots, together with an addition lemma for fundamental imaginary roots. As an application, we extend a necessary condition for wideness of regular subalgebras from finite and affine types to all symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebras: the symmetric closure of the roots associated to a wide regular subalgebra is the entire root system.

title: The inf spectrum of moduli space
abstract: Given a surface of genus $g \geq 2$, its inf spectrum is the ordered multiset of inf lengths of curves on the surface, the infimum being over all hyperbolic metrics. We show that the inf spectrum has exponential growth with coefficients that only depend on g, improving the earlier double exponential upper bound. The proof involves developing a number of tools including the process of "thickening" a surface and the notion of model surfaces. These tools may be of independent interest.

title: A clarification of Fermi's formula for the maximum of partial sums
abstract: In Fermi's 1926 note, the expression assigned to the probability that all partial sums remain below a threshold is the complementary crossing probability. We obtain the correct probability from the same diffusion equation and locate the inconsistency in the final integration. We then state the limit for independent increments under the Lindeberg condition. A counterexample with smooth densities shows that small individual variances do not suffice to justify this limit. The probabilistic results are classical; the purpose of this note is to reconcile the stated event with the printed calculation and to make the sufficient hypotheses for the discrete limit explicit.
comments: 5 pages; historical clarification with a precise diffusion-limit statement

title: Nonlinear Feedback Control in High Dimensions using the Polynomial-Polynomial Regulator
abstract: We consider the problem of computing Taylor approximations to the optimal feedback law and value function for infinite-horizon finite-dimensional nonlinear optimal control problem---also known as Al'brekht's method. The scalability of existing Al'brekht-based approaches to computing approximate solutions to the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation associated with the optimal control problem has been severely limited by computational resources. The computational time issue has been partially mitigated by recent works leveraging tensor-structure to develop efficient numerical methods. However, RAM requirements still have remained a major hindrance to scaling beyond state dimensions of a few hundred or low thousands. We propose an acceleration to compute the expensive higher-order terms in a reduced space, mitigating the curse of dimensionality. A fast and scalable \textsc{Matlab} implementation is provided open-source for general purpose use, with the ability to accommodate arbitrary polynomial nonlinearities in the control-affine state equation, as well as polynomial state-dependence in the cost function, and the ability to handle systems in generalized form with a non-identity mass matrix, such as finite element models. Combined with the exploitation of sparsity and modern low-rank Riccati solvers, this permits computing approximations to polynomial feedback laws based on Al'brekht's method in hundreds of thousands of states.

title: Uniform-in-Time and Uniform-in-Temperature Particle Approximations of Coulomb MMD Flows
abstract: We study particle approximations of maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) flows with the Coulomb kernel on the torus $\mathbb{T}^d$, $d\ge2$, driven by thermal noise of strength $\tau\ge0$. For smooth, strictly positive initial and target densities and i.i.d. initial positions, we prove that the expected Wasserstein-1 distance between the empirical measure and the mean-field solution is at most of order $N^{-1/d}$ for $d\ge3$ and $\sqrt{(\log N)/N}$ for $d=2$, uniformly in time and in the temperature $\tau\ge0$, including the deterministic case $\tau=0$. At each fixed $\tau>0$, we also prove propagation of chaos in total variation for any $k$-fold marginal distributions of particles, uniformly in time, with a bound of order $\sqrt{k/\tau}$ times the empirical convergence rate. Our proof uses the modulated free-energy method of Bresch, Jabin, and Wang to reduce the particle convergence estimate to a relaxation estimate that controls the time integral of the mean-field velocity gradient uniformly in $\tau\ge0$. Near zero temperature, where the smoothing effect of the noise degenerates, we obtain this estimate by recentering the dynamics at thermal equilibrium and using the damping generated by the Coulomb interaction.

title: Regularity theorems for Lipschitz viscosity solutions to the minimal surface system
abstract: We prove several regularity theorems concerning Lipschitz viscosity solutions to the minimal surface system. The main lemma (i.e. ``Decoupling Lemma") says that the component functions of such solutions satisfy the homogeneous Pucci inequalities. This allows us to apply the regularity theory for scalar viscosity solutions for elliptic PDE component-wise to a viscosity solution for the system. As a result of the Decoupling Lemma, we deduce that 2D Lipschitz viscosity solutions to the system are analytic in the interior, and obtain a quantitative partial regularity theorem. We also prove a geometric Harnack inequality for Lipschitz solutions. The Harnack inequality yields a strong maximum principle and half-space Liouville theorem. Another significant consequence of the lemma is a boundary regularity theorem for Lipschitz viscosity solutions. Notably, our theorem does not require any density assumption at the graph boundary, and we do not assume stationarity. This is used to prove a classification theorem for the singular set of a 4D stationary solution on a bounded domain. We also prove an $\varepsilon$-regularity theorem extending a result of the author. To conclude, we survey open problems. As an example, we have included a Bernstein-type theorem for 3D homogeneous entire Lipschitz viscosity solutions. Taken together, our results suggest that viscosity methods are a useful tool for studying the regularity of minimal graphs.

title: Small area learning
abstract: Small area estimation (SAE) traditionally borrows strength across domains through a prespecified working model. We introduce small area learning (SAL), a learner-agnostic framework that formulates SAE as a multi-target semi-supervised learning problem and treats outcome prediction as a nuisance task. Areas may differ through unrestricted covariate shift and structured conditional shift, with information shared through common and area-specific components. We develop standard and cross-fitted estimators for low-complexity and flexible learners, unifying synthetic, model-based, and fully residual-corrected estimation. For area means, we establish consistency and asymptotic normality and provide variance estimators and confidence intervals. We extend the theory to settings with only aggregated population covariates and characterize the resulting aggregation bias. SAL reveals a bias--variance trade-off: partial residual correction can reduce mean squared error, whereas full correction yields estimators robust to working-model misspecification, potentially at higher variance. Simulations yield RMSE reductions of 34\%--49\% relative to direct estimation, with the best configuration varying across settings. An empirical application favours a cross-fitted estimator using a flexible learner under the chosen validation criterion. The numerical studies also illustrate how shrinkage can produce overly optimistic confidence intervals at the expense of strong modeling assumptions.

title: Quantum simultaneous decoding via pretty-good measurements of tilted states
abstract: A multiple-access channel transmits messages from several senders to one receiver. For quantum outputs, the receiver must distinguish states depending on all messages, while tests for different decoding errors may not commute. In this paper, we give a self-contained account of simultaneous decoding, in which one joint measurement recovers the messages at the established achievable rates using independent codebooks. The proof combines Sen's tilted-subspace method with Cheng's analysis of the pretty-good measurement, a standard measurement for distinguishing quantum states. Auxiliary labels close to a common reference state separate the geometric directions associated with different errors. A Gram-matrix bound then allows separately chosen binary tests to certify the performance of one measurement. The labels are removed from the completed decoder, leading to a deterministic packing theorem that applies to finite state ensembles, including unequal priors. We develop the two-sender case first, with worked examples and figures, before treating any fixed number of senders. Sharper finite-error guarantees for the same decoder are developed separately, with sharp bounds for two specified steps of the analysis rather than a claim of globally optimal decoding. Applications recover known achievable rates for unassisted and entanglement-assisted classical communication, distributed classical compression with quantum side information, and coherent-state communication through a beamsplitter or passive multiport device. The common proof makes the geometric mechanism and its quantitative consequences available without repeating the construction for each application.

title: A Khintchine type inequality for non-independent random variables
abstract: In this short note we give a Khintchine-type inequality involving non-independentrandom variables. The basic setting is inspired by Breuer-Major theorem and the proof is based on a hypercontractivity argument.

title: The $\lambda$-chain condition for unit interval determinantal fiber rings
abstract: It is shown that certain finite partially ordered sets arising from unit interval determinantal facet ideals satisfy the $\lambda$-chain condition. In addition, their applications to commutative algebra are briefly discussed.

title: Exact Privacy--Distortion Design of Support-Constrained Randomized Response
abstract: Full-support local randomizers can incur unnecessary reporting distortion on ordered alphabets. We study randomized response whose output is restricted to a radius-$t$ neighborhood of the private input. Input-dependent supports create privacy leakage at their boundaries, so ordinary likelihood-ratio calibration is no longer sufficient. Under approximate local privacy restricted to input pairs at distance at most $H$, we derive the exact hockey-stick defect of the mechanism. We then solve the joint design of the truthful probability, off-truth probability, and support radius. The fixed-radius optimum is available in closed form, while the global optimum requires only a one-dimensional integer search. We characterize both the privacy floor and its inverse, namely the smallest defect attainable under a reporting-distortion budget. We further prove that stringent approximate privacy forces the support size to scale as $\Omega(H/\delta)$. Deterministic evaluations illustrate the resulting tradeoff.

title: Robust Nonparametric Methods for $\alpha$-Mixing Sequences via Median-of-Means
abstract: The median-of-means (MoM) estimator is a robust alternative to the sample mean for heavy-tailed or contaminated data. While its non-asymptotic properties are well understood for i.i.d.\ samples, much less is known for dependent sequences. We establish non-asymptotic deviation bounds for the MoM estimator computed from consecutive blocks of an identically distributed $\alpha$-mixing sequence, both for a single mean and uniformly over a class of functions (the median-of-means process). All bounds remain valid, with explicitly adjusted constants, when a sufficiently small fraction of the blocks is adversarially corrupted. As applications, we obtain deviation bounds for a median-of-means Nadaraya--Watson regression estimator, for the MoM kernel density estimator, and for empirical and Bahadur-type estimators of Value-at-Risk and Conditional Value-at-Risk. Finally, we show that the sampling of bulk materials, where the measurements form a spatially dependent random field, reduces to the one-dimensional setting if the samples are taken in well-separated groups.

title: Embedding Information in Policy Randomness: Distribution-Preserving Implicit Communication in MDPs
abstract: This paper investigates a new role of randomness in stochastic policies--as a medium for embedding and communicating information. Specifically, we consider an agent interacting with an environment according to a prescribed stochastic policy. By carefully modulating the random action realizations of the policy, information can be embedded into the agent's behavior without altering the prescribed action distribution. We cast this problem as a channel coding problem, in which the controlled system implicitly serves as a communication channel. We then propose a coding scheme, termed posterior-matching randomness modulation (PRAM), that selects actions according to the message to be transmitted. With the aid of common randomness independent of the control system, PRAM preserves the prescribed action distribution for every state and every message. We further prove that PRAM is asymptotically reliable: the message can be decoded with arbitrarily small error probability as the observed state trajectory becomes sufficiently long. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in applications including multi-bit policy watermarking and trajectory provenance.

title: Nonlinear twists of Rankin-Selberg coefficients in the eigenvalue aspect
abstract: Let $g$ be a fixed primitive Hecke--Maass cusp form, and let $f$ vary with spectral parameter $k_f=K$, at a fixed level and with trivial nebentypus. We study smooth sums of $\lambda_f(n)\lambda_g(n)e(\alpha n^\beta)$ for fixed real $\alpha\ne0$. The crucial input is the smooth spectral second moment of Lau, Liu, and Ye, for which the window length can be taken to be $L=K^{1/3+a}$ for arbitrarily small fixed $a>0$. We show that, for every $\kappa>0$, there is $\beta_0>0$ such that the sum is $O(K^{2/3+\kappa}X^{1/2})$ for $1\le X\le K^2$ and $0<\beta\le\beta_0$. We give a detailed Baire category argument which makes the dependence on the smooth weight uniform through one finite derivative norm. A second argument keeps the phase explicit, applies Voronoi summation and shifted convolution estimates, and gives the numerical bound $O(K^{423/224+(5/7)\beta+\varepsilon})$ at $X=K^2$ for $0<\beta<5/32$.

title: A Sharp Lower Bound for Integral Menger Curvature
abstract: We prove that round circles $C_L$ are the unique minimisers of integral Menger curvature among embedded closed $C^1$ curves $\gamma$ of prescribed length $L$ for every $p\geq 2$, i.e. $M_p(C_L) \leq M_p(\gamma)$, with equality if and only if $\gamma$ parametrises a round circle. The proof combines a three-point symmetrisation, an analysis of diagonal truncations, and the periodic Wirtinger inequality. For $p>3$, known self-avoidance and regularity results extend the minimisation result to closed rectifiable curves without assuming embeddedness or smoothness, provided the length of the curve image equals $L$. In particular, $M_p$ detects the unknot and is basic for $p>3$, thereby answering a question posed repeatedly in the literature.

title: Adaptive Confidence Sets for Nonparametric Density Estimation under Local Differential Privacy
abstract: In nonparametric density estimation without privacy constraints, it is known that a confidence set whose coverage holds uniformly over a `rough' class of regularity $r\geq0$ can simultaneously attain, in $L^2$-diameter, the minimax rate over a smaller, smoother class of regularity $s>r$ if and only if $s \le 2r$. We study such adaptive honest confidence sets under non-interactive $\alpha$-local differential privacy (LDP) constraints. Our main result is that, for bounded $\alpha$, such `smooth-rate adaptation' is now possible if and only if $s \le 4r/3$. In this smaller range we construct an honest private confidence set whose diameter is of the private minimax order on each of the two classes. As in the non-private case, the threshold arises because an honest set cannot, at a smooth density, be narrower than the separation rate arising in a related testing problem. Under LDP we prove that this private testing rate is of order $(n\alpha^2)^{-2r/(4r+3)}$, which is at most the private estimation rate $(n\alpha^2)^{-s/(2s+2)}$ over the smooth class exactly when $s \le 4r/3$. For $s > 4r/3$, however, we show that smooth-rate adaptation becomes possible once one discards from the rough class the densities that lie outside the smooth class but within an $L^2$-radius of the order of the private testing rate.

title: Stability of Diophantine Minimal Foliations in Arbitrary Codimension
abstract: We generalize Moser's stability theorem for minimal hypersurface foliations to arbitrary codimension. Let $\mathbb{T}^N=\mathbb{R}^N/\mathbb{Z}^N$ be the standard torus, and let $P\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be an $m$-plane satisfying a Diophantine condition relative to $\mathbb{Z}^N$. We prove that, under every sufficiently small smooth $\mathbb{Z}^N$-periodic perturbation of the Euclidean metric, the affine foliation of $\mathbb{T}^N$ induced by $P$ persists as a smoothly conjugate foliation by minimal $m$-dimensional submanifolds. The normalized conjugating displacement depends smoothly and tamely on the metric and is locally unique. The proof uses Hamilton's formulation of the Nash-Moser implicit function theorem.

title: Zero density in short strips and short-interval bounds toward Hypothesis S
abstract: We deduce zero-density estimates in short vertical strips from short-interval moments of globally tempered automorphic $L$-functions, by adapting the large-value estimate of Guth and Maynard and the Type II zero argument of Maynard and Pratt to the framework of Ye and Zhang. For the Riemann zeta function, we obtain $N_\zeta(\sigma;T,T+T^a)\ll T^{15a(1-\sigma)/(3+5\sigma)+\varepsilon}$ for $2/3\le a\le1$ and $7/10\le\sigma\le4/5$, improving Ye--Zhang's exponent in the interior of this range. Combining the localized density bound with the recent quasi-Riemann theorems, we estimate smoothed prime-power sums with phase $\exp(2\pi i\alpha n^\beta)$ on intervals of length $K^\delta$. For $0<\beta<13/20$, we obtain a power saving whenever $\max\{17/30,1-\beta\}<\delta<1$; in particular the square-root phase admits every $\delta>17/30$. A revised transform estimate retains both the stationary spread and the Fourier width $K/L$. For example, the bound at $\beta=1/2$, $\delta=3/5$ is $K^{15/26+\varepsilon}$, uniformly for frequencies $m\alpha$ with $1\le m\le K^{1/10}$. We also retain power savings for certain self-dual $GL(2)$ twists and self-dual $GL(3)$ cusp forms, without assuming Ramanujan. All three applications have explicit frequency dependence.

title: $(\alpha,\mathfrak{c})$-spaceability of continuous functions with prescribed Hausdorff graph dimension
abstract: Let $1<s\le2$ and let $H_{s}[0,1]$ consist of the real-valued continuous functions on $[0,1]$ whose graphs have Hausdorff dimension $s$. We prove that every finite-dimensional subspace $E\subset C[0,1]$ with $E\setminus\{0\}\subset H_{s}[0,1]$ is contained in a closed complemented subspace isomorphic to $c_0$, all of whose nonzero elements still belong to $H_{s}[0,1]$. This settles a question of Liu, Shi and Zhang. We also obtain the exact criterion: $H_{s}[0,1]$ is $(\alpha,\mathfrak{c})$-spaceable precisely when $\alpha$ is finite. We also show that every admissible finite-dimensional subspace is contained in a dense subspace of Hamel dimension $\mathfrak{c}$ whose nonzero elements have the same prescribed graph dimension. This also recovers maximal pointwise dense-lineability of $H_{s}[0,1]$.

title: Multiscale Sequential Auditing of Quantile Regression with Point Masses
abstract: For discrete outcomes, a valid conditional quantile can have a hit probability different from its nominal level. Errors in different covariate groups can also cancel when residual signs are pooled. We study sequential audits that address both problems by testing the two inequalities that define quantile-set membership. The audit records whether each response falls below, equals, or exceeds its forecast. We derive the information projection for this three-outcome experiment and use continuous betting mixtures within the cells of a covariate tree. Context-tree weighting combines the resulting audits over all prunings, with an explicit finite-path oracle bound. Under iid alternatives with uniformly positive sign probabilities, a countable mixture of refining trees attains the full conditional sign-information rate. A matching upper bound shows that no valid evidence sequence based on the same observations can attain a larger almost-sure exponential rate. We also bound the information lost through covariate coarsening, derive a recurrence for the local mixtures, and discuss quantile selection and confidence-sequence inversion. Simulations show how partition resolution affects detection, and a held-out count-data example illustrates the difference between quantile validity and exact-hit calibration.

title: Dot actions and Hessenberg spaces for dihedral groups
abstract: Splines on Weyl groups model the equivariant cohomology of regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties, and the natural group action on them encodes the monodromy action. The resulting representations are of great interest in algebraic combinatorics for their connections to Hecke algebra characters, LLT polynomials, and chromatic symmetric functions. We study the analogous construction for dihedral groups, which in general have no underlying geometry. Using purely algebraic methods, we show that these spline modules are free, construct explicit bases, and compute their Hilbert series, recovering the familiar properties of the geometric setting. We also determine the associated dihedral group representations completely. Unlike what is conjectured for the symmetric group case, these need not be permutation representations.

title: On bass orders in division algebras
abstract: A result by F.-T. Tu dating from 2011 states that the orders in a local matrix algebra of dimension four that can be written as a finite intersection of maximal orders are those having an Eichler Gorenstein closure. In a more recent paper, we gave a similar characterization for orders with a Bass Gorenstein closure. More precisely, we prove that these orders are the ones that can be written as a ghost intersection, i.e., the set of points defined over the base field of an intersection of maximal orders that is defined over a field extension. Although we proved this result only for the local four-dimensional matrix algebra, the statement makes sense also for a local quaternion division algebra, since the latter turns into a matrix algebra when we extend the base field to an even degree extension. In this work, we prove an analog of our previous result in the latter setting.

title: Low Lying Zeros of Dedekind Zeta Functions
abstract: Let $K$ be a number field of degree $n_K$, and let $h(K)$ denote the smallest absolute value of the imaginary part of a non-trivial zero of its Dedekind zeta function. In 1979, Hoffstein proved the unconditional bound $h(K)\leq 0.87+o(1)$ as $n_K\to\infty$. In a 1990 survey article, Odlyzko stated without proof that a different kernel in Weil's explicit formula could produce $h(K)\leq 0.54+o(1)$. No further improvement on Hoffstein's $0.87$ threshold accompanied by a published proof has since appeared. We choose a linear kernel and first show that Hoffstein's original parameters already yield the improved constant $0.825$. We then generalise his linear kernel method using Stechkin's trick and prove the unconditional bound $h(K)\leq 0.6+o(1)$ as $n_K\to\infty$, giving the best proved asymptotic bound to date.

title: Planar intrusions from a narrow, jet-like source in a linearly stratified ambient
abstract: We present two and three dimensional direct numerical simulations of planar intrusions injected from a continuously supplied, narrow source into a linearly stratified ambient at the level of neutral buoyancy. The evolution passes through three phases. A laminar leading vortex dipole first advances at constant speed with a varicose wave train behind it; the trailing jet then undergoes a sinuous instability whose initial growth rate and wavelength agree with inviscid unstratified planar-jet theory evaluated on the local jet; the flow finally relaxes into a buoyancy-controlled wedge whose area grows linearly in time. Three-dimensional simulations show that the transition remains organized by the planar instability, while three-dimensionality reshapes the near-source region into a slowly evolving, actively mixing zone that entrains an additional twenty to one hundred percent of the source flux depending on source width. Rescaled with this measured effective flux, the downstream intrusion collapses reasonably well onto the similarity solution for a wide-source intrusion.

title: On infinite knot families with the same HOMFLYPT polynomial
abstract: In this paper, we focus on the examples constructed by Kanenobu and provide new family knots with the same HOMFLYPT polynomial invariants, which are distinguished by the Kauffman polynomial.

title: A Mean Field Model of Consumption Inertia and Keeping Up with the Joneses
abstract: Households compare their living standard with others' and dislike changing it. We study consumption and investment when felicity depends on consumption relative to a benchmark, the population's geometric average consumption, and cuts in felicity weigh more than increases. Asset returns are exogenous. For finitely many types and arbitrary initial wealth and inherited standards, a mean field equilibrium exists under a weak interaction condition, and for fixed budget multipliers the benchmark is the fixed point of a contraction. In a complete market with common risk, a mean field equilibrium at empirical type frequencies is an exact Nash equilibrium of the finite game, for any preferences over relative consumption. We bound the gain from deviating when plans computed at another composition are used. We compute equilibria in which groups with different wealth, inherited standards, and loss aversion revise spending at different dates. With identical households and common risk, the unique symmetric equilibrium is the policy of a single loss averse household with modified curvature. In a baseline example, ignoring the inherited standard costs up to 17% of wealth, while small errors about the composition of the reference group cost less than 0.5%.

title: When Does Compensating Inherited Quantization Error Help? Mean-Square Guarantees for Layer-Wise Quantization and Their Limits
abstract: Layer-wise post-training quantization methods let each layer compensate for the quantization error inherited from earlier layers. We ask under what assumptions such compensation guarantees a network output error no larger than without it. For linear networks of any depth, with the required calibration Gram matrices invertible, if the rounding error of each layer has zero conditional mean and a deterministic second-moment map common to both schemes, as under subtractive dither on an unbounded grid, then compensation with strengths in $[0,1]$ fixed in advance gives a mean-square output error no larger than no compensation, each scheme being followed along its own trajectory. The exact gain separates error removed directly from reduced excitation of later rounding noise. Outside this setting the comparison can fail. With rectified linear activations it fails for two independent reasons: noise changes activation states, and, even when no state changes, the correction moves error from samples on which a unit is inactive to samples on which it is active. With stable activations, commutators between the calibration projection and the activation patterns bound the excess.
