We then construct the adjunctions for univalentization and Hermitian completion and identify univalentization with unitary completion.

title: Square integrable representations and Hecke eigenvalues over a local non-archimedian field
abstract: Let $G$ be a split connected semi-simple group over a local non-archimedean field $F$. In this paper we study the action of Hecke operators on the Schwartz space of half-densities on the moduli stack $\bpo$ of $G$-bundles on ${\mathbb P}^1$ endowed with a trivialization at $0$ and $\infty$. This space is a representation of $G(F)\times G(F)$ which contains the regular representation of $G(F)$. We show that this inclusion is an isomorphism on the cuspidal part. In addition we show that every irreducible square-integrable representation $\pi$ of $G(F)$ defines a Hecke eigenvalue. As a byproduct we show that every irreducible square-integrable representation of $G(F)$ with an Iwahori fixed vector defines a ${\mathbb C}$-point on the Calogero-Moser space associated to $G$. We also show that for $G=PGL(N)$ the eigenvalues of certain "simplest non-trivial" Hecke operators are essentially equal to the values of the character of $\pi$ on regular elliptic elements. These results are parallel to some of the results of our previous publication where some analogous statements are proved in the case when $F$ is a finite field.

title: Kinetic SDEs and kinetic Fokker-Planck equations with critical Morrey-type drifts, and local blow-ups
abstract: We develop a Sobolev theory for the kinetic Fokker-Planck equation subject to a singular Morrey-form $L^\infty+M^q_K$ force field which can produce local blow-ups due to strong attraction to a submanifold. Our approach is based on the fractional representation for the Duhamel series of the equation and on establishing kinetic Adams-type estimates. Accordingly, we construct weak solutions of Brownian-driven kinetic SDEs in a critical Morrey set-up, obtain kinetic Krylov-type estimates and a strongly continuous Feller propagator, and establish uniqueness criteria for a large class of weak solutions.

title: Arithmetic jet spaces and the unramified Zilber--Pink conjecture for subvarieties of abelian varieties
abstract: We show how the methods of delta geometry can be used to bound the degree of points in the Zilber--Pink locus of a subvariety of an abelian variety, if the varieties are defined over a number field and we restrict to points with bounded ramification at a fixed prime.

title: DynaSPLIT: Strong tail-optimal scheduling for the M/G/n with heavy-tailed job sizes
abstract: We study the asymptotic response time tail in the M/G/n queue with heavy-tailed (regularly varying) job sizes. For this setting, strongly tail optimal policies are known only at lower load, where n-1 servers suffice for stability. At higher load, the tail optimal scheduling has been open. This paper presents DynaSPLIT, the first strongly tail optimal policy at high load. Together with prior work, this result shows that strong tail optimality is achievable across the entire stability region of the M/G/n with heavy-tailed job sizes.

title: On the rank-one limit sets for maps in the constant-Jacobian shear group of $\mathbb{C}^2$
abstract: Let $\mathcal{S}_c$ be the subgroup of $Aut(\mathbb{C}^2)$ generated by affine maps and shear automorphisms with constant Jacobian. We determine the possible conformal types of the rank-one limit set of an invariant recurrent Fatou component when the induced dynamics has infinite order. In particular we show that, under this infinite-order hypothesis, the limit set of a finite composition of H\'enon maps (polynomial or transcendental), can only be conformally equivalent to a disk or an annulus. Thus we exclude the remaining three conformal types, i.e. $\mathbb{D}^*$, $\mathbb{C}^*$ and $\mathbb{C}$, from the classification result by Arosio, Benini, Forn\ae ss and Peters. We also prove that the set of fixed points of a finite composition of H\'enon maps (polynomial or transcendental) contains no entire curves.

title: Vanishing Events and Regularity-Conditioned Reachability in Linear Stieltjes Systems
abstract: We study linear Stieltjes control systems in which actuation is concentrated at finitely many temporal events, and we ask what happens when one of those events progressively loses its atomic weight in the associated Stieltjes measure. For constant coefficients, ordinary finite-atomic reachability is governed by a truncated Krylov space and is therefore insensitive to the positive values of the event weights. A different picture emerges once trajectory regularity is imposed. In the supercritical super-$g$-H\"older regime, we minimize the largest event-normalized state jump and characterize exactly the terminal directions for which this cost remains uniformly bounded as a prescribed event weight tends to zero. The characterization combines what can be reached before the vulnerable event, a drift-cancellability condition at that event, and the directions that remain available afterwards. Ordinary reachability of the deleted-event system can therefore be strictly larger than bounded-cost reachability in the singular limit. We also separate two mechanisms of divergence: loss of ordinary reachability after deletion and failure of the intermediate compatibility condition. For compatible targets, the minimum cost converges to a constrained deleted-event problem. A dimensionless position--velocity benchmark motivated by pulsed proximity maneuvers shows the distinction explicitly.

title: Higher derivatives of the Gram function
abstract: We study the nonlinear phenomenon of the asymptotics of higher-order derivatives of the Gram function $t_u$. We also prove the uniform distribution and continuous uniform distribution modulo one of $t^n_u$ for $n = 1, 2, \dots$. We use AI to formalize our proofs in Lean.
comments: 11 pages. Submitted for publication on August 27, 2026

title: A Gordon--Green-type result for Gorenstein-projective modules
abstract: Let \(\Lambda\) be a \(\Z\)-graded Artin algebra which is Iwanaga--Gorenstein. We prove that \(\Lambda\) is CM-finite if and only if the category of gradable Gorenstein-projective modules has finite type, and if and only if the lengths of the indecomposable gradable Gorenstein-projective modules are bounded. Moreover, if \(\Lambda\) is CM-finite, then every Gorenstein-projective \(\Lambda\)-module is gradable. These results provide Gorenstein-projective analogues of the corresponding theorems of Gordon--Green for graded Artin algebras of finite representation type.

title: Yang-Baxter deformed sigma models on $\mathrm{SU}(N)/\mathrm{SO}(N)$
abstract: We study Yang--Baxter deformations of two-dimensional sigma models on compact symmetric spaces $\mathrm{SU}(N)/\mathrm{SO}(N)$, with particular emphasis on their ultraviolet behavior. We claim that the ultraviolet fixed point is described by the $\mathrm{SO}(N,\mathbb C)/\mathrm{SO}(N,\mathbb R)$ non-compact WZW model together with $N-1$ compact free bosons. We determine the leading correction to this fixed point and identify it with the perturbation generated by the corresponding screening currents. We also extend our construction to the broader class of symmetric spaces of maximal rank.

title: Large Network limit for Latent Variable Process Models with Endogeneously Evolving Interactions among Multiple Types
abstract: Motivated by the opinion and social dynamics literature, we rigorously study dynamically co-evolving latent space network models, where agent opinions evolve based on a latent state space model influenced by and influencing an underlying dynamically evolving graph determining their interactions. In contrast to earlier work, see [18], agents are allowed to be heterogeneous, i.e., of different types, and their dynamic evolution can capture behaviors like attraction and repulsion between and within groups. In addition, the model encodes bidirectional feedback between the latent process and the underlying interaction network, persistence effects are included, and the interactions are localized, i.e., individual agents do not have global information. We produce weak and empirical limit theorems that encode the asymptotic joint distribution of agent opinion trajectories and their interaction network. In doing so, we describe and exploit the complex dependence structure of the model.

title: Global Extendability of Flat Cliques in Sparse Moment Relaxations
abstract: Moment relaxations provide lower bounds for polynomial optimization problems, while the moment matrix carries more information than the bound itself. When the moment matrix satisfies the flat truncation condition, the bound is tight and global minimizers can be extracted from the matrix. In correlatively sparse relaxations, it is common that only some blocks are flat. We study whether such partial flatness still reveals part of a global minimizer. On a unicycle trajectory optimization problem, repeatedly extracting the atoms of flat cliques and fixing them recovers feasible, near-optimal trajectories. We then construct a counterexample whose relaxation is tight and has a rank-one flat clique, yet the unique extracted atom cannot be extended to a global minimizer. Finally, we give sufficient conditions for global extendability that involve only the boundary of a clique. Every extracted atom minimizes its clique objective given its boundary value, and when the bound is tight and the boundary moment block has rank at most one, the extracted atom of the clique is globally extendable.

title: Beyond periodicity: Fourier methods for optimal control
abstract: Fourier-based spectral methods provide compact global approximations, permit simple differentiation and integration, and achieve spectral convergence for smooth periodic functions. Their use in finite-horizon optimal control problems (OCPs) is nevertheless challenged by the generally nonperiodic state and control trajectories: endpoint mismatch induces artificial discontinuities and can destroy spectral convergence. Leveraging Eckhoff-type endpoint-correction techniques, we develop a Fourier-based spectral framework for OCPs with possibly nonlinear dynamics and constraints. The correction improves convergence without enlarging the set of decision variables, yielding an efficient finite-dimensional numerical method. Furthermore, we formulate selected dynamics and obstacle-avoidance constraints through Sobolev residual bounds, which incorporate information about the residuals over the entire time horizon and improve constraint satisfaction. Numerical experiments on benchmark problems demonstrate competitive computational performance, lower residual errors, and improved solution accuracy.

title: Hanslick's Musical Formalism as a Mathematical Structure - Examining meaning in Music through the Lens of Category Theory
abstract: We investigate Eduard Hanslicks formalist aesthetics through the prism of Category Theory

title: A characterization of central extensions relative to n-nilpotent objects
abstract: We characterize the central extensions, in the sense of the categorical theory of central extensions of Janelidze and Kelly, relative to the Birkhoff subcategory of $n$-nilpotent objects of a semi-abelian and algebraically coherent category. An extension $f \colon A \to B$ with kernel $K$ turns out to be central precisely when the iterated Huq commutator $[A,[A,\dots,[A,K]\dots]]$, with $n$ occurrences of $A$, vanishes. For $n=2$ this condition reads $[A,[K,A]] = 0$, that is, $[K,A]$ is a central subobject of $A$. In the special case of groups this description was obtained by Everaert and the first author. The present proof is categorical, and applies in particular to Lie algebras, to crossed modules, to cocommutative Hopf algebras over a field, and to any category of interest.

title: A Method for Exact Enforcement of Boundary Conditions on General Curved Triangular Domains: Algorithm and Application to Scientific Machine Learning
abstract: We present a method for enforcing exactly Dirichlet, Neumann, and Robin conditions on general triangular domains with arbitrarily curved boundaries. The algorithmic constructions developed here complements those in a previous work for general quadrilateral domains. Our method combines (i) the exact mapping between a general curved triangular domain and the standard triangle, (ii) TFC constrained expressions, and (iii) Barnhill transfinite interpolations, to provide explicit closed-form trial ansatze that mathematically satisfy the imposed boundary conditions exactly. Corner compatibility induced by the boundary conditions is pivotal, and enforcing exactly the imposed boundary conditions hinges on the exact enforcement of the induced compatibility constraints. The corner compatibility associated with the acute vertices of the standard triangle and the coupling between gradient components when the hypotenuse corresponds to a Neumann/Robin boundary pose particular challenges. Two strategies are critical to resolving these issues, by reformulating conditional corner constraints into equivalent unconditional forms and by introducing a separate TFC-style auxiliary edge construction together with an associated linear solve on the hypotenuse. We analyze the corner compatibility constraints and present formulations for the general form of functions that exactly satisfy the imposed Dirichlet, Neumann, or Robin conditions on curved triangular domains. The proposed method has been implemented using extreme learning machine type randomized neural networks for solving PDE problems. We present ample numerical experiments with linear/nonlinear PDE problems on a variety of domains with complex boundary geometries. Numerical results show that the current method has enforced the Dirichlet, Neumann, and Robin conditions on curved domain boundaries to the machine precision.

title: Towards a Characterization of Matrix Monotonicity via Radial Convexity
abstract: The theory of matrix monotone functions of finite degree depends subtly on the matrix size. Motivated by this phenomenon, we introduce radial convexity of metrics with respect to matrix orders on the cone of positive definite matrices. We establish radial convexity of several natural metrics with respect to the Loewner order and then focus on the Frobenius norm. Using the Daleckii-Krein formula, we relate radial convexity to the positivity of the Hadamard square of the corresponding Loewner matrix. This leads us to conjecture that radial convexity of order $n$ is equivalent to matrix monotonicity of degree $n$, and we prove this equivalence in degree $2$. We further provide evidence in higher dimensions, obtain a characterization in degree $3$, and discuss extensions of our results to arbitrary unitarily invariant norms.

title: The rational homology of independence complexes of Kneser graphs on triples
abstract: The independence complex of the Kneser graph $\KG(n,k)$ is the simplicial complex of pairwise intersecting families of $n$-subsets of $[2n+k]$; equivalently, it is a Vietoris--Rips complex of the $n$-subsets of $[2n+k]$ under the symmetric-difference metric. Feng and Wang asked whether, for $n=3$, its reduced homology is nontrivial only in dimensions $6$ and $9$, and conjectured the rank in dimension $9$. We answer the question affirmatively over the rationals and determine all the associated Betti numbers. For every $k\ge0$, the only nonzero reduced Betti numbers using rationals of $\Ind(\KG(3,k))$ are \[ \beta_6=\binom{k+5}{7}+29\binom{k+6}{7} \qquad\text{and}\qquad \beta_9=\binom{k+6}{6}. \] The proof uses an inductive decomposition based on a simplicial retraction and Barmak's star clusters, Dowker duality together with Jonsson's computation of the homology of complexes of graphs with bounded covering number, and a relative Mayer--Vietoris spectral sequence which reduces the problem to the six-element sets.

title: A Controlled Null Result for Per-Gate Riemannian Optimization in VQE
abstract: Parametrized gates in a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) live on a product of unitary groups, which makes Riemannian optimization a natural candidate for improving training. We test this candidate in the clean per-gate setting: each single-qubit gate is optimized directly on U (2) and compared with Adam on an unconstrained Euler-angle chart representing the same physical gate, initialized from the same unitaries and tuned with a separate learning-rate sweep. On a validated hydrogen-chain benchmark, we find no measurable practical advantage from the Riemannian machinery. The direct manifold optimizer and the Euler-coordinate baseline are interleaved in final error and success rate; the classical coordinate baseline is not slower in iterations on the successful cells; and the choices of Riemannian metric, retraction, and momentum vector transport do not change the conclusion. We also identify four failure modes that can manufacture an apparent positive result: a trivial product-state benchmark, a projected-matrix Adam baseline that discards most of its own step, a non-unitary inherited Cayley retraction that lets the reported energy pass below the variational minimum, and a learning-rate grid whose optimum sits at its boundary. Each failure mode produced a plausible multi-seed result in our own workflow before being caught. The practical output of this paper is therefore a controlled null result and a validation checklist for VQE optimizer comparisons.

title: Fresnel scattering for open waveguide networks
abstract: This paper concerns the Helmholtz scattering problem for open waveguide networks, extending the analysis from [arXiv:2302.04353, arXiv:2310.05816, arXiv:2401.04674] to plane-wave incident data. We first reduce the problem to a Fredholm second-kind integral equation on an infinite interface. This produces an integral representation of the solution to the original scattering problem, which is then used to obtain detailed asymptotic estimates of the solution at infinity. To leading order and away from the waveguides, the scattered field is itself a plane wave. Its amplitude and phase shift exhibit a jump across a critical polar angle depending on the direction of the incident plane-wave. Our estimates also imply that the scattered field is outgoing in a weak sense, allowing us to establish a uniqueness result. We conclude by calculating the waveguide-mode contributions to the scattered field in a perturbative regime.

title: Steiner Minimal Trees in the Gromov--Hausdorff Space and in Gromov--Hausdorff Clouds
abstract: We prove the existence of Steiner minimal trees spanning a finite family of metric spaces in two cases of the Gromov--Hausdorff theory. In the compact Gromov--Hausdorff space $\mathcal{M}$, every finite family of nonempty compact metric spaces is spanned by a shortest Steiner minimal tree whose Steiner vertices are again nonempty compact metric spaces. In a fixed Gromov--Hausdorff cloud $\mathcal{C}$, every finite family of proper, isometrically cobounded spaces admits a finite-length Steiner minimal tree all of whose vertices remain in $\mathcal{C}$. The compact case uses compact replacement through distance profiles and the Hausdorff hyperspace, and the cloud case uses pointed ultralimits.

title: Overlap, Not Moments: Finite-Sample Theory for Bridge Sampling
abstract: Bridge sampling estimates of marginal likelihoods are routinely reported with a delta-method Monte Carlo standard error (MCSE). Existing theory is asymptotic and cannot say whether a given run is long enough to trust the estimate or its MCSE. We give finite-sample answers. The optimal bridge estimator fits a logistic regression that separates posterior from proposal draws, and its accuracy is governed by their overlap, within a factor of two of the classification's Bayes error. Because the estimating function is a sum of bounded terms, no moment conditions are needed, and all bounds hold uniformly over targets, proposals and dimensions. A number of draws inversely proportional to the overlap suffices and is necessary in the worst case, paralleling the exponential-in-Kullback--Leibler requirement of importance sampling. A Berry--Esseen bound with an explicit constant holds at the optimal rate, and the MCSE is accurate once the effective overlap is large; it is estimated at no cost. For Markov chain draws, the required sample size grows in proportion to the sampler's relaxation time, unavoidably in the worst case. The estimated bridge, the fixed-point iteration and the fitted proposal matter only at second order, and we give free diagnostics for sampler failure and misestimated autocorrelation.

title: Purely non-free actions on Riemann surfaces
abstract: A group of conformal automorphisms of a Riemann surface is said to act purely non-free, or to produce a gpnf-action, if each of its finite-order elements has fixed points. It is known that every finite group admits a gpnf-action on a suitable closed Riemann surface of genus at least two. If $G$ is an infinite countable group, and $X$ is an infinite-type orientable surface, without planar ends and whose space of ends is self-similar, then we observe that there is a Riemann surface structure on $X$ admitting a gpnf-action by $G$. We obtain upper bounds for those finite groups producing a gpnf-action on a closed Riemann surface of genus $g \geq 2$. If $G$ is a finite group, then its purely non-free genus $\sigma^{pnf}_{hyp}(G)$ is the minimum genus of at least two of a closed Riemann surface admitting a gpnf-action by $G$. This parameter is already known for cyclic, abelian non-cyclic groups, ${\mathcal A}_{4}$, ${\mathcal A}_{5}$ and ${\mathfrak S}_{4}$. For general $G$, we provide the value of $\sigma^{pnf}_{hyp}(G)$, correcting a previous statement on this value. In particular, we observe that every genus is the purely non-free genus of some group. As an application, we describe the minimal purely non-free actions for the family of metacyclic groups $G^{0}_{s}(n)=\langle x,y: x^{n}=y^{2}=1, yxy=x^{s}\rangle,$ where $n \geq 3$ and $2 \leq s \leq n-1$ is such that $s^{2} \equiv 1 \mod(n)$.

title: Group gradings, graded identities and central polynomials of algebras with almost polynomial $\delta$-growth
abstract: The finite-dimensional $F$-algebras $D=F(e_{11}+e_{33})+Fe_{22}+Fe_{12}+Fe_{13}+Fe_{23} \subseteq UT_3$ and $D_0=Fe_{22}+Fe_{33}+Fe_{12}+Fe_{13}+Fe_{14}+Fe_{23}+Fe_{24}+Fe_{34} \subseteq UT_4$ occupy a distinguished position in the theory of central polynomials. Together with the infinite-dimensional Grassmann algebra, these algebras generate the only varieties of almost polynomial growth of proper central codimensions. We determine finite generating sets for their $T$-spaces of central polynomials and compute their central and proper central codimensions. We also prove that every group grading on $D_0$ is isomorphic to an elementary grading and determine the identities and codimensions associated with all its $\mathbb{Z}_2$-gradings.

title: On the generators of separable unital C*-algebras
abstract: Using the recent single-generation theorem for von Neumann $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors with separable predual, we prove the following results on the generators of a separable unital C*-algebra. Let $A$ be a separable unital C*-algebra, and suppose that $\partial \mathrm{T}(A)$ is nonempty, compact, and zero-dimensional. Then (1) If $A$ has strict comparison of positive elements by tracial states, then $A$ can be generated by two ordinary elements. (2) If $A$ has real rank zero and $A$ has strict comparison of projections by tracial states, then $A$ is singly generated. In this case, its single generators form a norm-dense $G_\delta$ subset of $A$. (3) If $A$ has strict comparison of positive elements by tracial states and there is a unitary $u\in A$ such that for every $\tau\in \partial \mathrm{T}(A)$, (a): the spectral distribution of $u$ with respect to $\tau$ is atomless and has full support on $\mathbb T$, and (b): for every $a\in A$, $$\lim_{t \to 0}\sup_{p\in D_\tau, 0<\tau(p)\leq t} \| p\bigl(\pi_\tau(a)-\mathbb E_{D_\tau}(\pi_\tau(a))\bigr)p\|=0, $$ where $M_\tau=\pi_\tau(A)''$, $D_\tau=\pi_\tau(u)''$, $\mathbb E_{D_\tau}: M_\tau \to D_\tau$ is the trace-preserving conditional expectation, and $\pi_\tau$ is the GNS representation associated to $\tau$, then $A$ is singly generated. In particular, Conclusion (3) above implies that the reduced group C*-algebra $\mathrm{C}_r^*(\mathbb F_n)$ is singly generated for every $n\in\{2,3,\ldots,\infty\}$.
comments: Preliminary version, 38 pages. The work is carried out using ChatGPT, and is based on the recent result on the generators of von Neumann algebras

title: Plane Cremona maps preserving a Euclidean volume form
abstract: We give a presentation by generators and relations of the group of birational transformations of the plane preserving a differential form with poles along a triple line. This group strictly contains the automorphism group of the affine plane.

title: Model theory of quasitracial $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras and the absoluteness of monotone completeness
abstract: We examine various applications of logic to $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras, particularly the monotone completeness conjecture. We develop a model theory for $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras equipped with a faithful normalized quasitrace. Using this language, we provide a separable coding which allows us to reduce the finite case of the monotone completeness conjecture to monotone sequential completeness of $\mathrm{II}_1$ $\mathrm{AW}^*$-factors. Combining an explicit recursive axiomatization with the completeness theorem for continuous logic, we show that this case of the conjecture, and Kaplansky's problem whether every $\mathrm{AW}^*$-factor of type $\mathrm{II}_1$ is a von Neumann algebra, are each equivalent in ZFC to a $\Pi^0_2$ sentence of arithmetic, so that their answers are the same in every $\omega$-model of ZFC. We also consider real $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras. Here the Baer-$*$-ring notion of an abelian projection must be distinguished from commutativity; following the real-operator-algebra terminology we call the former semi-abelian. Handelman's matrix theorem implies that a real $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebra with no nonzero central semi-abelian projection has $\mathrm{AW}^*$ complexification. We answer a number of other open problems in real $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras.

title: Linear Laurent phenomenon algebras are of finite type
abstract: Laurent phenomenon algebras generalise cluster algebras by allowing irreducible exchange polynomials in place of binomials. Lam and Pylyavskyy proved finite type for those arising from graphs and conjectured that the same holds for every Laurent phenomenon algebra admitting a linear seed. We prove this conjecture over an arbitrary unique factorisation domain. Our proof constructs a nonzero element of the upper algebra divisible by every cluster variable. Comparing noninitial cluster variables with the prime factors of this element in the initial Laurent ring bounds the number of cluster variable classes and yields a finite normalised mutation pattern.

title: Spectral Self-Concordant Barriers: A Proof of a Conjecture by Tun\c{c}el
abstract: Let $Q \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be a open, convex, and symmetric set and let $f:Q \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be a $\vartheta$-self-concordant barrier function, that is also symmetric. We show the associated spectral function $F(X)= \mathcal{O}^2 (f \circ \lambda)(X)$ is a $\mathcal{O}^2\vartheta$-self-concordant function, where $\mathcal{O} = 8\max\{1+3\vartheta, 12\}$, on the domain of all $n \times n$ symmetric matrices $X$, with eigenvalues $\lambda(X) \in Q$. This generalizes the relationship between the standard logarithmic barriers $-\sum_{i=1}^n\log x_i$ and $-\log \det X$ and gives a solution to a conjecture by L.~Tun\c{c}el, 1995.

title: Effect of Spherical Parameter Space on Number of Non-Forgetting Tasks and Capacity of Continual Learning
abstract: We propose a continuous learning formulation for $T$ non-forgetting tasks with the spherical parameter space $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}(\sqrt{d})$ in asymptotic regime $d\rightarrow \infty$. Each task $i$ has an optimum $\bm{\Theta}_i$, minimizing its corresponding loss function $R_i(\bm{w})$ on sphere. We reduce each task $i$ to an acceptable loss region modeled by a geodesic ball $B_{\bm{\Theta}_i}(r_i(d))$ on $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}(\sqrt{d})$ centered at $\bm{\Theta}_i$ with radius $r_i(d)$. To model task dependencies (similarities), task optima $\bm{\Theta}_i$ are distributed by a Neyman-Scott clustered point process $\Phi$. Cluster centers $\{\bm{Y}_j\}_{j=1}^{N_p}$ form a homogeneous Poisson point process on sphere, while intra-cluster task optima follow a von Mises-Fisher distribution with mean $\bm{Y}_j$ and concentration $\kappa$. Each task $t\in \{1, ..., T\}$ learning algorithm is considered to be a channel $Q_{t}(\mathrm{d}\bm{w}_t | \bm{w}_{t-1}, \mathcal{K}_{t-1}(\bm{\theta}_{1:t-1}), \bm{\theta}_t)$, where $\bm{W}_t$ is the learned parameter of task $t$ and $\mathcal{K}_{t-1}(\bm{\Theta}_{1:t-1})=\bigcap_{i=1}^{t-1}B_{\bm{\Theta}_i}(r_i(d))$. Since in continual learning, the learner does not need to reach $\bm{\Theta}_t$ exactly to successfully learn task $t$, to avoid forgetting as well as reliable learning, it only needs for the learned parameter vector $\bm{W}_{t}$ to enter $B_{\bm{\Theta}_t}(r_t(d)) \cap \mathcal{K}_{t-1}(\bm{\Theta}_{1:t-1})$. Using this model, we derive an upper bound on $T$ ensuring $\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{K}_{T}(\bm{\Theta}_{1:T}) \neq \emptyset] \rightarrow 1$ as $d\rightarrow \infty$ and $\kappa/d \rightarrow \alpha$, where $\alpha>0$ is a constant. Finally, for $T$ tasks sampled uniformly from $\Phi$, we derive an upper bound for total information theoretic capacity under the non-forgetting constraint for each task.

title: Norm properties of quantum uniformity measures
abstract: We prove that for $k=4$ the quantum uniformity measures are norms, whereas for every $k\geq5$ the triangle inequality fails. This gives a complete answer to an open question of Bu, Gu, and Jaffe. The $k=4$ case is proved using the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality for the quantum uniformity pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{Q^4}$ introduced here, together with the triangle inequality in a suitable finite-dimensional Bochner $L^8$ space. For $k\geq5$, we construct systems of linear equations over a finite field and derive a contradiction from the structure theory of norming linear systems.

title: Functional Projection and Complexity Reduction
abstract: T\"ornquist (arXiv:1310.3250) proved that if there exists a $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^1_2$ maximal almost disjoint (MAD) family, then there exists a $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_1$ MAD family. Since then, several other "complexity reduction" proofs have been found for other combinatorial objects, such as maximal independent families or ultrafilters. All of these proofs have relied on $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_1$-uniformization, so they did not easily lift to higher projective levels. In this paper, we introduce a principle weaker than Uniformization which we call "Functional Projection", and show that this principle is sufficient for most complexity reduction proofs. On the other hand, we prove that in $L[U]$, the canonical inner model for a measurable cardinal, Functional Projection holds for $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_2$ relations. As an immediate corollary, we obtain that in $L[U]$ there are $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_2$ witnesses for many combinatorial families.

title: Co-Adaptive Entropy Modeling and Rate-Distortion-Optimal Bit Allocation for Perceptual Audio Coding
abstract: We present a perceptual audio coder in which the entropy-coding model and the bit allocation co-adapt across blocks without model side information. Mantissas are coded by a hybrid of bit packing and arithmetic coding with per-band probability models learned online. Encoder and decoder accumulate identical histograms from decoded blocks and advance the same model state. The model enters bit allocation directly: per-band rate--distortion frontiers combine measured perceptual distortion with entropy-coded rate estimates under the current model, and a dynamic program attains the exact minimum of total objective perceptual distortion for each block's budget under the model's rate estimates, with reservoir carry-over. Under a strict per-block rate, entropy-coding-aware bit allocation lowers this distortion (band noise-to-mask ratio in linear scale) by 15-24% relative to the same solver without it, and co-adaptation removes a further 3-4% (up to 15% on oboe) that a backward-adaptive coder alone cannot realize in one pass; a MUSHRA test at 80 kbps per channel confirms the ranking.

title: Optimal Feature-Based Newsvendor Policies under Censored Demand
abstract: We investigate a newsvendor problem where a decision-maker observes a $z$-dimensional vector of covariates, and wants to learn how much stock to order given a sample of size $n$ of censored demand data to minimize costs. Demand is censored when insufficient stock is available to meet it, and past stocking quantities are known. We propose a new model-agnostic loss function approach to estimate optimal order quantities using observational data, and characterize the optimal newsvendor policy as the policy that minimizes our proposed loss function. Our method requires only a single estimation step, can be scaled to datasets with hundreds of thousands of data points, and does not suffer from the same instabilities as inverse censoring probability weighting methods. We describe how this loss function can be implemented in linear empirical risk minimization, kernel weights optimization and deep neural network algorithms, and provide excess risk generalization bounds for their out-of-sample performance. Moreover, we show through numerical experiments that our method quickly converges to the optimal policy on synthetic data, and leads to improved performance on real world retail data.

title: Compactness of Cone Yang-Mills Connections
abstract: We consider the cone Yang-Mills functional recently introduced by Tseng and Zhou. This functional generalizes the Yang-Mills functional by coupling it to a closed 2-form which can represent a geometric structure of interest, e.g. a symplectic form or Ricci form. While the perspective of dimensional reduction is not always possible, we show that a cone Yang-Mills field is always locally the dimensional reduction of a pure Yang-Mills field. We then prove a monotonicity formula and use the dimensional reduction framework to prove an $\epsilon$-regularity theorem in two ways. Finally, we prove a compactness theorem for sequences of cone Yang-Mills connections with bounded action and $L^p$-bounded Higgs fields. Away from a singular set of codimension at least 4 and after suitable bundle identifications, the sequence subconverges in the $C^\infty_{\operatorname{loc}}$-topology.

title: $a$-Numbers, higher Cartier ranks and maximality of van der Geer-van der Vlugt curves
abstract:
Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $C_R$ be the van der Geer-van der Vlugt curve $y^p-y=xR(x)$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$, where $R(x)=\sum_{i=0}^{h}a_ix^{p^i}$ is an additive polynomial of degree $p^h$. We determine the image and the rank of every power of the Cartier operator $\Cart$ on $H^0(C_R,\Omg)$. For $1\le r\le h-1$ the image of $\Cart^r$ is spanned by an explicit set of monomial differentials that does not depend on $R$, and $ank(\Cart^r)=p^{h-r-1} inom{p+r}{r+2}$. The last iterate detects the linear coefficient: $ank(\Cart^h)=0$ if $a_0=0$ and $ank(\Cart^h)= inom{(p-1)/2+h}{h+1}$ if $a_0
eq0$, so the nilpotency index of $\Cart$ is $h$ or $h+1$. Hence, for $h\ge2$, the loci $a_0=0$ and $a_0
e0$ have the same $a$-number, which is the largest $a$-number of a one-point Artin-Schreier curve with pole order $p^h+1$, but they share no Ekedahl-Oort type. Over finite fields we deduce that a curve over $\F_{p^{2n}}$ that is geometrically isomorphic to $C_R$ can be $\F_{p^{2n}}$-maximal or $\F_{p^{2n}}$-minimal only if $n\ge h$, and only if $n\ge h+1$ when $a_0
eq0$. Explicit examples show that the second bound is attained for $(p,h)=(3,1)$, $(3,2)$ and $(5,2)$.

title: Balancing cost and demand in a smart grid - a mean-field game analysis
abstract: In a smart grid, consumers can also play the role of producers and sellers of energy. Therefore, the control of a smart grid over time becomes a dynamic game with a large number of small players and one or several large players. This is much more complicated than the control of an energy system with a single producer. The framework of mean-field games with common noise allows the transformation of such a complicated model into a control problem for a typical prosumer (producer and consumer in one) optimizing his behavior against a flow of other such prosumers. In our model, we introduce 2 decision variables for such a controller: one describing the amount of electric energy bought from the grid (or sold to it), and the second one describing the charging rate for our battery. The cost function is designed to satisfy two goals: satisfying the demand of the consumer (a single home) and minimizing the payment for energy. Players are allowed to sell/buy energy from the grid. Common noise is hidden in price volatility and sun irradiance, which influence all the players. We compute the optimal controls for our model and simulate solutions on real data. The novelty of our construction, compared to other works on smart grid control, lies in combining the minimization of the cost of energy and sustaining some level of demand satisfaction. We analyze the impact of battery usage on achieving a balance between these two criteria. We also take into account that the smart grid is only part of the energy market, which makes consumer strategies dependent on energy consumption outside the grid.

title: Limit Theorems for the Complete Feedback Card Guessing Game
abstract: We study the optimal score $T_{n,m}$ in a complete feedback card guessing game. The deck has $n$ types and $m$ cards of each type. Its predictable compensator $S_{n,m}$ is the sum of the conditional success probabilities. We prove that Var$(S_{n,m})\leq C((\log\log n)^2+m/\log n)$, uniformly in $m$ for large $n$. This bound yields a central limit theorem for every sequence $m=m_n\geq1$ as $n\to\infty$. The score variance is asymptotic to its mean. We also give uniform Kolmogorov bounds using the conditional Bernoulli moments. For $m,n\to\infty$, the excess mean is asymptotic to $(\log n)\log\min\{m,\log n\}+(\pi/\sqrt2)\sqrt{m\log n}$. The two contributions balance at $m\asymp(\log n)(\log\log n)^2$. The variance proof uses reversed occupancy hitting times. Discrete hypergeometric tail estimates control their fluctuations in the large-deviation, Gaussian, and saturation regimes. For fixed $n$, we also show that the compensator has a Brownian-bridge functional limit as $m\to\infty$.

title: Cyclic reflections and the flip equation for the graded Grothendieck-Teichm\"uller group
abstract: Furusho, Hirose and Komiyama reformulated the pentagon equation using an involution called the flip, which led to a new characterisation of the graded Grothendieck-Teichm\"uller group $\mathsf{GRT}_1$. We show that the flip is a reflection in the cyclic structure of the operad of framed Drinfeld-Kohno Lie algebras, with the framings removed. Applying the reflection twice to the pentagon gives the two-cycle relation for every Drinfeld associator. This relation is precisely the condition for cyclic compatibility on the associativity morphism, giving a new proof that $\mathsf{GRT}_1$ acts by cyclic automorphisms of parenthesized ribbon chord diagrams.

title: Fundamental Limits of Prescribed-Time Regulation: Gain Budgets, Accuracy Frontiers, and Arrival Costs
abstract: Prescribed-time controllers drive the state to the origin at a time $T$ chosen in advance, with gains that grow without bound as $t$ approaches $T$. This paper shows the growth is a necessity and computes the exact price of avoiding it. The starting point is a simple estimate: any trajectory with $\|\dot z(t)\|\le L(t)\|z(t)\|$ satisfies $\|z(t)\|\ge\|z(0)\|e^{-\int_0^t L}$. From this: a gain profile $L$ supports exact prescribed-time convergence, over the unrestricted class of closed-loop vector fields admitting it, if and only if its integral over $[0,T)$ is infinite; so every design must either use an envelope of infinite integral or violate the linear growth bound at the origin, as finite-time and fixed-time designs do. Under a finite gain budget $\mathcal B=\int_0^T L$ the best worst-case contraction over the class is exactly $e^{-\mathcal B}$, a floor valid for every plant, and a finite-budget trajectory converges to a definite point away from the origin. A comparison lemma then carries the theory beyond linear growth: for envelopes $\|\dot z\|\le L(t)\,\omega(\|z\|)$, first arrival at the origin requires budget at least $\int_0^{\|z_0\|}du/\omega(u)$; arrival is impossible whenever this integral diverges, and when it is finite it is the exact threshold, attained inside the class. The classical settling expressions of finite-time control reappear as hitting-time floors, and the known fixed-time condition is the two-ended convergence of the same integral. For linear time-varying loops the results refine to logarithmic-norm budgets, corollaries of a known two-sided estimate, with the terminal error of gain freezing described exactly.

title: Modeling soliton-potential interactions for the 1-D cubic NLS via an invariant-preserving finite-difference method
abstract: We consider the 1-D focusing cubic NLS with a smooth, spatially-dependent potential which decays rapidly as $x \rightarrow \pm \infty$. As is well known, under sufficient regularity conditions, solutions of the cubic NLS with such a spatially-dependent potential conserve both mass and energy. Additionally, in the absence of a potential, the 1-D focusing cubic NLS admits boosted soliton solutions. Furthermore, in the presence of a potential, the interaction of the potential with boosted soliton solutions to the free case is of active interest in the literature, particularly with respect to the dependence of this soliton-potential interaction on the velocity of the incident soliton. We adapt a finite-difference scheme to the setting of a smooth, rapidly-decaying spatially-dependent potential and show that this adaptation preserves the appropriate mass and energy invariants. Additionally, we use this algorithm to model soliton-potential interactions at a variety of incident soliton velocities.

title: What remains when integrability fails? Mathematical structure in the K(m,m) compacton equations
abstract: Peter Lax's 1968 discovery that certain nonlinear wave equations possess operator pairs (Lax pairs) opened the theory of completely integrable systems, yielding exact solutions, infinite conservation hierarchies, and perfectly elastic soliton collisions. When a nonlinear dispersive equation is provably non-integrable (admitting no Lax pair and only finitely many conservation laws), what mathematical structure governs its dynamics? The K(m,m) compacton equations, u_t + (u^m)_x + (u^m)_{xxx} = 0 for m >= 2, provide a testing ground: they support traveling waves with compact support, yet fail every known integrability test. We prove universal algebraic formulas determining the shape, width, and speed of every K(m,m) compacton. We develop a constraint-deficit mechanism explaining how the five independent conservation laws constrain emergent amplitudes and suppress the fundamental Fourier mode of the collision debris, while higher radiation modes remain unconstrained. The mechanism's conclusions rest on explicit hypotheses supported by numerical evidence. A phase-plane analysis reveals the compacton as a singular limit of smooth solitary waves through simultaneous regularity loss and support compactification. These results delineate intermediate territory between integrable order and generic nonlinear dynamics, organized by scaling universality and by the constraint deficit of a finite conservation structure.

title: Large Deviations of Invariant Measures of Fractional Reaction-Diffusion Equations Driven by Multiplicative Noise on R^n
abstract: In this paper, we establish large deviations of invariant measures for fractional stochastic reaction-diffusion equations with polynomial reaction term driven by unbounded multiplicative noise on R^n. Under a dissipativity condition, we first prove the Freidlin-Wentzell large deviation principle of solution trajectories uniformly over all initial data in L^2(R^n). The key ingredient is a positive-time L^\infty-estimate for differences of controlled solutions which is independent of all initial data and hence yields uniform convergence of controlled stochastic solutions over the entire tphase space. Then using the uniform trajectory estimates, contraction and a second-moment estimate, we further prove the large deviations of invariant measures of the equation with a good quasipotential without introducing weighted spaces or establishing exponential tightness. The non-compactness of Sobolev embeddings in R^n is circumvented by uniform spatial tail-ends estimates. This is the first result on large deviations of invariant measures of the equation with multiplicative noise on unbounded domains.

title: Another Brick in the Wall: A Computationally Assisted Proof of an Improved Upper Bound for Thrackles
abstract: Let $G$ be a thrackle, where a thrackle is a graph drawing in which each edge meets every other edge exactly once, either at a vertex or at a crossing. It is conjectured that, for all thrackles, the number of edges is less than or equal to the number of vertices. Fulek and Pach created a program to determine whether or not a graph can be a thrackle. Through a reconstruction and improvement of their algorithm, we computationally prove a key dumbbell to be non-thrackleable. Using this exclusion, we improve Xu's 8-face half-edge bound from five to four. Finally, using this stronger restriction with Xu's framework, together with separate arguments for graphs containing triangles and disconnected graphs, we improve the known upper bound toward this conjecture to $m\le1.385(n-1)$ for $n\ge4$.
comments: 30 pages, 11 figures. Computationally assisted proof. Source code and reproducibility materials are available at https://github.com/Peanut-soup/thrackle-db682-computation

title: Covariance-Rank Rounding and a Sharp Integrality Gap for a Matroid Edge-Coverage Moment Lift
abstract: Selecting vertices covers their incident edges, but a matroid can prevent selecting the combinations that cover the most weight. We study whether pair-selection information improves rounding from a semidefinite relaxation of this problem. A feasible point $(x,Y)$ records individual and paired selection values. Its relaxation objective is $U$, and the matrix $Y-xx^\top$ has rank $d$. We compare the feasible marginal vectors obtained by fixing one element as selected or excluded, then round only the best vector. For $d\ge1$, the resulting basis has value at least $(3/4+1/(4d))U$. The procedure is deterministic and polynomial-time for a supplied exact rational point and an independence oracle. Weighting the covariance spectrum by the objective gives a stronger version of the bound. To show the rank factor is sharp, we construct a rank-$2m$ rational linear matroid and $m$ disjoint four-cycles with integral optimum $3m+1$, relaxation optimum $4m$, and an optimal covariance matrix of rank $m$. Thus the relaxation has limiting reciprocal integrality gap $4/3$, despite its conditional constraints. One valid pair-exclusion inequality makes it exact on this family, as an explicit semidefinite certificate shows. The result concerns rounding and the strength of this relaxation; it does not supply a low-rank optimal point or a fixed universal approximation improvement.

title: Matroid-Aware Spectral Certificates for Multiplicative Coverage Approximation
abstract: We maximize the weight of edges covered by selected vertices, together with nonnegative individual rewards, under an arbitrary matroid constraint. The continuous coverage objective is quadratic and need not be concave. Our method searches projections onto a small set of directions and solves a concave subproblem for each projection center. A coverage-specific inequality converts the subproblem bounds into a multiplicative guarantee, while matroid rounding restores an integral solution. Let $A$ be the weighted adjacency matrix and $D$ the diagonal matrix of singleton values, restricted to positive-value elements after objective-preserving preprocessing. Set $\varrho=\lambda_{\max}(D^{-1/2}AD^{-1/2})$. For an integer budget $q\ge0$, let $\tau_q$ be the smallest nonnegative threshold for which $A+\tau_qD$ has at most $q$ negative eigenvalues on the span of differences of matroid bases. We obtain the factor $1-\varrho\tau_q/[2(\varrho+\tau_q)]-\varepsilon$ in time $(2+q/\varepsilon)^{O(q+1)}N^{O(1)}$, where $N$ is the binary input length and a zero-over-zero loss is zero. The algorithm returns a rational upper bound on the integral optimum. A separate exact-algebraic construction produces polynomial-bit low-rank rational corrections with positive threshold slack; its proof isolates eigenvalues, keeps eigenspace bases unnormalized, and approximates scalar factors only at the final step. The numerical proposal prototype is not used to justify this complexity statement. Supplied certificates also yield robustness to locally bounded edge additions. These are threshold-dependent coverage guarantees, not a new general spectral-search principle or a universal approximation improvement.

title: Alpern Lemma Independent of a Partition for Aperiodic Systems
abstract: We prove that for every $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$, an aperiodic, probability preserving system and $\mathcal{P}$ a finite measurable partition of $X$, there exists an Alpern Multitower whose base is independent of $\mathcal{P}$. This removes the ergodicity assumption in the original proof of the independent Alpern Lemma of \cite{MR3373823}. As a consequence, we remove ergodicity assumption from recent results on limit theorems in deterministic systems \cite{Kosloff_Volny_2022,kosloffVolnyStableCLT,MR4955410}.

title: Orthogonality of Defect Ideals for Jordan Homomorphisms
abstract: Let $\varphi\colon A\to B$ be a Jordan homomorphism of associative algebras over a field $\mathbb{F}$ of characteristic different from $2$, with defect ideals $V_{\varphi}$ and $W_{\varphi}$. If $A=\operatorname{Alg}([[A,A],[A,A]])$, then $V_{\varphi}W_{\varphi}=W_{\varphi}V_{\varphi}=0$ and $V_{\varphi}\cap W_{\varphi}\subseteq\operatorname{Ann}(\operatorname{Alg}(\varphi(A)))$. Moreover, the induced map modulo $V_{\varphi}\cap W_{\varphi}$ is standard. The annihilator bound is sharp, even in finite dimension. As an application, when $A$ is unital and $A=K(A)$, every Jordan homomorphism defined on $A$ is splittable and standard. In this setting, the corresponding result of Bre\v{s}ar and Zelmanov holds without the surjectivity hypothesis.

title: Recovery of Rough Sources in the Inverse Monge--Amp\`ere Problem
abstract: We prove that every nonnegative source \(f\in L^1(\Omega)\) in the Monge--Amp\`ere equation \[ \det D^2u=f\quad\text{in }\Omega, \] on a bounded uniformly convex \(C^{1,1}\) domain \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\), \(n\geq2\), is uniquely determined by generalized boundary measurements of Alexandrov solutions. The measurement is the extremal boundary slope, which extends the outward normal derivative and may equal \(+\infty\). For each \(\omega\in\mathbb S^{n-1}\), it suffices to know these slopes for the cylindrical Dirichlet data \[ \frac{t_k^\omega}{2}|P_\omega x|^2,\qquad t_k^\omega\to\infty, \] along any sequence of amplitudes, where \(P_\omega\) projects onto \(\omega^\perp\). The boundary value and extremal slope determine the interior subgradient image up to a Lebesgue null set. An exact change-of-variables formula and a large-amplitude limit then recover the Euclidean X-ray transform of \(f\), yielding uniqueness without a positive lower bound on the source. For nonnegative \(L^\infty\) sources, the extremal slopes are bounded and coincide with the interior normal derivatives, giving a Dirichlet-to-interior-Neumann formulation. The argument also extends to \[ \vartheta(\nabla u)\det D^2u=f, \] where the known weight \(\vartheta\) is locally integrable, Borel measurable, and bounded below by a positive constant. Conditional on existence of the corresponding Alexandrov solutions, the same cylindrical boundary-slope data determine every nonnegative \(L^1\) source.

title: Schauder estimate in large scale for compressible planar cavity flows with fast-decaying vorticity
abstract: In this paper, we study planar compressible cavity flows fast-decaying vorticity and establish a Schauder estimate in large scale. As an application, we obtain an a priori asymptotic growth rate estimate of the cavity, that $s^{\frac{1}{2}-\delta}\lesssim h(s)\lesssim s^{\frac{1}{2}+\delta}$. This is by far the most accurate asymptotic estimate for compressible cavity flows and is probably the first paper that takes vorticity into account in the asymptotic analysis.

title: Fractional Calder\'on problem with $L^{\infty}$-conductivities
abstract: We study the inverse problem for the fractional conductivity equation with uniformly elliptic conductivities $\gamma\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$. For every $n\geq1$ and $0<s<1$, we prove that the local exterior Dirichlet-to-Neumann map on any nonempty open subset of the exterior of a bounded open domain determines $\gamma$ uniquely almost everywhere in $\mathbb R^n$. No continuity, Sobolev regularity, or prescribed behavior at infinity is required. The proof works directly with the conductivity bilinear form and avoids the fractional Liouville reduction. It combines exterior determination at Lebesgue points, equality of weighted solutions, and a unique continuation principle for the fractional Laplacian in the weighted class \[ L_s=\left\{ g\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^n): \int_{\mathbb R^n} \frac{|g(x)|}{1+|x|^{n+2s}}\,dx<\infty \right\}. \] Specifically, if $g\in L_s$ and both $g$ and $(-\Delta)^s g$ vanish in a nonempty open set, with the latter equality understood distributionally, then $g=0$ almost everywhere. This result requires neither local boundedness nor Sobolev regularity of $g$. Its proof uses the Caffarelli--Silvestre extension and boundary unique continuation for the associated degenerate elliptic equation.

title: Monoidal structure on Rota-Baxter algebras via augmentation, and free cocycle bialgebras
abstract: A tensor product is known for commutative Rota--Baxter algebras through a universal construction, but its underlying algebra need not be the ordinary tensor product $A\otimes B$ and can be substantially larger. We show that, after passing to augmented Rota--Baxter algebras, the ordinary tensor product itself carries a natural Rota--Baxter operator which makes the category monoidal with the usual associator and unit constraints. The resulting structure is intrinsically nonsymmetric: over a field of characteristic zero, this operator and its flip-conjugated counterpart are the only possibilities among linear combinations of five natural terms, while over any field the full category admits no braiding. Its comonoid objects are precisely Rota--Baxter cocycle bialgebras. Moreover, the free Rota--Baxter adjunction yields a bimonad and free cocycle bialgebras on ordinary bialgebras, with compatible Hopf structures for connected filtered inputs, in both the associative and commutative settings.

title: On horn-shaped Reinhardt domains
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new class of unbounded Reinhardt domains in $\mathbb C^n$ ($n\geq 2$),which we call horn domains. We study the dimensions of the Bergman spaces,the holomorphic sectional curvature of the Bergman metric, and the holomorphic equivalence problem for such horn Reinhardt domains.

title: Hyperelliptic curves on $K3$ surfaces
abstract: We study hyperelliptic curves on $K3$ surfaces. We show that any number of general points on a $K3$ surface of Picard rank one can be connected by a hyperelliptic curve. As a by-product we recover the Beauville--Voisin decomposition of the small diagonal, together with some new bounds on its torsion order in the integral Chow group. On the arithmetic side, given a $K3$ surface $X$ of geometric Picard rank one defined over a number field $k$, we show that there exists a finite extension $k\subset k'$ such that quadratic points are dense in $X_{k'}$, extending a theorem of Corvaja--Zucconi to $K3$ surfaces of arbitrary degree.

title: On a finite group in which every non-supersolvable maximal subgroup is a TI-subgroup
abstract: We provide a complete characterization of a finite group in which every non-supersolvable maximal subgroup is a TI-subgroup, which generalizes some known related results.

title: Sharp Damping Location for Stability of a Locally Damped Wave Equation and its Galerkin Approximation
abstract: We study the stability of the variable coefficient wave equation $u_{tt}-u_{xx}-(1+x^{2})u_{yy}+\chi_{\mathbb G}u_{t}=0$ on the rectangle $(-1,1)\times(0,\pi)$ with Dirichlet boundary conditions, where the viscous damping acts on a vertical strip $\mathbb G=(\eta-\delta,\eta+\delta)\times(0,\pi)$. We establish a precise relationship between the location of the damping region and the rate of energy decay. We prove that the associated semigroup is exponentially stable whenever the closure of the damping strip meets the line $x=0$, i.e., $|\eta|\leq\delta$, despite the existence of rays that never enter the damped region. When the damping region is strictly bounded away from $x=0$, the semigroup decays at the sharp rate $(\log(2+t))^{-1}$. The proofs combine separation of variables, one-dimensional resolvent estimates, a reflection identity for the harmonic oscillator, and Gaussian quasimodes. We then consider the spectral Galerkin approximation based on the Dirichlet eigenfunctions of the constant coefficient Laplacian and show that, although the sequence of semigroups resulting from the approximation converges to the continuous one, it fails to be uniformly exponentially stable.

title: Convex-Analytic View of Query Selection for Safety Verification of Markov Decision Processes
abstract: Safety verification of a Markov decision process (MDP) asks whether the probabilities of reaching several failure states jointly lie in a convex safe region under every scheduler. Watanabe and Unno (2026) prove safety by refining an outer approximation of the failure probabilities, where each query bounds a nonnegative weighted sum of the probabilities. Their rule selects weights by the largest Euclidean violation. We present a unified framework to measure violation in an explicitly chosen error unit: directions are scored by the support-function gap between the outer approximation and the safe region, normalized by the support function of the unit. We show that the maximal score, when positive, equals the smallest enlargement of the safe region in multiples of that unit that contains the outer approximation. The Euclidean unit recovers the earlier rule; two new rules are generated by the unit cube and the safe region itself. We experimentally evaluate how the choice of measurement rule affects the performance of safety verification for MDPs.

title: Aperiodic automorphisms of the Razak--Jacelon algebra
abstract: We completely classify aperiodic automorphisms of the Razak--Jacelon algebra $\mathcal{W}$ up to outer conjugacy. As a technical ingredient, based on the works of Connes, Herman--Ocneanu, Kishimoto, and Sato, we introduce a notion of weak stability for automorphisms of simple separable monotracial C$^*$-algebras. We also consider automorphisms of UHF algebras of infinite type and the Jiang--Su algebra. In particular, we classify aperiodic ``UHF-absorbing'' automorphisms of UHF algebras of infinite type up to outer conjugacy.
comments: 29 pages v2: We have added the classification of aperiodic UHF-absorbing automorphisms of UHF algebras of infinite type (Theorem C)

title: Fragments of SRP, the nonstationary ideal, and diagonal reflection
abstract: We investigate the relationships between fragments of SRP and diagonal reflection principles. It turns out that the subcomplete fragment of SRP, augmented with CH, implies that the nonstationary ideal on $\omega_1$ is not saturated, but that Larson's diagonal reflection principle $OSR_{\omega_2}$ holds. In contrast, it was known that the full principle SRP implies the saturation of the nonstationary ideal on $\omega_1$, but it does not imply $OSR_{\omega_2}$. We find several instances of this phenomenon: pairing (variations of) the subcomplete fragment of SRP with stronger failures of the nonstationary ideal on $\omega_1$ to be saturated allows us to conclude more instances of diagonal reflection principles, while boosting (the corresponding variations of) the full principle SRP with strong forms of the saturation of the nonstationary ideal allows us to produce models where these principles still hold, yet weaker versions of diagonal reflection fail.

title: On the generalized cospectral mates of chain graphs of rank 4
abstract: A graph is called a chain graph if it is bipartite and the neighborhoods of the vertices in each color class are linearly ordered by inclusion. We study the generalized spectral determination of chain graphs of adjacency rank $4$. We first show that generalized cospectral chain graphs have the same number of isolated vertices, reducing the problem to the connected case. For connected rank-$4$ chain graphs, we derive four explicit equations in the cell parameters that are necessary and sufficient for generalized cospectrality. These equations reduce to a quadratic equation in a single parameter. As a consequence, every connected rank-$4$ chain graph has at most one generalized cospectral mate, and the possible mate can be reconstructed explicitly. We further obtain a simple sufficient condition for a rank-$4$ chain graph to be determined by its generalized spectrum (DGS) and, in particular, prove that every double star graph is DGS. Finally, we construct an explicit infinite family of non-double-star rank-$4$ chain graphs that are DGS but not determined by their adjacency spectra, with both the graphs and their complements being connected.

title: Efficient Shallow Ritz Method: 1D Semi-Linear Diffusion-Reaction and Allen-Cahn Equations
abstract: An efficient shallow Ritz method was developed in [8, 9] for one-dimensional linear diffusion and diffusion-reaction problems. In this paper, the method is extended to a nonlinear diffusion-reaction equation with a cubic reaction term: (1) a basic error estimate of the shallow Ritz discretization is established and (2) a reduced block Newton (rBN) method for solving the resulting non-convex optimization problem is developed. Again, the computational cost of the rBN method is $\mathcal{O}(n)$ for one-dimensional problems, where $n$ is the number of neurons. Combining a convex splitting scheme for time discretization with the efficient shallow Ritz method, we develop a time-stepping neural network method for solving the Allen-Cahn equation. The unconditional energy stability of the time discretization and an error estimate in the $L^2$ norm are established. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the neural network approach yields accurate solutions for singularly perturbed nonlinear diffusion-reaction equations and the Allen-Cahn equation. The method effectively resolves interior and boundary layers without oscillations and significantly outperforms the finite element method on fixed uniform meshes.

title: The $\ell$-degree Tur\'an densities of hypergraphs: infinite families and their finite subfamilies
abstract: Let $k>\ell\ge 1$ be integers. For a family $\mathcal{F}$ of $k$-uniform hypergraphs ($k$-graphs), its $\ell$-degree Tur\'an density $\gamma^{(k)}_\ell(\mathcal{F})$ is the asymptotic maximum of the normalized minimum $\ell$-degree over all $\mathcal{F}$-free $k$-graphs. In this paper, we prove that for all integers $k>\ell>2$ and every $\alpha\in[0,1)$, there exists an infinite family $\mathcal{F}$ of $k$-graphs such that $\gamma^{(k)}_\ell(\mathcal{F})=\alpha$, while every finite subfamily $\mathcal{F}'\subset \mathcal{F}$ satisfies $\gamma^{(k)}_\ell(\mathcal{F}')>\alpha$. This confirms the conjecture of Mubayi and Zhao on codegree Tur\'an densities for every $k > 3$. As an immediate consequence, the set $\Gamma^{k,\ell}_{\infty}$ of $\ell$-degree Tur\'an densities of nonempty $k$-graph families is $[0,1)$ whenever $k>\ell>2$, which answers a question of Lo and Markstr\"om from 2014.

title: Boundary Control of a Modified Timoshenko-Ehrenfest Beam via Reduced-Order Reinforcement Learning
abstract: In this paper, we study the active vibration control of an elastic beam using reinforcement learning (RL). The physical system is modeled by a modified Timoshenko-Ehrenfest type linear partial differential equation with simply supported boundary conditions. The dynamics are approximated by a reduced-order model (ROM) obtained through eigenvalue expansion and truncated Galerkin projection. Control is applied through boundary actuation. The resulting finite-dimensional system is formulated as a continuous-time Markov decision process and solved numerically using the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm. All modeling steps, from physical formulation to temporal discretization and control design, are explicitly described. A systematic comparison is performed between the controller learned via PPO and the classical linear quadratic (LQR) regulator. The analysis highlights the strengths and limitations of each approach, both from a theoretical and practical point of view, with particular emphasis on energy dissipation mechanisms and actuator constraints.
comments: 37 pages, numerical experiments, reinforcement learning (PPO), boundary control of a modified Timoshenko-Ehrenfest beam

title: On the Real Waring Rank of a Biharmonic Form
abstract: We develop an effective method for determining the real Waring rank and the real border rank of biharmonic binary forms. By means of real apolarity, we convert both of these problems into membership questions for regions bounded by a hypocycloid and an epicycloid. We further provide a computable algebraic criterion for the relevant memberships, which involves only the signs of certain real-valued resultants.

title: Targeted Entropy-Stable Nonlinear Artificial Dissipation for High-Order Spectral-Element Summation-By-Parts Discretizations
abstract: Artificial dissipation improves the robustness of high-order methods for under-resolved flows, but can compromise accuracy and suppress physically relevant structures if its strength and spatial distribution are not appropriately controlled. We present a sensor-activated nonlinear artificial-dissipation framework, inspired by the residual correction method, for continuous and discontinuous summation-by-parts discretizations. In contrast to many existing spectral-element dissipation operators that either reduce the formal order of accuracy or target only the highest polynomial modes, the proposed framework permits design- and higher-order dissipation with explicit control over its magnitude, spatial distribution, activation, and convergence rate under mesh refinement. This modular construction also recovers several existing methods through appropriate choices of its components. The dissipation preserves discrete conservation and semidiscrete entropy stability whenever the base method satisfies these properties. It is dimensionally consistent, element local, and discretization agnostic, as the added term is constructed independently of the base spatial residual. For smooth solutions under suitable mesh assumptions, we establish parameter choices that retain the formal accuracy of the base discretization. Numerical experiments with summation-by-parts discretizations of the Burgers and Euler equations demonstrate substantially improved robustness for under-resolved flows and flows with shock waves while retaining high-order accuracy for smooth solutions, using the same parameter choices across several test problems. Overall, these results show that targeted dissipation can improve the robustness of high-order methods without excessive damping of resolved flow structures.

title: A Structure-Preserving Effective Linear Approximation of the Quantum Boltzmann Collision Operator
abstract: We construct a structure-preserving effective linear approximation of the quantum Boltzmann collision operator for Bose and Fermi gases in the normal phase. For variable hard-sphere kernels, the resulting Fourier spectral evaluation costs $O(N_v^4\log N_v)$, with $N_v$ velocity nodes per direction and no angular quadrature factor. The continuous operator conserves mass, momentum and energy and satisfies a linearized $H$-theorem. We also use the operator at local quantum equilibrium as an approximate collision Jacobian in a modified Newton solver that retains the full nonlinear residual. Numerical tests show smaller errors than the quantum BGK model in homogeneous relaxation and fewer full collision evaluations for steady Couette and Fourier flows than the same Newton solver using a quantum BGK Jacobian.

title: An $\eps$-regularity criterion at one scale for 3-D Navier-Stokes equations and improved upper bound on the box dimension of the interior singular set
abstract: In this paper, we obtain an $\varepsilon$-regularity criterion at one scale for 3D Navier-Stokes equations using a coarse-to-refined estimate argument based on mean-fluctuation decomposition. Making use of this $\varepsilon$-regularity criterion, we improve the upper bound on the box dimension of the interior singular set to $15/13$.

title: Puncturing-inclusion constructions of optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes using semifield codes
abstract: Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes are essential components of the multilevel construction of constant dimension codes for random network coding. This paper aims to construct optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes, focusing on the diagram \([3,3,3,5]\) with rank distance \(3\). We construct an optimal \([[3,3,3,5],6,3]_q\) Ferrers diagram rank-metric code for every prime power \(q\), thereby answering an open problem posed by Etzion et al. in 2016~\cite{Etzion2016}. The construction first builds a \([3\times4,4,3]_q\) MRD code and then proves that the Delsarte dual of its puncturing on the last column contains a \([3\times3,3,3]_q\) MRD code, which comes from semifield codes. We further construct optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes for two infinite families of Ferrers diagrams: the first relies on the \([[3,3,3,5],6,3]_q\) construction and holds for every prime power \(q\), while the second is binary and obtained directly by the puncturing-inclusion construction.

title: Risk-Averse Inference-Time Diffusion Model Alignment with Finite-Sample Guarantees
abstract: Inference-time alignment steers diffusion models toward downstream objectives without costly fine-tuning, but existing methods typically optimize expected cost (or reward) without explicitly controlling tail risk. In this work, we propose a risk-averse framework for inference-time alignment of diffusion models that balances expected cost and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) under trajectory-level Kullback-Leibler regularization. We characterize the optimal path distribution and reverse transitions as functions of the CVaR threshold, reducing the alignment problem to a one-dimensional optimization problem over the threshold. We show that this one-dimensional optimization problem can be nonconvex in general, establish sufficient conditions for convexity, and introduce quadratic regularization to enable efficient derivative-free ternary search. Under suitable assumptions, we provide finite-sample guarantees for threshold optimization and value estimation, and combine them into a terminal total-variation bound relative to the regularized target under exact resampling. Experiments on synthetic data and image generation using Stable Diffusion demonstrate improved tail performance over risk-neutral baselines while maintaining competitive average cost.

title: Nonhomogeneous Subordinators and L\'evy Copulas for Reliability Analysis of Time-Dependent Degradation Processes
abstract: Many systems in engineering applications may experience complex multi-dimensional degradation processes involving random jumps. Analyzing the reliability of such degradation processes presents significant challenges. Previously developed models have utilized multi-dimensional L\'evy subordinators and L\'evy copulas to describe these processes, with reliability functions expressed through characteristic functions and Laplace transforms (Shu et al., 2015, 2016, Shi et al., 2020, Shi and Feng, 2024). However, these models are restricted to stationary linear paths and homogeneous L\'evy subordinators. In real-world scenarios, increments in a degradation process are often time-dependent and nonhomogeneous. To address this limitation of previous studies, this work extends existing degradation models by introducing nonhomogeneous L\'evy subordinators, which are designed to capture time-varying complexities inherent in degradation processes. Unlike conventional degradation models that often assume a constant rate of jumps, nonhomogeneous L\'evy subordinators aim to provide a more flexible representation of degradation behaviors that evolve under varying external conditions and internal system dynamics. Additionally, the joint behaviors of multiple degradation processes are characterized using L\'evy copulas, enabling a more comprehensive analysis of system reliability. Numerical examples are provided to illustrate the applicability of these models in lifetime analysis.

title: Global existence of large strong solutions to the 3D compressible micropolar equations with density-dependent viscosities
abstract: In this paper, we consider the Cauchy problem for the three-dimensional (3D) compressible micropolar equations with density-dependent viscosities. By classical $L^p$ estimates to elliptic system, defining suitable energy functions, after the elaborate index analysis, we establish the global existence of strong solutions to the system with all viscosities depending density as long as the initial density is large enough. By product, We also prove the existence of global large strong solutions with only large initial shear viscosity $\mu_1(\rho)$ and angular viscosity $\mu_2(\rho)$, which consists with the research work \cite{ZZ2014} of 3D compressible Navier-Stokes equations with constant viscosities and improve the recent result of \cite{HLZ} in some extent where they requiring both initial shear viscosity and bulk viscosity to be large.

title: Roth's theorem on weighted projective lines
abstract: Let ${\mathbb P}^1_{\mathfrak q}$ be the weighted projective line with coprime weights ${\mathfrak q}=(q_0,q_1)$ and $L=q_0q_1$. The weighted Veronese map $\Phi\colon {\mathbb P}^1_{\mathfrak q}\to {\mathbb P}^1$ satisfies $h\circ\Phi=L\,{\mathfrak s}$. Pulling back Roth's theorem gives the optimal exponent $2L$ for the full rational orbit set. For points represented by coprime integral coordinates, counting suggests the smaller exponent $q_0+q_1$. We formulate this as a conjecture and prove an $S$-adic radical form under the $abc$ conjecture. For ${\mathfrak q}=(2,3)$ the resulting inequality at the target $[1:1]$ is the coprime Hall-type inequality, and Danilov--Elkies examples show that the exponent $5$ is sharp. We also prove the expected exponent unconditionally over characteristic-zero function fields for constant targets and polynomial approximants, and for almost every real target. A weighted $abc$ formulation is introduced; in signature $(3,2)$ finitely many coefficient pairs are equivalent to $abc$, and weighted Belyi maps transfer this input to arbitrary algebraic targets. Applications include a pullback form of Schmidt's subspace theorem, weighted Thue inequalities, and a counterexample to a naive weighted rescaling of Roth's index construction.

title: On extending induced subgraphs
abstract: When characterizing graphs defined by forbidden induced subgraphs, it is often desirable to understand how a graph $G$ can be generated incrementally from a given induced subgraph $H$. In this paper, we study a number of problems within this framework. First, for several notions of connectivity, we determine all minimal induced subgraphs of $G$ that contain $H$ and attain the connectivity of $G$. Second, we establish how to grow $H$ inside $G$ while preserving twin-freeness and certain forms of connectivity. Third, we establish {\it finite test theorems} for various graph classes, proving that agreement with the recursively generated graphs for a few initial iterations forces agreement at all subsequent iterations. Consequently, such an infinite graph family can be completely determined by finitely many of its initial generations. As an application, we characterize $\{\mathbb L_1,\mathbb L_3\}$-free graphs, where $\mathbb L_1$ is the claw and $\mathbb L_3$ is another forbidden graph for line graphs. Our structural results reduce this problem to a finite verification, which is completed through computer-assisted computation.

title: Strong convergence rate of the implicit midpoint method for stochastic KdV equations
abstract: We establish a strong convergence rate for the implicit midpoint method applied to the periodic stochastic Korteweg-de Vries equation with additive noise, addressing a question that has remained open since the work of Debussche and Printems. To control nonlinear error growth, we obtain exponential integrability estimates for the exact and comparison solutions using the coercivity of a classical KdV invariant. We then derive local error bounds from estimates for the comparison solutions and control error accumulation through an $L^2$ error propagation identity that isolates a martingale increment. Under $H_0^{9/2}$ regularity assumptions on the noise and the deterministic initial data, we prove that, on every fixed finite time interval, the maximum $L^2(\mathbb{T})$ error at the time points is $O(h)$ in $L^p(\Omega)$ for every $1\le p<\infty$. Notably, the exponential integrability and the convergence rate hold for every damping coefficient $\lambda\ge0$, including the undamped case $\lambda=0$. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted first-order convergence.

title: Existence of positive solutions to anisotropic elliptic equations in the entire Euclidean space
abstract: In this paper, we research an anisotropic elliptic equation in the entire Euclidean space R^{N} . Under the assumption that the nonlinearity of the equation has exponential or critical growth, we prove, by means of the mountain-pass theorem, that the equation admits a nontrivial positive weak solution. Moreover, applying the mountain-pass theorem and Ekeland's variational principle, we show that a perturbation of the equation possesses two distinct positive weak solutions.

title: Clean handshake sequences
abstract: After a basketball game, each of the $n$ players on Team A must shake hands with each of the $n$ players on Team B.
