abstract: In this paper, we study the following Schr\"odinger-Newton system with a vanishing magnetic potential and an electric potential \begin{equation}\label{0.1} \left\{ \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.25} \begin{array}{ll} (-i\nabla +A(x))^2u+V(x)u=\Phi u, \ & x\in\mathbb{R}^3,\\ -\Delta \Phi =|u|^2, \ & x\in\mathbb{R}^3, \end{array} \right. \end{equation} where $i$ is the imaginary unit, $A:\mathbb{R}^3\to \mathbb{R}^3$ is a continuous magnetic potential, and $V:\mathbb{R}^3\to \mathbb{R}$ is a continuous electric potential. First, we show that the ground state energy of system with $A(x)\equiv0$ and $V(x)\equiv V_{\infty}>0$ is isolated. Using this fact together with a global compactness lemma, a barycenter function, and Brouwer degree theory, we prove that under suitable conditions on $A$ and $V$, system admits either a ground state solution or a high energy solution. Interestingly, whether a ground state solution exists is significantly affected by the magnetic potential $A$ and the electric potential $V$. Furthermore, we provide sufficient conditions that guarantee the existence of a ground state solution, as well as conditions under which no ground state solution exists and a high energy solution appears instead.

title: Optimal scaling and curvature correction for constrained MCMC on spheres
abstract: Sampling Gaussian measures restricted to nonlinear manifolds in high dimensions requires a proposal kernel that respects both geometric constraints and dimensional scaling requirements. We introduce tangent preconditioned Crank-Nicolson (pCN), which combines a manifold projection with a cancellation of the ambient Gaussian contribution, leaving only a geometric residual. Considering a shifted sphere with $\sqrt d$ scaling of radius and centre as a tractable benchmark embedded manifold, we prove that uncorrected tangent pCN results in a proposal noise scale of order $d^{-1/6}$ (compared to $d^{-1/2}$ for a tangent random-walk). We establish asymptotic optimal tuning for the geodesic expected squared jump distance which is maximised at an acceptance probability of 0.574 for the family of drift-corrected tangent proposals containing tangent pCN and tangent MALA. We also prove a joint diffusion limit for the parallel and orthogonal coordinates to the sphere's centre vector of tangent pCN. The orthogonal diffusion speed matches the limiting geodesic expected squared jump distance and is maximised at acceptance probability 0.574, whereas the parallel speed is maximised at 0.712, demonstrating that optimal tuning depends on the observable. We then identify an intrinsic precision correction characterised by potential Hessian and Ricci curvature that yields a proposal kernel with dimension-independent fixed step size limit. We discuss a generalisation to arbitrary hypersurfaces and present nondegenerate scaling of tangent pCN applied to conditioned diffusions under resolution refinement.

title: Latency-Aware Uplink NOMA-MEC with PASS: A Feasibility-First Resource Allocation Framework
abstract: Meeting hard task-completion deadlines for many simultaneously offloading users is the binding challenge in mobile-edge computing (MEC). As the user count grows, the transmit power required to satisfy every deadline within per-user budgets rises until no feasible allocation exists. We take a \emph{feasibility-first} view of this $K$-user problem in an uplink non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) MEC system served by a pinching-antenna system (PASS), whose radiating points establish strong line-of-sight (LoS) links that lower the received-power requirement. We formulate a latency-constrained joint optimization of transmit powers, CPU frequencies, and antenna configuration. We then derive a \emph{closed-form least-power feasibility test}: the componentwise-least allocation meeting every deadline. It certifies feasibility with the largest attainable margin to the power budgets and defines a practical \emph{quality-of-service (QoS)-feasibility outage} metric, the probability that no allocation meets all deadlines within budget. We solve the problem with a three-block alternating-optimization algorithm that is provably monotone-convergent and has polynomial complexity. Numerical results show that the proposed scheme sustains deadline feasibility at user loads where equal-power, orthogonal multiple access (OMA), and single-antenna baselines fail or degrade sharply, each by a mechanism predicted directly from the system model, whereas the proposed design degrades gracefully. Stress tests further show that feasibility is sustained under order-of-magnitude budget reductions, and that the pinching-antenna array itself enables constrained-budget operation. The result is a scalable, closed-form-initialized design for deadline-feasible offloading.
comments: 6 pages, Accepted at IEEE GLOBECOM 2026 Workshops (PASS for NGWC)

title: $\mathrm{CS}\mathfrak{X}$-groups and free constructions
abstract: Let $\X$ be a variety of groups. A group $G$ is $\CSX$ if its maximal $\X$-subgroups are malnormal. We prove that the amalgamated free product of two $\CSX$-groups with a malnormal amalgam and without any involutions is again $\CSX$. Using this, we describe conditions under which the HNN-extension of a $\CSX$-group is $\CSX$.

title: A generating function identity for finite and symmetric multiple zeta values via Dougall's bilateral ${}_2H_2$ summation
abstract: We establish a generating function identity for finite and symmetric multiple zeta values using Dougall's bilateral ${}_2H_2$ summation formula. As an application, we prove a restricted sum formula in which the parity of each component of the index is prescribed. We also derive a generating function identity for finite multiple zeta values $\zeta^{}_{\mathcal{A}}(\{1,2\}^n)$ and symmetric multiple zeta values $\zeta^{}_{\mathcal{S}}(\{1,2\}^n)$, thereby proving Kaneko's conjecture for finite multiple zeta values and its symmetric analogue.

title: Equivariant analytic torsion forms
abstract: In this paper, we first construct infinitesimal equivariant analytic torsion forms for K\"ahler fibrations. We then compare them with Ma's equivariant analytic torsion forms, modulo $\partial$- and $\overline{\partial}$-exact forms, in terms of equivariant Bott--Chern currents and the $I$-genus. Our comparison formula extends that of Bismut and Goette to families.

title: Two-Dimensional Torus Action on the Quadric Threefold and GW-DT-GV Correspondence
abstract: We compute Gromov--Witten (GW) and Donaldson-Thomas (DT) invariants (including descendant invariants) for local CY $4$-folds over a smooth quadric threefold $Q$, up to degree $4$. We use the virtual localization formula with respect to a two-dimensional torus action to compute DT invariants. Combining these results with the computation of the J-function of the variety $Q$, we confirm the correspondence between DT and Gopakumar--Vafa invariants suggested by Cao--Maulik--Toda in genus zero. Based on these results, we predict a genus one BPS invariant on $Q$.

title: Control Realization of Schr\"{o}dinger Bridges over Discrete-Time Nonlinear Systems via Maximum-Entropy Distribution Steering
abstract: This paper shows how a Schrodinger bridge (SB) structure emerges from maximum-entropy (MaxEnt) distribution steering of discrete-time nonlinear systems. We also establish that the resulting bridge can be realized by an optimal control policy. We consider general state and input costs, non-Gaussian endpoint distributions, and input constraints. Assuming the existence of a feasible policy with finite objective value, we show that the state-path measure under a MaxEnt optimal control policy is the unique SB. The reference measure of this SB is induced by an optimal policy of the corresponding terminal-unconstrained problem. Moreover, we give an equivalent characterization of the optimal state-path measure using a killed reference and its normalized Feynman--Kac measure, thereby interpreting the state cost as killing. We then characterize the finite-cost feasibility by the existence of an endpoint coupling having finite Kullback--Leibler divergence from the reference endpoint distribution. For compactly supported marginals with bounded target density, we derive reachability-based sufficient conditions guaranteeing this feasibility. We further provide specializations to fully actuated control-affine and reachable linear systems.

title: Rarity Determines Minimax Rates of Semantic Entropy From Weak Pairwise Judgments With a Known Channel
abstract: The semantic entropy of a language model is the entropy of the meanings of its sampled answers. The meanings are never observed, and the entropy is estimated from the verdicts of a pairwise equivalence judge. Given the meanings of $n$ answers, a known channel declares each pair equivalent independently, with probability $q+\Delta$ within a meaning and $q$ across meanings. At most $K$ meanings occur, and $q$ is bounded away from $0$ and $1$. For a weak judge, with $n\Delta^2\to0$, the global minimax rate is set by distributions near a vertex of the simplex and overstates the difficulty elsewhere. We show that the difficulty is set by how many meanings can be rare. Over distributions with at most $s$ meanings below a fixed probability $\tau<1/(K-s)$, the minimax squared risk is of order $N^{-1/s}$ for $s\ge2$, $N^{-1}\log^2(e+N)$ for $s=1$ and $N^{-1}$ for $s=0$, capped at one, where $N=n^K\Delta^{2K-2}$. The matching lower bounds hold on every fixed polynomial window $n\Delta^2\le n^{-\kappa}$. One estimator attains these rates without knowing $s$ or $\tau$: it averages products of centered verdicts along all spanning trees of every $k$-set of answers, projects the resulting power sums onto the valid moment set and inverts them. The case $s=K-1$ gives the global rate $N^{-1/(K-1)}$ and the consistency threshold: with $\Delta=n^{-\gamma}$ the entropy is uniformly consistently estimable exactly when $\gamma<K/(2K-2)$. On polynomial windows, the same estimator attains the sharp local minimax constant on shrinking neighborhoods of interior points with distinct probabilities. Restricting the average to stars multiplies the constant by $K^{K-3}$.

title: Simultaneous energy and entropy stability of volume-penalisation immersed-boundary methods for the compressible Navier--Stokes equations
abstract: Immersed-boundary methods avoid body-fitted meshes, but the energy or entropy stability of the underlying flow discretisation does not automatically extend to the immersed treatment. This manuscript analyses the volume-penalised compressible Navier--Stokes equations for both energy and entropy stability, on the continuous and semi-discrete levels, and integrates the isolated source exactly in time. The source is formulated as a one-parameter family indexed by $\theta$, whose momentum component relaxes the fluid velocity towards the prescribed solid velocity; $\theta$ sets how much of the resulting kinetic-energy loss leaves the domain rather than being converted to internal energy. The two stability requirements impose opposing bounds on $\theta$, with dissipation of the relative total energy requiring $\theta\geq0$ and stability of the mathematical entropy requiring $\theta\leq1$. Where penalisation acts, both conditions are therefore satisfied if and only if $0\leq\theta\leq1$, and the symmetric value $\theta=1/2$ divides the kinetic-energy loss equally between the domain and the internal energy. We conclude that any entropy-stable split-form discontinuous Galerkin spectral element method remains semi-discretely entropy stable once the source is added at the collocation nodes, for stationary and prescribed moving bodies alike.

title: Cohomology ring of the strata of holomorphic differentials of genus 3
abstract: We prove that the rational Chow ring of every connected component of the multi-scale compactifications of the genus three strata $\mathcal{H}(4), \mathcal{H}(2,2)$ and $\mathcal{H}(3,1)$ is generated by boundary-stratum classes. Our proof shows Chow-K\"unneth generation property of boundary strata of the multi-scale compactification by reducing the boundary analysis to lower-genus generalized strata of meromorphic differentials, including residueless loci, described through plane-quartic and plane-cubic models. As a consequence, the rational cycle-class map is an isomorphism and the compactifications have no odd rational cohomology.

title: The equivariant Ehrhart theory of polytopes with order-two symmetries: Part II
abstract: We give two counterexamples to Stapledon's Effectiveness Conjecture. Each counterexample is a $6$-dimensional lattice polytope with an order-two symmetry whose equivariant $H^*$-series $\varphi[t]$ is a polynomial with one coefficient that is not effective. For polytopes with a symmetry of order two, the goal of this paper is to build up a picture of the landscape of results for when the Effectiveness Conjecture holds. Our main result is a criterion, in terms of the faces of $P$, that determines when the Ehrhart ring of $P$ admits an invariant linear system of parameters of the correct representation type. We use these results to reduce the space of possible counterexamples to one of two cases. A randomised computer search produced counterexamples in each case. We also give an example where the equivariant $H^*$-series is effective but admits no invariant linear system of parameters, neither for $P$ nor any invariant subdivision of it, answering a question of Stapledon in the case of groups of order two.

title: The Brownian bubble tea
abstract: We use Loewner-Kufarev evolution to decompose the Brownian loop soup into a Poisson point process on Brownian bubbles which we call the Brownian bubble tea driven by $\rho$, where $\rho$ is the driving measure for the Loewner chain. The only assumption on $\rho$ is that the evolving boundaries are locally connected. This generalizes a similar disintegration result of Lawler and Werner to essentially optimal regularity, and includes foliations with finite Loewner-Kufarev energy as well as radial and whole-plane $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa$ for all $\kappa \geqslant 0$. As applications, we give Brownian loop interpretations of the conformal distortion formula for Loewner-Kufarev energy and the relationships between the Loewner energy, Loewner-Kufarev energy, and the Schwarzian action.

title: Colored Tur\'an densities and finite directed templates
abstract: Classical Tur\'an theory relates the asymptotic extremal problem for an ordinary forbidden graph to its chromatic number. This principle fails when a forbidden copy must respect prescribed vertex colors, as occurs naturally in multipartite extremal problems and in embeddings with prescribed clusters. We study properly vertex-colored graphs whose hosts have a prescribed density between every pair of color classes, with containment interpreted through color-preserving homomorphisms. Our main theorem gives a finite directed reduction: for every fixed $m$ and $\varepsilon>0$, every sufficiently many-colored $d$-dense host admits a colored homomorphism from an $m$-layer half-blowup $D[m]$ of a finite digraph $D$ with density at least $d-\varepsilon$, where $D$ may be chosen with $\lceil\varepsilon^{-1}\rceil$ vertices. Consequently, the colored Tur\'an density of every non-empty finite forbidden family equals the homomorphism Tur\'an density of its associated acyclic orientations. We then determine the complete finite value set: these densities are exactly the Lagrangians of finite loopless digraphs, and hence are rational. The main technical input is a low-resolution sampling method that preserves all pairwise bipartite degree profiles on a large subfamily of color classes while keeping the sample size independent of the number of retained classes.

title: Local Hadamard well-posedness of the 2D primitive equations without thermal diffusion under strict stratification
abstract: We study the two-dimensional non-rotating primitive equations with anisotropic viscosity and no thermal diffusion. For doubly periodic perturbations of a hydrostatic equilibrium with an affine temperature profile, we establish local Hadamard well-posedness in Sobolev spaces under strict stratification. The initial horizontal velocity and temperature have sufficient regularity and vanishing vertical means, but need not be small. The estimates close at the same Sobolev order for these variables despite the horizontal derivative loss in the diagnostic vertical velocity. Stratification-weighted energy estimates and a horizontal compensation argument avoid an additional temperature derivative while retaining the full vertical dependence and the vertically homogeneous velocity component determined by periodic compatibility. A one-sided comparison places higher-order norms of the more regular solution only in terms involving lower-order differences. This structure allows the Bona--Smith method to yield continuous dependence in the original Sobolev topology. We obtain a unique maximal strong solution in the strictly stratified class, together with continuous dependence of the diagnostic vertical velocity and pressure in their natural Sobolev spaces and lower semicontinuity of the maximal lifespan.

title: Sobolev Minimizers for Critical Vectorial $p$-Laplacian Problems
abstract: We study minimizers of the optimal Sobolev quotients for the critical embeddings $D^{1,p}(\mathbb R^N;\mathbb R^m)\hookrightarrow L^{p^*}(\mathbb R^N;\mathbb R^m)$ and $W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\hookrightarrow L^{p^*}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)$. In the whole space, we classify all minimizers as $\boldsymbol u=\boldsymbol c\,U_{\delta,x_0}$, where $\boldsymbol c\neq\boldsymbol0$ and $U_{\delta,x_0}$ is an Aubin--Talenti bubble. On bounded domains and for $\lambda>0$, we equip $W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)$ with $ \|\boldsymbol u\|_\lambda^p :=\int_\Omega \bigl(|D\boldsymbol u|^p+\lambda|\boldsymbol u|^p\bigr) $. Using scalar attainment results, we establish existence and synchronization of vectorial minimizers. At resonance, we consider the pure Neumann problem $ -\boldsymbol\Delta_p\boldsymbol u =|\boldsymbol u|^{p^*-2}\boldsymbol u\ \text{in }\Omega. $ For the associated quotient, we prove existence and global $C^1(\overline\Omega)$ regularity of minimizers. Finally, we prove synchronization of radial solutions and deduce symmetry breaking on balls.

title: The $2$-co-lacunary subsequence principle for arbitrary noncommutative $L_1$-spaces
abstract: For every von Neumann algebra \(\M\), we prove that each bounded sequence in the Haagerup space \(L_1(\M)=\M_*\) admits either a norm-convergent subsequence or a \(2\)-co-lacunary subsequence. This answers an open problem of Parcet and Randrianantoanina \cite[Remark~3.11]{ParcetRandrianantoanina2006} and removes both hyperfiniteness and semifiniteness.

title: Eigenvalue fluctuations for the crushed ice problem
abstract: We study the eigenvalues of the negative Dirichlet Laplacian $-\Delta$ in domain $D_{\epsilon,N}$ obtained by removing $N$ Euclidean balls of radius $\epsilon$ from a bounded open set $D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ ($d\ge2$). It is known that, for the balls centered at points drawn independently from a distribution with probability density $\rho$ and for $N\to\infty$ and $\epsilon\downarrow0$ so that the aggregate Newtonian capacity of the removed balls tends to some $\kappa>0$, the eigenvalues of $-\Delta$ in $D_{\epsilon,N}$ homogenize to those of the Schr\"odinger operator $-\Delta+\kappa\rho$ in $D$. Here we prove that, for the eigenvalues that are simple in the limit, a multivariate Central Limit Theorem holds in all $d\ge2$ under centering by expected values. Unlike earlier work in $d=3$ by Figari, Orlandi and Teta and, independently, Ozawa from 1980s that was based on resolvent expansions, we rely on martingale representations and one-ball perturbation asymptotic controlled by methods of harmonic analysis.

title: Optimal Control of Mean-field FBSDEs and Classical Solutions of the Related Generalized HJB Equations
abstract: In this article, we study optimal control problems driven by mean-field forward-backward stochastic differential equations (FBSDEs). The aim is two-fold: (i) to provide the unique optimal control; (ii) to establish classical solutions of the associated generalized Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equations on the space of probability measures. For (i), we study the coupled system arising from the maximum principle, which involves both the state FBSDEs and the adjoint FBSDEs. This system is non-standard and more complicated than that in standard mean-field type control (MFTC) problems. By extending the method of continuation in the coefficients to our framework, we establish the well-posedness result, and subsequently obtain the differentiability of the value functional with respect to the distribution argument --- thereby extending existing results for MFTC problems. For (ii), since the flow property does not generally hold for control problems of FBSDEs, standard dynamic-programming arguments cannot be applied directly. We therefore develop probabilistic approaches to the classical solvability of generalized HJB equations under three distinct sets of conditions. The auxiliary processes arising in these arguments differ significantly from those in standard MFTC problems. We establish new connections between the value function and the adjoint processes, derive equations for the relevant decoupling field, and obtain first- and second-order generalized HJB equations, including a coupled system on the space of probability measures. The standard HJB equations for MFTC problems are recovered as special cases. Our approach yields classical solutions without requiring non-degeneracy of the diffusion.

title: Generalized Topological Structures Induced by $H^{*}$-Open Sets and Their Separation Properties
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the family of $H^{*}$-open sets from the perspective of generalized topology and examine the structural and separation properties arising from it. For a topological space $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$, the family of all $H^{*}$-open subsets of $\mathbb{X}$ is considered as a natural candidate for an $H^{*}$-generated generalized topology. We establish conditions under which this family forms a strong generalized topology and identify additional assumptions that allow the resulting structure to be treated as an ordinary topology. This distinction provides a systematic framework for studying $H^{*}$-open sets without imposing finite-intersection properties in advance. Within this framework, we investigate the corresponding $H^{*}$-interior and $H^{*}$-closure operators and analyze separation properties determined by the $H^{*}$-open structure. When the $H^{*}$-generated family forms a topology, the resulting associated space is used to relate generalized $H^{*}$-separation properties to their classical topological counterparts. We further examine compactness-type properties, subspace behaviour, and preservation under suitable mappings. Examples are included to illustrate how the structure generated by $H^{*}$-open sets may exhibit separation behaviour different from that of the original topology. The results provide a unified setting for connecting $H^{*}$-open-set theory with generalized topological structures and offer a basis for further investigation of separation and covering properties in this framework.

title: Inclusion-wise extremal knapsack problems are (mostly) hard to approximate
abstract: We study two inclusion-wise extremal variants of the 0-1 Knapsack Problem (KP). Given $n$ items with integer weights and nonnegative costs or profits, the Minimum-Cost Maximal Knapsack Packing Problem seeks a minimum-cost packing for capacity $c$ to which no item can be added, while the Maximum-Profit Minimal Knapsack Cover Problem seeks a maximum-profit cover for threshold $d$ from which no item can be removed. Both problems are weakly $\mathrm{NP}$-hard and pseudo-polynomially solvable, as is the classical KP, but their approximability is fundamentally different: unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$, with positive values neither problem admits a polynomial-time $2^{p(n)}$-approximation for any polynomial $p$; allowing zero values rules out every multiplicative factor. Even with unit costs for packing and unit profits for covering, neither admits an $n^{1-\varepsilon}$-approximation for any fixed $\varepsilon>0$, whereas a trivial $n$-approximation exists. We identify restrictions that restore approximability. If every item weighs at least a fixed fraction of the capacity, respectively of the threshold, both problems can be solved exactly in polynomial time. For the cover problem, if each weight $w_i$ satisfies $w_i-1\ge\delta(d-1)$, we give an approximation scheme for arbitrary profits whose running time is polynomial in $n$, $1/\varepsilon$, and $1/\delta$. If values equal weights, a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme (FPTAS) was already known for the packing problem; we give an FPTAS for the cover problem, improving on the previously known factor $2$. If value-to-weight ratios differ by at most a factor $\kappa$, we obtain a $(1+\varepsilon)\kappa$-approximation for both problems.

title: The Gauss--Newton Method for Phase Retrieval from Coded Diffraction Patterns
abstract: We study the minimum-norm Gauss--Newton method for phase retrieval from random coded diffraction patterns with additive intensity noise. For bounded symmetric masks satisfying the standard complex moment conditions, we establish convergence guarantees with quadratic error recursions in both the resampled and fixed-data settings. In the resampled setting, $O(\log^2 n)$ masks per independent block suffice to obtain a spectral initializer within a constant-relative-radius neighborhood and to establish a local quadratic error recursion with an additive noise term. Consequently, in the noiseless case, the method achieves relative accuracy $\epsilon$ using $O(\log\log(1/\epsilon)\log^2 n)$ masks. In the fixed-data setting, $O(\log^6(en))$ masks suffice for spectral initialization within a neighborhood whose relative radius is proportional to $\log^{-5/2}(nL)$. Within this neighborhood, the method satisfies a linear contraction bound and eventually a quadratic error recursion. In particular, in the noiseless case, the method initially converges linearly and enters a quadratic convergence phase after $O(\log n)$ iterations, without acquiring additional masks. Numerical experiments on synthetic signals and a natural image demonstrate the method's efficiency relative to state-of-the-art algorithms.

title: Lifted Restricted Isometry Property and Fast Algorithm for Spectral Compressed Sensing With Near-Optimal Sample Complexity
abstract: This paper studies the spectral compressed sensing problem, which aims to recover an $r$-spectrally-sparse signal of length $N$ from linear compressive measurements. We reformulate the problem as the recovery of a low-rank Hankel matrix. Motivated by this formulation, we propose a Lifted Restricted Isometry Property (LRIP) for the measurement matrix and show that Gaussian measurement matrices satisfy LRIP under certain conditions. Unlike classical RIP, LRIP imposes a rank constraint in the lifted matrix domain while taking measurements in the signal domain through the adjoint Hankel operator. To solve the resulting nonconvex problem efficiently, we introduce a Fast Iterative Hard Thresholding (FIHT) algorithm. Based on LRIP, we show that FIHT converges linearly to the true signal with high probability using $\mathcal{O}(r \ln r \ln^2 N)$ scaled Gaussian measurements, which is near-optimal up to log factors and improves the state-of-the-art order of $r^2$ for nonconvex Hankel methods. Extensive numerical results demonstrate the superiority of FIHT as compared to state-of-the-art convex methods in terms of phase transitions, computational time, and robustness to noise.

title: Distribution tail of the distance to infinity in supercritical bond percolation
abstract: We give an estimate for the distribution tail of the passage time between $0$ and $\infty$ in first-passage percolation on $\mathbb Z^d$, when the weight distribution is bounded and has a supercritical atom at $0$. A special case involves the number of disjoint cutsets between $0$ and $\infty$ in supercritical bond percolation. Besides, we show that the rate function for the upper-tail deviations of the point-to-point passage time is asymptotically polynomial near $0$.

title: Non-Potential Congestion Games with a Continuum of Players
abstract: We study a class of congestion games with a continuum of heterogeneous players and a finite set of resources, without assuming the existence of a potential function. Players differ in their individual characteristics and may contribute differently to congestion, which is represented through general aggregate features of the population choosing each resource. We characterize the conditions under which such a game admits a potential and show that this structure generally fails when players have heterogeneous impacts on congestion. To analyze the non-potential case, we introduce the concept of Stochastic Variational Nash Equilibrium, in which players observe idiosyncratic cost shocks before selecting a resource. We show that equilibrium choices are pure conditional on players' characteristics and shock realizations, whereas the induced aggregate allocation is probabilistic. Under Gumbel-distributed shocks, the equilibrium is equivalent to a continuum-player logit Quantal Response Equilibrium. Using a fixed-point formulation and the Schauder--Tychonoff theorem, we establish existence for every positive noise level and recover a pure Nash equilibrium in the zero-noise limit. Under a coordinate-wise monotonicity condition on aggregate interaction costs, we further prove uniqueness and convergence of the regularized allocations to the pure equilibrium. An application to electric vehicle charging illustrates how heterogeneous energy demands jointly affect station choice, congestion, and market shares.

title: Contractor Filters
abstract: We introduce Contractor Filters (CFs), a set-membership architecture for nonlinear continuous-time state estimation with bounded uncertainties and sporadic outliers. CFs represent feasible states symbolically by compositions of contractors rather than rematerializing a geometric enclosure after each update. This provides an abstraction layer between the set-theoretic filtering equations and their numerical realization, so prediction, correction, ambiguity, and outlier handling can be expressed within one algebra without prescribing a state geometry. We derive an exact nominal recursion and a guaranteed robust enclosure, with validated flow inclusions preserving soundness. Optional sub-paving compression then provides finite outer representations. CFs are evaluated against a robust particle filter on range-only and terrain-based localization under outliers, probabilistic model mismatch, association ambiguity, and multimodality. CFs retain the simulated truth in all tested configurations, while particle-filter reliability degrades under persistent bias and spatial aliasing. Contractor strength and compression budget control the trade-off between paving tightness and computational cost, while preserving the enclosure guarantee.

title: Completely symmetric subspaces of noncommutative $L_p$-spaces
abstract: Let $2<p<\infty$. We prove that every infinite-dimensional closed subspace $F$ of a noncommutative $L_p$-space contains a subspace completely isomorphic to $\ell_p$, $C_p$, $R_p$, or $C_p\cap R_p$ and completely complemented in $F$. This answers the question of Junge and Xu on the existence of completely symmetric basic sequences.

title: Orthonormal Strichartz estimates over fractal time
abstract: We study Strichartz estimates for orthonormal families of initial data when time is integrated against an $\alpha$-dimensional Frostman measure $\mu$, $0<\alpha\le1$, with coefficients measured in $\ell^\beta$. For the fractional Schr\"odinger, wave and Klein--Gordon equations, we obtain orthogonality gains in the admissible region and necessary conditions on $\beta$. For the fractional Schr\"odinger equation the exponents are sharp up to an endpoint; the optimality of the threshold $\beta=q/2$ requires $\mu$ to be Ahlfors regular. For the Schr\"odinger equation in dimensions $d\ge2$, we prove a Lorentz endpoint estimate and, if $d>2\alpha$, the critical exponent $\beta=q/2$ at every pair $2\le q,r<\infty$ with \[\frac d2(\frac12-\frac1r)\ge\frac\alpha q, \quad r>\frac{dq}{d-\alpha};\] on $r=\infty$ we obtain a restricted weak-type estimate. Since the constants depend on $\mu$ only through its Frostman constant, Lebesgue measure yields global-in-time critical estimates in this range when $d\ge3$. The proofs combine Frostman fractional integration, a spectral near--far argument at the endpoint, and asymmetric Hilbert--Schmidt bounds with orthogonal frequency-block summation. We also obtain further estimates in the low-dimensional cases $d=1$ (fractional Schr\"odinger) and $d=2$ (wave and Klein--Gordon) with $\alpha>1/2$, and formulate the consequences for densities of freely evolving states.

title: How to Train Your Intercept: A Comparison of Intercept Update Strategies in Coordinate Descent
abstract: Coordinate descent solvers for regularized generalized linear models (GLMs) differ in how they update the intercept. This seemingly routine choice can substantially affect convergence when the response is imbalanced. For direct coordinate descent on the original GLM loss, we compare a conservative step based on worst-case curvature, a safeguarded Newton step based on current curvature, and repeated Newton steps that solve the intercept subproblem. The conservative update can leave much of the interaction between the intercept and the coefficients unresolved, producing a slowdown when that interaction controls convergence. A single Newton step avoids this attenuation and, in our experiments, follows nearly the same outer trajectory as exact minimization while requiring fewer inner steps. Simulated and real-data experiments, including comparisons across six production solvers and a controlled intervention within skglm, support this explanation. We also show how the same mechanism appears in quadratic-approximation methods and extends to multinomial models with rare classes. We recommend a safeguarded Newton update for direct coordinate descent and full intercept optimization within frozen local quadratic surrogates.

title: A Smoothed Augmented Lagrangian Method for Mathematical Programs with Vertical Complementarity Constraints
abstract: We propose a smoothed augmented Lagrangian method (ALM) for solving mathematical programs with vertical complementarity constraints (VCCs). The augmented Lagrangian function involving the VCCs is smoothed by the Lasry--Lions double envelope, which is an extension of the Moreau envelope that enjoys enhanced smoothness properties. This construction yields a smooth unconstrained subproblem within the ALM framework that can be efficiently solved by many fast optimization algorithms. In the limiting setting, we establish global convergence to Mordukhovich- and Clarke-stationary points. For the convergence rate, we show that, under appropriate assumptions, the smoothed ALM achieves Q-linear convergence. We further provide a worst-case iteration complexity analysis for computing an approximate stationary point of the original problem or of an associated feasibility problem. Preliminary numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: A new approach for estimating the number of spikes in high-dimensional Gaussian models
abstract: In this paper, we study the estimation of the signal subspace dimension $k$ in a $p$-variate signal-plus-noise complex Gaussian model, when the noise covariance matrix is assumed to be diagonal or Toeplitz. We consider the high-dimensional asymptotic regime in which both the data dimension $p$ and the available sample size $n$ diverge to infinity at the same rate, while we also allow $k$ to diverge at a slower speed. In this context, the classical estimates of the literature, consistent in the high-dimensional regime, often rely on the a priori knowledge of an upper bound $k_*$ of $k$, which can be misspecified in practice. Our proposed approach relies on building estimates of the tracial moments of the noise covariance matrix using the $p-k_*$ smallest eigenvalues of the sample covariance matrix (SCM), which are in turn used to build a threshold above which the $k$ largest eigenvalues are isolated. The resulting estimate of $k$ is proved to be consistent in the high-dimensional regime, even for the misspecified situations where $k_* < k$. Numerical experiments in different challenging scenarios illustrate the improvement of the proposed approach over the aforementioned methods.

title: Non-additive symmetric rank-metric codes
abstract: We study non-additive rank-metric codes contained in the space of symmetric matrices over a finite field. Our main focus is on symmetric $2$-codes. For odd $q$, we introduce a quotient construction for $\mathrm{Sym}_3(q)$ in which rank-one differences are described by isotropic vectors of a nondegenerate quadratic form on $\mathbb F_q^4$. This leads to a correspondence with partial ovoids of the elliptic quadric $Q^-(5,q)$. Using a construction of Cossidente and Pavese, we obtain a non-additive symmetric $2$-code in $\mathrm{Sym}_3(q)$ of cardinality $q^4+2q^3$, improving the previously known general lower bound. We also give an explicit matrix description of this family. Lastly, we present a block-based construction for symmetric $2$-codes that extends the three-dimensional improvement to all odd dimensions. In particular, for every odd $n\geq3$ and every prime power $q>2$, we obtain \begin{equation*} A_q^{\rm sym}(n,2) \ge q^{(n^2-1)/2}+q^{(n^2-3)/2}+q^{(n^2-9)/2}, \end{equation*} which is strictly larger than the maximum cardinality of an additive symmetric $2$-code with the same parameters. This yields the first infinite family (as the matrix dimension $n$ varies) of non-additive symmetric $2$-codes whose size is larger than the largest achievable size of an additive code with the same parameters; before this, such a gap had only been established for $n=3$.

title: On Berndt-Straub conjectures about zeros of generalized Ramanujan polynomials
abstract: We settle two conjectures of Berndt and Straub asserting that all nonzero zeros of the generalized Ramanujan polynomials $R_k(x;\chi,\psi)$ and $S_{2n}(x;\chi,\chi)$ lie on the unit circle for real nonprincipal Dirichlet characters. We prove their conjecture for $R_k$. For $S_{2n}$, we prove that at most four nonzero zeros lie off the unit circle, all purely imaginary. If $\chi_{163}=\left(\frac{\cdot}{163}\right)$ is the primitive quadratic character modulo $163$, then $S_6(x;\chi_{163},\chi_{163})$ has four exceptional zeros, showing that this bound is sharp. This disproves the second conjecture and establishes that the `Riemann hypothesis for period polynomials' can fail for Eisenstein newforms. Further, we introduce a transcendental invariant whose sign determines whether exceptional zeros of $S_{2n}(x;\chi,\chi)$ occur in all sufficiently large degrees, and show that these zeros converge to transcendental limits off the unit circle. For primitive odd characters, we relate this invariant and these limits to Fekete polynomials.

title: Groups with the fixed-point property
abstract: We propose the study of the class of groups that fix a point for every continuous action on any convex compact space. Oliver completed the corresponding program of classifying the finite groups that have this fixed-point property in finite dimensions. Turning to infinite groups, the Schauder--Tychonoff theorem establishes that the integers have the fixed-point property, but this has not been shown for any other infinite, finitely generated group. We establish a local transfer principle and use it to show, as a proof of concept, that $\mathbf{Z} \times (\mathbf{Z}/p\mathbf{Z})$ belongs to this class of groups.

title: An application of the parameterization method to evolution flows associated to nonautonomous systems
abstract: Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional complete Riemannian manifold of bounded geometry. We consider a time-dependent vector field $X : \mathbb{R} \times M \to TM$ with $X_t:=X(t,\cdot) \in \mathfrak{X}^r(M)$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$ that satisfies some further uniform continuity assumptions. We suppose that $X$ admits a globally defined integral curve $\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to M$. To any isolated subset $\Omega$ of the Sacker-Sell spectrum of $t \mapsto \nabla X_t(\gamma(t))$, Sacker-Sell theory associates a subbundle $\mathscr{N}^\Omega$ of $T_\gamma M$ invariant under $\nabla X_t$. Under additional nonresonance conditions on $\Omega$, we prove, by an application of the parameterization method (Cabr\'e et al., 2003), the existence of an invariant topological submanifold $\mathscr{W}^\Omega \subset \mathbb{R} \times M$ with $C^r$ fibers $W_t^\Omega:= \mathscr{W}^\Omega \cap \{t\} \times M$ that is unique in a sufficiently smooth subclass of invariant manifolds uniformly tangent to $\mathscr{N}^\Omega$ (made precise later). We moreover show regularity of $\mathscr{W}^\Omega$ with respect to parameters, and characterize the attraction towards $\mathscr{W}^\Omega$ via a foliation in the case $\Omega$ is the slowest part of the spectrum.

title: Optimization Inverse Spectral Problem for the Schr\"odinger Operator on a Compact Graph
abstract: We study the optimization inverse spectral problem (OISP) for the first $m$ eigenvalues of the Schr\"odinger operator on a compact metric graph. We prove the existence of a solution for every strictly increasing finite set of prescribed eigenvalues. On a graph without cycles, we obtain a representation of the optimal correction as a linear combination of squared eigenfunctions, provided that the selected eigenvalues are simple and separated from the next eigenvalue. On a graph with cycles, under the same simplicity and separation assumptions, we obtain a strong limiting representation of the optimal potential in terms of eigenfunctions of approximating operators. For a graph with a cycle, we give a counterexample with simple eigenvalues and linearly dependent squared eigenfunctions. We also prove that linear dependence of the squares of nonzero restrictions to an edge of eigenfunctions corresponding to distinct eigenvalues forces the potential on that edge to have an analytic representative

title: Tournaments, flags, and spinors
abstract: It is observed that the dimension of the space of invariant spinors on the manifold $\mathrm{SU}(n)/T^{n-1}$ of full flags in $\mathbb{C}^n$ equals the number $\mathrm{RT}(n)$ of labelled regular tournaments of order $n$, for $n$ odd. This space is decomposed under a double cover of the Weyl group, and realized as a pair of eigenspaces, first for the Dirac operator, then for a twisted version of it which acts equivariantly; this is used to show that multiplicities of irreducible representations are even for $n\equiv 1\pmod 4$.

title: Supersymmetric Observables from Surface Defect Anomalies in 4d and 6d SCFTs
abstract: We study the contributions of half-BPS surface defects to supersymmetric Casimir energy and the universal logarithmic term of supersymmetric R\'enyi entropy in four- and six-dimensional SCFTs. Using equivariant integration of defect anomaly polynomials and its extension to supersymmetric R\'enyi backgrounds, we obtain closed expressions for these observables in terms of defect 't Hooft anomalies. For Gukov--Witten defects preserving transverse rotations in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N} = 4$ super Yang--Mills theories, both observables depend on a single R-symmetry anomaly. For $\mathcal{N} = (0, 4)$ defects in six-dimensional $\mathcal{N} = (1, 0)$ theories, additional terms arise from the gravitational anomaly. We provide complementary checks using chiral algebras, five-dimensional localization, and holographic probe branes at large $N$, while localized chiral fermions reproduce the gravitational-anomaly contributions. The framework also recovers Wilson-surface results in six-dimensional $\mathcal{N} = (2, 0)$ theories.

title: Computational framework NetBiF predicts and classifies steady-state bifurcations in biochemical systems via reaction network structure
abstract: Dynamics of biochemical systems are dictated by the stoichiometry and kinetics of reaction networks. These systems may admit positive steady states that could undergo qualitative change in response to varying rate parameters. These changes are called steady-state bifurcations, and they correspond to biologically meaningful processes. Classical bifurcation analysis relies on exact kinetics and rate parameters, which are often unknown or difficult to measure for complex systems. To address this, structural bifurcation analysis (SBA) was introduced to predict bifurcations using only the system's associated reaction network. In this work, the computational package NetBiF (Network Bifurcation Finder) is introduced to implement SBA. NetBiF is applied across diverse biochemical systems, including fundamental metabolic pathways, signaling and gene regulatory networks, and a large-scale carbon cycle model, to predict steady-state bifurcations. Crucially, for biochemical systems governed by power law kinetics, the implementation of NetBiF also classifies the steady-state bifurcations as saddle-node, transcritical, or pitchfork via a structural analog of Sotomayor's theorem. To this end, explicit formulations for the bifurcation criteria were derived for these biochemical systems. Determining and classifying bifurcation behaviors provide insight into biochemical systems' abilities to adapt to changing and fluctuating conditions. Collectively, the study presents NetBiF as a scalable, structure-based, and consistent computational tool to implement SBA. Our findings enable researchers to systematically study dynamical behaviors of biochemical systems through their reaction network structures without requiring explicit kinetic information.

title: Degree growth of rational and meromorphic self-maps
abstract: Let $f$ be a dominant rational self-map of a normal projective variety over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic, or a dominant meromorphic self-map of a compact K\"ahler manifold. We prove that in every codimension, the degree sequence of $f$ differs from its dynamical-degree growth by at most a polynomial factor, with an explicit universal bound on the polynomial exponent. In particular, subexponential but superpolynomial degree growth cannot occur. At a strict dynamical-degree break, we prove the sharper asymptotic \[ \mathrm{deg}_{i,\omega}(f^n)=C_{f,\omega,i}\,\lambda_i(f)^n+O(\eta^n), \] for every $\sqrt{\lambda_{i-1}(f)\lambda_{i+1}(f)}<\eta<\lambda_i(f)$. This extends the degree-asymptotic theorem of Dang--Favre from codimension one in characteristic zero to arbitrary codimension and arbitrary characteristic, and recovers the surface theorem of Boucksom--Favre--Jonsson. Both results rely on a uniform estimate for the temporal discrete logarithmic Laplacian of the degree sequences, obtained by applying the Ptolemy inequality to ordered Hodge--Lorentz packages on varying finite-time orbit spaces.

title: On the Convexity of the Upper Bild
abstract: We give a proof of the convexity of the upper bild of a quaternionic matrix, a theorem of So and Thompson. After reduction to $2\times2$ matrices, we introduce real coordinates on a sphere and obtain two representations of the upper bild over the closed unit ball, involving a convex function and a concave function. Minimizing the first and maximizing the second over parameters with a fixed real part yield a convex lower boundary function and a concave upper boundary function, from which convexity follows.

title: Actions of central Morita monoidal groupoids, and seven term exact sequences of all types
abstract: We introduce a strict monoidal groupoid associated with a given commutative ring $K$. It acts on the Clifford extension systems of $K$-central algebras which are graded by a group $G$, as well as on the generalized collective characters, both of type $\phi \in$ Hom$(G,$ Aut$(K))$. These actions partition the two sets above with respect to graded Morita equivalence. By that we establish a seven term exact sequence of type $\phi$, which boils down to the celebrated Chase-Harrison-Rosenberg sequence when $\phi$ is Galois.

title: Stability Analysis of Bounded Solutions to 2-D Incompressible Navier-Stokes Equations in L^2_uloc Spaces
abstract:
This paper examines the stability analysis of two-dimensional incompressible fluids in $L^2_{uloc}$ spaces. Extending the classical stability framework for Euler equations in Yudovich-type settings, we establish the convergence of Navier-Stokes solutions toward Euler solutions as viscosity $
u 	o 0$, under the weakened assumptions $u^
u_0 \in L^\infty$ and $\omega^
u_0 \in L^\infty$ without imposing decay conditions at infinity. We first derive a priori estimates for the Navier-Stokes equations in $L^\infty$ spaces. Then, using harmonic analysis tools including Littlewood-Paley decomposition and Bony's paraproduct calculus, we prove the $L^\infty$-convergence of the velocity field and $L^2_{uloc}$-convergence of the vorticity as $
u 	o 0$.

title: The one percent property for free groups
abstract: We prove that for every $\varepsilon >0$, there is $\delta >0$ such that for every probability measure $\mu$ on a free group $\mathbb{F}$, if the operator norm of the action of $\mu$ on $L^2\mathbb{F}$ by convolution exceeds $\varepsilon$, then there is a coset of an abelian subgroup of $\mathbb{F}$ with $\mu$-mass at least $\delta$.

title: Density of polynomials whose Aron--Berner extensions attain their norms
abstract: We establish a polynomial analogue of Lindenstrauss' theorem in full generality. More precisely, we prove that, for every real or complex Banach space X and every positive integer n, the n-homogeneous scalar-valued polynomials whose Aron-Berner extensions to the bidual X** attain their norms form a dense subset of the space of continuous n-homogeneous polynomials on X. This resolves a problem posed by Aron, Garcia and Maestre in 2003, extending their result for quadratic polynomials to arbitrary degrees without imposing any structural assumptions on the underlying Banach space. We further establish the corresponding theorem for vector-valued polynomials with arbitrary Banach space codomains. Our approach relies on a new perturbation scheme based on averaged linear contractions, which provides simultaneous control of the multilinear variables and yields norm attainment through iterated limits in the bidual.

title: Extensions of Operator Systems, Hyperrigidity and Quantum Double Suspension
abstract: We introduce a class of extensions of unital operator systems satisfying a certain Toeplitz type property. We show that these extensions induce corresponding extensions of the $C^*$-algebras they generate. We prove that hyperrigidity is preserved under these extensions, yielding new examples through iteration. We introduce the quantum double suspension of operator systems as a special class of these extensions and show that its iterates yield the Hong-Szyma\'nski quantum double suspensions at the $C^*$-algebra level, encompassing, in particular, the Vaksman-Soibelman quantum spheres. We construct hyperrigid operator systems underlying these quantum spheres. As a further application, we show that every counterexample to Arveson's hyperrigidity conjecture gives rise to a sequence of counterexamples. We identify the $C^*$-envelopes of these extensions and use this identification to obtain a $K$-theoretic condition ensuring that each such sequence contains infinitely many pairwise non-isomorphic counterexamples. We also observe that the validity of the conjecture in the commutative setting is linked to its validity for an infinite family of noncommutative operator systems obtained through successive extensions. Finally, we compute the propagation number, an invariant of operator systems introduced by Connes and van Suijlekom, for these extensions.

title: Excess inertia of finite metric spaces
abstract: This paper classifies the possible inertias that are realized by an excess matrix of a finite metric space with at most nine points. For the classification, we make use of relationships between finite metric spaces and non-obtuse and acute sets in classical geometry. As an application, we prove that the small-scale limit of the magnitude function of any six-point metric space is at least one whenever this limit exists.

title: Topological entropy of saturated sets for Lorenz attractors
abstract: We study the topological entropy of saturated sets for continuous flows, with emphasis on singular hyperbolic dynamics. For a $C^r$-generic ($r \geq 2$) vector field $X$ carrying a geometric Lorenz attractor $\Lambda$, we prove that for every nonempty compact connected set $\mathcal{K} \subseteq \mathcal{M}(\Phi,\Lambda)$ and every open set $U \subseteq M$ with $U \cap \Lambda \neq \emptyset$, $h_{\mathrm{top}}(\Phi,G_{\mathcal{K}}(\Phi) \cap \operatorname{Trans}(\Phi,\Lambda) \cap U)=\inf_{\mu \in \mathcal{K}} h_\mu(\phi_1)$, where $\Phi=(\phi_t)_{t \in \mathbb{R}}$ is the flow induced by $X$ and $\operatorname{Trans}(\Phi,\Lambda)$ denotes the set of points whose positive orbits are dense in $\Lambda$. The same formula holds $C^1$-generically for singular hyperbolic attractors. In contrast with the uniformly hyperbolic case, we also prove that, for vector fields in a dense subset of $\mathcal{X}^r(M^3)$, geometric Lorenz attractors admit a positive-entropy invariant measure with no generic points. An analogous conclusion holds for vector fields in a dense subset of $\mathcal{X}^1(M)$ whose non-trivial singular hyperbolic attractors contain singularities and satisfy $\dim E^{cu}=2$. These examples show that the discrete-time saturated entropy theory does not extend directly to singular flows.

title: Standard identities for polynomial vector fields
abstract: Let $W_n$ be the Lie algebra of polynomial vector fields in $n$ variables over a field of characteristic zero, and let $s_k$ denote the alternating sum of compositions of $k$ vector fields. The identity $s_{n^2+2n-1}=0$ has been asserted for arbitrary $n$. We give an explicit counterexample in dimension five, verified by an exact integer computation of a $34$-commutator. Together with the known vanishing of $s_{35}$, this shows that $35$ is the least degree of a standard identity on $W_5$. We then prove that $s_{n^2+2n-1}=0$ for every even $n\geq2$. The proof uses Lie algebra homology with coefficients in the polynomial algebra modulo constants and a lemma on invariant tensors. We describe the computation and provide the source code and verification results.
comments: 8 pages, no figures; verification code and results available at https://github.com/nurtasshyntas/n-commutator-verifier

title: Reverse Translation and Convolution Estimates in the Framework of the Mehler-Fock Transform
abstract: In this paper, reverse translation and convolution estimates in the frame of $\mu^{th}$ order Mehler-Fock transform are obtained. Continuity properties of these operators on the test function space $\mathfrak{H}_{l,r,n}$ have been discussed. Moreover, Sobolev space $S_{r,p}^{N,\alpha}$ has been introduced and again continuity properties of these operators in this Sobolev space have been discussed.

title: Alternating Hamilton Paths and Cycles in Poset Products
abstract: We study alternating Hamilton paths and cycles in the comparability graphs of finite posets. We prove that if a finite poset $P$ with at least two elements admits an alternating Hamilton path, then $P\times B_r$ admits an alternating Hamilton cycle for every $r\ge2$, where $B_r$ is the Boolean lattice. As a corollary, we settle a conjecture of Katona [Discrete Appl. Math., 2013]. Furthermore, we characterize the divisor lattices admitting alternating Hamilton paths and cycles.

title: Learning a Group Element from Its Action: Galois Correspondences, Optimal ERM, and an Abel-Ruffini Threshold for the Natarajan Dimension
abstract: We study learning an unknown element $g$ of a group acting with finite orbits on a countable set, from examples $(x,gx)$. After a sample on $A$, the consistent hypotheses are the restrictions of a coset of the pointwise stabilizer of $A$, and the sample forces exactly the labels of points this stabilizer fixes; for a Galois group, they form the field generated by the data. Through this correspondence, multiclass dimensions become group invariants: the DS and graph dimensions equal the height, the Littlestone dimension the longest irredundant sequence length, and the teaching dimension the minimal base size. Among deterministic learners, symmetry makes empirical risk minimization optimal: on nondegenerate classes every consistent learner, whatever its tie-breaking, attains the optimal realizable sample complexity up to constant factors, and every consistent online learner the optimal mistake bound. Agnostically, every ERM's sample complexity exceeds the known lower bound by at most the DS-to-Natarajan ratio, up to constants. For finite Galois extensions of countable fields, the Natarajan dimension equals a group invariant, the coset-cube number, which is at least the number of complemented factors of any chief series of any subgroup. Hence the dimensions coincide for every solvable Galois group, while for the groups $A_5$ and $S_5$ of the quintic they are $2<3$ and $3<4$, and $A_5$ is the smallest group with a gap. For the Galois group $S_n$ of the general equation of degree $n$, they coincide exactly when $n\le 4$, i.e., in characteristic zero, exactly when the equation is solvable by radicals; the implication is one-way, as the simple group $\mathrm{PSL}(2,8)$ has no gap. For linear, orthogonal and unitary maps of $\mathbb R^d$ or $\mathbb C^d$ both dimensions equal $d$, and a two-fibered pseudo-cube is a disjoint union of Natarajan cubes exactly when its monodromy group is abelian.
comments: 55 pages, 5 figures. The abstract has been shortened to meet arXiv's submission requirements

title: UQ-ACE: Stability-Aware Counterfactual Controller Tuning via Bayesian SINDy
abstract: Retuning feedback controllers in critical processes is challenging when experiments are costly, open-loop excitation is infeasible, and candidate controllers must be screened before deployment. The existing Adaptive Sampling for Counterfactual Explanations (ACE) method provides a sample-efficient approach for finding minimal controller-parameter changes that recover prescribed closed-loop performance, but it does not explicitly account for stability of candidate controllers proposed during the search, which may be destabilizing under plant uncertainty. This paper introduces UQ-ACE, a stability-aware retuning method based on Bayesian SINDy. In UQ-ACE, closed-loop trajectories are used to infer a posterior distribution over local dynamical models, from which candidate controllers are screened for stability before implementation. Extensive simulations show that UQ-ACE achieves valid retunings with few closed-loop experiments while preventing deployment of unstable candidates.

title: Automorphisms of medium algebras and quasi-anisotropic real affine Grassmannians
abstract: We study automorphisms of Hausel's medium algebras by identifying them with equivariant cohomology algebras of affine Schubert varieties of a complex reductive group $G$. The automorphisms in question are then given by the action of either complex automorphisms or real structures of $G$ on affine Schubert varieties. We focus on describing the fixed points of those automorphisms on the spectra of medium algebras, and prove that the torsion-free quotients of the corresponding coinvariant algebras are isomorphic to equivariant cohomology rings of fixed loci in affine Schubert varieties. In the case of real structures, this naturally leads to and involves the study of affine Grassmannians for quasi-anisotropic (also called quasi-compact) real reductive groups, closely related to recent work of O'Brien. We also discuss relations to automorphisms of Higgs bundle moduli and to symmetric pair variants of medium algebras.

title: Numerical simulation of biological capsules based on interface-fitted polygonal meshes
abstract: In this work we introduce a numerical framework for the simulation of biological capsules based on meshes that adapt iteration-wise to the shape of the membrane. The discretization leverages a Hybrid High Order method (HHO) to solve a Stokes problem with a source term distributed on the interface between the internal and the external phases. The HHO discretization supports meshes composed of general polygons, permitting to use fitted meshes that can be easily generated by cutting the elements intersected by the interface. Moreover, polygonal meshes allow arbitrarily accurate interface discretizations without introducing bulk degrees of freedom. The presentation of the simulation algorithm is completed with a proof-of-concept numerical test on a well-established benchmark: the deformation of an elastic capsule immersed in a shear flow.

title: Multi-dimensional centered rarefaction waves of gas dynamics with vacuum states
abstract: We consider the two-dimensional isentropic compressible Euler equations for a polytropic gas, $p(\rho)=k\rho^{\gamma}$. The $R$--vacuum state--$R$ configuration---two rarefaction waves bounding a vacuum---occurs when the two constant states move apart with sufficiently large relative velocity and is essentially the only vacuum-forming Riemann pattern in the absence of external forces. Local-in-time rarefaction fronts have been constructed only away from vacuum, where the sound speed is bounded away from zero; their construction through the vacuum edge, and hence the structural stability of the $R$--vacuum state--$R$ configuration, has remained open. We establish this stability for $\gamma\in(1,1.3]\cup\{\frac{5}{3},\frac{7}{5}\}$: for sufficiently small perturbations, the Riemann problem admits a continuous entropy solution on a fixed time interval, with the domain partitioned by four characteristic surfaces and the solution in the three central regions belonging to $W^{2,\infty}$ in the self-similar coordinates $(t,x_{1}/t,x_{2})$, even though it may contain logarithmic singularities of the form $c^{\alpha}(\ln c)^{\beta}$ at the vacuum edge. The proof develops a geometric formulation directly on the first-order system, together with a direct analysis of the initial slice at the vacuum edge, where the formal high-order expansion fails.

title: Uniqueness of solutions to the 2D compressible Navier-Stokes equations for bounded densities
abstract: We prove the uniqueness of global solutions to the two dimensional barotropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations within the regularity class introduced by Danchin and Mucha [14], for general $C^1$ pressure laws. A crucial assumption is that both solutions have bounded divergence, locally integrable in time, which ensures that their densities remain bounded without excluding vacuum or requiring spatial regularity of the density.

title: Backward and reflected backward stochastic differential equations under initial enlargement of Brownian filtrations
abstract: We investigate the effect of initially enlarging a Brownian filtration by its terminal value on backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) and reflected BSDEs (RBSDEs). We establish the Brownian innovation representation and the predictable representation property in the enlarged filtration, highlighting the singular information drift arising from the semimartingale decomposition of the original Brownian motion. We derive transfer identities under suitable integrability conditions and provide explicit counterexamples showing that the resulting singular equations may fail to admit unique square-integrable solutions, including in the reflected case. We further develop a conditional parametrization of regular BSDEs and establish a conditional comparison principle for Snell envelopes, illustrating both the strict value of additional information and the failure of general pathwise domination. An exact projection identity is also obtained for zero-driver terminal payoffs. Finally, we discuss possible extensions to irregular obstacles and more general information structures.

title: Large deviations, gradient flows and fluctuating hydrodynamics for fractional diffusion
abstract: This work is a step towards a general understanding of fluctuations for systems of particles described at large scale by fractional diffusion. First, we derive formally a Large Deviation Principle for the empirical measure of mean-field interacting particles with a L{\'e}vy-type noise. In the case of independent particles, this unveils a generalized gradient flow structure at large scales. Second, we derive and solve numerically a stochastic Partial Differential Equation describing the fluctuating hydrodynamics of this system. The results compare well with direct numerical integration of the particles' dynamics.

title: Deterministic Distributed Linearly Separable Computation via Nested Cyclic Codes
abstract: We study the $(K,N,S,M,K_c)$ distributed linearly separable computation (DLSC) setting, where a master employs $N$ workers with a per-worker computation load of $M$ to recover $K_c$ deterministic linear combinations of $K$ messages in the presence of up to $S$ stragglers. We propose a DLSC framework based on nested cyclic codes that achieves $M=\frac{K}{N}(S+K_c)$. For sufficiently large $K$, we establish the matching converse $M\geq\frac{K}{N}(S+K_c)$, proving the asymptotic computation load optimality of the proposed framework. By instantiating cyclic locally recoverable codes (LRCs) as base codes in the framework, the master can recover the desired $K_c$ linear combinations by contacting fewer than $N-S$ workers under many straggler scenarios. This essentially softens the straggler threshold without increasing the computation load or communication cost. Finally, we extend the construction to reduce the per-worker communication load by a factor of $m$, while achieving an asymptotically optimal computation load of $M=\frac{K}{N}(S+mK_c)$.

title: Finite groups with conjugacy classes of size $2p^n$
abstract: We extend Burnside's $p^a$-Theorem on conjugacy classes of prime-power size by proving that no non-abelian finite simple group possesses a conjugacy class of size $2p^n$ for any prime $p$ and $n\geq 0$. Based on this, we partially extend a well-known result of L. Kazarin by showing that, given a finite group $G$, the subgroup generated by a conjugacy class $x^G$ of size $2p^n$ where $x$ has odd order, is a solvable normal subgroup of $G$. If instead the subgroup $\langle x^G \rangle$ generated by such a class $x^G$ is non-solvable (which forces $x$ to have even order), then $p= 5$ and $\langle x^G \rangle/S(\langle x^G \rangle)$ is isomorphic to the symmetric group $S_5$, where $S(\langle x^G \rangle)$ denotes the solvable radical of $\langle x^G \rangle$.

title: Singularities of Mean Curvature Flow with Bounded Total Curvature
abstract: We prove that every tangent flow at the first singular time of a smooth, closed, embedded mean curvature flow has smooth support, provided that the total curvature satisfies $\sup_{t\in[0,T)}\int_{M_t}|A|^n\,d\mu_t<\infty$. This extends Ilmanen's smoothness result for tangent flows to higher dimensions.

title: A counting proof for the smallest critical set in a Latin square
abstract: A critical set in a Latin square is a set of entries that determines the square uniquely and is minimal with this property. We prove that every partial Latin square of order $n$ with fewer than $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor$ filled cells has an even number of completions. Consequently every critical set in every Latin square of order $n$ has at least $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor$ entries. Since the cyclic Latin square has a critical set of exactly this size, the minimum size of a critical set over all Latin squares of order $n$ is $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor$. This confirms a conjecture attributed to Nelder (1979) and made independently by Mahmoodian and by Bate and van Rees. Hatami and Qian had shown that this minimum is at least $n^2/10^4$ for large $n$. The proof is a counting argument modulo two that uses only expansion of products, cancellation in pairs and the pigeonhole principle, and it is illustrated with partial Latin squares of orders three to seven. An appendix discloses the substantial use of AI in developing the proof and writing the exposition.

title: Interpolation and coherence in multiple testing
abstract: In the literature on multiple testing methods that control the familywise error rate, a fundamental concept is "coherence". A procedure is coherent if it is "logically consistent" (Hochberg and Tamhane, 1987) in the sense that if a hypothesis is rejected, then all hypotheses that imply it are also rejected. If a method is not coherent, then it can be made coherent without increasing the familywise error rate. Recently, the concept of coherence was generalized to a much broader class of multiple testing procedures, namely all methods that provide simultaneous confidence bounds for false discovery proportions. Such procedures were defined to be coherent if they cannot be further improved through a process called "interpolation". However, we show that such a coherent procedure can sometimes be further improved by exploiting remaining logical inconsistencies. This leads to what we call a "perfectly coherent" method. Thus, interpolation does not necessarily lead to perfect coherence. However, we provide conditions under which it does. Fortunately, many methods based on interpolation turn out to be perfectly coherent.

title: Hyperelastic Modeling of Cardiac Tissue Deformation for Data Registration
abstract: This work proposes a biomechanical registration framework designed to combine functional optical-mapping data with structural high-resolution MRI of cardiac tissue. The two acquisitions are performed in different mechanical configurations: optical mapping is obtained after stretching the sample, whereas MRI is acquired in a fixed resting state. To estimate the deformation between these configurations, the tissue is modeled as a nearly incompressible transversely isotropic hyperelastic material, and the traction amplitude is identified from optical-map marker positions through an inverse problem. Two-and threedimensional simulations show physically admissible deformations and provide a first proof of concept for the proposed strategy.
journal_ref: CinC 2026 - 53rd Computing in Cardiology conference, Sep 2026, Madrid, Spain

title: Combinatorial bounds for the v-number of binomial edge ideals
abstract: We study the local $\mathrm v$-numbers of binomial edge ideals from a combinatorial perspective. For each minimal prime $P_{\mathcal S}$ of $J_G$, indexed by a cutset $\mathcal S$ of $G$, we consider two combinatorial invariants, $\mathrm v^-_{\mathcal S}(G)$ and $\mathrm v^+_{\mathcal S}(G)$, defined in terms of transversals of suitable hypergraphs, and show that the local $\mathrm v$-number $\mathrm v_{P_{\mathcal S}}(J_G)$ satisfies $\mathrm v^-_{\mathcal S}(G)\leq \mathrm v_{P_{\mathcal S}}(J_G)\leq \mathrm v^+_{\mathcal S}(G)$. Under a suitable hypothesis on the connected components, we provide explicit graph-theoretic descriptions of these invariants and analyze when they coincide, giving a combinatorial way to determine the local $\mathrm v$-numbers. As an application, we derive a sufficient condition for this coincidence, which applies to a broad class of graphs. Furthermore, we identify a constant that controls the gap between $\mathrm v^-_{\mathcal S}(G)$ and $\mathrm v^+_{\mathcal S}(G)$, thereby showing that the local $\mathrm{v}$-number lies within a bounded interval. Applications to cycles and trees illustrate both the equality criterion and the resulting bounds.

title: A certified classical-strip comparison for the de Bruijn-Newman constant
abstract: We give a directed comparison beginning with the classical zero strip \(\lvert\Ima z\rvert\le1\) for the de Bruijn--Newman heat deformation. Under explicitly stated complete model-to-function source, localisation and global contact premises, translated-probe estimates imply \[ \Lambda\le\frac{148611789321711}{10^{15}} =0.148611789321711<0.148612. \] The construction uses Raymond's finite source data and 57 fixed translated kernels, independently checked by rational Bernstein certificates. An explicit finite Weyl estimate improves the positive first-head tail and its centred logarithmic moment. A centred cone transfer retains the original physical error allowances, exceptional debit and additive cone reserve, and charges the change in existing phase-surplus credits. Directed tail enclosures are regenerated at 192 and 256 bits; a separate exact-rational auditor accepts all 19,023 comparison steps. The controlled decrease from the complete two-source comparison is \(0.000021760452379\). We also prove a compatible matched logarithmic tail transfer and identify the finite requirements for stronger exponent pairs. A supplementary section records Raymond's ceiling below \(0.116398\) under the distinct \(7/8\) zero-free hypothesis.

title: T^2-invariant Einstein metrics on closed 4-manifolds
abstract: We construct $T^2$-invariant Einstein metrics with positive Ricci curvature on #_m(S^2 x S^2) for every integer $m>1$. These provide infinite family of Einstein metrics on closed $4$-manifolds with $\lambda>0$, which are in addition not Hermitian. We further establish the uniqueness of the $T^2$-invariant Einstein metrics on $S^4$, CP^2, S^2 x S^2, and CP^2#\bar{CP}^2.

title: Frobenius liftability of isolated complete intersections
abstract: We classify Frobenius liftable normal isolated complete intersection singularities of dimension at least three over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic. In dimension three, they are precisely the regular points and the ordinary double points; in higher dimensions, they are regular. We also characterize Frobenius liftability of the complete local hypersurfaces defined by $xy-g(z,t)$ without assuming that the singularity is isolated. Such a hypersurface is Frobenius liftable if and only if, after a formal change of coordinates, $g$ is a unit times $H^pz^at^b$ with $0\le a,b<p$.

title: Isometric dilations and Beurling quotient modules
abstract: In \cite{Dan-Guo}, the authors provided a characterization of all sequences of doubly commuting pure contractions that have the sequence $\textbf{M}_z,$ the sequence of the multiplication by the coordinate functions on the vector-valued Hardy space $H^2_\mathcal E(\mathbb {D}_2^{(\infty)})$ over the Hilbert's multidisk $\mathbb D_2^{(\infty)},$ as their minimal isometric dilation for some Hilbert space $\mathcal E$. In this article, we remove the hypothesis of doubly commutativity and characterize all sequences of commuting contractions that are unitarily equivalent to $(P_{\mathcal Q}M_{z_i}|_{\mathcal Q})_{i\geq 1}$ for some quotient module $\mathcal Q$ of $H^2_\mathcal E(\mathbb D_2^{(\infty)})$. We further characterize those sequences for which $\mathcal Q$ is a Beurling quotient module. This generalizes Theorem 3.2 from \cite{BKD} to a sequence of commuting contractions.

title: Counting matrices with given characteristic polynomial
abstract: Let $f$ be a monic polynomial of degree $n$ with integer coefficients. We use Fourier analysis to prove a new upper bound on the number of $n\times n$ matrices with characteristic polynomial $f$ and integer entries in $[-T,T]$, as $T\to \infty$. The implied constant in our bound only depends on $n$ and is otherwise uniform in $f$. Our bound improves on recent work of Habegger, Ostafe and Shparlinski for $n\geq 4$.

title: Generic Local Identifiability Does Not Imply Generic Global Identifiability in Linear Networks
abstract: We give a counterexample to the implication from generic local to generic global identifiability for linear networks with a fixed topology, independently unknown edge coefficients, and selected excited and measured nodes. A six-node network with nine unknown coefficients has exactly two compatible parameter vectors generically. Adding six excited and measured nodes preserves this ambiguity while making the added coefficients directly recoverable. The resulting twelve-node structure has forty-two independent unknown coefficients and zero diagonal. For every positive bound on the largest eigenvalue magnitude, a nonempty open set of parameters has two distinct compatible networks satisfying that bound. This holds for both real and complex coefficients. Other open regions have exactly one admissible solution. The proof uses a rational transformation exchanging the two solutions and a common limiting matrix whose fourth power vanishes. Exact rational-number certificates verify an explicit pair. The construction also extends algebraically when the unknown coordinates are whole rational transfer functions. Genericity in prescribed numerator and denominator coefficient families, and the requirement that every transfer function vanish at infinite frequency, remain separate questions.

title: Composite and Stochastic Smoothed Decentralized Bregman Proximal-Gradient Methods
abstract: Smoothed decentralized Bregman proximal-gradient (SDBPG) methods combine relative-smoothness geometry with edge-dual consensus. We extend SDBPG to node-specific convex nonsmooth regularizers and unbiased stochastic local gradients while retaining its Bregman primal-dual smoothing mechanism. The analysis isolates temporal subgradient motion and aggregation mismatch as two defect sequences. For trajectories in a forward-invariant compact subset of the kernel domain and admissible parameters, finite accumulated defects yield an $O(T^{-1})$ bound on the squared best-iterate proximal residual over $T$ iterations. The stochastic bound separates accumulated oracle variance from expected defects and attains the same order when the variance bounds and expected defects are summable. Common active-structure identification, together with local subgradient conditions, gives sufficient finite-defect conditions for $\ell_1$ and group $\ell_{2,1}$ regularization. Experiments with common regularizers and heterogeneous sensing operators relate defect decay to observed support stabilization and compare reconstruction and communication with decentralized proximal and gradient-tracking methods. A separate phase-retrieval study evaluates the effect of a quartic Bregman kernel. Code and experiment scripts are available at https://github.com/shengze-xu/composite-stochastic-sdbpg .

title: Sparse-group Convoluted Smoothed Quantile Regression in High Dimension
abstract: In many applications, covariates are naturally organized into groups, yet conventional group-selection methods often retain all variables within selected groups, failing to achieve within-group sparsity. To address this limitation, we propose an adaptive two-stage sparse-group selection procedure for high-dimensional quantile regression.
