The proposed method integrates convolution-smoothed quantile loss with $\ell_{2,0}$ and $\ell_0$ penalties to identify important groups and relevant variables within them, achieving sparsity at both levels. We establish theoretical guarantees for sure screening and exact support recovery at both stages, as well as consistent model-size selection using information criteria, with explicit bounds on failure probabilities. The proposed procedure is computationally efficient by restricting optimization to selected groups and active variables. Simulation studies and a breast cancer gene-expression analysis demonstrate its competitive performance in variable selection, estimation accuracy, and computational efficiency, while identifying biologically relevant genes and delivering accurate quantile predictions.

title: On Chen's conjecture for the log-concavity of the longest increasing subsequence distribution
abstract: Let $P_{n,k}$ count permutations of $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ whose longest increasing subsequence has length $k$. Chen conjectured that $(P_{n,k})_{k=1}^n$ is log-concave for every positive integer $n$. In this paper, we prove that Chen's conjecture is true when $n\ge 10^{10^{65}}$. The proof combines Gessel's determinantal formula with quantitative coefficient extraction, Tracy--Widom density estimates, and exact inequalities for the extreme lengths.

title: River ribbon tableaux and symmetric group characters
abstract: We introduce river ribbon tableaux, where a river of non-trivial ribbons is placed between two banks of single boxes. Compared to other ribbon peelings, this reduces the geometric differences across diagrams of different shapes, and the maximal number of ribbon configurations. This allows us to prove a uniform character bound for symmetric groups which, specialized to balanced diagrams, proves the conjecture of Moore and Russell. As an application, we prove a conjecture of Dousse and F\'eray on the number of standard tableaux of skew shapes.

title: One-way pressure-independent valves with hysteresis and chattering
abstract: We propose a model for the one-dimensional isothermal gas flow through a valve in a pipe. The valve aims at keeping the outgoing flow in an assigned interval; moreover, its opening and closing depend on a further parameter. The model is realized by a system of two conservation laws with suitable conditions coupling the ingoing and the outgoing flow. We study the corresponding Riemann problem, where non-classical shocks show up. Although simple, the model allows to study two key oscillatory behaviors of the flow, which are due, respectively, to the chattering of the valve, especially seen in the numerical simulations, and to the stabilizing hysteresis induced by the valve operation. We characterize the states leading to chattering and show how they depend on the parameters of the model. Through several numerical simulations, we study the interplay between the two above phenomena.

title: Integral trace duality and the Witt filtration on Lubin--Tate space
abstract: Let $\mathcal O$ be the Lubin--Tate deformation ring of a one-dimensional commutative formal group of finite height $n\geq1$ over a perfect field $k$ of characteristic $p$. We identify Rezk's Witt filtration $\{I_d\}$ with the divisibility filtration of integral trace pairings on subgroup algebras of fixed source lifts. This gives the geometric recursion \[ I_{d+1}=pI_d+J_{d,z}\qquad(d\geq0), \] where $J_{d,z}$ defines the targets of order-$p^d$ quotient isogenies from a $W(k)$-valued lift $z$ of the closed point. The corrected ideal is independent of $z$. We also compute the cokernel of the universal source trace pairing over $\mathcal O$: it is $\bigoplus_{j=1}^d(\mathcal O/p^j)^{r_j-r_{j-1}}$, where $r_j$ counts order-$p^j$ subgroups of $(\mathbf Q_p/\mathbf Z_p)^n$. The same duality extends the generic trace along two-step isogeny flags to an integral surjection, even when the flag-forgetting map is not flat. This computes composition in the subring of weighted trace operations. Applications include sharp projector denominators and congruence fibre products for full-torsion loci.

title: Interior Hessian estimates for $k$-convex solutions of Hessian quotient equations
abstract: We study interior Hessian estimates for $k$-convex solutions of Hessian quotient equations $\frac{\sigma_k(D^2u)}{\sigma_\ell(D^2u)}=1$ with $2\leq k\leq n$, $0 \leq \ell < k$, and $k-\ell \in\{1,2\}$. We first adopt the unified quantitative separation-propagation method of Li--Wu [LW26b] to derive a doubling inequality, and then use the compactness argument of Shankar--Yuan [SY25] to obtain the estimates. This approach also applies to a class of general Hessian equations.

title: Square-Root Profiles and Sharp Fourier Decay of Quasiperiodic Spectral Measures
abstract: We study spectral measures of one-dimensional quasiperiodic Schr\"odinger operators. For subcritical Schr\"odinger operator with Diophantine frequency, we prove sharp measurable-set bounds, answering a question of Avila and Jitomirskaya \cite{AJ}; we prove optimal Fourier decay and the sharp decay order of the time-averaged quantum return probability, confirming a conjecture of Aloisio, Carvalho, and de Oliveira \cite{ACO} and a prediction of Zhong and Mosseri \cite{ZhongMosseri}. For the subcritical almost Mathieu operator, we establish summable square-root envelopes for the spectral density, with an optimal density-one formulation of the lower bound, thereby answering a question of Avila \cite{Aqi}. These results follow from a general theorem for reflectionless measures under a summable square-root Craig-type condition. We establish an exact residue expansion of the squared Borel transform, which connects local density blow-up with long-time averaged return probabilities: the endpoint residues determine both the square-root edge profiles and the leading coefficient of the time-averaged return probability.

title: The influence of decay in dynamic models of gene regulatory networks
abstract: We investigate the influence of decay rates on the dynamics of three-dimensional gene regulatory networks modeled by nonlinear differential equations with logistic sigmoidal regulatory functions. Particular attention is paid to the existence, location, and stability of equilibrium points in systems involving numerous interacting parameters. An explicit analytical representation of a central equilibrium is obtained under suitable relations between the regulatory weights, thresholds, and decay coefficients, allowing its location to be determined without solving the corresponding nonlinear algebraic system numerically. General formulas for the characteristic polynomial of the linearized system are derived, and spectral conditions for instability are established for several classes of regulatory interactions. We demonstrate how variations in decay rates can change the number and stability of equilibria, transform oscillatory dynamics, and influence the emergence or suppression of complicated attractors. The possibility of chaotic behavior is investigated through eigenvalue configurations, Lyapunov exponents, and the Kaplan-Yorke dimension. Numerical examples illustrate the sensitivity of the dynamics to decay parameters, including the suppression of previously observed chaotic behavior. The results provide an analytical framework for investigating equilibrium configurations, stability transitions, and complex dynamics in parametrized gene regulatory networks.

title: Improved Analysis of Adaptive Task Allocation and Non-Stationary Processing Times
abstract: We study the task allocation problem, where our goal is to develop an online algorithm that efficiently distributes tasks among workers based on their computational performance. This task is challenging since computation times are random and non-stationary in practice. Recent works have introduced different online algorithms to address this problem. One of them is Adaptive Task Allocation (ATA), a bandit-style algorithm. However, previous theoretical guarantees leave substantial room for improvement, and existing methods are designed only for stationary computation times. Using new proof techniques, our work establishes an improved analysis of ATA with better gap-dependent and gap-independent regret guarantees, improving upon all previous approaches. We also introduce a new method, Sliding Window Adaptive Task Allocation (SW-ATA), designed for more practical non-stationary environments. Finally, we prove new lower bounds in both the stationary and non-stationary settings.

title: The operator-valued Schur-Agler class in infinitely many variables
abstract: Motivated by a recent work of G. Knese [Canad. Math. Bull., 2026], we introduce the operator-valued Schur-Agler class in infinitely many variables, consisting of functions whose restrictions to every finite-dimensional polydisk lie in the operator-valued Schur-Agler class. We first establish an operator-valued analogue of Montel's theorem and, using it as a key ingredient, establish an Agler decomposition and a realization formula for functions in this class. The series in the Agler decomposition converges in the strong operator topology, and we show that this convergence cannot, in general, be strengthened to norm convergence. The realization formula yields a holomorphic extension of every function in the operator-valued Schur-Agler class to $\mathrm{Ball}(\ell^\infty)$, the open unit ball of $\ell^\infty$. Finally, as an application, we prove an Agler-Pick interpolation theorem in infinitely many variables.

title: Radon Transforms of Projection Functions and Aleksandrov-Fenchel Inequalities
abstract: The Radon transforms on Grassmannians define two families of geometric operators on convex bodies when applied to their projection functions. On the one hand, these are Minkowski's projection body maps and on the other hand these operators coincide on origin-symmetric bodies with the mean section body maps introduced by Goodey and Weil in 1992. Over the past two decades various sharp isoperimetric inequalities for projection bodies were shown to also hold for mean section bodies. However, an analogue of Lutwak's log-concavity inequalities for the intrinsic volumes of projection bodies remained open for mean section bodies. We establish new Aleksandrov--Fenchel inequalities for averages of certain mixed volumes and apply them to show that also all the intrinsic volumes of mean section bodies are indeed log-concave.

title: Triple Junctions in Multi-Phase Obstacle type Problems
abstract: We study the regularity of the free boundary for a multi-phase obstacle-type problem associated to quadrature domains, which arises from the minimization of the energy $$J(U,F):= \int_{B_1} (\frac 1 2 |\nabla U|^2 + F \cdot U)dx$$ among all competitors $U=(u^1,\ldots, u^N)$ with non-negative components $u^i \geq 0$ with disjoint supports, and constant forcing terms $f^i>0.$ We focus on the geometry of the free boundary at points where at least three distinct components meet (triple junctions).

title: Goodman-type lower bounds for odd cycles I: The dense regime
abstract: Goodman proved a lower bound on triangle counts which, in graphon language, states that every graphon of edge density $p$ has triangle density at least $2p^2-p$. Bennett, Dudek, Lidick\'{y}, and Pikhurko established the corresponding bound for $C_5$, determining its minimum density at every Tur\'an density $p=1-1/k$ with an integer $k\ge3$. We extend this bound to every odd cycle in the dense regime: for every odd integer $m\ge3$ and every graphon $W$ with edge density $p\ge2/3$, $t(C_m, W) \ge p^m-p(1-p)^{m-1}.$ For $2/3\le p<1$, equality holds precisely for balanced complete $k$-partite graphons with an integer $k\ge3$, up to graphon equivalence, and we establish qualitative stability at these densities. In the same density range, we also strengthen Kim and Lee's density-sensitive commonality inequality for odd cycles by adding the nonnegative term $t(P_{m-1},1-W)-(1-p)^{m-1}$ to the lower bound, where $P_{m-1}$ is the path with $m-1$ edges. To prove the main results, we develop a spectral excursion expansion and use Dirichlet averaging to reduce the resulting polynomial inequalities in arbitrarily many spectral variables to a one-variable problem. We prove the one-variable inequality through a uniform inequality comparing odd and even moments of shifted Gamma random variables. We also formalise the odd-cycle lower-bound theorem in Lean 4.

title: Higher rank elliptic sieve via CM endomorphisms
abstract: A theorem of Landau and Ramanujan states that almost all integers are not sums of two squares (when ordered by their absolute value). Equivalently, almost all integers are not norms from the Gaussian rationals $\mathbb{Q}(i)$. In this paper, we prove a version of this norm result for elliptic curves $E$. Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over a number field $K$ with complex multiplication, such that $K$ contains the endomorphism ring of $E$. For a fixed non-torsion point $P \in E(K)$ and an abelian extension $L/K$, we show that subject to a technical condition, the $y$-coordinate of almost all multiples of $P$ does not belong to the norm group of $L$. The proof is an adaptation of an argument of Bhakta et al. , whose main tools are elliptic divisibility sequences and a sieve technique known as the elliptic sieve. To account for the points in $E(K)$ arising from the additional endomorphisms, we apply the elliptic sieve to elliptic nets, a higher-rank generalisation of elliptic divisibility sequences. This approach demonstrates the possibility of applying the elliptic sieve to $\mathbb{Z}$--linear combination of points on elliptic curves and the usefulness of elliptic nets to counting problems on elliptic curves.

title: Stable manifolds of heteroclinic chains in Ho\v{r}ava-Lifshitz cosmology
abstract: We consider vacuum spatially homogeneous models in Ho\v{r}ava-Lifshitz gravity, which are expected to describe generic singularities for these modified gravity theories. These models perturb the well-known Bianchi models in general relativity (GR) by a parameter $v\in (0,1)$, in which GR occurs at $v=1/2$. We show that all periodic heteroclinic chains of Bianchi type II orbits are robust for small perturbations of GR, i.e. they exist for any $v\approx 1/2$. Moreover, we prove the existence of a stable manifold for each heteroclinic chain within a Cantor set for the supercritical case, $v\in (1/2,1)$. In particular, we discuss the heteroclinic chains of periods three and four in detail.

title: Finite-on-Top-of-Temporal CSPs in Fixed-Point Logic
abstract: We study definability in fixed-point logic with counting (FPC) for a class of constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) that simultaneously generalises finite-domain CSPs and temporal CSPs. The templates for the CSPs are first-order expansions of the structure $([k] \times {\mathbb Q};<_1,\dots,<_k,\sim)$ where $<_i \, := \{((i,x),(i,x')) \mid x<x'\}$ and $\sim \, := \{((i,x),(i,x')) \mid i \in [k], x,x' \in {\mathbb Q}\}$, i.e., $k$ copies of $({\mathbb Q};<)$. Such a CSP is definable in FPC precisely when the template pp-constructs neither the ternary temporal relation $X$, which holds on three elements if the minimum is attained exactly twice, nor a nontrivial finite affine structure. Equivalently, the template has global polymorphisms that witness the tractability of the temporal CSPs on the copies, and that provide 3-4 weak near-unanimity operations on the set of copies of ${\mathbb Q}$. In this case, we prove that the CSP is even expressible in the less expressive logic FP$^*$, which is the restriction of FPC without counting terms (i.e., the extension of first-order logic by a fixed point operator and an ordered auxiliary number sort). Our algorithm samples finitely many values in each copy and then performs nested constraint-singleton consistency tests (which is a uniform polynomial-time algorithm for finite-domain CSPs). The correctness proof uses finite-domain CSP theory to combine consistency certificates by a single polymorphism term, fixing each variable to one copy without destroying the certificates needed for the temporal algorithm. We then use a known normal form for algebraic products to control the remaining interactions between different copies.

title: On Over-Conservatism Under Low-Probability Extreme Events: A KL-Regularized Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Planning Method
abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy makes power systems more vulnerable to low-probability extreme events, elevating system planning to a critical role in ensuring reliability. Distributionally robust optimization (DRO) based on the Wasserstein distance is widely used to address this challenge. However, we find that the conventional Wasserstein ambiguity set tends to excessively amplify the probabilities of low-probability extreme events, leading to over-conservative investment decisions. To mitigate this over-conservatism, this paper proposes a novel ambiguity set that modifies the Wasserstein distance with a Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence regularization term. By leveraging the KL divergence's sensitivity to relative probability changes, the proposed set effectively curbs the unrealistic magnification of low-probability events. A two-stage distributionally robust planning model built upon this new ambiguity set is developed to optimize the installed capacity of photovoltaic, wind, and energy storage. The complex model is then reformulated as an equivalent exponential cone program with strict theoretical proofs, making it computationally tractable. Numerical results on the PJM 5-bus and IEEE 118-bus systems reveal the over-conservatism of standard Wasserstein DRO under low-probability extreme events and validate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed planning model and solution algorithm.

title: A topological sphere theorem for pinched Legendrian submanifolds
abstract: Let $M^n$ be a closed simply connected Legendrian submanifold of $\mathbb S^{2n+1}$, where $n\geq5$, and let $\mathbf{B}$ and $\mathbf{H}=\operatorname{tr}\mathbf{B}$ denote its second fundamental form and mean-curvature vector. We prove that $M$ is homeomorphic to $\mathbb S^n$ if \begin{equation*} |\mathbf{B}|^2\leq \frac{(n-1)(n+2)}n+\frac{n^2+3n-2}{2n^2}|\mathbf{H}|^2-\frac{(n-1)(n-2)}{2n^2}|\mathbf{H}|\sqrt{|\mathbf{H}|^2+4n}. \end{equation*} The equality can be attained by the Calabi products, so simple connectivity cannot be omitted. For $n\geq4$, we also prove a sphere theorem under an explicit bound and the weaker assumption $b_1(M;\mathbb R)=0$. The proof combines phase-rotated Lawson--Simons variations with a systolic inequality for finite two-complexes. We also give local constructions showing that the pinching condition allows negative isotropic curvature at a point.

title: Weighted Norm Inequalities for Maximal Multi-sublinear Rough Singular Integrals
abstract: We continue our study of multilinear rough homogeneous singular integrals by establishing weighted estimates for their maximal truncations. Let $m\ge2$ and let $\Omega\in L^q(\mathbb{S}^{mn-1})$, $1<q\le\infty$, have mean zero. For $1<p_1,\dots,p_m<\infty$ with $p_j\ge q'$ and $1/p=\sum_{j=1}^m1/p_j$, we prove $$\big\Vert \mathcal{L}_\Omega^*(f_1,\dots,f_m)\big\Vert_{L^p(v_{\vec{\boldsymbol{w}}})} \lesssim \Vert\Omega\Vert_{L^q(\mathbb{S}^{mn-1})} \prod_{j=1}^m\Vert f_j\Vert_{L^{p_j}(w_j)}$$ whenever $\vec{\boldsymbol{w}}=(w_1,\dots,w_m)\in A_{(p_1/q',\dots,p_m/q')}$, where $q'$ is the H\"older conjugate of $q$ and $v_{\vec{\boldsymbol{w}}}=\prod_{j=1}^m w_j^{p/p_j}$. The estimate holds under the same multiple weight condition as the corresponding principal value estimate.

title: Actions in varieties of non-associative algebras: a survey
abstract: This article surveys the main results on the representability of internal actions in varieties of non-associative algebras over a field. We begin by recalling the general framework of internal actions and split extensions in semi-abelian categories, before specialising to Orzech categories of interest and varieties of non-associative algebras. We discuss action representability, weak action representability, and action accessibility, with emphasis on the relationship between the latter two notions. We then describe the constructions of the universal strict general actor in Orzech categories of interest and the external weak actor in action accessible, operadic varieties of non-associative algebras over a field, as well as their role in the study of weak action representability. We also give a tensor-domain formulation of partial algebras and adapt the construction of the external weak actor to this setting. These notions are illustrated by examples arising from associative, Lie, Leibniz, Jacobi-Jordan, anti-commutative anti-associative, alternative, and $2$-nilpotent algebras. We conclude with a summary of the known results and some open questions for future research.

title: Global well-posedness for a damped two dimensional fluid--beam system
abstract: We study the normalized surface system of an irrotational incompressible fluid of infinite depth beneath an elastic Euler--Bernoulli beam with structural damping. For every fixed damping coefficient $\gamma>0$, we establish global well-posedness for arbitrary initial data in $H^2(\R)\times\bigl(\dot H^{1/2}(\R)\cap\dot H^1(\R)\bigr)$. The main novelty is that the admissible data include finite energy initial potentials for which neither $\psi_0$ nor $u_0=\psi_0+G(\eta_0)\psi_0$ has an $L^2$ representative. We also prove the exact energy dissipation identity at the regularity of the constructed solutions. The main analytical difficulties are the possible failure of $L^2$ integrability at low frequencies and the justification of energy differentiation at the solution regularity. To handle the low-frequency difficulty, we fix the low-frequency part of the initial potential and evolving an $L^2$ remainder. Homogeneous Dirichlet--Neumann estimates and a high-frequency Fourier symmetrizer yield local well-posedness with $H^{-1}$ forcing. Continuous Fr\'echet differentiability of the energy in these affine coordinates, together with a chain rule on $H^1\subset L^2\subset H^{-1}$, justifies the dissipation identity. The Energy identity and coercivity provide uniform bounds that yields global continuation tharough the local theory. Iterating the local uniqueness and stability estimates gives global uniqueness within the stated affine solution class and Lipschitz dependence on bounded sets over every finite time interval.

title: Critical oriented percolation enhanced along random supercritical horizontal lines
abstract: We consider the oriented site percolation model in a random environment introduced by Kesten, Sidoravicius and Vares (2022), in which the horizontal lines of the lattice are independently declared bad or good, sites being open with a probability that depends only on the type of their line. We study the boundary case where the bad lines are critical and the good ones supercritical, so that the model is critical oriented site percolation enhanced along a random set of good lines. We prove that percolation occurs for any positive density of the good lines. An arbitrarily sparse set of arbitrarily weakly enhanced lines suffices, the density of good lines and the strength of the enhancement being decoupled. The proof adapts the renormalization scheme of Archer, Hartarsky, Kolesnik, Olesker-Taylor, Schapira and Valesin (2026). We show that the edge of the process travels at a positive speed, which yields crossing estimates for tilted boxes; during runs of bad lines, we rely on the box-crossing property of Duminil-Copin, Tassion and Teixeira (2018); and the renormalized model dominates the oriented percolation with geometric defects of Hil\'ario, S\'a, Sanchis and Teixeira (2026).

title: Endpoint power weight inequalities for spherical maximal functions
abstract: We prove sharp $L^p(|x|^\alpha)$ estimate for spherical maximal functions. We resolve the remaining open problem for the full maximal operator for $\alpha=1-d$ and $p<2$ and prove a more general result involving a local version of Assouad dimension of the underlying dilation set. We also make a case study with endpoint bounds for a model case involving convex sequences in $[1,2]$.

title: Untrodden pathways in the study of partitions with parts separated by parity
abstract: In this paper, we study a partition function with parts separated by parity from a family of partition functions introduced by Andrews in 2019. We first show that its generating function admit representation in terms of mock modular forms of weight $3/2$. We then initiate a study of smallest-part partition function analogues of partitions with parts separated by parity, which, to the best of our knowledge, has not previously been investigated in the literature. We show that the generating functions of these smallest-part partition functions are likewise expressible in terms of mock modular forms, mock Maass theta functions and Zagier's $q$-series $H(q)$, which he describes as a ``half-derivative of the Dedekind eta-function". Our study also leads to new combinatorial interpretations of the coefficients of the aforementioned mock modular form, function $\sigma^*(q)$, and mock theta functions $\psi(q)$ and $A(q)$ in terms of odd Ferrers graphs. Moreover, we provide a quantum $q$-series identity involving Ramanujan's famous $\sigma(q)$ function. We also derive the leading asymptotic term of one of these partition functions, whose generating function we first express in terms of $\sigma^*(q)$.

title: Lifting Prym Divisors on a Bielliptic Loop of Loops
abstract: Let $C$ be a bielliptic curve over an algebraically closed nonarchimedean field of odd characteristic or characteristic zero, and let $f \colon \widetilde{C} \to C$ be an \'{e}tale double cover. We prove that, if $f$ specializes to a certain double cover of a loop of loops, then every Prym divisor on the loop of loops lifts to a Prym divisor of the same rank on $\widetilde{C}$. As consequences, we compute the dimension of the Prym-Brill-Noether variety $V^r (C,f)$, show that it is reduced and irreducible when the dimension is positive, and compute its cohomology class.

title: Attainment of the sharp stability constant of Beckner conformal log-Sobolev inequality
abstract: The existence of minimizer for stability of the fractional Sobolev inequality and the stability of Beckner conformal Log-Sobolev inequality (the endpoint case of fractional Sobolev inequality) have been established by K\"onig and Chen-Lu-Tang. The existence of minimizer for stability of the Log-Sobolev inequality is unsolved. In this paper, we solve this problem. For every $n\geq2$, we prove that the sharp $L^2$-stability constant of Beckner conformal log-Sobolev inequality on $\mathbb S^n$ is attained and is strictly less than $\frac{2\log2}{n}$. Moreover, the normalized stability constant of the fractional Sobolev inequality converges to the stability constant of the log-Sobolev inequality as $s\to0^+$. After Hersch normalization, every sequence of $L^{p_{s_k}}$-normalized minimizers for stability of the fractional Sobolev inequality, with $s_k\to0^+$, has a subsequence converging strongly in $L^2(\mathbb S^n)$ to an $L^2$-normalized minimizer of stability of the log-Sobolev inequality.

title: A Practical Combinatorial Interior Point Method for Minimum-Cost Flow
abstract: In a recent breakthrough, Chen, Kyng, Liu, Peng, Probst Gutenberg, and Sachdeva (arXiv:2203.00671) designed the first almost-linear-time algorithm for minimum-cost flow. Their approach uses an Interior Point Method (IPM) to achieve complexity $m^{1+o(1)}\log U \log C$. However, the $m^{1+o(1)}$ factor hides intricate recursive data structures, large constants and multiple log factors. In this paper, we give an implementation following the core ideas of their IPM with practical data structures and empirically obtained decision rules. We compare our solver with the cost scaling and network simplex solvers of LEMON on the instance families of the DIMACS Flow Challenge 2.0 core benchmark. Our implementation scales competitively on five of twelve families and better on two. On grid_wide we observe close to linear scaling: $m^{1.04}$ against $m^{1.48}$ for LEMON. We read these results as first evidence that the almost-linear-time framework can be relevant in practice, discuss our insights gained during the implementation process, and motivate where future work should focus to bridge the theory-practice gap.
comments: Submitted to the 13th DIMACS Implementation Challenge: Network Flows 2.0

title: Nonuniform dichotomies via time rescaling
abstract: We establish characterizations of general nonuniform dichotomies for linear nonautonomous dynamical systems in terms of nonuniform exponential dichotomies of appropriately time-rescaled systems. In discrete time, for a class of slowly growing rates, such a characterization requires an additional condition involving a suitable notion of nonuniform ordinary dichotomy, which can be omitted for invertible systems. In continuous time, we obtain a more general characterization for a large class of growth rates, without imposing this additional condition. Our approach does not rely on adapted Lyapunov norms and applies to evolution families on arbitrary Banach spaces. As applications, we show how several results concerning general nonuniform dichotomies can be derived from their counterparts for exponential dichotomies.

title: Multilevel Main Effects Matrix Factor Model
abstract: We propose a multilevel main effects matrix factor model (MMEFM) to extract meaningful row and column effects from groups of matrix data. As a generalization of a multilevel matrix factor model, we provide rigorous definitions of MMEFM and identifications, together with iterative algorithms for the estimators of all global and local components in the main effects and common component, including global/local main effects and core ranks, with rates of convergence spelt out. An important feature of the model is that all main effects can be nonstationary and still be consistently estimated at each time point. At the same time, our estimated global common factors are alignment independent, and hence are truly global, and can be presented and given interpretations more easily. We propose a Bootstrap procedure for detecting the existence and identifying the groups of data that are driven by the global common factors. The power of the test, together with the accuracy of various estimators, are demonstrated in extensive simulation settings. Estimation performance is also compared to other state-of-the-art methods for matrix time series by simulations and a set of U.S. equity data. All numerical works are done using the R package MMEFM, which is available at CRAN.

title: Prescribed and simultaneous failures of log-concavity in trees with perfect matchings
abstract: We construct trees with perfect matchings and independence sequences that fail log-concavity near the independence number $\alpha$. For every integer $k\geq1$, one family fails at $\alpha-k$ and has a witness of order $O(k^2\log(k+2))$. For every integer $t\geq2$, a single tree has simultaneous failures at $\alpha-1,\alpha-3,\ldots,\alpha-(2t-1)$, with a witness of order $O(t^3)$. All these trees satisfy $\alpha=N/2$, where $N$ is the number of vertices, and contradict Conjecture 4.2 of Ramos and Sun. A sufficient condition uses a fixed tree and the numbers of attached leaves. For fixed $k$ or $t$, explicit bounds give geometric decay of $a_j^2/(a_{j-1}a_{j+1})$ at these indices as the trees grow; $a_j$ counts independent $j$-sets. The proofs count independent sets by empty matching pairs. The Lean proof assistant checks formal proofs of the parameterized results and their quantitative bounds; exact 90- and 180-vertex examples illustrate the constructions.
comments: 21 pages, 1 figure. Lean formalization included as ancillary files. Code available at: https://github.com/HUSTFRED/Math_open_problems

title: Frequency-dependent capacitance matrix formulation for Fabry--P\'erot resonances. Part II: One-dimensional periodic media
abstract: We study Bloch resonances of one-dimensional periodic systems of high-contrast resonators beyond the subwavelength regime. An exact transfer-matrix formulation identifies the limiting wavenumbers with the union of the interior Neumann frequencies and the Dirichlet frequencies of the separating intervals. At each fixed reference wavenumber, we introduce a periodic frequency-dependent capacitance matrix whose positive eigenvalues determine all leading square-root splittings in the contrast parameter. A direct cyclic matching expansion proves the approximation, including multiple eigenvalues and small complex contrasts. A spectral exclusion result outside the limiting set yields a direct bandgap statement. At a common resonance of all intervals, we also derive uniform eigenmode approximations and distinguish the zero-frequency mode from nonzero double Bloch eigenvalues. For positive contrast, exact linear crossings are characterized by the monodromy matrix being proportional to the identity. A complete local classification is obtained for two resonators per cell and, through band folding, for fully symmetric arrays with any number of resonators per cell. We further formulate the weighted Zak phase for isolated bands and its quantization under reflection symmetry. Explicit two-resonator formulas and numerical illustrations complement the analysis.

title: Waring rank of certain complete intersection forms
abstract: The complete intersection forms are the homogeneous polynomials whose annihilator ideal or the Macaulay dual, is an Artinian complete intersection ideal. In this paper, we compute the Waring rank of certain complete intersection forms. As an application, we compute the Waring rank of binomials whose annihilator is a complete intersection ideal. Further, we also compute the Waring rank of the product of binary forms in different sets of variables.

title: On the existence of $F$-irregular graphs for disconnected graphs $F$
abstract: For a given graph $F$, a graph $G$ is $F$-irregular if all its vertices have pairwise distinct $F$-degrees, where the $F$-degree of a vertex $v$ is the number of subgraphs of $G$ containing $v$ and isomorphic to $F$. While the existence of $F$-irregular graphs has been actively studied for connected graphs $F$, the case where $F$ is disconnected remains entirely unexplored. In this paper, we provide a complete solution to this problem. We prove that for every disconnected graph $F$ with $|E(F)| \ge 2$, there exist infinitely many $F$-irregular graphs. Conversely, if $|E(F)| \le 1$, we show that no non-trivial $F$-irregular graph exists.

title: Free energy of non-convex multi-species Ising spin glasses with external fields
abstract: We identify the limit free energy of mean-field multi-species spin glasses with +/-1 spins, allowing for the presence of external fields, and without assuming any convexity property of the covariance function of the Hamiltonian. The limit is given by an "uninverted" variational formula over Brownian martingales. The proof consists in first identifying the limit free energy of configurations with a fixed magnetization. Once the magnetization is fixed, we can show the convergence of the enriched free energy to the solution of a Hamilton-Jacobi equation. The magnetization constraint is also used to show the convexity of the initial condition in this equation, and this yields a variational representation of the solution, as a Hopf formula. Convex duality then turns this formula into an optimization over martingales whose initial values are the prescribed magnetizations.
comments: 60 pages + 10-page appendix. The results of the appendix are meant to facilitate understanding but are not used in the main text

title: An explicit dimension-free isoperimetric plateau in the cube
abstract: We prove that, in every dimension, the relative Euclidean isoperimetric profile of the unit cube equals one whenever the prescribed volume differs from one half by at most $6.25\times10^{-12}$. The only minimizers in this interval are coordinate slabs. This answers Glaudo's question on the existence of a dimension-free central plateau. The proof combines a dimension-free local optimality estimate for slabs, established through BV slicing and a small-support estimate, with a quantitative Gaussian rigidity argument that forces the normal of an approximating half-space to be close to a coordinate direction.

title: Strong Invariance Principle for Random Dirichlet Series
abstract: It is shown that the random prime Dirichlet series $ X(s)=\sum_{p\in \mathcal{P}}\frac{\xi_p}{p^{s+1/2}} $ can be almost surely approximated by a Brownian motion, where $ \{\xi_p\}_{p\ge 1} $ are independent and identically distributed random variables with zero mean and finite variance, and $ \mathcal{P} $ is the set of prime numbers. As a consequence, the functional law of the iterated logarithm, limit laws of the iterated logarithm, and Chung's law of the iterated logarithm for $ X(s) $ are obtained. It is also shown that the random Dirichlet series $ Y(s)=\sum_{k=2}^{\infty} \frac{(\log k)^{\alpha}}{k^{s+1/2}} $ with $ \alpha=-1/2 $ admits the same approximation as $ X(s) $, and a direct relationship between $ X(s) $ and $ Y(s) $ with $ \alpha=-1/2 $ is established. The strong invariance principle for $ Y(s) $ with $ \alpha>-1/2 $ is also obtained.

title: Blowup of smooth solutions to 2D quasilinear wave equations with higher-order null conditions and short pulse initial data
abstract: This paper investigates the 2D quasilinear wave equation $\displaystyle\sum_{\alpha,\beta=0}^{2}g^{\alpha\beta}(\partial\phi)\partial_{\alpha\beta}^{2}\phi=0$ with the short pulse initial data $(\phi, \partial_t\phi)|_{t=1}=(\delta^{2-\varepsilon_0}\phi_0(\frac{r-1}{\delta},\omega), \delta^{1-\varepsilon_0}\phi_1(\frac{r-1}{\delta},\omega))$, where $0<\varepsilon_0<1$ is a fixed constant and $\delta>0$ is a small parameter. In our previous work [Ding Bingbing, Xin Zhouping, Yin Huicheng, Sci. China Math., Vol. 69 (2026), No. 3, 667-736], we have established the global existence of a smooth solution $\phi$ under the $k$-th order null condition ($k\ge 2$) when the $(k+1)$-th order null condition fails, provided that $0<\varepsilon_0<\varepsilon_k^*=\frac{k}{k+1}$. As a natural continuation, the present paper demonstrates that for $\varepsilon_0\ge \varepsilon_k^*$, the smooth solution $\phi$ blows up in finite time. Consequently, the threshold $\varepsilon_0=\varepsilon_k^*$ is shown to be the critical exponent that precisely characterizes the global existence and finite-time blowup for smooth short pulse solutions to the aforementioned 2D quasilinear wave equation, under the assumption that the $k$-th order null condition holds while the $(k+1)$-th order null condition does not. A key novelty of our approach lies in deriving sharp orders of $\delta$ for almost all quantities in both energy and pointwise estimates. This is achieved by utilizing the higher-order null structure in conjunction with a new good unknown recently introduced by us and the transport equation for the difference between this good unknown and its corrector.

title: A note on the proof of nonamenability of F
abstract: The goal of this note is to provide a human written exposition of OpenAI's recent proof that Thompson's group F is nonamenable.

title: Pseudolocality and strong uniqueness for complete Ricci flows
abstract: In this paper, we prove a uniform pseudolocality theorem for smooth complete Ricci flows whose initial metrics have Ricci curvature bounded below and uniformly positive injectivity radius. No a priori curvature bound is assumed on the flow. As a consequence, we obtain strong uniqueness for smooth complete Ricci flows from a complete metric with the above geometric bounds. We also prove that every smooth complete Ricci flow from a complete Ricci-flat metric with uniformly positive injectivity radius is stationary. The same conclusion holds for any complete flat initial metric. In particular, we give an affirmative answer to Chen's question on the strong uniqueness of Ricci flow from Euclidean space in every dimension.
comments: 37 pages. The main ideas of the proofs in this paper are due to ChatGPT-6 Astra. The paper is written all by the authors after they absorb the ideas from AI and interact with AI. The authors take full responsibility for the final content of this paper. All comments are welcome

title: Beyond Gaussian Entanglement: Practical Criteria for Polynomially Excited Quantum States
abstract: Polynomial excitations consisting of creation and annihilation operators are studied. Subsystem entanglement is proven produced and preserved by such manipulations. NPT entanglement already present between any two subsystems of a general pure or mixed multipartite Gaussian state is preserved under all polynomial excitations. Nevertheless, these excitations can create NPT entanglement between initially separable subsystems, implying that the number of NPT entangled pairs cannot decrease. Polynomial excitations of a wide class of initially separable pure states are considered. For these states, the method reduces the infinite-dimensional positivity problem to a finite-dimensional one: after partial transposition, NPT entanglement is equivalent to a corresponding bilinear representation matrix not being positive semi-definite. Furthermore, using symplectic diagonalization and spectral decomposition, an explicit transformation is constructed between the Fock-space and position representations. It is applied to quadratic excitations of a three-mode mixed Gaussian state. The behavior of the NPT entanglement is tracked between subsystems as a function of a parameter $\kappa$, which tunes the non-locality of the excitation, and quantum negativity is evaluated. Under a chosen quadratic Hamiltonian, the resulting unitary time evolution maintains NPT entanglement for long intervals, interrupted only by short periods of PPT states. Finally, a closed analytical expression is derived for the covariance matrix of a general quadratic operator for an arbitrary number of degrees of freedom in phase space. Our framework directly connects mathematical foundations, theoretical modeling, and experimentally feasible implementations.

title: Uniform Decay for Ruggeri's Relaxed Navier-Stokes-Fourier Equations
abstract: This work studies the linearization of Ruggeri's classical symmetric hyperbolic model of viscous, heat-conductive fluids about a homogeneous equilibrium. In three space dimensions, we show that perturbations in $L^1\cap L^2$ decay in $L^2$ at the rate $(1+t)^{-3/4}$, uniformly as a common parameter scaling the three relaxation times tends to zero. The estimate controls the equilibrium variables together with the appropriately weighted stresses and heat flux, and has the same decay rate as the formal Navier--Stokes--Fourier limit.

title: A Projection Anderson Acceleration Algorithm for Non-quasi-monotone Variational Inequalities with H\"older Continuous Terms
abstract: This paper proposes a Projection Anderson Acceleration (PAA) algorithm for variational inequality (VI) problems, where the underlying function is expressed as a finite sum of H\"older continuous functions and satisfies the $\sigma$-star strongly monotone condition that includes the star strong monotonicity with $\sigma = 1$ as a special case. In the absence of quasi-monotonicity and Lipschitz continuity, we establish the evaluation complexity of the PAA algorithm for finding an approximate solution. Specifically, for the star strongly monotone VI problems, the PAA algorithm needs at most $O (\log (\epsilon^{-1}) \epsilon^{2 (\underline{\alpha} - 1)})$ evaluations of the function and projection for finding an $\epsilon$-approximate solution, where $\underline{\alpha} \in (0, 1]$ is the smallest exponent of H{\"o}lder continuity of the component functions. We illustrate our theoretical results by numerical examples of non-quasi-monotone complementarity problems and non-monotone semilinear elliptic equations with non-Lipschitz terms.

title: A Combinatorial Proof of Partition Identities for the Number of Distinct Part Sizes
abstract: In 1984, Bressoud and Subbarao established an interesting weighted partition identity connecting the partition function and the divisor function. Recently, the first author, jointly with Bhoria, Eyyunni, and Maji, extended the work of Bressoud and Subbarao and obtained the following analogous weighted partition identity. For any $n \in \mathbb{N}$, they obtained \begin{equation*} p^{(2)}(n) = \sum_{\pi \in \mathcal{D}(n)} (-1)^{ \# (\pi) }s(\pi) \left( \ell(\pi) - s(\pi) \right). \end{equation*} In the present paper, we provide a combinatorial proof of the above identity and extend the result for $p^{(k)}(n)$, where $p^{(k)}(n)$ denotes the number of partitions of $n$ into exactly $k$ distinct part sizes.

title: Quantitative Convergence of Markov Equilibria for Time-Inconsistent Controlled Diffusions
abstract: Time-inconsistent stochastic control admits a natural game-theoretic interpretation in which successive decision dates are represented by different selves. In the Markovian framework of Bj\"ork-Khapko-Murgoci, the corresponding continuous-time equilibrium HJB system can be motivated by discrete subgame-perfect games, but the general discrete-to-continuous passage is not automatic. We establish a quantitative convergence theorem for a smooth uniformly elliptic class in which the control may enter both drift and diffusion. Using the exact sample-and-hold transition law on each time step, we construct, near a verified continuous equilibrium branch, a unique regular discrete Markov subgame-perfect equilibrium and prove first-order convergence of the continuation objects in an anisotropic $C^{2+\beta}$ topology and of the equilibrium policies in $C^0$. The key stability mechanism is structural: the discrete first-order condition forces the differential feedback correction in the frozen linearization to be nilpotent, which yields mesh-uniform block estimates through a two-norm dyadic Schauder argument despite the second-order coupling caused by controlled volatility. We also formulate a conditional transfer principle for structured polynomial-growth classes, with error-space stability stated as a separate hypothesis.

title: Proof of a nonnegativity conjecture of Prellberg--Stanton
abstract: In 1994, Friedman, Joichi and Stanton conjectured that coefficients of the power-series $q+(1-q)\prod_{i=n}^{2n-1}\frac{1}{1-q^{i}}$ are nonnegative for $n\geq3$ and $n$ being odd. Let $\qbinom nm$ denote the Gaussian polynomial. In 2003, Prellberg and Stanton conjectured that coefficients of the power-series $(1-q)\qbinom nm\prod_{i=0}^{m-1}\frac{1}{1-q^{i+m}}$ are nonnegative for $0<m<n$, except when $n$ is even and $m\in\{2,n-2\}$. The latter conjecture implies the former. In this paper, we prove a stronger result concerning coefficientwise nonnegativity of another power series, which implies the conjecture of Prellberg and Stanton. The proof uses a M\"obius correction from Gaussian polynomials, weight-preserving injections on partitions, explicit linearly independent vectors in the kernel of a derivation operator and the KOH identity.

title: Coding multiplicity in self-similar sets on the line
abstract: We study coding multiplicity for self-similar sets on the real line. When the similarity dimension exceeds one, almost every point with respect to the natural self-similar measure has infinitely many codings. We focus on the case when the similarity dimension is at most one. Our analysis proceeds through the recurrence properties and the size of the critical set, defined as the union of the pairwise intersections of the first-level pieces. Our main structural result shows that when the critical set is finite, unboundedness of coding multiplicity is equivalent to periodic recurrence to the critical set. Moreover, every commensurable system with a finite critical set has uniformly bounded coding multiplicity. This conclusion is sharp in the incommensurable setting. We construct a one-parameter family of four-map systems such that for Lebesgue almost every parameter, the critical set is a singleton and the open set condition fails, while the attractor contains a point with infinitely many codings. More generally, for transversal families, the set of parameters admitting an infinite coding fibre is dense among those for which the strong separation condition fails. We also obtain a quantitative lower bound for the Hausdorff dimension of this parameter set. Such parameters can form a meagre set. We continue the study of the geometric size of branching, obtaining dimension formulae for typical coding fibres and almost-sure upper bounds on the dimension of the critical set in transversal families. In contrast, we construct an exponentially separated system with no dimension drop whose critical set has the same Hausdorff dimension as the attractor and whose coding map has a fibre of continuum cardinality. Although we work in the one-dimensional setting, several results and arguments extend to higher dimensions.

title: Improved Upper Bounds for the Rank of the Determinant Tensor via Glynn's Formula
abstract: In this paper, we improve the upper bound for the tensor rank of the $n \times n$ determinant tensor to $\mathcal{B}_n-2^{n-1}+n+1$ by finding a new tensor decomposition of the tensor, where $\mathcal{B}_n$ denotes the $n$-th Bell number. The main idea is to replace a part of the tensor decomposition suggested by Houston--Goucher--Johnston with a tensor that is essentially the same as the $n \times n$ permanent tensor, and to use Glynn's formula. This upper bound gives an improved upper bound for the Waring rank of the $n \times n$ determinant polynomial for $n \geq 17$ as well.

title: Remarks on the monodromy conjecture for symmetric determinantal hypersurfaces
abstract: We compute the local and global Denef--Loeser topological zeta functions of the determinant on the space of symmetric matrices. It verifies the strong monodromy conjecture of the symmetric determinant function. The computation relates to the geometry of complete quadrics and wonderful embeddings.

title: Optimal Transport for Continuous-Time Mean-Variance Portfolio Selection
abstract: The continuous-time mean-variance portfolio selection problem is investigated in this paper through a rigorous integration of backward stochastic differential equation (BSDE) and Kantorovich duality theory. We propose a novel analytical framework for addressing feedback control in McKean-Vlasov stochastic systems. By solving three coupled systems of ordinary differential equations (ODEs), we derive an explicit, closed-loop optimal feedback investment strategy.

title: Ramsey properties of trees and $C$-relations via the partite construction
abstract: Finite convexly ordered binary branching $C$-relations have been viewed as a notable exception to the broad applicability of the partite construction in structural Ramsey theory. The absence of a proof of their Ramsey property by the partite construction was noted by Bodirsky in his 2015 survey and pointed out again by Hubi\v{c}ka and Kone\v{c}n\'y in their 2026 survey. We overcome this limitation by giving proofs based on the partite construction of the known Ramsey properties of the class $\mathcal{CT}$ of finite convexly ordered treeable meet semilattices and of the classes of finite convexly ordered $C$-relations with arbitrary branching and with binary branching. Our proofs do not rely on Milliken's tree theorem. The key is to expand $\mathcal{CT}$ by level predicates and a predecessor function so that the locally finite subclass method applies. We then transfer the resulting Ramsey witnesses to the corresponding reduct classes and to the classes of convexly ordered $C$-relations.

title: Doubly commuting invariant and co-invariant subspaces
abstract: Given complex separable Hilbert spaces $\mathcal{H}_i$ and bounded operators $T_i$ on $\mathcal{H}_i$, for $i=1,\ldots,n$, we consider the tensor product space $\mathfrak{H}:=\mathcal{H}_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal{H}_n$ and a tuple $(\tilde{T}_1,\ldots,\tilde{T}_n)$ on $\mathfrak{H}$ where \[\tilde{T}_i=I_{\mathcal{H}_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes I_{\mathcal{H}_{i-1}}\otimes T_i\otimes I_{\mathcal{H}_{i+1}}\otimes\cdots\otimes I_{\mathcal{H}_n}.\] A closed jointly $(\tilde{T}_1,\ldots,\tilde{T}_n)$-invariant subspace $\mathfrak{M}$ of $\mathfrak{H}$ is said to be doubly commuting if the tuple $(\tilde{T}_1|_{\mathfrak{M}},\ldots,\tilde{T}_n|_{\mathfrak{M}})$ is doubly commuting. In this paper, we show that if the hereditary polynomials in each $T_i$ are dense in $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_i)$ with respect to the weak operator topology for $i=1,\ldots,n$, then doubly commuting jointly $(\tilde{T}_1,\ldots,\tilde{T}_n)$-invariant subspaces $\mathfrak{M}$ of $\mathfrak{H}$ are characterized in the form \[\mathcal{M}_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal{M}_n,\] where $\mathcal{M}_i\subseteq\mathcal{H}_i$ is $T_i$-invariant, for each $i=1,\ldots,n$. As applications, we provide a unified framework for understanding and characterizing doubly commuting quotient modules of weighted Bergman spaces over the open unit polydisc, doubly commuting quotient modules of tensor products of complete Nevanlinna-Pick spaces, and doubly commuting invariant and co-invariant subspaces of certain operators acting on tensor products of de Branges-Rovnyak spaces $H(b)$ associated with both extreme and nonextreme points $b$. This recovers, through a different approach, the known characterizations of doubly commuting quotient modules of the Hardy space over the open unit polydisc and doubly commuting submodules of Jordan blocks of Hardy space over the open unit polydisc.

title: Full classification of $\mathbb{Z}_{p^s}$-linear generalized Hadamard codes
abstract: The $\mathbb{Z}_{p^s}$-additive codes are subgroups of $\mathbb{Z}_{p^s}^n$. A $\mathbb{Z}_{p^s}$-linear generalized Hadamard (GH) code is a GH code over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ which is the Gray map image of a $\mathbb{Z}_{p^s}$-additive code. A recursive construction gives such codes $H_p^{t_1,\dots,t_s}$, of type $(n;t_1,\dots,t_s)$ and length $p^t$, and a partial classification of them is known. In this paper, we complete the classification of these codes for every prime $p$. The main tool is the derived code, obtained by puncturing the code outside a block of coordinates determined by its kernel. For a nonlinear code $H_p^{t_1,\dots,t_s}$ with $t_1\geq2$, the derived code is a $\mathbb{Z}_{p^{s-1}}$-linear GH code of the same family, although the mechanism for odd $p$ differs from the binary one. As a consequence, for $t\geq3$, there are $\mathcal P(t+1)-\mathcal P(t)$ nonequivalent such codes of length $p^t$ if $p$ is odd, and $\mathcal P(t+1)-\mathcal P(t)-1$ if $p=2$, where $\mathcal P(n)$ is the number of partitions of $n$. In particular, this completes the classification of the $\mathbb{Z}_{2^s}$-linear Hadamard codes. We also prove a conjecture on the codes with $t_1\geq2$ and $t_s=0$.

title: Scalar curvature rigidity of small spherical caps with arbitrary fill-ins
abstract: We prove an analogue of Min-Oo's conjecture for sufficiently small spherical caps in the unit round sphere. For every dimension $n\ge3$, there exists $r_*(n)>0$ such that the following holds for every round cap of radius $0<r\le r_*(n)$: any smooth compact connected oriented Riemannian fill-in with the same intrinsic boundary metric and with scalar curvature and outward boundary mean curvature at least those of the cap is isometric to the cap.

title: A parity constraint on the topological numbers of self-complementary triply-periodic surfaces
abstract: The stability zone of Novikov's problem of planar sections of triply periodic surfaces are labeled by indivisible triples of integers, which we call the soul of the zone. Which triples may occur is not known. We show that, if a Morse function $f$ on $\mathbb T^3$ admits a translation $\tau(x)=x+v$ with $f\circ\tau=-f$, so that the sets $\{f<0\}$ and $\{f>0\}$ are congruent, then in the generic genus-$3$ situation every topological number $L$ satisfies $\langle L,2v\rangle\equiv1\pmod2$. The mechanism is that the electron/hole type of a null-homologous closed trajectory is invariant under the period lattice and is reversed by $\tau$. For $f=\cos2\pi x+\cos2\pi y+\cos2\pi z$ and the $\mu$-cube, this means that the sum of the components of each soul is odd.

title: Low-cost non-iterative Sylvester solvers for dynamical low-rank approximation of reaction-diffusion equations
abstract: In this work, we develop low-cost non-iterative Sylvester solvers for dynamical low-rank approximation of reaction-diffusion equations and incorporate them into a basis-update \& Galerkin mass-lumped finite element method (\mbox{BUG-MLFEM}). By incorporating mass lumping via Gauss-Lobatto quadrature, the spatial discretization yields a matrix differential equation equipped with diagonal positive-definite mass matrices. We establish the weighted dynamical low-rank approximation (WDLRA) within the Galerkin framework of the MLFEM system, proving the theoretical equivalence between the BUG integrator and MLFEM on low-rank subspaces, which guarantees the discrete well-posedness of the implicit BUG steps. To overcome the severe computational bottleneck of standard $O(m^3+n^3)$ Sylvester solvers, we develop tailored, low-cost non-iterative solvers that exploit the inherent sparse-by-small algebraic structure. Under Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions (BCs), the large coefficient matrices are banded, enabling efficient diagonalization of the small $r \times r$ factor matrix and reducing the per-step computational complexity to $O((m+n)r^2)$ and storage to $O((m+n)r)$. For periodic BCs, we combine this diagonalization strategy with a rank-2 Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury update to handle wrap-around corner entries at negligible additional cost. Numerical experiments demonstrate first-order temporal and $(k+1)$th-order spatial convergence of the proposed BUG-MLFEM in the discrete $L^2$ norm, where $k$ denotes the polynomial degree of the finite element space, together with significant computational speedups over existing low-rank integrators.

title: Spectral Theory of an Exactly Solvable Quantum-Optical Oscillator
abstract: We study a one-dimensional single-excitation model of a scalar photon field coupled to a continuum of two-level atoms with quadratic density. The resulting matrix Hamiltonian has an unbounded spatially varying coupling and is not semibounded. We prove that it is essentially self-adjoint and determine its spectrum explicitly. The continuous spectrum is the half-line $(-\infty,\Omega]$, where $\Omega$ is the atomic resonance frequency, while the spectrum above $\Omega$ consists of a strictly increasing sequence of simple eigenvalues. These eigenvalues are characterized by the interlaced zeros of the Airy function and its derivative and satisfy \begin{align*} \omega_n = \left(\frac{3\pi g n}{4}\right)^{1/2} + \frac{\Omega}{4} + O(n^{-1/2}). \end{align*} The analysis is based on a nonlinear spectral reduction that yields a confining massless relativistic oscillator above $\Omega$ and an inverted oscillator below $\Omega$.

title: Curvature measures and volume preserving flows in h-convex geometry
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a concept of modified curvature measures for h-convex domains in hyperbolic space and prove a shifted version of the generalized Alexandrov theorem, which characterizes geodesic balls in hyperbolic space via modified curvature measures. This result generalizes the classical work of Kohlmann (1998). We further investigate a volume-preserving shifted $\alpha$-Gauss curvature flow for strictly h-convex hypersurfaces in hyperbolic space and prove that for any $\alpha>0$ the solution exists for all time and converges smoothly to a geodesic sphere. The theory of modified curvature measures developed in the first part serves as a key ingredient in characterizing the Hausdorff limit shape of the flow.
comments: 37 pages. The paper was submitted on May 14, 2026

title: Adaptive Variance-Reduced Stochastic Sequential (Quadratic Constrained) Quadratic Programming
abstract: In this paper, we propose an adaptive variance-reduced stochastic sequential (quadratic constrained) quadratic programming (AVR-SS(QC)QP) method for nonlinear constrained optimization. The framework integrates SPIDER-based variance reduction, stochastic quasi-Newton curvature information, merit-function globalization, and adaptive switching between stochastic SQP and SQCQP models. The switching mechanism is governed by a relative constraint model curvature indicator that measures the second-order constraint information neglected by the linearized SQP model. A smoothed hysteresis rule ac?tivates the SQCQP model only when the relative constraint curvature is significant. An exact L1 merit function with Armijo backtracking globalizes the resulting directions, while a coupled stochastic Lyapunov analysis controls the interaction between gradient-estimation error and optimization progress. Under standard smoothness, sampling, regularity, and second-order conditions, we establish almost-sure consistency of the variance-reduced gradient estimator and global convergence of the KKT residual. We further show that, near regular KKT points, the curvature indicator vanishes and the method eventually selects the computationally cheaper SQP model. Numerical experiments on a sparse principal component analysis problem illustrate the practical be?havior of the proposed framework.

title: On Permutations Whose Adjacent-Sum Reciprocals Sum to One
abstract: In this paper, we give a constructive proof that for any integer n>7 (resp. n>6), the numbers 1,2,...,n can be arranged in a circle (resp. in a line) such that the sum of the reciprocals of all adjacent sums equals 1. The above conjecture was originally posed by Zhi-Wei Sun. Partitioning the integers according to n mod 12 into nine residue classes, we prove a recursive proposition and inductively construct new examples. Main lemmas and propositions in introduction are proved in Section 2. The rest of the cases are handled by explicit constructions in appendix.

title: Counterexamples to prescribed scalar curvature in the null case
abstract: We construct smooth functions on the flat torus $\mathbb{T}^{n\ge5}$ that change sign and have negative mean but cannot be realized as the scalar curvature of any metric in the given conformal class.

title: Algebraic Direct Sums and Generalized Drazin Invertibility
abstract: Let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on a complex Banach space $X$. We prove that the algebraic decomposition \[ X=\K(T)\oplus \Hq(T) \] forces both summands to be closed and hence characterizes generalized Drazin invertibility. This improves the classical characterizations of Mbekhta~\resultcite{Theorem~1.6}{MbekhtaKato}, Schmoeger~\resultcite{Theorem~4}{Schmoeger}, and Daji\'c and Koliha~\resultcite{Theorem~6.7}{DajicKoliha}, by removing their closedness assumptions. We also show that $T$ is generalized Drazin invertible if and only if \[ \dim\bigl(\K(T)\cap \Hq(T)\bigr)<\infty \quad\text{and}\quad \codim\bigl(\K(T)+\Hq(T)\bigr)<\infty. \] For ordinary Drazin invertibility, we obtain analogous finite-defect characterizations involving the hyperkernel and the hyperrange. We also give a characterization using pointwise nilpotence on an invariant summand. Finally, we consider arbitrary invariant algebraic decompositions and give a counterexample when the inverse of the restriction to one summand is not assumed bounded.

title: Stability of the Markov-Krein Transform Under Classical Convolutions
abstract: We prove that, for every $c>0$, the image of the generalized Markov-Krein transform on probability measures with finite logarithmic moment is closed under classical additive convolution and under the Mellin convolution. This resolves the positivity conjecture for the additive high-temperature convolution, a one-parameter interpolation between classical and free convolution arising in random matrix theory and representation theory in the regime $N\to\infty, N\beta_N/2\to c$. Our proof relies on a convolution theorem for universally prestarlike functions.

title: Connection between MP and DPP for Mean-Field Stochastic Optimal Control Problems
abstract: This paper deals with the optimal control problem for the general mean-field stochastic differential equations, in which the coefficients depend on both the state process as well as on its law. We focus on the connection between the general maximum principle and the dynamic programming principle for such a control problem. We establish the relationship between the value function of the mean-field optimal control problem and the adjoint equations in the maximum principle. We also give a general mean-field stochastic verification theorem. Some examples are solved explicitly to illustrate our results.

title: A Central Limit Theorem for High-Temperature SYK Model
abstract: The Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev (SYK) model is a quantum many-body model of Majorana fermions with all-to-all random interactions. It has attracted wide interest in condensed matter and high-energy physics as a solvable model of non-Fermi liquids and holography. Fix an even integer $q\geq4$, and let $Z_N(\beta)$ be the partition function of the Gaussian $q$-body SYK model. We prove that for all sufficiently small inverse temperatures $\beta > 0$, there exists $\rho=\rho(\beta)>0$ such that \[ N^{q/2 -1}(\log Z_N(\beta)-\mathbb{E}[\log Z_N(\beta)]) \Longrightarrow \mathcal{N}(0,\rho^2). \] In addition to the mathematical results, we discuss how the proofs were developed and refined through interaction between human researchers and AI, and we describe the subsequent formalization of the main arguments in Lean 4. This work thus serves as a case study of a research workflow that integrates human insight, AI-assisted exploration, iterative proof refinement, and formal verification.

title: The Singularity Has a Distribution: Exact Timing Laws and Detection Limits for a Stochastic Intelligence Explosion
abstract: Automating AI research creates a positive feedback loop between software capability and research effort. We study a stochastic realisation of this loop in which independent, positive, multiplicative improvements arrive at a rate proportional to a power of current capability. Within this model, randomness leaves the deterministic explosion threshold unchanged but replaces the blow-up date by an explicit distribution. For equal-sized improvements the explosion time is a geometrically weighted sum of independent exponentials; its $q$-series representation gives its transforms, moments and tail behaviour, including a two-term small-time asymptotic. For Lomax-distributed improvement sizes the explosion time is exactly Gamma distributed. Self-similarity implies that, with parameters known, the relative uncertainty about the remaining time does not vanish as explosion approaches. We formulate a fixed-sample test between constant and geometrically increasing idea-arrival rates. If the baseline rate and the alternative log-rate increment $\ell$ are known, the minimum sample size at error level $\alpha$ is asymptotic to $(12z_\alpha^2)^{1/3}\ell^{-2/3}$, where $z_\alpha$ is the upper-$\alpha$ standard normal quantile. Uncertainty about the growth exponent near its critical value produces a $1/t$ tail with an explicit constant, and hence an infinite conditional mean waiting time, although explosion is certain given a positive exponent. Separate extensions show that a fixed deployment delay prevents explosion in the specified delayed-feedback models, that power-law diversion of effort shifts the growth threshold, and that in a deterministic oversight race a fixed allocation share does not change the asymptotic regime, except at a critical equality of exponents. Numerical illustrations, which are not empirical forecasts, show how timing and detectability depend on the granularity of improvements.
comments: 24 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/xiaoyulics/singularity-distribution

title: The forward-loop-erased ants walk
abstract: In this paper, we study a new variant of the ants walk: a model of reinforced random walks for the phenomenon of a colony of ants being able to find the shortest path between their nest and a source of food. In this model, the nest and the source of food are two distinguished nodes in a finite graph. The ants perform successive random walks on this graph, started at the nest and stopped when they first hit the food source; the transition probabilities of each random walk depends on the trajectories of the previous ants, through some edge-weights that represent the amount pheromones deposited on each edge. In our new variant of the model, the ant (1) forgets loops made on the way to the food as soon as they are made, and (2) comes back to the nest following this loop-erased version of its forward trajectory, and deposits pheromone on the edges it crosses by doing so (i.e. adds one to these edges' weights). We say that the ants "find the shortest path" if, almost surely as the number of ants tends to infinity, the proportion of ants that travel along a graph-geodesic path from the nest to the food tends to one and the proportion of ants that travel along the remaining edges tends to zero. We are able to prove that this new variant of the model finds the shortest path when the graph distance between the nest and the source is at most 2. The strength of our result is that there is no other assumption on the shape of the graph. We prove this result using stochastic approximation theory, the electrical network method for random walks on weighted graphs, and the theory of weighted uniform spanning trees (WUSTs). In particular, the link with WUSTs is unique to the model studied in this paper due to the way the ant erases loops on the outward journey.

title: The group generated by a graph's derangements
abstract: We introduce the leap group of a graph, the subgroup of the symmetric group on the vertex set generated by graph derangements. We summarize historical results on graph derangements, which we call hops, and prove additional existence and complexity results. The leap groups of various canonical graphs are computed, and their behavior under basic graph operations is analyzed. We offer partial results on which groups can appear as leap groups, and study hops and leaps for infinite and directed graphs.

title: Lie groups are countably representable
abstract: We prove that every Lie group can be realized by permutations of a countable set, answering a classical question of Ulam. The key deformation construction originated in an argument produced by OpenAI's GPT 6 Astra during extended mathematical discussions.

title: Dynamic viscoelastic membranes
abstract: We rigorously derive a dynamic membrane theory for nonlinear viscoelastic solids with Kelvin-Voigt rheology from the corresponding three-dimensional bulk theory, in the limit of vanishing thickness. The bulk model accounts for inertia, a nonsimple elastic energy depending on the second deformation gradient, and a frame-indifferent dissipation. Orientation preservation is ensured by the energy, while self-interpenetration of the limiting membrane is prevented by a uniform averaged invertibility condition. Our analysis relies on a hyperbolic minimizing movements scheme with two time-scales, which recasts the evolution into a hierarchy of incremental, sequential, and time-delayed problems. For fixed thickness, we prove the existence of solutions to the scheme and their convergence to a weak solution of the continuous-time problem as the time-scales vanish. We then identify the membrane limit at each level of the hierarchy, proving the $\Gamma$-convergence of the incremental functionals and the convergence of solutions to the sequential and time-delayed problems. Since the constant in the Korn inequality is not uniform in the thickness, these limits rely on estimates for the time derivative of the Cauchy-Green tensor rather than for the velocity gradient. Finally, as the outer time-scale vanishes, the membrane time-delayed solutions converge to a measure-valued solution of the membrane continuous-time problem.

title: A pedestrian's approach to Bayesian methods for inverse problems
abstract: In the past two decades, the Bayesian approach to inverse problems in infinite dimensional spaces has seen significant developments in theory, Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods, and in applications. The Bayesian approach in finite dimension produces posterior distributions of finite dimensional random variables. In infinite dimensions, the desired objects are random fields and their laws as measures on Hilbert or Banach spaces. There are many textbooks and tutorials available that explain Bayesian methods and MCMC in finite dimensions. To enter the field of Bayesian inverse problems in infinite dimensions, a newcomer has to engage with a quite diverse and extensive literature. The purpose of this article is to provide a basic path to the subject that is easily accessible to a reader with general knowledge in probability and mathematical analysis. We start with a swift introduction to the finite dimensional case. The infinite dimensional case is introduced for Gaussian priors on Hilbert spaces and Gaussian-type likelihood functions. In this situation, mere continuity of the forward map suffices to prove that the posterior measure is well-defined. We also give some new and simple stability results. Two application examples are elaborated, one finite dimensional, one infinite dimensional.

title: When do lazy and invertible cellular automata generate all cellular automata?
abstract: Let $G$ be a group and let $A$ be a set with at least two elements. A lazy cellular automaton over $A^G$ acts as the identity except at the cells where a fixed pattern occurs, where it replaces the central symbol by a fixed different symbol. Let $M(G;A)$ be the submonoid of $\mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ generated by the lazy and the invertible cellular automata. We study when $M(G;A) = \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$. Since no lazy cellular automaton is surjective, every surjective element of $M(G;A)$ is invertible; hence $M(G;A) \neq \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ whenever $A$ is infinite or $G$ has an element of infinite order. Moreover, if $|A| = 2$ and $G$ has a quotient isomorphic to the Klein four-group $C_2 \times C_2$, then $M(G;A) \neq \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$. For locally finite $G$, and in particular for finite $G$, these are the only obstructions: we prove that $M(G;A) = \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ if and only if $3 \leq |A| < \infty$, or $|A| = 2$ and $G$ has no quotient isomorphic to $C_2 \times C_2$.

title: Sign-indefinite transmission conditions and near-zero eigenvalues and resonances
abstract: We consider the linear operator for metamaterial modeling $$L_{c,d }=(\chi_{\RE^{3}\backslash\overline \Omega}+c)\nabla\!\cdot (\chi_{\RE^{3}\backslash\overline \Omega}+d)\nabla\,,$$ where the material parameters $c>0$ and $d$ are constant on each connected component of the bounded domain $\Omega$, $d$ is negative on at least one component of $\Omega$ and transmission boundary conditions hold at the interfaces. It turns out that $L_{c,d }$ has, as in the sign-definite case, an absolutely continuous spectrum equal to $[0,+\infty)$; however, contrary to the latter, it has a non-empty point spectrum; in particular, we find conditions on the parameters so that zero is a threshold eigenvalue. In the case $\Omega$ is connected, we study how such a threshold eigenvalue behaves under $\varepsilon$-small analytic perturbations of the parameters. We show that, depending on the position of the number $\frac12\,\frac{1+d(\ve)}{1-d(\ve)}$ relative to the nearest eigenvalue of the Neumann-Poincar\'e operator of the interface, the zero eigenvalue splits into two branches (analytic in $\varepsilon^{1/2}$), consisting either of two branches of resonances, or of one branch of negative eigenvalues and one of resonances.

title: Irrational families of Fano weighted complete intersection fourfolds
abstract: We study the irrationality of smooth Fano complete intersection fourfolds in weighted projective spaces, using an atom theoretic approach based solely on Gromov--Witten invariants. We prove symplectic irrationality, and hence irrationality for every smooth member, in a wide range of families for which irrationality was previously known only for very general members.

title: Some applications of the quasi-Riemann hypothesis to class groups and small generators of number fields
abstract: We prove an effective version of the Chebotarev density theorem, conditional on the quasi-Riemann hypothesis for the Dedekind zeta function. Drawing on recent breakthroughs of OpenAI and Cureton--Thorner, we make unconditional the Ellenberg--Venkatesh bounds on $\ell$-torsion in class groups of number fields and extend an averaged result of Lemke Oliver--Smith to arbitrary families of degree-$d$-fields. Further applications are given to the least prime splitting and to small generators in number fields.
comments: 11 pages; comments welcome; added references and fixed minor typos

title: Endochain Conditions on Modules and $p$-quasi-Frobenius Rings
abstract: Analogous to quasi-Frobenius rings, dual rings, and Johns rings, the classes of $p$-quasi-Frobenius rings, $p$-dual rings, $p$-Johns rings are introduced and used to discuss and settle principal analogues of the Faith-Menal, Faith, and FGF conjectures. A chain symmetry theorem establishes that for quasi-injective semi-projective modules with semiprime endomorphism ring, endonoetherianity and endoartinianity are equivalent and force the endomorphism ring to be semisimple artinian. Within this unified setting, it is shown that (1) two-sided $p$-Johns rings are $p$-quasi-Frobenius, giving a principal Faith-Menal analogue, with a counterexample showing that the one-sided hypothesis is insufficient; (2) semiprimary principal right ideal rings that are right principally injective and right Kasch are $p$-quasi-Frobenius-this affirmatively answers a question of Faith (Q2) in the principal two-sided ideal ring case and settles the principal Faith conjecture, with a counterexample showing the hypotheses to be indispensable; and (3) right $p$-Johns rings that are left CF and left perfect are $p$-quasi-Frobenius, yielding a principal FGF analogue, with a counterexample demonstrating that the hypotheses are essential. Wherever needed, examples are provided to show that various classes introduced are different from the existing classes in the literature.

title: Tur\'an numbers of triangular pyramids
abstract: Let $\TP_k$ denote the triangular pyramid with $k$ layers. For a graph family $\mathcal F$, let $\ex(n,\mathcal F)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph containing no member of $\mathcal F$ as a subgraph. For a graph $H$, let $\cJ(H)$ be the family of subgraph-minimal graphs among all such graphs $H-I$, where $I\subseteq V(H)$ is an independent set.
