We prove that, for a certain choice of data, a new way integral for $SL_2^{(n)}(\mathbb{A})$ represents the partial $L$-function $L^S(ns+\tfrac12,\pi\times\tau)$. The integral is derived from the generalized doubling integral of Cai, Friedberg, Ginzburg and Kaplan, following the idea of Ginzburg and Soudry.

title: Wetting theorems in capillarity theory
abstract: We prove the uniform convergence of Plateau borders to Plateau singularities in the vanishing-volume limit of a soap film model based on capillarity theory. The results are formulated in the context a new type of local area minimizer that takes into account how a soap film locally separates its surrounding space.

title: An algebro-geometric approach to profinite iterated monodromy groups
abstract: We carefully construct the profinite iterated monodromy group of a rational map as a quotient of the \'etale fundamental group of the punctured projective line. In doing so, we prove a number of folklore results regarding profinite IMGs; in particular, their topological generation by inertia concentrated in the post-critical orbit, and their relationship with the discrete iterated monodromy group over $\mathbb{C}$.

title: A combinatorial proof of the Chan--Robbins--Yuen volume formula
abstract: The Chan--Robbins--Yuen polytope $\mathrm{CRY}_{m+1}$ has normalized volume $\prod_{j=1}^{m-1}C_j$, a product of Catalan numbers. Zeilberger proved the formula using the Morris constant-term identity; finding a combinatorial proof remained an open problem. We give such a proof by counting nonnegative integer flows. We add an extra edge from each vertex to a common sink and count flows according to how many of these edges carry positive flow. A double count proves a special case of a recurrence of Morales and Shi and gives these counts in terms of Narayana numbers. Deleting the first vertex then yields the Catalan product. We also give an explicit bijection for the recurrence and prove the corresponding reduction formula posed by Postnikov.

title: The zeros of point evaluation extremals in Paley-Wiener spaces
abstract: For $1\le p < \infty$, $\varphi_p$ is the function of minimal $L^p$ norm among all functions $f$ of exponential type at most $\pi$ for which $f(0)=1$. We start from the ansatz that the positive zeros $\tau_n$ of $\varphi_p$ are close to \(n+1/p-1/2\) and use a weighted convex correction to first place them in an \(\ell^2\)-neighborhood of this sequence. A bootstrap argument then improves this to a {Poincar\'e asymptotic} expansion of $\tau_n-(n+\frac1p-\frac12)$ in terms of odd powers of $(n+\frac1p-\frac12)^{-1}$. We also get precise information about the Fourier transform $\widehat{\varphi}_p$, a result that in particular implies that for all integers $n\ge 2$, $\widehat{\varphi}_{2n}$ is an integrable function which, when convolved with itself $2n-2$ times, is constant on the interval $[-\pi,\pi]$. In particular, we identify the extremizer in an autoconvolution problem posed by B. Green in 2001.

title: $L^p_\mu$-Normed Spaces of Bounded Multilinear Operator
abstract: We study the spaces of bounded multilinear operators $\mathcal L^i(X,Y)$ endowed with $L^p_\mu$-norms, where $X,Y$ are normed spaces and $\mu$ is a measure with $p$-moments. These are norms without taking a quotient, under suitable support conditions. The topology induced coincides with the strong operator and compact-open topologies on operator-norm-bounded subsets. Furthermore, we identify the completion of these spaces with spaces of Hilbert--Schmidt operators on the reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) for $p=2$; with iterated $\gamma$-radonifying multilinear operators on the RKHS in the Gaussian case, for general $p$.

title: Remarks on Lattice Actions Corresponding to Automorphism Groups of Smooth Cubic Fourfolds
abstract: The automorphism groups of smooth cubic fourfolds over the complex numbers, together with actions on defining equations, are classified in previous works. In this paper, we complete the calculation of group actions on the primitive integral cohomology lattice for all of the $156$ families in the classification. We distinguish similar families, determine the remaining action-maximal cases, and use restriction to complete the list. We also determine the generic algebraic lattices for each family. The calculation depends mainly on OSCAR.

title: Homological reduction of Courant algebroids
abstract: We develop a homological model for hamiltonian reduction of Courant algebroids, parallel to the BFV formulation of hamiltonian reduction in symplectic geometry. To a hamiltonian action on a Courant algebroid, we associate a differential graded Courant--Dorfman algebra, obtained from the BFV algebra of the corresponding graded symplectic manifold; under usual regularity assumptions, its cohomology recovers the Courant--Dorfman algebra of the reduced Courant algebroid.

title: A direct theory of strain-gradient special Cosserat rods via the principle of virtual work
abstract: Motivated by recent advances in the synthesis of effective one-dimensional mechanical metamaterials, we develop a direct theory of strain-gradient special Cosserat rods based on the principle of virtual work. The internal virtual work is formulated intrinsically in terms of variations of the classical Cosserat strains and their spatial derivatives, without requiring a three-dimensional parent material or a stored energy. Objectivity and insensitivity to rigid virtual displacements characterize the admissible internal-work density, while localization yields the dynamic field equations, higher-order contact interactions, natural boundary conditions, and balances of linear and angular momentum. For inextensible and unshearable rods, the constrained principle determines a unique multiplier functional, although its representation by reactive force and double-force fields possesses a gauge freedom absent from classical rod theory. We also formulate objective elastic, hyperelastic, and viscoelastic constitutive laws, extend transverse hemitropy, transverse isotropy, and flip symmetry to strain-gradient rods, and derive invariant representations of symmetric stored energies. As an application, we study a planar inextensible cantilever under a compressive terminal force. We prove that the eigenvalues of the linearized problem are simple and coincide precisely with the loads at which bifurcation from the straight state occurs. In addition, each bifurcation point generates a connected global branch of nonlinear equilibria that is locally analytic near its origin.

title: Even and Odd Integer Values of the Secondary Zeta Function
abstract: The secondary zeta function is defined by $$ Z(s)=\sum_{\gamma>0}\frac{1}{\gamma^{s}}, $$ where $\tfrac12+i\gamma$ runs over the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function with positive ordinate, and the Riemann hypothesis is assumed throughout. In this article, we derive convergent integral representations of $Z(s)$ at positive even and odd integer argument, expressed through a differential operator acting on the logarithm of the Riemann $\xi$-function. Define $$ L(x)=\log\left(\frac{\xi(x+\tfrac12)}{\xi(\tfrac12)}\right), \qquad \mathcal{E}=x\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}, \qquad \mathcal{D}_k=\mathcal{E}\prod_{j=1}^{k}(\mathcal{E}-2j). $$ Then, for $k\geq1$, $$ Z(2k)=\frac{(-1)^k}{2^k(k-1)!}\int_{0}^{\infty}\frac{\mathcal{D}_k L(x)}{x^{2k+1}}\,\mathrm{d}x $$ and $$ Z(2k+1)=\frac{(-1)^k}{\pi\,(2k-1)!!}\int_{0}^{\infty}\frac{\mathcal{D}_k L(x)}{x^{2k+2}}\,\mathrm{d}x. $$ In the last part, we write these formulas out explicitly for $Z(k)$, $2\leq k\leq 7$, both in terms of $L(x)$ and in terms of $\xi(x+\tfrac12)$ for reference. We also derive a limit formula for $\gamma_1$, the ordinate of the first nontrivial zero, and demonstrate its convergence numerically.

title: Aggregated Column Generation for Two-Stage Stochastic Mixed-Integer Programs
abstract: Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation applied to two-stage stochastic mixed-integer programs (SMIP) has been shown empirically to yield a formulation with strong bounds that can be solved via column generation. However, the time to solve the restricted master problem grows significantly with the number of scenarios due to the increasing number of nonanticipativity constraints (NACs). Moreover, the associated high-dimensional dual space can cause the dual multipliers to oscillate between iterations, further slowing convergence. We propose an aggregated column generation framework for solving a Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation. Applied to SMIP, this method partitions the NACs into groups and replaces each group with a weighted surrogate constraint, leading to a reduced size and providing implicit stabilization by restricting the dual space. While aggregation leads to a relaxation, we develop two strategies for recovering the standard Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation bound. The first iteratively refines the partition by splitting groups that contain violated constraints. The second keeps the partition fixed and adaptively updates the aggregation weights. We prove convergence of the two approaches and study their computational performance on two benchmark problem classes.

title: Symmetries, Lax pair, and nilpotent Darboux transformation for the KdV-ghost system
abstract: We analyze the KdV--ghost system arising from the BRST formulation of BF-type topological field theory, its symmetries, Lax pair, spectral problem, zero-curvature formulation and Darboux formalism. The system is invariant under shifts of the ghost field, whose generator does not commute with the BRST symmetry of the KdV--ghost system. Their generators allow the introduction of a systematic procedure for generating new solutions from a given one, and the corresponding expressions in the Grassmann algebra are obtained explicitly. We introduce a Grassmann-valued Lax pair and prove an isospectral theorem relating the spectral problem of the spatial Lax operator for the KdV equation to that of its KdV--ghost extension. We also construct a triangular zero-curvature representation and show that the Grassmann-valued spatial Lax operator is related to the KdV spatial Lax operator by a nilpotent conjugation. The natural variable for a local Darboux formulation is the differentiated ghost $v=C_x$, for which the ghost equation coincides with the Fr\'echet linearization of the KdV flow. We then construct a nilpotent lift of the scalar KdV B\"acklund--Darboux transformation. Using Riccati variables and off-shell factorization identities for the KdV residue and its Fr\'echet derivative, we prove that the transformation closes on the local KdV--ghost system. Successive Darboux transformations yield a recursive ghost extension of the bosonic Darboux chain, with a new odd homogeneous contribution introduced at each step. For the solitonic examples, the resulting local ghost fields are naturally identified with tangent directions associated with the soliton phase parameters. The construction provides a Darboux-theoretic interpretation of the ghost sector while remaining distinct from the standard supersymmetric KdV hierarchies.

title: A Bounded-Defect Construction for the Mondrian Art Problem
abstract: We construct an infinite family of solutions to the Mondrian art problem with absolute defect bounded above by $280$, of side lengths $n_0 = 315$, $n_1 = 106785$, and $n_{j+2} = 340n_{j+1} - n_j$, where $n_j$ is congruent to $315 \pmod{630}$. This absolute bound shows that the minimum defect does not necessarily increase with $n$, providing a counterexample to a conjecture which has been open since the problem's original proposal. Our design is derived from a well-known seven-rectangle dissection over the real quadratic field $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{19})$, with non-integer side lengths; we tailor the side lengths to be integers via an infinite Pell family. Using the same method, we devise a second family with defect $560$ that contains infinitely many side lengths which are divisible by any given positive integer, implying that for any $k$ there are infinitely many side lengths $n \equiv 0 \pmod{k}$ with defect bounded above by $560$. This constant bound offers a dramatic improvement on the previous quadratic bounds.

title: Enumeration of one-cycle signed chord diagrams and their duals for optimal Morse flows on closed surfaces
abstract: Optimal Morse vector fields on closed surfaces, i.e.\ fields with the minimal possible number of critical points (a single source and a single sink), are classified up to topological trajectory equivalence by one-cycle signed chord diagrams in Kybalko, Prishlyak and Shchurko (2018). We recall this construction and the associated duality, which corresponds to reversing the direction of the flow, in a unified encoding in which both endpoints of a chord carry the same label, and we make it algorithmic. We give an explicit traversal procedure that detects one-cycle diagrams, a canonical form of an equivalence class under cyclic shifts, reversal and relabeling of chords, and a construction of the dual diagram. On this basis we describe an algorithm that enumerates all one-cycle signed chord diagrams with a given number of chords, both for orientable and for non-orientable surfaces, groups them into equivalence classes, pairs each class with its dual, and identifies the self-dual ones. The algorithm is implemented in Python and archived in Zenodo; its output is validated against the Harer--Zagier numbers in the orientable case and against orbit-size counts in both cases. We also note that, when a one-cycle diagram is read as a cellular embedding of a one-vertex graph, its dual diagram describes the embedding of the dual graph.

title: On optimal Wannier decay in dimension three
abstract: For a Chern nontrivial Bloch bundle over the three torus, we construct an orthonormal Wannier basis with the optimal pointwise decay $\mathcal{O}(|x|^{-5/2})$. All but one of the generators decay exponentially. This resolves the question left open in arXiv:2505.01999.

title: Analytic Properties of Self-Reproducing Families under Contour Convolution
abstract: This note grew out of two questions arising in different settings. The first concerns recognizing holomorphic functions among continuous functions on an annulus. The second concerns what self-reproducing subsets can tell us about semigroups of functions arising in analysis. Our analytic starting point is a variation on the classical relation between holomorphy and invariance of contour integrals. It identifies the holomorphic functions as the largest class containing the constant function 1 for which a contour convolution is independent of the chosen curve for every pair of functions. On this class, convolution amounts to multiplying Laurent coefficients. We then study families $B$ satisfying $B\diamond B=B$. We show that expressing a function as a convolution product of $m$ holomorphic functions corresponds precisely to its extension to a wider annulus determined by $m$. This identifies the largest self-reproducing family as the functions extending holomorphically to the punctured plane. We also prove that uniform boundedness on a fixed subannulus surrounding the unit circle forces all members of such a family to have Laurent expansions supported on one common finite set. A general semigroup theorem describes the minimal self-reproducing families.

title: The Euler Characteristic of Spherical Bestvina-Brady Kernels
abstract: We compute the Euler characteristic of Bestvina-Brady kernels $\operatorname{BB}(\Gamma)$ for all Artin groups of spherical type. Our method involves discrete Morse theory to describe the cellular structure of a classifying space for the Bestvina--Brady kernel, through the action of $\operatorname{BB}(\Gamma)$ on non-integer level sets of the universal cover of the Salvetti complex. We extend the method of computation of $\chi(\operatorname{BB}(\Gamma))$ to Artin groups that satisfy the $K(\pi,1)$-conjecture and whose nerves are rationally acyclic, and we provide an example by realising the projective plane as the nerve of a Coxeter group.

title: Invariant factors from products of cyclotomic polynomials, with applications
abstract: Let $f,g\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ be products of cyclotomic polynomials such that either $g/\gcd(f,g)$ or $f/\gcd(f,g)$ (or both) is squarefree. We give explicit formulae for the invariant factors of $f(C_g)$, where $C_g$ is the companion matrix of $g$, expressing them in terms of the indices and multiplicities of the cyclotomic factors of $f$ and $g$. A more compact formula holds for the circulant case $g(t)=t^n-1$, assuming that every cyclotomic factor shared by $f$ and $g$ has multiplicity $1$ in $f$. We discuss applications to several topics, including abelianizations of cyclically presented groups, homology groups of cyclic branched covers of knots, adjacency matrices and shifted graph Laplacians, $K$-theory, and Smith forms of matrix powers. For example, for two families of hyperbolic knots we give the first integral homology in every covering degree; or, when $g$ is squarefree, we determine the least eventual period of the Smith forms of powers of $f(C_g)$.

title: Finite-sample certification of coverage regret for budgeted document selection under adaptive stratified auditing
abstract: Selecting a budget-constrained set of documentary fragments, for instance the knowledge base of a retrieval-augmented generation system, raises a statistical question: how much expected query coverage is lost relative to the best feasible selection when the query distribution is unknown? We construct finite-sample, distribution-free upper confidence bounds for this coverage regret that remain valid after data-dependent selection. A pilot stage may select the document set, screen competitors, build comparison networks and learn an annotation policy. Then an independent audit acquires relevance labels with probabilities that are constant within observable strata. The main result is a simultaneous bound for all retained coverage contrasts. The bound is made observable by empirical-Bernstein variance calibration or by a one-stage construction without calibration, and it accounts for estimated stratum proportions. For maximum-type coverage we prove variance contractions for swaps of redundant fragments, give a condition under which multiscale radii improve on a direct union bound, and show that such redundancy cannot be certified from samples alone. A simulation study confirms validity and quantifies the gains from variance calibration and certified redundancy.

title: Pointwise minimax lower bounds under a multi-index constraint: the price of an unknown orientation
abstract: We consider nonparametric regression with random design and non-Gaussian noise, where the regression function has the multi-index form $F(x)=f(\Theta x)$ with an unknown link $f:\RR^m\to\RR$ in an anisotropic H\"older class and an unknown matrix $\Theta$ with $m\le d$ orthonormal rows. For estimation of $F$ at a fixed point we prove that the minimax risk is bounded from below by a multiple of $L^{1/(2\gamma+1)}(n^{-1}\ln n)^{\gamma/(2\gamma+1)}$, where $\gamma$ is the harmonic mean of the smoothness indices of the link divided by $m$. For $m<d$ this extends a Gaussian white noise result to regression. The main new case is $m=d$, where no dimension reduction takes place: the logarithmic factor still appears as soon as the link is anisotropic and the orientation of its axes is unknown. In contrast, when the link is isotropic with smoothness index at most one, the class is rotation invariant up to a constant and the classical rate without logarithm is attained. The logarithmic loss is therefore caused by the unknown orientation of the directions in which the function is least smooth

title: Orthogonal partition by four hyperplanes
abstract: We study orthogonal $(4,3)$-equipartitions of finite measures absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure: every three of four mutually orthogonal affine hyperplanes must divide each measure into eight equal parts. For every number $m$ of measures, we determine the exact dimension threshold of Musin's polynomial criterion and express it in terms of the binary expansion of $m$. The threshold coincides with the geometric lower bound precisely when $m=2^j-1$. Consequently, $\Delta^*(2^j-1,4,3)=7\cdot2^{j-1}-2$ for every $j\geq1$.

title: The grounded spirituality of mathematics
abstract: We propose that mathematics is done largely as a means of both coping with and celebrating our physicality in the natural world. Inspired by David Abram's "Becoming Animal", we suggest that -- in opposition to the popular image of an otherworldy Platonic realm-- the spiritual component of doing mathematics is grounded on and in the Earth. We explore this as a means of questioning the widespread adoption of AI in the workflows of research mathematics.

title: On the Mathematical Structure of Helical Shear in Anelastic Continua
abstract: We study helical shear of a thick-walled tube made of an incompressible, isotropic hyper-anelastic solid carrying a radially symmetric distribution of axial screw dislocations. Through the Bilby--Kr\"oner--Lee decomposition, the dislocations are encoded in a Weitzenb\"ock material manifold, whose Riemannian metric alone enters the elastic response. Equilibrium reduces at each radius to an algebraic system for the azimuthal and axial shear strains, whose cross terms are proportional to the dislocation strength and to the dependence of the strain energy on the second invariant; the two shear modes therefore couple only in the presence of dislocations. Exact solutions are obtained for neo-Hookean, Fung--Demiray, Gent, Knowles, and Mooney--Rivlin materials, and numerical ones for Gent--Gent materials. The universal relations of Horgan and Saccomandi are extended to dislocated generalized neo-Hookean tubes. Dislocations stiffen the tube when the strain energy stiffens with the first invariant, couple the two shear modes chirally when it depends on the second, and may restrict admissibility: they cap the dislocation strength in Gent and Gent--Gent materials, and contract the admissible traction region in Knowles materials with power-law index below n = 1/2. A weakly nonlinear analysis to third order in the applied tractions and dislocation strength shows that, at first order (linear elasticity), the dislocations leave the shear response unaffected while carrying a residual stress. The chiral coupling enters at second order, through the dependence of the strain energy on the second invariant, so that every dislocated material couples the modes as the Mooney--Rivlin solid with the same second- and third-order moduli. At third order, no new coupling arises; the modes interact through stiffness corrections involving the fourth-order modulus, which the dislocations further correct mode by mode.

title: On generalized embeddability of a non-elliptic self-map
abstract: We study the structure of the centralizer of a non-elliptic holomorphic self-map of the unit disc and its relation with continuous dynamical structures. We prove that if the identity is not isolated in the centralizer of a non-elliptic self-map $\varphi \in \mathrm{Hol}(\mathbb D)$, then $\varphi$ is univalent and its centralizer contains a non-trivial continuous one-parameter semigroup of holomorphic self-maps. This result provides a general criterion for the existence of continuous dynamics arising from discrete iteration. Our approach is based on the theory of holomorphic models and on simultaneous linearization techniques for commuting self-maps. In particular, we exploit recent developments on simultaneous linearization for parabolic self-maps with positive hyperbolic step. As a consequence, we obtain new sufficient conditions for the embeddability of holomorphic self-maps into continuous semigroups.

title: Moment-optimal Gamma approximation of Bessel Process exit times
abstract: We construct finite Gamma convolutions approximating the first hitting time of $1$ by a Bessel process of index $\nu>-1$ started at the origin. The scale measure in the classical exponential representation of this law is obtained by squaring the positive half of a dilated modified Lommel polynomial orthogonality measure. Its Jacobi recurrence yields an $N$-factor Gamma convolution that uniquely matches the first $2N$ cumulants, the maximal number attainable in this class. From an exact Gaussian quadrature remainder we derive supergeometric convergence of the Laplace transforms on compact subsets of a common slit plane and geometric convergence of the distribution functions uniformly on the real line. The approximants have total Gamma shape $N(N+\nu+1)$, and their Laplace transforms and negative moments decrease to those of the exit law.

title: An oral history of FPSAC
abstract: As its 40th anniversary nears, we present a history of the International Conference on Formal Power Series and Algebraic Combinatorics (FPSAC), through interviews with figures from its past, present, and future.

title: With Leverage, the Gambler is Not the One Who Gets Ruined
abstract: In this note we explore the following simple question: How does the classic \emph{gambler's ruin} phenomenon change if we allow the gambler \emph{financial leverage}? We show that, with a moderate amount of leverage, it is possible for an (idealized) gambler to sustain seemingly improbable profits over a remarkably long time horizon without ever going bankrupt, \emph{even} if the gambler makes only fair bets. With a leverage ratio of $L = 10$ (less than what Lehman Brothers Holdings had from 1995--2008), the probability of multiplying one's money by $1000\times$ without going bankrupt is roughly $50\%$. More generally, given $L$-fold leverage, and given the goal of multiplying one's money by a factor of $r > 1$, the optimal gambling strategy has probability roughly $r^{-1/L}$ of success. The results in this note are designed as part of the course development for the CMU randomized algorithms course.

title: Existence of exhaustions with controlled sign of mean curvature in noncompact manifolds
abstract: Given a complete and non-compact Riemannian manifold of dimension $3\le n\le 7$, we find conditions for the existence of compact exhaustions $\{U_i\}_{i=1}^\infty$ such that all boundaries $\partial U_i$ have the same sign of mean curvature. In particular, we show that in these dimensions, a manifold with one end satisfying a no tentacle condition always has a weakly mean convex, weakly mean concave, or minimal exhaustion, according to the behaviour of the area profile of separating hypersurfaces. This is a version of a result sketched by Gromov, under a condition which is weaker than his thickness at infinity. In more general situations, we study the existence of exhaustions which are weakly mean concave or weakly mean convex apart from an arbitrarily small $L^1$ error. That is, we find sufficient conditions for the existence of exhaustions $\{U_i\}_{i=1}^\infty$ which satisfy $\int_{\partial U_i}H^+\to0$, $\int_{\partial U_i}H^-\to0$, or $\int_{\partial U_i}|H|\to0$, where $H^-$, $H^+$, and $|H|$ are the negative part, positive part, and the absolute value of the mean curvature respectively. As an application of our methods, we study the existence of almost $c$-convex exhaustions, that is, exhaustions whose boundaries satisfy $\int_{\partial U_i}(H-c)^-\to0$ for some $c>0$.

title: Eremenko's conjecture on higher-order Briot--Bouquet equations
abstract: The Briot--Bouquet theorem describes the meromorphic solutions of autonomous first-order algebraic differential equations. We prove Eremenko's conjecture extending it to all orders: if $f$ is meromorphic in $\mathbb{C}$ and $P(f,f^{(n)})=0$ for a nonzero polynomial $P$, then $f$ is rational, elliptic, a rational function of $e^{cz}$ with $c\neq 0$, or satisfies $f^{(n)}=af+b$. In particular, every meromorphic solution with $P$ irreducible of degree at least two belongs to the Weierstrass class. Solutions with poles were classified by Eremenko, Liao and Ng. We settle the remaining entire case with a rigidity theorem for polynomial compositions: if $h$ is nonconstant entire and $D^nR(h)=S(h)$, where $D=d/dz$ and $\deg R=\deg S\ge 2$, then $h(z)=Ae^{bz}+Be^{-bz}+C$. No growth assumption is needed. The proof turns the cancellation of leading terms into a contraction of indicator diagrams and obtains incompatible zero counts near an exposed edge. As an arithmetic application, an algebraic Laurent expansion at one algebraic point and an algebraic value at another force a solution to lie in $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}(z)$. Hence any two distinct derivatives of a function in Mahler's class (transcendental meromorphic functions with algebraic Laurent coefficients at every algebraic point) are algebraically independent over $\mathbb{C}$.

title: Graph binomial coefficients and a positivity conjecture of Guo and Krattenthaler
abstract: We investigate Conjecture 7.4 of Guo and Krattenthaler \cite{GK}, which predicts that for every positive integer $n$, the polynomial \[ P_n(q) = \frac{(1-q)^2}{(1-q^{10n-1})(1-q^{15n-1})}\qbin{30n}{5n} \] has non-negative coefficients, except for $q^1$ and $q^{125n^2-25n+3}$, which equal $-1$. We study this problem through three main perspectives: First, by linking the boundary coefficients to the second differences of the partition function, we settle the first and last $25n+1$ coefficients via a novel partition injection. Second, by introducing a ``defect'' generalization of Andrews' classical lemma, we reduce the conjecture to an almost-unimodality property and employ a uniform saddle-point analysis to prove it analytically for all large $n \ge 2\cdot 10^{29}$. Finally, we connect these quotients to graph binomial coefficients, providing a natural orbit-counting interpretation via Burnside's lemma on directed cycles and paths.

title: Full-Order Safety for Nonlinear Reduced-Order MPC
abstract: Reduced-order models (ROMs) make model predictive control (MPC) of high-dimensional nonlinear systems tractable, but the resulting modeling error can lead to constraint violations on the real system. We introduce CoRE-MPC, a robust MPC formulation that plans with a nonlinear ROM and guarantees recursive feasibility and constraint satisfaction for the full-order system. It can be applied with a broad class of nonlinear model reduction techniques and the resulting MPC does not require evaluating the full-order model online, thus ensuring computational efficiency. The key insight is in how the ROM affects the dynamics of the prediction error. We account for this with two error radii that are propagated alongside the ROM and provide a guaranteed bound on the prediction error. The approach is validated in simulation on an 80-state oscillator chain, a Burgers equation, and a 9,768-state finite-element soft robot, where a two-state ROM with data-driven bounds keeps all 1,628 nodes clear of a wall at a median solve time below 1 ms for a 20 ms control period. Across these examples, CoRE-MPC is 13 to 61 times faster than full-order robust MPC at only 27 to 35% higher closed-loop cost, whereas existing certified schemes are either infeasible or at least twice as conservative. Code: [released upon publication].

title: An analog of Quillen-Venkov for eventually negligible classes and radicality for finite irreducible Coxeter groups
abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group, $M$ a $G$-module, and $F$ a field. A continuous group homomorphism $i : \Gamma_L=\text{Gal}(L_{\text{sep}}/L) \rightarrow G$ yields a homomorphism $i^* : H^d(G,M) \rightarrow H^d(L,M)$ for every $d\in \mathbb{N}$. An element $u \in H^d(G,M)$ is negligible over $F$ if $u\in\ker(i^*)$ for every $i$ and every field extension $L/F$. If $M=\mathbb{F}_p$ for a prime $p$ with a trivial $G$-action, an element $u$ is eventually negligible over $F$ if $u^k$ is negligible over $F$ for some $k\geq1$. The (eventually) negligible elements over $F$ form an ideal of the cohomology ring $H^*(G,\mathbb{F}_p)$, called the (eventually) negligible ideal. We prove an analog of Quillen-Venkov for eventually negligible elements. An element $u\in H^*(G,\mathbb{F}_p)$ is eventually negligible over $F$ if and only if the restriction of $u$ to the cohomology of each elementary abelian $p$-subgroup of $G$ is eventually negligible over $F$. Paired with applications of a Gysin-type long exact sequence, we identify generators of the negligible ideal over $\mathbb{Q}$ of the mod-2 cohomology of dihedral groups, cyclic $2$-groups, and generalized quaternion groups. We prove that the negligible ideal over $\mathbb{Q}$ of the mod-2 cohomology of every finite irreducible Coxeter group is radical. The result was previously known for Weyl groups; we prove it for the remaining non-Weyl types $I_2(m)$, $H_3$, and $H_4$.

title: Natural Geometry Based on the Rectilinear Plane
abstract: The aim of this note is to introduce natural geometry, in which the rectilinear plane is a primitive. This plane is admitted together with its rectitude, and its rectitude states that a Lambert quadrilateral has its fourth angle right. The fourth angle of a Lambert quadrilateral may be right, acute or obtuse, and this trichotomy distinguishes three planes. Starting from the rectitude, we prove the uniqueness of the parallel by a chain of neutral steps: the rectangle, the triangle whose angles sum to $\pi$, and Legendre's theorem \cite{legendre}, all borrowed from the classical literature. That uniqueness is equivalent to the fifth postulate, which we thus reach in Euclid's own wording: the equivalence is read in the natural direction, and it is not a derivation of the fifth postulate from the other four, since the independence of that postulate is not in question. In the rectilinear plane the parallels are characterised as exactly the images of a line under a point-reflection, and equivalently as the pairs of equidistant lines. The other two planes are then placed beside the rectilinear one, and the same definitions serve for all three.
comments: 7 pages, no figures. A foundational note on the fifth postulate, in contrast with Hilbert's neutral primitives. Keywords: parallel postulate, rectilinear plane, Hilbert's foundations, non-Euclidean geometry. Comments welcome

title: Conformal dimension and self-similar groups
abstract: We study the Ahlfors-regular conformal dimension of spaces with locally expanding self-covering maps and, more generally, limit spaces of contracting self-similar groups. We show that the conformal dimension is characterized by combinatorial moduli associated with the Schreier graphs of these groups. We compare these moduli with contraction coefficients of self-similar group actions and with algebras of functions on the limit spaces satisfying asymptotic $p$-energy conditions. We also give conditions on the group when the conformal dimension is equal to the infimum of visual metrics on the self-similarity complex.

title: Beyond the lemon: Spectra of random Lindblad operators with a Hamiltonian component
abstract: Generators of continuous-time quantum Markovian evolution, known as Lindblad operators, play a key role in the theory of open quantum systems. The question of how to define and characterize random Lindblad operators has attracted considerable attention in recent years. Purely dissipative random Lindbladians have been extensively studied using toolboxes of free probability and non-Hermitian random matrix theories, which helped, among other results, to uncover a characteristic lemon-like spectral support. In this work, we focus on random Lindbladians with a Hamiltonian component. We analyze three ensembles of increasing complexity, designed to illustrate the joint effects of dissipative and Hamiltonian dynamics. While the first two ensembles allow for an exact analytic treatment with standard probabilistic and free-probability methods, the generic case of independently random Hamiltonian and dissipative components requires a novel framework that combines operator-valued free probability with sequential noise averaging. For this ensemble, our approach preserves the underlying tensor-product structure of the Lindblad operator and derives a general equation for the spectral boundary. We characterize the effect of Hamiltonian-induced spectral squeezing and explain how the spectral support changes with the relative Hamiltonian strength and the rank of the dissipative component.

title: Exotic $\mathbb{R}^4$'s as unions of two thickened circles
abstract: We give an infinite family of non-diffeomorphic exotic $\mathbb{R}^4$'s, each of which is the union of two copies of a standard open tubular neighborhood of the circle, which intersect in a standard open tubular neighborhood of the wedge of two circles. This gives the simplest known decomposition of an exotic $\mathbb{R}^4$ into two open sets, making progress on Question 4.43 (A) of Kirby's 1995 problem list. The decompositions are obtained by studying fibered slice disk complements in certain Casson-Gordon homotopy 4-balls, for which we provide similar decompositions. We distinguish the $\mathbb{R}^4$'s using end Floer homology.
comments: 10 pages, 7 figures, No AI. Comments welcome!

title: Long-Time Behavior of the $\alpha$-Ricci Flow on the 2-Torus
abstract: We study the $\alpha$-Ricci flow $(g(t),\alpha(t))$, which is a Ricci flow coupled with a harmonic 1-form heat flow, on the 2-torus $M$. We prove global existence for this flow as well as a Type III curvature estimate. The long-time behavior of the $\alpha$-Ricci flow depends on the cohomology class $[\alpha] \in H^1(M,\mathbb{R})$, which is invariant under the flow. If $[\alpha]$ is rational, then as $t\to\infty$, $(M,t^{-1}g(t))$ Gromov--Hausdorff converges to $S^1$ with length $\ell([\alpha])/\sqrt 2$ where $\ell([\alpha])$ is the primitive length of $[\alpha]$. On the universal cover, the rescaled flow $(s^{-1}\tilde g(st),\tilde\alpha(st))$ smoothly converges to an expander $(g^*(t),\alpha^*(t))$ on $\mathbb{R}^2$ as $s\to \infty$ where $\alpha^*(t)$ is nonzero and constant in spacetime and $g^*(t)$ is flat and expanding in the $\alpha^*$ direction. If $[\alpha]$ is irrational, then there is a sequence $s_i\to\infty$ such that $(M,s_i^{-1}g(s_it))$ Gromov--Hausdorff converges to a point. Moreover, on the universal cover, $(s_i^{-1}\tilde g(s_it),\tilde\alpha(s_it))$ smoothly converges to $(g^*(t),\alpha^*(t))$.

title: What David Teaches Goliath: An Inevitable Extension of ZFC
abstract: We examine the metamathematical significance of the Levy scheme $\Lambda$, which asserts, for each natural number $n$, the existence of an $n$-Mahlo cardinal $\kappa$ such that $V_\kappa\prec_{\Sigma_n}V$. Several initially unrelated constructions single out $\mathsf{ZFC}+\Lambda$: comparisons with the model theory of arithmetic and finite set theory; class theories in which the class of ordinals has the tree property; set theories with a proper class of indiscernibles; and interpretations of ordinary set theory in Cantorian parts of models of the extension $\mathsf{NFUA}$ of Quine--Jensen set theory $\mathsf{NFU}$. Taken together, these results provide a precise sense in which $\mathsf{ZFC}+\Lambda$ is an inevitable extension of $\mathsf{ZFC}$ if one attempts to generalize certain metamathematical results about the universe of all finite sets to the entire universe of sets.

title: Heat Kernel Estimates for Random Walks with Killing on Transient Graphs
abstract: We give matching two-sided estimates for heat kernels obtained from Schr\"odinger operators $\Delta+W$ on weighted graphs. The graphs we consider are transient and admit two-sided sub-Gaussian heat kernel estimates for the Laplacian $\Delta$, and the potentials $W$ decay to zero at infinity. We offer two proofs for one of our main results: one using the Feynman-Kac formula, and one without using it. Our results apply to fractal-type graphs such as graphical Sierpinski carpets, among other examples.

title: Density of Products of Solutions and the Linearized Calder\'on Problem in an Analytic Background
abstract: We study the linearization, with respect to zeroth-order perturbations, of the local Dirichlet-to-Neumann map of a formally self-adjoint elliptic operator $P=-\Delta_g+Q$ on a compact Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ of dimension $n\geq 2$ with boundary, where $Q$ is of order at most one. Near a boundary point where the boundary, metric, and $P$ are analytic, we show that the linearized map is a classical analytic pseudodifferential operator of order $-1$ if and only if the zeroth-order perturbation $q$ extends analytically across the boundary. We also prove that local boundary data in an arbitrary open analytic boundary patch determines $q$ locally. In particular, if the measurement set meets every connected component of $M$, the local linearized DN map is injective on $L^\infty$ perturbations. Finally, we obtain a global completeness result for products of pairs of solutions whose boundary traces are supported in the measurement set. The global recovery proceeds by local steps using Runge approximation.

title: Reductions of Galois representations of slope $2$
abstract: Let $p$ be a prime $\ge 5$. We determine the semisimplifications of the mod $p$ reductions of irreducible two-dimensional crystalline representations of the Galois group of ${\mathbb Q}_p$ of slope $2$ and weights $k\ge3p+4$ with $k \not \equiv 6 \bmod (p-1)$. The proof relies on the compatibility between the $p$-adic and the mod $p$ Local Langlands Correspondences for $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$.

title: Variationally correct loss functions for nonlinear parametric problems and their neural approximations
abstract: We construct computable a posteriori error estimators for parametric families of nonlinear elliptic problems by measuring the residual of a variational formulation in the dual norm of a closed subspace of the test space. A single abstract theorem shows that the resulting estimator is bounded above and below by the error in the trial norm, i.e., it is a variationally correct loss function. Two instances are covered. The first considers an $L_2$-like test space, yielding a nonlinear first-order system least-squares loss function that certifies arbitrary, possibly meshless, approximations. The second breaks the test space, yielding a nonlinear discontinuous Petrov-Galerkin loss function computed by element-local problems. All assumptions are verified for quasilinear diffusion, including monotone fluxes and semilinear problems, and a nonlocal Kirchhoff model. Numerical studies train neural networks approximating the parameter-to-solution maps with the latter loss and measure the ratio of loss to squared error.

title: The Capacity of the Noisy Torn Paper Channel and the Noisy Shuffling Channel
abstract: The torn paper channel breaks a codeword into fragments and returns all fragments without their original order. The noisy torn paper channel additionally introduces bit substitution errors to each fragment. Recovering the message therefore requires accounting for both bit errors and uncertainty about the fragment order. We establish a capacity upper bound for the noisy torn paper channel that matches the achievable rate of Ravi, Vahid, and Shomorony and resolves their conjecture. Our results also determine the capacity of the noisy shuffling channel of Shomorony and Heckel, in which all fragments have the same length, and resolve their open question.

title: Relative Entropy and the Inviscid Limit for Planar Shocks of the Multi-D Burgers' Equation
abstract: In recent work (arXiv:2610.10341), the authors introduced a framework for studying the vanishing viscosity limit for sequences of weak solutions of the multi-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes equations to planar shocks of the compressible Euler equations. In this paper, we introduce these methods and apply them to the multi-dimensional viscous Burgers' equation. We show that arbitrarily large viscous shocks enjoy $L^2$-stability among perturbations whose gradients in the directions transverse to the shock are controlled in an appropriate manner. As an application, we study the rate of convergence to the inviscid shock in the vanishing viscosity limit.

title: Zero-cycles and Brauer groups on certain Enriques surfaces
abstract: In this paper, we study the Chow group of zero-cycles $\text{CH}_0(S)$ for certain Enriques quotients $S$ of the Kummer surface associated to the product of two geometrically non-isogenous elliptic curves $E_1$ and $E_2$. We show that over fields of characteristic different from $2$ or $3$, the degree-zero subgroup $A_0(S) \subset \text{CH}_0(S)$ is 16-torsion. Over p-adic fields, we compute the transcendental Brauer group $\text{Br}(S)/\text{Br}_1(S)$. Using the Brauer-Manin pairing, we construct examples of Enriques surfaces for which $A_0(S)$ attains nontrivial 2-torsion elements arising from push-forward from the abelian surface $E_1\times E_2$.

title: Ternary polynomial relations and periods of cusp forms
abstract: Bachmann and van Ittersum conjectured that every polynomial $f\in\mathbb{Q}[x,y,z]$ satisfying $$ f(x,y,z)=f(y,z,x),\qquad f(x,y,z)+f(-y,x-y,z)+f(y-x,-x,z)=0 $$ is a sum of polynomials in two variables. We prove this conjecture over every field of characteristic zero and determine all homogeneous solutions. Moreover, restriction to $z=0$ identifies the degree $n$ solution space with the space of binary period polynomials of degree $n$ normalized to vanish on both coordinate axes. The solution corresponding to such a polynomial $q$ is $$ f(x,y,z)=q(x,y)+q(y,z)+q(z,x). $$ There are no nonzero homogeneous solutions of odd degree. For even degrees $n$, the symmetric and alternating solution spaces are each isomorphic over $\mathbb{C}$ to the space of weight $n+2$ cusp forms on $SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$. The proof connects the polynomial relations with the cohomology of arithmetic groups through the rational Tits building for $GL_3$. Cusp forms enter both the description of the solutions and the proof that there are no others. The main theorems and the essential argument are formalized unconditionally in Lean~4 by AxiomProver.

title: A Nontrivial Lattice Scalar Quantum Field Model
abstract: We introduce a new Euclidean quantum model with zero-spin scaled scalar fields on a spacetime hypercubic lattice, which we refer to as the hybrid model. The model coupling parameters are the hopping parameter $\kappa^2>0$ and the field interaction coupling $\alpha>0$. Using the technique of lattice scaled fields, with a noncanonical scaling that corresponds to a partial renormalization (wave function renormalization), we show that the partition function of this model satisfies both thermodynamic and ultraviolet stability bounds, with constants which are uniform in the lattice volume $\Lambda_s$ and the lattice spacing $a\in(0,1]$. As a consequence, the model has a finite free energy per degree of freedom in the thermodynamic limit $\Lambda_s\nearrow\infty$, at least in the subsequential sense. Subsequently, we can also take the ultraviolet or continuum limit $a\searrow 0$. Besides the finiteness property of the free energy, for sufficiently small values of the model coupling parameters $\kappa^2$ and $\alpha$, we show the model satisfies Osterwalder-Schrader positivity and construct the underlying physical quantum mechanical Hilbert space, and, using a polymer expansion, we show correlations also remain bounded in the thermodynamic limit. Finally, we perturbatively compute an infinite volume truncated four-point correlation showing it is nonzero. Noting that, for fixed $a$, perturbation series in $\kappa^2$ and $\alpha$ converges, these results are sufficient to show that our hybrid model makes sense as a lattice quantum field theory in spacetime dimension $d=3,4$, with possible extensions to other higher values of $d$.

title: Shapes of tame abelian number fields
abstract: The shape of a number field $K$ of degree $n\geq2$ is the similarity class of the lattice obtained by projecting $\mathscr{O}_K$ orthogonally away from the rational line in Minkowski space. It defines a point in the space of shapes of rank-$(n-1)$ lattices, $\mathscr{S}_{n-1}:=\mathrm{GL}_{n-1}(\mathbb{Z})\backslash \mathrm{GL}_{n-1}(\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{GO}_{n-1}(\mathbb{R})$, where $\mathrm{GO}_{n-1}(\mathbb{R})$ is the group of orthogonal similitudes. Let $G$ be a fixed nontrivial finite abelian group, and let $K/\mathbb{Q}$ vary over tamely ramified Galois extensions with Galois group isomorphic to $G$. We study the variation of the shapes of such number fields in $\mathscr S_{n-1}$, where $n=|G|$.

title: Solving a sequence of eigenvalue problems using snapshot and row subsampling
abstract: A sequence of eigenvalue problems requires solving $A_i\vec{x}_i= \lambda_i\vec{x}_i$ where $i \in \{1, \dots, N\}$, $N \gg 1$ and (usually) $\lambda_i$ is the largest or smallest eigenvalue of $A_i$. Often, the matrices $A_i$ come from a discretization of a smooth map depending on a parameter $p \rightarrow A(p)$, that is $A_i = A(p_i)$, so the matrices $A_i$ change gradually along the sequence. Under this latter assumption, we introduce an efficient algorithm for solving sequences of eigenvalue problems. Our algorithm combines the ideas of reduced order model and row subsampling, as done in [E. Jones and Y. Nakatsukasa, arXiv, 2025] for linear systems. In addition, in our approach, the same set of rows is guaranteed to work well independently of the value of the parameter $p$ or the matrix $A(p)$ as long as the snapshot matrix is unchanged and given that the row subset was chosen well at the beginning. Furthermore, we implement an update strategy of the snapshot matrix. Along these results, we present theoretical analysis of the snapshot matrix for eigenvalue problems, showing an exponential decay of the singular values, and we give bounds on the error on eigenvectors for unseen value of the parameter. This analysis generalizes that in [M. Guido, D. Kressner, and P. Ricci, J. Sci. Comput., 2024] and shows that, regardless of the distribution of the snapshot points, the convergence is always (asymptotically) exponential in the number of snapshot points if the function $A(p)$ admits an analytical extension. We further generalize our algorithm for computing largest or smallest singular values and relative singular vectors and to generalized eigenvalue problems. We conclude with numerical results showing the efficiency of our approach.

title: Nondegeneracy and asymptotic behavior of type I blow-up for semilinear heat equations with general nonlinearities
abstract: We study the local asymptotic behavior of nonnegative type I blow-up solutions to semilinear heat equations with nonlinearities that need not be scale invariant. Using a quasi-similarity transformation adapted to the associated ordinary differential equation, we establish locally uniform convergence to a constant profile on the parabolic spatial scale near every interior blow-up point. Under a quantitative assumption on the nonlinearity at infinity, our results cover regularly varying nonlinearities in the Sobolev subcritical and critical ranges and, in one and two space dimensions, rapidly growing nonlinearities including double exponentials. A key ingredient in this analysis is a positive lower bound for the normalized solution at interior blow-up points. In fact, under weaker assumptions on the nonlinearity, we prove this bound in arbitrary space dimension without assuming radial symmetry.

title: Algebraic overtwistedness of contact $(+1)$-surgeries via augmented Floer theories
abstract: We prove that contact $(+1)$-surgery along a Legendrian $n$-sphere $\Lambda\subset(\mathbb{S}^{2n+1},\xi_{\mathrm{std}})$ with \[ \mathrm{tb}(\Lambda)\ne (-1)^{\frac{n(n-1)}{2}+1} \] has vanishing contact homology. In dimension three, this produces new examples of tight algebraically overtwisted contact manifolds, vastly extending the authors' previous results: If a Legendrian knot in $(\mathbb{S}^3,\xi_{\mathrm{std}})$ admits an exact, oriented Lagrangian filling that is not a disk, then contact $(+1/k)$-surgery on it is algebraically overtwisted and tight for every positive integer $k$. Our proofs use versions of symplectic cohomology and wrapped Floer cohomology defined by augmentations of a chain-level contact homology algebra.

title: Uniqueness of Limit Cycles for Abel Equations and Planar Systems
abstract: We study positive limit cycles of the Abel equation $$\dot{x}=A(t)x^{3}+B(t)x^{2},$$ where $A$ and $B$ are $2\pi$-periodic functions. By developing a half-period convexity method, we establish a new criterion ensuring that the equation has at most one positive limit cycle. Moreover, if such a limit cycle exists, it is hyperbolic. As applications, we consider two classes of planar polynomial systems that can be reduced to Abel equations. For a subfamily of cubic rigid systems, we prove that there is at most one limit cycle, thereby giving a partial answer to the first problem in Gasull's list of 33 open problems. For quadratic systems, we derive a new uniqueness criterion for limit cycles surrounding the origin and provide explicit parameter regions under which the criterion is satisfied.

title: On Local Inference for Functionals of Ill-Posed Inverse Problems
abstract: We study inference for continuous linear functionals of solutions to ill-posed inverse problems, including Euclidean parameters arising in nonparametric instrumental variables, proximal causal inference, and shadow-variable models. Although pointwise root-$n$ inference is possible under standard conditions, we show that this need not translate into locally reliable inference. Under a model imposing only minimal regularity conditions, the target is Hellinger discontinuous when both inverse problems are ill-posed: arbitrarily small changes in the data-generating law can produce arbitrarily large changes in the target, ruling out informative locally uniform inference. Imposing a uniform bound on a minimum-norm solution restores Hellinger continuity under regularity conditions, but does not by itself ensure stable root-n inference. If, in addition, both inverse problems are ill-posed and the solution whose norm is uniformly bounded is nonunique at a law $P_0$, then under regularity conditions the target fails to be pathwise differentiable; consequently, asymptotically linear estimators exhibit nonvanishing root-$n$ bias under some local alternatives, causing Wald confidence intervals to undercover asymptotically. Under regularity conditions, pathwise differentiability is restored if the uniformly bounded solution is unique at $P_0$. It is also restored, regardless of uniqueness, under the stronger requirement that the corresponding solution satisfy a uniformly bounded $\beta$-source condition for some $\beta$>0. We relate these regimes to very weak, weak, and strong identification in instrumental variables models.

title: Discrete Edge Multiscale Space based Hybrid Schwarz Preconditioner for High-Frequency Helmholtz Problems
abstract: In this work, we develop a novel hybrid Schwarz method, termed as edge multiscale space based hybrid Schwarz (EMs-HS), for solving the Helmholtz problem with large wavenumbers. The problem is discretized using $H^1$-conforming nodal finite element methods on meshes of size $h$ decreasing faster than $k^{-3/2}$ such that the discretization error can be bounded by the data uniformly with respect to $k$. EMs-HS consists of a one-level Schwarz preconditioner (RAS-imp) and a coarse solver in a multiplicative way. The RAS-imp preconditioner solves local problems on overlapping subdomains with impedance boundary conditions in parallel, and combines the local solutions using partition of unity. On the PDE level, this coarse space corresponds to an edge multiscale space proposed in {[S. Fu, G. Li, R. Craster, and S. Guenneau, \emph{Multiscale Model. Simul.}, 19(4):1684-1709, 2021]}. The approximation properties of this coarse space to the discrete solutions from the primal and adjoint problems are derived by a novel conforming Galerkin finite element method based upon a nonstandard variational formulation. This work represents the first theoretical analysis of an edge multiscale space at the discrete level. We prove that the EMs-HS preconditioner leads to a convergent fixed-point iteration uniformly for large wavenumbers, by rigorously analyzing the approximation properties of the coarse space to the global Helmholtz harmonic extension part and to the solution of the adjoint problem. We provide extensive numerical results on the sharpness of the theoretical findings and also demonstrate the method on challenging heterogeneous models.

title: Two non-semisimple quantum invariants of lens spaces
abstract: We calculate the chromatic spherical invariant $\mathscr{K}_{\mathrm{Rep}(H)}(L(p,q))$ of lens spaces $L(p, q)$ for arbitrary finite-dimensional unibalanced, unimodular Hopf algebras $H$. In the case of the index-2 Nichols Hopf algebra $\mathcal{K}_2$ and $q=1$, we find that the invariant of $L(p, 1)$ depends only on the parity of $p$ for $p\geq 1$. We also describe the duals $\mathcal{S_I}(M)^*$ of the admissible skein modules of handlebodies $M=H_g$ and of $M=L(p, q)$ for arbitrary tensor ideals $\mathcal{I}$ of a ribbon tensor category. In particular, $\mathcal{S_I}(L(p, q))^*$ corresponds with cyclic traces on $\mathcal{I}$ satisfying a property reminiscent of the modified trace condition.

title: Fluctuations in the Potts spin glass model at high temperature
abstract: We study the fluctuations of the free energy of the Potts spin glass with $\kappa$ colors at high temperature. The disorder is symmetric with unit variance and finite fourth moment. For configurations with a balanced, or nearly balanced, color profile, the log-partition function satisfies a central limit theorem whenever $\beta^2<\alpha_c(\kappa)$. Here $\kappa\alpha_c(\kappa)$ is the critical inverse temperature of the Curie-Weiss-Potts model. A comparison of color profiles transfers this limit to the unconstrained model for $\beta<\beta_{\max}(\kappa)$, an explicit threshold. In the same range, the magnetizations of two replicas and their overlap matrix satisfy a joint quenched central limit theorem with independent Gaussian limits. The fourth cumulant of the disorder enters the limiting mean and variance explicitly.

title: On the Arnold corank, the Zariski multiplicity, and the tangent Milnor fiber problems
abstract: In this article, we approach the Arnold corank problem posed by Arnold himself in 1975, which asks whether the corank of a holomorphic function is a topological invariant. Here, the corank of a holomorphic function is the corank of its Hessian matrix at 0, which is one of the most basic and fundamental invariants of a holomorphic function. Here, we prove the topological invariance of the corank mod 2. Consequently, we obtain another proof of the Arnold corank problem in dimension 3, which was recently proved by Fernandes, Jelonek, and the author of this article. We also prove that the corank is constant in a continuous family of holomorphic functions with isolated singularities and constant Milnor number. We also approach a conjecture recently posed by Budur, Fern\'andez de Bobadilla, L\^e, and Nguyen (2022), which states that if two germs of holomorphic functions are right topologically equivalent, then the Milnor fibers of their initial forms are homotopy equivalent. We prove that a (much) weaker version of this conjecture, which states that if two holomorphic functions are right topologically equivalent, then the Milnor fibers of their initial forms have the same Euler characteristic, is equivalent to the Zariski multiplicity conjecture for right topological equivalence. Some other results are also presented here. For instance, the multiplicity $> 2$ of generalized semi-Bireskorn-Pham hypersurfaces is an invariant for the right topological equivalence.
comments: This article firstly appeared on ResearchGate on August 26th, 2026. 19 pages

title: Asymptotic Behavior of Transformers
abstract: In this paper we study the behavior of transformer networks generating text over long periods of time. We show that even a three-token, single-layer attention-only transformer can fail to converge. We then study a rich class of transformers with arbitrary finite depth, layer normalization, MLPs, RoPE encodings, and an arbitrary mix of local and global layers. Every transformer in this class has a softmax temperature threshold above which its empirical cache distribution converges to a unique limit, independent of initial conditions. We show further that, while each transformer has a temperature threshold, the supremum of this set is infinite, so there is no global minimal temperature that forces all transformers to converge.

title: Poincar\'e compactifications of pullbacks of parallel vector fields under counterexamples to the real Jacobian conjecture
abstract: Let $F: \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ be a polynomial map with nowhere zero Jacobian determinant. It is known that the global invertibility of $F$ is equivalent to the pullback of a parallel vector field being parallel. In this paper, we construct the phase portraits on the Poincar\'e disc of the pullbacks of the canonical annular, radial, and strip vector fields under non-injective maps $F$ that have recently appeared in the literature. Our arguments use local and global properties of vector fields as well as local and global properties of functions, thereby connecting techniques from dynamical systems and singularity theory.

title: Bicolored Eulerian quasisymmetric functions, affine lengths, and Theta operators
abstract: We introduce a $q$-analogue of the bicolored Eulerian quasisymmetric functions by incorporating an additional grading arising from affine length, obtained by interpreting bicolored permutations as affine permutations. We also provide an intrinsic description of this refinement in terms of bicolored permutations by introducing notions of alignments and crossings, together with an explicit bijection identifying these statistics with the alignments and crossings in the existing literature. Finally, we prove that our refinement is symmetric by expressing it in terms of the Theta operators appearing in the Theta coinvariant Conjecture and the modified Macdonald symmetric functions. Assuming the Theta coinvariant conjecture implies the Schur-positivity of our refinement.

title: Reduction for flag-transitive symmetric 2-designs with gcd(k, {\lambda}) = p
abstract: We study symmetric 2-(v, k, {\lambda}) designs admitting a flag-transitive point-primitive subgroup G of automorphisms, where gcd(k, {\lambda}) = p and p is a prime. In this paper, we show that G is of affine or almost simple type.

title: Weight-adapted ANOVA kernels for high-dimensional periodic approximation
abstract: In this paper, we construct normalized periodic kernels from univariate functions satisfying suitable moment conditions and derive sufficient conditions for high-order convolution approximation. Two computable quasi-interpolation schemes are obtained by discretizing the convolution integral using either a full tensor grid or random samples. In each case, the analysis separates the continuous convolution error from the error introduced by discretization. The contribution of kernel energy to the error exposes the dimensional dependence of tensor-product kernels and motivates our weight-adapted ANOVA constructions. Under suitable summability conditions on the weights, we establish convolution error and kernel energy estimates that yield dimension-uniform error bounds for the resulting quasi-interpolants. Numerical experiments corroborate the theoretical convergence rates and illustrate the effect of coordinate weighting on dimensional dependence.

title: Fractional elementary symmetric functions and Hessian estimates in the plane
abstract: We prove an endpoint Pucci maximum principle for domains in $\mathbb R^2$, formulated using a generalization of elementary symmetric polynomials to noninteger orders. As a result, we sharpen an earlier result of Astala, Iwaniec and Martin, and deduce a new Sobolev inequality for $q$-Hessians where $1 < q < 2$. The fractional elementary symmetric functions we use are derived through fractional differentiation. Their signed singular value extension coincides with the Burkholder functional introduced by Burkholder and gives us access to a local Burkholder inequality due to Astala, Iwaniec, Prause and Saksman, leading to a different proof of the Pucci maximum principle from the one in that used quasiconformal maps. We include an elementary real-variable proof of this local Burkholder inequality, obtained by combining a few known techniques from existing literature.

title: A note on the A.C. spectrum of limit-periodic Jacobi matrices
abstract: We show that limit-periodic Jacobi matrices in the weak exponential class $EC(\eta)$ have purely absolutely continuous spectral type when $\eta$ is sufficiently large, depending only on the $R$-boundedness constant. The proof first establishes homogeneity of the spectrum from the weak exponential approximation rate. A closure theorem for reflectionless Jacobi matrices then transfers reflectionlessness from the periodic approximants to the limit, and a theorem of Poltoratski and Remling rules out singular spectrum on a homogeneous set.

title: Softplus Affine(1, 1) Processes: Enlarged Stationarity Region, Stationary Unit Roots, and Inference
abstract: Softplus affine\((1,1)\) models keep the conditional mean positive while allowing coefficients of either sign. We study them under Poisson, negative binomial, gamma and related conditional distributions. A stationary solution with moments of all positive orders exists whenever the coefficient sum is less than one, strictly enlarging previously known sufficient regions. At the unit root, the coefficient sum equals one. Under an invertibility condition, a stationary solution exists in this case if and only if the intercept is negative. At a stationary unit root, the conditional mean has a power-law tail with an explicit index, and the observations can exhibit long memory. For a fixed softplus scale, the Poisson quasi-maximum likelihood estimator is consistent and asymptotically normal at the usual \(\sqrt n\) rate below and at the unit root, with the coefficient sum left unrestricted in estimation. At the unit root, these results require only a finite mean and yield standard Wald inference even when the observations have infinite variance or long memory. Simulations and two applications examine finite-sample inference and sensitivity to the softplus scale.

title: Dirac Points in High-Contrast Dielectric Honeycomb Structures
abstract: We study Dirac points for a two-dimensional scalar Helmholtz equation in a periodic dielectric medium with two penetrable inclusions per honeycomb cell. In a joint small-inclusion and high-contrast regime, we reduce the Bloch eigenvalue problem to a two-dimensional interaction matrix and derive a two-term asymptotic expansion for the two relevant eigenvalues, uniformly for quasi-momenta separated from the reciprocal lattice. At a vertex K of the Brillouin zone, rotation and inversion-conjugation symmetries force these eigenvalues to coincide. A Schur-complement analysis of the exact operator pencil, together with a nonvanishing lattice Green-function coefficient, proves that the resulting double eigenvalue has a nonzero conical splitting and gives an asymptotic formula for the conical slope in the scaled eigenvalue. For fixed sufficiently large contrast, symmetry-preserving changes of variables and analytic perturbation theory then continue this Dirac point as the inclusion size varies: it remains nondegenerate except at a relatively closed discrete set of admissible sizes.

title: A potential projection method for the nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger equation with low regularity potential
abstract: We propose a potential projection (PP) method for the nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger equation (NLSE) with low-regularity and singular potentials by replacing the potential with its Fourier projection (truncated Fourier series). This gives rise to an NLSE with projected potential (NLSEwPP). We rigorously establish its well-posedness under low-regularity potentials, and its convergence to the original NLSE. The NLSEwPP is then directly discretized by the standard time-splitting Fourier pseudospectral (TS-FP) method with the mesh size chosen according to the potential projection parameter, resulting in the fully discrete TS-PP-FP method. Numerically, TS-PP-FP consistently achieves optimal temporal and spatial convergence rates with respect to the regularity of the exact solution under low-regularity and even singular potentials. Compared with the time-splitting Fourier spectral method, TS-PP-FP attains the same convergence rates at significantly lower computational cost and preserves the mass conservation and time symmetry (that are lost in the Fourier spectral discretization of the time-splitting method); compared with the time-splitting FP method, it is substantially more accurate for low-regularity potentials with the same computational cost.

title: Symplectic extension graphs and Ribet's lemma
abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime, and let $\rho\colon G\to \GSp_{2n}(\Z_p)$ be an irreducible symplectic residually multiplicity free representation. We define the symplectic extension graph $\Gamma_\rho^\GSp$ associated with $\rho$ to be the directed graph whose vertices are the residual factors of $\rho$ and a directed edge between two vertices corresponds to a nonsplit extension between the vertices realized by $\rho$. Using the Euclidean Bruhat--Tits building associated with $\GSp_{2n}(\Q_p)$, under some assumptions, we prove the existence of certain paths in $\Gamma_\rho^\GSp$ and show that $\Gamma_\rho^\GSp$ is a disjoint union of nonempty strongly connected subgraphs. Moreover, we provide examples to show that the result we obtain is optimal.

title: A pure source transfer domain decomposition method for Helmholtz equations in 3D unbounded domain
abstract: We develop and analyze a three-dimensional pure source transfer domain decomposition method (PSTDDM) for the Helmholtz equation in free space. Extending the two-dimensional PSTDDM proposed by [Du and Wu, J. Sci. Comput., 83(2020),83:68], the proposed method transfers sources successively along the $x_1$, $x_2$, and $x_3$ directions, yielding layer-wise, bar-wise, and block-wise PSTDDMs. The main challenge in the convergence analysis is deriving wavenumber-explicit truncation-error estimates. To address this challenge, we establish inf--sup conditions for the uniaxial perfectly matched layer (UPML) problem under relaxed restrictions on the PML parameters and reformulate the source-transfer operators. We then introduce a positive-definite reconstruction step that produces a globally conforming approximation. In addition, a new quantitative lower bound is established for the imaginary part of the complex PML distance, more easily yielding exponential decay estimates in three dimensions. These lead to wavenumber-explicit convergence estimates for all three PSTDDMs. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods both as direct solvers and as preconditioners for GMRES.

title: Birational maps of moduli spaces of stable sheaves on a K3 surface induced by Fourier-Mukai transforms
abstract: We shall study birational maps of moduli spaces of stable sheaves on a K3 surface with Picard number 1 induced by Fourier-Mukai transforms.

title: Large-Step Last-Iterate Convergence of Random-Reshuffling Stochastic Gradient Descent
abstract: Random reshuffling stochastic gradient descent (RR-SGD) is widely used for finite-sum optimization in machine learning. For convex $L$-smooth components, recent work establishes convergence guarantees for an averaged iterate with component stepsizes as large as order $1/L$. However, the final iterate is a natural output in practice, and existing last-iterate guarantees in this setting require stepsizes that scale inversely with the number of components $n$. We establish an expected objective-gap bound for the last iterate of standard RR-SGD on unconstrained problems with a constant component stepsize satisfying $0<\eta\lesssim 1/(L(1 + \log(nK)))$, where $K$ is the number of epochs. By retaining the sampling bias at random comparison points, we remove the explicit $1/n$ factor from the stepsize restriction. Combined with existing small-step bounds, our result matches the corresponding averaged-iterate convergence rate up to logarithmic factors.

title: Fourier-Mukai transforms by a family of stable sheaves and preservation of stability
abstract: For a Fourier-Mukai transform whose kernel is a family of Gieseker stable sheaves, we shall give a condition for the preservation of Gieseker stability of sheaves.

title: Every cubic graph has four total dominating sets covering each vertex at most twice
abstract: In 2018, Goddard and Henning conjectured that every cubic graph has four total dominating sets covering each vertex at most twice, and asked the analogous question for transversals of $3$-uniform $3$-regular hypergraphs. We prove the conjecture, which also answers the question in the affirmative.

title: High-Girth QLDPC Codes from Circulant and Affine Permutation Matrices
abstract: We study two explicit constructions of binary Calderbank--Shor--Steane quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes with check weight six. The first uses a fixed circulant shift pattern and yields parameters $\code{6N}{2N+2}{6}$ with Tanner graph girth twelve for $N=31$ and every $N\ge37$. A graph incidence interpretation gives the ranks and girths, and a uniform weight six logical operator establishes the exact distance. The second construction uses fixed matrix polynomials with circulant and affine permutation coefficients. Here, a polynomial commutation identity guarantees orthogonality for every cyclic lift. Four realizations give $[[192,16,8]]$, $[[288,16,12]]$, $[[384,16,14]]$, and $[[576,32,20]]$, with Tanner girth eight and computationally certified distances. We give reproducible construction data, distinguish classical cycle distance from quantum distance, and identify the limitations of both families.

title: Global solvability with arbitrary mass for a chemotaxis--fluid model with sensitivity growth between linear and quadratic
abstract: We study a Patlak--Keller--Segel--Navier--Stokes system on $\mathbb T\times\mathbb R$ with density-dependent diffusion and chemotactic sensitivity growing like $n^{1+\alpha}$, where $0<\alpha<1$. The coefficients satisfy the constitutive relation of Painter and Hillen (Can. Appl. Math. Q. 2002; 10(4): 501--543). Near a sufficiently strong Couette flow, we prove global classical solvability and uniform density bounds for smooth initial data with arbitrary finite cell mass. A key ingredient is a joint energy estimate for the full density and the non-zero-mode vorticity, which preserves the positive nonlinear diffusion and avoids the mixed diffusion terms arising from separate estimates of the density modes. Bounded Fourier corrections yield enhanced dissipation within this energy, allowing the non-zero-mode density--fluid interactions to be controlled. For the density zero mode, which is not mixed by Couette transport, we observe that $\alpha<1$ allows one-dimensional interpolation to absorb its chemotactic production into diffusion for every finite mass. Together, these estimates control the nonlinear diffusion and fluid coupling without imposing a smallness condition on the initial cell mass.

title: New Qualitative and Quantitative Estimates for Neumann Eigenvalues toward P\'olya's Conjecture
abstract: We introduce the Enhanced Neumann P\'olya inequality, which is stronger than P\'olya's conjecture, and verify it for many classes of domains, including strip-tiling domains, Euclidean balls, thin product domains, and certain higher-dimensional tiling domains. We develop a geometric removal approach for the Enhanced Neumann P\'olya inequality. In particular, our results provide new classes of domains satisfying the Neumann part of P\'olya's conjecture.

title: Weak Private Information Retrieval for Graph-based Storage under $\epsilon$-privacy
abstract: The problem of Private Information Retrieval (PIR) across graph-based replicated systems has seen a surge of interest in recent literature. In such systems, servers are modeled as the vertices of a graph, and each file is represented by an edge connecting the pair of servers that store it. While previous research on Graph-PIR (G-PIR) has focused mostly on perfect information-theoretic privacy, relaxing this constraint has the potential for significantly higher retrieval rates. In this work, we consider the setting of Graph-based Weak Private Information Retrieval (G-WPIR), under an $\epsilon$-privacy metric. We adapt an existing G-WPIR scheme for arbitrary graphs to analyze its performance under the $\epsilon$-privacy metric. Additionally, we establish a lower bound on the expected download cost for arbitrary graphs under the $\epsilon$-privacy metric and derive from it an explicit rate upper bound for complete graphs. Finally, we show the achievable rate-privacy trade-offs for two specific graph classes---complete graphs and complete bipartite graphs.

title: Quantum LDPC Codes from Polynomial Minors
abstract: We construct quantum codes from codewords of a cyclic code and the minors of a polynomial matrix. The construction uses a two-row, three-column matrix whose minors yield a second matrix satisfying the CSS orthogonality condition. We derive the code dimension from the greatest common divisors of the entries and minors, with a simplified formula for odd lifting factors. A residue characterization identifies additional common factors of the minors and leads to a method for controlling the dimension through polynomial selection. We also give a condition for changing the minor generator without changing the code. Explicit polynomial constructions yield 13 quantum codes with verified minimum distances, including a $[[255,80,12]]$ code of rate $80/255$.

title: Quantitative P\'olya inequalities for annular sectors
abstract: We prove explicit positive corrections to the Dirichlet and Neumann P\'olya inequalities at every positive eigenvalue index of every annular sector. The coefficients depend only on the radii and are uniform in the aperture. Real-order angular integration preserves the exact area term, while directional rounding estimates and radial trials control all frequencies. Optimized bounds attain the sharp circular-arc coefficient for the continuous count. We identify the full sector perimeter asymptotic and a low-index obstruction to using its coefficient throughout the spectrum. The strict Neumann inequality also passes to products with bounded Lipschitz domains.

title: ${\mathcal R}$-boundedness of Riesz transforms and spectral multipliers of Schr\"odinger operators
abstract: Let $\LL = -\Delta + V$ be a Schr\"odinger operator with a non-negative potential. It is known that its associated Riesz transform $\nabla \LL^{-\sfrac{1}{2}}$ is bounded on $L^p(\RR^d)$ for $p \in (1,2]$, with a bound independent of $V$. We prove more, namely that the set \[ \{ \nabla \LL^{-\sfrac{1}{2}},\ 0 \le V \in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\RR^d) \} \] is ${\mathcal R}$-bounded on $L^p(\RR^d)$ for $p \in (1,2]$.
