We also prove the ${\mathcal R}$-boundedness on $L^p(\RR^d)$, for $p \in (1,\infty)$, of the spectral multipliers \[ { m(\LL),\ 0 \le V \in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\RR^d) } \] for any $m:[0, \infty) \to \CC$ satisfying a H\"ormander type condition. Our approach is based on the analysis of Schr\"odinger operators $-{\bf \Delta} + {\bf V}$ on vector-valued spaces $L^p(\RR^d,\ell^2)$. In particular, we prove heat kernel estimates, Riesz transform bounds, and spectral multiplier results.

title: A folklore conjecture on multiplicative exponential sums
abstract: We prove a folklore conjecture on exponential sums with multiplicative coefficients: if $f$ is multiplicative with $|f(n)|\le1$, $(a,q)=1$, $|\alpha-a/q|\le q^{-2}$ and $q\le N/(\log N)^2$, then \[ \sum_{n\le N}f(n)\operatorname{e}(n\alpha)\ll\frac N{\log N}+\frac N{\sqrt q}. \] Complete multiplicativity is not required. We also prove two related conjectured bounds: the refinement in which $q$ is replaced by $q(1+N|\alpha-a/q|)$, when this quantity is at most $N/(\log N)^2$, and the corresponding bound for the sum with logarithmic weights. Finally, we show that the bound can fail for multiplicative $f$ satisfying only $|f(p)|\le A$ at primes and $\sum_{n\le x}|f(n)|^2\le A^2x$, for every fixed $A>1$.

title: Relative knot concordance
abstract: Motivated by the relative-slice problem in $4$-manifold topology, we define for a knot $R$ the notion of a relative knot concordance group $\mathcal{C}_R$ and analyze the structure of its algebraic analogue $\mathcal{AC}_R$ modulo torsion. Using Milnor signatures, we show that $\mathcal{AC}_R$ has infinite rank for every $R$. We also show that any prescribed finite set of natural numbers can be realized as orders of elements in a single relative concordance group.

title: Sparse bounds for rough non-translation-invariant Calder\'{o}n-Zygmund operators
abstract: In this paper, we establish sparse bounds for singular integral operators with rough non-translation-invariant Calder\'{o}n-Zygmund kernels. Our approach verifies the localized hypothesis in the sparse domination framework introduced by Conde-Alonso, Di Plinio et al. The proof refines Seeger's microlocal decomposition using a Littlewood-Paley analysis adapted to the non-translation-invariant setting. As applications, we obtain quantitative weighted estimates for Calder\'{o}n-type commutators and other singular integrals with rough kernels.

title: Weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for Riesz transforms of elliptic operators and magnetic Schr\"odinger operators
abstract: Let $M$ be a complete Riemannian manifold and define a magnetic Schr\"odinger operator $\LL = ({\bf d}+ iA)^*({\bf d}+iA) + V$ where $A$ is a real $1$-differential form in $L^2_{loc}$ and $V \in L^1_{loc}$ is a nonnegative electric potential. We prove that the magnetic Riesz transform $({\bf d} + iA) \LL^{-\einhalb}$ is of weak type $(1,1)$ with bound at most $2$. It extends to a bounded operator on $L^p$ for $p \in (1, 2]$ with norm bounded by a constant $c_p$ depending only on $p$. It is then independent of the dimension of the manifold and independent of $A$ and $V$. We also prove weak type $(1,1)$ bounds for symmetric elliptic operators subject to various boundary conditions on rough domains of $\RR^d$. The proofs are based on a new weak type $(1,1)$ criterion for operators.

title: Positivity and negativity for $h$-bases for $n$
abstract: A set $A$ of integers is an $h$-basis for $n$ if every integer in $[0,n] = \{0,1,2,\ldots,n\}$ belongs to the sumset $hA$, that is, can be represented as the sum of exactly $h$ not necessarily distinct elements of $A$. The classical postage stamp problem asks for the largest integer $n_h(k)$ such that $[0,n_h(k)] \subseteq hA$ for some set $A$ of nonnegative integers of size $k+1$. We consider the effect of allowing negative elements. Let $n^{\flat}_h(k)$ be the largest integer such that $[0,n^{\flat}_h(k)] \subseteq hA$ for some set $A$ of integers of size $k+1$ containing at least one negative integer. For $k=2$, we have $n^{\flat}_h(2) < n_h(2)$ if $h$ is odd or $h=4$ and $n^{\flat}_h(2) = n_h(2)$ if $h$ is even and $h \neq 4$. Proofs of these comparison results were autonomously discovered and formally verified in Lean by https://aristotle.harmonic.fun/}{Aristotle}, a formal reasoning agent developed by https://www.harmonic.fun/}{Harmonic}. In this paper we give new proofs of these results.

title: Convergence Rates of Factorized Gradient Descent for Overparameterized Asymmetric Matrix Sensing with Balancing Regularization
abstract: We study factorized gradient descent (FGD) for overparameterized asymmetric matrix sensing with the balancing regularizer $\frac18\|L^\top L-R^\top R\|_F^2$. An exact indefinite lifting of the population objective decomposes the dynamics of FGD into positive, negative, and null spectral subspaces. The first two components have linear restoring terms, whereas the null component contracts only quadratically. For independent isotropic sub-Gaussian sensing matrices and independent centered sub-Gaussian noise with scale proxy $\sigma$, we prove the local bound \[ \|L_tR_t^\top-X^\star\|_2 \lesssim\max\left\{\frac{1}{\eta t+1/\sigma_r}, \kappa\sigma\sqrt{\frac{d_1+d_2}{n}}\right\}, \] under a sufficiently small initialization error, the number of linear measurements $n\gtrsim\kappa^2(d_1+d_2)\max\{k^2,\sigma^2/\sigma_r^2\}$, and step size $\eta\lesssim\sigma_1^{-1}$. Here $\sigma_1$ and $\sigma_r$ are the largest and smallest nonzero singular values of the target $X^\star\in \mathbb{R}^{d_1\times d_2}$ respectively, and $\kappa=\sigma_1/\sigma_r$. Furthermore, a population trajectory was constructed to have tight product error $\Theta(1/t)$. These results provide a local rate characterization for ordinary gradient descent for overparameterized asymmetric matrix sensing with balancing regularizer.

title: A nonequilibrium-capturing unified gas-kinetic scheme I: discrete orthogonal basis construction and expansion on velocity space
abstract: Velocity space discretization is a primary source of computational cost in deterministic methods for multiscale gas flows. A fixed velocity grid often retains redundant kinetic degrees of freedom (DOFs), particularly under near equilibrium conditions. To address this issue, this work develops a nonequilibrium-capturing formulation based on the unified gas kinetic scheme (UGKS), in which the number of kinetic DOFs adapts locally to the degree of nonequilibrium. A discrete orthogonal basis is constructed for numerical implementation, and the velocity distribution function is decomposed into an analytical local equilibrium and a basis expanded nonequilibrium component. The retained, locally adapted DOFs are evolved directly, substantially lowering computational overhead while preserving the discrete conservation of mass, momentum, and energy, as well as accurately capturing nonequilibrium states. The formulation retains the core multiscale coupling of molecular transport and collision inherent to UGKS, providing explicit and implicit schemes for unsteady and steady flows, respectively. Numerical tests across a wide range of flow speeds and rarefaction regimes (from continuum to highly rarefied) demonstrate close agreement with benchmark solutions. For unsteady flows, the explicit scheme achieves speedups of 12.64 to 58.50 over the standard UGKS. In steady state tests, only about $2\%$ of the original kinetic DOFs are required in continuum regions, accelerating each implicit iteration by a factor of 33.87. Even in the most rarefied cases, the scheme captures nonequilibrium behavior using only about $27\%$ of the original DOFs.

title: Digital Self-Interference Cancellation for In-Band Full-Duplex Systems Based on Transformer Neural Operators
abstract: Digital-domain self-interference cancellation is essential in in-band full-duplex radios after passive suppression and analog cancellation. It is particularly challenging when the desired signal is strong relative to the residual self-interference. In this regime, conventional iterative digital cancellers update their coefficients from desired-signal-contaminated received samples and may suffer substantial performance degradation. This paper reformulates digital-domain self-interference cancellation as an operator-learning problem. The proposed framework learns the temporal evolution of the residual self-interference channel from historical observations and uses the learned operator together with the known local transmit signal to reconstruct the current residual self-interference. A Transformer neural operator is used to realize this framework. The resulting method is trained in a desired-signal-free setting and then applied in the presence of a desired signal. A continuity-based analysis characterizes the sensitivity of the learned operator to the resulting input perturbation. Numerical experiments in static and time-varying channels, including time-varying SIR conditions, demonstrate stable cancellation performance over a wide range of interference levels. At 30 dB SIR, the proposed method improves the cancellation performance by 5--15 dB over the considered conventional methods.

title: On generators and relations for $O_n^\circ(V)$ in higher-level Zhu algebras, Part I
abstract: We study the circle-relation subspace $O_n^\circ(V)$ in the defining relations of the level-$n$ Zhu algebra of a vertex operator algebra $V$. We assemble the residue relations generating $O_n^\circ(V)$ into generating functions and obtain an explicit recursion that replaces every sufficiently deep mode by retained modes with indices at least $-2n-1$, modulo $O_n^\circ(V)$. This recursion is encoded in a left truncated field $Y_L$. Since such mode replacements are valid only in the leftmost position of an operator product, we prove the replacement, derivative, commutator, and one-step iterate identities for $Y_L$ needed for finite-length calculations. For a finite homogeneous strong generating set $S$, we define the finite-length circle subspaces $O_n^\circ(N,S,V)$ and their plus subspaces. We formulate a finite-length conjecture under an explicit auxiliary-degree hypothesis and a separate termwise conjecture for the correction residues of one-sided iterates. We prove reductions to the $k=0$ strip and to last vacuum mode $-1$, recover the length-one relation spaces, and give explicit Virasoro computations at word length two for $n=1$ and $n=2$. The $Y_L$ identities are the input for the companion paper (Part II).
comments: 41 pages; ancillary Python verification scripts included. First of a series; companion paper to follow

title: Right Coideal Subalgebras, Hopf Galois Objects, and $\imath$-Hopf Algebras
abstract: We study right comodule algebras and their connections with Hopf bi-Galois objects and right coideal subalgebras. For a Hopf $2$-cocycle $\sigma$ on $K$ and a unital right-colinear algebra map $\Gamma:A\to K$, we show that $\Gamma:A_\sigma\to K^\sigma$ is an algebra map precisely when $\sigma$ is trivial on $\operatorname{im}\Gamma\otimes\operatorname{im}\Gamma$. We describe comodule-algebra morphisms $A_\sigma\to K^\sigma$ by characters and establish injectivity criteria using the coradical and extensions of characters to convolution-invertible functionals. For coactions on Hopf quotients projecting to the coproduct, character-evaluation maps are injective, and equality of their images is determined by a unique algebra character. For the $\imath$-Hopf algebras $H^\imath_\tau$ of Chen--Lu--Pan--Ruan--Wang, with $H$ having a bijective antipode and a Hopf pairing, we obtain a Hopf bi-Galois realization $H^\imath_\tau\hookrightarrow F_\sigma(H\otimes H^{\mathrm{cop}})$. We identify algebra characters with nonzero $\tau$-twisted compatible maps $\chi$ and prove that the corresponding morphisms $\xi_{\tau,\chi}$ of Chen--Lu--Pan--Ruan--Wang are injective, yielding right coideal realizations in $(H\otimes H)^\imath$. We classify the $H^\imath_\tau$ up to comodule-algebra isomorphism and determine when these realizations have the same image.

title: Arithmetic Visibility in Polygons: Curved Sight in the Art Gallery
abstract: In the classical art gallery problem, a guard sees a target when the segment joining them lies entirely within the polygon. We explore what changes when sight may bend along regular arcs on absolutely irreducible curves, but only those defined by primitive integer polynomials of total degree at most \(d\) and coefficient height at most \(H\). We call such curves admissible sight carriers. Arcs can dramatically improve sight. In a one-sided comb, no straight-line guard sees selected targets in two different teeth, yet a single central guard sees a chosen target in every tooth along parabolic carriers. Sight can also fail in two different ways. Geometrically, the polygon may block every sight arc of the allowed degree between two points. For instance, in an alternating comb, the number of guards needed for a row of targets spanning the comb grows linearly with the number of sides at each fixed degree, even for carriers with arbitrary real coefficients. Arithmetically, no admissible carrier may pass through the points at all. Even in the unit square, at fixed \(d\) and \(H\), the proportion of rational targets that must guard themselves tends to one as the height bound grows. An algebraic target may lie on no rational curve of degree at most \(d\), however large \(H\) is. Both failures can be overcome for finite target sets by allowing the degree and coefficient height to grow. We show that every finite set of algebraic targets in a rational polygon becomes visible from any rational interior guard, with explicit bounds. We also construct, for every \(d\), arbitrarily large Galois orbits in the unit square, all of projective height \(4^{d+1}\), whose points must each guard themselves at degree \(d\) for every \(H\). Yet at degree \(d+1\) and coefficient height one, a single guard sees the whole orbit along \(Z(Y-X^{d+1})\).

title: High-Probability Regret Bounds for Feel-Good Thompson Sampling
abstract: Feel-good Thompson sampling (FGTS) augments the posterior of vanilla Thompson sampling with an exploration term that favors reward functions with high predicted optimal values. This modification achieves minimax-optimal regret up to logarithmic factors in linear contextual bandits, but existing analyses of its two standard variants establish regret guarantees in expectation. In this paper, we derive the first high-probability regret bounds for both cumulative and current-step FGTS in contextual bandits with general realizable function approximation. Our bounds depend on the corresponding decoupling coefficients and the prior mass near the true reward function. In the $d$-dimensional linear setting, both variants satisfy $\mathrm{Regret}(T)=O\big(d\sqrt T\log(2T)+\sqrt T\log(1/\delta)\big)$ with probability at least $1-\delta$, where $T$ is the time horizon. This bound matches the dimension and horizon dependence of algorithms based on the upper confidence bounds, up to logarithmic factors. Relative to the expected-regret guarantees, the cost of controlling the regret with high probability is confined to additive terms with at most linear dependence on $\log(1/\delta)$. The proof ideas are partially developed by GPT-6 Astra under the authors' guidance.

title: A Stabilized CR-CR Method for Fourth-Order Elliptic Problems
abstract: We present a CR-CR method for strain gradient elasticity and prove its robustness with respect to the Lame parameter $\lambda$ and the length scale $\iota$. The method introduces the strain as an independent symmetric tensor and discretizes both the strain and the displacement using CR elements. The commuting properties of the CR interpolation operator with the relevant differential operators leads the robustness with respect to $\lambda$. A stabilization term weakly imposes the relation between the strain and the symmetric gradient of the displacement. The method also applies directly to the biharmonic equation and singularly perturbed fourth-order problems. For these problems, we prove that the CR-CR method is equivalent to an RT-CR method proposed by Huang and Tang. This result extends the classical equivalence between the RT-P0 mixed method and the CR method for the Poisson equation to fourth-order problems. The equivalence shows that the stabilization term arises naturally from the RT-CR mixed formulation.

title: Nearly sharp $W^{1,\infty}$ stability of polynomial spectral Ritz projections
abstract: We establish nearly sharp $W^{1,\infty}$ stability estimates for the Legendre spectral Ritz projection associated with Laplacian on a square domain. Its norm grows proportionally to the square root of the polynomial degree, up to a cubic logarithmic factor. The upper bound uses an integral representation of the discrete gradient projection in terms of one-dimensional semigroup kernels and a rank-two Duhamel comparison between the mass-matrix semigroup and its infinite-dimensional counterpart. The lower bound follows from the endpoint concentration of the Legendre kernel. As an application, we derive gradient maximum-norm error estimates for the Poisson and heat equations, with spatial factors optimal up to logarithmic terms.

title: Markov maps and quasi-conformal deformations associated to geometrically finite Kleinian groups
abstract: It is known that the dynamical properties of Kleinian groups with parabolic elements are much more complex than those without parabolic elements. In this paper, we mainly study the quasi-conformal deformation properties of geometrically finite Kleinian groups with parabolic elements. We show that, for a Kleinian group $G$ with parabolic elements, there exists a subset $K$ of the limit set $\Lambda(G)$ such that the first return map $f_{K}$ is (eventually) expending. Furthermore, the expending property is invariant under quasiconformal deformations. As an application, we show that the geometrically finite Kleinian groups have Ruelle's property. Finally, we use eigenvalue algorithm to calculate the precise Hausdorff dimensions of Hecke groups, which serves as an example to support our results.

title: On a problem on partitions into distinct primes
abstract: For a positive integer $n$, we write $L(n)$ in place of the maximum number of distinct primes whose sum is $n$, assuming there is a way of writing $n$ as a sum of distinct primes, with $L(n) = 0$ otherwise. Again if $n$ admits a partition into distinct primes, then we let $K(n)$ denote the number of parts in the unique partition that has a largest product, with $K(n) = 0$ otherwise. In the latest editions of Guy's classic text on unsolved problems in number theory, the problem as to whether or not $L(n) - K(n)$ is unbounded was left open, and it appears that this has remained open. We solve this problem in the affirmative. Our proof relies, to a large extent, on a consequence of Vinogradov's theorem together with a 1948 result due to Sierpi\'nski on the existence of primes whose gaps to the immediately preceding and following primes both exceed any prescribed positive bound.

title: Local Linearization and Exact Oscillations for the Nonlinear Stochastic Heat Equation with Spatially Rough Noise
abstract: Consider the one-dimensional nonlinear stochastic heat equation $$ \frac{\partial u(t,x)}{\partial t} = \frac{\partial^2 u(t,x)}{\partial x^2} + \sigma(u(t,x))\dot W(t,x), \qquad t>0,\ x\in\mathbb R, $$ where $\dot W$ is a Gaussian noise that is white in time and fractional in space with Hurst parameter $H\in(1/4,1/2)$. Hu et al. ({\it Ann. Probab.} {\bf 45} (2017), 4561--4616) established existence and uniqueness of the solution under the assumptions that $\sigma$ is differentiable, both $\sigma$ and $\sigma'$ are Lipschitz continuous, and $\sigma(0)=0$. Hu and Wang ({\it Ann. Inst. Henri Poincar\'e Probab. Stat.} {\bf 58} (2022), 379--423) subsequently removed the technical condition $\sigma(0)=0$ by developing the well-posedness theory in a suitable weighted space associated with the weight $\lambda(x)= c_H (1 + |x|^2)^{H-1}$. In this weighted framework, which allows $\sigma(0)\ne0$, we establish temporal and spatial local linearizations: small increments of the nonlinear solution are approximated by the corresponding increments of the solution to the additive equation, multiplied by the local coefficient $\sigma(u(t,x))$. The main difficulty lies in handling the nonlocal fractional-difference structure induced by the rough spatial noise. We address this difficulty using weighted heat-kernel increment estimates. These approximations yield exact L\'evy-type uniform moduli of continuity in both time and space, together with Khinchin and Chung laws of the iterated logarithm.

title: Normalized Orbit Frames and Essential Spectrum, II
abstract: Given $0<r_{j}<1$ with $r_{j}\to1$, there exist a normal operator $T$ on $\ell^{2}$ with eigenvalues $\lambda_{j}$ satisfying $|\lambda_{j}|=r_{j}$ and $g\in\ell^{2}$ such that \[ \left\{ \frac{T^{n}g}{\left\Vert T^{n}g\right\Vert }\right\} _{n\geq0}\text{is a frame}\:\Longleftrightarrow\:\sum_{j\geq1}\left(1-r^{2}_{j}\right)=\infty. \] Whenever this condition holds, the frame bounds can be chosen with ratio arbitrarily close to one.

title: Shrinking targets versus recurrence: A survey on the Hausdorff dimension theory
abstract: This survey reviews results on the Hausdorff dimension of shrinking target sets and recurrence sets in dynamical systems. In their basic formulations, shrinking target sets concern orbits approaching a prescribed centre, whereas recurrence sets concern orbits returning close to their initial points. A central theme is the comparison of the Hausdorff dimensions of these two classes of limsup sets. The dynamical systems considered include expanding conformal systems, irrational rotations, affine iterated function systems, and matrix transformations. Related results on Hausdorff measure are also included when they provide natural refinements of the dimension theory. Finally, we review results on badly approximating orbits and non-recurrent sets, with particular attention to winning properties and intersections with self-conformal and self-affine sets.

title: Continuous Narayana Interpolations: Hankel Total Positivity and Log-Convexity Preservation
abstract: We study a continuous interpolation between the type $B$ and shifted type $A$ Narayana triangles and its extension through affine moments of the continuous $q$-ultraspherical (Rogers) measure. For every fixed $0<q<1$ and $-1<\beta<1$, these affine moments form a coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive sequence in the polynomial variable $t$. The proof rests on a general continuant criterion: decreasing nonnegative off-diagonal weights and coefficientwise positivity of the leading continuants imply total positivity of the full tridiagonal matrix. A telescoping identity gives positive certificates for shifted continuants and stability under coordinatewise decreases of the weights. We determine the exact power of $t$, palindromicity, and extreme coefficients of arbitrary Hankel minors. Classical limits recover the continuous Narayana family, including its moment representation and gamma positivity. We further prove that the continuous Narayana transformations preserve strong $t$-log-convexity for every real $\theta\ge0$, and that the $d$-Hoggatt transformations have the same preservation property for every integer $d\ge1$. The preservation proofs use the Zhu--Sun criterion and a mixed-minor one-sign-change argument whose local ingredient is a hypergeometric hitting-probability inequality.

title: The Two-Level Poset Game is PSPACE-Complete
abstract: Poset games form a fundamental class of combinatorial games that includes classical games such as Nim and Chomp. Determining the outcome of a poset game is known to be PSPACE-complete even for posets of height at most three. However, the exact computational complexity of Two-Level Poset Game, played on posets of height at most two, has remained an open problem for over a decade. We resolve this problem by proving that Two-Level Poset Game is PSPACE-complete via a polynomial-time reduction from Avoid True on positive CNF formulas.

title: On Inherent Privacy of Posterior Sampling: A Unified R\'enyi-Divergence Framework
abstract: Differential Privacy (DP) provides a rigorous framework for quantifying privacy guarantees. While most methods achieve DP by injecting calibrated random noise, the intrinsic randomness of certain procedures such as sampling can yield DP guarantees ``for free''. In this work, we develop a unified R\'enyi divergence framework to characterize the inherent DP guarantees of sampling from a Bayesian posterior distribution. We show that the privacy loss incurred by One-Posterior-Sampling (OPS) is governed by posterior exponential moments of the single-record log-likelihood ratio, and establish explicit DP guarantees under uniformly bounded, sub-Gaussian, or sub-exponential tail regimes. We apply the framework to representative Bayesian models, including categorical likelihoods with arbitrary priors, Gaussian-Gaussian conjugate pair, generalized linear models from the exponential family and linear regression with Gaussian likelihood, both with Gaussian priors on the regression coefficients. Our results elucidate sample size, model structure, neighboring relations in DP (bounded or unbounded), and how prior if applicable, jointly determine the inherent DP guarantees of OPS. Furthermore, our results recover the existing DP guarantees for OPS as special cases -- often with tighter privacy loss bounds -- and substantially broaden the class of Bayesian models for which the inherent DP guarantees of OPS can be rigorously characterized.

title: The Density and Quantitative Upper Bound of Integers Not Expressible as the Sum of a Prime and a Zumkeller Number
abstract: A Zumkeller number is a positive integer whose set of positive divisors can be partitioned into two disjoint subsets of equal sums. In this paper, we investigate the additive properties of these numbers in conjunction with prime numbers. Specifically, we study the natural density of the exceptional set \(\mathcal{E}\) consisting of all positive integers not expressible as the sum of a prime and a Zumkeller number. Let $\alpha(x) = \#\{n \le x : n \in \mathcal{E}\}$ denote its counting function. We establish a quantitative upper bound for $\alpha(x)$, demonstrating that $\alpha(x) \ll x(\log \log x)^{-A}$, where $A = \log_2\left(\frac{2\pi^2}{2\pi^2-3}\right) \approx 0.2378$, thereby proving that the natural density of this exceptional set is $0$.

title: Maximizing Reaction via Spatial Localization: A PDE-Constrained Variational Approach
abstract: We study a PDE-constrained variational problem for the optimal spatial distribution of a catalytic material reacting with a substrate in a biological or materials system. With a given catalyst concentration, the substrate concentration is determined by a reaction-diffusion equation. The reaction functional for the catalyst concentrations is defined to be the total reaction output, which is the product of catalyst and substrate concentrations. Both the linear and Michaelis-Menten reaction kinetics are considered. We construct reaction-maximizing sequences through the localization of catalysts using barrier functions and show the non-existence of a global maximizer. We also derive the first and second variations of the reaction functional. By constructing a competing catalyst concentration, we show the non-existence of a local maximizer. Based on our analysis, we propose a regularized variational model and prove the existence of its global maximizer.

title: A short open space curve of unit width
abstract: In this work, we propose a curve to be a minimum of length among rectifiable, continuous curves of unit width in three-dimensional Euclidean space. We show that a previously conjectured minimizer of that problem is not of unit width, give the numerical derivation of a candidate family of unit width curves, prove that it admits a strict local minimum within that candidate family and that this minimum is of unit width and length $3.905124162243593\ldots$. The curve consists of eight straight segments, two cone geodesics, and three circular helices. Its parameters are specified by a uniquely isolated solution of the joining and stationarity equations. To establish unit width in every direction, we combine analytic estimates with interval arithmetic on a finite covering of the remaining directions. We conjecture that the curve is globally minimizing. We supplement this work with the programs used to identify the candidates, replicate the computer-assisted parts of our proof, as well as a formalization of our proof in Lean.

title: Seven Limit Cycles in a Periodically Forced Three-Zone Equation
abstract: We construct a seven-cycle example for a periodically forced scalar equation with a continuous three-zone piecewise-linear nonlinearity. Symbolic integration and linear elimination reduce the four-flight matching conditions to two equations in the residence times. The competing exterior visits produce an additional turn of the critical response and lead to the rational parameters $(A,B,\mu)=(9,3/2,181363/100000)$. At these parameters, finite Taylor estimates give three sign changes of the return displacement. Scalar order, analyticity along transverse itineraries, and half-period reflection then establish at least seven distinct isolated periodic orbits on the phase cylinder.

title: On the Isomorphism of Semicircular Algebras
abstract: Building on OpenAI's proof of isomorphism of free group factors, we give a self-contained proof of a corresponding result for $C^{*}$-algebras generated by free semicircular systems: the isomorphism class of a $C^{*}$-algebra generated by a semicircular $n$-tuple does not depend on $n\in\{2,3,\dots,+\infty\}$. Similarly, reduced free products of $n$ copies of the Jiang--Su algebra are isomorphic for different $n$ in this range. While reduced free group $C^{*}$-algebras of different ranks are not isomorphic (by a result of Pimsner--Voiculescu), we show that they have strong free absorption properties. At the heart of the proof is an automorphism approximation property for inclusions of $C^{*}$- and $W^{*}$-algebras; a relative version of that property was previously used to derive free complementation results.
comments: Based on: OpenAI, An isomorphism of the free group factors, preprint, September 23, 2026, family 287 in the collection at github.com/openai/math

title: On the Erd\H{o}s--Odlyzko--S\'ark\"ozy conjecture for prime-power moduli
abstract: Erd\H{o}s, Odlyzko and S\'ark\"ozy conjectured that every reduced residue class modulo $q$ contains a product of two primes not exceeding $q$. O. Klurman, A. P. Mangerel and J. Ter\"av\"ainen (2023) have shown that three primes suffice when $q$ is sufficiently smooth. We study the moduli $q=p^\gamma$ that are powers of a fixed prime $p$ and we show that the third prime can be taken subpolynomially small. For any $q_\bullet\le q$ for which $q_\bullet\ge\exp\bigl(C(\log q)^{2/3}(\log\log q)^{4/3}\bigr)$, we give an asymptotic formula for the weighted number of representations of each reduced class as a product of two primes not exceeding $q$ and a third not exceeding~$q_\bullet$. We also show that the conjecture holds for all but a proportion $\exp\bigl(-c(\log q)^{1/3}(\log\log q)^{-1/3}\bigr)$ of the reduced classes. Here $C$ and $c$ are positive constants that depend only on $p$. Both results are unconditional and they rely on a wide zero-free region with no exceptional zeros for the Dirichlet $L$-functions attached to characters modulo $p^\gamma$.We also present conditional versions of these results for arbitrary $q$ under a quasi-Riemann hypothesis.

title: The $RO(C_2)$-graded Hurewicz image of Atiyah's Real K-theory
abstract: We determine the $RO(C_2)$-graded $k\mathbb R$-Hurewicz image, where $k \mathbb R$ denotes the connective Atiyah's Real $K$-theory spectrum. As a consequence, we obtain four infinite families in the $RO(C_2)$-graded equivariant stable stems that are $C_2$-equivariant refinements of the classical $\mu$-families. Using a $C_2$-equivariant $v_{1,0}$-self map, we explicitly construct an equivariant Adams periodicity operator $P_{C_2}$ that captures these $v_1$-periodicity phenomena in the $C_2$-stable stems.

title: Sharp Constants, Threshold, and Failure of Uncertainty Principles on Non-trivial Flat Finsler Manifolds
abstract: By uncertainty principles we mean the generalized Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg (CKN) inequality and the Heisenberg--Pauli--Weyl (HPW) uncertainty principle, with the latter being an endpoint case and the Hardy inequality a further limiting case. We study these \(L^p\)-type inequalities \((1<p<n)\) on \(n\)-dimensional non-trivial flat Finsler manifolds, which arise from Hilbert's fourth problem. These manifolds are forward complete but not backward complete, projectively flat, with zero flag curvature, and have infinite reversibility, making them highly asymmetric. They are the simplest non-Riemannian, non-Minkowskian solutions to Hilbert's fourth problem, providing a natural framework in which classical inequalities exhibit new behavior. For the full class, we establish a sharp threshold at the parameter value \(s=2\): the generalized CKN inequality and the HPW uncertainty principle hold for \(s>2\) but fail completely for \(s\le2\). When the generating Minkowski norm is reversible (while the Finsler metric itself remains irreversible with infinite reversibility), we determine the sharp constants for \(s>2\), which were previously unknown. These constants are approached in the limit by compactly supported radial functions. As a corollary, our results cover Berwald's metric space and resolve the open questions on its sharp constants. These findings reveal that the threshold phenomenon is structural for the entire class and is a genuinely non-Riemannian feature with no analogue in the Riemannian flat case.

title: Percolative MDLA: phase transition and critical behaviour
abstract: In this paper we introduce the model of Percolative MDLA (PMDLA) on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ which engulfs the entire occupied percolation component of each particle that reaches the aggregate. We prove a phase transition of finite time explosion, as a function of the particle density $\lambda$, where the critical value equals $\lambda_c=-\log(1-p_c^{\rm site}(\mathbb{Z}^2))$. Below $\lambda_c$, the process is nonexplosive and has a linear upper bound on its radius. For $2/3<\lambda<\lambda_c$, it also has a linear lower bound on the growth rate. Above $\lambda_c$, an infinite component is swallowed in finite time a.s. At $\lambda_c$, every update is finite, but the updates accumulate in finite time, causing a blowup. Excluding criticality, the results are generalized to all higher dimensions.

title: Isometries of Unit Spheres of SFS-Spaces and a Geometric Approach to Tingley's Problem
abstract: We investigate surjective isometries between the unit spheres of facially symmetric spaces and their interaction with the underlying facial structure. It is shown that such isometries preserve the essential geometric relations associated with symmetric faces, orthogonality, and geometric tripotents. In particular, a surjective sphere isometry induces a natural correspondence between the geometric tripotents of the underlying spaces and preserves the principal structural features determined by the Peirce decomposition. These results provide a geometric framework for studying linear extension problems for sphere isometries. As an application, we establish a positive solution of Tingley's problem for finite-dimensional real neutral strongly facially symmetric spaces satisfying the joint Peirce property. We also obtain an extension result for a wider class of real neutral strongly facially symmetric spaces admitting an appropriate approximation by finite-dimensional Peirce subspaces. In these settings, every surjective isometry between unit spheres extends uniquely to a surjective real-linear isometry of the ambient spaces. The results demonstrate that the facial and tripotent structures play a decisive role in the rigidity of spherical isometries.

title: Sharp $L^q$ estimate of adjoint problem and Pucci conjecture
abstract: Let $L$ be a linear second-order elliptic operator satisfying a nondegeneracy condition. We establish sharp $L^q$ estimates for solutions of the adjoint problem associated with $L$ and, by duality, derive sharp $L^p$ estimates for solutions of $Lu = f$. In particular, this confirms a conjecture of Carlo Pucci.

title: Catalan polynomials for the Wishart-Laguerre $\beta$-ensemble
abstract: By means of $W$-representation, we investigate the Wishart-Laguerre $\beta$-ensemble and present a compact expression for Catalan polynomials. For a special Nekrasov partition function associated with the Wishart-Laguerre $\beta$-ensemble, we show that it can be expressed as a exponential form of the special Catalan polynomials. Furthermore, we make a rule to calculate the Catalan polynomials by means of Feynman diagrams and present another expression for Catalan polynomials. We also establish the connection between certain Catalan polynomials and knot theory.
comments: 15 pages, accepted for publication in Physics Letters B

title: What Inverse Problems Can Be Solved Using Neural Networks?
abstract: The relationship between classical methods for solving inverse problems and neural network methods is examined. An answer is provided to the question of what inverse problems can be solved using neural networks. The answer is that neural network algorithms can solve only conditionally well-posed problems (well-posed according to Tikhonov). The reason is that the design of standard neural network algorithms violates the well-known Bakushinsky veto from the theory of ill-posed problems. It requires that any method theoretically guaranteeing a stable solution to an ill-posed problem must depend explicitly on the error level of data. The article highlights the distinction between the concept of regularization (RA) in the theory of ill-posed problems and regularization as understood in neural network training, where Bakushinsky's veto is violated. Due to this violation, any changes to the neural network architecture, regularization during training, or training dataset augmentation cannot alter the answer specified above. It is theoretically demonstrated that an ill-posed inverse problem can be solved only by using a parametric set of neural networks that explicitly depend on the known error levels (as parameters) of data. Accordingly, as an alternative to standard neural network algorithms, \neural network based regularization algorithms (NNBRAs) are proposed to solve ill-posed inverse problems. One approach to their construction involves using a regularized dataset. Such a dataset can be generated from perturbed inverse-problem data using a specific base RA explicitly depended on the error level of the data. Test solving the simplest finite-dimensional ill-posed inverse problem demonstrate that the accuracy of the NNBRA approximate solutions is comparable to that of the base RA. At the same time, errors of conventional neural network methods may be unacceptable.

title: Model-Induced Hazard Geometry and Functional Representations in Survival Analysis
abstract: Individualized survival predictions are often summarized by scalar risk scores or event probabilities at selected time horizons, although clinically relevant risk may also differ in its temporal organization. We consider finite-dimensional representations of individual hazard trajectories through interpretable hazard functionals, such as peak timing, cumulative hazard over prespecified intervals, and persistence of elevated risk. A central issue is that the richness of such representations is constrained by the hazard geometry supported by the underlying survival model. We formalize this through model-induced tangent spaces and functional ranks, derive an exact decomposition of model-supported variation into directions retained and lost by a chosen representation, and introduce a model-relative notion of local completeness. We further distinguish intrinsic model capacity from the variation actually activated by covariates. These results motivate a structured extension of AFT time scaling through a positive-affine deformation on the log-time scale, yielding a power-warp mechanism with an additional temporal deformation direction. Combined with a log-logistic reference hazard, this gives a parsimonious likelihood-based working specification for which peak timing and peak height provide complete coordinates over the unimodal regime. We also establish plug-in recovery and asymptotic inference for hazard functionals. Simulations and a lung-cancer application illustrate how model-induced restrictions propagate to hazard-functional representations.

title: The Big Match under translation-invariant charges
abstract: We study two-player zero-sum stochastic games in which a stream of stage payoffs is evaluated by a translation-invariant charge on the set of stages. Every patient valuation, that is, every diffuse charge that obeys the time value of money principle, is translation-invariant, and by Mertens and Neyman each player has, for every $\varepsilon>0$, a strategy that is $\varepsilon$-optimal for all patient valuations simultaneously. We show that this robustness breaks down for translation-invariant charges. In the Big Match with $0$--$1$ payoffs, whose uniform value is $1/2$, every strategy of Player 1 is worthless: for every strategy of Player 1 and every $\delta>0$, Player 2 has a pure reply, and there is a translation-invariant charge under which Player 1's payoff is less than $\delta$. Consequently, the Big Match has no value with respect to all translation-invariant charges. This contrasts with finite Markov decision processes, where every stationary Blackwell optimal strategy is optimal for every translation-invariant charge. We pose questions on robust guarantees in general stochastic games and on optimality with respect to a fixed translation-invariant charge.

title: Sharp radial--angular mixed norm Fourier extension and global stability on spheres
Calabi metric on the space of k-Hessian potentials
abstract: Let $(X,\omega)$ be a compact K\"ahler manifold of complex dimension $n$, and let $1\leq k\leq n$. We consider the space of smooth $k$-admissible potentials introduced in the study of the Hessian-cscK equation by Guo--Smith--Tong. The complex $k$-Hessian equation identifies this space, modulo constants, with the space of smooth positive densities of fixed total mass. We compute the differential of the Hessian density map and use it to pull back the Fisher--Rao metric. The resulting Riemannian metric is \[ G^{\HC,k}_{\varphi}(u,v) =\int_X \bigl(\Delta_{\varphi}^{(k)}u\bigr) \bigl(\Delta_{\varphi}^{(k)}v\bigr) \,\omega_{\varphi}^{k}\wedge\omega^{n-k}. \] We then show that the square-root Hessian density map \[ \varphi\longmapsto 2\sqrt{\frac{\omega_{\varphi}^{k}\wedge\omega^{n-k}}{\omega^n}} \] is a global Riemannian isometry onto the positive part of the $L^2(X,\omega^n)$-sphere of radius $2\sqrt{V}$, where $V=\int_X\omega^n$. For $k=n$, this recovers the spherical description of the classical Calabi metric. We also derive the curvature, geodesic and diameter formulas, and prove a quantitative local comparison between adjacent Hessian--Fisher distances.

title: Time-Inconsistent Singular Dividend Control with Regime Switching and Bankruptcy
abstract: This paper studies infinite-horizon equilibrium dividend distribution for a firm whose surplus follows a diffusion under observable Markov regime switching and is absorbed at bankruptcy. Dividend payments are modeled as singular controls, and non-exponential discounting leads to time inconsistency. We formulate equilibrium control laws and establish a verification theorem for a general finite-state model with surplus-dependent coefficients. For a two-state model with constant positive drifts and volatilities and bi-exponential discounting, we prove the existence of a regime-dependent equilibrium barrier policy for arbitrary positive switching intensities. The policy retains surplus below the prevailing regime's threshold and distributes any excess immediately. Numerical experiments examine how shareholder patience and economic conditions affect dividend decisions. Over the parameter ranges considered, greater discount-rate dispersion at a fixed initial average rate raises both barriers, while switching speed can generate nonmonotone responses and reverse their ordering.

title: Weighted composition--differentiation operators on mixed-norm, derivative Hardy and F(p,q,s) spaces
abstract: We study weighted composition--differentiation operators on mixed-norm, derivative Hardy and F(p,q,s) spaces. Explicit dyadic criteria yield boundedness, compactness and two-sided norm and essential-norm estimates, including endpoint and quasi-Banach cases. We also obtain multiplier and approximation results, Schatten criteria on weighted Dirichlet spaces, and exact singular values for monomial weights and linear symbols.

title: Algebraically Integrable Smooth Convex Bodies
abstract: We prove that a convex body with $C^\infty$ boundary in an odd dimension $n\ge3$ is algebraically integrable if and only if it is an ellipsoid. This answers Arnold's problem for smooth convex bodies. Together with Vassiliev's even-dimensional nonexistence theorem, it gives the classification in every dimension $n\ge2$. More generally, in odd dimensions, a convex body with $C^\infty$ semialgebraic boundary is an ellipsoid whenever its section volume function satisfies a joint algebraic relation.

title: C1 Virtual Element Methods for the Optimal Control of Oseen Equations with Stream-Function Formulation
abstract: This work analyzes a $C^1$-conforming virtual element method for the optimal control of generalized Oseen equations, formulated using the stream-function on simply connected polygonal domains. The method is based on a conforming discretization in $H^2$ of arbitrary order $k \ge 2$. The discrete scheme considers an approximation of the state and co-state equations which involves a specifically designed operator for the convective term and a \textit{variational discretization} of the control variable. We derive quasi-optimal a priori error estimates in the $H^1$ and $H^2$-norms for the stream-function, and in the $L^2$-norm for the control, under standard assumptions on the family of polygonal meshes. The proposed method recovers the fluid velocity, vorticity, and pressure using suitable projections. Finally, we report several numerical experiments to support the theoretical findings using different polygonal meshes including the cavity problem. We highlight that this analysis also covers OCPs governed by Brinkman and Stokes equation.
comments: Accepted for publication in Mathematical Models and Methods in Applied Sciences

title: The fence conjecture for convex projective polygons
abstract: We prove the fence conjecture of Dumas and Wolf: for a convex projective polygon with at least five vertices, every zero of the Pick differential lies in the interior of the region obtained by cutting off the triangles at consecutive triples of vertices. The proof gives a stronger estimate for arbitrary properly convex domains. In affine-sphere coordinates normalized at a Pick zero, the domain contains the closed disk of radius $2^{-1/4}$ and its closure lies in the open disk of radius $2^{1/4}$, unless it is a rotated square. The proof compares the canonical Monge-Amp\`ere potential of the domain with that of a normalized square. Their third-order contact gives alternating local sign sectors. A planar separation argument and the maximum principle show that the negative sectors belong to four distinct components, each meeting a different side of the square. Rotation gives the inner disk bound, and conormal duality gives the outer bound. Both constants are optimal for the class of properly convex domains normalized at a Pick zero. The argument requires neither boundary smoothness nor any restriction on the multiplicity of the Pick zero.

title: Invariable Generation of Groups of Homeomorphisms
abstract: We provide a sufficient condition for a group of homeomorphisms of a compact Hausdorff space to be non-invariably generated, generalizing previous results proved using the dynamics of a group's action. We exhibit new applications among Scott-R\"over-Nekrashevych groups and among groups of tree automorphism of with (almost) locally prescribed actions.

title: Remarks on prescribed scalar curvature functions
abstract: This short article is devoted to the study of the positive solution of Yamabe-type semi-linear equation with prescribed coefficient on general closed manifolds. Our main result is to provide some sufficient conditions for the existence of the positive solutions and give some examples to show that those conditions are sharp. An application to scalar-flat manifold settles a long standing question in prescribing scalar curvature problem in negative form.

title: Maximum Likelihood Degrees via One-Edge Chordal Completion
abstract: The maximum likelihood degree of a Gaussian graphical model measures the algebraic complexity of its likelihood equations. This paper studies maximum likelihood degrees of Gaussian graphical models through chordal completion. When a graph becomes chordal after one missing edge is added, its maximum likelihood degree is determined by the maximal cliques and clique-tree separators containing that edge. This recovers Uhler's formula for complete bipartite graphs with one part of size two, and extends it to deleted-spine clique books, whose degree is unchanged when a page is thickened to a clique. For several fill edges, the same method gives a product formula when no clique or separator bag contains two fill edges. We also determine four classes of vertices at which clique blow-up preserves the degree. Two follow from known results, and two are established here.

title: Exponential functionals of two random walks and stationary measures of discrete growth processes
abstract: We study random walks with geometric or log-gamma increments, reweighted by certain exponential functionals. We establish precise asymptotics for all moments of exponential functionals, revealing a phase transition as the drifts of the walks vary. To describe the large time limit of reweighted random walks, we introduce a discrete $T$ transformation on random walk paths and establish Girsanov relations. As a corollary, we show that the stationary measures of geometric last passage percolation and the log-gamma polymer on a strip converge to their half-space counterparts as the strip width tends to infinity. In the log-gamma case, this provides an alternative proof of a recent result in arXiv:2607.17030.

title: On Completely Positive and Semidefinite Programs for Moment Bounds on Maximum of Random Quadratics
abstract: Completely positive programs are known to provide an exact representation to several NP-hard optimization problems. In this work, we look at the maximum of random quadratic functions and compute the maximum expected value over ambiguity sets defined with moment and support information. We propose exact completely positive programs and semidefinite programs when the random variables are Bernoulli, nonnegative and unrestricted in support. Our experimental study demonstrates the utility of these formulations.

title: The regular inverse Galois problem over fields avoiding a curve
abstract: Let $k_0$ be a field of characteristic $0$, and let $C/k_0$ be a smooth geometrically integral curve of positive genus with $C(k_0)=\varnothing$. We prove that the regular inverse Galois problem is solvable over every field existentially closed in the class of $k_0$-fields avoiding $C$, including the curve-excluding fields of Johnson and the author. To this end, we show that for every finite group $G$, there is a parameter variety over $\mathbb Q$ whose function field admits a regular realization of $G$ without adding points to $C$. Finally, we establish $\mathrm{RIGP}$ over the variety-excluding fields of Szachniewicz and the author, when the excluded variety is a locally closed subvariety of an abelian variety.

title: Efficient construction of subspace design codes over constant alphabet
abstract: Subspace-design codes form a central unifying framework in coding theory, connecting probabilistic existence results and explicit algebraically structured constructions. The two core families are folded Reed-Solomon codes and univariate multiplicity codes, both possessing the subspace-design property. These codes reach list-decoding capacity with polynomial-size lists, but their alphabet size grows with code length and hurts practical efficiency. Goyal, Guruswami, and Hsieh achieved a major breakthrough: they constructed the first explicit subspace-design codes over constant-size alphabets via the Alon-Edmonds-Luby expander framework, settling an open problem and showing subspace-design properties can hold without large alphabets. Despite recent progress, constructing subspace-design codes with low-complexity efficient encoding remains a critical open challenge. This work gives an explicit construction of r-dimensional subspace-design codes over a constant alphabet whose size grows exponentially with r. By comparison, Goyal et al. (FOCS 2026) built r-dimensional subspace-design codes with alphabet size doubly exponential in r squared. Our construction is computationally efficient: encoding scales quadratically with block length and linearly with dimension r in field operations. We use modified algebraic geometry codes, replacing rational evaluation points with higher-degree places to obtain a valid additive code. To confirm parameter bounds, we use Moore matrices to analyze determinants with many zero entries. We also generalize univariate multiplicity codes, originally built from Reed-Solomon codes, to algebraic geometry codes, and prove these AG-multiplicity codes achieve optimal parameters.

title: On the sum of eccentric subgraph numbers of the vertices of a connected graph
abstract: Let $G$ be a connected graph. The eccentric subgraph number $\epsilon(v)$ of a vertex $v$ of $G$ is defined as $\epsilon(v)=\min\{f_G(v,u): u\in V(G)\}$, where $f_G(v,u)$ is the number of connected subgraphs of $G$ containing both $v$ and $u$. The eccentric subgraph index $ES(G)$ of $G$ is defined as $ES(G)=\displaystyle\sum_{v\in V(G)}\epsilon(v).$ In this paper, we obtain the unicyclic graph that maximizes the eccentric subgraph index among all unicyclic graphs on $n$ vertices with a fixed girth. The graph that maximizes the eccentric subgraph index among all unicyclic graphs on $n$ vertices is also obtained. We then characterize the trees that maximize the eccentric subgraph index over trees on $n$ vertices with fixed diameter. Among all connected graphs on $n$ vertices with a fixed number of pendant vertices, the graph which maximizes the eccentric subgraph index is also characterized.

title: Coherent-State Integrals Beyond the Domain of Operator Products
abstract: Inserting a resolution of the identity between two operators turns a matrix element of their product into a phase-space integral. For unbounded operators the product need not exist on the vector at hand, while the integral may still converge. We follow this gap through the chain $e^{\mu a^2}e^{\lambda a^{\dagger2}}$ of two-photon exponentials, where it can be traced completely. Five regions of parameter space appear: where the Bochner conditions of the strong formulation hold, where the product exists as a vector, where it exists as a sesquilinear form, where the coherent-state integral converges, and where the Fock-space series converges. The first three are strictly nested inside the intersection of the last two, and these two overlap without either containing the other. A single Hermite-type function agrees with the matrix element where it exists and with the integral and the series wherever they converge, so the integral carries the analytic continuation of the matrix element beyond the domain of the product and beyond the convergence of its Fock series. On the real slice of parameter space, an iterated form of the integral also reaches every point where the series converges. The analysis rests on a weak composition lemma whose hypotheses concern only the bra, the ket and the resolving family. For bounded chains the same identity is unconditional, and worked examples of that kind are given in a companion paper.

title: The Weil-Petersson diameter of moduli space for large genus
abstract: We determine the large-genus order of the Weil-Petersson diameter of $\mathcal{M}_{g,n}$ for each fixed number of punctures: namely, $\mathrm{diam}(\mathcal{M}_{g,n})\asymp\sqrt g\log g$. The main new ingredient is an integrated Ricci estimate for geodesics that minimize in moduli space and have thick endpoints, with no systole bound along their interiors.

title: Capacity Bounds for Optical Interference Channels Subject to Average Power Constraints
abstract: Accurate information-theoretic analysis of multiuser wavelength-division multiplexed (WDM) optical links is complicated by Kerr nonlinearity and chromatic dispersion. Existing capacity bounds for first-order regular perturbative (RP) channel models have relied on per-symbol peak power constraints to simplify the underlying extremal analysis. In this paper, we replace these peak constraints with the more practically relevant average input power constraints and study the resulting RP WDM interference channel. Unlike the peak-constrained formulation, an exact finite signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) analysis under average power leads in general to a nonconvex, high-dimensional optimization problem with no closed-form solution. We show that the problem admits a tractable characterization in the high-SNR regime. Using a genie-aided argument, we derive closed-form single-user high-SNR capacity bounds for the RP interference channel and identify constant-amplitude interferer signaling as extremal. Furthermore, under an empirically validated non-negativity condition on the dominant RP kernels and within a truncated first-order RP model, we establish a finite-SNR extremality result, yielding a single-user capacity characterization within the RP model under average power constraints. Building on these single-user corner points, we construct an all-helpsone achievable region via time sharing, which strictly improves upon treating nonlinear interference as noise. Numerical results and split-step Fourier simulations of the nonlinear Schrodinger equation channel confirm that the qualitative conclusions persist over practical launch powers. The results provide new insight into extremal signaling and multiuser trade-offs for nonlinear WDM systems within the RP approximation.

title: Gaussian approximation for the integrated intensity of counting processes: application to Hawkes processes
abstract: In this paper, we establish quantitative central limit theorems for the integrated fluctuations of the intensity of a counting process. Building on the work of Coutin and using the Clark-Ocone formula, we first derive a general upper bound on the Wasserstein distance between a Gaussian random variable and the normalized integral of the centered intensity. We then apply this result to subcritical linear Hawkes processes. In this setting, we prove that the integrated fluctuations of the intensity converge in distribution to a centered Gaussian random variable, with a convergence rate governed by the tail behavior of the resolvent associated with the underlying Volterra equation.

title: Asymptotic stability and Rayleigh-Taylor instability of stratified states for the three-dimensional rotating primitive equations with gravity
abstract: We study the 3D rotating primitive equations with gravity in a horizontally periodic channel, with viscous horizontal velocity and no density diffusion. For every Coriolis parameter, stably stratified equilibria are asymptotically stable. Small compatible \(H^4\) perturbations yield global classical solutions with uniform \(H^4\) bounds. The oscillatory density and velocity decay like \((1+t)^{-1}\); the density converges at the same rate to a stratified profile, its horizontal mean faster. For small data, the limit profile is the decreasing vertical rearrangement of the initial density, the unique potential-energy minimizer among rearrangements, independent of rotation, viscosity, and initial velocity. Kinetic plus available potential energy is dissipated exactly by viscosity and decays like \((1+t)^{-2}\), and each fluid particle settles where the limit density equals its own. These rates are optimal for every rotation rate. The linearized problem has real, slowly decaying normal modes, viscously overdamped high-vertical-wavenumber internal gravity waves, whose small solutions show the \(H^r\) density rates \((1+t)^{-(1-r/4)}\), \(0\le r<4\), pressure rate \((1+t)^{-1}\), and energy rate \((1+t)^{-2}\) cannot be improved uniformly for small data. Key difficulties are the loss of a horizontal derivative in the vertical velocity, the failure of \(H^1(\mathbb T^2)\subset L^\infty\), and rotation-induced coupling of divergent and vortical motion, controlled at top order by a positive power of the initial low-order energy. If the stratification is unstable somewhere, every horizontal mode is linearly unstable with real growth rates and the equilibrium is nonlinearly unstable; rotation strictly lowers each growth rate, with an explicit Taylor-number bound depending on the horizontal wavelength, but leaves their supremum unchanged.

title: Continuous and compact embeddings for a class of modular sequence spaces
abstract: In this article we prove the existence of continuous and compact embeddings for a class of modular sequence spaces generated by Orlicz functions. The class under consideration contains sequence spaces of Orlicz-Sobolev type, including certain special cases that have played an important role in a number of applications regarding problems arising in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, as well as Nakano's class of Lebesgue sequence spaces with variable exponents. In a few exceptional cases we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for such embeddings to hold, in many others only sufficient conditions and in that situation we clearly indicate why these are not necessary by means of additional criteria and specific examples. Our results are complementary to those already available in the literature. We illustrate them with several concrete examples.

title: Finite Volume Methods
abstract: This chapter focuses on finite volume methods. The finite volume method is a discretization method that is well suited for the numerical simulation of various types (for instance, elliptic, parabolic, or hyperbolic) of conservation laws; it has been extensively used in several engineering fields, such as fluid mechanics, heat and mass transfer, or petroleum engineering. Some of the important features of the finite volume method are similar to those of the finite element method: it may be used on arbitrary geometries, using structured or unstructured meshes, and it leads to robust schemes. The finite volume method is locally conservative because it is based on a ``balance'' approach: a local balance is written on each discretization cell that is often called ``control volume;'' by the divergence formula, an integral formulation of the fluxes over the boundary of the control volume is then obtained. The fluxes on the boundary are discretized with respect to the discrete unknowns.
journal_ref: J. L. Lions; Philippe Ciarlet. Solution of Equation in ?n (Part 3), Techniques of Scientific Computing (Part 3), 7, Elsevier; Elsevier, pp.713-1020, 2000, Handbook of Numerical Analysis, 9780444503503

title: Global well-posedness of the energy-critical nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on the three-dimensional torus with additive L\'evy noise
abstract: This paper establishes global well-posedness for the defocusing energy-critical nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on the three-dimensional torus with a class of additive L\'evy noises. For arbitrary deterministic initial data in the energy space, we construct probabilistically strong solutions that are pathwise unique in the critical solution class. Continuous dependence on initial data, convergence of finite-activity approximations, and a vanishing-noise limit hold on finite time intervals. When the effective noise is nonzero, quantitative bounds for mass exit times imply almost-sure unboundedness of the mass and exclude free scattering. The expected energy then admits a cubic lower bound in time. The analysis couples pathwise critical perturbation theory with energy estimates adapted to Poisson compensation and stopping-time arguments based on the exact mass balance.

title: Prefixes of Coxeter elements are Coxeter elements of the reflection subgroups they generate
abstract: Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system of finite rank, let $T$ be its set of reflections and let $c \in W$ be a Coxeter element. For $x$ in the interval $[1,c]_T$ of the absolute order, let $P(x)$ be the subgroup generated by the reflections $t\le_T x$. We prove that $x$ is a Coxeter element of $P(x)$ with respect to the canonical Coxeter generators of $P(x)$, that $P(x)$ is generated by the factors of any reduced reflection factorization of $x$, and that the Hurwitz action on the reduced reflection factorizations of $x$ is transitive. The proof reduces the general case to the case of a Coxeter system whose Coxeter matrix has entries in $\{1,2,3,\infty\}$, which was treated by Hubery and Krause.

title: On blow-up for the supercritical defocusing nonlinear scalar wave equation
abstract: We study finite-time singularity formation for the scalar defocusing nonlinear wave equation $-\partial_t^2u+\Delta u=u^p$. First, for fixed $d\geq4$ and odd $p\geq3$, we establish a conditional blow-up result under the assumption that a smooth self-similar imploding profile exists for the leading-order relativistic Euler system, with associated normalized coefficients satisfying quantitative analytic radius conditions. Second, we verify both the profile and the analytic radius conditions in dimensions four and five for all sufficiently large odd $p$. Using finite speed of propagation, we obtain a dimension-independent threshold $p_0$ such that, for every $d\geq4$ and every odd $p\geq p_0$, finite-time blow-up occurs for some smooth, compactly supported, real-valued initial data. The proof combines a normalized formulation that separates the leading periodic oscillation from the unknown modulation, growth of the spatial analytic radius induced by an outgoing property, and frequency-dependent matrix multipliers that control the cumulative growth caused by the periodic linearized potential.

title: From Global to Tail Convergence: Dynamics of $\alpha$-Stable Score-Based Generative Models
abstract: Score-based generative models driven by $\alpha$-stable L{\'e}vy processes have been proposed as an alternative to Brownian diffusion models, with empirical evidence suggesting improved sampling and better modeling of heavy-tailed data. Yet theoretical guarantees for these models remain limited. We develop a non-asymptotic convergence analysis for scale-preserving $\alpha$-stable generative dynamics, covering both compactly supported and power-law targets. In p-Wasserstein distance, we quantify the effects of early stopping, initialization, score approximation, and time discretization, and show exponential decay of the initialization error. A comparison with Brownian dynamics reveals that global Wasserstein convergence alone does not fundamentally distinguish the two models: both initialization errors decay exponentially with the forward horizon on the common class of heavy-tailed targets. A sharp separation emerges instead in the tails. At any positive generation time, stable dynamics produces power-law tails with index $\alpha$, whereas Brownian dynamics remains light-tailed. For a target with tail index $\nu$, asymptotically correct extreme-quantile scaling is possible precisely when $\alpha$=$\nu$. These results identify tail-index matching as a principled mechanism behind the ability of stable generative models to capture extreme events.

title: On the Lattice Tilings by Lee Balls: Q-Polynomials, Group-Ring Equations, and a Decision Algorithm
abstract: More than 50 years ago, Golomb and Welch conjectured that no tilings of $\mathbb{Z}^n$ by Lee balls of radius $r$ exist for $n \geq 3$ and $r \geq 2$. This conjecture remains open even under the additional assumption that the tiling is a lattice tiling. In general, there are two known effective approaches to the lattice case which are based on symmetric polynomials and on the arithmetic of group-ring equations, respectively. In this paper, we develop both approaches. First, we determine all coefficients of the Q-polynomials associated with Lee balls; previously, only leading coefficients and certain special cases were known. Second, for arbitrary radii, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of lattice tilings by Lee balls in terms of group-ring equations, extending earlier results for radii $r=2$ and $3$. We then derive new necessary conditions for such tilings. For every radius $3\le r\le 50$, we prove that the set of dimensions for which no lattice tiling exists has positive density in \(\mathbb{Z}^+\). We also give an algorithm that combines the available necessary conditions and apply it to all pairs $(n,r)$ for which the corresponding Lee ball of radius $r$ and dimension $n$ has size less than $2^{30}$. Among these $1{,}358$ pairs, the combined method excludes $1{,}356$, leaving only $(n,r)=(35,3)$ and $(805,3)$.

title: Free-Material Optimization in a Peridynamic World
abstract: We study free-material optimization for nonlinear bond-based nonlocal diffusion and its localization as the interaction horizon $\delta$ vanishes. Bond conductivities are subject to pointwise bounds and a global material budget constraint. After normalization, the asymptotic behavior of these problems is governed by the fraction $\theta_\delta$ of potentially active bonds that can be assigned the maximal conductivity. We identify three distinct limiting regimes. If $\theta_\delta\to0$, the normalized optimal values converge to those of the classical vanishing-material optimal design problem, equivalently formulated as a Lipschitz-constrained state problem or a measure-valued flux problem. For $\theta_\delta\to\theta\in(0,1)$, we obtain a directional local free-material problem governed by the upper tail of the directional $p$-strain over position-direction space. Thus the state variable localizes, while the limiting constitutive law retains an internal directional variable inherited from the bonds. If $\theta_\delta\to\theta\geq1$, the limit is the isotropic local $p$-Dirichlet problem. A convex minimax argument eliminates the normalized conductivity variable exactly, after which the analysis combines convex duality, nonlocal compactness, and $\Gamma$-convergence for convex integrands. We prove a unified $\Gamma$-convergence result for the reduced state energies whenever $\theta_\delta\to\theta\in[0,+\infty)$, yielding convergence of normalized optimal values and compactness and identification of optimal states throughout the full parameter range. At the vanishing-material endpoint, we additionally recover optimal measure-valued local fluxes from optimal nonlocal two-point fluxes.

title: Computational compressive imaging reconstruction with a simulated-annealing-based Ising solver
abstract: Computational compressive imaging, such as single-pixel imaging and lensless imaging, is a promising imaging technique, enabling the reconstruction of objects from under-sampled measurements through compressed sensing algorithms or deep learning methods. However, the demand for electronic computational resources grows rapidly when recovering high-resolution and multi-dimensional images and training neural networks with numerous parameters, which has become a bottleneck for the widespread adoption of this technique. Here, we propose a physics-driven reconstruction framework that formulates imaging inverse problems as Ising models and directly recovers target objects through the self-evolution of non-von Neumann Ising machines toward the ground state of the Hamiltonian. We employ a simulated-annealing-based Ising solver to demonstrate this proof-of-concept by reconstructing objects in both single-pixel imaging and a lensless diffuser camera at sampling rates ranging from 1% to 25%. By further incorporating a foreground-sparsity constraint and a smoothness constraint, the reconstruction quality of our method is comparable to or even better than that of mainstream algorithms. This approach has the potential to substantially reduce the electronic computational burden of inverse reconstruction, paving the way for real-time, low-power computational imaging.

title: Joint Identification, Transmission, and Sensing over State-Dependent Channels with Noiseless Feedback
abstract: We consider a discrete memoryless state-dependent channel with noiseless feedback, where the transmitter uses randomized encoding to jointly perform message transmission, identification, and state sensing. In this setting, the transmitter sends a conventional transmission message and an identification message while estimating the unknown channel state sequence under an average distortion constraint. We establish a single-letter characterization of the randomized identification-transmission-sensing capacity-distortion region. The result reveals a single-letter separation structure: the communication rates are determined by the averaged channel, subject to the sensing-induced constraint on admissible input distributions. Specifically, the transmission rate is characterized by mutual information, while the identification rate is characterized by output entropy under the same distortion constraint. The achievability proof combines constant-composition transmission coding, output partitioning, and combinatorial identification coding, while the converse follows from an averaged-channel reduction, distortion lower bounds, and feedback-identification converse arguments.

title: Drift and joint minimal displacement for groups acting on hyperbolic spaces
abstract: We obtain a uniform lower bound for the drift of random walks on hyperbolic spaces in terms of joint minimal displacement. Our main theorem applies to weakly acylindrical actions on Gromov-hyperbolic spaces and is quantitative in all relevant constants. For discrete isometry groups of Hadamard manifolds with pinched negative curvature, the required assumptions are automatically satisfied by the Margulis lemma. This yields uniform gaps at zero in drift spectra for pinched negatively curved Hadamard manifolds, hyperbolic groups, and mapping class groups acting on curve graphs.

title: The volume of foliated surfaces with geometric genus one
abstract: We prove the sharp volume bound $\mathrm{vol}(\mathcal{F})\ge 1/6$ for complex foliated surfaces of general type with positive geometric genus. We also study the equality case and apply the bound to the algebraic integrability and finiteness of small volumes on irregular surfaces.
comments: 26 pages. Comments and suggestions are welcome

title: Spectral truncations of SU(2) and the spectral localizer
abstract: We study operator systems arising from Peter-Weyl and Dirac spectral truncations of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ in the sense of Connes-Van Suijlekom. We determine operator system invariants for these systems, including the $C^*$-envelope and uniform bounds on the propagation number. For Peter-Weyl truncations, we find $\mathrm{prop} \leq 2$ for all connected compact Lie groups, generalizing known results for the torus. We also carry out an analysis of the spectral localizer by Loring and Schulz-Baldes on $\mathrm{SU}(2)$. In this analysis, we find numerical evidence that an index map for operator systems previously proposed by Van Suijlekom only captures the right information in a suitable interval of the parameter $\kappa$, instead of the limit $\kappa \downarrow 0$.

title: Smooth periodic extensions by extrapolation and blending for FFT-based differentiation
abstract: Non-periodic functions on closed intervals are extended into sufficiently smooth periodic functions through a continuous Hermite interpolation framework with necessary and sufficient endpoint conditions, using smooth blend-to-zero operators and short extrapolation recurrences. A matrix-free method is introduced for generating these smooth periodic extensions on the fly directly from function values at equidistant points. No precomputed continuation operator or auxiliary basis construction is required. The resulting extensions can then be used for FFT-based differentiation of non-periodic functions. Numerical tests are provided to show the effectiveness of the method, including for the highly accurate solution of a 1D linear advection equation.

title: On several judicious partitioning problems of graphs and hypergraphs
abstract: Judicious partition problems ask for vertex partitions of graphs or hypergraphs that optimize several quantities simultaneously. In this paper, we investigate judicious partitions of graphs and hypergraphs in which each class meets many edges and establish the following results. (1) Every hypergraph with nonnegative edge weights and all edges of size at most $2$ has a bipartition in which each vertex class meets edges of total weight at least $(w_1-\Delta_1)/2+2w_2/3$, where $w_i$ is the total weight of the edges of size $i$, and $\Delta_1$ is the maximum weight of an edge of size $1$. (2) Every hypergraph with all edges of size at most $3$ has a bipartition in which each vertex class meets at least $m_1/2+3m_2/4+7m_3/8+o(m_1+m_2+m_3)$ edges, where $m_i$ is the number of edges of size $i$. (3) For any integer $k\ge4$, every graph with $m\ge2(k-1)(k-2)$ edges has a partition into $k$ classes, each meeting at least $2m/(2k-1)$ edges. Both the coefficient of $m$ and the edge threshold are best possible. (4) For all sufficiently large $m$, every $4$-uniform hypergraph with $m$ edges has a partition into four classes, each meeting at least $4m/7$ edges. The first three statements are conjectures of Bollob\'as and Scott, and the last is a conjecture of Bollob\'as and Thomason on 4-uniform hypergraphs. All of the above results are best possible.

title: Stability of the P_2 semi-Lagrangian scheme
abstract: Among the various space interpolation operators used in high-order semi-Lagrangian schemes, the case of finite element interpolation presents a somewhat incomplete stability theory, partly due to the impossibility of applying in a standard form the framework of Von Neumann analysis, even in the constant coefficient case. In this work, the stability of the P_2 semi-Lagrangian scheme is stated in the case of the constant coefficient equation on a uniform mesh, using a suitable extension of the Von Neumann technique to treat block circulant matrices.

title: Finite volume quotients of bounded domains with piecewise smooth boundary
