This demonstrates that the absence of magic is accompanied by the absence of type III factors in the local algebras, therefore prohibiting the appearance of a quantum field theory. Second, for the hyperfinite factors of Araki, Woods and Powers, we prove a quantitative equivalence: The limiting factor is of type III if and only if the locally optimized min-relative entropy of magic diverges. This divergence is necessary to generate the continuous spectrum associated to a type III factor. Thus, in this setting, the emergence of a type III factor requires not merely the presence of magic, but an infinite amount of it. These results provide a rigorous setting supporting the proposal that infinite magic is a necessary structural ingredient for the emergence of a relativistic continuum from lattice systems.

title: Mixed moment and joint non-vanishing of $\mathrm{GL}(3)\times\mathrm{GL}(1)$ and $\mathrm{GL}(1)$ $L$-functions
abstract: In this article, we study the mixed-moment problem for the product of central values of two $L$-functions twisted by a Dirichlet character of large conductor $q$. Precisely, for a fixed $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ Hecke-Maass cusp form $\pi$, we asymptotically evaluate the first moment, with $\textit{power-saving}$ error term for the product of central $L$-values $L(1/2, \pi\times\chi)\overline{L(1/2, \chi)}$ averaged over the $\textit{full family}$ $\{\chi\,(\mathrm{mod}\,{q}): Q\leq q\leq 2Q\}$ of primitive Dirichlet characters modulo $q$. And as a consequence, we also established the simultaneous non-vanishing of the aforementioned central $L$-values.

title: Precise Asymptotics for Dense High-Dimensional Huber Regression under Heteroscedasticity
abstract: We study Huber regression in a heteroscedastic linear model in the proportional regime $n/p \to \delta \in (1, \infty)$. Our main result is an exact characterization of the asymptotic empirical distribution of the Huber estimator. This characterization is in terms of three scalar parameters which determine the first-order centre and the asymptotic variance of the Huber estimator. The result shows that with heteroscedastic noise, the first-order centre may contain an additional component along the variance index coefficient. We derive the displacement coefficients that determine this centre, as well as the exact asymptotic variance. The analysis uses the matrix approximate message passing (AMP) framework to jointly track the regression and variance index coefficients, extending the existing framework for homoscedastic M-estimators. We illustrate the implications of this characterization by constructing a test for centre displacement and examining its empirical size and power through simulations.

title: Weighted Fourier capacities and Frostman restriction estimates
abstract: We study a weighted Fourier capacity attached to compact sets, $ c_{p,k}(K)=\inf\left\{\|k\widehat u\|_{L^p(\mathbb{R}^d)}:u\in C_0^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d),\ u\geq 1 \text{ on } K\right\},$ where $k$ is a positive tempered weight. The paper develops complementary upper and lower estimates for this quantity. The upper bounds are obtained from Frostman data, Fourier restriction estimates, and Bessel-potential majorants, which together provide admissible smooth majorants of the compact set. The lower bounds follow from a dual testing argument against positive measures supported on $K$, yielding estimates in terms of the weighted $L^{p'}$ size of their Fourier transforms. For sets of positive Lebesgue measure, testing with $\chi_K\,\mathrm{d}x$ connects the capacity with the weighted integrability of $\widehat{\chi_K}$. A Lebedev-type Sobolev criterion then gives non-triviality ranges governed by the upper Minkowski dimension of $\partial K$ and the growth of the weight. We also record consequences for Ahlfors-David regular sets and positive-measure Cantor-type examples.

title: Nilpotent Deformation Theory via Ultrasolid Algebra
abstract: Deformation theory studies how varieties and other algebro-geometric objects vary in families. A central part of the subject is formal deformation theory, where one deforms over an Artinian base; such deformation problems are governed by Lie algebraic models. We pose the question of deforming varieties over nilpotent but not necessarily Artinian bases. These turn out to be classified by the same Lie algebraic models plus some topological structure. More precisely, we will consider partition Lie algebroids in the category of ultrasolid modules, a variation of the solid modules of Clausen and Scholze that give a well-behaved category akin to topological modules. To approach this result, we decompose deformation problems into n-nilpotent layers. Each of these layers is individually easier to understand, and is classified by simpler variants of partition Lie algebras.

title: Two Short Proofs of the $A^A$ Theorem
abstract: In 1984, D.~Duffus asked whether $A^A\cong B^B$ implies $A\cong B$ for finite, nonempty ordered sets $A$ and~$B$. J.\,D. Farley and the author proved that it does. In this paper, we give two short proofs using all intervals of maximum height and the elements with exactly one lower cover. The first proof averages over these intervals; the second takes their disjoint sum and constructs three invariants. Both avoid the auxiliary ordering, direct factorization, and canonical coordinates of the earlier proof.

title: The $A^A$ problem for finite ordered sets
abstract: For ordered sets $X$ and $Y$, let $Y^X$ denote the ordered set of order-preserving maps from $X$ to $Y$, ordered pointwise. In 1984, D. Duffus asked whether $A^A\cong B^B$ forces $A\cong B$ when $A$ and $B$ are finite ordered sets. We prove that it does. The proof combines direct decompositions with an auxiliary ordering of connected ordered sets and a careful choice of intervals of maximum height. We then extend the reconstruction result to several forms of repeated exponentiation.

title: Linear Independence of Polynomial Compositions with Bounded Input Degree
abstract: We prove the weak composition-independence conjectures of Kohn, Marchetti, Massarenti and Mella. The proof uses deformations of rational curves and a single kernel of the linearized equation. Riemann-Roch gives a contradiction from tangent fields with controlled poles. By settling these conjectures, we prove that a neural network with a general polynomial activation function of sufficiently large degree is identifiable.

title: A nonstandard fractional Jacobi pseudospectral method for weakly regular right-sided Caputo terminal problems
abstract: Right-sided fractional differential equations arising in terminal value problems present substantial analytical and numerical challenges due to their intrinsic nonlocal structure and the presence of weak algebraic-type singularities near the terminal point. These singular behaviors significantly degrade the performance of classical finite-difference, finite-element, and standard spectral methods, which typically rely on smoothness assumptions that break down in the fractional setting. In this work, we develop a comprehensive fractional pseudospectral framework specifically designed for nonlinear right-sided Caputo terminal value systems. The proposed method employs a versatile family of nonstandard fractional Jacobi basis functions whose endpoint-weighted structure naturally reflects the asymptotic behavior of right-sided fractional operators. This construction enables the accurate approximation of solutions with limited regularity near the terminal point, without requiring smoothing transformations or mesh grading. We establish the existence and uniqueness of the discrete numerical solution and derive rigorous convergence estimates that faithfully capture the inherent singularity structure of the problem. A series of numerical experiments validates the theoretical developments and demonstrates that the proposed approach delivers high-order accuracy and superior resolution of terminal-layer behavior compared with traditional spectral techniques. The resulting framework provides an efficient and reliable computational tool for challenging nonlinear fractional terminal value systems characterized by weak solution regularity.
comments: Subitted to Applied Mathematics and Computation 8th January 2026

title: Analog RF Computing for Integrated Data and AI Flows Over Wireless Networks
abstract: Many resource-constrained edge devices require artificial intelligence (AI) services but are not powerful enough to store or execute neural networks (NNs). Analog radio frequency (RF) computing addresses this limitation by letting a base station (BS) multicast a waveform encoding NN weights to different clients. Each client then multiplies the received weight-encoded waveform with its locally generated input-encoded waveform through a passive mixer in its RF frontend, thereby realizing the matrix-vector multiplications (MVMs) needed for AI inference with an extremely low power and memory requirement. This can enable telecom operators to provide AI inference services to the edge devices connected to their networks. In practice, however, this multicast AI flow must share the spectrum, power, and spatial resources with other data flows. This paper considers a multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) downlink scenario and studies the resulting relative aggregate data rate reduction from integrating the multicast AI flow with the unicast data flows. We formulate a joint beamforming problem for the data and AI flows to maximize the aggregate data rate subject to computing accuracy, client energy, total power, and hardware-related constraints. We develop a weighted minimum mean-square error (WMMSE)-based algorithm to solve the problem. Numerical results based on 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) channels show that the relative aggregate data rate reduction from integrating an AI flow with data flows is below 5% in representative settings. This indicates that telecom operators can use analog RF computing to provide edge AI services while providing data communication services simultaneously.
comments: We take a step toward wireless networks that can compute as well as communicate, using analog RF computing to deliver AI inference to resource-constrained edge devices while simultaneously serving conventional data transmission. This is a follow-up to our analog RF computing framework: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14331. To be presented at IEEE Globecom 2026

title: Directional Coefficient Inequalities for Strongly Starlike Mappings in Complex Banach Spaces
abstract: We study a class of strongly starlike mappings of order $\alpha$ on the open unit ball of a complex Banach space under a scalar-profile condition. Using a slice reduction along one-dimensional complex subspaces, we prove a coefficient correspondence theorem identifying the directional coefficients with the Taylor coefficients of an associated one-variable strongly starlike function. We further prove a lifting theorem showing that every one-variable strongly starlike function can be realized by a scalar-profile Banach-space mapping. Consequently, the extremal problems for polynomial directional coefficient functionals coincide exactly with their one-variable counterparts. We apply this correspondence to obtain bounds for $|A_2A_3 - A_4|$, $|A_2A_4 - A_3^2|$, and $|A_3 - A_2^2|$, together with the corresponding estimates for $|A_4|$ and $|A_5|$. We also establish a parameterized Fekete--Szeg\H{o} estimate and a sharp bound for the second Hankel determinant of directional logarithmic coefficients.

title: Perfect and peak state transfer on IBM quantum hardware
abstract: We run continuous-time quantum walks with perfect and peak state transfer on a present-day superconducting quantum processor, IBM Quantum's $156$-qubit Heron device ibm_kingston, deliberately without error correction or error mitigation. Perfect state transfer and its relaxations have been studied extensively in algebraic graph theory, where one can prove exactly which graphs move a quantum state from one vertex to another with probability one (or with the largest probability the graph allows, in the case of peak state transfer), and at what time. Our experiments cover perfect state transfer on the hypercubes $Q_2 = C_4$ and $Q_3$, and on the Hamming-weighted paths $\mathrm{HP}_n$, the equitable-partition quotients of the hypercubes $Q_n$, for $n$ up to $20$; peak state transfer on the $X_n$ family for $n$ up to $11$; and, for comparison, moving the state along a path of qubits by a sequence of SWAP gates.

title: $p$-Laplace Serrin problem on planar annuli
abstract: We prove a rigidity result for the problem $\Delta_p u=-2$ defined on a ring-shaped domain in $\mathbb{R}^2$, when homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions are imposed and $p\in(1,2)$. This problem admits a natural physical interpretation, as it describes the steady laminar flow of a generalised Newtonian fluid exhibiting shear-thinning behaviour. Our symmetry result is obtained assuming that the set of maximum points, denoted by $\Sigma$, is a smooth closed curve, and there are no other critical points outside it; moreover, an appropriate asymptotic expansion of the solution near $\Sigma$ is required. Although our approach is inspired by the comparison strategy of [arXiv:2505.04458], the main ingredients used there are intrinsically linear and have no direct counterparts for the $p$-Laplacian. This requires the introduction of new ideas and techniques.

title: Nonproduct Minimal Submanifolds with Cylindrical Tangent Cones
abstract: This article constructs, via perturbation methods, infinite-dimensional families of non-product minimal submanifolds which have singular sets locally modeled on cylindrical tangent cones. This answers a question raised by Leon Simon in the 1980s, and generalizes work Caffarelli-Hardt-Simon, who treated the case of isolated singularities. This setting requires substantially more work, however, since the natural obstruction space for the problem is infinite dimensional and the map which is meant to compensate for this obstruction using deformations of the singular set exhibits a loss of regularity. This necessitates working in the category of tame Frechet spaces and using the Nash-Moser Implicit Function Theorem.
comments: 52 pages, comments welcome. Companion article to appear soon

title: Third-moment cancellation and predictable representation in finite-state BSDE approximation
abstract: We study finite-state approximations of Brownian-driven Markovian backward stochastic differential equations when the same one-step increment is used both for weak propagation and for martingale representation. For a centered isotropic state-independent increment with vanishing third moment, we prove first-order convergence of the Markov value field, its spatial gradient, and the predictable $Z$-field under suitable smoothness assumptions. The corresponding orthogonal martingale has maximal $L^2$ size $O(h^{1/2})$. We identify its quadratic representation defect and prove a joint functional limit theorem for the state process and the normalized orthogonal martingale, which in particular yields a mixed-normal terminal limit with path-dependent conditional variance. On the trace-free quadratic sector, the representation defect has the sharp universal operator lower bound $d/[2(d+2)]$; equality holds exactly for normalized laws that are weighted spherical 4-designs. In dimension $d\geq 2$, vanishing third moment is incompatible with exact scalar one-step predictable representation for any finite-state centered isotropic increment. Consequently, every such exact-representation law has a nonzero cubic direction, and a smooth Fourier terminal condition converts this direction into a sharp global $h^{1/2}$ weak error. For the centrally symmetric regular-simplex rule we also identify the leading quadratic GKW component, compute the exact first-order asymptotic of the accumulated orthogonal-martingale variance, and recover it from the general functional limit. Thus the same third-order tensor links weak accuracy and predictable representation, yielding an accuracy-representation tradeoff for finite-state BSDE approximations.

title: Commutative rings with square-difference factor absorbing factorization
abstract: We introduce and study sdf-absorbing factorization rings (SAF-rings), in which every regular ideal is a finite product of square-difference factor absorbing ideals. We investigate their behavior under direct products, localizations, factor rings, and module idealizations, and establish connections with SP-rings, Dedekind rings, and N-rings. We also introduce strongly sdf-absorbing factorization rings (SSAF-rings), relate them to SSP-rings and almost multiplication rings, and prove that the Noetherian SSAF-rings are precisely the ZPI-rings. Applications to module idealizations and monoid rings are also presented.

title: $L^\infty$-regularity thresholds for a generalized Gross-Pitaevskii equation: dispersive blow-up vs. nonlinear stability
abstract: We study a generalized Gross-Pitaevskii equation arising in the mean-field description of exciton-polariton Bose-Einstein condensates. The dynamics close to macroscopic wave functions $r_0e^{i\omega_0 t +ik_0x}$ is governed by a stabilizing relaxation mechanism without suppressing dispersive blow-up. We show that this competition yields $L^\infty$-regularity thresholds. More precisely, we construct solutions for which arbitrarily small perturbations from $C^4_b$ can develop finite time blow-up in $C^3_b$ whereas perturbations from $C^{4+\eta}_b$ for every $\eta>0$, satisfy a global-in-time $C^3_b$-stability estimate. The stability analysis is carried out in modulation spaces $M_{\infty,1}^k$.

title: Path Covering Spaces of Posets
abstract: In this paper we extend results concerning a kind of covering space for finite posets that bears some analogy to the topological theory of covering spaces. Previous work focused on ranked, locally-finite posets with a unique minimal element. In this previous work the notion of a covering space based on preservation of path weights was defined, and it was shown that, given a poset, there is a unique universal covering space which has an explicit description. Numerous examples of combinatorially significant posets and their universal covers were explored. In this paper we consider finite posets that have a unique minimal element, but that need not be ranked. We give a combinatorial description of these covering spaces, which we call path covers. We then show these covers naturally form a supersolvable lattice and deduce some of its properties. Finally, we investigate an analogue of deck transformations and give some results relating these transformations, poset automorphisms, and the automorphisms of the lattice of path covers.

title: Radiation Conditions and Uniqueness Theorems for Open Wave-guide Networks
abstract: We state radiation conditions and prove a variety of uniqueness theorem for models of wave-guide networks, including acoustic wave-guide networks, and electromagnetic wave-guide networks described by the time harmonic Maxwell equations. To analyze Maxwell wave-guide networks we need to establish generalizations of the Mourre estimates from [29, 32].

title: Learning Warm Starts for the Simplex Method from Measured Solver Cost
abstract: Learned warm starts for the simplex method build starting bases using predictions of which variables will be basic at optimality. Prior work has shown that starting bases predicted by graph neural networks can sharply reduce iteration counts, but the time saved may fall well short of the iterations saved. On 25 classes of linear programs (LPs), we find that a strong supervised basis predictor removes two thirds of the dual simplex's iterations but only a third of its time. Two effects explain the gap: the iterations removed by a good start tend to be cheap, and closeness to an optimal basis does not rank starts by cost. We prove that two starts with equal overlap with an optimal basis and equal pivot counts can differ in linear-algebra work by a factor that grows with the square root of the number of rows. Empirically, across the starts of one LP, the pivot count explains 71% of the variance of log solve time, while the CPU instruction count explains 98.5%. We introduce CostStart, which uses supervised prediction for the basis and trains a small policy on measured instruction counts to choose, per LP, how many predicted columns to use, which algorithm and pricing rule to run, and whether to warm-start at all. On unseen LPs of the training classes, including LPs four times the training size, CostStart roughly halves the solve time relative to the solver's default start and is 1.4 to 2.2 times as fast as two published methods retrained on the same data.

title: Stochastic Gradient Descent: A Nonlinear Time Series Perspective
abstract: This paper investigates the statistical behavior of Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) with constant step size under the framework of iterated random functions. Compared to previous studies establishing the convergence of SGD in probability measure, e.g., Wasserstein distance, our approach directly provides the convergence in Euclidean distance by showing the Geometric Moment Contraction (GMC) of SGD. This new convergence can address the non-stationarity of SGD due to fixed initial points and can provide a more refined asymptotic analysis of SGD. Specifically, we prove quenched central limit theorem, invariance principle and $\alpha$-stable convergence for averaged SGD (ASGD) regardless of initialization. Furthermore, we provide a novel perspective to understand the impact of step sizes in SGD by studying its derivative with respect to the step size. The existence of stationary solutions for the derivative processes is shown, enabling the use of interpolation to recover the full-trajectory of SGD. Subsequently, we utilize multiple step sizes and show an enhanced Richardson-Romberg extrapolation with improved bias representation, which brings ASGD estimates closer to the global optimum. Finally, we propose a new online inference method and a bias-reduced variant for the extrapolated ASGD. Empirical confidence intervals are constructed and the coverage probabilities approach the nominal level as $n$ grows.

title: The Q-process for the general mother-dependent multitype branching process
abstract: The general mother-dependent neutral mutations model is a multitype branching process describing a population evolving in discrete time, in which mutations occur among a finite set of alleles: each mutant, independently of the others, acquires an allele different from its mother's, according to a prescribed distribution. We study the associated mutant and clone-mutant chains conditioned on extinction in the distant future, that is, their $Q$-processes, and we give an explicit description of their laws in the (sub)critical and in the supercritical regimes alike. Even under this conditioning, the clone-mutant process associated with the mother-dependent neutral mutations model is obtained from the corresponding infinite-alleles BGW process (studied in Bertoin (2010) and Blancas and Rivero (2018)) by an independent multinomial colouring with specific parameters. We also obtain the spine decomposition of the multitype mutant chain, from which we derive a Kesten--Stigum theorem in the supercritical regime and a genealogical construction of the Q-process in the (sub)critical one.

title: Ehrhart Polynomials of Triangles in $\mathbb{R}^3$
abstract: We present two ways of constructing Ehrhart polynomials corresponding to certain triangles in $\mathbb{R}^3$. One of our methods employs Popoviciu's Theorem, while the other method uses a version of Pick's Theorem adapted to rank-2 lattices in $\mathbb{R}^3$. We then apply our methods to linear Diophantine equations of the form $ax+by+cz=n$ and develop upper and lower bounds on the number of solutions in nonnegative integers $x$, $y$, and $z$. The bounds we develop are closed form quasi-polynomials, and the difference between them is bounded by a constant depending only on $a$ and $b$. As an application, we prove that the $k$th Frobenius number exists for any triple of positive integers and any $k$.

title: Co-designing a Layered Control Architecture
abstract: Layered control architectures (LCAs) are ubiquitous in complex engineering systems. However, in practice they are largely designed ad hoc and mostly dictated by the experience of the designer. This is because there is currently no systematic and practically applicable theory available to holistically design LCAs. Hence, systematically reasoning about the optimality, stability, and feasibility of the LCA design is not possible. We set a first step toward such a theory by presenting a framework for co-designing a two-layer LCA for a linear time-invariant plant. The resulting co-design problem optimizes over architectural design variables (e.g., reduced order model dimension and sampling ratio between the layers) and tuning-based design variables (e.g., the numerical values of the feedback gain or the matrices of the reduced order model), all subject to constraints that ensure stability, feasibility, and compute properties of the closed-loop LCA. The proposed formulation allows to make informed tradeoffs along the Pareto front traced over different axes of optimality, e.g., speed, accuracy or computational effort. We demonstrate the effect of making various tradeoffs in a simple numerical example.

title: The $(n-1)$-linear restriction estimate in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with degenerate curvature
abstract: We revisit the $(n-1)$-linear restriction estimate in $\mathbb{R}^n$ proved by the first author in \cite{Be-6} and refine the result in the case when the curvature assumptions contain small parameters. The standard $L^p$ estimate is replaced by a more complex norm/quasi-norm of type $\ell^p L^\frac{2}{n-2}$ which reflects the geometry of wave packet propagation and the degenerate curvature assumptions. The primary motivation for this work stems from a concrete application to the study of the quadratic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation in $\mathbb{R}^{3+1}$, which is done in a companion paper \cite{BeBoCh}.

title: Equality of the Jellium and the Uniform Electron Gas Energies
abstract: Jellium, a system of electrons in a uniform neutralizing background, and the uniform electron gas (UEG), a system of electrons with constant density and no background, are two standard models of the electron gas. We prove that the ground-state energy per unit volume of Jellium, as defined by Lieb and Narnhofer, coincides with the UEG energy defined by Lewin, Lieb and Seiringer, i.e. \[ e^\hbar_{\rm Jel}(\rho_0)=e^\hbar_{\rm UEG}(\rho_0). \] This equality was previously established in the classical case by Lewin, Lieb and Seiringer and independently by Cotar and Petrache.
comments: GitHub repo with Lean formalization: https://github.com/xyzw/jellium_ueg

title: Symplectic groupoid multiplication and Poisson integrators
abstract: In this paper, we study the role of local symplectic groupoid multiplication in the construction of approximation methods for Hamiltonian flows on the underlying Poisson manifold. We show it can be used to construct a novel multiplicative type of approximating sequences for the relevant Lagrangian bisection. We describe the corresponding theoretical results, their practical implementation into approximation methods on coordinate charts via generating functions, and illustrative examples.

title: Canonical Kummerian Kernels in 1-Smooth Pro-$p$ Poincar\'e Duality Groups of Dimension Three
abstract: Let $(G,\theta)$ be a finitely generated 1-smooth oriented pro-$p$ group with torsion-free orientation, and suppose that $G$ is a Poincar\'e duality pro-$p$ group of dimension three. The orientation determines a canonical closed normal subgroup $K_\theta(G)$ contained in the Frattini subgroup, and for a Kummerian pair the quotient $G/K_\theta(G)$ is the maximal $\theta$-abelian quotient. We prove that \[K_\theta(G)\text{ finitely generated} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad K_\theta(G)=1.\] Thus every non-$\theta$-abelian 1-smooth $\textrm{PD}^3$ pro-$p$ group has an infinitely generated canonical kernel, where ``infinitely generated'' means not topologically finitely generated. The proof combines the normal-subgroup theorem for pro-$p$ $\textrm{PD}^3$ groups with the classification of $p$-adic analytic 1-smooth pro-$p$ groups. We also obtain a cohomological description of the canonical extension from the Hochschild--Serre five-term sequence and Poincar\'e duality. Writing $K=K_\theta(G)$, $Q=G/K$, and $V=H^1(G,\mathbb{F}_p)$, we identify $H^1(K,\mathbb{F}_p)^Q$ with the kernel of the map $\bigwedge^2V\to V^*$ induced by the triple cup-product form of $G$. Consequently, whenever $K\neq1$, its first cohomology is infinite-dimensional, whereas its $Q$-invariant subspace is nonzero and finite-dimensional. We obtain exact dimension restrictions in small generator ranks and show that a non-$\theta$-abelian group with $2\leq d(G)\leq4$ is not Bloch--Kato. In the finitely generated-kernel case, $G$ is a three-dimensional uniform $\theta$-abelian group with exterior mod-$p$ cohomology.

title: Infinite-variation L\'evy processes are either strongly eroded or abrupt
abstract: We prove that every real L\'evy process of infinite variation is either abrupt or strongly eroded, resolving the conjectured geometric dichotomy on the smoothness of the convex hull of the graph of a L\'evy path [Ann. Inst. H. Poincar\'e Probab. Stat. 60(4) (2024), 2352-2381]. We give counterexamples to the stronger point-hitting conjecture of Vigon. As applications, we classify convex-hull smoothness, Lipschitz-minorant contact sets and Burgers shock geometry.

title: $q_x$-Bass Martingales: Optimality, Existence and Convergence
abstract: We introduce the class of $q_x$-Bass martingales, extending the notion of $q$-Bass martingales. These are martingale couplings with prescribed marginals whose transition kernels are closest to a given family of reference kernels $(q_x)_{x \in \mathbb R^d}$ in the sense of a suitable weak optimal transport problem. We show that $q_x$-Bass martingales are optimizers of this problem and establish a strong duality result. Building on this duality, we introduce an algorithm for their computation and, under compactness assumptions on the prescribed marginals, prove its convergence, thereby establishing existence. We then specialize to one-dimensional marginals and show that the algorithm reduces to a fixed-point iteration.

title: Defining and Generating Compositional Structure
abstract: Compositional structure is pervasive in nature and across scales: atoms combine into molecules, molecules into cells, and cells into organisms, while further compositional hierarchies appear within each level. More broadly, compositionality, the reuse and recombination of parts into novel structures, is a fundamental source of interesting complexity in both natural and artificial systems. Yet despite its importance, and despite our apparent ease in recognizing it, mathematical accounts capturing what we intuitively mean by compositional structure remain limited. Here, we fill this gap by formalizing a simple idea: compositional structure emerges when parts, considered together, reveal shared structure that is not captured when those parts are modeled separately. We express this idea using algorithmic information theory, the mathematics of information and compression, which provides a natural way to identify structure in arbitrary data without specifying in advance what that structure must look like. Applied across scales, our definition informs where and how compositional structure emerges within an object. Using tractable approximations, we then invert the framework to generate compositional objects: we specify the desired form of their compositional structure without prescribing their particular content, and optimize directly over strings and images. The resulting objects exhibit readily recognizable hierarchical reuse and part-whole organization, suggesting that the definition captures compositional structure rather than merely complexity, regularity, or shared information. Finally, we discuss implications for machine learning, including a new perspective on depth in neural architectures and principles for constructing compositional data curricula capable of supporting open-ended learning.

title: Planning to Learn: Real-Time Robust Adaptive Control on the GPU with Guaranteed Future Learning
abstract: Robust adaptive control is vital for keeping robots safe while actively reducing uncertainty in unfamiliar settings. However, traditional methods are often conservative since they fail to account for guaranteed future parameter learning during planning and struggle to scale to high-dimensional systems. In this work, we present A-SLS, a learning-aware robust adaptive model predictive control (RAMPC) framework based on system-level synthesis. A-SLS forecasts future parameter uncertainty and preserves correlations between process disturbances, parameter error, and estimate updates to construct tight, guaranteed reachable sets that account for future information gain. We also develop a GPU-accelerated A-SLS solver to enable real-time performance. Across nonlinear robotic systems, A-SLS reduces reachable-tube conservativeness, maintains real-time performance, and scales to whole-body control for a quadruped with 61 states, 8 uncertain parameters, and 12 control inputs. We further demonstrate the approach on hardware, where a physical Crazyflie drone learns an uncertain dynamics parameter online to stabilize on the fly.

title: On the Diophantine equation $X^2+p^m=p_1^{n_1}p_2^{n_2}$
abstract: We consider the Diophantine equation \[ X^2+p^m=p_1^{n_1}p_2^{n_2}, \] where $p,p_1,p_2$ are distinct odd primes. Using factorizations in quadratic fields, sharp bounds for linear forms in two $p$-adic logarithms, elementary methods, and known results on exponential Diophantine equations, we obtain explicit bounds for $m,n_1,n_2$, and consequently the finiteness of the number of solutions for fixed $p,p_1,p_2$.

title: Resolutions of orbifold generalised triangle groups
abstract: Let $T=\langle f,g\mid f^{l}=g^{m}=W^{n}=1\rangle$ be a generalised triangle group in which $W$ is the Farey word of a rational slope $q=r/s$, and suppose that $T$ is the fundamental group of a hyperbolic $3$-orbifold whose singular locus has no spherical vertices. Let $G=\langle f,g\mid f^{l}=g^{m}=W^{n}\rangle$ be the associated central extension. We compute an explicit free resolution of the trivial module over $\mathbb{Z}G$ of minimal length, with differentials given in closed form by Fox derivatives. From this resolution we deduce an explicit free resolution over $\mathbb{Z}T$ which is $2$-periodic in degrees at least two, and we compute the integral homology and cohomology of both groups. Strebel treated the classical family $q=0/1$ in 1983. Since then only the family $q=1/2$ has been treated, by Ellis and Williams, and for that family our resolution over $\mathbb{Z}T$ has strictly smaller rank in every degree.

title: Factor-Assisted Density Estimation: When Ambient Dimension Enables Oracle Rates
abstract: We study density estimation in the high-dimensional factor model, whose fixed-dimensional latent factors have an unknown smooth density. We propose factor-assisted density estimation (FADE), a non-iterative procedure that applies kernel density estimation to spectral estimates of the latent scores. The score proxies are dependent and do not follow the latent density, so standard kernel-density arguments do not apply. A refined rowwise expansion separates error into a conditionally centered Gaussian perturbation and a uniformly controlled remainder. We show that FADE achieves the oracle rate in sufficiently high ambient dimension and prove a minimax lower bound separating ordinary nonparametric difficulty from a Gaussian deconvolution obstruction. Together, the upper and lower bounds establish rate optimality of FADE in specified high-dimensional regimes. We also derive $L^1$ upper and lower bounds for the induced observation density, distinguishing latent-distribution uncertainty from the cost of estimating a growing number of parameters. These results formalize a blessing of ambient dimension: sufficiently many observed coordinates can make a simple spectral reduction statistically lossless even for the nonparametric task of recovering an unobserved low-dimensional density.

title: Emergence of partially hyperbolic skew-products with circle fibers
abstract: We study the statistical behavior of partially hyperbolic skew-products over Axiom A diffeomorphisms using emergence. Generically, these systems satisfy the Palis conjecture: they have a finite number of physical measures whose basins together have full volume. In particular, for Lebesgue almost every point, the empirical measures converge to one of finitely many physical measures. We study the non-generic case and prove that, even when the sequence of empirical measures may have uncountably many accumulation points, these systems have low emergence.

title: Duality Theory for Sequent Algebras
abstract: Sequent algebras were introduced by D. Vakarelov \cite{VakarelovSequentALg} as a generalization of contact algebras, replacing the binary contact relation with a relation between finite sets of regions and regions. In this paper, we present sequent algebras as Boolean algebras endowed with a finitary closure operator satisfying four conditions. We study the irreducible closed sets of these operators, which coincide with Vakarelov's clans, and use them to develop a topological representation theory for sequent algebras. We introduce the categories of sequent algebras and sequent spaces and establish a dual equivalence between them, as well as a restricted dual equivalence for morphisms preserving the full Boolean structure. We also characterize sequent congruences in terms of positive filters and minimally decreasing closed subsets of the associated sequent spaces. Finally, we show that the category of sequent algebras with sequent homomorphisms is topological over the category of Boolean algebras, obtaining completeness and cocompleteness and a complete lattice structure on the sequent structures over each Boolean algebra.

title: A Coupled Fluid Naghdi Shell Windkessel Model for Pulmonary Artery Banding: Partitioned Numerical Scheme and Parameter Estimation
abstract: We develop a 3D fluid structure interaction model for blood flow through deformable vessels with localized constrictions, motivated by pulmonary artery banding in neonates with congenital heart disease. The model couples incompressible Navier Stokes equations in an Arbitrary Lagrangian Eulerian framework with a Naghdi shell model for the arterial wall and a three element Windkessel model for downstream circulation. The shell describes a 3D cylindrical vessel wall with variable radius and is defined on a 2D reference domain. Its low regularity formulation retains membrane, bending, and transverse shear deformation while requiring only first derivatives of the reference midsurface, accommodating piecewise smooth geometries with discontinuous surface slopes. We derive the coupled variational formulation and develop a non-iterative partitioned scheme with a Robin-type interface condition incorporating arterial wall inertia. For a linearized fixed domain problem, we establish a discrete energy estimate under suitable assumptions. A unscented Kalman filter estimates proximal and distal resistances and compliance from inlet-pressure observations. Numerical experiments demonstrate consistent pressure wave propagation and wall deformation under spatial and temporal refinement. Comparisons of the standard Naghdi shell and a modified, predominantly radial shell model reveal how structural deformation mechanisms affect wave speed and displacement. An idealized pulmonary artery banding example demonstrates the coupled fluid shell Windkessel model with parameter estimation. The framework enables investigation of the hemodynamic and mechanical effects of localized constrictions and their dependence on downstream vascular properties.

title: Statistical Mechanics of Spike Trains: Self-Consistent Activity Ensembles and Phase Transitions
abstract: We introduce a statistical-mechanical framework for spiking neuronal systems in which entire spike trains, defined as spatiotemporal configurations of discrete events, are treated as microstates of the system. Instead of modeling explicit network dynamics, we construct an ensemble over complete spike histories and assign to each configuration an effective energy functional that quantifies its consistency with intrinsic synaptic interactions. This formulation leads to a Boltzmann-like distribution over spike configurations, where an effective temperature captures the influence of external inputs acting as a stochastic drive. Macroscopic states are described in terms of coarse-grained observables, such as population firing-rate densities, and arise from a competition between energetic contributions favoring interaction-consistent spike patterns and entropic contributions favoring spatio-temporal disorder. Within this framework, we primarily characterize the transition between oscillatory and non-oscillatory activity. The non-oscillatory regime contains both broadly distributed, approximately uniform states and temporally localized collapsed states, whereas the oscillatory regime is characterized by repeated activity peaks. These regimes are diagnosed using order parameters derived from the population spike-rate density, including its entropy, temporal localization measures, and autocorrelation-based indicators. To complement the analytical treatment, we perform Monte Carlo simulations that sample the ensemble of admissible spike configurations using a Metropolis-Hastings scheme defined directly on spike trains. The simulations reveal the emergence of the predicted macroscopic regimes and provide a direct sampling-based probe of the free-energy landscape.

title: $\lambda$-geodesic convexity of the squared sliced-Wasserstein distance
abstract: The squared Wasserstein distance with respect to a fixed target measure is not a convex function along Wasserstein geodesics over $\mathbb{R}^d$ when $d\geq 2$. Still, in dimension $d=1$, this function is $2$-geodesically convex. We prove that the square of the sliced-Wasserstein distance (which is a distance constructed averaging one-dimensional Wasserstein distances) is $\lambda$-geodesically convex (possibly with $\lambda \leq 0$) on sets of measures satisfying upper bounds on their density, when the target measure satisfies some given geometric conditions. We also present some consequences of this result in the study of the sliced-Wasserstein flow.

title: Chemotaxis models with signal-dependent sensitivity and a logistic-type source, III: Bifurcation and spike-like solutions
abstract:
This third paper in a series on a parabolic-elliptic chemotaxis model studies bifurcation of positive constant equilibria in one space dimension. We consider $$ \left\{  egin{array}{ll} u_t=\Delta u-\chi_0
abla\cdot\left( rac{u^m}{(1+v)^ eta}
abla vight)+au-bu^{1+\alpha}, & x\in\Omega,\ 0=\Delta v-\mu v+
u u^\gamma, & x\in\Omega,\  rac{\partial u}{\partial n}= rac{\partial v}{\partial n}=0, & x\in\partial\Omega, \end{array} ight. $$ where $\Omega$ is a bounded interval, $\alpha,\gamma,m,\mu,
u>0$, $\chi_0\in\mathbb R$, and $a,b, eta\ge0$. Building on earlier results on global existence, boundedness, persistence, and stabilization, we take $\chi_0$ as the bifurcation parameter and examine the effects of $ eta$ and the domain size on the bifurcation. Center manifold reduction yields a coefficient $ eta_{n_0}$ at a simple bifurcation mode $n_0$ of a positive constant equilibrium. The pitchfork bifurcation is supercritical if $ eta_{n_0}>0$ and subcritical if $ eta_{n_0}<0$. Stronger desensitization raises the sensitivity required for loss of linear stability. Bifurcation may be supercritical for small $ eta$ but is always subcritical for sufficiently large $ eta$. Thus, desensitization makes patterns harder to trigger and favors abrupt rather than continuous emergence. The bifurcation mode increases with domain size, allowing more complex spatial patterns. Under suitable conditions, we prove unbounded continuation of local bifurcation branches. We also show that large-sensitivity stationary sequences satisfying a peak-gap hypothesis develop spike-like profiles. Numerical continuation and time-evolution experiments illustrate the bifurcating branches and spike-like solutions and suggest unbounded continuation and increasingly sharp stationary profiles.

title: Two-Stage Score Estimation for Group-Specific Diffusion Models
abstract: Generative modeling across related distributions raises a question: how can shared structure support accurate generation for a target distribution with limited observations? We develop a statistical framework for diffusion transfer that analyzes a shared pooled score together with a target-specific offset. Under Besov regularity of the pooled density and a stable hierarchical composition model for the offset, we derive convergence rates that separate the costs of learning these components and identify when a simpler offset yields a faster risk-bound rate than separate fitting. Under suitable boundary and regularity assumptions, we prove that the offset remains bounded and jointly regular as diffusion time approaches zero. These results allow the lower time cutoff to vanish polynomially and provide total-variation guarantees for diffusion models as density estimators. Synthetic simulations and image benchmarks provide a proof of concept for the framework.

title: Competitive displacement in the grass-bushes-trees process on a scale-free network
abstract: The grass-bushes-trees process is a two-type contact process in which the types face asymmetric birth mechanisms. Vertices of a graph can either be occupied by a tree, occupied by a bush, or empty (containing grass). The trees die with rate $1$ and give birth with rate $\lambda_{\mathcal T}$ on any neighbouring vertex (possibly taking the place of a bush). Bushes die with rate $1$ and give birth with rate $\lambda_{\mathcal B}$ on any empty neighbouring vertex; in particular, they are forbidden from taking the place of trees. We study this process on a power law random graph, namely the erased configuration model. We study which graph parameters lead to the possibility of coexistence versus the necessity of competitive displacement, i.e. joint metastability or fast extinction of the bushes.

title: Quantitative Volume Estimate on Singular Sets of One-phase Free Boundary Problems in Ricci Limit Spaces
abstract: We study limit solutions of the one-phase free boundary problem on noncollapsed Ricci limit spaces. We introduce a quantitative stratification $\mathcal{S}^k_{\varepsilon,r}$ of the singular set of the free boundary that simultaneously captures the approximate splitting of the ambient space and the approximate homogeneity and translational invariance of the solution. We also introduce a new truncated parabolic Weiss quantity that provides quantitative homogeneity via pinching across scales. Although this quantity may not be uniformly bounded across all small scales, it effectively shows that, among the first $j$ scales in a fixed decreasing geometric progression, at most $C\sqrt{j}$ scales fail to exhibit quantitative homogeneity. Such slow growth in $j$ enables us to adapt the covering argument of Cheeger and Naber [arXiv:1103.1819] to show, for every $\eta>0$, a $Cr^{n-k-\eta}$ upper bound for the volume of the $r$-tubular neighborhood of the $k$-th quantitative singular stratum, $\mathcal{S}^k_{\varepsilon,r}$. The same tubular-neighborhood estimate holds for the effective stratum $\mathcal S_\varepsilon^k$, and in particular we get the Minkowski dimension bound $\dim_{\mathcal M} \mathcal S_\varepsilon^k \le k$, from which the previously known sharp bound $\dim_{\mathcal H} \mathrm{Sing} \le n-3$ in Chan, Zhang, and Zhu [arXiv:2112.06962] follows. As another corollary, we prove that the free boundary admits a H\"older manifold structure away from a set of Minkowski dimension at most $n-3$.

title: Normal complex surface singularities with rational homology disk smoothings
abstract: We prove that a normal surface singularity whose minimal good resolution graph has at least two nodes does not admit a rational homology disk smoothing. Together with the earlier graph classifications and the analytic classifications of Fowler and Wahl, this gives a complete classification of normal surface singularities admitting rational homology disk smoothings and proves Wahl's conjecture. The same argument also proves Wahl's Rational Conjecture.

title: Quadratic fields of values of finite solvable groups
abstract: We show that if $G$ is a finite solvable group such that $E = \mathbb Q(\{\chi(g)\, |\, \chi\in{\rm Irr}(G),\ g \in G\})$ is an extension of degree 2 over the rationals, then $E = \mathbb Q(\sqrt{\pm d})$ for a positive integer $d$ all of whose prime divisors lie in $\{2, 3, 5\}$. Moreover, if $G$ has a composition factor of order 7, then either $E = \mathbb Q(\sqrt{2})$ or $E = \mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$. This provides a partial answer to a question of G. Navarro.

title: Automorphisms of twisted Chevalley groups of type ${}^2E_6$ over local rings
abstract: We classify abstract automorphisms of the elementary and full twisted Chevalley groups of type ${}^2E_6$ over commutative local rings with involution and $2$ invertible, for both isogeny types. Every automorphism is standard, with no invertibility assumption on $3$. In the adjoint case, it has a unique expression as a composition of conjugation by an element of the full twisted group and a ring automorphism commuting with the involution. For the simply connected form, the full group equals its elementary subgroup, and the factors are strictly inner, diagonal, and ring automorphisms. The main step replaces a linear change of basis by a group element. Invariant alternating tensors determine the transported Chevalley bracket. We correct this bracket over a faithfully flat local extension and descend the resulting conjugating element by uniqueness. Root-subgroup relations then recover the coefficient automorphism.

title: A Physical-Space Approach to Modified Scattering for the 3D Hartree Equation: Full-Space and Robin Half-Space
abstract: We prove global well-posedness and modified scattering for the three-dimensional Hartree equation for small data in $H^{0,k}$, with $k>\frac12$ on $\mathbb R^3$ and $k=1$ on the half-space $\mathbb R^3_+$ with a real Robin boundary condition. For these data, the nonlinear and asymptotic analysis is carried out entirely in physical space, combining slow-growth estimates for Galilean vector fields with a scale-invariant interaction estimate. For the half-space problem, we construct an extension intertwining the Robin and free flows and a boundary-adapted field that overcome the loss of normal Galilean symmetry.

title: Skew fields of non-commutative meromorphic functions affiliated to finite operator algebras
abstract: We embed skew fields of meromorphic functions in several non-commuting variables into the topological $*-$algebra of closed linear operators affiliated to a finite von Neumann algebra, $\mathfrak{M}$, with faithful, normal tracial state, $\tau$. Namely, let $\mathscr{O} _d (r)$, $r \in (0, +\infty]$, denote the rings of formal power series in $d \in \mathbb{N}$ non-commuting variables with ``radius of convergence" at least $r$ and let $\Xi \in \mathfrak{M} ^{1\times d}$ be a tuple of row-norm $<r$ with the property that there exist no non-zero trace-class operators $T_1, \cdots, T_d \in \mathscr{B} (L^2 (\mathfrak{M}, \tau))$ obeying $\sum _j [T_j , \Xi _j] =0$. Then the unital homomorphism $\mathscr{O} _d (r) \rightarrow \mathfrak{M}$ defined by the evaluation, $\mathfrak{z} _j \mapsto \Xi _j$, extends to an embedding of the universal skew field of fractions of $\mathscr{O} _d (r)$ into the $*-$algebra of closed operators affiliated to $\mathfrak{M}$. In their $L^2-$homology theory of von Neumann algebras, Connes and Shlyakhtenko defined a certain quantity, $0 \leq \Delta (\Xi) \leq d$, as the Murray--von Neumann co-dimension of the Hilbert module generated by all $d-$tuples of finite rank operators obeying the above commutator condition with $\Xi \in \mathfrak{M} ^{1\times d}$. As demonstrated by Mai, Speicher and Yin, this $\Delta$ measures, in a certain precise sense, the algebraic independence of the components of $\Xi$. Connes--Shlyakhtenko proved that $\Delta$ is an upper bound for Voiculescu's non-microstates free entropy dimension, $\delta ^* (\Xi)$, and remark that it is of interest to determine whether these two quantities are equal. Using non-commutative function theory, we show that this is generally not the case, by constructing a triple of self-adjoint operators, $\Xi = (\Xi_1,\Xi_2,\Xi_3)$, for which this inequality is strict, $\delta^*(\Xi) < \Delta(\Xi)$.

title: Zhang twists for semigroups and groupoids, with applications to Steinberg algebras
abstract: Zhang twists provide a powerful mechanism for deforming graded algebras, while preserving their graded module categories. We extend this theory by introducing Zhang twists for graded semigroups and graded ample groupoids. We show that the twisting construction preserves a broad class of semigroup structures, and that two graded monoids are twists of each other if and only if their categories of graded sets are pointedly equivalent. We show that Zhang twists are compatible with noncommutative Stone duality: twists on graded-Boolean inverse semigroups are in correspondence with those on the associated graded ample groupoids. Moreover, in the setting of Steinberg algebras we prove that twisting the groupoid gives the same result as twisting the corresponding algebra. These results provide a unified framework linking graded semigroups, inverse semigroup duality, ample groupoids, and graded algebras, while extending the scope of Zhang twists to settings arising from symbolic dynamics, graph algebras, and Steinberg algebras.

title: Length control for foliations by Jordan curves via smooth quasiconformal maps
abstract: Let $\Omega\subsetneq\mathbb C$ be a non-empty simply connected domain and $0<p<2$. Bouchala and Koskela [Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (2024)] proved that there exists a quasiconformal map $f:\mathbb D\to\Omega$ such that $\int_0^1\ell(f(r S^1))^p\,dr<\infty$, and asked whether this conclusion holds at $p=2$, or even for every $0<p<2+\varepsilon$ with some $\varepsilon>0$. We answer this question affirmatively with $\varepsilon=2/157$ by constructing a single smooth $5$-quasiconformal map $f:\mathbb D\to\Omega$ satisfying this integrability condition simultaneously for every $0<p<2+2/157$.

title: Operator Algebraic Quantum Hypergroups
abstract: We develop a theory of operator algebraic quantum hypergroups and their representations, formulated using a special case of the algebraic quantum hypergroup framework of van Daele and Delvaux. As part of the axioms, every operator algebraic quantum hypergroup admits a dual object of the same type. We prove that a certain universal completion in the compact case satisfies the axioms of an earlier notion of a compact quantum hypergroup in the sense of the second author and Chapovsky. As part of this theory, we discuss their (co)amenability properties. We consider examples induced by conditional expectations of algebraic quantum groups satisfying certain properties, which include quantum hypergroups corresponding to double cosets and automorphisms of quantum groups, and quantum hypergroups induced by representation categories of Kac type compact quantum groups.

title: LWM-TF: A Wireless Foundation Model on 5G NR Time-Frequency Resource Grids
abstract: Received OFDM grids preserve both pilot and payload observations, yet wireless foundation models are rarely pre-trained on them. We introduce LWM-TF, a 9.58M-parameter factorized masked autoencoder pre-trained on complex 5G NR uplink grids taken after the FFT and before channel estimation. Each block attends first across OFDM symbols and then across resource blocks and receive antennas, and the mask follows the same two axes. Because the payload phase is unpredictable, the model reconstructs the normalized log-power of each masked token and predicts its scale separately; ablations show that the two terms are complementary and that this target outperforms complex-signal reconstruction. The encoder is pre-trained on 850,496 physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH) slots from a 10^6-slot dataset simulated with the NR transmit chain under various channel conditions. With the encoder frozen, linear probes classify modulation, predict CRC success, and detect UE mobility. On a separately generated test set, 16 labeled slots per class give 0.85 modulation accuracy, 0.82 CRC area under the ROC curve (AUROC), and 0.73 mobility AUROC, ahead of a supervised CNN on every paired draw. With 10,000 labels the probes reach 0.94, 0.96, and 0.92, well above engineered receiver statistics, and detect mobility where the CNN stays at chance. Without any impairment labels, distances in the frozen feature space flag unseen waveform impairments with 0.78 macro AUROC, against 0.68 for receiver statistics. A single pre-trained encoder thus provides receiver features that transfer across tasks, most strongly when labels are scarce.

title: Measure Theory in Convergence Spaces Part II: Abstract Integration in Net Convergence Structures
abstract: The construction of a coherent and general integration procedure is the central question of this second part of our study of measure theory in convergence spaces. We define, and establish convergence theorems for such process of integration, called the net Riemann integration, in convergence groups and commutative monoids, preserving the prescribed convergence throughout. The underlying interchange theorem admits noncommutative groups and requires right completeness only at the cardinality of the error family. Under intrinsic stability assumptions, countable error control therefore needs only sequential completeness, even for arbitrary integration nets, from which we also stablish a general version of Henstock's lemma. The resulting uniform theorems reaches incomplete ranges in which no complete subspace contains a tail of the approximating integrals. In the ordered locally solid convergence theory side, countability of the inner direction replaces countable accessibility of the approximants, and local existence arguments yield monotone and dominated convergence and, under additional controller assumptions, a further extension through increasing integrable barriers with pointwise coverage and uniformly vanishing excess primitives. This constructs the limiting integral without a common integrable envelope and gives uniform control of primitive variation. We finish with two appendices on new and general results of abstract metrization of net convergences and related topics.

title: Crossing numbers of simplicial complexes
abstract: This paper studies crossing numbers of $d$-dimensional simplicial complexes drawn in $\mathbb R^{2d}$ or $\mathbb S^{2d}$. We clarify and generalize a number of known results and conjectures from the graph case to higher dimensions: the crossing lemma (including the exceptional case of two-dimensional complexes drawn in dimension $4$), a generalized Harary-Hill conjecture (and evidence for it), existence of a midrange crossing constant (in a weak sense), and upper bound constructions based on stochastic geometry (related to Sylvester's problem) and the cyclic polytope. Some of our results are new even in the case of graphs: we give a simple proof of the Harary-Hill conjecture for antipodal drawings, and sharpen the threshold above which the rectilinear and spherical crossing numbers of the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi random graph behave like those of the complete graph.

title: Acceleration and its Limits in Gaussian Variational Inference
abstract: We study whether the classical momentum-based acceleration that improves the condition-number dependence of gradient descent from $\kappa$ to $\sqrt{\kappa}$ for strongly convex, smooth objectives extends to Gaussian variational inference (GVI) for strongly log-concave, log-smooth target distributions. With exact Gaussian expectations, a convex composite formulation of GVI yields the classical accelerated $\sqrt{\kappa}$ convergence rate. However, when only pointwise derivatives are available, we construct a family of strongly log-concave targets for which any randomized algorithm requires $\kappa^{1-o(1)}$ queries to achieve a fixed objective accuracy, even when the initial objective gap is bounded independently of $\kappa$. Thus curvature bounds alone cannot guarantee uniform accelerated total-query complexity. We then ask which additional structure permits acceleration and give positive examples: under a Hessian-Lipschitz assumption, variance-reduced stochastic methods yield accelerated guarantees when the Hessian variation is sufficiently small. Finally, experiments on real datasets show substantial empirical speedups from acceleration across a broad range of methods.

title: Stationarity equations for fractional affine area measures: ellipsoid rigidity and polytopal solutions
abstract: Xi and Zhao established a first variation formula for affine inequalities involving radial mean bodies, and asked two geometric questions about the resulting stationarity equation: whether the bodies already known to satisfy it are the only ones, and whether its smooth solutions are exactly the ellipsoids. We answer both. Every strictly convex solution of the equation with $q>-1$, $q\ne0,n$ is an ellipsoid, which answers the second question affirmatively while replacing smoothness and everywhere positive Gauss curvature by strict convexity. Every full-dimensional facet-transitive polytope satisfies the equation, and so does the polar of every vertex-transitive polytope with respect to its volume centroid; the rhombic dodecahedron, the thirteen Catalan solids and the bipyramids over regular polygons other than the octahedron provide infinitely many affinely inequivalent solutions that are not affine images of regular polytopes or balls, so the answer to the first question is negative. The rigidity proof compares overlap integrals along a continuous Steiner path: stationarity forces an increase of order $o(t)$, whereas a nonaffine chord midpoint function forces an increase of order $t$. For negative parameters the required comparison rests on a minimization formula over bounded measurable auxiliary sets.

title: On the Last-Iterate Convergence of Clipped Gradient Methods
abstract: In stochastic (strongly) convex optimization, establishing last-iterate convergence guarantees for first-order methods has recently garnered increasing attention, as this not only deepens the theoretical understanding of these algorithms but also aligns more closely with practice. Notably, people have demonstrated that one of the most famous, simple, and popular methods, Stochastic Gradient Descent ($\mathtt{SGD}$), provably achieves last-iterate convergence. However, the existing results may have limited applicability, since they typically rely on strong conditions on the gradient noise (e.g., an exponentially decaying tail) rather than the more realistic heavy-tailed noise. Unfortunately, when faced with heavy-tailed noise, $\mathtt{SGD}$ is known to exhibit undesirable behavior or even fail to converge. To address the challenge of heavy-tailed noise, people have proposed $\mathtt{Clipped}\text{-}\mathtt{SGD}$, an algorithm that combines $\mathtt{SGD}$ with a simple mechanism, gradient clipping. Although $\mathtt{Clipped}\text{-}\mathtt{SGD}$ performs well in practice, its last-iterate convergence property remains highly underexplored. In this work, we prove the first optimal last-iterate rates in high probability for $\mathtt{Clipped}\text{-}\mathtt{SGD}$ under heavy-tailed noise, thereby closing a gap in the literature.

title: Efficient Agnostic Learning of Univariate Densities Under Local Differential Privacy
abstract: We propose a general framework for non-interactive locally differentially private (LDP) learning of structured univariate distributions that can be approximated by piece-wise polynomials. This gives the first sample-efficient LDP learners for several distribution classes, including mixtures of log-concave distributions, such as Gaussian mixture models (GMMs). These learners also provide agnostic guarantees and are computationally efficient. We also prove a lower bound for learning GMMs under LDP, improving on the standard pure-DP packing lower bounds of Bun et al. [BKSW19]. To obtain our general learning framework, we develop an efficient non-interactive LDP algorithm for synthetic data generation over large domains, which may be of independent interest. We then use it together with a deterministic adaptation of the non-private piecewise polynomial learner of Acharya et al. [ADLS17].

title: Linear bounds for rich-neighbor edge-colorings
abstract: An edge in a proper edge-coloring is rich if all edges adjacent to it receive pairwise distinct colors. A rich-neighbor edge-coloring is a proper edge-coloring in which every non-isolated edge is adjacent to a rich edge. The rich-neighbor chromatic index $\rn(G)$ is the minimum number of colors in such a coloring. We prove that every loopless multigraph $G$ satisfies $\rn(G)\le3\chi'(G)$, where $\chi'(G)$ is the chromatic index. Exact values are also determined for complete bipartite graphs and complete graphs. For all positive integers $m,n$, $\rn(K_{m,n})=m+n-1$, except that $\rn(K_{2,2})=4$. For $n\ge3$, $\rn(K_n)=2n-3$, except that $\rn(K_4)=6$ and $\rn(K_6)=10$. Moreover, for $n\ge7$, the rich edges in every optimal rich-neighbor edge-coloring of $K_n$ form a star forest.

title: Single generation of transformation group algebras
abstract: We prove that $C(X)\rtimes\Gamma$ is singly generated whenever $\Gamma$ is a finitely generated discrete amenable group and its action on the nonempty compact metrizable space $X$ is free, minimal, and has the uniform Rokhlin property and Cuntz comparison of open sets. In particular, every free minimal $\mathbb Z^d$-crossed product with metrizable underlying space is singly generated.
comments: Preliminary version, 19 pages. The work is carried out using ChatGPT

title: Holomorphy rings and the Nullstellensatz over large fields
abstract: For an infinite field $K$ and an ideal $I\subseteq K[X_1,\dots,X_n]$, let $J(Z_K(I))$ be the ideal of polynomials vanishing on the $K$-rational zero locus of $I$. A Nullstellensatz over $K$ is an algebraic description of this closure operator on ideals. Hilbert's classical theorem provides such a description via the radical of $I$ over any algebraically closed field. In the present article, we introduce a unifying framework for Nullstellens\"atze over arbitrary rings using the notion of an $A$-radical, for $A$ is a subring of $K(X)$ containing $K[X]$. We show that a single canonical holomorphy ring gives a Nullstellensatz over every infinite field, recovering Hilbert's theorem when $K$ is algebraically closed. In addition, we give a new characterization of large fields (in the sense of Pop) via a particular Nullstellensatz: a perfect field is large exactly when the \emph{rational} holomorphy ring $A_n(K)$--the intersection of all $K$-rational places of residue field exactly $K$--satisfies the corresponding Nullstellensatz. Finally we study the order structure of the class of rings $A$ for which the $A$-radical gives a Nullstellensatz. We show that over non-algebraically closed fields this class has no minimal element, showing there is no optimal Nullstellensatz over such fields.

title: Singular wave functions and quantum collapse in inverse-power potentials
abstract: Quantum collapse (QC) occurs under the action of the inverse-power potential U(r)=-U_{0}/(2r^{n}) in the framework of the Schroedinger equation. The corresponding stationary wave functions feature an infinite number of spatial oscillations at $r\rightarrow 0$. The ground state (GS) is missing in the presence of the QC, but the available bound states at finite energies may be physically relevant, as they are normalizable. This work aims to produce singular stationary wave functions. The analytical findings represent an asymptotic form of the stationary wave functions at $r\rightarrow 0$, which fill a continuous spectrum, and some exact solutions for the wave functions, obtained under appropriate conditions. As a regularized version, we also consider the potential truncated at a finite difference from the center. The regularized wave functions feature a finite number of spatial oscillations, the missing GS reappears, and the spectrum of the bound states is discrete.

title: SALTO: Solver-Anchored Lifted Transfer Operators for Nonlinear Event Inference
abstract: Learned dynamical models can accurately predict trajectories while producing unreliable sensitivities when differentiated or transposed, limiting their use in inverse problems and scientific decision-making. Classical adjoints provide exact local derivatives, but a single adjoint cannot represent the nonlinear response of a system to a family of finite-amplitude perturbations. We introduce SALTO (Solver-Anchored Lifted Transfer Operators), a Koopman-based framework for inferring finite-amplitude sources. In the lifted space, the nonlinear dynamics are approximated by a linear propagator, and its transpose carries each sensor backward in a single solve. The result is a reusable lifted adjoint that predicts the measurement produced by any candidate localized event with one encoder pass and an inner product. To give the model the simulator's exact local behavior, SALTO imposes three structural constraints: it anchors the physical-state dynamics to the simulator's linearized propagator, centers the learned observables so that they vanish to second order at the reference state, and uses a block-triangular lifted propagator. These constraints guarantee that the model reduces to the simulator's tangent dynamics and classical adjoint as the amplitude vanishes, while the learned observables carry only the finite-amplitude correction. On three nonlinear PDE systems, SALTO predicts the measurements of finite-amplitude sources to within 2-8% where the classical adjoint is in error by 41-165%, recovers source position and intensity from sparse sensors nearly as accurately as inversion through the solver, and samples the joint posterior of two interacting sources, matching the solver's posterior on reaction-diffusion at a twentieth of its cost. One trained model serves new sensor layouts and measurement times with a single backward solve.

title: A counterexample to a conjecture of Plotnick on knot exteriors
abstract: We resolve a conjecture of S. Plotnick from 1983 concerning the homotopy type of four-dimensional knot complements. We show that the exteriors of two branched twist spins of the trefoil, which were shown by Plotnick not to be homotopy equivalent as boundary pairs and hence not homeomorphic, are in fact simple homotopy equivalent. The main ingredient of the proof is the construction of an explicit element of augmentation $49$ in the integral group ring of $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_5)$ which is a unit modulo the group norm and commutes with the element inducing the monodromy on the fundamental group.

title: CM Elliptic Analogue of the Coleman--Ihara Formula
abstract: The Soul\'{e} characters are Kummer characters constructed from cyclotomic units and also arising from the Galois action on the pro-$p$ geometric fundamental group of $\mathbb{P}^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$. The Coleman--Ihara formula describes the restrictions of these characters to the local Galois group at $p$ as products of the Coates--Wiles homomorphisms and Kubota--Leopoldt $p$-adic $L$-values at positive odd integers. In this paper, we prove an elliptic analogue of this formula for elliptic curves with complex multiplication by the ring of integers of an imaginary quadratic field $K$. We consider certain Kummer characters associated with elliptic units, which we call elliptic Soul\'{e} characters. These characters are elliptic counterparts of the classical Soul\'{e} characters and also arise from the Galois action on the pro-$p$ geometric fundamental groups of once-punctured elliptic curves. For suitable pairs of positive integers $(i,j)$, we give an explicit description of their restrictions to the relevant local Galois groups as products of the two-variable Coates--Wiles homomorphisms introduced by Yager and the two-variable $p$-adic $L$-values of $K$.

title: Coefficient lifting for skew divided differences and triple Schubert coefficients
abstract: Skew divided difference operators \(\partial_{w/v}\), introduced by Macdonald, play an important role in the study of Schubert polynomials and their structure constants. For permutations \(u,v,w\in S_n\), we show that the coefficient of each monomial \(\xx^\alpha\) in \(\partial_{w/v}\SSch_u(\xx;\yy)\), where \(\SSch_u(\xx;\yy)\) is the double Schubert polynomial, is a single triple Schubert coefficient evaluated at \(\tb=0\), whose indices form an explicit lift of \((u,v,w)\) to \(S_{n+\abs{\alpha}}\). As an application, we show that every coefficient of \(\partial_{w/v}\SSch_u(\xx)\) is a single Schubert structure constant. This gives a new proof of Kirillov's conjecture that these coefficients are nonnegative.

title: Infinitely many closed geodesic images on simply connected compact rank-one symmetric spaces
abstract: We prove that every smooth Riemannian metric on the underlying smooth manifold of a simply connected compact rank-one symmetric space, namely $S^n$ $(n\ge2)$, $\CP^m$ $(m\ge1)$, $\HP^m$ $(m\ge1)$, or $\OP^2$ admits infinitely many geometrically distinct prime closed geodesics. Here a prime closed geodesic is a nonconstant closed geodesic which is not an iterate of a shorter one, and geometric distinctness means that the images in the manifold are pairwise different. Thus iterating a geodesic, changing its starting point, or reversing its orientation does not count as a new geodesic. No nondegeneracy assumption on the metric is imposed. These manifolds have bounded loop-space Betti numbers, so the usual homological growth criterion does not yield this conclusion. We use the length filtration together with rotation and reversal of loops. A controlled cut construction gives a uniform filling estimate in the based loop space, with a fixed increase in length independent of degree, which we transfer to free loops. We then calculate global equivariant classes associated with odd and even iterates. Assuming finitely many prime geodesic images forces incompatible requirements at a class's first critical level. The proof treats spheres and projective spaces within a common framework and does not assume a sphere infinitude theorem.

title: Galerkin finite element method for time fractional diffusion-wave equations with constant time delay
abstract: This paper studies numerical methods for the time fractional diffusion-wave equations with the constant delay. Using a symmetric fractional-order reduction technique and introducing the auxiliary variable $w$, we reformulate the original problem as an equivalent coupled system and for the first time carry out a rigorous regularity analysis of $w$. Based on the symmetric graded time mesh, the coupled problem is discretised by the $L1$ scheme in time and a standard finite element method in space, and the stability result of the developed fully discrete finite element scheme is established by means of a discrete fractional Gr\"onwall inequality. Furthermore, we derive a new comparison principle and reconstruct a new barrier function on each interval $((k-1)\tau,k\tau]$, $1\le k\le K$ according to the properties of the symmetric graded mesh. Based on the new barrier function, we obtain new relevant properties, which lead to a novel and crucial stability property for the discrete fractional operator. Combining the obtained local truncation error in time gives a local error estimate for the fully discrete finite element scheme, which shows that our convergence result provides a unified framework that seamlessly encompasses both pointwise-in-time error estimates on uniform meshes and global-in-time error estimates on symmetrical graded meshes. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical results.

title: A $p$-adic Riemann--Hilbert correspondence over Robba rings
abstract: We construct overconvergent period sheaves $\mathcal{O}\widetilde{\mathbb{C}}^{I,\dagger}$ and $\mathcal{O}\mathbb{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}^{\dagger,+}$ on the $v$-site of a liftable semi-stable formal scheme $\mathfrak{X}_Z$. By establishing a decompletion theorem for small representations, we prove a $p$-adic Riemann-Hilbert correspondence relating small $\widetilde{\mathbb{C}}^I$-local systems (resp. $\mathbb{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}^+$-local systems) on the generic fiber $X_Z$ to small flat connections on the associated period ringed spaces. We further analyze the local Frobenius action and show that this correspondence is compatible with the Frobenius structure. As an application, we prove a comparison theorem between the cohomology of these period sheaves and the rigid cohomology of the special fiber, refining results of Le Bras and Colmez--Nizio{\l}.

title: Superfast Spectral Compressed Sensing with Quadratic Convergence
abstract: In this paper, we study the spectral compressed sensing problem of recovering a spectrally sparse signal from linear compressive measurements. Exploiting the low-rank Hankel structure associated with the signal, we formulate a nonconvex fixed-rank optimization problem with a Hankel regularization. We propose a Superfast Iterative Hard Thresholding (SIHT) algorithm, where each iteration consists of a tangent-space least-squares update followed by a fixed-rank hard thresholding projection. SIHT is the first nonconvex algorithm with provable quadratic convergence for spectral compressed sensing. For random Gaussian measurements, it achieves exact recovery in the noiseless case and stable recovery in the noisy case with near-optimal sample complexity. To efficiently implement SIHT, we develop a parameterized conjugate gradient method for solving the least-squares subproblem, endowing SIHT with state-of-the-art computational and memory efficiency. Numerical experiments are provided to validate our results.

title: Exact Endpoint Asymptotics and Almost-Sure Limits for Uniform Empirical Measures in Two Dimensions
abstract: For the empirical measure of the first $n$ points of one infinite sequence of independent uniform samples in the unit square, we identify the leading constant in the bounded-Lipschitz distance to area measure, equivalently in $W_1$, both in expectation and almost surely along all sample sizes. The constant is $c_*=\kappa_1/(2\sqrt\pi)\in(0,1/4]$, where $\kappa_1$ is the linear-growth Gaussian variational constant of Armegioiu--Goldman--Grotto--Trevisan. This answers the two-dimensional bounded-Lipschitz convergence question posed by Yukich in 1989.
