abstract: Probabilistic constellation shaping (PCS), originally designed to fill the gap between finite uniform constellations and continuous capacity-achieving input distributions, has recently emerged as a central tool in adjusting the expected integrated sidelobe level (EISL) in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). In this paper, we show that PCS goes beyond EISL: A large class of PCS methods, termed as type-based PCS, are capable of providing precise control over codeword-wise integrated sidelobe level ratio (ISLR) for systems employing orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), thus yielding a stronger sensing performance guarantee than EISL control. We further show that OFDM is almost the only unitary modulation basis whose codeword-wise ISLR can be precisely controlled by type-based PCS. Based upon the analytical results, practical type-based PCS methods compatible with the probabilistic amplitude shaping (PAS) framework are conceived, which achieve higher communication rates than existing ISAC-oriented PCS methods under identical ISLR constraints.

title: A prime plus a square: A conditional 11/20 upper bound
abstract: Let $E_\square(N)$ count the positive integers at most $N$ that cannot be expressed as a prime plus a nonnegative integer square. Assuming that every nontrivial zero of every primitive Dirichlet $L$-function has real part at most $7/8$, we prove $E_\square(N)\ll_\eps N^{11/20+\eps}$ for every $\eps>0$. The proof combines a conductor-weighted mean-square estimate with a uniform estimate for certain families having a prescribed quadratic component. For these families, the large sieve depends on the varying part of the conductor, while an approximate functional equation controls the fourth moment using the full conductor. A zero-detection argument then absorbs all bands of zeros with real part at least $129/167$. The remaining bands and the minor arcs give the exponent $11/20$. The proof includes even denominators, completion and positivity of the singular series, and removal of proper prime powers.

title: Automorphisms of triality groups over local rings
abstract: Let $R$ be a nonzero commutative local ring with $2,3\in R^\times$, and let $\rho\in\Aut(R)$ satisfy $\rho^3=\id$. We classify abstract automorphisms of the elementary and full triality groups in the adjoint and simply connected forms of type $D_4$. Every automorphism is uniquely determined by an adjoint group element and a ring automorphism preserving the trace $T=\id+\rho+\rho^2$; conversely, every such pair defines an automorphism. A square-zero example shows that trace-preserving coefficient automorphisms need not normalize $\langle\rho\rangle$ when $\rho$ is nontrivial on $R$ but trivial on its residue field. We also prove a relative rigidity theorem for homomorphisms from elementary triality groups over arbitrary coefficient rings to local targets with $2$ and $3$ invertible, assuming that an adjoint conjugation makes the parameter-one root images standard modulo the maximal ideal. Conversely, every unital trace-preserving ring homomorphism into such a local coefficient ring induces the corresponding homomorphism of elementary groups.
comments: 29 pages, including two appendices. A 10-page computational supplement and exact verification code are included as ancillary files

title: Data-driven Smooth-to-hard Spectral Regularization for General Linear Inverse Problems
abstract: The logistic smooth-to-hard shrinker is the proximal map of an explicit saturating spectral penalty for general linear inverse problems. Its exact weak convexity yields a unique scaled update and proximal-gradient stationarity guarantees, while independent validation provides finite-grid parameter-selection control. We use MRI as an illustrative example.

title: A logarithmic Brascamp--Lieb variance inequality
abstract: We prove a strengthened Brascamp--Lieb inequality for even log-concave measures whose positive sublevel bodies satisfy the local logarithmic Brunn--Minkowski inequality. The conclusion can be written either by adding a rank-one term to the Hessian of the potential or by adding an explicit nonnegative remainder to the variance. The proof uses sublevel volume variations, a one-dimensional Brascamp--Lieb inequality, and the coarea formula. The derivative of the potential under dilations gives an equality function whenever it is square-integrable. For potentials homogeneous of degree greater than one, we obtain a sharp radial remainder.

title: An Adaptive Cubic Regularisation Algorithm Based on Interior-Point Methods for Optimization with General Inequality Constraints
abstract: Nonlinear constrained optimization has a wide range of practical applications. The interior-point method is considered to be one of the most powerful algorithms for solving nonlinear inequality constrained optimization. In this paper, we consider optimization with general inequality constraints and propose an Adaptive Regularisation algorithm using Cubics Based on Interior-Point methods (ARCBIP). For solving the barrier problem, we construct ARC subproblem with linearized constraints and the well-known fraction to the boundary rule that prevents slack variables from approaching their lower bounds prematurely. We employ a composite-step approach and reduced Hessian methods to deal with linearized constraints, where the trial step is decomposed into a normal step and a tangential step. They are obtained by solving two ARC subproblems approximately with the fraction to the boundary rule. Requirements on normal steps and tangential steps are given to ensure global convergence. To determine whether the trial step is accepted, we use exact penalty function as the merit function in ARC framework. The updating of the barrier parameter is implemented by adaptive strategies. Global convergence is analyzed under mild assumptions. Preliminary numerical experiments and some comparison results are reported.

title: Equivariant $K$-theory as a global localization
abstract: We establish a global equivariant refinement of the theorem of Snaith that presents the complex $K$-theory spectrum as a localization of the suspension spectrum of $\mathbb C P^\infty$. We prove that the morphism of ultra-commutative global ring spectra from $\Sigma^\infty_+ B_{\text{gl}} U(1)$ that classifies the tautological $U(1)$-representation exhibits the global $K$-theory spectrum as a specific localization, in both the $\infty$-categories of ultra-commutative ring spectra and of commutative global ring spectra. The classes to be inverted are certain representation-graded $U(n)$-equivariant homotopy classes of $\Sigma^\infty_+ B_{\text{gl}} U(1)$, the pre-Bott classes. We also show that for every compact Lie group $G$, the $G$-equivariant $K$-theory spectrum is a telescopic localization of $\Sigma^\infty_+ B_G U(1)$ by the pre-Bott classes of all unitary $G$-representations.

title: Projection-Based Parareal for Nonlinear Initial-Value Problems
abstract: Parareal is a parallel-in-time method for initial-value problems that has found extensive applications and given rise to many variants. Krylov-enhanced parareal is a variant of parareal that uses projection techniques to accelerate convergence substantially for linear problems. In this paper, we study a projection-based parareal algorithm for nonlinear initial-value problems with a modified iteration scheme and an arbitrary orthogonal projection. For a general nonlinear problem, we prove a convergence estimate for each iteration step on a fixed time grid. We analyze the errors of the modified scheme and the scheme of Krylov-enhanced parareal relative to the old error as the coarse grid is refined. For a coarse solver of order $p$ and step size $h$, we prove error bounds of $O(h^{p+1})$ for the modified scheme and $O(h)$ for that of Krylov-enhanced parareal at the first potentially inexact time point under mild assumptions. Numerical experiments on two nonlinear problems are consistent with the theoretical analysis.

title: Boundary Harnack inequalities for the fractional $p$-Laplacian in Reifenberg flat domains
abstract: We prove a scale-invariant boundary Harnack inequality and H\"older continuity up to the boundary of quotients of positive fractional $p$-harmonic functions in Reifenberg flat domains with sufficiently small flatness constant, for $0<s<1$ and $2\le p<2/(1-s)$. The solutions are globally nonnegative, vanish on a common exterior boundary patch, and belong to the natural local energy and $(p-1)$-tail class. Their distant exterior values may be unrelated and unbounded. After normalization at a corkscrew point, the comparison and H\"older constants depend only on $n,s,p$. We first establish local half-space boundary comparison for every $p\ge2$ and prove relative approximation by the half-space profile in Reifenberg domains. The compactness argument identifies escaped exterior mass and excludes its constant source term. Interior $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity then yields gradient non-degeneracy and lower increment bounds in a cone of directions. To treat the degenerate kernels produced by linearization, we develop estimates for weighted non-local forms and prove a localized Harnack inequality for bounded quotients, retaining the full exterior interactions. Ordered variational deformations and a common fractional $p$-harmonic majorant yield comparison for solutions with unrelated exterior data. Truncation of distant data and fractional $p$-harmonic replacement extend the estimates from the variational energy class to the natural tail class.

title: On the Complexity of Finding Stationary Points in Stochastic $(L_0, L_1)$-Smooth Nonconvex Optimization
abstract: We study the stochastic first-order oracle (SFO) complexity of finding $\epsilon$-stationary points of $(L_0,L_1)$-smooth nonconvex functions. Under bounded-variance noise, existing analyses of normalized and clipped stochastic gradient descent (SGD) establish optimal dependence on $\epsilon$ and $L_0$, but the jointly optimal dependence on $L_0$, $L_1$, and $\epsilon$ remains unclear. We resolve this question for an unbiased SFO whose gradient noise has a $p$th central moment bounded by $\sigma^p$ for some $\sigma\geq 0$, where $p\in(1,2]$.Specifically, we establish an SFO lower bound of $\Omega\big(\big(\sigma^{\frac{p}{p-1}}\epsilon^{-\frac{p}{p-1}}+1\big) (L_0 \Delta\epsilon^{-2}+L_1\Delta\epsilon^{-1})\big)$, where $\Delta>0$ is the initial optimality gap.This bound identifies an unavoidable contribution proportional to $L_1\epsilon^{-1}\Delta$. We also prove that mini-batch (smoothed) normalized SGD can attain a matching upper bound, thereby establishing the optimal SFO complexity.

title: A proof of the interlacing conjecture for the singular values of Sylvester-Kac matrices
abstract: Boros and R\'ozsa (Linear Algebra Appl. 421 (2007) 407--416) reduced the singular value problem for the odd-order Sylvester--Kac matrix $P\in\mathbb{R}^{(2m+1)\times(2m+1)}$ to those for $Q^{(m)}\in\mathbb{R}^{(m+1)\times m}$ and $S^{(m)}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times(m+1)}$ via a permutation similarity transformation. They noted that $(Q^{(m)})^{T}Q^{(m)}-S^{(m)}(S^{(m)})^{T}$ is positive definite, and also conjectured that $\sigma_i(S^{(m)})\ge\sigma_{i+1}(Q^{(m)})$ for $1\le i\le m-1$ and $m\ge2$. In this paper, we prove that these inequalities are strict and establish the strict interlacing relation \begin{equation*} \sigma_1(Q^{(m)})>\sigma_1(S^{(m)})> \cdots>\sigma_m(Q^{(m)})> \sigma_m(S^{(m)})>0 \end{equation*} for all $m\ge1$. Here, $\sigma_i(\cdot)$ denotes the $i$-th largest singular value of a matrix.

title: Recovery of coefficients in a Schr\"{o}dinger system with nonlinear coupling
abstract: We consider the inverse problem of recovering time-dependent coefficients in a system of Schr\"{o}dinger equations with coupled nonlinear terms. We first address the well-posedness of the system for small boundary data and trivial initial data. Then, we show that the linearized Neumann data stably determines the nonlinear coefficients provided that, at any given time, they are known in some neighborhood of the boundary. The proof relies on linearization and complex geometric optics (CGO) solutions for the linear Schr\"{o}dinger equation. We conclude by outlining an approach based on the direct use of Carleman estimates to recover time-independent coefficients in the setting of trivial boundary data but nontrivial initial data.
comments: 29 pages (2 pages for the bibliography); comments welcome

title: Optimizers for the finite-rank fractional Lieb--Thirring inequality
abstract: The finite-rank fractional Lieb--Thirring inequality provides an estimate on the Riesz sum of the first $N$ negative eigenvalues of the fractional Schr\"odinger operator $(-\Delta)^s-V$ in terms of the $L^{\gamma+\frac{d}{2s}}(\mathbb R^d)$ norm of the potential $V$, where the Riesz exponent $\gamma>\max\left\{0,1-d/(2s)\right\}$. We prove the existence of optimizers for every finite rank by establishing a result on the spectrum in the case of dichotomy. We further characterize the spectral gap and qualitative properties of optimizers, including the Euler--Lagrange equation, regularity, and asymptotic behavior at infinity. In particular, under the condition $\gamma+{d}/{(2s)}\geq 3+{4s}/{d}$, we show that all normalized maximizing sequences are precompact modulo translations. Moreover, we derive a strict binding inequality for the optimal constants in the finite-rank setting, which implies that the optimal fractional Lieb--Thirring constant, if it exists, cannot be attained by a potential with finitely many negative eigenvalues.

title: The $L\log L$-Luxemburg Discrepancy for Nonnegative Weights Suffers from the Curse of Dimensionality
abstract: We study the normalized discrepancy in the Luxemburg norm generated by $\Phi(s)=s\log(1+s)$. For arbitrary nonnegative quadrature weights, we prove that the associated information complexity suffers from the curse of dimensionality: for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, there exist constants $c_\varepsilon>0$ and $d_0=d_0(\varepsilon)\in\mathbb{N}$ such that \[N_{\Phi,+}(\varepsilon,d)\ge c_{\varepsilon} d^{-1}(1.07735\ldots)^d \qquad \mbox{for all } d\ge d_0. \] The result therefore also applies to equal-weight quasi-Monte Carlo rules.

title: Stability analysis of the steady solution for incompressible lid-driven cavity flow
abstract: Steady solutions at high Reynolds numbers are computed using an iterative method that linearizes the nonlinear convective terms. This linearization reduces the original nonlinear boundary-value problem to a sequence of linear problems, one solved at each iteration, thereby improving the numerical robustness of the algorithm and enabling convergence over a wide range of governing parameters. The stability of steady incompressible fluid flows is studied within the framework of a linear problem for perturbations. The original steady velocity and pressure fields are subjected to small perturbations, after which the equations are linearized with respect to the perturbations. The resulting linear problem allows one to analyze the evolution of small perturbations and to establish whether the steady solutions under consideration are stable with respect to infinitesimal perturbations. In this work, the computational implementation is based on spatial discretization by the finite element method on triangular meshes. The stability of the obtained solutions is analyzed by solving a generalized algebraic eigenvalue problem formed after discretization of the linear problem for perturbations. The presence of eigenvalues with positive real part indicates instability, whereas their absence indicates stability. Calculations were performed on a sequence of refined meshes at various Reynolds numbers for the flow in a square cavity.

title: Operator-Space Entanglement Entropy in Random Fermionic Gaussian Dynamics
abstract: We study the von Neumann operator-space entanglement entropy (OSEE) of initial product operators evolved under random gaussian dynamics, as modeled by a Brownian SYK$_2$ model. By exploiting a mapping to a domain-wall melting problem, we derive an exact expression for the time-dependent bipartite OSEE in the thermodynamic limit, and obtain an analytic characterization of the corresponding gaussian Page curve emerging at late times. Our results build on recent work on the entanglement dynamics in the all-to-all quantum simple exclusion process, leveraging tools from RMT, including the Coulomb-gas approach and a mapping to the free Jacobi process. Finally, based on our results, we discuss the possibility of relating the OSEE with non-gaussianity measures in the Heisenberg picture.

title: Graphs with three eigenvalues from group divisible designs
abstract: We construct biregular graphs with three distinct eigenvalues from semiregular group divisible designs. For every prime power $q$, we use the spectral structure of Muzychuk's Construction~A on $q+1$ copies of $\operatorname{AG}(2,q^2)$ to produce suitable group divisible designs. The resulting biregular graphs have $2q^5+q^4+q^2$ vertices and distinct eigenvalues $q^5+q^3+q^2$, $q^2$, and $-q^2$. Their coherent closures have rank $12$ and type $\left[\begin{smallmatrix}3&2\\2&5\end{smallmatrix}\right]$. We also determine the four-class symmetric association schemes that are the coherent closures of the auxiliary graphs in this family. Computational searches provide further graphs on $81$ and $156$ vertices, using Muzychuk's Construction~B and a generalised quadrangle, respectively; their coherent closures have ranks $13$ and $10$. The $156$-vertex example has a strongly regular design as its coherent closure, of type $\left[\begin{smallmatrix}3&2\\2&3\end{smallmatrix}\right]$, answering a question of the authors. We also realise a $126$-vertex example by switching a strongly regular graph.

title: B\'ezout bounds and rational points on quasianalytic graphs
abstract: For functions $f : [0,1] \to [0,1]$ in quasianalytic Denjoy-Carleman classes $\mathcal C_M$, we establish explicit bounds for the number of intersection points of the graph $\Gamma(f)$ with algebraic curves of degree at most $d$. The bounds are given in terms of the Bang degree determined by the weight sequence $M$, the degree $d$, and the norming constant of $\Gamma(f)$ with respect to the space of real bivariate polynomials of degree at most $d$. We give instances, where the bounds are at most polynomial in $d$ and, consequently, the graph $\Gamma(f)$ contains few rational points: the number of rational points of height at most $H$ is bounded by a polynomial in $\log H$.

title: Fisher Information and Support Complexity of Gaussian Mixtures
abstract: We study lower bounds on the Fisher information of Gaussian location mixtures and their applications to estimation problems. First, for a discrete mixing distribution, we derive a universal positive-semidefinite lower bound on the Fisher information matrix in terms of the R\'enyi entropy of order two. For a mixing distribution supported on $K$ points, this bound scales as $\log(K)/K^2$, improving by a logarithmic factor on the support-size dependence obtained from Stam's inequality. We then develop dimension-aware trace bounds using classical Sobolev inequalities. These bounds are expressed in terms of Sibson's $\alpha$-mutual information and yield the scaling $K^{-2/n}$ in dimension $n$. A complementary bound involving the $\alpha$-mutual information of order $1/2$ is obtained using the sharp Young convolution inequality. The derived inequalities are further specialized to rotationally invariant mixing distributions supported on discrete spherical shells. In this setting, an intrinsic-dimensional bound on Sibson mutual information leads to lower bounds on the Fisher information in terms of the number of occupied shells. As applications, we study least favorable priors for bounded Gaussian mean estimation. In the scalar case, we show that the least favorable prior on $[-R,R]$ has at least $\Omega(R\sqrt{\log R})$ support points and that each of its probability masses is of order at most $1/R$. In the vector case, we show that the number of occupied shells grows at least linearly with $R$. Finally, Brown's identity and the I-MMSE relationship are used to translate the Fisher-information inequalities into upper bounds on the MMSE and mutual information.

title: Only their cardinality can prevent groups from being quotients of weakly branch groups
abstract: It is a well-known fact that every proper quotient of a branch group is a virtually abelian group. We record that every group of cardinality at most $2^{\aleph_0}$ is a quotient of a weakly branch group; in fact, there are weakly branch groups that are split extensions with free complements. Furthermore, if a group is generated by $d$ elements, there is a weakly branch group generated by $(d+2)$ elements mapping onto it. As applications of this fact, we resolve a question of Thillaisundaram on the existence of weakly branch but non-branch groups with maximal subgroups of infinite index and, partially, a question of Cox and Thillaisundaram on the existence of weakly branch groups that are not invariably generated.

title: Resolutions of compact balanced spaces
abstract: Let $X$ be a compact reduced balanced complex space of pure dimension $n\geq2$. We prove that every resolution of singularities of $X$ is a balanced manifold; in particular, $X$ belongs to the class $\mathscr{B}$. This removes the additional cohomological assumptions appearing in earlier results of Fu-Meng-Xia. The main new ingredient is the linear independence of the Aeppli classes of the exceptional prime divisors of a projective bimeromorphic morphism onto a normal complex space. This follows from the vanishing of curve degrees for Aeppli-trivial divisors and the relative negativity lemma. For non-normal spaces, strict positivity is used to eliminate divisors mapping onto codimension-one subsets before passing to the normalization. We also recall a classical surface example of Grauert showing that the inclusion of compact balanced spaces in $\mathscr{B}$ is strict.

title: Short-Boundary Signaling for Asynchronous Grant-Free Control-to-Control Communications
abstract: In asynchronous grant-free access, receivers must detect variable-length transmissions and identify their start and end. Existing decoder-aided receivers use start and tail sequences which are as long as one codeword, causing substantial overhead for short commands. This paper treats the boundary (i.e., start and tail sequences) length as an independent design parameter and proposes a convolutional neural network that detects both boundaries from the received waveform and the decoder soft output. Its waveform input size decreases with the boundary length, while the decoder input keeps the codeword length, so the boundary can be shortened without altering the decoder. Analysis and simulations quantify the resulting tradeoff among payload efficiency, collision exposure, and boundary detection. The results show that the proposed receiver can exploit very short boundaries: in the considered setting, the shortest tested boundary, $L_{\mathrm{b}}=16$, yields the highest effective payload efficiency at all tested loads, whereas a correlation-based benchmark with the same sequences performs best with $L_{\mathrm{b}}=64$ at moderate and high loads.

title: A New Bound for the Gauss Circle Problem
abstract: Let $E(X)=\#\{(a,b)\in\Z^2:a^2+b^2\le X\}-\pi X$. We prove that $E(X)=O_\varepsilon(X^{209/670+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, uniformly for real $X\ge4$. This breaks the $5/16$ threshold suggested by Huxley as a possible limit of the Bombieri--Iwaniec method at the time. The proof introduces two refinements: a cone distribution estimate that preserves separate fourth- and sixth-power contributions in the double large sieve, and an explicit inversion of Taylor-coefficient constraints that cancels the linear error in a pair-counting argument. These refinements, together with the Robert--Sargos and Watt spacing estimates and the Vinogradov mean value theorem, yield the improvement.

title: A multi-point maximum principle to prove the global Harnack inequality for the doubly nonlinear heat equation
abstract: This work aims to present a new proof of the global pointwise Harnack inequality satisfied by positive viscosity solutions of the doubly nonlinear heat equation on $\mathbb{R}^d$. Our approach is based on a multi-point maximum principle argument introduced by the authors in a recent article [Calc. Var., 2026]. Required for the proof is a new variation of the maximum principle for semicontinuous functions, which is a standard tool in the analysis of viscosity solutions. In particular, our techniques provide a new proof of the Harnack inequalities satisfied by positive solutions of the porous medium equation and the $p$-heat equation, which were derived by Auchmuty and Bao [Proc. Amer. Math. Soc., 1994] using results of Aronson and B\'enilan [C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris, 1979] and Esteban and V\'azquez [Arch. Rational Mech. Anal., 1988]. The results contained in this article have also been discussed in the third author's doctoral thesis.

title: A sharp criterion for well-posedness of semilinear Schr\"odinger equations on the real line
abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for semilinear Schr\"odinger equations on the real line. We establish a sharp necessary and sufficient condition on the nonlinearity for local well-posedness in Sobolev spaces of regularity greater than five halves. This criterion is formulated in terms of the Mizohata condition and is equivalent to explicit algebraic conditions on the nonlinearity. To prove sufficiency, we combine energy estimates with a gauge transformation adapted to the bounded primitive arising from the Mizohata condition. To prove necessity, we show that the failure of the condition yields a dense set of initial data for which no solution exists on any positive time interval.

title: Local definable $(p,q)$-theorem and a refinement
abstract: We prove the definable $(p,q)$-conjecture for NIP formulas in arbitrary first-order theories. We also prove a refinement and apply it to dense pairs.

title: An IMEX multi-level domain-decomposition method for the Boltzmann equation on unstructured meshes
abstract: We introduce a dynamically adaptive multi-level method for the multiscale Boltzmann equation on unstructured meshes, coupling the compressible Euler, Navier-Stokes, and full Boltzmann descriptions within a single asymptotic-preserving IMEX framework. Unlike standard domain-decomposition approaches, where independent solvers exchange data only through interface conditions, the three models form a unified multiregime scheme. They share the same globally stiffly accurate IMEX Runge-Kutta discretization and are synchronized at every internal stage through kinetic-to-fluid moment projections and fluid-to-kinetic lifting. This stage-wise coupling maintains temporal consistency across model interfaces, while the asymptotic-preserving structure ensures compatibility with the fluid limit as the Knudsen number becomes small. The active description is selected in each cell through moment-realizability indicators derived from successive Chapman-Enskog approximations. The hierarchy uses Euler in near-equilibrium regions, Navier-Stokes where first-order nonequilibrium corrections are sufficient, and the full Boltzmann equation where a kinetic description is required. Using Navier-Stokes as the intermediate level avoids evolving a velocity distribution in mildly nonequilibrium regions, which is particularly advantageous on unstructured meshes, where kinetic transport dominates the cost. The spatial discretization combines finite-volume WENO reconstruction on triangular meshes with a conservative fast spectral method for the Boltzmann collision operator. Numerical experiments show that the method closely reproduces the full Boltzmann reference while significantly reducing the computational cost. These results suggest that tightly coupled AP model hierarchies are a viable alternative to interface-based domain decomposition for deterministic kinetic simulations in complex geometries.

title: Moment Propagation for the Vlasov--Poisson System with Gyroscopic Forces, Velocity Diffusion, and Specular Reflection
abstract: This paper studies the three-dimensional Vlasov--Poisson system with gyroscopic forces and velocity diffusion. For the Cauchy problem in $\mathbb R^3$ and the specular--Dirichlet problem in bounded domains, we prove the propagation of velocity moments of order $k>2$ for weak solutions with bounded $L^1\cap L^{\infty}$ norms and kinetic energy. The proof applies Serre's compensated integrability to weighted mass--momentum tensors to derive density estimates. A finite iteration alternating moment propagation with improved density integrability then closes the estimates. These estimates provide a simplified approach to moment propagation and yield global continuation of classical solutions.

title: On a critical curl-curl system of Lane-Emden type
abstract:
We study the system $
abla	imes
abla	imes u = |v|^{q-2}v$, $
abla	imes
abla	imes v = |u|^{p-2}u$ of Lane-Emden type in $\mathbb R^3$, with exponents $p,q>3$ on the critical hyperbola $1/p+1/q=1/3$. We prove the existence of a ground state solution by reducing the system to a quasilinear fourth-order curl-curl equation and minimizing the associated Sobolev-curl quotient. A concentration-compactness argument shows there are finitely many concentration points for a Palais-Smale sequence $(u_n)$. This yields a.e. convergence of $
abla	imes
abla	imes u_n$ to $
abla	imes
abla	imes u$ where $u$ is the weak limit of $(u_n)$. We also prove that the optimal Sobolev-curl constant is attained and is strictly larger than the usual second-order Sobolev constant. If $p=q$, we show $u$ and $v$ are necessarily equal for every solution. In an appendix we show that our concentration argument also applies to a scalar quasilinear fourth order equation.

title: Pseudoconvex domains in complex Euclidean space with one-dimensional Bergman spaces
abstract: For any $n \geq 2$, we construct a pseudoconvex domain in $\C^n$ such that the Bergman space is one-dimensional. This disproves Wiegerinck conjecture.

title: Quotients of Calabi-Yau Generalized Fermat manifolds and Log Enriques varieties
abstract: Enriques manifolds and Log Enriques varieties have attracted a lot of interest in the last years. In this paper we study Enriques manifolds and Log Enriques varieties that are respectively \'etale and quasi-\'etale quotients of Calabi-Yau manifolds. We produce several examples by studying quotients of generalized Fermat manifolds of Calabi-Yau type. These are complete intersections of Fermat type manifolds all of the same degree and were described recently by Hidalgo, Hughes and Leyton-\'Alvarez. We describe all their quotients by a fixed-point-free automorphism. Most of the quotients are Log Enriques varieties or Calabi-Yau varieties with terminal singularities. In one case we get a family of Enriques manifolds which is a subfamily of a family described previously by Boissi\`ere, Camere and the third author, which is one of the two so far known families of Enriques manifolds of Calabi-Yau type. This family is obtained as an \'etale quotient of order two of a Calabi-Yau manifold complete intersection of quadrics, the other family is the Hilbert scheme of $n$ points on an Enriques surface. In the last part of the paper we show that these two families are different by computing their second Betti numbers, which are equal to one and eleven respectively.

title: Backward stochastic porous media equation with polynomial growth
abstract: We investigate the well-posedness of a backward stochastic porous media equation whose nonlinear term is a polynomial operator corresponding to the slow diffusion regime. The main challenge stems from the structure of this nonlinear operator, which causes the operator to lose maximal monotonicity and prevents the use of standard weak-strong convergence techniques to identify the limit. Moreover, since the Laplace operator makes it difficult to separate the operators and discuss them individually, we attempt to obtain the of limit by investigating the global properties of the operator.

title: Model-Driven Deep Learning for Distributed Detection with Low-Bit Quantization
abstract: Distributed detection plays a fundamental role in communication-efficient collaborative inference over large-scale networks, where spatially distributed nodes must cooperate using severely quantized messages due to bandwidth constraints. While low-bit quantization is essential for reducing communication overhead, it can significantly degrade detection performance, particularly when prior knowledge of observation noise is unavailable. To address this challenge, we propose a model-driven deep learning framework for distributed detection with low-bit quantization. For fixed local quantizers, we first derive the exact finite-sensor maximum a posteriori (MAP) detection error and prove that, under conditionally independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) observations, independent local randomizations, and a common quantization-level constraint, identical quantizers preserve the supremum of the average network Chernoff information. Guided by these results, we develop a binary probabilistic quantizer with a trainable neural probability controller and design a tree-structured probabilistic quantizer for scalable multi-bit quantization. The exact finite-sensor MAP error provides the training objective for the binary quantizer, while we derive a computationally tractable Bhattacharyya surrogate objective for training the multi-bit quantizer. For both cases, we derive analytical MAP fusion rules based on the class-conditional probability mass functions (PMFs) of the quantized messages. When the observation statistics are unknown, these PMFs are estimated from held-out labeled data, yielding plug-in MAP detectors. Simulation results show that the proposed method approaches centralized-oracle performance at higher quantization resolutions and remains effective under changes in network size and test-time signal amplitude.
comments: 16 pages, 10 figures. Accepted by IEEE JSAC

title: The linear positive torsor presentation and arithmetic purity of strong approximation
abstract: In this article, we define a notion for varieties called linear positive torsor presentation. For varieties with a linear positive torsor presentation over number fields, we establish the arithmetic purity of strong approximation with the Brauer--Manin obstruction off the empty set. As a consequence, we recover arithmetic purity for smooth toric variety with no non-constant global section. Moreover, we classify the chain connected class for rational points on such varieties over any field of characteristic zero.

title: Visible parts and projections of the affine fractal percolation
abstract: We study the visible parts and orthogonal projections of the affine fractal percolation. We show that for the affine fractal percolation $E$, conditioned on $E \neq \varnothing$, almost surely the dimension of the visible part is equal to $\min\{1, \dim_{\rm H} E\}$ from all directions except for the major contracting direction. The visible part from the major contracting direction is notably different from the other directions, and we provide a formula for its Hausdorff and box dimensions. In addition, we show that almost surely conditioned on $E \neq \varnothing$, $\dim_{\rm H} \pi(E) =\min\{ 1, \dim_{\rm H} E\}$ for every orthogonal projection $\pi$ excluding the one onto the major contracting direction, and given $\dim_{\rm H} E >1$, these projections contain intervals.

title: Causal Sobolev spaces and gradient flows
abstract: We develop a relaxation-based approach to Sobolev functions and Cheeger energies on metric spacetimes, in analogy with the construction used in positive signature. For an exponent $p<0$, we introduce a pre-$p$-Cheeger energy built from a local steepness constant on causal functions, and define the $p$-Cheeger energy as its relaxation in $L^0$; this yields, by construction, a convex and lower semicontinuous functional together with an associated maximal relaxed subslope. We establish natural calculus rules for the resulting Sobolev class. We then define the $p$-heat flow as the gradient flow of the $p$-Cheeger energy in $L^2$ and its generator, the $p$-d'Alembertian. Combining a Kuwada-type lemma with entropy growth estimates along the flow, we show that our notion of Sobolev class and relaxed subslope coincides with the Sobolev class and weak subslope introduced by Beran et al.

title: Localization induced by Sinai disorder in mass-exchange models
abstract: We introduce a conservative continuous-mass-exchange model with quenched disorder in the splitting laws on the bonds of a finite segment. Although the dynamics is generically irreversible, its stationary mean mass profile remarkably turns out to be exactly solvable through an associated birth-and-death chain and has a Gibbs representation in terms of a simple random-walk potential. If $N$ is the number of bonds and $\beta$ measures the strength of disorder, the parameter $\beta\sqrt N$ separates an asymptotically flat profile, a Brownian crossover, and a profile localized near the global minimum. We characterize the fluctuations of macroscopic masses and identify arcsine laws for the localization centre, the competition between left and right valleys, and the disorder-averaged mass measure. Furthermore, for the extremal masses, we discuss the emergent limiting random variable in terms of the literature linking finite RW paths seen from its minimum to infinite-horizon walks conditioned to stay positive. Finally, in proximity of the localization transition point $\beta=0$, we show that the inverse participation ratio for the extremal masses give rises to a scaling with decay of order $k^{-3/2}$ consistent with the scaling limit of the latter conditioned walk. In the same limit, the inverse participation ratio shows a scaling form.

title: Fundamentals of Potential theory for a hypoelliptic process
abstract: This article aims at solving open questions related to the well-posedness of Potential theory objects in a hypoelliptic setting. We provide here the expression of the equilibrium measure, capacity and electrostatic energy between smooth open sets $\A$ and $\B$ for the underdamped Langevin process. Additionally, the capacity is shown to be the solution of two variational principles which extend the well-known Dirichlet and Thomson principles in the hypoelliptic setting. Due to the degeneracy of the operator at hand, the results display significant differences with the standard elliptic setting.

title: Quantum-compatible Riemannian conjugate gradient for ground-state preparation
abstract: Riemannian optimization provides a natural geometric framework for designing quantum algorithms for ground-state preparation, most notably through quantum imaginary-time evolution. However, existing geometry-aware approaches primarily employ steepest-descent updates, leaving more advanced methods from classical Riemannian optimization largely unexplored. In this work, we introduce quantum conjugate gradient descent (QCGD), a quantum-compatible implementation of Riemannian conjugate gradient that combines the steepest descent direction with information retained from previous search directions. In our numerical experiments, the proposed approach achieves faster convergence per iteration than the baseline double-bracket quantum imaginary-time evolution (DB-QITE) algorithm, and we quantify the associated circuit cost with gate counts produced by Qrisp. This improvement, however, comes at the cost of increased circuit depth for each update step, revealing a trade-off between convergence rate and implementation complexity. Nevertheless, since the circuit depth for those algorithms grows exponentially with the number of iterations, the proposed method may offer practical advantages, particularly in the early fault-tolerant regime.

title: Hydrodynamic limits of finite range exclusion processes
abstract: We consider variants of the simple symmetric exclusion process (SSEP) where particles are 'large'; while in the SSEP, each lattice point is either occupied or not occupied by a single particle, in our model each particle is represented by a fixed shape, and the dynamics is so that shapes cannot overlap. In one dimension, this reduces to a finite range interaction that prevents particles from coming closer to each other than a certain distance. In this case, we prove the existence of the hydrodynamic limit, and identify the relevant macroscopic PDE, which is a porous medium equation. In two dimensions, we have no rigorous results, but instead rely on numerical simulations to approximate the diffusion matrix. Under the assumption that the hydrodynamic limit exists in two dimensions, we derive properties of the diffusion matrix based on the shape of the particles.

title: Extremals for linear functionals on $H^p$ are outer when $0<p<1$
abstract: Let $L$ be a nontrivial bounded linear functional on the Hardy space $H^p$ of the unit disc. We prove that if $0<p<1$ and if $f$ in the unit sphere of $H^p$ satisfies $L(f)=\|L\|$, then $f$ is an outer function. The proof is short and relies on a construction due to de Leeuw and Rudin. Our result complements work of Duren, Romberg, and Shields on the failure of the Hahn--Banach theorem for $H^p$. When applied to the special case $L_k(f) = f^{(k)}(0)/k!$ for $k=1,2,3,\ldots$, it resolves two conjectures of the first-named author and Saksman and one conjecture of Suffridge.

title: Controlled-Memory Identification with Shared Generators: Dimension--Horizon Tradeoffs and Quantum--Classical Separation
abstract: We determine the finite-horizon identification limits of a \(d\)-dimensional memory when the control interface is restricted to four shared, time-homogeneous generators. A writer encodes a message by applying a prefix word to a common root state. The verifier then applies a candidate-dependent query word followed by a shared terminal binary test, with each word of length at most \(T\). For fixed error tolerances \(\lambda_2>0\) and \(\lambda_1+\lambda_2<1\), the optimal identification sizes satisfy \(\ln N_{\mathsf Q,4}=\Theta_{\lambda_1,\lambda_2}(\min\{d^2,T\})\) for arbitrary CPTP generators and \(\ln N_{\mathsf S,4}=\Theta_{\lambda_1,\lambda_2}(\min\{d,T\})\) for stochastic maps. Four unitary letters and four permutation letters attain these respective bounds, showing that a four-letter reversible alphabet reaches the static code-size orders in optimal quadratic and linear word length. In the fully dimension-limited regime, this yields \(\ln N_{\mathsf Q,4}=\Theta(d^2)\) versus \(\ln N_{\mathsf S,4}=\Theta(d)\), establishing a quadratic quantum--classical separation in logarithmic code size. Low-overlap Grassmann and agreement-code packings supply the orbit endpoints, while exact inverse query words match each encoded state to its designated test. At the sharp boundary \(\lambda_2=0\), \(0\leq\lambda_1<1\), all four model classes satisfy \(\ln N=\Theta(\min\{\ln d,T\})\). Thus any fixed positive false-acceptance tolerance activates the metric-packing regime, whereas zero false acceptance imposes an exclusive-witness constraint and yields the logarithmic-dimension boundary.

title: A number field extension of Ramanujan's identity and its integral representation via the generalized Riemann $\Xi$-function
abstract: On pages 219--220 of Ramanujan's Lost Notebook appears an intriguing modular transformation whose integral representation is expressed in terms of the Riemann $\Xi$-function. In this paper, we establish a number field analogue of this identity. We also obtain an integral representation for the transformation formula associated with the functional equation of the higher power of the Dedekind zeta function recently studied by the present author and Maji. Interestingly, we recover Hardy's integral representation of the well-known Jacobi theta relation involving the Riemann $\Xi$-function. We further obtain a number-field analogue of the extended Ramanujan--Koshliakov formula established by Dixit.

title: Orlik-Solomon algebras determine the Tutte polynomials of matroids of rank at most three
abstract: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a simple matroid of rank $r$ on the ground set $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $T_{\mathcal{M}}(x,y)$ denote its Tutte polynomial, and let $\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{M})$ denote its Orlik-Solomon $\mathbb{C}$-algebra. We say that $\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{M})$ determines $T_{\mathcal{M}}(x,y)$ if, for every simple matroid $\mathcal{N}$, an isomorphism $\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{M})\cong\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{N})$ of $\mathbb{C}$-algebras, without regard to the grading, implies $T_{\mathcal{M}}(x,y)=T_{\mathcal{N}}(x,y)$. Falk conjectured that the Orlik-Solomon $\mathbb{C}$-algebra of every simple matroid of rank three determines its Tutte polynomial. We prove that this holds for every simple matroid of rank at most three, thereby resolving Falk's conjecture.

title: Lipschitz-free spaces over separable Banach spaces and their complementability in the bidual
abstract: We prove that the Lipschitz-free space over a separable Banach space is complemented in its bidual if and only if the underlying Banach space is isomorphic to a Hilbert space. This answers negatively a long-standing question of Godefroy, Lancien, and Zizler concerning the case of $\ell_1$. We also characterize the existence of a projection of norm one and extend both characterizations to nonempty open convex subsets. Our approach yields several further results which we believe may be useful for understanding the structure of Lipschitz-free spaces over Banach spaces. These include an isometric representation of such spaces as quotients of Bochner $L^1$ spaces constructed using Gaussian measures.

title: Legitimate Reconstruction Advantage in Wiretapped Semantics-Aware Remote Monitoring
abstract: This paper investigates joint accuracy and security in semantics-aware remote monitoring, where source updates intended for a legitimate receiver may also be intercepted by an eavesdropper. We define legitimate reconstruction advantage (LRA) as the joint event that the intended receiver correctly reconstructs the current source state using received updates while the eavesdropper reconstructs it incorrectly. Source evolution changes the relevance of received updates at the two receivers, so their marginal reconstruction accuracies do not, in general, determine the probability of this joint event. Under randomized stationary (RS) transmission and zero-order-hold reconstruction at both receivers, we derive an explicit joint stationary distribution and closed-form expressions for LRA probability and persistence for general finite-state ergodic Markov sources. For two-state and uniform-transition sources, we obtain algebraic expressions that enable low-complexity optimization of RS policies. Analytical and numerical results show that maximizing the probability of legitimate advantage need not maximize its persistence. For two-state sources, rare-transmission analysis reveals that, at a fixed sum of transition probabilities, greater transition asymmetry can increase persistence while reducing LRA probability. Moreover, optimizing marginal accuracy and security metrics can select policies that are suboptimal for LRA. Counterintuitively, more frequent transmission or improved legitimate-channel reliability can increase legitimate reconstruction accuracy while reducing LRA probability. Finally, a geofencing application translates prescribed LRA requirements into spatial constraints on eavesdropper locations.

title: Inverse Wave Problems on Graphs
abstract: We study inverse wave problems on finite graphs from time-dependent measurements on a prescribed set of vertices. With the graph geometry known, we consider recovery of either the initial signal or the vertex wave speeds when the other is given. Initial-signal recovery is characterized by observability of the associated finite-dimensional system, while a single experiment determines the vertex wave speeds under a zero forcing condition and a natural nonharmonicity assumption. We establish stability estimates for both recovery problems, develop a nonlinear least-squares reconstruction method, and extend the results to positively weighted graphs. Numerical simulations illustrate the reconstruction and examine the effects of observation geometry, time horizon, coefficient localization, and measurement noise on its performance. Our results are motivated both by numerical approaches to continuous inverse wave problems, where spatial discretization leads naturally to graph-based systems, and by applications in which the underlying dynamics are inherently discrete and evolve on networks.

title: Generalized Cluster Algebra Homomorphisms Induced by Cluster Tube Embeddings
abstract: We relate multiplication formulas for regular modules in coefficient-free acyclic affine cluster algebras with skew-symmetric exchange matrices to the imaginary exchange relations of Reading-Stella. Introducing a parameter $z$ into the construction of Zhou-Zhu, we define a weighted cluster character on cluster tubes that satisfies generalized exchange relations of type $C_{n-1}$ and yields a bijection between indecomposable rigid objects and cluster variables. Using the multiplication formulas and difference property of Ding-Xiao-Xu, we show that non-homogeneous tube embeddings induce injective homomorphisms into ordinary affine cluster algebras under $z\mapsto X_\delta$. Comparison with Reading-Stella's relations identifies $X_\delta$ with the corresponding theta function, giving a representation-theoretic interpretation of the generalized exchange parameter.

title: Finite Time Noncollapsing K\"ahler-Ricci Flow: Gaussian Type Heat Kernel, Gromov-Hausdorff Limits
abstract: In this paper, we study heat kernel estimates along the K\"ahler-Ricci flow with finite time noncollapsing singularities over a compact K\"ahler manifold. The starting point is the type-II scalar-curvature estimate, which gives the natural parabolic scale $r\lesssim T-t$ near the singular time. By combining the distance distortion and space-time cut-off estimates of Bamler--Zhang with entropy, mean-value inequality, and conjugate heat-kernel estimates, we obtain two-sided Gaussian bounds and gradient bounds that are uniform on this scale. Under the global type-I scalar-curvature estimate, the same estimates hold on every scale. We then use these estimates and the monotonicity of the $W_1$-distance between conjugate heat flows to construct a canonical singular-time pseudo-distance. The distances $d_t$ (induced by $\omega(t)$) converge uniformly to this pseudo-distance. Its metric quotient is the unique Gromov--Hausdorff limit. Finally, we apply Bamler's theory and the recent work of Hallgren--Zhang to obtain the following. Every fixed-base-point type-I blow-up admits a subsequential metric-flow limit whose time slices are singular shrinking K\"ahler--Ricci soliton spaces with normal complex-analytic and log-terminal structure, unique tangent cones, and a polarized Fano fibration. For moving base points, the limiting metric flow, equipped with its limiting conjugate heat flow, is a metric soliton precisely under an entropy-pinching condition.

title: On the uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for the Motsch-Tadmor model
abstract: We consider the Motsch-Tadmor model, a modification of the Cucker-Smale model for flocking dynamics that incorporates asymmetric communication weights. In the case of uniformly positive interactions, we consider the validity problem for the limiting kinetic equation, proving a uniform-in-time propagation of chaos result in the moving frame given by the consensus velocities. The result is obtained by studying the reversibility of the communication weights and by implicitly characterizing the asymptotic consensus.

title: Modules and operator rings of Reynolds algebras
abstract: We develop a module theory for weighted Reynolds algebras by constructing an associa?tive ring that records the algebra action and the module operator. The categories of left and right Reynolds modules are equivalent to the corresponding module categories over this ring, and their tensor products agree under these equivalences. We construct free Reynolds modules and give an explicit graded description of the operator ring for idempotent classical Reynolds operators fixing the identity. When the Reynolds operator on the algebra is bijective, modules with bijective module operators correspond to differential modules satisfying an invertibility condition. The operator ring transfers the Hom-tensor adjunction, Morita theory and derived functors to Reynolds modules. Explicit computations over a field show that the identity operator gives an operator ring of global dimension one, whereas the zero operator gives one of infinite global dimension.

title: The space of polarized compactifications of an affine variety
abstract: Let $X$ be a normal affine variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Through the lens of non-Archimedean geometry, we study the space of polarized compactifications of $X$, consisting of pairs $(\bar X, D)$ where $\bar X$ is a normal projective variety containing $X$ as a dense open subset, and $D$ is an effective ample $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor with support equal to the complement of $X$ in $\bar X$. We identify this space with a natural class of functions--the Fubini--Study functions--on the Berkovich analytification of $X$. Through a Rees correspondence, we also give a bijection with the space of homogeneous $\mathbb{Q}$-valued, finitely generated negative non-Archimedean norms (or filtrations) on the coordinate ring of $X$. Using the above identifications, we equip the space of polarized compactifications, and numerical classes thereof, with natural metrics and identify the metric completions. The latter include a space of continuous plurisubharmonic functions in the sense of Chambert-Loir and Ducros, and a space of birational curve classes as studied by Dang and Favre.

title: Surjective maps preserving quasi-nilpotence of products of operators
abstract: Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional complex Banach space and let $\mathcal B(X)$ the full algebra of all bounded linear operator on $X$. In this paper, we give a complete characterization of surjective maps $\phi:\mathcal B(X)\to\mathcal B(X)$ satisfying \[ r(AB)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad r(\phi(A)\phi(B))=0 \qquad(A,B\in\mathcal B(X)). \] Without assuming additivity, injectivity, or continuity, we show that there exists a function $\gamma : B(X)\mapsto \C \setminus\{0\}$ such that the map $\phi$ takes one of the following forms: 1. there exists a bounded linear or conjugate-linear, invertible operator $S:X\to X$ such that : \label{eq:direct} \phi(A)=\gamma(A)SAS^{-1},\qquad \text{ for all } \quad A\in B(X), 2. the space $X$ is reflexive and there exists a bounded linear or conjugate-linear, invertible operator $S:X^*\to X$ such that \label{eq:dual} \phi(A)=\gamma(A)SA^*S^{-1},\qquad \text{ for all } \quad A\in B(X).

title: Feeling the generalised rough SABR boundary
abstract: We provide an in-depth analysis of a generalised rough version of the SABR volatility model, widely used in the financial industry. We specifically focus on its behaviour at the origin, whether it can reach it and how fast it may do so.

title: A geometry-independent endpoint estimate for the Littlewood--Paley $g$-function generated by the Poisson semigroup
abstract: We prove a weak $(1,1)$ estimate for the full Poisson Littlewood--Paley $g$-function on every complete Riemannian manifold without boundary, with an explicit universal constant approximately equal to $3.33606$. The estimate requires no curvature restriction, volume doubling, heat kernel bound, or stochastic completeness. The proof combines a precise Poisson maximal inequality with a convex entropy identity; local elliptic regularity identifies the extension to arbitrary real $L^1$ data. As an application, we obtain weak $(1,1)$ estimates for certain spectral multipliers represented by Poisson time derivatives with coefficients in $L^2((0,\infty),dt/t)$.

title: The Calder\'on operator for time-harmonic Maxwell's equations in closed waveguides
abstract: We consider the time-harmonic Maxwell's equations in a closed, cylindrical waveguide with longitudinal invariant but heterogeneous permittivity and permeability. We consider minimal smoothness assumptions, i.e., the material parameters have to be in $L^\infty$ and the cross section has to be Lipschitz with a possibly non-trivial topology. First, we show that the associated Calder\'on operator is well-defined and bounded in the natural trace spaces $\mathbf{H}_0^{-1/2}(\operatorname{curl}_\Gamma;\Gamma) \to \mathbf{H}_0^{-1/2}(\operatorname{div}_\Gamma;\Gamma)$. Second, we consider interior Maxwell problems obtained from using the Calder\'on operator and analyze their well-posedness. Furthermore, we report some additional results on the location and group velocities of the waveguide wavenumbers.

title: High-order positivity-preserving well-balanced schemes: combining flux globalization with modified Patankar deferred correction methods
abstract: Positivity-preserving schemes for hyperbolic balance laws are typically built from the Zhang-Shu limiter and strong-stability-preserving Runge-Kutta (SSP-RK) time stepping, at the cost of a restrictive time-step condition. The modified Patankar deferred correction (mPDeC) method removes this restriction, offering high-order accuracy, conservation, and unconditional positivity. However, its solution-dependent Patankar weights make the time update nonlinear, so, unlike with RK methods, preserving (steady and moving) equilibria, i.e., well-balancing (WB), is no longer straightforward. In this paper, we construct high-order, WB, positivity-preserving mPDeC schemes by combining mPDeC with a flux-globalization approach. We demonstrate the idea on the one-dimensional shallow water equations, using a WB A-WENO spatial discretization, and introduce a modified local characteristic decomposition that remains stable in the presence of dry states. Numerical experiments on one-dimensional benchmarks confirm that the method satisfies the desired properties.

title: Weight structures and t-structures on the triangulated category generated by a $\mathbb{P}$-object
abstract: $\mathbb{P}$-objects were introduced by Huybrechts and Thomas as a generalization of spherical objects. We classify the weight structures and t-structures on the triangulated category generated by a $\mathbb{P}^n[k]$-object in the sense of Krug. For $n=1$, this recovers the classification of weight structures and t-structures on the triangulated category generated by a spherical object due to Holm, Jorgensen and Yang. We also compute the Koszul-dual model of the triangulated category generated by a $\mathbb{P}^n[k]$-object.

title: Diffusion-Induced Stabilization of Nonreciprocal Wealth Dynamics
abstract: We study the stability of equal wealth shares in a spatial model combining local sharing, global redistribution, and random nonreciprocal interactions. On a two-dimensional square lattice in the infinite-system limit, the effect of local sharing depends on whether the influence of one site on another tends to have the same or opposite sign as the reverse influence. When these influences are nonnegatively correlated, diffusion reduces the redistribution required for stability, but a positive rate remains necessary. Negative correlations instead allow stability without redistribution, with the largest stability margin at finite diffusion and a return toward marginal stability at strong diffusion. This nonmonotonicity reflects a competition between spatial smoothing and the weakening of the stabilizing contribution of reciprocal anticorrelations. Equal shares can even remain stable under wealth-concentrating transfers, but only within an intermediate range of diffusion strengths.

title: Localisation of the monkey walk with an "impurity" at the origin
abstract: The monkey walk is a model of reinforced random walk introduced by Boyer and Solis-Salas as a model for the exploratory behaviour of capuchin monkeys. At each step of the walk, the walker flips a biased coin to determine whether to take a simple, symmetric random walk step on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ or to "relocate", i.e. choose a time uniformly at random in its past and jump to where it was at that time. More recently, Boyer, Falc\'on-Cort\'es, Giuggioli and Majumdar looked at a modification of the model, where the probability to relocate is $\xi_0$ when the walker sits at the origin and $\xi>\xi_0$ anywhere else. We prove that, for all $\xi_0\in (0,1)$, if $\xi$ is sufficiently close to 1, then the monkey walk "localises", i.e. the position of the walker at time $n$, $W_n$, converges in distribution without any renormalisation. (We in fact prove convergence of the occupation measure of the walker.) This is in contrast with the case when $\xi = \xi_0$, for which it is known that $W_n/\sqrt{\log n}$ converges in distribution to a standard Gaussian (we say that the walk "diffuses"). Our proof relies on seeing the monkey walk as an infinitely-many colour P\'olya urn (a.k.a. measure-valued P\'olya process - MVPP) and then prove convergence of this urn, which is not straightforward as theorems from the literature on MVPPs do not apply directly.

title: Edge ideals of gapfree graphs with matching number $3$
abstract: We prove that if $G$ is a gapfree graph with matching number $3$, then every power $I(G)^q$, $q\geq2$, of its edge ideal has linear quotients, and hence a linear resolution. Our approach combines graph reductions based on clique domination of gapfree graphs and matching number with operations preserving linear quotients. We reduce the problem to $26$ non-co-chordal graphs on at most seven vertices. A new preservation theorem for gapfree edge addition, together with known results on duplication and gapfree expansion, handles all but one of these graphs. For the remaining graph on seven vertices, we construct a linear quotients ordering for the square and extend it recursively to every higher power.

title: Rich-neighbor 5-edge-colorings of subcubic graphs whose 3-vertices induce a matching
abstract: Let $\varphi$ be a proper edge-coloring of a graph $G$. An edge is called rich if all edges adjacent to it receive pairwise distinct colors. The coloring $\varphi$ is a rich-neighbor edge-coloring if every non-isolated edge is adjacent to a rich edge. Petru\v{s}evski and \v{S}krekovski introduced this notion as a relaxation of strong edge-coloring and conjectured that every connected subcubic graph other than $K_4$ admits a rich-neighbor $5$-edge-coloring. We establish the conjectured bound for every subcubic graph $G$ satisfying $\Delta(G[V_3])\leq 1,$ where $V_3$ is the set of vertices of degree $3$ in $G$. Equivalently, the $3$-vertices of $G$ induce a matching together with isolated vertices. This extends the result of Chen, Tan and Zhou for subcubic graphs with no adjacent $3$-vertices.

title: Provably Efficient Risk-Sensitive Offline Reinforcement Learning via Optimized Certainty Equivalents
abstract: Risk-sensitive reinforcement learning (RL) addresses decision-making under uncertainty and adverse outcomes. Learning risk-sensitive policies from fixed datasets is important when additional interaction with the environment is costly. Existing work on risk-sensitive RL focuses on online settings or specific risk measures, leaving a general theoretical understanding of its offline setting underdeveloped. In this work, we investigate efficient offline risk-sensitive RL using the optimized certainty equivalent (OCE), a general class of risk measures. We consider two formulations: dynamic-OCE RL, which applies OCE recursively at each step, and static-OCE RL, which applies a single OCE to the cumulative rewards. Under the tabular setting, we develop pessimistic value-iteration algorithms for both formulations and establish tight sublinear suboptimality bounds, explicitly capturing how risk sensitivity, encoded by utility functions, affects learning difficulty. Moreover, we establish minimax suboptimality lower bounds to characterize the problem's fundamental limits. To handle large state spaces, we further develop pessimistic least-squares value-iteration algorithms that incorporate the general OCE risk criterion into linear function approximation. We establish utility-dependent sublinear guarantees with explicit dependence on the feature dimension $d$. To our knowledge, we provide the first offline algorithms along with the first upper and lower suboptimality bounds for both dynamic- and static-OCE RL.

title: Twisted Artin-Schreier Theory I: $(C_p \rtimes C_{p-1})$-extensions of local function fields
abstract: Over any field $K$ of characteristic $p$, we parametrize the $(C_p\rtimes C_{p-1})$-extensions of $K$ using pairs of elements $(g,a) \in K\times K^\times$, via a "twisted" variant of Artin-Schreier theory. Focusing on the case of the local function field $K := \mathbb F_q(\!(\pi)\!)$ over a finite field $\mathbb F_q$ of characteristic $p$, we use this parametrization to obtain an exact formula for the count of all $(C_p\rtimes C_{p-1})$-extensions of $K$ with a given discriminant.

title: On Minimum Divergence for Distribution Reconstruction
abstract: We study the possibility of generalizing maximum-entropy reconstruction, which approximately recovers a probability distribution from finitely many (generalized) moments by minimizing the Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence to a reference measure. The reconstruction lies in an exponential family and is also the best KL approximation of the unknown distribution within that family: moment matching and information projection coincide. Replacing KL by a smooth f-divergence, the reconstruction still exists in an associated family, but the best approximation property does not. Specifically, a family is called entropy-adapted if the projection of any distribution matches its moments. We show that, up to equivalence, KL is the only $C^2$ f-divergence that is entropy-adapted, whatever the choice of the generalized moments. We illustrate the consequences of this failure numerically.

title: Volterra operators on the BMOA space of Dirichlet series
abstract: In this paper, we completely characterize the boundedness and compactness of Volterra operators on \(BMOA_{\mathcal D}\), the BMOA space of Dirichlet series, and estimate their essential and weak essential norms. We further prove that compactness, weak compactness, and complete continuity are equivalent for these operators. In particular, every Dirichlet polynomial symbol induces a compact Volterra operator on \(BMOA_{\mathcal D}\). We also prove that every such symbol induces a compact Volterra operator on the Bergman space of Dirichlet series \(\mathcal A_\mu^1\) for every admissible measure \(\mu\), extending the corresponding compactness theorem, previously established for \(1<p<\infty\), to the endpoint \(p=1\).

title: Strong NP-Hardness of Rank-2 Nonnegative Matrix Factorization
abstract: Nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) approximates a nonnegative matrix by the product of two nonnegative matrices with a prescribed inner dimension~$r$. The existence of an exact NMF can be decided in polynomial time for every fixed~$r$, and a best rank-$1$ NMF in the Frobenius norm can be obtained from a truncated singular value decomposition. We prove that computing a best rank-$2$ NMF in the Frobenius norm is strongly NP-hard. Our proof uses a polynomial-time reduction from \textsc{Clique} that produces symmetric positive-definite, completely positive matrices with polynomially bounded integer entries. The same reduction also establishes strong NP-hardness of rank-$2$ symmetric NMF.

title: One generation of the Standard Model as a quantum error-correcting code
abstract: Together with a right-handed neutrino, the fermions of one generation of the Standard Model are labelled by five bits, a combinatorial structure tied to anomaly cancellation. We make this precise. Anomaly cancellation is the vanishing of a cubic form, the defining property of triorthogonal codes, the quantum error-correcting codes behind magic state distillation. Removing the right-handed neutrino gives a $[[15,1,3]]_p$ code for every prime $p$, including the Bravyi-Kitaev code for $p = 2$. For qutrits it is the unique shortest distance-three triorthogonal code.
comments: 5 pages, 1 figure, 1 table; 12 pages of Supplemental Material. Code available at github.com/spdei/standard-model-code

title: Cohomogeneity one Hermann actions and backward mean curvature flows
abstract: Principal orbits of cohomogeneity one Hermann actions form a natural class of equifocal hypersurfaces in symmetric spaces of compact type. Based on Kollross's classification of cohomogeneity one actions on irreducible symmetric spaces of compact type, we obtain the time evolution of the squared norm of the shape operator and the mean curvature along the long-time solution of the backward mean curvature flows starting from their principal orbits. These results explicitly describe the authors' previous generalization of the results of Liu-Terng on backward mean curvature flows of isoparametric hypersurfaces to this class of equifocal hypersurfaces.

title: Scalar curvature, volume, and Weil-Petersson translation length
abstract: We construct metrics on pseudoAnosov mapping tori that make every fiber an intrinsically hyperbolic stable minimal surface, and which have scalar curvature identically -6. Using this, we give a new proof (with improved constant) of an inequality bounding the hyperbolic volume of a pseudoAnosov mapping torus by the Weil-Petersson translation length (and consequently, the entropy) of its monodromy.

title: Tauberian rates and the Baire property of ideals
abstract: We study Tauberian conditions on the successive differences of real sequences which ensure that: (i) ordinary convergence coincides with ideal convergence; or (ii) every ordinary accumulation point is an ideal cluster point; or (iii) every ordinary accumulation point is an ideal limit point. First, we prove that an ideal $\mathcal{I}$ has the Baire property if and only if there exists a positive sequence $(r_n)$ tending to zero, with $\sum_n r_n=\infty$, such that $$ |x_{n+1}-x_n|=O(r_n) $$ is a Tauberian condition for any of the three previous statements. Second, for analytic $P$-ideals, we characterize the validity of the Tauberian rate $O(1/n)$ in terms of properties of lower semicontinuous submeasures which represent it. Lastly, in the case of statistical limit points, we prove that $o(1/n)$ is a Tauberian condition for the statement (iii), whereas $O(1/n)$ need not suffice: in this sense, $o(1/n)$ is an optimal Tauberian rate for (iii). On the other hand, for statistical cluster points in (ii), $O(1/n)$ is an optimal one among nonincreasing rates. For every positive null sequence $(r_n)$ with divergent sum, we also construct a summable ideal $\mathcal{I}$ for which $o(r_n)$ is an optimal Tauberian rate for both statements (ii) and (iii).

title: GPU Parallel Pareto Local Search for Multi-objective QUBO
abstract: We revisit Pareto Local Search (PLS) for multi-objective quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problems. Multi-objective QUBO formulations have gained increasing attention as a universal modeling method and natural input for quantum optimization. While exact methods exist, their unconstrained binary structure makes them well-suited for heuristics such as PLS. At the same time, GPUs offer a powerful classical alternative to quantum-inspired optimization. We develop an efficient GPU-based parallel implementation of PLS for multi-objective QUBO problems. Our approach combines coarse-grained and fine-grained parallelization. On the coarse-grained level, an initial set of supported solutions is generated using weighted-sum optimization, from which multiple PLS processes are started in parallel. At the fine-grained level, neighborhood exploration is parallelized on the GPU by simultaneously evaluating binary-flip candidate solutions across all objectives. Non-dominated solutions are maintained using an ND-Tree data structure to support efficient Pareto updates. The implementation combines several known PLS techniques within a unified CPU/GPU hybrid architecture. We describe the algorithmic components, the GPU-specific design decisions, and report results from a computational study evaluating the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: A family of algebras that connects positroids, the Theta conjecture, the Delta conjecture, and Eulerian quasisymmetric functions
abstract: We define a family of algebras $\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,a,b}$ whose Hilbert series, when $n\le a+b\le n+2$, $a>0$, and $0<b<n$, enumerate certain positroid cells by codimension. Equivalently, these series enumerate certain affine permutations by length. We determine the graded $\mathfrak{S}_n$-module structure of these algebras by using exact sequences to derive an invertible recursion for their graded Frobenius characteristics when $a+b\ge n$ and then passing to the limit $a\rightarrow\infty$. In particular, the graded Frobenius characteristic $\mathrm{grFrob}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_{a+b-1}]/I_{a+b-1,a,b};q)=\operatorname{rev}_q(\omega((\Theta_{e_{a-1}}\Theta_{e_{b-1}}\nabla e_1)\mid_{t=0}))$, where $\operatorname{rev}_q$ reverses the $q$-coefficients and the specialization $(\Theta_{e_{a-1}}\Theta_{e_{b-1}}\nabla e_1)\mid_{t=0}$ appears in the Theta conjecture. For $a,b\ge1$, we also show that $e_a^\perp\mathrm{grFrob}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_{a+b}]/I_{a+b,a,b};q)=q^{\binom{a}{2}}\operatorname{rev}_q(\omega((\Delta_{e_{a-1}}^\prime e_b)\mid_{t=0}))$, where $\Delta_{e_{k-1}}^\prime e_n$ occurs in the Delta conjecture. In the three cases $a+b-n=0,1,2$, the ungraded Frobenius characteristics agree with three families of Eulerian quasisymmetric functions, respectively. We also construct an open subvariety of $(\mathbb{P}^{k-1})^n$ whose rational Chow ring is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,k,n-k}$. This variety admits a stratification induced by certain positroids. Its strata need not be affine, and their codimension generating function equals $\mathrm{Hilb}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,k,n-k};q)$.

title: Cutoff Phenomenon for the Glauber-Misanthrope process in a perturbative regime
abstract: We investigate the Glauber--Misanthrope process, obtained by superposing a Misanthrope dynamics with finite site capacity and a Glauber dynamics which creates or annihilates particles one at a time at each site. In a perturbative regime around the diffusively scaled partial exclusion process, we prove the cutoff phenomenon and identify the limiting mixing time. Our approach relies on the information percolation framework developed by Lubetzky and Sly and extended by Tran, which we adapt to accommodate multiple occupancy per site and account for the two distinct correlation mechanisms generated by the Misanthrope and Glauber dynamics. Our lower bound on the mixing time holds under assumptions more general than those required for the matching upper bound.

title: Isaac's Condition (TU) is false
abstract: In 2006 Isaac reduced the simple normality to base $2$ of $\sqrt s$, for $s$ not a perfect square, to a property of dyadic expansions that he called Condition~(TU): the upper frequency of the digit~$1$ in $\sqrt\nu$, along any subsequence, depends only on the tail of the expansion of $\nu$. We show that Condition~(TU) is false, already for the full sequence. We give two proofs. The first is elementary and turns Isaac's own reduction against the condition. The second uses the theorem of Kaufman and Mosquera--Shmerkin on the Fourier decay of smooth images of self-similar measures, and gives counterexamples for almost every point of a Cantor measure. All results are machine-verified in Lean~4; the second proof uses the two cited theorems as hypotheses.

title: Local Convexity and Planarity Estimates for Mean Curvature Flow
abstract: We establish local convexity and cylindrical pinching estimates for hypersurface mean curvature flow under an intermediate convexity condition and integral bounds on the mean curvature. These estimates hold after a positive waiting time and do not require pointwise upper bounds for the mean curvature on the parabolic boundary. In arbitrary codimension, we also establish local planarity estimates for properly defined flows satisfying a uniform $c_n$-pinching condition, without assuming bounded curvature. As applications, the hypersurface estimates yield convexity and cylindrical pinching for complete, spacetime-proper ancient hypersurface flows with uniform Euclidean area growth, without any bounded-curvature assumption. The planarity estimates imply that every complete, connected, spacetime-proper ancient flow satisfying the uniform $c_n$-pinching condition is either a static affine $n$-plane or lies in a fixed affine $(n+1)$-plane for all time.

title: Reconstruction of Fano manifolds from the orthogonal to an exceptional vector bundle
abstract: Let $X$ and $Y$ be smooth complex Fano manifolds of dimension at least three with very ample anticanonical bundles and let $V_X$ and $V_Y$ be exceptional vector bundles on $X$ and $Y$, respectively. We prove that a Fourier--Mukai equivalence $V_X^\perp\simeq V_Y^\perp$ implies $X\simeq Y$.

title: The Tilted Sampling Problem: Optimism, Posterior Sampling, and Logarithmic Regret
abstract: Many modern learning systems are used not to select a single best action, but to sample diverse high-quality outputs. Examples include entropy-regularized reinforcement learning, RLHF, and reward-guided generative modeling. Motivated by these settings, we study tilted sampling: an online learning problem in which the goal is to sample from the Gibbs distribution induced by an unknown reward function. We define sampling regret as the temperature-normalized cumulative KL divergence between the learner's distribution and the Gibbs target, corresponding to the suboptimality gap in entropy-regularized reward maximization. Our framework generalizes recent sampling-based and KL-regularized formulations in bandits and reinforcement learning. Our main contribution is a general regret framework that captures the different uncertainty structure of tilted sampling and classical regret minimization. While standard regret scales as $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{T})$ due to first-order uncertainty, sampling regret is governed by squared confidence widths, yielding logarithmic-in-$T$ regret in standard settings at fixed temperature. We develop sampling analogues of UCB and Thompson sampling (UCS and TS$^2$) and provide unified regret decompositions that explain and extend recent logarithmic guarantees, including the first Bayesian sampling-regret decomposition based on new bounds for posterior-random Gibbs distributions. Our results show that learning to sample from a soft-optimal distribution is statistically distinct from learning to identify a hard optimum.

title: A variation on local trilinear form
